title: Offense shines in Wildcats’ third straight win, moves to 3-0 in UAC play
author: Zion Webb
content: Wildcat football seems to have hit a groove with three straight wins ahead of its bye week, taking down North Alabama 31-28 on a walk-off field goal to improve to 3-0 in United Athletic Conference play and 4-4 overall after starting 1-4. The dagger came from the guy who did it before: Brandon Perez, the senior kicker who connected on a 37-yard field goal as time expired, capping a 54-yard drive that began with 3:34 remaining. He did the same to secure a win over Tarleton State last season, which helped ACU become back-to-back UAC champions. Head coach Keith Patterson said the team would get back to this point at some time. ACU also started 4-4 in 2025, then went on to win out the rest of the season before falling to Stephen F. Austin in the second round of the playoffs. Patterson also said he had no problem trusting his guys late down the stretch. “We have nothing but confidence in our specialists, and we have every year that I’ve been here,” Patterson said. “We feel very prepared and very comfortable in those situations. So I think the walk-offs are just a byproduct of it.” A big reason the Wildcats were in this game was their redshirt sophomore quarterback, Tucker Parks. Parks completed 21 of 25 passes for 264 yards, the highest total of his career, and two touchdowns without an interception. That has become normal lately, with no interceptions in the past three games after he threw five in his first three games. A lot of his success came from the return of senior running back Alex Broome and redshirt senior wide receiver Cristian Driver, who had both been out for about a month. Driver opened the game with a 76-yard touchdown and finished with five catches for 120 yards and a score. Broome was limited to 10 yards on seven carries but scored the Wildcats’ first third-quarter touchdown of the 2026 season. Redshirt senior tight end Jayden York, who has become a top target for Parks recently, added five receptions for 67 yards and a touchdown. He also caught a special 2-point conversion in the fourth quarter, which began with a Parks pitch to freshman wideout Romelo Boykin, who dumped it off to York when a North Alabama defender came at him. Offensive tackle Luke Roaten said the team remained confident heading into the final drive. “We knew what we had to do, and we had to drive the ball down,” Roaten said. “I think the biggest thing was confidence.” Linebacker Darius Moore emphasized the importance of the victory as ACU heads into its open week. “We needed that one real bad,” Moore said. “You know, we’re going 3-0 in conference. It’s huge.” The Wildcats will take advantage of the open week to continue to get better ahead of their Homecoming game against West Georgia on Halloween. “This is just an open week, not an off week,” Moore said. “I don’t think we’re really approaching this week any differently than we would any other week. That’s our program, character, discipline, toughness at all times. So, I feel like it’s no different.” The post Offense shines in Wildcats’ third straight win, moves to 3-0 in UAC play appeared first on The Optimist .

title: ACU alumni relations plans second international trip to Portugal
author: Makayla Clayton
content: Alumni will have the opportunity to travel to Portugal in September 2027 as the university continues developing a travel program designed to strengthen connections between alumni and the university. The 13-day trip will take participants through several regions of Portugal, beginning in Porto and continuing along the Portuguese Riviera to the medieval city of Évora and the Algarve before ending in the capital, Lisbon. The tour includes 17 meals and opportunities to experience Portugal’s coastal scenery, historic towns, cobblestone streets and cultural attractions. The cost is $6,649 per person for double occupancy or $8,149 per person for single occupancy. Single accommodations are limited and available on a first-come, first-served basis. The price includes round-trip airfare from Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport, air taxes and fees, surcharges and hotel transfers. The trip will be the second international trip organized through the Alumni Relations Office, following a trip to Austria at the end of summer 2026 that included 14 participants. Craig Fisher, vice president for advancement and alumni, said the program is intended to give alumni opportunities to travel together while building relationships with fellow Wildcats. “We want to develop an opportunity for alumni to travel together,” Fisher said. “It’s a way for engagement back at the university, but also with fellow ACU kids.” The Alumni Relations Office spent about a year researching travel companies, talking with alumni and gathering feedback from the Alumni Advisory Board before launching the program. The university partnered with Colette, a travel company that organizes international and domestic group trips. Fisher said the office hopes to offer a trip every 12 to 18 months, depending on the destination and cost. The office is also considering future domestic trips and shorter travel opportunities. The trips include visits to multiple cities, historical sites and cultural experiences, along with time for participants to explore independently. Some meals and activities are scheduled as a group, while others allow travelers to choose their own experiences. Fisher said working with a larger travel company also gives alumni access to group rates and experiences that might be more difficult to arrange independently. Athena Crum, alumni and university relations officer, said the travel program offers alumni a way to maintain the connections they built while attending ACU. “I think it’s really unique that we have opportunities like this as ACU alums that we might not get in other places,” Crum said. “There really is that difference of the bond between ACU alums no matter where you go.” Fisher said the university wants alumni to remain connected long after graduation, especially because their college years often shape their faith, relationships and transition into adulthood. “It’s not just you go there for four years and you’re done,” Fisher said. The Alumni Relations Office plans to continue exploring ways for alumni to reconnect through travel, reunions and other university events. Fisher said future trips could also include faculty members or university representatives who could provide additional educational experiences related to history, art or culture. He said the goal is to build opportunities that allow alumni to continue learning and connecting with the university and one another throughout their lives. “The people that have made ACU stronger over the years,” Fisher said. “We want to see our people continue to love this place dearly.” Alumni interested in the Portugal trip or seeking additional information can contact Athena Crum: athena.crum@acu.edu The post ACU alumni relations plans second international trip to Portugal appeared first on The Optimist .

title: Missions Week encourages local and international missions
author: Kendall Stacey
content: Missions Week began with the nonprofit and volunteer fair on Monday. This week, events will lead up to the World Wide Witness application night on Wednesday. At the nonprofit and volunteer fair, students were encouraged to explore missions opportunities in Abilene and their hometowns before considering an overseas mission. “We’re really trying to move towards pushing students to think about service and missions as an everyday way of life,” said Zane McGee, director of Halbert Center for Missions. Tuesday night featured international worship where international students led worship in their languages. “That will kind of give us an insight into the reality that God’s working in other cultures, and other countries, with other people so different than us,” said Larry Henderson, Director of World Wide Witness. In addition to the worship, the event also included tables for students to come together and pray about different issues around the world “that need God’s presence,” Henderson said. Wednesday night will feature the World Wide Witness kickoff. This night of Missions Week is an informal gathering with fire pits and s’mores, where students can ask questions about summer internship opportunities with World Wide Witness. Students who apply for a World Wide Witness trip Wednesday night will receive a $1,000 scholarship toward their trip costs. In addition to the scholarship, students will receive training for their mission, which will help them raise money. This year, mission directors wanted to emphasize that missions opportunities are available in Abilene, regardless of whether students go on a trip. McGee said the week began with the nonprofit fair to introduce students to local volunteer opportunities. In continuing this idea, there was a luncheon with the nonprofit leaders and faculty where they discussed ways that students and faculty could collaborate with them, McGee said. Students from every major and background are invited to participate in missions and service opportunities, Henderson said. Staff members are also open to hearing how students can use their individual roles and skills to glorify God. title: Beyond the ballot: Voting and civic engagement at ACU
author: Taylor Harrison
content: For ACU students planning to vote in the Nov. 3 general election, early voting begins Monday, Oct. 19, and runs through Friday, Oct. 30. Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3. The deadline to register to vote in Texas for this election was Monday, Oct. 5, so students who missed it cannot register for the November election. Students who are already registered can check their registration status and find election information through VoteTexas . Students registered in Taylor County can vote early at any early-voting location in the county. Taylor County Elections provides polling locations, hours and current election information through its Current Election page . Students registered in their home counties may still be able to request a mail ballot, depending on whether they qualify and their county’s deadlines. In Taylor County, the Elections Office must receive written applications for a ballot by mail by Friday, Oct. 23; deadlines and eligibility rules can differ by county. Before voting, students can review a sample ballot, research candidates and learn about the offices and measures that will appear on their ballot. Madelynn Garrett, a sophomore government major from Abilene, said researching candidates is often the most intimidating part of voting, but it is also one of the most valuable steps. “You can literally just go on Google and be like, ‘Who is running for Senate and governor right now in Texas?’” Garrett said. “Find out what they said in the past year about what they would like to implement in Texas, what they really stand for and whether that aligns with your values.” For students who feel disconnected from politics, voting can be a starting point for civic engagement. Garrett said voting is one of the most important ways students can use their voice. “It is probably the most important thing you can do because it is a right given to you,” Garrett said. “If you don’t use that right, then what is it there for?” Garrett said many students want generational change and new policies, but those changes require participation at the ballot box. “If you don’t vote, then the people’s opinions that are voting are going to take over your life,” Garrett said. “This is your time to be able to have your voice out there and be able to vote in people that will represent you.” Dr. Benjamin Peterson, assistant professor of government and criminal justice, said voting is one way students can participate in the communities that affect them. Rather than treating it as a required civic test, Peterson said students can view voting as an opportunity to become more involved in public life. “I think of it as an important civic opportunity,” Peterson said. “A kind of badge of citizen membership in various communities.” Peterson said students should not feel pressured to support a candidate simply because the candidate appears on the ballot. Students may leave a race blank if they do not have an informed position. “I think people should earn your vote,” Peterson said. “You can vote for things that you have a view on and leave blank, you know, abstain from things that you don’t have a view on.” However, Peterson said civic participation should not begin or end with a general election. Primary elections, local elections and political organizations give voters opportunities to participate before candidates reach a November ballot. “Politics is shaped by the people who get involved in a sustained way,” Peterson said. Peterson said the options voters see in general elections often are shaped months or years before Election Day. “When we come to the general election, a lot of us are kind of like, ‘Oh, well, we only have two bad options,’” Peterson said. “But that’s because all the shaping and agenda setting has been done months, years before that, leading up to that choice.” Primary elections often receive less attention than general elections, but they determine each party’s nominees. Students who want to influence later ballot choices can research candidates earlier, participate in primaries, attend local political-party activities or organize around issues important to them. Garrett said she understands the frustration students may feel with a political system that often presents only two major-party choices. Still, she encouraged students not to disengage completely. “Neither party is perfect,” Garrett said. “But definitely go toward one that you think will do good for everybody, not just yourself.” Dissatisfaction with candidates can become a reason to participate earlier in the political process rather than a reason to disengage completely. Students can attend local meetings, connect with campaigns, discuss issues with other voters or consider public service. “If you don’t like the candidates, maybe that means you should get involved,” Peterson said. Garrett said students do not need to be government majors or complete internships in Washington, D.C., to make a difference. Local government, student government and community organizations offer accessible ways to begin. “Staying local is honestly the best way to go,” Garrett said. “You can work for the mayor’s office or someone on City Council. You can join SGA, be on a board in Abilene or volunteer in the community.” Garrett said Student Government Association is a particularly useful starting point because it mirrors the structure of government through executive, legislative and judicial branches. “SGA doesn’t have direct politics involved, but we pass legislation,” Garrett said. “You get to work on passing bills, learn how the process works and see how things run.” Peterson said voting can be a starting point rather than the only form of civic engagement. “I hope voting can serve as a kind of … impetus for realizing we are involved and embedded in a lot of different communities and a lot of different arenas and avenues for collective action,” Peterson said. Garrett said volunteering is another civic activity every college student should try because it reveals how policy and community conditions affect real people. She volunteers with Breakfast on Beech Street, a downtown Abilene program that serves breakfast and prepares lunches for people experiencing homelessness. “You get to see there are a lot of people in Abilene who are homeless, and it’s only rising,” Garrett said. “It gives me passion to say, ‘We need to solve this homeless crisis.’ They’re not homeless just because they choose to be. This is how society is affecting them.” Garrett said community service and volunteer work can help students understand why political engagement matters beyond Election Day. “Volunteering shows you how politics affects people,” Garrett said. “It’s rewarding because you’re giving back to your community, and it helps you see the issues you may want to address through policy.” Through voting and beyond, students have many opportunities to participate in civic life and take steps toward making a difference in their communities. title: Soccer gains confidence with strong road performances
author: Carter Calvin
content: ACU soccer is finding its rhythm as conference play continues, with the team gaining confidence from recent road wins and looking to carry momentum into the final stretch of the regular season. The Wildcats enter Friday’s matchup with a 6-2-5 overall record and a 3-0-2 record in conference play. “We’re peaking at the right time,” head coach Stephen Salas said. “We feel pretty good about where we’re at.” ACU will host West Georgia at noon Friday at Elmer Gray Stadium after the game was moved from its originally scheduled Thursday evening time because of the weather forecast. The game is scheduled to proceed Friday as long as weather conditions cooperate The Wildcats have continued to improve offensively as conference play has progressed. After several low-scoring games earlier in the season, ACU scored three goals against Tarleton State and two against Austin Peay. Salas said the team has created more scoring opportunities, including corner kicks and shots, but still needs to be more effective in the final third of the field. Defensively, the Wildcats also showed improvement during their recent road trips, allowing just one goal across two games. Salas said maintaining that defensive strength while continuing to produce offensively will be important during the remaining five regular-season conference games. Addison Briscoe, freshman forward, said one of the biggest differences she has noticed is how the team has grown together since the beginning of conference play. “I just feel like the team has clicked really well on the field,” she said. She also pointed to the team’s leadership as a major factor in its progress. The captains have led through their actions and communication, she said, helping motivate players through difficult games and reminding them that they are working toward a common goal. Salas highlighted sophomore goalkeeper Bella Medrano for her performances in goal and junior captain Gracie Kelly for her leadership on the back line. He also recognized Briscoe, who leads the conference with seven goals and has recorded three assists. Despite the recent success, the Wildcats know they cannot afford to become comfortable. Briscoe said the team needs to stay focused and continue working toward its larger goals rather than relying on its recent wins. “We can celebrate that and take wins in for some confidence, but we can’t just be OK with that,” she said. “We have a bigger goal in mind.” With five regular-season conference games remaining, including four at home, the Wildcats are looking to build on their recent performances and finish the season strong. title: GSP 68-hour volleyball event fundraises for Hope Weavers
author: Amelie Aquino
content: Gamma Sigma Phi’s 68-hour volleyball fundraiser event is underway at the Student Recreation and Wellness Center. The event began at 7 p.m. on Thursday and will go on until Sunday at 3 p.m. Anyone can participate, even those from the Abilene community. GSP has held its annual 68-hour volleyball since 2012 and the number 68 comes from the club being founded in 1968. Every year, GSP picks a different nonprofit organization to donate money to, via their fundraiser. Last year, GSP fundraised for Habitat for Humanity, which is an international Christian nonprofit organization that seeks to build affordable housing. This year, the organization they chose is Hope Weavers, an Abilene-based nonprofit organization that serves educators and their families during medical crises and other life-altering events, according to the Texas Retired Teacher’s Association. Jonah Pedroza, senior management major from Mansfield, serves as GSP’s senior service activities coordinator and is in charge of the club’s activities as well as connecting the club to the community. Pedroza said that this year’s organization was a great pick because it relates more to Abilene. “I really wanted to find an organization that was a little bit more rooted in the Abilene community,” Pedroza said. “Because Habitat, they do great things here, but it’s a nationwide thing” Over the summer, Pedroza got lunch with David Chavez, a retired educator who founded Hope Weavers, and began planning this fundraiser. “At the time I was looking for our official club volunteer partner too, and it became pretty clear that his need was definitely more in getting his organization started,” Pedroza said. “He needed the funds to give to the teachers.” The focus of Hope Weavers is to give back to educators who have spent countless hours giving back to the community. “I didn’t know this until I got lunch with him, but like teachers, when stuff happens, they’re kind of left out to dry with their benefits,” Pedroza said. “So [Hope Weavers] are kind of trying to fill that need between the district and the teachers.” The link to donate money went live earlier this week, allowing anyone to donate and support Hope Weavers. When filling out the form, click “other” under Area To Support and type “GSP 68 hour volleyball” under details. All of the money donated will go straight to the organization. “Even though GSP is putting this on, GSP benefits nothing from this,” Pedroza said. “We’re not taking home a penny, we’re literally just the ones giving the check to Hope Weavers.” There will be an organized volleyball tournament on Friday night and GSP will bring a volleyball net to New Member Orientation to get the chance to meet some potential new members. “It’s another chance for us to hang out and play volleyball,” Pedroza said. “Even if you’re not a volleyball player, I think when you have something that’s kind of out of the ordinary, but on your calendar, you’re more incentivized to do it.” Evan McAlister, senior Bible major from Franklin, Tennessee, serves as GSP’s president and will be present for a significant portion of the event. “I’m gonna be here a whole bunch over the next three days,” McAlister said. “Me and at least one other person will be here at 3 a.m. playing volleyball.” McAlister said that volleyball is a big aspect of GSP, adding to its significance as a charitable event. “Volleyball is just a big thing for our club,” McAlister said. “We do volleyball club nights, we participate in volleyball intramural and we win it often.” The focus of the event isn’t to connect with students who are rushing, but more for the general public and to draw attention to Hope Weavers. “Do I hope that there’s freshmen and PNMs here? Yes,” McAlister said. “But more from the perspective of, I hope that everyone is here, and I hope that everyone is involved with this.” McAlister wants this event to stretch beyond the club. “We’re always looking for opportunities to do things around campus in the ACU community, and I think 68-hour volleyball is a really special way that we get to do that,” McAlister said. “I just hope [this event] is bigger than just GSP.” After 68-hour volleyball, GSP will focus on their biking to Malibu fundraiser, which will take place during Spring Break with the ultimate goal of fundraising to support students affected by the Los Angeles wildfires. title: Greek Life prepares students for spring rush with teas, coffees
author: Makayla Clayton
content: Students interested in joining Greek Life will have the opportunity to learn more about campus clubs during Sorority Teas and Fraternity Coffees, which begin Friday as part of the spring rushing process. Robin McPherson, senior coordinator for Greek Life, said the events give potential new members the opportunity to learn about each organization participating in spring recruitment and meet other students going through the process. “It’s part of a mandatory part of the process,” McPherson said. “They have to go through both of these activities, whether they’re men or women.” The men’s coffee events will take place in the mall area, where organizations will set up tents in a tailgate-style atmosphere. Students can rotate between organizations, scan QR codes and have conversations to learn more about each club. The women’s tea events will take place in scheduled classrooms in the Onstead-Packer Biblical Studies Building. Students will meet in groups of about 30 to 40 and rotate through informational sessions about each organization, including its values, colors, motto and philanthropy. McPherson said the events help students explore their options before deciding which organizations they want to pursue. Registration opens Oct. 17 through Suitable, with a $20 nonrefundable fee. The fee increases to $40 Nov. 17, and registration closes Dec. 2. Open rushes will take place in two rounds, Nov. 18-20 and Nov. 30-Dec. 2. During the first two rounds, potential new members are expected to attend rush events for at least three different organizations. Four organizations also participated in fall pledging this year, including three men’s organizations and one women’s organization. McPherson said the opportunity allows smaller organizations to bring in additional members during the fall while still participating in spring recruitment. Athena Crum, alumni and university relations officer at ACU, said rushing helped her find community when she first arrived on campus. She said as an introvert who moved halfway across the country for college, the process pushed her and helped her meet other students. “Rushing really got me out of my comfort zone and out of my shell,” Crum said. Crum said her involvement in club later helped her develop leadership skills, build friendships and become more involved in campus life. She encouraged students to consider rushing even if they are unsure whether they will ultimately join an organization. McPherson encouraged students to consider their ability to balance Greek Life with their academic responsibilities and personal well-being. “We’re here to get a degree,” McPherson said. “Academics will always take priority over rushing.” For students deciding between organizations, McPherson encouraged them to look for groups that genuinely want to know them. “Who is intentional about wanting to know me, the real me?” McPherson said. “And who is really interested in me the way I am?” Crum offered similar advice, encouraging students to pay attention to where they feel welcomed and connected. “Choose the people who choose you,” Crum said. title: Lars Larson: Lessons from the riots
author: In the news
content: By Lars Larson NW and national radio host, The Northwest Nonsense: The riots and violence in France seem like a great warning to Americans (and those of us here in the Northwest). After all, we’re told that the chaos comes from people unhappy with their circumstances. France has a guaranteed 35-hour work week, paid family leave and universal health care. Citizens enjoy subsidized child care, generous housing subsidies, and heavily subsidized college. In other words, France spends most of its government budget providing goodies for citizens…exactly the same policies that the Democrats propose for Americans. And therein lies the danger: when you promise everything to everyone at no cost, then it’s easy for folks to get dissatisfied when anything falls short. If you, instead, guarantee equal opportunity to citizens and they know it’s up to them to make something of it, if people aren’t happy with the results, they know who has to work harder. I’m told the polls show socialism has amazingly high popularity. It’s tough to top Santa Claus. 43 years ago, Ronald Reagan told folks “a government big enough to give you everything you want is big enough to take away everything you’ve got.” He’s still right today. That’s the Rose City Rap. Join me at noon on KXL for 4 hours of honestly provocative talk. I’m Lars Larson The post Lars Larson: Lessons from the riots first appeared on Oregon Catalyst .

title: Angela Plowhead wants health care fixes, not health care tax hikes
author: In the news
content: By Oregon Campaign Profile Series, Angela Plowhead is running for Senate District 10 in the Salem area. Working in the health care field, Plowhead is very concerned about a new universal health care plan being cooked up in Salem, which is expected to cost taxpayers 43% in higher taxes . Picking up this seat would make it harder for a one-party supermajority to pass new taxes like this new plan calls for.   Plowhead said instead of a massive new government health system, she would like to see, increased access to care, “by eliminating Oregon’s certificate of need currently restricting treatment capacity, adding reciprocity of licensure for providers across state lines which would help increase the number of providers, and reducing the cost of licenses to make it easier to recruit, retain providers, and open up clinics.” A new 100-bed psychiatric hospital would be providing much needed services in Wilsonville right now but the state denied a Certificate of Need a few years ago. — You can find more information on candidate Angela Plowhead at Angela4Oregon.com . — Oregon Campaign Profile is a project of the Taxpayers Association of Oregon The post Angela Plowhead wants health care fixes, not health care tax hikes first appeared on Oregon Catalyst .

title: Sen. Anderson on Pacific Seafood fire
author: In the news
content: Sen. Dick Anderson Statement on Pacific Seafoods Fire in Newport By Oregon State Senator Dick Anderson,   SALEM, Ore. – Sen. Dick Anderson (R-Lincoln City) issued the following statement on the fire at the Pacific Seafoods facility on Newport’s Historic Bayfront:   “My thoughts are with the people of Newport today, especially the workers at Pacific Seafoods, the families and businesses along the bayfront, and the first responders who are working to keep our community safe.   “My message to everyone is simple: please steer clear of the area and let the officials do their job. Don’t go to the bayfront to watch or take photos. If you are within a mile of the facility, follow the evacuation orders from the Lincoln County Sheriff’s Office. The sheriff’s office website has an evacuation map, and the city has opened a shelter at Sam Case Elementary School, 459 NE 12th St., where evacuees can bring their pets. Every road that stays clear helps firefighters and hazmat crews work safely and quickly.   “I’ve been in contact with State Fire Marshal Mariana Ruiz-Temple. Her office has sent a hazmat team, which is monitoring the air because of anhydrous ammonia used for refrigeration at the facility. The Fire Marshal reports that the ammonia tank has been located and doesn’t appear to be punctured or leaking. Additional firefighters from Marion and Lane counties are on their way to relieve Newport crews.   “I’m grateful to the Newport firefighters, the Lincoln County Sheriff’s Office, and the state and regional crews who are responding. My office will keep working with state and local officials to support Newport and Lincoln County through the response and recovery. If you need help connecting with state resources, please contact my office.”   Constituents can reach Sen. Anderson’s office at Sen.DickAnderson@oregonlegislature.gov . The post Sen. Anderson on Pacific Seafood fire first appeared on Oregon Catalyst .

title: Oregon kids’ film unsafe, violent
author: In the news
content: By Jason Williams, Taxpayers Association of Oregon OregonWatchdog.com …It appears our tax dollars are going to another film that would have been made without it. This time, it is a children’s film that is grossly unsafe for children — and topped off with an Oregon story-line setting. The story is based in Portland with local icons like Pittock Mansion, St. John’s Bridge and Powells Books. The film begins with a naked boy who commits suicide by jumping to his death. It is visceral. One parent who saw it said, “This caused my daughter to wail uncontrollably, forcing me to exit the theater.” Aaron Jamelle Morgan posted online, “The opening scene is a 12yr old kid committing suicide by jumping from the top balcony of the mansion and no it’s not blacked out or cut scene it’s SHOWN. There is zero trigger warning. There is cussing and heads being cut off in the war scene and eyes being pecked out by birds.” This pro-violence kids’ tale has already become one of the biggest box-office bombs of the year. It took 15 years to make and $400 million to fund, and it only brought in a projected $11 million over the weekend. There are beheading scenes and scenes where a baby is almost stabbed and scenes where blood splatters on people’s faces. It doesn’t matter that the film is PG-13. If you make a classic, child-fashioned animated film and put young people in the lead roles, kids will see it. There are six year olds in the theater. The director refused to ease up on the violence, saying there was no other way of communicating violence without showing disturbing violence. The entire history of film has shown ways to show terrible things without being graphic. The director just refused to do it. The director wanted to be edgy and daring but at our children’s innocence’s expense. These progressive films treat our kids like garbage. If you want fewer school shootings by disturbed teens, try not filling their young brains with bloody, graphic scenes when they are six years old. The entire liberal Hollywood is dumping violence on our kids … and taxpayers are subsidizing it. Disney bought the kids’ favorite Star Wars franchise, and then began to introduce scenes of a stripper bar, prostitutes, profanity, and the hero shooting a police officer who was on his knees begging for mercy. Disney bought Marvel Comics and featured the hero Star-Lord shooting another law enforcement officer when he was wounded on the ground and hurting. In Disney’s Black Widow, the superheroes blow up an entire prison, killing everyone inside. Many of our children’s shows feature heroes doing villainous, unethical, and outright violent things. The new Wildwood may be an artistic genius, but the more talented it is, the more evil it is to shove it on our children. Putting poison in a cake does not make it right. If the cake is a $1,000 wedding cake, it doesn’t make it less wrong. The Wildwood creators and their bloody ways should stay out of the children’s world if you aren’t going to be responsible. title: A Policy Renaissance Begins at Home: Kimberley Strassel’s Message for Oregon
author: Cascade Policy Institute
content: By Naomi Inman Cascade Policy Institute’s 35th Anniversary Dinner offered many memorable moments, with Kimberley Strassel’s keynote as the highlight of the evening. Speaking to a packed room of Oregonians yearning for better governance, Strassel delivered a sweeping, humorous, and ultimately hopeful assessment of American politics today. While Washington, D.C. may be mired in dysfunction, she emphasized that many states are leading a renaissance of policy innovation—and Oregon has an opportunity to join them. Strassel opened with personal reflections rooted in her Oregon upbringing. Recalling childhood trips to Seaside’s “very old aquarium” and the Ashland Shakespeare Festival, her affection for the state and her wry humor immediately warmed the audience. “At my amazing old age,” she laughed, “this is the first time I have ever, ever been invited to speak in Oregon. This is also the first time that most of my family has ever seen me speak.” She added, “To read the press, you wouldn’t think that there were this many free market, liberty loving people in all of Oregon—and here you all are.” From nostalgia, she pivoted to a candid diagnosis of federal politics. After three decades covering national affairs, Strassel argued that Congress has abandoned its core responsibilities, describing Washington, D.C. as “a certifiable clown car… every time you think it can’t get more absurd, something crazy jumps out at you.” Budgets go undone, appropriations stall, and major national challenges remain unaddressed. Instead, she said, “Washington has devolved into politics all the time,” a perpetual cycle of investigations and partisan trench warfare. The result is institutional decay, executive overreach, judicial politicization, and—she emphasized—“It took this country 230 years to reach its first 20 trillion in debt. It took this recent Congress nine years to double it.” “We’re not doing policy, we’re doing politics,” she lamented, before breaking the tension with a smile: “So, are you all demoralized yet?” Then she lifted her tone. “We are seeing something amazing going on in the country right now. It’s the kernel of rejuvenation that we need. But it is not happening in D.C.—it’s happening in the states.” She highlighted a “school choice revolution” surging in 33 states, with dozens of programs expanding and 19 states adopting universal eligibility. During COVID, she noted, “parents suddenly saw the extraordinarily deplorable state of education in this country and it absolutely energized them… demanding that politicians give them choice in education.” She pointed to additional reforms gaining traction: tax reform, property tax revolts, occupational licensing reform, litigation reform, and pluralism in higher education. Millions of Americans, she noted, are leaving high-tax coastal states for places offering lower taxes, safer communities, stronger schools, and more freedom. “This brings me to the elephant in the room,” she said. “Why all this talk about revolution when we aren’t seeing it in Oregon?” She acknowledged Oregon’s challenges—high taxes, struggling schools, homelessness, and a hollowed-out downtown Portland—but insisted that political change begins locally. Recent signs of voter pushback, including the 83–17 rejection of new transportation taxes, suggest Oregonians may be ready for a new direction. Strassel closed with a tribute to Cascade Policy Institute and its supporters. Free market organizations in blue states, she argued, do the hardest and most essential work: educating, equipping, and sustaining the ideas that make reform possible when political tides finally turn. “If we aren’t involved in groups like Cascade, then the other side takes over, and we have no voice anymore.” “All this work—the education, the good ideas, the fortitude—this is going to be, I promise you, the basis of a revival in the state. But it also very much depends on you… Get re-involved in your universities, your civic groups. Our founders viewed that world as the place where almost everything was supposed to be happening. Politics was supposed to be very limited.” Her message landed as both warning and encouragement. Oregon may be near rock bottom—but renewal is possible. “The revolution always starts at home,” she concluded. “It’s a republic if you can keep it. And keeping it starts right here. Go out there and save Oregon.” Naomi Inman is External Relations Manager at Cascade Policy Institute, Oregon’s free market public policy research organization. As a staff journalist and writer, Naomi helps Cascade make the case for free-market policies through media affairs and publications. title: Adam Wilson seeks the tools needed to help reduce homeless
author: In the news
content: By Oregon Campaign Profile, In House District 7 covering Springfield, Republican contender Adam Wilson wants to overturn a five-year-old law (House Bill 3115), which he says limits what local governments can do to eradicate vagrancy and homeless encampments. “Why are the police not arresting someone who’s just clearly walking around on drugs, littering and that?” Wilson added repealing the law will help with the current problems. “In Salem they just keep throwing more money at it and raise taxes to do so, and it’s obviously not working.” Portland just cleaned up a homeless camp and found dead bodies inside. This is happening near schools and people’s homes. If elected, Wilson says he will present legislation to do away with HB 3115 and allow for vagrancy laws, “meaning vagrancy essentially defined as public intoxication of narcotics while camping where you do not have a permanent residence.” He explained, “it’s something that people have really locked into in my district because it’s actionable, like there is a law on the books preventing police departments from actually doing the job citizens want them to do, and it’s a very quick fix if we could get the votes. — You can find more information on candidate Adam Wilson at Wilson for Oregon . — Oregon Campaign Profile is a project of the Taxpayers Association of Oregon The post Adam Wilson seeks the tools needed to help reduce homeless first appeared on Oregon Catalyst .

title: Accountability coming to Oregon — Governor Race 2026
author: In the news
content: Accountability Is Coming to Oregon: Oregon Governor Race 2026 By Jim Pasero and Bridget Barton Oregon Transformation Newsletter The Cook Political Report on Oregon’s governors race: “Oregon’s gubernatorial race is one of the rare races moving in the Republican direction despite the national climate. Polling shows the race between Democratic Gov. Tina Kotek and 2026 nominee Christine Drazan is tied with Kotek underwater.” Why? Simple answer: The reason Oregon governors race has moved in this unusual direction, despite Oregon Democrats having won 11 gubernatorial races in a row, is because nobody – nobody, not even the Democrats – wants Tina Kotek to serve a second term. In fact, the thought of a second Kotek term makes most Oregonians queasy. Kotek’s approval rating, according to an October poll by DHM Research, is at a historic record low for Oregon governors at 38%. That’s down from a year ago when Gov. Kotek was polling at 49%, which made her the most unpopular governor in America at the time. OPB’s Dirk VanderHart offers empirical analysis from the DHM poll that reinforces the idea that Oregon Democrats have soured on the governor: “A central question of the Nov. 3 election is whether voters are so upset with Trump’s policies, that they will opt to reelect a Democrat they might disapprove of. In OPB’s poll, more than 20% of those who said they planned to vote for Kotek indicated that they had an unfavorable impression of her.” It’s unprecedented that a sitting governor might be reelected when 20% of those planning to vote for her have an unfavorable opinion. Although, when you’ve won 11 elections in a row a lot of unprecedented stuff happens. It’s also unprecedented that a sitting governor would be running for reelection when her signature accomplishment, the Gas Tax, was repealed in the May primary election (Measure 120) by a vote of 83% to 17%. If we lived in a parliamentary system, which we do not, that vote would have been considered a resounding vote of “No Confidence” and the prime minister or governor would have immediately resigned. But not so if you’re an Oregon Democrat and have not lost an election since 1982. In Kotek’s mind, the governor’s office belongs to her and her public employee unions’ Democrat political party. To her, it’s annoying even to have to ask voters for a second term. Accountability being a terrible pest. The anecdotal evidence from Democrats about Gov. Kotek and her party’s performance matches the empirical. Here’s former Oregon Democratic Party chair Marc Abrams on his Facebook page this month: “Ted Wheeler said he’d cut homelessness in half when there were 4,000 homeless in the city. We passed a billion-dollar tax to work on the problem. The Washington Post reports there are 775,000 homeless in the USA, but 17,000 of them in Multnomah County. In other words, a county with 0.2% of the nation’s population has 2% of the homeless … Clearly we are a spending a ton of money and not getting results.” While the governor is annoyed that she’s in the middle of a messy reelection effort, Oregon Business and Industry (OBI), the state’s chamber of commerce led by Angela Wilhelms, has been keeping score on her performance with what they’ve named the “Oregon Competitiveness Agenda.” Here’s what they found: • “In 2025, Oregon’s economy grew by only 1% , less than half the national rate. Oregon’s economy has grown more slowly than the national average for five straight years. • In 2025, employment in Oregon fell by 0.5% even as employment nationally increased by 0.5%. Employment growth in Oregon has trailed the national average for six consecutive years. • Per capita personal income – a key indicator of prosperity – grew more slowly in Oregon in 2025 than in the nation as a whole. Despite significant gains in prior years, Oregon per capita personal income has been stalled at about 96% of the national average since 2020. • Oregon ranked 35th in the nonpartisan Tax Foundation’s 2026 State Tax Competitiveness Index . Oregon has fallen 28 places since 2019 . • CNBC in 2026 dropped Oregon to 42nd in its annual America’s Best States for Business ranking. Oregon has plummeted 25 places since 2017 .” Meanwhile, despite OBI’s analysis of Oregon’s economic performance, Gov. Kotek gave the state’s business climate a “B” when asked to grade it in a recent gubernatorial debate. Chuckle, chuckle. The governor’s ignorance of our state’s economic woes must have something to do with her belief in the ability of the mostly fictitious Governor’s Prosperity Council she created. The 15-member council never once talked about or suggested that the Gov. Kotek opt in to the newly created Federal Scholarship Tax Credit program. Of course, the state’s economic failure comes with a human price. An Oregonian headline reads, “Gen Z Sees ‘More Opportunity’ Outside Oregon.” The article is based on still another DHM poll – this one revealing that 54% of Oregonians between the ages of 18 and 29 years old are “considering moving in the next five years.” The depressing headlines keep coming: “Oregon adults have the highest rate of mental illness in the U.S. at 31.6%.” (Source: USA Facts.) Why wouldn’t Oregonians be suffering from mental issues? With lack of opportunity often comes depression. On education: Willamette Week’s Oregon Journalism Project provides the recent headlines: “Oregon Students Edge up in Math, Science and English Proficiency but Still Lag Far behind Scores of a Decade Ago” “In Dozens of School Districts, Parents Opted Their Children out of Federally Mandated Tests at Rates that Undermine Accountability” Heard enough. Seen enough. Christine Drazan, on the other hand, has run a solid error-free campaign. The WSJ’s Kimberley Strassel, an Oregon native from Banks, keynoted Cascade Policy Institute’s 35th anniversary dinner this October. In Strassel’s speech, she outlined Oregon’s dysfunction at length and praised Drazan for running a “smart” campaign – keeping the focus on economic issues. It’s true – Drazan’s solid campaign has stayed away from both the personal issues and sensational politics, asking voters to hold Gov. Kotek “accountable” for her weak economic performance. Drazan has also established herself during the campaign as a “not so scary” Republican alternative to Kotek. But will voters hold Kotek accountable on Nov 3? If they don’t, younger Oregonians might be forced to do what the voters may fail to do – hold the governor accountable by moving to another state. Their parents and grandparents will be left to ponder, “How did everything in Oregon go so wrong?” One way or another, accountability is coming to Oregon. title: Why Republican “Red Wave” Did Not Come in Midterms
author: Mandy Jones
content: Most polls leading to 2022 midterm election predicted a big red wave sweeping the House and Senate where Republican candidates would steal seats from Democrats and take control of the House and Senate. Although Republicans are slated to take control of the House, Democrats were able to hold onto the Senate majority even with a run-off coming between Herschel Walker and Raphael Warnock. Republicans were hopeful to win Senate seats in Nevada, Pennsylvania, and Arizona. None of this worked out with Democrats cruising to clear victories except for Nevada which was much closer. Republicans took control of the House but by a thin margin which will make it difficult for the Majority Leader to gather aligned support especially from the more fringe Representatives. So Why Did The “Red Wave” Not Come? The Republican “red wave” did not come for two main reasons: Overturning Rowe vs Wade proved to frighten large amounts of people enough to reject Republican politicians who they fear would further take away women’s right to choose. The sneaky Democratic strategy of spending their funds to promote more alt-right election denier Republican candidates paid off in a big way. By helping these less-electable candidates become the Republican winners heading into midterms, they stacked the deck in Democrat candidates favor because although the country generally prefers the Senate and House to be led by the opposite party of the President, they did not want election deniers and low quality Republicans enough to overcome their desire for checks and balances with a split Government. There you have it. The red wave did not come and the United States goes into the next two years with a Democratic President and Senate. And a Republican controlled House. title: In Replay of 2016, CNN, Pollsters Get Election Very Wrong Again
author: Carla Anderson
content: There are so many polls and media reports of the tiny chance President Trump had to win that both of these industries need a major change. As recently as this morning, some major news outlets had 3% and 10% chances for President Trump to win. Then shortly after ballots began getting counted and Florida was looking more and more like a Trump victory, the odds suddenly switched to 50/50 and shortly after 60/40 toward Trump. Pollsters didn’t learn much from their embarrassing 2016 debacle but they basically followed up with the same tomfoolery in 2020 . They got Florida wrong, many got Texas wrong, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin and Michigan polling numbers are also so far off that it is embarrassing. Nate Silver of FiveThirtyEight looks like he is not taking any accountability or responsibility for how wrong his site has been yet again. Nate Silver showing no self reflection after being so wrong in 2016 and now 2020. In a predictable move to take attention away from President Trump’s strong, unexpected performance in several states tonight they make this the headline on their home page – If the President does in fact go on to win the election tomorrow or in the coming days, we all know CNN will find anything and everything to sensationalize and bash the President about instead of reflecting on what they got wrong and how they continue to let their left ideology get in the way of fair and balanced reporting. We also know that CNN and MSNBC need President Trump to continue their higher viewership count, which results in more ad revenue dollars. If Joe Biden wins the election, viewership will drop and potentially force CNN and MSNBC into large cuts. Now you’re starting to understand the double whammy that CNN pulls – they sensationalize their left leaning Democratic support and bashing of Trump because it incites emotional responses from their viewers thereby sucking them in for longer periods. And then they have to come up with as angering and fearmongering headlines as possible because that’s what allows them to retain their visitors which keeps ad revenue higher. title: 2020 Election is Here
author: Carla Anderson
content: Four years ago , President Donald Trump pulled off the single biggest upset in politics, sports, anywhere. The morning of this day four years ago, all pundits and the world were expecting a convincing win by Hillary Clinton. As the day went on, tiny hints of a lack of Clinton domination were starting to appear but even by 3pm PST when the first exit polls from the east coast were sprinkling in, the consensus was still a strong victory for Hillary. From there with each passing our, watching CNN and FoxNews was a surreal experience. On CNN, the anchors were in visible disbelief at the strength of the Trump vote. Soon after the election, CNN lost all objectivity in their reporting but on this day four years ago they still pretended to be objective. The look on every CNN anchor was one of shock, disbelief and near tears at the inevitability of Trump’s win becoming more clear. Who knows what will happen tonight in the 2020 election of Joe Biden vs President Trump but we will know a lot more in 12 hours, even if we do not yet know the winner. title: Debt Settlement – How it Really Works, Told by an Insider (Beware)
author: Brandon Jones
content: Exclusive: This is an article from a real insider who spent two years working at a debt settlement firm in a major city; taking thousands of calls and really learning the ins-and-outs of how debt settlement works. He contacted us to write his story, giving us details, truths and best practices for the industry that is supposedly helping real people get out of debt. Read it and decide for yourself if they are helping or preying on people. The Dark Secrets of Debt Settlement: To be blunt – Debt Settlement firms prey on your stupidity, laziness and fears.  Take it from me, an ex-insider who did his fair share. In contrast to the other representatives at my firm, I presented other paths to venture down if the customer was uninterested in our service.  Very few ever do.  I was eventually fired because I did not meet the quota.  I’m not angry for being fired.  I don’t think I was helping people.  I was helping my company be a middleman who takes advantage of people struggling to make it.  I’m writing this to inform the customer of the true merits of Debt Settlement. The Debt Settlement Firms There are about 10-15 prominent debt settlement firms in the U.S.  Just to let you know, they are all controlled by a few players.  So if you don’t go with one company and you go with the other, more than likely you are still working with the same owner.  The only difference is the customer representative or salesman that you are working with. You may also notice that new companies pop up but have the same background story.  The reason being that an old company closed down because they had a bad reputation and just created a new entity to use.  Sound like Boiler Room to you? The Process: Debt settlement firms will discuss in general terms what debt settlement is, how it differentiates from credit counseling, a rough estimate of how much they can save you on a monthly basis and on your total principal amount (usually a whopping 50%). They will talk about the pros of the program, which all sounds good and dandy, making you feel good that there is something out there to help you out. The firm will then pry information from you to use as leverage.  This is called the “ qualification process “. Questions include: How much debt do you have? How long have you had this debt? Which credit cards? Are you just making the minimum payments (of interest) or are you paying off the principal? Have you noticed that your interest rates have been going up?” Then they tell you things like: “These credit card companies are trying to take advantage of your situation.  You are a victim to these corporate giants.”  You might hear, “In order to get a better understanding of your financial situation, what is your annual income, monthly expenses?” After getting this information from you, they will state that you are the perfect candidate for the program.  99.9% of the customers are “perfect” for the program.  “You sound like you are eager to take control of your finances and want to have a new beginning.” But what they will do is pull it away from you.  Classic Bait and Switch tactic. Both you and the firm knows that you are a good candidate for the program, but the firm will stress that this program is for people who really want to help themselves.  And people who are committed, a trust that you have with each other.  They will ask to pull your credit to get a better understanding of your finances.  Also, they will review it with you free of charge in order to figure out if they can really help you.  Once reviewed, they will say that they need to take your file to the “underwriters” to see if you are approved. The truth is – there aren’t any underwriters.  They will call you back in 30 minutes while you squirm and hope that you are approved..  To create a sense of urgency, they will state that they had to make an exception for you and create a time limit of 48 hours for you to sign up, otherwise you cannot apply for another 30 days.  Basically leading/urging you to sign the forms.  Don’t worry though, they will go over the entire 20 page document with you.  (Note: This is me being sarcastic.) The Game Plan Once in the program, you stop paying the credit cards that you have agreed upon.  As a result, you cannot use those credit cards to buy anything.  You will make a payment to a third party Bank that is the custodian of your savings account.  This prevents any kind of conflict of interest between the Debt Settlement firm and the bank.  Within the first several monthly payments, half of those payments go to the Debt Settlement firm as fees and the other half is accumulated into  your savings account. Firms differ in the way they collect the initial fees.  Some may even collect 100% of the first couple of months as fees so you are not saving any money until three months down the road.  Please note that Debt Settlement firms don’t start negotiating with a Credit Company until you have approximately 50% of the debt load of your smallest credit card principal.  So if you have three credit cards: 1 st is for $2,000, 2 ne for $5,000, and the 3 rd for $8,000, in most cases they will not start negotiating on the first credit card until you have $1,000 accumulated in your savings account.  However, since the Debt Settlement firm deals with hundreds to thousands of clients, they can group some clients together who have X credit card together.  As an individual you have $8,000 of debt but with a combination with other clients there is a total of $150,000.  As a result the Debt Settlement firm has more leverage to negotiate with the bank and will get a better deal on reducing the debt. In this example, if they were negotiating for you alone, they could drop it down to $3,500 (a savings of 56.25%).  But for the combination of clients, they can negotiate it down to $40,500 (a savings of  73.00%).  Sounds good to you, but remember, they take a % of the savings at the end of the program.  In a way they have an interest in saving you money, because the larger the savings, the more money the firm makes.  But you can do it yourself, and possibly get the same results of a Debt Settlement firm.  Saving you even more money that usually the Debt Settlement firm gets paid on. Your Representative aka The Professional Salesman: The most important thing to know about Debt Settlement firms is that they’ll do whatever it takes to close a deal.  The motto “ABC – Always Be Closing”.  The representatives of these firms are professional salesmen (usually ex-mortgage bankers who helped create the housing bubble). Consequently: You are a number to them They have to meet a quota in order to maintain their job (at least 25 deals/month) The monthly payment plan a representative puts you on directly affects the money in the representative’s pocket.  The firm has a fee structure for the representatives.  For example, if a representative brings in 22-25 deals, then he/she takes home 25% of client’s first month’s payment.  30 deals brings in 30%, so on and so forth.  Max payment is 40-42%.  Minimum payment to a representative is approximately $2,500. I have even heard of a female representative flirt with a client by adding him to a myspace page in order to close the deal.  Dirty. Urgency strategies that they utilize: only a limited number of people can sign up a month, therefore sign up today. they make an “exception” for you to make you feel important, but then put a time limit of “This is only good for the next 48 hours.” infuse fear that you could lose everything, the credit card companies are going to constantly harass you or even sue you, or the fear that you won’t be able to fund your children’s college, etc. convince you that the program empowers you by creating your own financial freedom use the total amount that you have paid the credit card company to overwhelm you with how these corporate giants are taking advantage of you.  The calculation is as follows:  the principal amount on your credit card, for x amount of years at a y interest rate, in reality you paid off z amount if you paid  the minimum payments that covered the interest.  Example is if you had $10,000 of unsecured debt, that you’ve had for 5 years, at an interest rate of 15%, then in reality you have paid $7,500 of interest only.  You have  really paid off 75% of your debt but it’s only interest.  So why don’t do a debt settlement plan and attack the principal only. the firm states that with this program, you will be debt free in less than 36 months.  The reason being is that they sometimes state federal law requires a person who enrolls in a Debt Settlement program to settle his/her debt  within 36 months.  This is BS.    In reality, the Firm and banks know that the longer a customer prolongs paying off  debt, the less likely he/she will be able to complete the program.  Also, credit card companies and banks want their money sooner rather than later.  Once you enter a program, it’s a “promise” to the bank that you will pay them in a certain amount of time.  If by chance you renege during the program (which you can, but not recommended), you will be penalized by the banks as they will charge you backed up interest and fees that you should have originally been paying them. Talk about making a deposit in a third party bank. Pros of working with a Debt Settlement Firm: 1)      You don’t deal with the credit card companies directly.  Basically you are paying a Debt Settlement firm to take care of it for you.  Usually they charge 2.5% (or whatever they charge these days) upfront that will be taken out of your first several months payment and then when you finish the program they take another haircut of approximately 30% (again whatever they charge these days) of your savings.  So for instance if you had $10,000 of debt, they negotiate it down to $4,000, there is a savings of $6,000 or 60%.  But then the firm takes a cut of 30% of your savings, so they will take another $1,800 (which is already included in our payment schedule so it’s not anything out-of-pocket).  In reality you save $4,200 or 42%. 2)      You are debt free within 36 months. 3)      You have empowered yourself and created your financial freedom – that’s what they like you to think. Cons of working with a Debt Settlement Firm: 1)      More than likely your credit score will be negatively affected.  For instance if you have a 700 FICA score, it will drop into the high 500s.  If you already have a 500 credit score, then it really won’t change.  Reason being is that when you sign up for a program, you will stop paying the credit cards on the balances.  As a result, to the banks, you have defaulted on your unsecured debt.  They report this to the credit bureaus and there will be statement on it that you have defaulted with X Company. 2)      The customer service is sub par.  Once you have signed up, the representative throws you into “the dog pound” with all the other clients.  There will be another client service representative that will be corresponding with you afterwards.  Unfortunately, these companies are understaffed and do not get back with you in a timely manner.  The industry is changing and some companies have been touting that if you call, the client service rep has x amount of hours to call you back or they are disciplined/fired.  Do you think this really happens if they are already understaffed? 3)      You cannot participate in a program if you have some government jobs.  For instance if you have like a Top Secret clearance or have access to classified information, then this may be conflicting with your job agreement.  Also, once your credit score drops and you are applying for a job, employers frown upon you being financially irresponsible. 4)      The government will tax the savings that you have accumulated throughout the DS process. 5)      There is still the possibility of the Credit Card company suing you.  I have heard horror stories.  It’s a small percentage, but has become more widely adopted. 6)      The Better Business Bureau (who really doesn’t do anything) have negative ratings about Debt Settlement Firms.  The rumors are that the BBB was created by the giants that are collecting money from you, but who knows. The reality of it all: You have several different options that are pretty much similar. 1)      Debt Settlement.  Again DS firms negotiate on your behalf to reduce your total unsecured debt by approximately 50%.  You are only paying on the principal amount of your debt.  NOT paying any interest. 2)      Consumer Credit Counseling.  They help you lump your credit card payments into one (just like Debt Settlement), but reduce your interest rates.  For instance, CCC will lower your interest rates from 20% to 13% on a $10,000 debt.  You are paying both the principal amount of $10,000 AND interest.  There are instances where CCC can reduce your debt load.  In these instances your credit score will be negatively affected. 3)      Declare Bankruptcy.  If you can’t pay your bills, can’t live off the money you currently make/have, then you should declare bankruptcy.  There are two types for individuals.  Most people file Chapter 7: basic liquidation for individuals.  This is also known as straight bankruptcy; it is the simplest and quickest form of bankruptcy available.  This clears all of your debt, but a record of this stays on the individual’s credit report for up to 10 years.  If you do not qualify for this, you will be subject to Chapter 13: rehabilitation with a payment plan for individuals with a regular source of income.  Basically if you are above the income limits stipulated, then you are required by the courts to develop a plan to repay all of your debts with a 3-5 year time frame. This record stays on the individual’s credit report for up to 10 years.  It is important to note that when applying to jobs, employers usually ask if you have ever declared bankruptcy and usually check your credit report.  So depending on your situation, you really have to think about this option. 4)      DO IT YOURSELF.  This is by far the best choice, but requires YOU to change and become financially responsible.  Why pay a Middle Man when you can do it yourself.  I know, I know, you are going to say “It’s too much work”, which really means you are just lazy.  YOU are the one that overextended your credit. NOT ME! The best way to combat your unsecured debt is to first start saving $ in another bank account that is dedicated to pay off your debt.  In the meantime, call your credit card company and ask what they can do to help you.  More than likely, if you have been paying the minimum payments on your bills on time, they will tell you they can’t help you.  Why would they when you are constantly making the minimum payments, and thus more money in the bank’s pocket (interest upon interest upon interest).  In reality, you will have to stop paying the credit card bills for a couple of months, just like at a DS (Note that this will negatively affect your credit score).  Note, don’t stop paying all your credit cards at the same time because once you stop paying your bill, that credit card company will cut you off from using that credit card.  Other CCs will follow.  But this is a good thing, because credit cards are what got you into trouble in the first place).  I suggest you attack the credit card with the lowest principal, so that you can get that out of your way and feel like you accomplished something as it will be paid off sooner. Just like a TO DO LIST.  Once you stop paying your bills, the CC companies realize you have some kind of “hardship”, that you cannot afford to pay your bills.  After a couple of months of not paying your bills, call the CC company and let them know that you cannot pay the bill.  Threaten that you will declare bankruptcy (Then they will think you are serious that you can’t pay your bills, when you declare BK, a bank gets $0).  They will run around like chickens with their heads cut off.  Consequently, ask them to reduce your debt load.  If you owe $10,000 mention to them that you can come up with $2k in a month (don’t tell them that you have money saved).  They will counter your offer with $7,500.  This is the negotiating process, you have to low ball them at first.  In the back of your mind, since you have been saving over the past couple of months you know you have $5,000 saved.  When you think an amount is fair (30-50% is fair), then agree with the CC company that you will pay them x amount within y months.  GET THE AGREEMENT IN WRITING and make sure that you have them remove the default statement from your credit report.  Tell them to replace it with PAID IN FULL or something to that extent.  After about a year of  all your credit cards being paid off, your credit score will start to rebound and be back to where it used to be. title: Donald Trump Wins Presidential Election
author: admin
content: In  a truly shocking result yesterday, America has voted Donald Trump as the next President by a large margin. The overwhelming majority of polls predicted a clear Clinton victory but as it turned out, Trump dominated last night. It looks like Trump will finish with close to 310 electoral college votes. We cannot reiterate enough how large of a victory this is given how much people thought Trump had no chance to win. The only polls that accurately predicted a Trump victory were the USC / LA Times Poll and Investors Business Daily. The LA Times / USC poll was run by USC economist and public opinion expert, Arie Kapteyn. He deserves credit for correctly predicting public sentiment. America Spoke Loud and Clear Last night’s result tells us that the pain American’s feel is very real. The dissatisfaction with the current government, direction of the country and Congress runs very deep. Congress is viewed as a political machine that acts as a cog in politics and gets nothing done. During the Obama administration this was largely true. Trump’s rhetoric of DRAIN THE SWAMP resonated with the people. Those who voted for Trump were tired of the government getting bigger and bigger; and TELLING Americans what they can and cannot do. Obamacare is one example but there are many more. People have long felt that the Government is not good at efficiently allocating our hard earned tax dollars. We have been moving toward a more socialist society with more and more feelings of entitlement and handouts. The people said NO MORE to this direction last night. It was LOUD and CLEAR. The Rust Belt States Trump’s path to victory came through the important states of Michigan, Wisconsin, Ohio, and Florida. Previously, Barack Obama won these states easily and Clinton was projected to easily take them. She did not spend much time in the first three states and did not make one visit to Wisconsin. It could be said she took that state for granted. Trump predicted early and often that he would get the votes of the Rust Belt as well as Florida but few believed him. In the end, Donald Trump pulled off the greatest election feat in modern times and we must give him credit for running a tireless, dedicated and long campaign. title: Adelaide Plans on Becoming First Carbon Neutral City
author: Mandy Jones
content: The time has come to focus on alternative and renewable sources of energy and Adelaide in Australia is trying to lead the way. Solar energy is one of the most viable and cost effective renewable source of energy for residential and commercial buildings. Because of this, the Australian government is now offering generous solar grants to promote the use of solar energy in businesses and households. The solar grant scheme provides landlords up to: $5000 for apartment solar upgrades $5000 for installing solar panels $5000 for installing energy storage $1000 for switching to LED downlights $1000 for a hot water system powered by solar power $500 for each electric car charging station The solar grant totals $150,000 to Australian businesses equipped with solar energy panels and storage. With the Labour Government announcing a $1.1 million tender to install battery storage in several government buildings and businesses, South Australia has become the leading state in battery storage using solar energy. The storage batteries will store solar power during the day that could be used at night. This initiative has been started in the city of Adelaide, which became the first in the nation to offer financial incentives to businesses and households to install battery storage systems. If the plan is successful we can count on it’s expansion to other cities. The objective of this grant scheme is to encourage the community to invest in solar energy storage, in order to enhance energy efficiency. The initiative will augment the demand for renewable energy and encourage the growth of green industries. It also promotes cleaner modes of transport by adding $500 per electric automobile charging station. Battery storage of renewable energy is growing at a fast pace all across the world, and according to Australian Energy Minister Tom Koutsantonis, this solar grant will help in making Adelaide the world’s first carbon neutral city. title: 60 Minutes Correspondent Bob Simon Dies in Car Accident
author: Brandon Bennett
content: In sad news just in, long-time “60 Minutes” correspondent Bob Simon, on the popular CBS show has passed away tonight at the age of 73. Bob Simon first joined CBS News in 1967 and has continued working as a reporter for the network for the next 48 years. Simon’s career covered many war zones including Vietnam, Ireland, Portugal, the Persian Gulf, Cyprus, Grenada, Haiti and Somalia. Simon was well respected by his colleagues and appeared frequently on the Sunday night show “60 Minutes”. The details of the crash are still sparse but early reports state that Simon was riding in a Lincoln Town Car that collided with a Mercedes and then lost control. This occurred at 7pm EST and according to the driver of the Mercedes, the Lincoln Town Car driver appeared to drive erratically. Speculation is that the driver may have suffered a heart attack causing him to have lost control. Story developing. title: Understanding Affordable Healthcare in 2013
author: Brandon Bennett
content: It is a widely held notion that healthcare is not cheap but it is a necessity. The last thing you would want to deal with is large hospital bills because you do not have any health insurance. If you have been searching for affordable healthcare but have been unable to find a plan that meets your needs, here are a few tips you can consider to help you find the perfect healthcare plan. Now here are some general tips that may apply to you. Use your Parent’s Plan Many people do not realize they can still qualify to be a part of their parent’s healthcare plan even if they are an adult. As long as you are under the age of 26, you can get insured under your parent’s plan. This is even true if you are married, not living with your parents and not financially dependent on them. While this is a temporary solution until you are over the age of 26, receiving coverage as a part of your parent’s health care plan is a great way to find affordable short term healthcare. Understand the Different Plans If you are unable to qualify for discount healthcare under your parent’s plan, you will need to understand the different plans that are available to truly determine which type of plan you need. Knowing the difference between an HMO and PPO can help save you money as you will be able to select the plan that best fits your health care needs and is the cheapest option. Emergency coverage is another option to consider when you are working with a small budget. If you are a relatively healthy person who is simply looking for coverage in case of a serious medical emergency, then emergency coverage may be the perfect healthcare plan for you. This type of plan will cover your emergency room visits but not allow for routine wellness checkups. Because these plans do not offer comprehensive coverage, they are often much more affordable than other healthcare plans. Another healthcare plan you will need to research when determining the type of coverage you should purchase is a high deductible, HSA-compatible health plan. This type of plan often offers lower monthly payments because a high deductible, often thousands of dollars, needs to be met before the insurance coverage kicks in. Once your deductible is met, your health insurance plan will start to cover your medical expenses. Taking advantage of an HSA account to save pre-tax dollars is a good way to help cover those medical expenses you will need to pay out of pocket before your insurance starts to cover some of your medical costs. Always Compare Rates Once you determine the best type of healthcare plan for your current situation, you will need to shop around and compare rates. Different insurance companies will offer different rates so it is important that you do not purchase the first healthcare plan you come across. Thoroughly researching the different amounts and levels of coverage offered by specific healthcare providers will help you discover the cheapest plan possible that will meet all of your healthcare needs. Finding affordable healthcare is often not an easy task. Knowing how to go about your research will help you discover the right healthcare plan to meet your needs. As long as you understand all of the different types of policies and compare the rates across several insurance companies, you should be able to find an affordable healthcare solution.
