title: Have You Ever Moved Across the World With Your Handbags?
author: Kaitlin Serio
content: This time last year, I was likely sitting at my bistro table, overlooking Église Saint-Sulpice in Paris’ 6ème, during my two-month stint to investigate what it would actually be like to live in Paris. It’s safe to say it was better than I could have ever imagined, and one year later, I sit at my high-top table in New York, surrounded by a sea of boxes, ready to embark on one of the greatest journeys of my life. After a months-long process of visa applications, red tape, and French bureaucracy, I’m excited to share that yes, I am moving to Paris! In 10 days, no less! Moving to Paris: What About My Handbags? The all have to come with me! I imagined making this exciting announcement with a bag review shot around the city, or something much less practical, but truthfully, I can’t wait to share this news because I need your help—and quickly! I am currently (very, very slowly) looking for a furnished rental to settle into for the year while I see how things pan out, which thankfully means packing only my wardrobe and some decor. Still, with plans to potentially stay in the city long-term, that means bringing the entirety of my wardrobe, including somewhere around 20 designer handbags. While I will be packing three suitcases, I won’t be able to fit all of my bags in them, which means I’ll have to ship some or use a moving service of some kind, like Send My Bag or My Baggage. Have any of you moved internationally with your bags (and other precious items)? Let’s talk!

title: Eight Bags From Paris Fashion Week Spring 2027 That I Can’t Stop Thinking About
author: Kaitlin Serio
content: Fashion month may be over, but I’m not quite ready to move on from Paris. After eight days in my home-away-from-home city, I’m still thinking about the collections, the little moments in between appointments, and, of course, the bags. Over the years, our fashion week coverage has grown to include more than just what we see on the runway. We also get a closer look at the collections through resees, which typically take place a day or two after a show. These appointments give editors and other guests the chance to revisit the collection up close, take in the details, and get a better feel for the bags beyond their runway debut. Resees also offer a broader look at the collection as a whole, including pieces and details that may not have been fully visible on the runway. This season, I was back in Paris for a week packed with shows and appointments, with the occasional pastry from Copain, far too little sleep, and plenty of late nights writing back in my hotel room. If you’ve been following along on Instagram , you’ve likely caught glimpses of it all, from the shows themselves to the street style outside and those much-anticipated closer looks at the collections. I saw a lot of bags this season, and while we’ll be breaking down the biggest handbag trends from Spring 2027 soon, today’s roundup is a little more fun! These are eight of the bags that caught my eye, stuck with me long after I left the city, and have me already excited for spring. Let’s get into it! Dior We kicked off the week with Dior , which offered a mix of new designs and familiar favorites. There were plenty of nods to classic Dior House codes, including Cannage detailing on the Dior Toujours, which returned in a beautiful lilac suede, alongside an edgy new asymmetrical messenger complete with D-I-O-R charms. Loewe This insane sunny-yellow embossed croc bag from the Loewe runway is part clutch, part structured flap bag. Photos don’t even do it justice! Celine Wow was the consensus among everyone who attended the Celine resee. Held in a beautiful venue brimming with quintessential Parisian charm, the presentation made it easy to appreciate the collection up close. The bags arguably stole the show, especially the new, smooshy Celine Triomphe. Simple but so chic, it feels like the epitome of Michael Rider’s vision for Celine . But the bag that first stopped me in my tracks was the Celine Frame Vanity. It was an immediate favorite when Rider introduced it in his debut collection for the House, and now it’s back in leopard. The Vanity is quickly becoming one of Rider’s signature designs, with this season bringing a fresh range of iterations. Chanel Red and burgundy are two of my favorite colors that can double as neutrals, and the two together? No notes. As for the beaded feather bag? Bags should be fun! This one is so fun. Valentino I’m a sucker for a good purple bag—what can I say? Plus, the gathered silk layering on this runway version of the Valentino DeVain feels incredibly luxe.

title: How Do You Know When You’ve Found the One?
author: Kaitlin Serio
content: A new handbag is a big investment. Many of us only make one big bag purchase a year, or even every two years, so when we finally commit, we want to be sure. Plus, with the ever-changing luxury landscape and never-ending price increases, making the wrong choice can be a costly regret—one many of us have, unfortunately, experienced. Below, we’re sharing three ways to know you’ve found the one . You Can’t Stop Thinking About It Have you ever “visited” the bag you want in-store, only to walk out empty-handed and immediately feel sad? I have! And while I’ve occasionally made impulsive purchases, it’s just not in my nature to see something for the first time and buy it right then and there. Even when I’ve found myself completely smitten, I’ve walked away because, as I mentioned, regretting a big purchase truly stinks. But when you’ve been thinking about a bag for months, dreaming about making it yours, stopping by the store just to see it, looking at it online more times than you can count, and texting all your friends to tell them about it, that’s a pretty good sign you’ve found your next bag. You Plan Outfits to Wear It With For me, this is the telltale sign that I’m making a good choice when purchasing just about anything! It helps me determine whether a bag—or any item, for that matter—is truly my style. If I can’t picture it with pieces I already own, chances are it’s not meant for me. While I can certainly appreciate the beauty of most bags (duh, it’s why I do what I do!), that doesn’t mean every beautiful bag is right for my wardrobe. If I can’t see myself wearing it with what I already have, chances are it’s not going to work out in the long run. The Thought Of It Gives You Butterflies This might be the most obvious sign of all: if it doesn’t make your heart skip a beat, then it probably just isn’t meant to be. Sure, there are plenty of bags I like and wouldn’t mind having in my closet. But then there are those super-special pieces that would make me feel like the luckiest girl in the world to own. That’s how you should feel about your next big bag purchase, too!

title: Think Leopard Is Leaving Us? Think Again—and We’ve Got a Fresh Crop of Carries to Prove It
author: Kaitlin Serio
content: Leopard print has a way of making a comeback without ever really going away. After the mob wife aesthetic brought the pattern back into the spotlight in early 2024, leopard quickly proved it was more than a passing TikTok obsession. What began as a maximalist fashion moment has since found a lasting place in our wardrobes—and this fall, it’s making a compelling case for staying put. Of course, leopard is hardly new territory. The print has cycled through decades of fashion, shifting from a bold statement to a closet staple and back again. But its current iteration feels different. Designers are finding fresh ways to work it into their collections, balancing its naturally wild appeal with a more polished, modern sensibility. The result? A print that feels just as at home with relaxed denim and everyday essentials as it does with tailored separates and evening looks. Leopard Isn’t Going Anywhere, and Fall 2026 Is Proof That evolution is especially exciting when it comes to handbags. From heritage fashion houses to contemporary favorites, designers continue to revisit leopard through new silhouettes, textures, and finishes. Houses like Chanel and Saint Laurent are helping keep the print in the conversation, proving that leopard can feel sophisticated, versatile, and undeniably current. No longer reserved for the boldest dresser, it has become an easy way to give even the simplest look a little more personality. And that’s precisely why we’re not ready to say goodbye. Leopard has the rare ability to act as both a neutral and a statement, adding texture and character without demanding an entirely new wardrobe. Whether you prefer a subtle touch or a bag that does all the talking, there’s a version that feels right for you. For Fall 2026, the question isn’t whether leopard is still in style—it’s which leopard bag deserves a spot in your rotation. We’ve rounded up a fresh crop of carries that make a convincing case for keeping this classic print in the mix, season after season. title: Prada Celebrates Its Most Iconic Re-Nylon Bag Ever With a New Installation
author: Kaitlin Serio
content: A luxury house is distinguished by far more than its name or instantly recognizable logo. Its identity is shaped by a rich heritage, defining design codes, signature aesthetics, and enduring silhouettes. For Prada, few elements embody this identity quite like Re-Nylon. Beyond the House’s unmistakable triangular logo, Re-Nylon has become one of Prada’s most enduring signatures, featured across its bags and accessories for over four decades. Mention Prada, and the image of a sleek black Re-Nylon bag with a sporty, utilitarian edge and the iconic triangle emblem is likely to spring to mind—a testament to just how deeply the material is woven into the brand’s identity. Prada Re-Nylon: Where Heritage Meets Modernity Among Prada’s most celebrated designs, the Re-Nylon backpack holds a particularly special place, standing as a timeless icon in the world of luxury handbags. This season, Prada celebrates the universal appeal of its Re-Nylon backpacks with a new installation at its New York flagship on Broadway. Commemorating the significance of the Prada Re-Nylon backpack and emphasizing its fashion-meets-function appeal, the installation feels like the intersection of two worlds: art and fashion. Inside Prada’s Celebration of the Iconic Re-Nylon Backpack The installation features a range of Prada Re-Nylon backpacks displayed atop classic Prada Pergamena trunks, bringing together different elements of the House’s history in a contemporary design space. The display emphasizes that while fashion and the world around it are ever-changing, the Prada Re-Nylon backpack continues to evolve, bridging the gap between historic tradition and modern innovation. Prada Re-Nylon remains at the epicenter of the gallery-like display, underscoring its importance to the House, while leather, corduroy, and quilted variations are also on view. The new installation is available to view through November 15 and is fully shoppable, with a curated online capsule available for those who are not in New York or planning a visit.

title: Gucci’s Revamped Marmont Bag Deserves Your Attention
author: Kaitlin Serio
content: The Gucci Marmont celebrates its 10th birthday this year, first introduced in 2016 by then-creative director Alessandro Michele. The Marmont, in all of its padded, GG glory, marked a pivotal moment, not only for Gucci but for handbags as a whole. The Marmont, which was an instant hit, defined a specific period of time in fashion: the late 2010s, a life before COVID completely changed the world and the luxury landscape. The Gucci Marmont Enters a New Era Still, despite changing times, new creative directors, and shifting aesthetics for the House of Gucci, the Marmont has remained one of the House’s best sellers—and most beloved bags. In 2026, a decade after the Marmont first burst onto the scene and into our collective consciousness, we’re falling back in love with the Marmont. Under Demna’s creative eye, the Gucci Jetset Marmont gets a softer, more relaxed feel and takes the edge off the Marmont we’ve always known and loved, modernizing it without straying from the iconic details that have always defined the bag. These include the archival Double G, which originated from a 1970s emblem that pays homage to Guccio Gucci, the House’s founder. Inside Gucci’s Beauty and the Bag Campaign Jetset GG Marmont Medium Shoulder Bag , $3,100 What’s most exciting about the new Jetset Marmont is not only its edgy, contemporary feel but also the way it combines two of Gucci’s most important motifs, joined by the iconic Gucci Web. This season, Gucci continues to celebrate its newest Marmont with a new chapter of its Beauty and the Bag campaign, this time starring Italian model Vittoria Ceretti. The idea behind the viral campaign is that beauty and the bag are one, shifting the focus to the significance that a handbag can have. Shop the Gucci Jetset Collection now via Gucci .

title: A$AP Rocky Just Wore the Most Talked-About Bag of Chanel Spring 2027
author: Kaitlin Serio
content: It’s not even been a month since Chanel presented Matthieu Blazy’s second Spring ready-to-wear collection in Paris, but that doesn’t mean that everything we saw isn’t immediately available to wear. That is, of course, as long as you’re a celebrity with deep ties to the House. Us mere mortals will have to wait months for even a chance to get our hands on what A$AP Rocky carried to the sixth annual Academy Museum Gala on Saturday. In the words of his beau, Rihanna, A$AP showed up in a black tuxedo with satin lapels adorned with jeweled buttons and a Phresh Out the Runway Cloud Clutch from Chanel Spring 2027 . Swoon. Chanel in the Clouds The Grammy-nominated rapper from New York has had a longstanding relationship with Matthieu Blazy , dating back to the designer’s days at Bottega Veneta, so, of course, it’s not surprising that he is now one of Chanel’s most loyal ambassadors. Not to mention, if ever there were a handbag closet we’d like to raid, it would be the joint closet of A$AP Rocky and Rihanna, who’ve both been spotted carrying some of the most-wanted bags of the 2020s, from Chanel and Dior to Louis Vuitton, Bottega Veneta, and more. Le sigh. View this post on Instagram

title: A ’90s Fendi Icon Returns
author: Kaitlin Serio
content: Real OG Fendi fans know that the Baguette is not the only Fendi bag named after a French baked good. While the Baguette remains, arguably, one of the most beloved and widely recognized bags in the Fendi universe, the Croissant was once just as popular, and this season, it is back from the archives, given new life under Maria Grazia Chiuri’s creative reign. The Fendi Croissant Bag: A Y2K Icon Returns The Fendi Croissant bag first debuted on the runway for the Fall 1999 season, two years after the Baguette’s debut. The bag, which takes its name from the French pastry, mirrors a croissant with its soft, slouchy construction and crescent-like silhouette. At the time, the Croissant bag was just as coveted as the Baguette, garnering waitlists by the early 2000s. Like its boulangerie-inspired sister, the Croissant bag arrived in a myriad of sizes and variations. Think suede, iconic Fendi Zucca, animal print, neoprene, and beaded iterations. If you could dream it, there was a Croissant bag for it. Now, the Croissant returns to the Fendi lineup for Cruise 2027, celebrating the youthful ease and multifaceted appeal of Maria Grazia Chiuri’s Fendi. This revival was imagined as an extension of Chiuri’s revival of the Baguette® 26424 , building upon Fendi’s signature design codes and refreshing them with a modern feel. Fendi Croissant Bag , $1,900 Fendi Croissant Bag , $2,100 Meet the New Fendi Croissant Bags for 2026 Designed as the ideal day-to-night accessory, the 2026 iteration of the fan-favorite mini features an adjustable strap for shorter or longer wear, adding a touch of functionality to Fendi’s distinct stylistic codes. Available for pre-order starting today, October 16th, 2026, the new Fendi Croissant arrives in a range of collectible iterations, ranging from on-trend animal print and fringe to metallic cracked leather, all-over paillettes, and more. Prices start at $1,990. Discover more and pre-order yours now via Fendi . Fendi Croissant Bag , $2,100 Fendi Croissant Bag , $3,450

title: Fall is Officially Here and Here Are 12 More Things I Can’t Stop Thinking About
author: Kaitlin Serio
content: Fall is officially here, and if you read my last fall wish list, you already know that my shopping radar has been working overtime. Back in August, I shared ten things I couldn’t stop thinking about, and somehow, a couple of months later, my list has only gotten longer. There’s just something about fall that makes me want to rethink my wardrobe. Maybe it’s the layers, the coats, the boots, or the fact that a few really good pieces can completely change how you wear the things you already own. I love the idea of finding those items that feel special but still work seamlessly into my everyday wardrobe, whether that’s a great jacket, the perfect bag, or a pair of shoes that makes even the simplest outfit feel more put together. And now that fall collections are fully landing, I’m officially in that mindset. I’m less interested in buying things just for the sake of buying them and more drawn to pieces that feel worth making room for: the ones with personality, the ones I’ll reach for on repeat, and the ones that make getting dressed a little more exciting. Of course, that doesn’t mean my wish list has gotten any shorter. If anything, the opposite has happened. Just when I think I’ve narrowed things down, something new catches my eye, and suddenly I’m back to mentally rearranging my wardrobe around a few more things I absolutely do not need but would very much like to own. So, consider this part two of my fall shopping obsession. Here are 12 more things I can’t stop thinking about right now. And if I had to pick just one to buy first? Well, I’m not sure I’m any closer to making that decision than I was in August. title: That time I flunked out of college
author: By Nicholas Chen, Chief Copy Editor
content: Any high schooler who lived through March 2020 can fill in the details: unenthused classwork, questionable get-togethers, general isolation. But I would characterize finishing my secondary education as a mental health reckoning. Some telehealth therapy and overwhelming parental expectations later, I still decided college was my next step. I was at the University of Missouri-Columbia for three semesters, from August 2020 to December 2021. I couldn’t see a future for myself or a reason why I was there. I lost motivation, not just for schoolwork, but for life. During my first semester, I continued the teletherapy sessions and I’d focus more on how to “fix” myself, not absorbing much on asking for help. Schoolwork became secondary, something I considered unimportant compared to a campus newspaper or food pantry where people could count on me. That wasn’t always manifested as selflessness. One night I played “Counter-Strike: Global Offensive” till a taunting robin song fluttered through the open window. Hard to call that selfless dedication, and I never even made it past the Gold Nova rank. That radical selflessness got me an academic probation letter. I wrote an appeal, and my therapist wrote a letter; I managed to stay in my program another semester. My final semester in mid-Missouri was my lowest point. I had an iron foundation of friends and educators but was too ashamed to chirp a note about it. The familiar pattern of a strong start followed by a total collapse had a bit of variety: I learned the joy of cooking with friends and rotted in my first apartment. The parental freakout over winter break and a quiet trip back to empty out my room was new. Back home, I’d take classes at the College of Dupage with varying success: a lot of one step forward, two steps back. The failures became my self-concept. My therapist suggested group therapy a few months after I returned home. I figured I didn’t have many options, but I responded well. Hearing relatable struggles helped me understand something I hadn’t absorbed from my therapist for about two years: I deserved some of the grace and understanding I would offer a friend. The routine of listening and validating, this time in a group, gradually changed how I talked to myself. There was no more retrospective judgement and anger, less regret and embarrassment. Four months after flunking out of Mizzou, I could start thinking about how I could have looked after myself. Now, almost five years later, where I once saw failure and loathing, I see compassion and care. I feel sad for that version of myself that couldn’t ask for help. Even after therapy, I still struggle to treat myself with kindness, but I’m learning to listen to myself and answer “how are you?” honestly. Therapy is an option among many, but compassion is the goal. People I’ve met in class and at work have taught me that everyone really is “on their own time.” I used to be tired and embarrassed of explaining why I ran home from college with my tail between my legs. I still see peers thriving and friends moving out, and I can’t help but swat at the gnats of jealousy. More annoying to admit, however, is that I’ve accepted that fortune-cookie advice.

title: Medical research is worth the effort
author: By Alejandro Barbosa, Opinion Writer
content: Funding medical research, especially for rare genetic diseases, is worth the $35 billion effort. It allows society to advance and be able to provide opportunities for thousands of people affected by these conditions to reach their goals, whether academic, career or personal. On Oct. 14, the Food and Drug Administration launched a new initiative introducing a more holistic framework for drug development focused on rare diseases. About a week later, according to an Oct. 22 CNBC article, a bipartisan bill called the Faster Clinical Trials Act was introduced by U.S. Reps. D-MA Jake Auchincloss and R-VA Morgan Griffith, which, if passed, would accelerate development of treatments, especially for rare and chronic conditions. The FDA defines a rare disease as a disease or condition that affects fewer than 200,000 people in the U.S. There are over 10,000 of these diseases, affecting over 30 million people in the .S. Many of these diseases are genetic and can be life-threatening without treatment, such as Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Duchenne muscular dystrophy is a progressive genetic disorder caused by a mutation that prevents the body from producing dystrophin, an essential protein that helps protect muscle cells. This disease affects the muscular system, causing muscle weakness and loss of muscle mass, eventually leading to respiratory and cardiac failure, which is ultimately fatal if left untreated. Median life expectancy is approximately 28 years, and there is currently no cure. However, it is treatable; many treatments meant to address the genetic root cause have been developed and approved by the FDA in recent years. Treatments addressing the genetic root cause of rare diseases rely on understanding the genome of affected individuals. Although genetic disorders are not related to viruses, public health interventions, such as vaccines, also rely on understanding an organism’s genome. Pallavi Singh, assistant professor of microbiology in the Department of Biological Sciences, explains how advances in genetic sequencing and mRNA technology helped scientists develop vaccines against COVID-19. “I think one classic example is the COVID-19 vaccine. We had the sequences of these viruses, and we were actually generating them in real time. But then also, the mRNA vaccine that was based on the sequence of a previously known coronavirus was found to be able to be used against it,” Singh said. Singh also adds that understanding an organism’s genome is helpful for new drug development, especially when addressing issues such as microbial resistance. “New drug discovery can also be helpful,” Singh said. “The reason for that is we know there’s a bigger issue at hand right now. Once people fall sick, they usually go to the doctor and the doctor prescribes antibiotics. However, taking antibiotics leads us to this problem of antimicrobial resistance. And antimicrobial resistance actually means that the bacteria no longer respond to the antibiotics we take.” Understanding how genetic changes affect the body can help researchers develop treatments for conditions that previously had few or no options. “Because of that, we have to then look for new drugs. We have to find drugs and antibiotics that the bacteria will be susceptible to and will respond to,” Singh said. “The way the bacteria generate resistance is usually by changing something in its DNA. If we can use genome characterization or genome sequencing to understand the sequences of these pathogens, then we can see what they are resistant to and which antibiotics they are resistant to,” Singh said. One of the first available treatments was eteplirsen, sold as Exondys-51, approved by the FDA in September 2016. According to a 2017 article published in the journal Nucleic Acid Therapeutics, the treatment is targeted at a specific mutated part called an exon within the mutated gene, found only in about 13% of all patients with the disease. More recently, the FDA approved Elevidys, another treatment, in June 2023 . This treatment is a type of gene therapy , which consists of a harmless virus, called a vector, delivering a shortened but functional version of dystrophin called micro-dystrophin. It then instructs muscle cells to produce micro-dystrophin. While originally approved for ambulatory patients ages 4 and up, in June 2024 , the FDA expanded approval to non-ambulatory patients as well. However, according to a November 2025 FDA press release , the FDA returned to its original approval and added a warning label after the reported deaths of two non-ambulatory patients from liver failure following treatment. Although newer treatments to address the genetic cause of this disease have their limitations and still require further evaluations regarding effectiveness and safety, this is still an endeavor worth pursuing. If these treatments, for both Duchenne muscular dystrophy and other rare diseases, offer at least a small chance for patients suffering from them to have a longer, more satisfying life, and pursue whatever goals they have, then I think this is an endeavor worth pursuing.

title: The Penguins slip past Huskies in consecutive games
author: By Lily Camargo, Sports Reporter
content: On their home turf in Ohio, the Youngstown State University Penguins (11-10, 7-3 Horizon League) edged past the Huskies (7-13, 1-9 Horizon) 3-1 in a game that looked as if it could swing either way. Coming off a 3-0 win the previous day , Youngstown State was able to carry that momentum forward into Saturday’s game. Head coach Sondra D’Amore was unavailable for comment. Set 1 The set was highly competitive from the middle to the end. The Huskies were down by four points at 10–14, but NIU began clawing their way back into striking distance. In the midst of the action of set one, NIU called a timeout, later returning to a score of 15–18. The Huskies came back strong with a surge of momentum. Playing with both aggression and tactical precision, NIU caught up to YSU at 21–21. The Huskies took the lead 22-21 and from that moment, both teams fought fiercely for every exchange. Junior outside hitter Ava Grevengoed ’s two service aces helped put the Penguins away in the first set 25-23. Set 2 The Huskies came into set two hot. They quickly established a at 2-0 lead, maintaining that distance as they pushed into the middle of the set The score remained tight until the 11th point where they tied; from then on, the two opponents repeatedly traded leads until the final point. Freshman outside hitter Katie Pahl put on a notable performance, leading the team with 13 kills. She proved crucial on defense as well, accumulating 11 digs by the end of the match. Unfortunately for the Huskies, their fire was put out at match point by the Penguins, 25-23. Set 3 and 4 Moving on from the previous set, the Huskies were unable to replicate the spark they found in the opening set, failing to secure a set lead against the Penguins. Youngstown State continued NIU’s losing streak, extending it from six to seven matches. A hard-fought match that could have moved the Huskies up in the Horizon League rankings now leaves them plagued at the bottom of the conference, sitting second to last. UP NEXT — The Huskies will take on Robert Morris University at 6 p.m. on Friday at home in the Victor E. Court.

title: Former NIU student pleads not guilty during arraignment
author: By Diego Martinez, News Editor
content: Lester E. Bowen, a former NIU student who majored in history, was arraigned during a Wednesday status hearing and pleaded not guilty. An arraignment is a court proceeding where a defendant is brought before a court to hear the charges and potential penalties against them. The defendant then pleads guilty or not guilty. Bowen was arrested on Aug. 15 following reports of a stabbing on 100 N. First St. He was charged with attempted murder and aggravated assault. The Northern Star obtained court documents filed shortly after the Wednesday status hearing. A status hearing is a pretrial court appearance where a judge, prosecutor and defense attorney meet to check on the progress of a case. There were modifications made to Bowen’s order for GPS electronic monitoring. The modifications specified that Bowen is not allowed within 1,000 feet of a specified DeKalb residence and a specified local home-improvement store. Bowen can be released for work and classes during hours approved by the court. The university confirmed that Bowen is no longer enrolled at NIU. The documents also stated Bowen is not allowed to have any contact with the victim. The documents do not state where Bowen would reside while on GPS monitoring. An order of continuance was filed and Bowen’s next status hearing will take place at 9 a.m. Dec. 1 in the DeKalb County Courthouse, 133 W. State St. in Sycamore.

title: Women’s soccer draws against Robert Morris in second consecutive game on the road
author: By Eric Avila, Sports Reporter
content: NIU women’s soccer (4-7-5, 3-4-3 Horizon League) tied on the road to the Robert Morris University Colonials (5-8-4, 2-5-3 Horizon) by a score of 2-2 Sunday afternoon. In the first half of the game, the Huskies produced 7 shots with 3 being on target, but were unable to put one in the back of the net. In the second half of the game, NIU produced 8 more shots, with 3 being on target. The first goal came via an own goal from the Colonials at the 51:21 mark of the game. The Colonials tied the game 16 minutes later. Colonial junior midfielder/forward Alyssa Mella put it past freshman goalkeeper Alexandra Devory , assisted by senior forward Madison Sievering . Not even a minute later, redshirt freshman forward Monica Correa found the back of the net in the 69th minute of play, scoring for the second consecutive game, bringing her season total to four goals. It was assisted by sophomore midfielder Abby Foulk , giving the Huskies a 2-1 lead. Foulk has assisted Correa in two consecutive games. The Huskies maintained the lead for almost 12 minutes as the Colonials tied the game in the 81st minute of action. Senior midfielder/forward Ava Tretheway evened it up for Robert Morris. The remainder of the game saw only 3 more shots, 2 from the Colonials and 1 from the Huskies. With one game remaining, NIU sits three points off the last playoff spot, currently held by their last conference opponent, the Indiana University Indianapolis Jaguars. The Huskies need to defeat IU Indy and for Cleveland State University to either draw or lose to Purdue University Fort Wayne to clinch the last playoff spot. UP NEXT — The Huskies will play the IU Indy Jaguars at 1 p.m. on Friday at the Michael A. Carroll Track and Soccer Stadium in Indianapolis, Indiana.

title: Carrion Feeder and Skinblasted send chills at Fargo
author: By Zoe Camardo, Lifestyle Writer
content: Carrion Feeder and Skinblasted performed a Halloween-themed concert on Sunday at Fargo Venue, 651 E Lincoln Hwy. The concert was intended for local bands to cover iconic metal and hardcore bands. Carrion Feeder covered the Misfits and Mortician, and Skinblasted covered Hatebreed. In the spirit of Halloween, the audience was encouraged to dress up. People wore lots of gothic inspired make up and costumes. There were the typical skeletons and vampires, but many people dressed in unique costumes. On the sillier side, there were also people dressed up as a banana and someone as a taco. Originally, hardcore band Termina was supposed to cover Acid Breath, but they weren’t able to make it to the show. Instead, Carrion Feeder, another hardcore band, added a set as the Misfits, a band they’ve covered in the past. The band members dressed as the Misfits and styled their hair to imitate them. It was the Northwest Indianian band’s first time playing in DeKalb. Vello Martinez was Carrion Feeder’s main vocalist for the Misfit set. She sings with the group occasionally when they need a vocalist with a clearer tone. Due to Termina’s cancellation, she was called to do the set with four days to prepare. “I just spent the last four days just memorizing all the songs I forgot,” Martinez said. “It was honestly fine because they have such good music anyway, so it’s not like I wouldn’t listen to it anyway. But it was a little scary because I noticed some songs that I know I know, I was forgetting random words.” Following Carrion Feeder, Skinblasted covered Hatebreed. While Carrion Feeder dressed up as the band they covered, Skinblasted blended into the crowd. Their lead singer dressed as Hatebreed’s lead singer, including a fake beard, however, the rest of Hatebreed had a Wolverine, Jason from Friday the 13th, a shark, and an original who they called Thomas Richards. Skinblasted guitarist Gabe Aguilar, the shark, was responsible for covering Hatebreed. “I remember hearing them first and doing a deep dive into the whole discography. And they influenced me so much. Their lyrics are super inspirational and motivational, and their riffs are amazing,” Aguilar said. “Carrion Feeder, we’re very close with them, they were like ‘we’re doing this cover show, do you want to cover a band?’ We were like ‘Hatebreed, why not? We love Hatebreed.’” As Skinblasted played their set, Carrion Feeder did a quick costume change from the Misfits to Mortician, the band they originally planned to cover. Rocco Popovich is the vocalist and bassist for Carrion Feeder. He said they wanted to cover Mortician for a while. “It was really cool playing punk stuff, but I want to do something really hard — both like headbanging and hard, kind of a bit more technical. So we decided to do Mortician,” Popovich said. “They’re very influential to a lot of brutal death metal bands, sometimes even beatdown bands love Mortician.” After they had said their goodbyes, an audience member convinced Carrion Feeder to quickly play one of their original songs. Learn more about the bands on their Instagrams @carrionfeederband and @skinblastedband . For more concerts see f argovenue .com.

title: Early voting brings ballot boxes to students
author: By Valeria Solis, Lifestyle Writer
content: With the hecticness of school, jobs, fun and other responsibilities, it may be difficult to cut time in a busy schedule to get the chance to vote. Early voting on campus can grant students convenience in casting their vote, and getting their voice heard. Michaela Holtz, director of career readiness and success, shared ways in which early voting is helpful to students. “Election Day doesn’t always fit those schedules, and unexpected conflicts can come up. Early voting gives students the flexibility to vote at a time that works for them. If an issue comes up, like missing ID or going to the wrong location, they still have time to fix it,” Holtz said. From 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., voting can be done at the Holmes Student Center in the Glass Gallery Lounge. Early voting started Oct. 23 and will continue through Friday.. Holtz believes easy access to voting on campus can benefit students and other DeKalb residents. “Students don’t need a car or a trip across town. Early voting is right here on campus at the Holmes Student Center, and any DeKalb County voter can use it,” Holtz said. To register, all DeKalb County residents must show two forms of identification, as well as their current address. Huskie Vote is a non-partisan initiative at NIU that helps students navigate the voting process. The Huskies Vote website has resources for voters, including the “ Research Your Ballot ” link for before they head to the polls.

title: Huskies Vote gets students poll-ready
author: By Keegan Nowman and Diego Martinez
content: Midterm elections are on Nov. 3 and Huskies Vote is helping students navigate the ballots. Huskies Vote, an organization on campus, is providing students with resources to help them register to vote and where to vote. Michaela Holtz, director of career readiness and success, said Huskies Vote is providing voting cards and tablings to promote student voting. “We have Huskies Vote peer ambassadors who have been very busy at different locations on campus, tabling and sharing information with students,” Holtz said. They have also partnered with the DeKalb County Clerk’s Office, where several students and faculty trained to be deputy registrars for volunteer events. Huskies Vote sources their information for students from the Illinois Board of Elections to give them only accurate information. “We are partnering with the clerk’s office, so we hopefully help students narrow down the sort of sources of where they find information, making sure that it is accurate, nonpartisan work, and they can then make their decision,” Holtz said. The online and regular registration deadlines have already passed; however, Holtz said students can go participate in early voting from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. until Friday in the Holmes Student Center, Glass Gallery Lounge. “Students can register to vote during early voting periods. The only thing they have to remember is that at the time when they register to vote, they have to vote,” Holtz said. “Being able to research what’s on the ballot and having a plan for how to vote is important before they go in.” Huskies Vote also encourages students to have a voting plan. Students can develop this plan through Huskies Vote’s website , which has multiple outside sources to help best inform students. A source provided through Huskies Vote is BallotReady . BallotReady helps to prepare voters for the election by researching who is on the ballot, seeing who represents certain areas and finding polling places. March to the Polls , an event hosted by Huskies Vote, will help students learn more about the importance of voting, while also giving the opportunity to cast an early vote. Jennifer Groce, director of community promotion at NIU and an organizer of the event, said she is excited to see the efforts students put in to promote democracy. “I am most excited about the opportunity to highlight the efforts of our students and their work in promoting democracy and civic participation and civic engagement, and just showcasing their opportunities to participate in this election,” Groce said. Groce also said Huskies Vote ambassadors will be helping at the event. “There are some students that we have that are part of our Huskies Vote Ambassadors. They are actually paid positions, and so they have become deputized registrars and that kind of thing,” Groce said. Huskies Vote will have volunteers on Election Day in the Glass Lounge of the Holmes Student Center to help navigate students through the voting process. Holtz said students should give themselves time to register. “Plan ahead, give yourself time during the early voting,” Holtz said. “There is plenty of time to sit down with the election judge to get registered to vote, to help them explain the process to you.”

title: Operation Vivaldi: Ukraine’s drone warfare changes the rules of battle
author: By Santiago Montañez Bertoletti, Opinion Writer
content: “The Four Seasons” is the most famous work of Antonio Vivaldi, an Italian Baroque composer and one of the most iconic figures in classical music. As its name suggests, “The Four Seasons” is a group of concertos composed for violin and orchestra, each representing a season of the year: spring, summer, autumn and winter. Operation Vivaldi is one of the last masterpieces of the Ukrainian High Command: a four-phase secret operation that remained unknown to the public, including the Russians and Western press services. In the four months since the operation began on May 22, Ukrainian forces did not post anything about it on social media. What is impressive about the operation is not only the stealth with which it was carried out, especially when social networks are a major front in the war, but that practically the spearhead of the operation had no humans. Ukraine needed to stop the Russian offensive at Lyman, Donetsk, an area where roads converge to major cities of the oblast claimed by Russia. Operation Vivaldi began in the summer with an entire bombing campaign to weaken Russian positions. First, they hit Russian logistics in the rear, between 50 and 120 kilometers, using only drones. Additionally, the Ukrainians brought BTRs, Soviet light armoured vehicles, to the Russian defensive lines. Ukraine also repurposed BTR armored personnel carriers as remotely controlled explosive vehicles to attack Russian defensive positions. Ukrainian armored vehicles and tanks subsequently advanced with drone support. The operation also relied on aerial and ground drones for surveillance, counter-drone operations, evacuating wounded soldiers and transporting supplies. To date, Ukraine has only liberated at least a few hundred square kilometers and inflicted a few thousand casualties. The goal of this operation was to disarm the next offensive that Russia was eager to unleash on the Donetsk fortress belt located in four heavily defended cities: Sloviansk, Kramatorsk, Druzhkivka and Kostiantynivka. Ukraine has integrated aerial and ground drones with mechanized and infantry brigades into a coordinated operation, demonstrating a shift in military doctrine. And for the first time since WWII, the U.S. is not at the forefront of the latest military-related technological developments. Trump’s decision not to support Ukraine weighs now that all the European heavyweights are just waiting for him to expand their production to buy the latest in field-tested military technology. As a result, the emergence of new military power leaves Trump in an awkward position: Moving away from Kyiv weakens the U.S. military, and re-engagement is another blow to his childhood ego.
