title: Minneapolis rallies to stop ICE and police terror
author: fightbacknews.org
content: By Montana Hirsch and Mikael Pensec Minneapolis, MN – On October 24, more than 60 protesters lined Lake Street to demand an end to ICE and police terror. The protest was organized by the Minnesota Immigrant Rights Action Committee and co-hosted by the Twin Cities Coalition for Justice to connect the violence inflicted on the community by both the police and ICE. As threats of a second ICE surge loom, with the beginnings of increased ICE sightings reported from community rapid response groups, the people of Minnesota show that they will fight back harder – they have fought militantly against ICE before and will do so again. The protest was held on Lake Street in the heart of South Minneapolis’ immigrant community. Up and down lake street supportive honks were heard from passing cars as protesters chanted, “When immigrants are under attack, what do we do? Stand up, fight back!” Jana Williams spoke about a recent win in the fight for justice for her niece Allison Lussier. Allison Lussier was murdered two years ago, and her case was neglected by the Minneapolis Police Department. Only two days before the protest, and after years of her family and community members fighting for justice, a murder charge was finally filed in her case. Williams stated, “The other day when I sat across from the six women from the Hennepin County Attorney’s Office. They sat across the table from me, telling me that we were finally getting Chuck Foss charged. And I had a sigh of relief; I can maybe exhale. And I said, ‘Do you know what MPD did? They surrounded me and us with armored vehicles.’ They said yes, we did know that. Shame on you! You were willing to harm us, arrest us, tear gas us, put us behind bars, but you were not willing to do this with violent criminals!” Williams urged the crowd to continue to put pressure on Mayor Frey to hold all the officers involved accountable. Alissa Washington, representing the Twin Cities Coalition for Justice, told protesters, “My fiancé, Cornelius Jackson, has been incarcerated for 20 years. My family is fighting for answers about Stephen Washington’s death in prison while also living with my uncle’s deportation. These struggles meet in my family and in so many others. That is why our solidarity reaches across prison walls and borders, including to Palestine and people resisting war and occupation. Every family deserves safety, dignity, and a future together.” Greg King, representing the North STAR Alliance said: “Nobody in our community, regardless of their immigration status, should be hunted down and assaulted or shot in the street for their perceived immigration status. There is no reason on earth that we should not be giving immigration agents guns to enforce civil immigration law. And by the same token, we should not be giving law enforcement officers in our state, who have guns and a history of racial profiling ending in fatal encounters in our streets, permission to start asking people for their papers.” The protest ended with a speech from Aizar Cabrera of the Minnesota Immigrant Rights Action Committee. “We immigrants know about scary times. We are living in exile,” said Cabrera, “but make no mistake, it did not start in January of 2025, and it has not ended yet. We are living in a state of terror. The immigration enforcement machine has been grinding through our communities for decades, across every administration.” The speech ended with a call to Governor Walz to make Minnesota a sanctuary state. MIRAC will continue to pressure Governor Walz to take executive action and ensure that Minnesota is prepared for another onslaught of federal terror. MIRAC demands that Walz issue a sanctuary state executive order that would ban 287(g) agreements and any type of collaboration between local law enforcement and ICE, keep ICE out of sensitive locations and off state property, outlaw secret police, and more. MIRAC will also continue to support the fight for community control of the police in Minneapolis. # MinneapolisMN # MN # ImmigrantRights # InJusticeSystem # MIRAC # TCC4J

title: Tacoma: New evidence in Ronald Amir Harris case
author: fightbacknews.org
content: Tumwater, WA – Members of the Tacoma Alliance Against Racist and Political Repression held a press conference outside the Washington State Office of Independent Investigation (WA OII) on Friday, October 23, to urge the WA OII to investigate the death of Ronald Amir Harris. TacAARPR members delivered a petition with over with over 450 signatures to the office, as well as new evidence obtained by Ronald Amir Harris’s family. “The county didn't do an investigation that produced really any type of evidence that could conclusively concur with a suicide,” said Christian Tullar. “And that's why petitioning the state is so important here.” Ronald Harris was found dead in his Pierce County jail cell before his trial on May 2, 2022. The county’s sheriff’s office ruled it a suicide, but refused to release key evidence to Ronald’s father, Ray Charles Harris. Concerned community members wrote in over 60 letters to the WA OII urging them to open an investigation into this death. When TacAARPR members met with WA OII on Oct 8, the office would not take up the investigation unless Ronald’s family and community were able to provide new evidence. “My son did not commit suicide,” stated Ray Harris, “My son told me three days before his death, he said, Dad, if something happens to me, I did not kill myself.” The petition’s two main demands were for Pierce County to release key evidence to Ronald Harris’s family, and for WA OII to do a full, transparent investigation into the death. The first demand was met earlier this week, when Harris’s family obtained new evidence by appealing directly to the county medical examiner’s office. This came after almost a year of denials by the sheriff’s office and the family’s FOIA requests. According to documents available on the TacAARPR website, the toxicology report, autopsy report and autopsy photos were never entered as evidence in the original suicide investigation. “The WA OII gets 14 million tax dollars a year to investigate deaths like Ronald’s, yet the onus is put on us to find new evidence,” said TacAARPR member Moon Gosserand. “And when we do present new evidence, they have the power to just dismiss it, like they’ve done on other cases. But we won’t let them dismiss Ronald’s case without a fight!” Gosserand was referring to the cases of Jason Hale and Andrea Churna, where new evidence, including new video and testimony, was dismissed by the WA OII. Since forming in 2021, the WA OII has never completed a “prior investigation.” According to their website, all eight existing prior investigation cases were either denied, passed to another body, or still in progress. TacAARPR members affirmed that despite this track record, they would continue the community investigation to obtain even more new evidence. “One of the pieces of evidence that really worried us was in what’s called a CAD log,” Tullar continued, referring to the computer-aided dispatch log, which was released to TacAARPR via a FOIA request earlier this month. “In the CAD log we had seen the term hanging, and, when you're Black in America, especially when you're a Black man, the term hanging has a very particular racialized connotation. It instantly makes us think of the type of political and racial repression against Black people. And Pierce County has a long history of oppression and neglect and violence and brutality against Black men and Black people and people who are in the prison and jail system here.” “My son's going to get justice,” Ray Harris re-stated. TacAARPR and the Harris family confirmed they will not back down until a full, transparent investigation has been completed. # TacomaWA # WA # InJusticeSystem # KillerCops # NAARPR

title: Tallahassee voting rights panel gives perspectives and how to fight back
author: fightbacknews.org
content: Tallahassee, FL – Over 30 people gathered at The Bark restaurant to hear from city commission candidates and local organizers about the attacks on voting rights, and on how we can fight back. On the panel were city commission candidates Dot Inman-Johnson and PJ Perez. The city commission has had a 3-2 conservative-to-progressive split for eight years, during which the majority has served developers over the people. Three seats are up for election this year, with progressive candidates in each, including Inman-Johnson and Perez, so the balance could swing to progressive control. Also on the panel were Jackson Vanderley from Tallahassee SDS, Kevin Louis-Jeune from FAMU SDS, Lunchbox from Black on Black Rhyme, and Delilah Pierre with the Tallahassee Alliance Against Racist and Political Repression. Louis-Jeune, a first year FAMU student, spoke to the differences he had seen in town: “Walking around the immediate area around campus, compared to around on campus, is like walking into a whole different city.” Lunchbox responded to an audience question about what to do when the elections are over, “We vote with our time, we vote with our dollar, we vote with our energy. So besides the election process, which is important, we have the power to have conversations with our neighbors.” When asked about the effects in Tallahassee of racist redistricting in other parts of Florida, Inman-Johnson said, “When [former representative] Al Lawson’s district was eliminated through gerrymandering, the legislature tried to do a fairer district. Desantis vetoed it and had his team develop the district. It’s important that [Democrat nominee for governor, David] Jolly get elected because it would be a fairer governor who would oversee those decisions.” Perez kept it simple: “Just do away with partisan gerrymandering altogether, at all levels. That’s what we should all be aspiring to.” An audience member asked about how elected officials can balance holding their values with making small movements towards progress, especially when more and more Republican voters are moving to Florida. Pierre responded by saying, “There might be more Republican voters moving here, but there’s one unity between Republican voters and Democrat voters: we broke as hell. We ain’t got no money. We have to rephrase the question. It’s not Republicans versus Democrats; it's the working class versus the billionaires and multimillionaires.” # TallahasseeFL # FL # PeoplesStruggles # VotingRights

title: Interview with Michael Humaña of the National Union of Education Workers in Chile
author: fightbacknews.org
content: Fight Back! interviewed Michael Humaña, a trade union leader from Chile, on October 14 to learn about the trade union struggle there and in Latin America. Fight Back! : Which organizations are you a member of? Michael Humaña: I am the president of the National Union of Education Workers in Chile (SNTE) and organizational secretary of the Continental Federation of Education Workers. Fight Back!: What took place in Bolivia on October 10 and 11? Humaña: In the Trópico of Cochabamba, Bolivia, we founded CIMA, la Coordinación Internacionalista de los Movimientos Sociales Antiimperialistas del Abya Yala. It is an organization that looks to be the anti-imperialist wall of the peoples to confront the criminal “Shields of the Americas” of Donald Trump. With the leadership of President Evo Morales, we hope to be the anti-capitalist, socialist alternative of the peoples who struggle. Fight Back!: What was your role in the meeting to form CIMA? Humaña: In this anti-imperialist gathering, I was part of the coordination team. Fight Back!: What is the significance of the presence and participation of Evo Morales at the gathering? Humaña: Evo Morales is the leader of the revolutionary left and of the movements of peasants and popular in the south of our America. After the kidnapping of President Nicolás Maduro of Venezuela, Evo Morales transformed into the main anti-imperialist leader of all the continent. The experience of 14 years in the government of Bolivia, the proposal of Living Well and Pluri-Nationality, are examples for peoples of “Indoamérica.” Fight Back!: Did the gathering result in any agreements, points of unity, or plan for action? Humaña: The main objective of the encuentro was to advance a programmatic unity, therefore the resolution to found CIMA. There are the fundamentals to create a solid continental organization with real capacity to mobilize a front against U.S. imperialism and Israeli Zionism. Some of the points of agreement are: Declare October 9 as an International Anti-Imperialist Day to honoro Che Guevara; to advance to building of a Continental Network of Popular Communication; defense of Mother Earth and common goods – this will be a fundamental task to confront predatory extractivism and confront electoral processes to retake local and national governments, but with a program that is socialist, anti-colonial,and anti-imperialist, without trusting the neoliberal politicians. To demand the freedom of our political prisoners like President Nicolás Maduro, First Lady Cilia Flores of Venezuela, President Pedro Castillo and Victor Polay in Perú, former Assembly Representative Freddy Mamani in Bolivia, and to end the political persecution of social leaders on the continent like our brother Evo Morales Ayma. Fight Back!: What are the lessons to share with movements in the U.S. that are to be learned from the national mobilizations in Bolivia? Humaña: We believe in the fundamental task of unity of the social movements of the continent, from Alaska to Patagonia. The social movements in Bolivia give us the lesson that the bravery of the people can take down criminal and tyrannical governments. Unity of the working class, the peasants and students is fundamental to stop the oligarchies in our countries. The anti-imperialist conviction of the people of Bolivia must be an example to all the peoples of the world. Fight Back!: Can you provide a brief explanation of the situation in Chile? Humaña: Today in Chile, there is the return of Pinochetism to the government; the criminal military dictatorship returns to push reforms and deepen neoliberalism. Sadly, the previous governments of progressive neoliberalism and social democrats governed with the laws and constitution of the dictatorship. They have allowed education, healthcare and pensions to be run like a business and we have lost many social rights. So now, the far right comes to deepen the neoliberal agenda further. The popular movement and trade union movement are weakened and only the students maintain the call to rebel and engage in struggle against neoliberalism. But, from the teachers and other popular forces, we continue giving battle to rebuild the Chilean popular movement behind a program and project with a socialist perspective and popular power. # International # Chile # Labor # SNTE # CIMA

title: NAARPR Dallas calls for anti-ICE resolution
author: fightbacknews.org
content: Dallas, TX – On October 14, organizers with the Dallas chapter of the National Alliance Against Racism and Political Repression (NAARPR Dallas) spoke at Dallas City Hall to call for the city council to move forward a resolution denouncing the crimes of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and demanding for an independent investigation into ICE violence. Lili Delgado, an organizer with NAARPR Dallas, said at the open mic period, “Dallas City Council has a responsibility towards its residents, be they documented or undocumented. We demand the city of Dallas issue an official statement denouncing ICE shootings and killings and also pledges to use all its available powers to investigate directly or fund an independent investigation in the event of an ICE shooting or killing here in Dallas.” Delgado continued, “This is about actions and not just words and we have to ensure that there are independent investigations into these shootings; it is our duty to our community to ensure there is justice for the actual events.” ICE has shot at least 24 people since last year, including Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, who was killed by ICE in Houston earlier this year, and Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, who was shot and is being held captive by ICE in Austin. # DallasTX # TX # InJusticeSystem # NAARPR # ImmigrantRights # ICE # KillerCops # KillerICE

title: Bozeman police, city commission sign Axon contract amid public outcries
author: fightbacknews.org
content: Bozeman, MT – On Thursday, October 15, the Bozeman chapter of Montana for Palestine (MT4P) learned that the newly-published agenda for the upcoming October 20 City Commission meeting contained a vote to approve a five-year, $2.4 million contract with Axon Enterprise Inc. Despite Axon's collaboration with the terrorist Immigration and Customs Enforcement, they were selected to replace the Bozeman Police Department's aging body cameras, in-car camera systems, and tasers. Over the next five days, MT4P both reached out to commissioners, providing them with recommendations for alternatives and highlighting issues with Axon, and organized a public comment campaign against the item. Despite the limited forewarning, the vote October 20 saw around 25 community members come to give public comment. In the over 60 minutes of concern and opposition, community members were clear with their statements against the brutalization of immigrants, the surveillance of their community, and their distrust in the commission. Riley Ophus, a Montana State University student, stated, “This company is actively involved in escalating mass surveillance, and also enabling ICE's abuse of immigrants. Over the summer, Axon sold $220 million worth of tasers to ICE, following a multi-million dollar investment in the company by Donald Trump. No company which sells tasers to ICE, or accepts major investments from Donald Trump, should receive even a dime of Bozeman's money.” Natsuki Nakamura said, “We've been told that BPD [Bozeman Police Department] will not use facial recognition and automatic license plate readers because 'Montana law generally prohibits it.' While we know Montana law has exceptions for law enforcement to use it, we also know state laws can change, and we also know that Bozeman had fully intended to put up red light cameras until the state preempted cities from doing so.” The commissioners provided lip service to the comments but unanimously voted the contract through anyway. Resident Homa Masood responded, “There is nobody forcing you to take on this contract – you already made the decision, before you came here, that you were going to pass it. And if that's the case I don't know why we even bother with having public comment! You have people coming in and telling you that the Israeli military, police, navy, and prison services are deploying Axon manufactured tasers – and you're just shrugging and saying, 'Yeah, sorry, that sucks.'” The commission's blatant disrespect for the public's opinions on the city's actions are not a deterrent. Public comment campaigns in Bozeman are far from over, because, even if Mayor Joey Morrison believes that “[this] isn't how things get done – you can't just cajole people into doing what you want,” the Bozeman community is losing trust in the commissioners' ability to meaningfully affect city processes in a way that benefits them. Bozemanites want a city commission that will fight for them – the hardworking people of Bozeman – and are prepared to continue the fight! # BozemanMT # MT # InjusticeSystem # Police # Axon # Surveillance # ICE

title: Anaheim rallies for Albert Arzola during city council meeting
author: fightbacknews.org
content: Anaheim, CA – On Tuesday, October 13, the Community Service Organization, Orange County (CSO OC) alongside the family of Albert Arzola protested outside an Anaheim City Council meeting. Matthew Compton, a member of CSO OC’s Police Accountability Committee, told the crowd, “We stand here today to demand justice for Albert Arzola. It has been 10 months, and killer cop Nathan Garcia is still on the force!” Anaheim Officer Nathan Garcia is the officer responsible for killing 19-year-old Albert Arzola outside his mother’s home. Compton continued, “Officer Garcia still being on the force is why we fight for community control of the police. Community control will give us, the working-class residents of Anaheim, direct authority over how we are policed, decide punishments for cops who kill or violate policy.” After Compton’s comment, chants were hurled at the council chambers while the council meeting was ongoing. “Fuck Anaheim PD!” and “Nathan Garcia! Lock him up!” being the loudest and angriest chants. During chanting, several attendees came outside and noted that the protest could be clearly heard from inside the chambers. Sergio Pelayo, cousin of Albert Arzola, had this to say, “Albert’s life didn’t need to end so young. He was the sweetest, most caring and thoughtful man that you would ever know. Albert had a bully within the Anaheim Police Department. Officer Nathan Garcia would sit in his car and call out and harass Albert up until his death.” Grace Arzola, Albert’s aunt, followed, “Today, inside the council chambers, the council is going to vote to increase Anaheim PD’s budget by $9 million. Ordinary people struggle to make ends meet, but Anaheim PD wants their raise for killing people.” During the protest, Anaheim PD officers would peer out the windows looking uncomfortable, all while the angry voices of the family rang out “Justice for Albert Arzola!” CSO OC along with the family of Albert Arzola and residents of Anaheim will keep protesting until Officer Nathan Garcia is fired and jailed. # AnaheimCA # CA # OrangeCounty # InjusticeSystem # AlbertArzola # KillerCop # PoliceMurder # OppressedNationalities

title: LSU students rally at Board of Supervisors meeting amidst police repression
author: fightbacknews.org
content: Baton Rouge, LA – On October 16, students at Louisiana State University (LSU) mobilized at the Board of Supervisors meeting to demand an end to LSU’s recent attacks on Title IX. While students gathered inside to speak, other supporters held a rally directly outside the meeting. The protest was organized by a coalition of organizations including Students for a Democratic Society (LSU SDS), Injustice Reform, Feminists in Action, Tiger Prison Project, Freedom Road Socialist Organization and Tigers Against Sexual Assault. During public comment, board members repeatedly interrupted Ziad Eissa, vice president of LSU SD. Eventually, the board had police forcefully remove him from the meeting. They also removed three other members of SDS who were waiting to give their comments. This meeting had a significant increase in police repression in comparison to previous ones, with officers from the LSU Police Department, Baton Rouge Police Department, and even an undercover officer from the local sheriff’s department. When supporters learned that their fellow students were denied the right to speak, the rally outside intensified. Students ensured that their voices could be heard from inside the building. Chants like “LSU you can’t hide! Protecting rapists is a crime!” “ Hey hey! Ho ho! The BOS has to go!” and “LSU what do you say, how many girls got raped today?!” could be heard from inside the building while the board met. The rally raised demands for the cultural centers on campus to be restored to their full capacity. It also demanded the restoration of Title IX offices like the office of engagement, and that LSU expel Damien Shanklin and all other rapists on campus. Students criticized the LSU administration for escalating its clearly racist, sexist and homophobic actions under Trump. “Across the nation, universities and police work hand in hand to protect rapists, bigots and racists, while punishing students who dare to fight back. Why? Because the capitalist ruling class feeds on oppression,” explained Enola Guyer, a speaker from Freedom Road Socialist Organization. Despite heightened police presence at the event, protesters made it clear that they will not quit fighting against the university administration’s repression. “We want Landry’s lapdogs to know that we know who they are, we know what they stand for, and we will not stop fighting until our demands are met!” said Guyer as she closed out her speech. The coalition has planned a week of action from October 19 to the 23, with a range of activities from an open mic night to a sit-in, closing out with a rally to demand that LSU expel Damien Shanklin. Shanklin is a rapist who was allowed on campus with no consequence, and permitted to play for LSU’s football team even after a LSU investigation determined he raped another student. # BatonRougeLA # LA # StudentMovement # SDS # WomensMovement

title: Milwaukee community marks third annual Stolen Lives Day
author: fightbacknews.org
content: Milwaukee, WI – On October 22, 50 people gathered at the King Center on Milwaukee’s Northside to mark Stolen Lives Day to uplift the memories of loved ones whose lives have been stolen by police crimes. The Cole, Sharpe, Anderson, Thomas, Robinson-Scarborough, and Lawhorn families were present as were members of Milwaukee’s Palestinian community. All these families have unjustly lost their sons and daughters to police murders and negligence. Brian Verdin, one of the original founders of the Milwaukee Alliance, gave a moving account of the dozens of families the Alliance has struggled alongside for justice over the years. Milwaukee poets Lea V, Mario “The Poet” and Jonah Denae offered up poems that celebrated the lives lost, made space for community anger, and uplifted the importance of the struggle for justice. Denae received a standing ovation for her poem that indicted the entire system for its violence against Black men. Taleavia Cole, the sister of Alvin Cole, who was murdered by killer cop Joseph Mensah, stated, “No punishment can bring our loved ones back, and no words can undo the devastation violence leaves behind… the conversation cannot end with just justice. We need accountability, we need transparency, we need action.” Families needed space to grieve, but they were also angry and ready to fight back. Indictments and convictions for killer cops are a start for these families, but they plan to keep fighting until they get the whole system changed. Cole continued, “At the end of the day we cannot fight this alone, we need more grassroots organizations like the Milwaukee Alliance, we need more alliance.” For the last three years, the Milwaukee Alliance Against Racist and Political Repression has hosted Milwaukee’s Stolen Lives Day. # MilwaukeeWI # WI # InJusticeSystem # OppressedNationalities # AfricanAmerican # NAARPR # MAARPR # KillerCops

title: Loyola New Orleans students rally against sexual violence on campus
author: fightbacknews.org
content: New Orleans, LA – On October 22, the Liberate and Unite New Orleans chapter of Students for a Democratic Society (LUNO SDS) rallied as part of a national day of action against sexual violence and rape culture on university campuses. The day of action was called in response to the ongoing coverage surrounding the Cornell 57 and rampant sexual violence on college campuses in general. At the rally, Loyola students expressed that their university had repeatedly failed to keep them and their peers safe and called for stronger systems of accountability from their administrators. Speaking for LUNO SDS, Loyola freshman Jessica Monahan stated, “It is imperative that bodies of authority in our universities hear out and defend people like Jane Doe. Not only because it is their job, but because these people need to be and feel safe speaking out about their experiences.” Monahan continued, “What precedent does it set when sexual predators are made to pay for the trauma and dehumanization they've enacted with mere essays and suspensions?” Incidents of sexual violence do not exist in isolation and are indeed a part of a wider systemic problem. Juleea Berthelot of the Freedom Road Socialist Organization spoke to the Republican-led effort to roll back Title IX protections. “The rollbacks put in place are being used to protect the status quo as it exists. The ruling makes it impossible for there to be a real legal pathway to hold fraternities accountable for perpetrating sexual assault on campus and lets rapists know they can commit their crimes with little to no accountability,” Berthelot said. Berthelot continued, “The rollback lets schools get off the hook for refusing to come to the aid of victims. It defends rich and powerful students from even being accused of rape by demoralizing those who come forward.” Berthelot finished their speech by reminding the crowd that “more people are becoming conscious of the rotten corruption and injustice allowed on campuses,” and “the struggle for socialism will only intensify as more people in the United States are forced to realize it is the only way to truly end rape culture and anti-LGBTQ attacks on campus and in our communities.” The rally concluded with the final demand to convict the Cornell 57 and for justice for all survivors. # NewOrleansLA # LA # StudentMovement # SDS # LUNO # WomensMovement # SexualViolence # LGBTQ

title: FBI attempts to question immigrant rights activists in Provo, Utah
author: fightbacknews.org
content: Provo, UT – On October 23, FBI agent Mitchell Kutterer knocked on the door of Venna Burkhardt, a leader of the grassroots organization People of Provo Against ICE (PoPAI). Burkhardt was not home at the time, but her roommate confirmed that she lived there. The FBI gave the roommate an information card with the name and number of the agent but was unsuccessful in getting the roommate to answer other questions. The agent was not let inside. Burkhardt stated of the encounter, “Where’s my freedom of speech?” On the same day, activist Collin Grannis had his door knocked on by FBI agent Nick Zollinger and his partner. His roommate answered the door. The roommate got the contact information from them, and the pair of agents left. Then later, after the visit to Grannis’ apartment, Chase Barrett arrived home to find a pair of agents sitting inside. His parents had let them in before he was around. Grannis states, “As a result of my involvement with the local grassroots movement People of Provo Against ICE, I was approached by two FBI agents at my home.” The FBI’s investigations into People of Provo Against ICE are meant to intimidate activists. Protesting is not a crime, and PoPAI will not stop fighting back against ICE. Chrisley Carpio, of the Committee to Stop FBI Repression states, “Activists should not talk to the FBI. We need to meet them with a wall of silence.” # ProvoUT # UT # InJusticeSystem # PoliticalRepression # FBI # StopFBI # CSFR # ImmigrantRights # Featured

title: Twin Cities Coalition for Justice statement on charges filed for the murderer of Allison Lussier
author: fightbacknews.org
content: Fight Back News Service is circulating the following statement from the Minnesota-based Twin Cites Coalition for Justice. Yesterday, October 22, 2026, Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty announced she is charging Chuck Foss with second-degree murder in the 2024 killing of Allison Lussier. This announcement comes two-and-a-half years after Allison’s body was found in her apartment. Two-and-a-half years of Allison’s family, community and local organizers fighting for answers. Two-and-a-half years of press conferences, rallies, meetings with police and city leadership, court hearings, and gaslighting from the mayor and the chief of police. Two-and-a-half years of Allison’s family being retraumatized by having to convince people in power that her life mattered. That her death was worthy of investigation and that her murderer should be held accountable. There would be no opportunity for justice for Allison today without the tireless advocacy of her aunt, Jana Williams, and community organizers who have fought to make sure Allison’s name continues to be uplifted. Allison’s family and the Minneapolis community have been lied to continuously by the Minneapolis Police Department. Disgraced former Police Chief Brian O’Hara said publicly that Allison died from a drug overdose, with substantial evidence available to the contrary. The city auditor’s report showed that the MPD didn’t even bother to request an autopsy report before spreading false information and victim-blaming Allison for her own murder. In fact, the autopsy wasn’t requested at all until the city auditor requested it themself. The announcement simply confirms what Allison’s family and community already knew. If MPD had properly investigated this murder when it happened, Allison’s family could have been spared the trauma of seeing their loved one’s name dragged through the mud. Her community wouldn’t have had to do the prosecutors’ jobs for them by finding witnesses and collecting evidence to create a chargeable case. “it’s been a long two years. You know what? Can I rest and relax tonight? Probably not, because there’s a bigger system here that needs attention,” said Jana Williams, aunt of Allison Lussier The lack of accountability in this case demonstrates yet again that we cannot depend on the mayor to hold the police accountable. We need real mechanisms of accountability. No more toothless review boards, no more city audits that the police can refuse to participate in. This is why we are fighting for community control of the police through an all elected Civilian Police Accountability Commission. Victims of intimate partner violence like Allison Lussier and Mariah Samuels deserve to be believed when they call for help. They deserve to be protected. And when, tragically, their lives are stolen, they deserve justice. # MinneapolisMN # MN # InjusticeSystem # OppressedNationalities # Indigenous # AllisonLussier # PoliceAccountability # TCC4J

title: ASAP group gathers substitute teachers for town hall
author: fightbacknews.org
content: New York, NY – On October 21, the Alliance of Substitutes and Paraprofessionals (ASAP) held a Substitute Teacher Townhall, where over 25 substitutes and others within the United Federation of Teachers gathered on Zoom. The town hall heard from substitutes and former subs in the NYC Department of Education on what issues they have faced in their workplaces that could be turned into a campaign by ASAP. ASAP is a group of militant substitute teachers, paraprofessionals and teachers in the UFT who are developing campaigns around the most underserved and underpaid groups within the NYC Department of Education. Subs on the call discussed long-term substitute assignments, withholding pay, lack of clarity on the job, as well as low compensation. One sub teacher on the call said, “I have a lot of concerns come up when I go in to cover a teacher’s parental leave. The job is usually just short of the 30-day mark to make it a [long-term] status, so I don’t get paid the same. There are a lot of grey areas when I get called in for long-term assignments. The schools should be upfront and declare them right away.” Another sub teacher said, “Sometimes the school I work at a lot will call me right before the school day, and because I want to help I will. But then I go look at my check and I see a certain percentage taken out. Your pay gets docked if you go in past 8:00, but they’re the ones that asked me to come in. I’m doing them a favor, and it’s the same percentage taken out for the entire day even if you’re there a few minutes after 8:00!” The ASAP organizers will be taking back what was learned from the Sub Town Hall and building a campaign. Joe Diodato from ASAP stated, “Coming away from the call, one common thread was that subs are tired of being exploited, especially as it relates to long-term jobs. We're going to plan out a campaign that is grounded in what we heard tonight, bring more and more subs into the fold, and make sure that the city knows we're going to fight for long-term sub rights and everything else that we can.” # NewYorkNY # NY # Labor # UFT # Teachers # ASAP

title: St. Paul educators fight back against plan for mid-year cuts
author: fightbacknews.org
content: St. Paul, MN – Hundreds gathered at the Saint Paul Public Schools District Administration Building on Tuesday, October 21 to protest proposed mid-year budget cuts. The cuts would hit English Language Learner students and their families the hardest and would mean over a dozen English Language (EL) teachers across the district would have their positions terminated. The Saint Paul Federation of Educators (SPFE) called to rally immediately before the school board meeting where voting was to take place on the proposed cuts. SPFE requested community members to stay for the meeting and make their voices heard in the public comment section. Community member and immigrant Belquis Rivera reminded the crowd of the importance of EL teachers during ICE’s Operation Metro Surge, “I am a working mother. And in this past year, there has been much adversity to immigrants in this country. The teachers that are being cut made it possible for us to live last year, for immigrant families to live last year. And while there is so much racism in this country, we escaped countries that were dangerous, where there was real risk. And this teacher put herself at risk to make sure that my family had what they needed to live.” “I grew up in a small village in Somalia, and came here to Saint Paul as a refugee. I went to public school in Saint Paul,” said union-endorsed Saint Paul School Board candidate Omar Syed to thunderous applause. “The language I speak today, these are the educators who taught me! SPPS is already losing immigrant families to charter schools. Cutting educators who help their children succeed risks pushing even more families out of the Saint Paul Public Schools.” Monica Byron, elementary teacher and president of Education Minnesota, condemned the mid-year firing of teachers. “What is happening right now in St. Paul is not normal. Laying off educators, after the year has already started, isn’t just highly unusual. It's unprecedented.” Byron continued: “Our educators have welcomed students into their classrooms. They’ve built relationships. They've created safe, welcoming, learning environments. And now, just weeks into the school year, they're being told their jobs could disappear. Shame. That is not how we support our educators. And it's certainly not how we support our students. Our students deserve better.” The rally moved into the school board meeting, where coordinated chanting forced the board to allow a hugely extended public comment section that lasted around five hours. The board moved unanimously to postpone the vote until the week of October 26 so that more engagement and other options can be explored. Follow SPFE for action items and rally times to continue this fight. # StPaulMN # MN # Labor # Teachers # SPFE # JobCuts

title: Chicago activists host town hall on the campaign to end police and ICE collaboration
author: fightbacknews.org
content: By Ash P and Gio Araujo Chicago, IL – On October 14, over 50 Chicagoans gathered at Casa Michoacan in the Pilsen neighborhood for a town hall meeting on the ongoing campaign to end collaborations between the Chicago Police Department and federal agents. This town hall, organized by the Immigrant Rights Working Committee of the Chicago Alliance Against Racist and Political Repression (IRWC of CAARPR), served as both a celebration of the progress that has been made on the campaign and as an open discussion of how to move forward. This town hall comes after a recent victory in the IRWC’s campaign. After a year of pressure and mobilization at the Community Commission for Public Safety and Accountability’s (CCPSA , the city’s police accountability board) monthly meetings, a resolution was passed by the commission to hold special quarterly hearings regarding how CPD implements and enforces the Welcoming City Ordinance. This win signifies a new phase in this campaign. Louise Carhart opened up the discussion addressing the basis to the campaign, stating, “A lot of people were very upset because they had seen their communities torn apart by ICE in the preceding months, and had seen very little action on any CPD collaborations that had taken place.” She continued, “The CCPSA would be where that accountability starts, given their position at the top of the accountability bureau in Chicago. After that, there wasn’t a lot of follow up from the CCPSA, despite repeated community outcry about this issue, despite increasing reports of CPD and ICE collaboration.” Omar Flores, a leading member of the IRWC, and someone who has been on the ground to document police collaboration, talked about how CPD escalated confrontations between federal agents and community members. Flores stated, “A lot of CPD’s justifications to how they respond to these situations and why they do ‘crowd control’ is because they say they’re there to calm the situation. But any of us who have been in the movement for any amount of time, or even just in communities that police tend to arrest, know that they are not de-escalators. They are escalators, that is their whole goal. To go in there and make the situation worse.” A member of Pilsen Unidos por Nuestro Orgullo (PUNO) spoke up during the discussion, “We have seen in the last month or so instances where there have been known ICE vehicles in police-only areas. This is something that we also will have to go to the CCPSA and COPA [Civilian Office for Police Accountability] you know, to raise the alarm.” They referred to instances where ICE agents have used CPD parking lots as staging grounds for raids. Investigations into these events are currently underway, and the struggle against police collaboration is growing across the city. It has become a major criteria to the selection of the next Chicago Police Department superintendent. The campaign is far from over, and the IRWC is ready to mobilize for meetings and to the streets. # ChicagoIL # IL # ImmigrantRights # ICE # CPD # OppressedNationalities

title: Out of Africa protest for the International Month of Action against AFRICOM
author: fightbacknews.org
content: Minneapolis, MN – On October 17, the U.S. Out of Africa committee of Women Against Military Madness held its first protest at Mayday Plaza in the Cedar Riverside neighborhood. The protest was part of the International Month of Action against AFRICOM, a month of actions focused on the withdrawal of U.S. military from Africa and bringing an end to U.S. involvement in African wars. AFRICOM is the U.S. military command that focuses on for Africa. Protesters rallied in the predominantly East African neighborhood with signs that said, “Shut down AFRICOM” and “End U.S. drone strikes.” The neighborhood gave them a friendly response with honks and waves. Lina Jebara, a member of the US Palestinian Community Network, spoke about the connection between U.S. imperialism in Africa and Israel’s genocide in Palestine and about how the Minneapolis Honeywell plan is contributing to these atrocities. Jebara stated, “Today, we’re seeing the oppression of African countries subject to U.S. imperialist aggression converging and aligning with the oppression faced in the Middle East. The MQ-9 Reaper drone is yet another example that proves that the tools used by U.S. imperialism are one in the same, built and honed from centuries of plundering, colonizing and occupying nations.” Honeywell makes the engines and navigational components for the MQ-9 Reaper drones used by Israel in its genocide of Gaza and by the U.S. in Somalia and Nigeria. Honeywell produces Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs), a navigational component for the MQ-9 Reaper drones, at its navigation lab and production plant in northeast Minneapolis. Protesters demanded an end to Trump’s racist war on Somalia. Trump has escalated U.S. air war in Somalia, increasing U.S. drone strikes and civilian casualties. Donald Trump has so far bombed Somalia 215 times in his second term as president and 434 times total. President Trump has bombed Somalia more than all the other presidents combined in the 20 years that the U.S. has been at war in Somalia. Domestically, Trump is also engaged in a racist hate campaign against Somali people, and has called Somali people “garbage,” “low-IQ”, and “bad people,” and said that Somalia was “barely a country.” Trump has repeatedly attacked the Somali community in Minneapolis, using ICE during Operation Metro Surge to target Somali neighborhoods and most recently using ICE to raid Congresswoman Ilhan Omar’s Washington DC house as part of the attempt to revoke her citizenship. Speakers from Black Lives Matter Minnesota and the Twin Cities Coalition for Justice highlighted the connections between the U.S. intervention in Africa and police militarization, racist police violence, and mass incarceration here in the U.S. Alissa Washington, the founder of the Wrongfully Incarcerated & Over-sentenced Families Council-MN, talked about the importance of international solidarity, stating, “Our experiences are different, but they compel us to stand together. We want an end to the killing and exploitation of Black people, wherever it happens. If I want people to care about my family, I have a responsibility to care about families in Palestine, in Sudan, in Congo, in Somalia, and across the whole continent of Africa.” The U.S. Out of Africa committee is a new committee in Women Against Military Madness. The organization calls for the abolition of AFRICOM, withdrawal of U.S. bases, and an end to U.S. drone strikes in Africa. The U.S. Out of Africa committee is working alongside the Minnesota Anti-War Committee on a campaign to stop Honeywell from producing weapon components in Minneapolis. # MinneapolisMN # MN # AntiWarMovement # International # Africa # AFRICOM # WAMM # USPCN

title: At No Kings, Colorado Springs FRSO calls for joining an organization
author: fightbacknews.org
content: Colorado Springs, CO – On Saturday, October 17, Freedom Road Socialist Organization (FSRO) members tabled at the fourth national No Kings protest in Colorado Springs, where hundreds gathered in Acacia Park and around City Hall. Genevieve Richard, an organizer with FRSO who tabled at the event, states, “As bad as Trump is, he is ultimately a symptom of the broken system we find ourselves in. We've been fighting against capitalism long before Trump showed up, and we'll continue fighting once he's gone. We understand that we need socialism, and we need a party to get there.” The FRSO table encouraged people to vote no on Colorado ballot measures 134 and 135, which would strip rights from transgender people, as well as no on ballot measure 81, which would increase collaboration between ICE and local law enforcement. Brandon Rincon, another FRSO organizer who tabled at the event, states, “Socialists need to stand with the people when they stand up against reactionary attacks. We need a united front of all who can be united so we can fight back. We want to help illuminate the path forward for all those who are fed up with our current system and what’s happening around us but aren’t sure what to do about it.” October 17 reportedly saw No Kings protests in over 2500 cities and towns across the country; all focused on opposing Trump’s agenda. # ColoradoSpringsCO # CO # FRSO # NoKings # PeoplesStruggles

title: Portland City Council candidates questioned on ICE at Immigration Town Hall
author: fightbacknews.org
content: Portland, OR – On the evening of October 19, 150 people attended an immigrant rights-centered town hall meeting with Portland City Council candidates. Candidates running for city council in Districts 3 and 4 were invited to participate and present their position on questions of immigration, the police, sanctuary policy, and the Macadam ICE facility in South Portland. The candidates in attendance included incumbents Mitch Green, Tiffany Koyama Lane, Angelita Morillo, and new candidates such as Dr. Esther Leon, Tom Sollitt, Jamey Evanstar, Eli Arnold and Jeremy Beausoleil Smith. Immigrant rights organization Portland Contra Las Deportaciones hosted the event. In the opening statement, Taylor Goss, a member of PDXCD stated, “This town hall is so important because it affords us the opportunity to elect councilors who are willing to be bold, and fight with us to defeat Trump’s attacks. We need action now to shut down the facility and stop the terrorizing of immigrants in Portland!” PDXCD is in the midst of a campaign to shut down the Portland ICE facility that operates under a permit approved by Portland City Council in 2011. They’ve held many actions demanding city council take action to shut down the facility and had sparred with some of the incumbents at the town hall in the past. The demand to shut down the facility resonated with many in attendance, receiving applause and cheers. When asked about the mayor’s response to the ICE surge, candidate Jeremy Smith scrutinized the lack of action from Mayor Keith Wilson on shutting down the facility. Another question asked about the city council’s response to ICE, to which some non-incumbents replied that council should have done more. Dr. Esther León echoed the demand to revoke the ICE facility permit, stating that the city should have already shut it down. León added that the current council’s capitulation to Trump does not keep Portland safe from his attacks, but in fact, lays the groundwork for further federal overreach. One line of questioning asked about existing law and if city council has the obligation and responsibility to change it if it is no longer working. Candidate Tom Sollitt responded, “if the [laws/code] made sense in the past, but we see in the moment when things don’t work out, there is an obligation to make change. The lack of desire to enforce the facility impact fee and action from the mayor and executive branch, city council should continue moving forward with proposals even if it includes a proposal to revoke [the ICE facility’s] permit.” Moderators also inquired about the ways councilors can fight for immigrant rights outside public office, and the police’s role in ICE activity as well as their activity against immigrant rights protesters. Cami Saunders asked a question about the use of police to forcefully remove protesters from city hall, saying “Members of our organization have been violently removed from city hall by the Portland police when no one was being harmed. Do you condemn that use of the Portland police?” Mitch Green, a sitting councilor during many forceful removals of protesters, stated that the police should not be used to “remove the people from the people’s house,” and subsequently condemned the use of the police in that manner. The rest of the candidates, including other incumbents who allowed the police to eject protesters, unanimously aligned with Green and condemned it. “I’m confused by Mitch Green’s response,” Saunders said after the event. “He condemned the use of police to kick out protesters from city hall, yet he was a part of the group of councilors that allowed police to be called on us for protesting last year. We need more than statements, and I hope to see this reflected in his actions if he is re-elected.” When asked how she felt about the responses at the town hall, Beatriz Ibarra said, “Some of the excuses that were given about the lack of action on the facility have been said before, such as issues with the mayor, the supremacy clause, as well as the lengthy legal process. These came mainly from the incumbent candidates. It was refreshing to see other candidates take the stand for revoking the permit and show willingness to fight back against Trump's attacks in a bold manner.” Ibarra was one of the many people that have been arrested for protesting outside the ICE facility. In closing out the event, PDXCD urged the attendees to support them in their next action for the revocation of the Macadam ICE facility permit. A hearing on the ICE facility land use violation case is scheduled for November 20. The violation was issued in September of 2025 and has been stalled and appealed every step of the way. Activists demand the judge overseeing the case, Judge Steffan Alexander, stop allowing landowner Stuart Lindquist to delay consequences for human suffering at the facility he leases to ICE. On the topic of the outcome of the event, Stephanie Wilde, one of the main organizers, said, “one of my highlights of the evening had to have been the groups that came out. It gave me such a feeling of camaraderie and togetherness. I spoke with a lot of the groups on just how coming together like this strengthens all of us and strengthens our resolve to keep going.” The event was supported and endorsed from Sunrise Movement PDX, Centennial Education Association, Oregon Working Families Party, Freedom Road Socialist Organization, Knitters Against Fascism, Multnomah Democrats, SW Indivisible Resistance, Portland For Palestine, Shannon Singleton for Multnomah County, Parkrose UCC and Singing Resistance. # PortlandOR # OR # ImmigrantRights # ICE # PDXCD # ICEDetentionCenter

title: AI Agents Reached Anthropic’s Business Systems in Under 12 Hours
author: Krishi Chowdhary
content: AI agents found ways into Anthropic’s internal systems in under 12 hours, security startup says Security startup Cathedral says autonomous AI agents found access paths into Anthropic’s internal business systems in under 12 hours via sales, HR and IT software rather than the Claude model itself. The test was conducted under Anthropic’s authorized vulnerability disclosure program, an arrangement that lets outside researchers test a company’s systems and report what they find. Cathedral, a cybersecurity startup founded months ago by four former staffers of the Department of Government Efficiency, carried out the exercise and disclosed it on October 26, 2026. The way in: ordinary business software The entry point was not Anthropic’s model. Cathedral says the agents exploited unglamorous third-party software every company runs in the background: tools for administration, sales, HR and IT. Once inside, the agents reached employee compensation details, internal communications, meeting transcripts, salary and job-offer information, and Slack messages discussing Anthropic’s advanced models, according to Cathedral’s draft report. That detail is the point for enterprise security teams: the agents did not beat the AI, they beat the procurement stack around it. Every company that buys software from vendors now has the same exposed surface, whether or not it builds models. Anthropic itself has reported similar offensive capability before, saying in November 2025 that Chinese state-sponsored hackers used its Claude Code coding tool to attack roughly 30 organizations, and disclosing in July that Claude models hacked real organizations in three incidents during its own tests. Anthropic disputes the severity Anthropic confirmed that a limited set of sales, HR and IT systems was accessed, but says customer conversations, Claude responses, source code and model weights were never reached. Model weights, the trained parameters of an AI model, are considered a company’s most sensitive AI asset. “Our monitoring flagged some of Cathedral’s activity before they reported it to us, we shut off their access the same day,” an Anthropic representative said. The two sides disagree on more than the timeline. Anthropic says Cathedral overstated the national security implications of the findings and did not disclose all of its testing. Cathedral says data access was kept to the absolute minimum in line with security research best practices. Neither account is independently settled, and Cathedral’s report is still a draft. Which vendors supplied the affected software, and which specific vulnerabilities the agents exploited, have not been named. title: Bitcoin Core Speeds Up Security Fixes as AI Makes Old Bugs Easy to Find
author: Krishi Chowdhary
content: Bitcoin Core changed its security policy on October 22, 2026, so that fixes for easily rediscovered vulnerabilities can be shipped to older release lines within days instead of waiting out a year-long embargo, and the change comes as data from the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology shows 43.6% of sampled Bitcoin Core peers running software that no longer receives patches. The amendment, merged into the project’s site repository as pull request #1281 by developer Antoine Poinsot, ends the practice of holding medium- and high-severity bug details secret until two weeks past the end of life of the last affected release. Under the new policy, a developer can flag a flaw that takes little effort to rediscover, a judgment made during triage and one that explicitly accounts for tools like large language models turning up old bugs again. Once flagged, the fix gets backported to every maintained release line and published with an advisory. Bitcoin Core currently maintains its three newest major lines: 29.x, 30.x and 31.x. Why AI ended the embargo The old policy assumed a latent bug could stay hidden for a year. Large language models undermine that assumption: a flaw that one researcher found in 2024 is a prompt away from being rediscovered by anyone in 2026, so the secrecy window increasingly protects nothing. Poinsot, the policy’s author, wrote on the bitcoindev mailing list that the change trades some caution for speed. “The embargo period achieves little but it delays the availability of a fixed release,” he wrote, adding that under the new policy mitigations “won’t have as much ‘bake time'” in development branches. The case that shaped the policy: CVE-2024-52911, a high-severity use-after-free in block validation, was reported to Bitcoin Core developers in November 2024, fixed in version 29.0 in April 2025, and disclosed on May 5, 2026, about 388 days after the fix. The flaw affected versions from 0.14.0 to before 29.0, and a crafted invalid block could crash a node. The new category has not yet been publicly used for a specific bug as of October 23. Half the sampled network is outside the safety net The timing matters because of who is running what. A KIT network monitor snapshot from October 18 counted 3,671 of 8,422 self-reported Bitcoin Core peers on end-of-life release lines, 43.6% of the sample. The snapshot counted 3,243 peers on 31.x, 712 on 30.x and 635 on 29.x. It covers only public IPv4 and IPv6 peers, so Tor-only and non-listening nodes, plus private infrastructure run by exchanges, custodians and miners, fall outside it. The sample is about to tip. Bitcoin Core maintains three lines, so when version 32.0 ships, 29.x leaves the maintenance window; a frozen sample would push the share of peers outside the safety net past half: 4,306 of 8,422, or 51.1%. As of October 24, the download directory still listed only release candidates and the project’s lifecycle page listed the 32.0 release date as TBA. The release notes also state that details of three medium- or high-severity flaws fixed in version 30.0 will go public two weeks after the new release, the old embargo rule still applying. Version 32.0 brings its own upgrade hazard: it switches the default partially signed Bitcoin transaction format from version 0 to version 2. A user reported on October 14 that wallet files from the new graphical interface failed to import in older Core co-signers in a multisignature setup, and a fix was deferred toward version 32.1; RPC users can request the older format. Operators running older nodes, the same population that already misses patches after end of life on other platforms, face the choice between upgrading and leaving their software exposed. Bitcoin has no central authority to force an upgrade, so the network’s security rests on operators acting on their own. The policy change is written in that spirit: it acknowledges that obscurity no longer protects anyone, and that speed is the trade-off worth making. title: Ethereum Postpones Glamsterdam on Hoodi, Stalling Its 200M Gas-Limit Test
author: Krishi Chowdhary
content: Ethereum core developers postponed the Glamsterdam upgrade on the Hoodi testnet on October 22, pulling the October 26 activation, and its planned gas-limit raise to 200M, off the calendar. The decision came at ACDE #248, the recurring call where Ethereum’s execution-layer client developers make protocol calls, and it was announced on the Ethereum Foundation blog the same day. The stated reason is EIP-8037: developers want more time to investigate how the proposal, one of the components of Glamsterdam, interacts with smart contracts already deployed on Ethereum mainnet. The blog post said the update “supersedes the schedule and activation instructions in the Hoodi testnet announcement.” The 200M gas test is gone for now The postponement removes three things at once: the Amsterdam activation on the execution layer, the Gloas activation on the consensus layer, and the gas-limit schedule that would have lifted Hoodi’s limit to 200M at the same epoch. That last piece was the point of the exercise. Hoodi, a testnet used to rehearse network upgrades before they reach mainnet, was set to run a gas-limit test of roughly 3.3 times the current limit ahead of Glamsterdam. With the activation postponed, the protocol’s scaling validation slips with it, and the 200M target now has no date attached. The mechanics of the rollback are narrow. The change rolls back Hoodi’s configuration for a future upgrade; it does not revert the testnet’s chain history. Client releases tagged for the old schedule, including Lodestar v1.50.1, Besu 26.10.1, Ethrex v30.0.1-rc.2 and Nethermind 2.2.1, remain as release tags for a plan that no longer stands. What it means for the mainnet timeline The announcement concerns Hoodi only. The Ethereum Foundation said it “does not set a Glamsterdam mainnet activation date, and no action is required from Ethereum mainnet users or ETH holders as a result of this update.” A mainnet fork at 200M gas was never scheduled, so nothing mainnet has moved; what has moved is the rehearsal that would have de-risked it. The earlier preview of the Glamsterdam upgrade on Hoodi ran through the ePBS design and the node upgrades the original October 26 date required. The delay also lands amid an unresolved technical question. Two days before the postponement, a Lido engineer warned publicly of a staking deposit hijack risk at Glamsterdam, but the blog post cites only the EIP-8037 investigation, and no official statement connects the two events. No new activation date for Glamsterdam on Hoodi has been set. The post Ethereum Postpones Glamsterdam on Hoodi, Stalling Its 200M Gas-Limit Test appeared first on Techreport .

title: Qubic restarts chain, opens claims after $1.4M weak-seed hack
author: Krishi Chowdhary
content: Qubic restarted its network on October 19 and announced the open claims platform on October 20 after predictable wallet seeds let an attacker drain roughly $1.4 million in QU tokens from 1,404 accounts. The project announced on X that its validator quorum, the Computors, approved the recovery plan, the reclaim platform is open, and the first funds have already gone back to verified owners. The Qubic network is live again. The Computor quorum approved the recovery, the reclaim platform is open, and the first funds have already gone back to verified owners. Here's what's new and what you need to do. pic.twitter.com/2pIM0IfiFB — Qubic (@_Qubic_) October 20, 2026 The root cause sits in the wallet software, not in the chain itself. Qubic said the flaw affected seed phrases generated with its Qubic web wallet on certain Apple devices and browsers: the insecure random-number generator used there could produce predictable seeds, which in turn left the corresponding wallets open to unauthorized token movement. A wallet seed is the secret from which all of a wallet’s keys are derived, so anyone who guesses it effectively owns the account. An attack that guesses seeds does not touch Qubic’s consensus rules, which is why the project rejects describing this as a hack of the protocol. What the network did about it Qubic halted the mainnet on Sunday, October 18, to stop further movement of stolen funds. Its blockchain explorer shows processing resumed at 8:00 pm on October 19, advancing past tick 85,371,949, the point where the network had paused. Qubic released web wallet version 4.26.4 the same day, fixing the seed-generation flaw. Affected users submit a claim through weak-seed-reclaim.qubic.org, with a deadline of May 1, 2027. Recovery rules reported October 22 require ownership checks even on unstolen funds held in vulnerable wallets, a measure some users may contest. What wallet holders should do now Qubic warned that any wallet created with the Qubic web wallet before version 4.26.4 should be treated as insecure, even if no funds ever left it. The team urged users to update to 4.26.4 or later, create a new wallet, move their funds across as soon as possible, and never use the old wallet again. Previous coverage of the mainnet halt reported 87.1% of stolen funds frozen within hours of the exploit. The attack itself echoes a recurring pattern in crypto security , where audits of a protocol offer no protection when the weakness sits in client-side software. title: Webull Puts a Date on Bitcoin Perpetual Futures: US Rollout Begins in November
author: Krishi Chowdhary
content: Webull will roll out Bitcoin perpetual futures to its US clients starting in November, the Nasdaq-listed brokerage said on October 20 in an announcement that puts a date on a product most American retail platforms do not offer. The launch brings perpetual futures to a mass US retail audience. The derivative, which crypto exchanges pioneered, lets traders hold leveraged long or short positions indefinitely, and with about 6 million clients in the United States, Webull is moving a product once confined to offshore venues onto regulated rails. How the product works A perpetual future tracks Bitcoin’s price but never expires, unlike a conventional quarterly futures contract. Traders post margin and can take leveraged positions in either direction. The mechanism that keeps the contract price near spot is the funding rate: periodically, whichever side of the market is overleveraged pays the other. On regulated US venues, the CFTC oversees that clearing and settlement, which is the main difference from offshore exchanges where retail traders currently get most of their perps exposure. Why the date matters US retail access to crypto derivatives has been widening all year. The CFTC approved the first perpetual futures contracts earlier in 2026, with Coinbase and Kalshi among the initial approvals. A Nasdaq-listed retail broker now building its own offering on those same regulated rails is a signal of how quickly the line between fintech and crypto infrastructure is dissolving. What Webull said The company said the November start covers US clients, and that details on the rollout schedule and trading terms are in its announcement . Specific funding rates, margin requirements, and per-contract specs were not itemized in the release. title: CME Group’s 2026 Crypto Expansion Reaches Uniswap’s UNI
author: Krishi Chowdhary
content: Uniswap’s UNI becomes the first DeFi protocol token with futures on CME Group CME Group marked the first trades in its new Uniswap and Bitcoin Cash futures on October 20, 2026, in the announcement of the first trade on its press room. Uniswap called UNI the first DeFi protocol token with futures on the exchange, saying in a post on X : “UNI is now the first DeFi protocol token with futures on @CMEGroup.” The claim is specific to CME: DeFi tokens have long traded as perpetual futures on offshore venues, but none had carried a contract on the US derivatives exchange before. The listing gives institutional traders a regulated, cleared way to hedge or take exposure to UNI without touching a decentralized exchange directly. UNI is now the first DeFi protocol token with futures on @CMEGroup https://t.co/dE0SjToLyR — Uniswap (@Uniswap) October 19, 2026 CME Group confirmed on X that both contracts are officially live, with the inaugural block trade executed between crypto market makers FalconX and GSR. Bitcoin Cash and Uniswap futures contracts are officially live – marked by the inaugural block trade between FalconX and GSR. See the announcement. https://t.co/XaihrqAv4a https://t.co/8mYKNKwtwJ — CME Group (@CMEGroup) October 20, 2026 A year of steady expansion The UNI and Bitcoin Cash listings cap a busy year for CME’s crypto derivatives desk. The exchange has been building out its crypto derivatives suite all year, reportedly adding contracts on Cardano, Chainlink and Stellar in January, and the new listings push the lineup further past its original Bitcoin and Ether core. Chief executive Terry Duffy has also flagged perpetual futures, prediction markets and around-the-clock trading as areas of exchange focus. A block trade, the format CME used to mark the launch, is a privately negotiated derivatives deal executed away from the open market but cleared through the exchange, a common way to open a new contract with a large, known counterparty. That two established crypto market makers, FalconX and GSR, took the first trade points to early institutional liquidity in the contracts. DeFi infrastructure itself has a mixed security record: a study of flash loan attacks found logic exploits drained $1.2 billion from decentralized finance over four years, a reminder that regulated exposure to a protocol token does not remove the protocol’s own risks. A smaller contract for smaller traders Beyond the standard UNI contract, CME Group also lists a Micro UNI futures product, a smaller-sized contract aimed at retail and smaller traders, on its product page . title: 76 minutes to blacklist: how Cysic’s response speed still left 7.2M tokens loose
author: Krishi Chowdhary
content: Cysic froze an address that received an unauthorized mint of 10 million CYS tokens on BNB Smart Chain 76 minutes after the mint, but only about 2.8 million of those tokens were still there, the Cysic Foundation said in an incident report. The mint hit the bridge at 12:31 UTC on Oct. 17, 2026, the Cysic Foundation said in its incident report . The Cysic Foundation added the recipient address to the token contract’s blacklist at 13:47 UTC. At that moment about 2.8 million CYS sat at the address with transfers restricted. The other 7.2 million were no longer at the address, and the foundation said it is tracking where they go. A fast response with partial results Seventy-six minutes was not quick enough to catch most of the tokens. Blacklisting restricts transfers from one address; once tokens move to other addresses, the freeze no longer applies to them. That is the gap the response ran into: the mint, the movement and the blacklist were three separate events, and the attacker used the time in between. The Cysic Foundation said preliminary findings point to unauthorized access to a database supporting the bridge combined with weaknesses in the bridge’s processing logic. It has not confirmed the full attack vector or the root cause, and both are still under evaluation. The company has hired a third-party security firm, which it has not named, and plans a follow-up report after the current investigation phase. What the freeze does not cover The foundation said the incident was limited to bridge message processing and minting, that the mainnet and other operational systems were unaffected, and that no CYS or other assets held in user wallets were stolen or transferred without authorization. The dollar loss is not established: the foundation itself said the number of tokens minted does not determine it, since transfers, swaps and actual losses remain under review. The bridge is offline indefinitely, with no timeline given for its return. The supply math gives the unfrozen tokens their weight: CYS has a maximum supply of 1 billion tokens and roughly 160.8 million were circulating as of Oct. 18, per CoinMarketCap’s token data . If the 7.2 million loose CYS re-enter circulation, they would add about 4.5% to the circulating supply, on top of the 2.8 million already frozen. The incident follows a similar bridge mint exploit at Syscoin in June 2026 and, reportedly, the first notable operational security problem tied to Cysic’s bridge infrastructure. Cysic launched its mainnet and held its CYS token generation event in December 2025. title: Qubic halts mainnet after seed exploit drains 1,404 wallets
author: Krishi Chowdhary
content: An attacker drained 1,404 Qubic user wallets of roughly 2.94 trillion QU tokens, worth about $1.3 million at the time, prompting the network to pause its mainnet on October 18, 2026. A flaw in the wallets, not the chain Qubic’s developers traced the exploit to weak, predictable wallet recovery seeds created on legacy Apple devices, Safari browsers and early iOS applications. A seed is the secret string from which a wallet’s keys are generated; where the generator draws too little randomness, attackers can reproduce the same seeds and the wallets they unlock. The team said the flaw sat outside the network’s code, and it released client version 4.26.4 to fix seed generation. Developers also said they secured additional funds exposed to the same weakness before they could be taken, and that QEARN, the network’s staking feature, was untouched. The attack ran from 23:42 UTC on October 17 to 01:26 UTC on October 18, a window of about one hour and 44 minutes. Validators stopped the chain Qubic’s validators halted the chain at tick 85,371,949 to freeze the stolen tokens. About 87.1% of the drained QU never left the network and is immobilized on-chain, while the remaining 12.9% reached the MEXC exchange, which froze the receiving account within an hour on suspicion it was tied to the attack. The 87.1% figure comes from the most detailed account of the drain ; another outlet covering the story said only that most funds were frozen. MEXC and Bitget both suspended QUBIC deposits and withdrawals on October 18: MEXC said its suspension was requested by the Qubic project team, and Bitget cited wallet maintenance. Whether the 1,404 affected users are reimbursed now rests with Qubic’s validator cluster, and affected users are being told to file police reports. The mainnet restart date on the patched client has not been announced. The incident is the second this year to hit Qubic through a component adjacent to its core, after the Vottun Bridge was exploited in August 2026, and it underlines a risk that reaches past this one network: wallet software that generated weak seeds on older Apple devices and browsers leaves those funds exposed regardless of how sound the chain itself is. title: Ethereum’s Glamsterdam Upgrade Enshrines Proposer-Builder Separation on Hoodi Testnet October 26
author: Krishi Chowdhary
content: Ethereum’s Glamsterdam upgrade will bring proposer-builder separation into the protocol itself when it activates on the Hoodi testnet at epoch 132,352 on October 26, 2026, the Ethereum Foundation announced on October 16 . What EIP-7732 changes EIP-7732, the upgrade’s headline inclusion, writes the split between block proposers and block builders directly into Ethereum’s consensus rules. Today that separation exists only as an out-of-protocol market: a validator proposes a block, specialized builders compete to fill it, and the handoff between the two runs on trusted intermediaries and side agreements that Ethereum itself does not guarantee. Under the enshrined design, the protocol takes over that handoff. A payload timeliness committee attests to whether a builder revealed its block payload and blob data on time, so the network itself verifies that the promised block actually arrived, and when. Glamsterdam is the combined name for two upgrades landing at the same fork: Amsterdam, the execution layer change named after the Devconnect 2022 host city, and Gloas, the consensus layer change named under the protocol’s star-naming convention. EIP-7732 sits on the consensus side. The wider package Proposer-builder separation is the largest of 19 EIPs scheduled for inclusion, tracked by EIP-7773, along with 7 supporting networking and informational EIPs. EIP-7928 adds enforced block-level access lists, a per-block record of the accounts and storage locations a block touched, together with the resulting state changes. That per-block record of every account and storage slot touched is what lets the protocol price state access explicitly. The package also carries smaller quality-of-life changes: logs for ETH transfers, an opcode that returns the current slot, a raised cap on contract size, a factory contract whose address is predictable, and extra instructions for stack manipulation. What it means for validators and builders For validators, enshrined PBS replaces the current trust-based arrangement with a protocol commitment: the committee’s attestation becomes the check on whether a builder delivered. For builders, the rules of engagement move from off-chain deals to consensus-level requirements. For users, the change strengthens censorship resistance, because the network no longer depends on intermediaries outside the protocol to connect those who order transactions with those who build blocks. Hoodi’s gas limit will also rise to 200M at the activation epoch, and every client on both the execution and consensus sides needs an update before the fork. The Ethereum Bug Bounty Program remains active for the Glamsterdam specifications and EIPs. Glamsterdam already activated on Sepolia on October 6. No date for the mainnet fork has been chosen yet.
