title: Apartheid chain of command: ‘I know everything,’ Eugene de Kock tells TRC inquiry
author: Marianne Thamm
content: The man who took the fall for apartheid-era atrocities, former Vlakplaas commander Eugene de Kock, has told the Khampepe Commission of Inquiry into delayed post-TRC prosecutions that while he served 20 years in C-Max, no one in the prosecutorial authority approached him to provide the names, times and dates of those further up the chain of command who gave the orders. The man who bore the weight of moral burden of apartheid-era atrocities and who was sentenced in 1996 by Justice Willem van der Merwe to two life terms, plus 212 years’ imprisonment (to run concurrently), has finally found a platform to tell his truth. De Kock’s appearance on Monday, 26 October, at the Khampepe Commission is a significant moment as the inquiry approaches its scheduled date for wrapping up on 18 December this year. His appearance follows that of former president Thabo Mbeki last week. Meanwhile, it has emerged that the memo of a secret meeting of then president FW de Klerk and his last Cabinet 28 hours before South Africans were set to vote in the country’s first democratic election on 27 April 1994 was only prepared on 4 May that year and signed on the 5th. Eugene de Kock was arrested the day the memo was officially signed off. ‘No one served time but me’ Now 77-years-old, the former torturer, assassin, bomber and supplier of arms to the Inkatha Freedom Party testified that prosecuting the generals who were his superiors would have “exposed the chain of command and those who gave instructions”.  Eugene de Kock, former Vlakplaas commander, arrives to testify before the Khampepe Commission of Inquiry. (Photo: Felix Dlangamandla) “I can explain command structures, operational relationships, requests for assistance, the movement of instructions and covert liaison arrangements. “I can identify where the intelligence or target selection originated outside Vlakpaas. I can explain which senior people approached me and which structures possessed direct knowledge. Decisions and instructions moved through the chain of command and liaison. I am able to identify where the instructions came from and who executed them.” He told the panel that out of all those involved in the violent application of apartheid ideology, “none served a day in a South African prison – except me”. De Kock has waited for this moment for a long time. Eugene de Kock at the Khampepe Commission of Inquiry on 26 October 2026. (Photo: Felix Dlangamandla) ‘They simply never approached me’ In an 18-page affidavit, De Kock, led by veteran advocate Geoff Budlender, recipient of the 2024 George Bizos Human Rights Award, set out that he was the central “operations figure” at Vlakplaas, a farm outside Pretoria along the Hennops River and which served as the secret headquarters for Section C1 (also referred to as C10) of the security police. He said that while the public face of C-Section had been counter-insurgency “rehabilitation” of turned liberation Struggle members, in reality it operated “as a death squad” responsible for extra-judicial killings, kidnappings, interrogations and bombings. Eugene de Kock testified in Gqeberha at the inquest into the killing of the Cradock Four on 23 March 2026. (Photo: Deon Ferreira) He singled out advocate Anton Ackermann, appointed by presidential proclamation by Thabo Mbeki in 2003 to head the Priority Crimes Litigation Unit to prosecute post-TRC matters, for the failure to prosecute the bigger fish in deeper, darker waters. “In order to understand what was stopped and why this happened, it is necessary to understand what was available before 2003, who possessed this evidence, and the prosecutorial strategies. “I was arrested in 1994 and charged with 89 charges including six counts of murder, conspiracy to murder, attempted murder, assault and kidnapping.”  He said that immediately after his sentencing, Ackermann approached him, vowing to use De Kock “to move upward through the chain of command”. However, this had never happened. Once he was safely behind bars and removed from society he was kept at arms’ length. Eugene de Kock at the Khampepe Commission of Inquiry on 26 October 2026. (Photo: Felix Dlangamandla) Was always ready to spill the beans The highly-trained soldier said he had a great deal of information that would have been of relevance to the prosecution of other individuals, including the generals in command as well as the politicians who in turn had instructed them. “However very little attempt was made by advocate Anton Ackermann or Attorney-General advocate Jan d’Oliveira to interview me regarding my knowledge of apartheid-era crimes.” He was already in custody, he said, and was in a position to provide “operational details of the involvement of those personas as part of a cooperation agreement. I have never been reluctant to provide information to prosecuting authorities, however, they simply never approached me.” He rejected suggestions that he might not have been available or was reluctant to provide evidence. Not only did he openly disclose his crimes and submit a 1,000+ page TRC amnesty application, he said, he also testified for the prosecution in the Motherwell bombing trial that resulted in the convictions of Security Branch officials Gideon Nieuwoudt, Wahl du Toit, and Martiens Ras. On 14 December 1989 these senior Security Branch members blew up one of their own colleagues in Motherwell near Gqeberha to conceal their past crimes. ‘Sickened’ Sentencing De Kock in 1996, Judge Willem van der Merwe noted that a “rotten system” enabled the security policemen to perpetrate these human rights violations. He added it was this same system that had approved of De Kock’s actions and helped him to conceal and continue his diabolical work for the state. De Kock told the panel that even though Van der Merwe had explicitly noted at the end of his trial that “there was more than enough evidence to charge General [Krappies] Engelbrecht”, head of the security police, who was a “sweeper” deployed to cover up state-sponsored crimes, he was never held to account.  Engelbrecht was fingered with tampering with evidence in the plane crash that killed then Mozambican president Samora Machel and 24 others on 19 October 1986. Key figures  Key figures De Kock named in his statement to the commission were Colonel Johan Victor who established the Vlakplaas operation in 1979, as well as early commanders Van Heerden, Dirk Coetzee, Jan Coetzee and Colonel “Jac” Cronje. De Kock served as a captain under Cronje before being appointed commanding officer on 1 July 1985. Captain Adrian David Baker was second in command under De Kock and Peter Caselton, an operative based in London funded via laundered secret funds. Vlakplaas hitman Dirk Coetzee. (Photo: Gallo Images / Oryx Media Archive) In the police and security police chain of command he listed Brigadier Willem Schoon, head of C-Section responsible for C1/Vlakplaas activities and who received daily morning operational reports from De Kock at South African Police (SAP) headquarters in Pretoria; General Johann Coetzee, National Head of the Security Police; Major Martin Naudé, head of Section C2, responsible for selecting turned Askaris for regional deployments; Colonel/Brigadier Johannes Petrus Koekemoer, head of the Security Branch national secret fund who instructed financial falsifications and handled bounty payments, Major-General “Krappies” Engelbrecht, senior to De Kock in the chain of command; Major-General Nick van Rensburg, head of the SAP Security Branch who controlled SADF access to Askaris and admitted to extra-judicial killings; Military Intelligence Liaison, Colonel At Nel, second-in-command of the Directorate of Covert Collection (DCC) and Tony Oosthuizen, head of the PAC desk at the DCC. Former minister of law and order Adriaan Vlok during an interview on June 30, 2015, in Pretoria. (Photo: Gallo Images / Rapport / Deaan Vivier) Political leadership In his statement, De Kock explained that while operational officers did not typically interact directly with political leadership as this was a function reserved for police generals, his experience proved that political office-bearers were fully aware of, and directly involved in, state-sanctioned operations “My own experience demonstrates that political office bearers were aware of what was happening and were involved in it.” Minister of law and order (1982-86) Louis le Grange had signed off on the bombing of ANC offices in London, De Kock said, adding “he decorated the people who were involved in this, including me”. A note Adriaan Vlok wrote to Eugene de Kock. Translated, it reads, ‘Dear Eugene, I have sinned against God and you by supporting Apartheid and helping to prop it up and that I used you for this, Please forgive me.’ (Photo: Facebook Eugene de Kock) Adriaan Vlok, deputy minister of law and order (1985-86) and minister of law and order (1986-91) visited Vlakplaas “on many occasions”. “One occasion he came there to congratulate me on the bombing of Khotso House (the offices of the South African Council of Churches) and Cosatu House.” De Kock said Brigadier Schoon had told him that the order to bomb Cosatu House had come “from very high”, meaning then state president PW Botha. De Kock told the commission that prosecuting senior generals would have inevitably implicated the political leaders who issued the orders. He concluded that the failure to prosecute high-ranking officials had been driven by political decisions “to shield those at the top of the chain of command who ultimately benefitted from this protection”. Vlakplaas, a farm 20km west of Pretoria, was the headquarters of the South African Police counterinsurgency unit C10 in the apartheid years. It was commanded by Eugene de Kock and functioned as a paramilitary hit squad. (Photo: Gallo Images / Foto24 / Craig Nieuwenhuizen) The innards of Vlakplaas De Kock told the inquiry that turned former liberation fighters (Askaris) were central to Vlakplaas “death squad” operations as they could easily infiltrate townships and gain trust without raising suspicion. Vlakplaas did not recruit Askaris directly, he noted, saying they were “assigned” after being held under Section 29 of the Internal Security Act (tortured, sometimes for up to two-and-a-half years).  These turned individuals were placed in a moral no-man’s land, as author Jacob Dlamini has so eloquently written in his book Askari. De Kock said Askaris were initially recorded as “Registered Sources”. Later, most were trained and registered as SAPS officers in about 1988/89. Section C2 (headed by Major Martin Naudé) maintained a database of turned individuals and selected Askaris “based on regional language and customs”.  Vlakplaas also maintained photo albums containing thousands of photographs, including copies of every refugee applicant entering Swaziland from South Africa, to identify “operational targets”. When regional Security Branch offices requested C1 operatives, it was Brigadier Schoon who approved deployments, and teams reported to the local commanding officers in those regions. Former Vlakplaas commander Eugene de Kock at the Khampepe Commission of Inquiry on 26 October 2026. (Photo: Felix Dlangamandla) Head money Vlakplaas operated with a monthly standing advance of up to R17,000 (about R650,000 today) managed by De Kock for operational expenses and Askaris’ food and contacts. On instructions from Colonel Johannes Petrus Koekemoer (head of the national secret fund), De Kock created false receipts, claims, and reports to launder money to fund covert operations (such as paying London-based operative Peter Caselton) and parties attended by generals. Cash incentives or “head money, ranging from R1,000 (R40,000) to R7,000 (R280,000) was paid out for the arrest/killing of MK/Apla members or the recovery of weapons (landmines, SAM-7 missiles). Eugene de Kock arrives to testify before the Khampepe Commission of Inquiry on 26 October 2026. (Photo: Felix Dlangamandla) Vlakplaas, he said, maintained “liaison relationships” with other intelligence structures, including the National Intelligence Agency (facilitated by Brigadier Loots) and the SA Defence Force’s Directorate of Covert Intelligence and Directorate of Covert Collection under formal written agreements. De Kock ended his testimony noting that he had mentioned the names of a number of people who were involved in the South African police death squad bombings “and related activities and who gave instructions in this regard. “I am also able to provide information and evidence about a large number of other members of the South African police who were involved in these activities.” DM The post Apartheid chain of command: ‘I know everything,’ Eugene de Kock tells TRC inquiry appeared first on The Namibian .

title: Lula’s comeback in Brazil dents Trump’s ambitions for Latin America
author: Ione Wells
content: “Brazil will not accept being anyone’s backyard,” Brazil’s left-wing President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva declared in his election victory speech, a message squarely aimed at Washington. Domestic elections are rarely won on foreign policy, and this one was no different. But Lula’s defiance against what he has described as US interference in Brazilian affairs evoked a patriotic spirit that proved an effective campaigning tool. It also chimed with his wider brand of politics as a former union leader: standing up to powerful figures. Paradoxically, it seems to have earned him President Donald Trump’s respect. “I like Lula, we get along well,” Trump said, responding to the result. “I didn’t take sides,” he added, before calling the election “terrible” and “rigged”. If that sounds muddled, it is because the relationship between the two men is not straightforward. Trump did not explicitly endorse Lula’s rival Flávio Bolsonaro, who has refused to recognise the result despite the Supreme Electoral Court finding no evidence of irregularities and his own party recognising the result. But Trump was a close ally of Flávio’s father, the former President Jair Bolsonaro. When I spoke to Lula at his residence about a year ago, relations had hit rock bottom. He told me he had “no relationship” with Trump, that they had never spoken, and that he had no intention of picking up the phone. Trump had recently imposed punitive tariffs on Brazil, largely as a political response to Jair Bolsonaro’s coup trial, which the US president called a “witch-hunt” . Rather than tiptoeing around Trump, as some US allies did, Lula fought back – and it paid off. He made fiery speeches invoking Brazilian sovereignty, attacked US interference in the judicial process, and took to wearing a blue cap reading “Brazil belongs to Brazilians”. His approval ratings jumped. He accused the Bolsonaro family, who had lobbied for the tariffs, of being unpatriotic – a blow to a political right that so often claims patriotism as its terrain. Even some in the agricultural lobby, typically strong Bolsonaro supporters but reliant on US trade, thought Lula had a point. The US eventually backed down and reduced the tariffs, although they have since risen again. Relations then improved. The two men spoke at the United Nations and later met in the Oval Office, where Trump called the talks “very good” and Lula said he left “very satisfied”. Another indication, perhaps, that Trump likes a strongman. So why might Trump be unhappy with the result? Latin America has swung to the right, with Ecuador, Chile, Colombia, Argentina and Peru all electing presidents closely aligned with the Trump administration. Trump has sought to use these allies to establish US dominance in the Western Hemisphere, a strategy he has dubbed the “Donroe Doctrine”. Christopher Sabatini, senior fellow for Latin America at Chatham House, notes that Trump thought Brazil would be the “10th and biggest prize” after Flávio Bolsonaro won the first round. Brazil is Latin America’s largest economy, and the younger Bolsonaro was expected to join Trump’s “Shield of Americas” coalition against narco-trafficking. Brazil also holds the world’s second-largest reserves of rare earth minerals after China, and the US had been eyeing preferential access. The relationship has thawed, but with four more years ahead for Lula, several issues could reignite tensions. Brazil accused the US earlier this year of trying to cast doubt on its electoral system and denied visas to two state department officials planning to visit. The US called this “baseless” and revoked the Brazilian ambassador’s visa in response. If Trump keeps calling this result “rigged”, further diplomatic fallout is likely. Lula has also vehemently opposed US military action in the region, from the seizure of Nicolás Maduro in Venezuela to the bombing of alleged drug-trafficking vessels. He lambasted Washington for designating Brazil’s two major gangs as terrorist organisations after lobbying from Flávio Bolsonaro, and warned of attacks on Brazilian sovereignty. It is a sensitive subject for a political left that remembers the region’s brutal 20th Century dictatorships, many backed by the CIA in the name of stopping communism. Then there is US tech. Lula’s campaign accused Meta of favouring Flávio Bolsonaro. Meta denied this but admitted moderation issues and technical errors had wrongly removed some posts or limited their reach. Lula’s supporters responded by sharing his messages through a 10-million-strong WhatsApp group to bypass the algorithms. Separately, the Trump administration is unhappy with Pix, Brazil’s instant payment system, which has boosted the economy, but which the US sees as taking business from Visa and Mastercard. The relationship has exposed political divisions. In the campaign, Bolsonaro supporters waved US flags at their rallies and, in one case, an inflatable saying “Trump Nuke Brazil”, while Lula and his supporters accused Flávio Bolsonaro of protecting US interests over Brazil’s. Still, tensions can be overstated. The US remains Brazil’s second-biggest trading partner after China, and for now the two leaders get on. Whether that lasts will depend on how far the US tries to intervene in Brazilian affairs, and how bullish Lula is in response. – BBC The post Lula’s comeback in Brazil dents Trump’s ambitions for Latin America appeared first on The Namibian .

title: Algeria to send troops to Niger in first foreign deployment since 1973
author: Ondiro Oganga
content: Algeria is to send troops to Niger in its first foreign deployment since sending forces to Egypt during the Arab-Israeli war in 1973. The deployment follows a visit to Algiers by Niger’s defence minister, as the country seeks support against armed groups, some of which are linked to al-Qaeda or Islamic State. Algeria has economic interests in Niger, including a planned gas pipeline that would carry Nigerian gas through Niger to Algeria. The troops are expected to protect energy facilities in northern Niger, near the Libyan border. The deployment comes as the two neighbours rebuild ties after a diplomatic rift in 2025, when Niger recalled its ambassador to Algiers. Algeria’s upper house of parliament held an emergency session on Sunday to vote on the proposed deployment. According to AFP news agency, 148 of the 174 senators voted in favour. It was later backed by the lower house of parliament. However, the timing and number of soldiers to be deployed have not been announced. The move would mark the first use of a 2020 constitutional provision allowing overseas military deployments and a significant shift in Algeria’s long-standing policy against sending forces abroad. “We are not sending our soldiers to wage war in Niger, but for a mission to secure economic infrastructure,” Algerian senator Belkacem Boulghiti told reporters after the vote. Algeria’s state-owned energy company, Sonatrach, has also signed an agreement with Niger’s petroleum ministry to explore for oil in the Kafra region. Two exploration wells are estimated to contain 168 million and 100 million barrels, respectively, Reuters reported. Relations between Algeria and Niger have not always been smooth in recent years. Algeria condemned the 2023 coup that ousted Niger’s elected President, Mohamed Bazoum, and brought Gen Abdourahamane Tchiani to power. Tensions rose again in 2025 after Algeria shot down a Malian drone near its border. Niger recalled its ambassador to Algiers in solidarity with Mali, a close ally which is also under military rule. Relations have since improved. Tchiani visited Algeria in February 2026, and in late August, President Abdelmadjid Tebboune sent fighter jets to Niger to help suppress a coup attempt and also donated four military helicopters. – BBC The post Algeria to send troops to Niger in first foreign deployment since 1973 appeared first on The Namibian .

title: More than 60 Christians killed in Ethiopia ‘massacre’, church official says
author: Ondiro Oganga
content: More than 60 people have been killed in a series of attacks on Christians in Ethiopia’s Oromia region, according to the country’s Orthodox Church. One resident, whose 75-year-old father was killed, described it as an ambush. “We were completely unprepared and had no prior knowledge. They surrounded us from all four directions,” he told BBC Amharic. The regional government said that it would take action against those responsible. A local official blamed the attacks on a newly formed rebel coalition, the Alliance for Survival, which includes the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA). The OLA has not commented but has denied carrying out previous such attacks. A statement from the Holy Synod of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church said that 20 houses were burnt to the ground in the attacks. It did not say who was responsible. Eyewitness told BBC Amharic that five of those killed were children. A church official described the attacks on three areas in the Shirka district as a “massacre”, saying security forces arrived at the scene but were unable to stop the assault. Many residents have now fled the area. Condemning the violence, the Orthodox Church said attacks against Christians had been increasing recently, and that “such actions undermine the country’s values of mutual respect and peaceful coexistence”. In a statement posted on Facebook, the Orthodox Church said it had repeatedly raised concerns about insecurity with authorities at different levels of government, but that “so far there has been no solution”. The Ethiopian Human Rights Council, a non-governmental organisation, said in a report released in July 2026 that 458 people had been killed in attacks in that area over the previous four years. But this is one of the most deadly attacks in that period. The report said armed groups had repeatedly targeted local communities, particularly followers of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, in what it described as religiously motivated attacks. The government has previously blamed the OLA for the attacks, with Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed saying violence targeting civilians and religious institutions was part of a plan to destabilise the country. The group, which says it is fighting for greater rights for the Oromo people, denies these allegations. Previous reports have also documented attacks against Muslims in the area. Residents who spoke to the BBC on various occasions have described the violence as both ethnic and religious in nature. About two-thirds of Ethiopians are Christians, mostly Orthodox, while one third are Muslim. – BBC The post More than 60 Christians killed in Ethiopia ‘massacre’, church official says appeared first on The Namibian .

title: Kane beats Yamal and Mbappe to taste Ballon d’Or glory
author: AFP
content: Harry Kane became England’s first Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years in his native city of London on Monday, beating Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe. Alexia Putellas claimed the women’s prize for a third time to extend Spain’s domination of the award, thanks to her role in leading Barcelona to last season’s Champions League before moving to London City Lionesses. The first ever Ballon d’Or ceremony on English soil got off to an inauspicious start as the London traffic caused a delay of nearly an hour, with many of the star names arriving late. But there was a happy ending for the hometown hero as Kane collected the crowning glory of his career to date, becoming the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001. The 33-year-old Bayern Munich forward struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double. He also scored six times as England finished third at the World Cup. “I love to represent my country and to bring this trophy back to them and have an English winner I think is something that’s really, really special, especially here in London,” Kane told AFP. “What a crazy night and I’m really, really happy.” Despite being England and Tottenham’s all-time record goalscorer, Kane’s medal collection is limited to German domestic triumphs. He was on the losing side for Spurs in the 2019 Champions League final against Liverpool and twice tasted bitter defeat in the final of the European Championship with England. But joining Bayern in 2023 and his remarkable goalscoring consistency have earned him the highest individual award in football. “Making the move to Bayern Munich was a big step in my career,” Kane told AFP earlier. “Some people saw it as a risk but for me it was always about improving and seeing if I could get better around the team-mates, the team, the club and it has pushed me onto another level. “Being a number nine for Bayern and England you are expected to score goals and to do that the number of times I did last year is something I’m really proud of,” he added. – Putellas back on top – The winner in 2021 and 2022, Putellas’s third Ballon d’Or caps her return to the top of the women’s game after an anterior cruciate ligament injury derailed her rise four years ago. Putellas succeeds Spain team-mate Aitana Bonmati, the winner the past three years whose season was quashed by a leg break. “This is a consequence of all that we achieved last season,” said Putellas. “I am really grateful for having been (at Barcelona) 14 seasons as a player, it is something incredible. It was like a perfect story.” Yamal made the boldest fashion statement of the contenders with a pink flower on the front of his black suit. The Barcelona winger scooped up the first award of the night for young talent of the year for the third consecutive time. But the 19-year-old fell short of becoming the youngest ever Ballon d’Or winner, finishing third, after he failed to produce his best form during Spain’s World Cup success. Mbappe finished second but his wait to win the Ballon d’Or goes on despite being the top scorer in the World Cup, Champions League and La Liga as his goals did not lead to collective triumphs for France or Real Madrid. Luis de la Fuente beat out Paris Saint-Germain’s Luis Enrique and Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta to be named men’s coach of the year after leading Spain to World Cup glory. “This is recognition for a job very well done over many years,” De la Fuente told AFP. “I believe Spanish football, both in terms of coaching and the game itself, serves as an example of excellent youth development, which ultimately paves the way for future success.” Barcelona’s Pere Romeu scooped the prize for women’s coach of the year. Paris Saint-Germain missed out on any of the main individual awards despite winning a second consecutive Champions League, but did have the consolation of men’s club of the year. Spanish duo Unai Simon and Cata Coll were named best men’s and women’s goalkeeper. The post Kane beats Yamal and Mbappe to taste Ballon d’Or glory appeared first on The Namibian .

title: Fake news alert
author: Staff Reporter
content: A social media post claiming The Namibian reported that farmer Koos Brandt and his wife were attacked at their farm is fake. The Namibian confirms that the post did not come from the newspaper. Brandt confirmed to The Namibian that a robbery took place at his farm but said he was out of the country at the time. The newspaper urges the public not to share the fake post and to read the full report in Friday’s edition. The Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) warned last year about the spread of false information on social media. Through its Namibia Fact Check project, the institute found that artificial intelligence (AI)and WhatsApp played a major role in spreading misinformation during Namibia’s 2024 presidential and National Assembly elections. IPPR media lead Frederico Links said social media platforms were used to spread false claims and attack political leaders. At the time, IPPR director Graham Hopwood warned that AI was increasingly being used to create fake images and clone voices to mislead the public. title: ||Kharas farmers fear FMD restrictions will cost jobs
author: Ellen Albertz
content: Farmers in the ||Kharas region say foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) restrictions are threatening their businesses, markets and jobs, and are urging authorities to allow supervised livestock movement from unaffected farms. Farmer Johan Blaauw says the government should consider allowing farmers to move livestock to abattoirs under veterinary supervision so they can continue selling their animals and protect their financial viability, markets and employees’ livelihoods. The farmers made the remarks after stakeholders in the ||Kharas Region gathered at Keetmanshoop for an information session on FMD in the region with veterinary officials from the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Land Reform. “Veterinary officials do not have answers for us on when the livestock movement and slaughtering ban will be lifted, or even lifted partially for farms not affected by FMD and not located within the identified zone where FMD was discovered. “We do not have that luxury. We have to move towards retrenching people now. I’m spending at least N$50 000 a day while I am not making any income, and to make matters worse, the future is uncertain,” Blaauw says. He says animals can be moved from feedlots to abattoirs for slaughter after testing and under veterinary supervision, before the meat products are delivered to the businesses they supply. “I still have 300 cows in the kraals. I supply butcheries with meat at Lüderitz, Rosh Pina, Oranjemund and other places. I am about to lose those markets that I’ve developed over the years. Something has to happen so I can save my business,” Blaauw says. He employs about 50 people across the feedlot, abattoir and butchery, whom he would have to give one month’s notice before retrenchment. Wikus Swiegers says talks about markets are being misunderstood by veterinary officials. Swiegers owns a piggery business that supplies the local market. He says local farmers do not rely solely on markets such as the European Union (EU), South Africa and Botswana. “Piggeries do not export at all to foreign markets. We supply to a local market. In fact, when we cannot supply the local market, we import. But the officials talk as if the EU is the only market that has to be waited out, protocols followed and trade resumed with,” Swiegers says. He says the situation varies from one local business to another and that the government should assess each business individually and make decisions to ease the turmoil facing the meat industry. “I have businesses that I supply in Windhoek with pork. I’m losing those markets now because I can’t supply them anymore and other businesses are supplying them,” Swiegers says. ||Kharas governor Dawid Gertze has raised concerns about subsistence communal farmers. “My heart is bleeding for these farmers. Imagine communal farmers, who, every month sell,about five to six small livestock just to make ends meet. How are they coping?” he says. Natangwe Amuthenu from veterinary services says the entire ||Kharas region has been declared an FMD control area and that domestic movement of all live cloven-hoofed animals (cattle, sheep, goats, pigs, and game) into, out of, or within this region remains entirely suspended. Amuthenu noted that the Directorate of Veterinary Services is actively executing a plan to divide the traditionally FMD-free zone into smaller, localised containment zones using game fences to completely isolate the outbreak pockets. “We are aware that red meat industry bodies (such as the Namibia Agricultural Union) are currently petitioning veterinary authorities for highly controlled, bio-secure direct transit routes from uninfected commercial farms straight to designated abattoirs, but we do not know how long this will take to be approved,” Amuthenu says. title: Ngurare raises alarm over alleged Psemas fraud
author: Martin Endjala
content: Prime minister Elijah Ngurare has alleged a cartel involving doctors and scheme insiders may be exploiting the Public Service Employees Medical Aid Scheme (Psemas), as the government seeks an additional N$535 million to fund the medical aid scheme. The allegations have raised fresh questions about oversight and accountability within the medical aid scheme, as the government moves to address what finance minister Ericah Shafudah has described as an unsustainable funding model. Ngurare alleged that a network of individuals could be working together to exploit the scheme, warning that authorities were keeping a close eye on suspected irregularities. “It cannot be that already, as we speak, N$4 billion has been used just on Psemas, and that cartel seems to be working very well. It seems somebody is working hand in hand with doctors to overclaim,” Ngurare alleged. He said he would issue a statement in due course to respond to concerns surrounding Psemas and the alleged dubious dealings, adding that the government was monitoring the situation and working to address the problems. The allegations come as Shafudah announced additional funding for Psemas during last week’s midterm budget review for the 2026/27 financial year. Of the proposed additional N$665 million under the Ministry of Finance, N$535 million is earmarked to meet Psemas funding requirements, while N$130 million will replenish the contingency fund. The adjustment increases the total national budget appropriation from N$87.9 billion to N$88.6 billion. Shafudah said the government had successfully completed the first phase of the Psemas reform programme through the establishment of a governance council, the introduction of a benefits cap and changes to member contribution structures. Although these measures have strengthened governance, she acknowledged that concerns raised by members were still being addressed. “The government will accelerate more reforms to the Psemas, as the current model has been assessed to be fiscally unsustainable,” Shafudah said. She added that the government remained concerned about allegations of fraud and abuse within the scheme and was taking steps to strengthen oversight, improve accountability and protect public resources. Meanwhile, Landless People’s Movement deputy chief whip Eneas Emvula questions the additional funding, arguing that the money was needed to address irregularities that had resulted in financial leakages. “The additional N$650 million that the minister is requesting is to effect reforms within the medical aid system, where there was a big leak due to irregularities,” Emvula said. “It is very unfortunate that this had to take so long before such a leak could be detected.” Emvula questions the effectiveness of the oversight mechanisms meant to protect public funds, arguing that the apparent delay in identifying the irregularities raised concerns about accountability. He also criticises the budget for focusing heavily on administrative reforms without sufficiently addressing the immediate socio-economic challenges facing ordinary Namibians, including elderly people and other vulnerable groups. He further questions the projected creation of 7 000 jobs through the N$115 million National Youth Development Fund, saying the government had not clearly explained the nature of the jobs or the period over which they would be created. “It is not even certain how those jobs and what type of jobs will be created over what period of time,” Emvula says. He argues that Namibia needed a stronger production-based economy capable of generating sustainable employment and improving livelihoods, rather than spending plans without a clear direction for stimulating economic activity. Separately, the Ministry of Health and Social Services has been allocated N$41 million to cater for 456 medical and dental interns. title: Slow project delivery puts Govt spending under scrutiny
author: Shania Lazarus
content: Ministries were allocated N$6.5 billion this financial year to develop the country, but by the end of September they had used only 42% of it. They have about five five months left to deliver the rest of their projects before the year closes on 31 March 2027. During the tabling of the mid-term budget review, minister Ericah Shafudah announced that the government reallocated N$110.6 million from underperforming development projects. Economists warn that the figures expose a gap between money spent and tangible improvements in the economy, because salaries, grants and other running costs absorb most public spending while infrastructure projects struggle to advance. The mid-year budget review identifies recurring problems that delay implementation, economists say. This includes projects receiving funding before feasibility studies and engineering designs are complete, environmental approvals are outstanding, and land rights have not been secured. Economist Jason Kasuto says the country was unlikely to deliver all its plans this financial year, despite the headline spending figures suggesting the government was on track. “The difficulty is that the operational budget, which pays salaries and grants, is always spent in full, while the development budget, which builds the roads, schools and clinics that people actually see, had reached only 42%,” Kasuto says. He warns that capital projects could not simply double their pace because the financial year was approaching its end. “With revenue revised down by N$1.5 billion and ministries receiving N$0.7 billion of the N$13.1 billion they asked for, I expect the capital plans to be partly delivered this year and the balance rolled over into the next,” he says. “The government is running on schedule, but building behind schedule,” economist Almandro Jansen says. Jansen says roughly N$3.7 billion of the N$6.5 billion development budget still had to be delivered in the second half of the financial year. “That is more than was delivered in the first half,” he says, adding that he did not expect every planned capital project to be completed this financial year. The development budget is intended to finance infrastructure and other projects that can expand economic activity, improve public services and support job creation. Ministries are also spreading limited funds across too many projects, leaving individual sites without sufficient resources to progress quickly. Jansen says new projects were sometimes introduced during the financial year without adequate preparation, while too many projects were being implemented simultaneously. The N$110.6-million reallocation was intended to move money away from underperforming projects towards those progressing faster and urgent spending needs. Donor-funded projects have also struggled. Their projected spending was reduced from N$2.6 billion to N$1.8 billion because implementation was slow. SPENDING DOES NOT MEAN DELIVERY The figures also raise questions about how much of the money the government spends translates into new infrastructure, jobs and productive capacity. Jansen says the N$47 billion figure includes commitments, such as contracts and orders signed but not yet paid. Actual cash payments are, therefore, lower than the headline figure suggests. “Partly. The answer depends on what the money is spent on,” he says when asked whether the spending was being felt in the economy. Government spending supports household incomes and economic activity through salaries, grants and purchases. However, Jansen argues that this does not necessarily expand the economy’s ability to grow. By the end of September, reported infrastructure outputs included 13 kilometres of new bitumen roads, 14 kilometres of low-volume sealed roads, 18 kilometres of gravel roads and 32 kilometres of rehabilitated roads. The government also completed 92 pre-primary classrooms and 38 permanent school classrooms. “Against a country of three million people, they do not change what people see on the ground,” Jansen says, referring to the scale of these outputs relative to the country’s needs. The revised economic growth forecast of 2.3% adds to the pressure on the government to ensure that public expenditure produces stronger economic activity. Debt costs are another concern. The government’s interest bill is projected at N$15.4 billion for the financial year, equivalent to 17.5% of revenue and more than the entire Ministry of Health and Social Services budget, according to Jansen. “Every year that debt grows, more money goes to lenders and less to services,” he says. TREASURY PROMISES TIGHTER CONTROLS The mid-year review proposes stricter conditions for future capital funding, including requiring completed feasibility studies, verified bills of quantities, environmental approvals and procurement plans before projects receive money. The Ministry of Works and Transport is also expected to help ministries plan and cost projects, while the government intends to prioritise completing existing projects that support the sixth National Development Plan rather than starting new projects that are not ready. Jansen says the reforms could help improve execution from next year, but would not resolve the immediate delivery risks facing the current budget. The pressure is compounded by the weaker revenue outlook. The government revised revenue down by N$1.5 billion to N$8.1 billion, while the budget deficit remains at 5.5% of gross domestic product (GDP) and public debt is projected to reach 68.7% of GDP. title: The viral COVID-conscious lesbian bar is closing
author: mashable.com
content: The COVID-conscious lesbian bar in Western Massachusetts is closing. Last Ditch Bar and Arts Venue went viral after the Boston Globe reported on conflict sparked by the relaxation of its KN-95 mask policy.  SEE ALSO: How this lesbian watering hole became the most (in)famous bar in the world Last Ditch announced the closure in an Instagram post on Monday, effective immediately (though excluding events that had already been booked). This doesn't necessarily mean that the COVID-conscious lesbian bar is gone for good. Last Ditch stated that it was a "soft" closure, and put out a call for anyone interested in joining the business as owners — or taking over completely. However, without such a saviour, it seems likely that this will be the end for Last Ditch. "We have put our lives on hold to foster networks of care, resources, and a home base for organizing. It's time we pass it on," Last Ditch wrote in its Instagram post. "We've been fighting since the beginning to fill out the team, and we still don't have a board/leadership to manage workers owned Co-op transfer." View this post on Instagram Last Ditch gained internet fame last month following a Boston Globe article detailing uproar surrounding changes to its masking policy. Online commenters had harshly criticised the decision, accusing Last Ditch of ableism and even calling for violence in some cases. The situation quickly spiralled out of control, involving apologies, retractions, public meetings, and furiously dissatisfied commenters, with the venue's leadership team falling apart. This outsized reaction may have been enough to spark Boston Globe readers' interest, however it was the strange details and anecdotes within the article that really captured the internet's attention. Though deputy editor Annalisa Quinn was reporting on the facts, the facts seemed to border on parody, with people reposting quotes such as "one [Last Ditch owner] had enrolled in clown school." While Last Ditch has been overshadowed by the furore surrounding it, the venue aimed to provide an inclusive and welcoming space for lesbians. With this week's announcement, the LGBTQ community is now left mourning the loss of one of the scant few lesbian bars in the U.S. This Tweet is currently unavailable. title: Instagram is testing 90-minute videos
author: mashable.com
content: Instagram is introducing longform video. Called Features, the new format will allow users to upload videos up to 90 minutes long. SEE ALSO: Instagram will now edit the first draft of your Reel for you "So many creators are producing longer videos, and they're using clips of those videos to drive discovery on Reels and help build their audience," said Instagram VP of Product Tessa Lyons , announcing Features in a video alongside Head of Instagram Adam Mosseri on Monday.  "Reels is still going to be a core part of Instagram. But when you want to go deeper with creators you love and the content they're creating, you should be able to do that on Instagram." Longform video creators have typically favoured YouTube, which allows verified accounts to upload videos up to 12 hours long . In contrast, Instagram Reels are restricted to a maximum length of 20 minutes . Features aims to allow these creators to share their longer videos on Instagram as well, keeping their audience on the platform. View this post on Instagram Features appears to focus on content shot in landscape, and will be available on desktop, the mobile app, and Instagram for TV . Lyons stated that part of the new format's purpose is to help populate Instagram's television app, which allows users to watch Reels and video content on their TV. "We've been working on a TV version of Reels, and we know that to do that well, we need more than just short-form video," said Lyons. "People might discover a long form video that they love by seeing a Reel that's a clip of the video when they're watching Reels on mobile, and then when they go at the end of the day and open their TV and open Instagram on TV, we'll know that they watched that Reel and we'll be able to say, 'Hey, do you want to finish watching…?'" Though Instagram is introducing longform functionality, it doesn't yet offer creators the same financial incentives as YouTube. While Instagram creators are primarily paid through third-party brand partnerships and collaborations , the YouTube Partner Program gives YouTubers a cut of revenue from ads placed on their videos (55 percent for longform and 45 percent for Shorts). At time of writing, the most liked comment on Mosseri and Lyons' post was from mental health content creator Divija Bhasin ( @awkwardgoat3 ), who asked, "Why would anyone post an unpaid long video on Instagram if we can just post it on YouTube and actually get paid for the effort?" In a statement to TechCrunch , an Instagram spokesperson said that it is exploring potential monetisation models, "including performance-based incentives." However, it isn't ready to announce any such plans, the spokesperson instead focusing on users potentially being able to find more brand partnerships by expanding their audience through Features. "Over time, we think there will be compounding benefits for creators to tell new stories, reach new audiences, and find new partners, which should lead to many monetization opportunities," the Instagram spokesperson told TechCrunch. Judging from Lyons and Mosseri's announcement video, Instagram Features is currently missing a lot of the functionality available on YouTube. While viewers can adjust the playback speed, features such as captions and chapters appear absent during this early testing stage. Of course, such functionality may be added later, with Instagram currently conducting small tests of Features in the U.S. and Brazil.

title: What’s happening with Ethan and Hila Klein? The H3 Podcast fallout, explained
author: mashable.com
content: Ethan Klein has spent years dissecting other people's internet scandals on the H3 Podcast , the comedy and commentary show he built with his wife, Hila. Now, their own relationship is at the center of the conversation. Hila has accused Ethan of having an affair lasting more than six months, leaving the couple's marriage and the future of their show in question. Fans are trying to make sense of the news, while people across social media are digging through old episodes and swapping what they believe are clues. If you've seen the posts but don't know the people behind them, here's what happened — and how a marriage, a podcast, and years of internet history became tangled together. First, who are Ethan and Hila Klein? Before the podcast, there was h3h3Productions . Ethan and Hila launched the YouTube channel in 2011, posting sketches and reaction videos that poked fun at viral clips, internet trends, and other creators. Ethan was often the louder, more confrontational presence, with Hila appearing alongside him. One of their breakout videos was 2016's "Vape Nation, " (30 million views) which followed Ethan around New York City playing an exaggerated vaping enthusiast. The outfits, enormous vape clouds, and interactions with strangers helped make him a recognizable figure in YouTube comedy. The couple met in Israel in 2007, while Ethan was visiting on a Birthright trip, and married in 2012. As their audience grew, viewers got to know them as both creative partners and a couple. Their H3 Podcast expanded that world into longer conversations, mixing internet commentary with interviews featuring guests such as Post Malone and Joji . The production crew became part of the show, too, joining discussions and developing their own followings. That dynamic also powered Frenemies , the show Ethan began co-hosting with YouTuber Trisha Paytas in 2020. Sitting in front of a pink-and-black backdrop, the two traded personal stories, discussed other creators, dressed in costumes, and, most commonly, argued. SEE ALSO: Trisha Paytas steps down from 'Frenemies' podcast after tense dispute on the show The partnership ended in June 2021 amid disputes over money, production, and creative input. But Paytas remained connected to the family: She married Hila's brother, Moses Hacmon, later that year. Through these different versions of H3, the Kleins' relationship remained a familiar presence. Viewers followed them as they built businesses and raised their three children. Hila also founded the clothing brand Teddy Fresh in 2017 and later launched the makeup brand Teddy Glow. How to play Pips If you've ever played dominoes, you'll have a passing familiarity with how Pips is played. As we've shared in our previous hints stories for Pips, the tiles, like dominoes, are placed vertically or horizontally and connect with each other. The main difference between a traditional game of dominoes and Pips is the color-coded conditions you have to address. The touching tiles don't necessarily have to match. SEE ALSO: Wordle today: Answer, hints for October 27, 2026 The conditions you have to meet are specific to the color-coded spaces. For example, if it provides a single number, every side of a tile in that space must add up to the number provided. It is possible — and common — for only half a tile to be within a color-coded space. Here are common examples you'll run into across the difficulty levels: Number : All the pips in this space must add up to the number. Equal : Every domino half in this space must be the same number of pips. Not Equal : Every domino half in this space must have a completely different number of pips. Less than : Every domino half in this space must add up to less than the number. Greater than: Every domino half in this space must add up to more than the number. title: Firefox brings back internet icons for new anti-tracking, anti-AI campaign
author: mashable.com
content: Sick of web browsers tracking your every move and forcing intrusive, unnecessary AI features on you? Apparently, you’re not alone. Some of your favorite internet personalities — and real-life memes from the late 2000s and early 2010s — are joining forces to promote Firefox, a browser that's pushing back against online tracking and unwanted AI features. Mozilla, the non-profit organization behind the Firefox web browser, has just launched a new ad campaign to draw internet users away from AI-filled Google Chrome and back to Firefox's heyday in the late 2000s and early 2010s, when Firefox commanded up to 32 percent of the global browser market share. To do that, Mozilla has brought together some of the biggest internet personalities of that era for a new ad campaign called "Come Back to Firefox." "What happened to the internet?" asks the Numa Numa Guy in the opening of the new campaign video. "It used to be fun." Overly Attached Girlfriend, Annoying Orange, Tay Zondaday of "Chocolate Rain" fame, and a slew of other internet memes appear in the ad longing for the internet days of old, before modern web browsers tracked your every move, sold user data for advertising purposes, and pushed AI features on its users. Firefox offers an alternative to many other browsers that seem to be obsessed with AI and monitor users' online habits. Firefox includes a built-in free VPN to help keep users' browsing activity private, AI controls so users can decide just how much AI-related features they want accessible in their browser, and an ad blocker in the mobile version of the browser. The full list of internet personality cameos includes: Numa Numa Guy Bad Luck Brian Overly Attached Girlfriend Where the Hell is Matt? Kelly's Shoes Annoying Orange Apparently Kid Tay Zonday  Chuck Testa Success Kid The video isn't AI-generated. It actually features the real-life online personalities as they are today. For example, if you've been wondering what the Success Kid looks like all-grown up, you'll find out here. “I kept going back to Firefox’s heyday, when the internet was really fun, weird, and interesting…That's the feeling we wanted to bring back with this campaign," Mozilla's Chief Marketing Officer John Solomon said in a statement provided to Mashable.  "We wanted to remind people of what made the internet so wonderful in the first place," Solomon explained. "These are people who helped make it strange, creative, surprising, and fun. None of them were trying to go viral. They were normal, everyday people who were using the internet. That’s the way the internet should be and why we feel it’s a great moment for Firefox. Always independent and unlike big tech, not trying to extract more from everyday people.” Firefox currently has an estimated 2.8 percent share of the global web browser market.

title: Maxxing named Dictionary.coms 2026 Word of the Year
author: mashable.com
content: Apparently, getting better at something now requires adding "maxxing" to its name. There's sleepmaxxing , proteinmaxxing, looksmaxxing, and even cozymaxxing, because a night on the couch can apparently be optimized, too. As of Oct 26, "maxxing" is Dictionary.com ’s 2026 Word of the Year . The publisher describes it as: “the practice of pursuing an activity to the fullest or optimizing a certain aspect of your life.” The shorthand for "maximizing" can describe a serious self-improvement effort or a joke about doing very little. Its versatility has helped it spread across beauty, wellness, work, and everyday internet conversation. Dictionary.com traces the term’s roots through "min-maxing," a gaming strategy that involves developing a character’s strengths until their weaknesses matter less. Online communities eventually gave "maxxing" another "x" and an expanding list of things to work on. One of its most recognizable forms is "looksmaxxing," which focuses on improving physical appearance. But the template has spread into workplace conversations about "tokenmaxxing," or using as much AI as possible, and lifestyle trends like " frictionmaxxing ," which implores you to "rethink your relationship to your device — and your humanity." Increasingly, Dictionary.com says, people also use "maxxing" as a word on its own. The dictionary recognition has been building, too. In September, Merriam-Webster added "looksmaxxing" among 1,400 new words and definitions, alongside "vibe-coding" and "cuffing season." The word's history also goes beyond jokes about optimizing your bedtime. Looksmaxxing grew out of incel forums and sits within the broader manosphere, a network of online communities often associated with misogyny and rigid ideas about masculinity. Mashable has explored the subculture through its looksmaxxing glossary and coverage of its racist beauty standards and dehumanizing language about women. SEE ALSO: The Looksmaxxing Glossary: Every term you need to understand the internet's most unhinged subculture One of looksmaxxing's most recognizable figures is Braden Peters, better known as Clavicular , who shares appearance-focused ( and often misogynistic ) advice with millions of followers. While looksmaxxing can involve everyday grooming and skincare, its more extreme forms include crash dieting and "bone smashing" — striking facial bones in the unfounded belief that doing so will create a more defined face. There's also " pheromone-maxxing ," which involves skipping showers, avoiding deodorant, or wearing unwashed clothes in the hope that a stronger natural scent will attract potential partners. The concerns extend beyond physical injury. New Zealand's Classification Office , for example, warns that some looksmaxxing content can encourage disordered eating, obsessive scrutiny of appearance, and feelings of hopelessness, while exposing viewers to misogynistic or extremist messaging. That history matters as the language becomes mainstream, even as people adopt "maxxing" for pursuits far removed from those communities. What else made the shortlist? Dictionary.com’s other finalists were " affordability " " data center, " " odyssey ," and "unc." Its explanations, respectively, pointed to the cost of living, debates over AI infrastructure, Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey , and slang for someone considered older or out of touch. Together, the choices offer a recognizable portrait of 2026: money worries, AI everywhere, a major movie event, and, yes, slang with roots in incel forums. If that all sounds exhausting, there's always touching-grass-maxxing.

title: Why French and Japanese users are beefing on X, explained
author: mashable.com
content: The Elon Musk -owned X has a new main character — or, this time, two entire countries. While the platform is no stranger to users from different countries trading barbs with their neighbors (see: the FIFA World Cup ), what's happening between France and Japan has gotten a little ugly. As protests in France continue over the rising cost of living and demands for better learning conditions in schools, X users in the country began to fight back against Japanese users who blamed the unrest on Black and Arab people. At the end of the day, it's ugly internet beef. But to understand why it's these two countries in particular, here's some context. France's "Act 3" protests France is in the middle of a major protest movement. It started in mid-September at a high school in Créteil, southeast of Paris, where students and staff were frustrated by a shortage of teachers and resources. Since then, parents and union members have joined high school students, and some demonstrations have ended in clashes with police using tear gas. On Oct. 6 alone, about 56,000 people marched through Paris. Frustration over rising living costs and struggling public services has fueled the unrest, too. Given that mass movements like these create unruly environments, there has also been rioting and looting in the streets of Paris. Because the protests are about the state of education in France, the turnout skews toward students — and Gen Z loves anime. As Bloomberg reports , a Sony Group study of anime watchers across 10 countries found that "79 [percent] of anime fans between the ages of 13 and 17" had watched more anime than the year prior, with 68 percent of Gen Z respondents saying the same. At Oct. 17 demonstrations in Paris, Lyon, and Montpellier, students carried the Straw Hat Pirates' flag from One Piece , along with references to Naruto , Dragon Ball , and Jujutsu Kaisen . One slogan going around declared, "The world will be saved by Otakus." The Straw Hat Jolly Roger is not an uncommon sight at protests these days. In the show itself, the main character, Monkey D. Luffy, and his pirate crew spend much of their adventures fighting corrupt governments and freeing oppressed peoples. The flag, as a symbol of rebellion, has appeared at demonstrations in Indonesia and Nepal . Ironically, though, some Japanese users on X did not like this. On Oct. 19, the X account Anime Spotlight  shared a roundup of Japanese users  who were angry that the flag had become associated with violent unrest. It’s unclear how widely that view is shared. Some Japanese X users then blamed France's unrest on Black and Arab immigrants, often with slurs and images of monkeys or the trans-Atlantic slave trade . Those posts echoed anti-immigration talking points that circulate among right-wing influencers and politicians in Europe and the U.S., even though the protests are about underfunded schools. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. French users hit back, and they weren’t any gentler. Their posts, translated from French, have gone viral — primarily going after Japanese men, playing on stereotypes about brutal work culture , loneliness , and the sexualization of young girls in some anime and manga. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. While the beef started with Japanese users attacking Black people, plenty of the French jokes are racist, too. Why France and Japan? What makes the feud strange is that these two countries usually get along famously. Japan has long held a romantic view of France, and France has been one of manga's biggest markets in Europe. Their leaders have even gotten in on the anime fandom: In April, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and French President Emmanuel Macron struck the Dragon Ball Kamehameha pose together at a joint news conference. In fact, Japan has its own fantasy version of France, so well known that there’s a name for the shock some tourists feel when the real city doesn't match it, called  Paris syndrome . The fantasy of what Paris and France are is part of the reason this feud kicked off. Many Japanese fans love an idealized "Western" version of Paris, not one with tear gas in the streets. Plenty of Westerners hold an equally idealized picture of Japan, largely shaped by anime, in which the country is viewed as polite, safe, quirky, and seemingly problem-free. The lens through which many in the Western world view Japan is now being shattered, as the feud sheds light on some very real issues in the country. It's been an open topic for a while now that foreigners can face less-than-stellar treatment in Japan. Nationalist party Sanseito won 14 seats on a "Japanese First" platform. In February , Takaichi’s Liberal Democratic Party won a landslide while taking a tougher line on immigration. A Stanford survey found that opposition to bringing in foreign workers rose to about 53 percent in February, roughly 17 percentage points higher than in 2022. Takaichi became Japan’s first female prime minister last October and is a staunch conservative. Before taking office, she regularly visited Yasukuni Shrine. The shrine honors Japan’s war dead, including 14 convicted World War II war criminals. Takaichi also considers the late nationalist Prime Minister Shinzo Abe a mentor . Japan’s neighbors, especially China and South Korea, see the shrine as a symbol of the country’s wartime aggression. Another well-documented part of Japanese culture that's being poked at is its work culture. The problem of overwork is serious enough that the government is required by law to report on it to parliament every year, and its 2025 white paper was the 10th such report. The first report, published in 2016 , found that 22.7 percent of surveyed companies had employees logging more than 80 hours of overtime a month, the official threshold at which the risk of death from overwork becomes serious. Relatedly, there is great concern over mental health. Japan recorded 19,097 suicides in 2025, the first time the yearly total fell below 20,000 since records began in 1978. That brought the suicide rate down to 15.4 per 100,000 people. Men accounted for 13,117 of those deaths, compared with 5,980 women. The picture is more complicated than overwork alone, though. Health problems were the most commonly cited factor, followed by economic struggles and family issues. And while overall numbers fell, suicides among children hit a record high in 2025 for the second year in a row, reaching 532. The bigger picture As stated, online beef between citizens of two countries is not new. This particular moment in digital culture is a bit different, as it targets the West's mythical image of Japan, shaped by anime, games, and the Japanese government’s own "Cool Japan" soft-power push. Japan may be propped up as safe, polite, and a bit quirky, but its image, like every country's, has blind spots too. The same Western audiences that idealize Japan can overlook its immigration fights, its overwork crisis, its abusive justice system , or the way its wartime history is still contested at home and across Asia. Race plays a part in which stories stick, too. Asian American immigrants, particularly from East Asian countries, are often held up in the West as model minorities , a "flattering" stereotype often used to justify continued oppression of Black American and Asian communities. None of that excuses the racism flying both ways. Many of the posts from French users attacking the Japanese are no better than the posts they’re answering, and stereotypes about either country don’t add up to a fair critique of it. But the feud illustrates why a country’s pop culture exports rarely tell its whole story. That’s true of Japan seen through anime, and of Paris seen through postcards.

title: With hundreds dying in crashes, LA turns to speed cameras for change
author: mashable.com
content: Los Angeles turned on approximately 20 cameras at dangerous intersections around the city on Monday (Oct. 26), intended to catch speeding drivers and, hopefully, save lives. For the next 60 days, drivers exceeding the speed limit by at least 11 miles per hour will receive written warnings by mail. Following that, tickets will be issued to offenders, with fines ranging from $50 to $500, depending on the driver's speed. By the end of the year, the Los Angeles Department of Transportation (LADOT) plans to activate 125 cameras across the city. SEE ALSO: This Flock Camera map shows more than 300,000 devices LA is currently trying to get a handle on vehicular violence, with car crashes in the city claiming about 300 lives annually, a toll that exceeds the annual number of homicides in the city of 4 million, according to the Los Angeles Times . The city has placed cameras near high-injury/high-death intersections, near schools, and at spots known for street racing. LA is years behind other large cities like New York , Oakland, and San Francisco, which have already installed speed cameras. In the latter city, the cameras brought about a dramatic 80 percent drop in speeding. LADOT expects its cameras to reduce fatal crashes at their locations by 53 to 71 percent. Malibu, a nearby city in Los Angeles County, recently launched a speed camera pilot program on 21 miles of the Pacific Coast Highway. Over the course of nine days last month, the cameras recorded approximately 100,000 speeding violations .

"The response to iPhone Duo from early users has been incredibly positive, and we are seeing exciting things from developers who are rapidly updating their apps to take advantage of its unique form factor,” Apple said. “We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units. If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement." The statement doesn’t say what’s causing the problem, how many units are affected, or whether Apple plans a broader fix. Apple appears to have sent the same statement to several other outlets covering the reports. Still, it’s the company’s first public acknowledgment of the problem. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. The Duo has drawn plenty of attention as Apple’s first foldable iPhone. It sold out almost immediately when pre-orders opened Oct. 16, with some delivery estimates stretching into January 2027. But early owners have found that it’s very much a first-generation device, and the display reports are just one of several complaints. Beyond durability, users have flagged a few other issues, as reported by Mashable Senior Editor Stan Schroeder . First, as JerryRigsEverything points out , the protective matte screen on the foldable dulls its color and vibrance, and it picks up heavy glare. The FaceTime camera, as Schroeder notes, is bad for photos, with Apple leaning heavily on AI processing that can leave selfies looking plasticky and smudged. Finally, many apps aren’t yet optimized for the Duo’s inner display, including Apple’s own App Store — though Schroeder reported that he expects app developers to catch up within the next month. Durability concerns had been building before the display reports went viral. YouTuber Tim Pan ran the Duo through 10,000 folds in a folding machine, plus another 1,000 at -4 degrees Fahrenheit. Before-and-after images from the test spread online, appearing to show a much deeper crease. Samsung seems to be enjoying this. While the Korean tech giant hasn’t taken any direct shots at the Duo, at least not officially, its Samsung Mobile US account has been playing reply guy under iPhone Duo posts on X. One reply simply read "mogged. respectfully." This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. Cringe looks-maxxing speak aside, Samsung is getting plenty of free marketing out of the Duo’s rocky start. The company is now on its eighth-generation Galaxy Z Fold. Although its foldables went through their own early durability problems, Samsung has had years to refine the hinge, crease, and display that Apple is only attempting for the first time. Every viral post about a cracked Duo screen is, in effect, an ad for the competition. If your Duo’s inner display is showing problems, Apple recommends contacting AppleCare for a replacement. title: Samsung TVs might use the mics of connected devices to listen to you, researcher says
author: mashable.com
content: If you own a Samsung TV without a built-in microphone, it might still be listening to you, according to a researcher who shared his findings this week. On the social media platform X, cybersecurity researcher @log4j shared that an investigation into Samsung smart TVs found that televisions without a mic will scan for connected devices that are equipped with a microphone. The smart TV will then utilize the audio data collected from the soundbar or other connected Bluetooth devices. "This is pretty evil and clever," @log4j said about their discovery. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. The researcher recently gained administrator root access to their own 2025 Samsung smart TV and has been sharing their findings in a series of posts on X. Your smart TV is likely listening to you. At this point, that shouldn't be a surprise. Many televisions advertise this functionality, since your TV has to be listening to you to take voice commands and interact with other smart home devices. However, other unadvertised and concerning privacy issues are arising from the device's ability to listen in. For example, @log4j started looking into their TV after receiving oddly specific advertisements and found that their television was logging things like "dog barking" and "baby crying" under an event called EV201/SOUNDSENSOR_ON. As NotebookCheck.net points out, while Samsung 2025 Vision AI TVs advertise that the devices detect barking dogs and crying babies and send alerts through the company's SmartThings app, Samsung does not advertise that this data is also sent back to the company. Researcher @log4j also found that Samsung TVs track what happens inside specific apps. For example, the TV monitors what a user does in the YouTube app and even logs data such as the ads a user skips. Mashable has reached out to Samsung for more information about the reports from @log4j and will update this piece when we hear back. These privacy issues are not unique to Samsung TVs either. Last month, Mashable covered a report from YouTuber Gamers Nexus , which claimed to find that LG TVs were secretly recording users even when the televisions were turned off. LG later responded , denying some but not all the claims. Want to learn more about getting the best out of your tech? title: CapCut is adding a ChatGPT plugin. See it in action.
author: mashable.com
content: CapCut is coming to ChatGPT . The ByteDance-owned video editor announced a ChatGPT plugin on Oct. 24 at CapCut World in Los Angeles, an event for creators and partners. The plugin isn’t available yet; CapCut says it will arrive in the coming months. According to CapCut, creators will be able to develop a video idea in ChatGPT and have CapCut put together a rough first cut. From there, they can keep tweaking it by chatting. CapCut’s examples include holding a shot for longer, making captions more readable, or keeping music playing quietly under a voiceover. SEE ALSO: FBI warns against foreign mobile apps like CapCut in new PSA Creators aren’t limited to prompts, either. CapCut says users can make hands-on changes themselves, and ChatGPT will take those edits into account as the conversation continues. CapCut shared a demo of the plugin on X. In the video, a user uploads clips from a sports game and asks ChatGPT, "@capcut turn these clips into a 12-second highlight reel." The plugin generates the reel, and the user then refines it, including asking ChatGPT to add on-screen text. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. "Creators across the Americas are showing us that a great idea can begin anywhere," Xiaoqi Fu, CapCut’s global head, said in a statement . Fu added that the company’s new tools aim to keep the creator’s own imagination and judgment at the center of the process. The plugin was one of several AI features CapCut announced at the event. This includes new generative AI features for its web and mobile apps, as well as an AI agent for CapCut that'll be tested in the coming months. CapCut also says it labels AI-generated content and uses watermarks and C2PA Content Credentials, an industry standard for tracking how media was made. It is also testing a tool that lets anyone upload a file to see whether it was made with AI tools from CapCut or its sister apps, Dreamina, Pippit, and Hypi. title: Apple iPhone Duo screen crack: See the phone fail JerryRigEverything’s bend test
author: mashable.com
content: How tough is Apple 's first-ever foldable phone? JerryRigEverything , the YouTube channel that made a name for itself by putting phones through a series of very tough stress tests, has now done the same to the iPhone Duo . The tests included scratching the phone's surface with a scalpel, burning it with a lighter, covering it with dirt, and bending it the wrong way to see how much force its hinge mechanism can absorb. The iPhone Duo passed some of the tests fairly well; for example, the minor scratches on its display appeared to magically heal. However, when Jerry covered it with sand and dirt, some of it appeared to enter the Duo's hinge mechanism, which is concerning. Also, the phone failed the most brutal test: it was bent until its screen broke, rendering the Duo nearly useless. SEE ALSO: Apple iPhone Duo review: This changes everything To be fair, most of these tests go way harder than normal use, and most phones ultimately fail several of them. However, compared to some other foldable phones, the iPhone Duo seemed a tad more fragile. The message is clear: Don't bend, scratch, or burn this one, folks. title: McDonalds has relaunched the McRib this week — where to find yours
author: mashable.com
content: Four years after embarking on an official Farewell Tour that fooled absolutely no one, McDonald’s is resurrecting its most polarizing creation well ahead of schedule. Yes, you guessed it: From Oct. 27, the McRib will begin rolling out to select McDonald’s restaurants across the U.S. Love it or hate it, the McRib isn't going anywhere. First introduced in 1981, the sandwich features a seasoned, boneless pork patty shaped like a miniature rack of ribs, drenched in tangy barbecue sauce, and layered with onions and pickles on a toasted homestyle roll. Rather than executing a nationwide launch, McDonald’s confirmed early availability across six hubs: Los Angeles Chicago Miami Atlanta Philadelphia Dallas By staging a regional rollout instead of a nationwide release, McDonald's is deliberately feeding into that scarcity dynamic that we see in other areas like Pokémon . And because availability varies by region, blindly driving to your local drive-thru is a recipe for disappointment. Instead, we recommend checking the McDonald’s App and the McRib Locator website to plan your attack
