title: Anthropic sued for allegedly training Claude on Elvis Presleys music
author: mashable.com
content: Anthropic is reportedly being sued for allegedly training its AI on Elvis Presley's music without permission. Billboard reports that owners of Presley's intellectual property rights filed the lawsuit on Friday, claiming that Anthropic used 274 of the rock icon's songs to train its Claude AI models. Such songs allegedly included hits such as "Can't Help Falling in Love," "Don't Be Cruel," "Return to Sender," and "(You're the) Devil in Disguise." SEE ALSO: Anthropic’s AI safety bill would pause AI models if 50+ people could die The complaint alleges that Claude's generated content now adapts or copies Presley's discography without appropriate licensing or consent, and accuses Anthropic of having "built its entire business model on infringing copyrights at an unfathomable scale." The lawsuit specifically described instances in which users could request Claude recreate and update Presley's songs. "These renders keep landing very close to the originals: same structure, same hooks reused with light rewording, and full sets of verses/choruses/bridges," read the filing. "That's edging past 'inspired by' into reproducing the copyrighted song, even when the words are swapped out." Anthropic has refuted the allegations, a spokesperson stating , "We disagree with the claims and intend to defend this case fully." The plaintiffs are requesting a permanent injunction to prevent Anthropic from using Presley's songs, as well as damages of up to $150,000 for each work allegedly infringed upon. At 274 works, that would be a fine of up to $41.1 million. Anthropic has been the target of multiple prior lawsuits alleging unauthorised use of intellectual property. Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell Music sued Anthropic in August, claiming that it had conducted a "brazen campaign of illegally torrenting, scraping, and downloading copyrighted works on a massive scale." In July, Anthropic settled a $1.5 billion class action lawsuit in which authors accused it of illegally downloading pirated books. title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on October 26, 2026
author: mashable.com
content: The Full Moon reaches its peak on October 26 just after midnight in ET, meaning some parts of the US will see it become full just after midnight, while others will experience the peak on the evening of October 25. If you want to spot some lunar features on the Moon's surface, here's what you might be able to see. What is today's Moon phase? As of Monday, Oct. 26, NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Full Moon phase, with 100% of its surface visible. Tonight, without the use of visual aids you should be able to spot the Copernicus Crater, Tycho Crater, and the Mare Crisium. If you have binoculars you'll also see the Endymion Crater, the Alphonsus Crater, and the Grimaldi Basin. Finally, if you have a telescope, you'll also see the Apollo 15 and 16 landing spots, and the Caucasus Mountains. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on November 24. What are Moon phases? The Moon takes around 29.5 days to travel around Earth, and its appearance changes throughout the month. As it moves around our planet, we see different amounts of its sunlit side, from a slim crescent to the quarter phases and eventually a Full Moon. It then begins the cycle again. As NASA explains, these phases are caused by the Moon's changing position relative to Earth and the Sun. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet. Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible. Waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere) Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit. Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

content: Across the nation, there appears to be growing frustration with the explosion of AI-generated advertising plaguing small-business storefronts and restaurant interiors. Last Thursday, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act into law, mandating that all ads, from million-dollar television commercials to printed flyers passed out on the street, contain a disclosure label in the same format as the ad itself. SEE ALSO: Hackers find a way to turn users' own AI agents and Downloads folders against them The purpose of the bill is to combat false or misleading advertising, which is much easier to engage in with the help of AI-generated content. The bill, as introduced, states: "An advertiser may not create and disseminate or cause to be created and disseminated an advertisement that uses synthetic content in a manner that creates a false consumer perception about the nature, origin or authenticity of the goods or services being advertised, without clear and conspicuous disclosure. A disclosure under this section must state that the advertisement contains content that was modified or generated using artificial intelligence." And because it applies to all advertising shown in Pennsylvania, it will impact, for example, television commercials created in other states or advertisements made in other countries, so the consequences of this bill will be far-reaching.  According to reporting by The Verge , though, critics of the bill wonder how effective it will be, given the imprecise nature of some of the language used. As The Verge notes , language like "significantly modified" is subjective and open to wide ranges of interpretation, while extensive exceptions made for "parody, satire, commentary, or criticism" offer advertisers legal wiggle room.  Whatever the ultimate impacts of the bill or the future interpretations by the court system, it represents another attempt by elected representatives to respond to  the overwhelming will of voters  to bring artificial intelligence under legislative control, so we expect this bill to initiate a trend.

title: Why Google is linking your phone number to all your signed-in accounts
author: mashable.com
content: Android users, listen up: Google is quietly verifying and attaching your phone number across all your signed-in Google accounts, according to reporting from Android Authority . The policy change happened between August and October of 2025, under the "Verify phone numbers automatically" setting, which must now be opted out of rather than opted into. What does this mean in practice? All Google accounts used on your phone are going to be associated with your phone number, whether you want them to be or not, including accounts you add in the future. Furthermore, because Google periodically attempts to re-verify phone numbers, you could incur carrier charges associated with that verification process. SEE ALSO: Anthropic’s Claude can now send Gmail emails without asking first It might seem like a shady practice, especially because it was set to function by default, but there's also a good rationale for allowing Google to do this, as it improves the sharing functionality across your Google accounts, and makes things like phone recovery much easier, in the event that you lose your phone and want to restore a new phone to the old one's settings. There's also a slew of quality-of-life features, from faster sign-ins to emergency location services, that work better or faster with this feature enabled.  Of course, there's also an incentive for Google as well, since connecting all your Google accounts via phone number helps to optimize their ad performance, allowing them to show you more targeted advertisements across your devices or accounts.  If you do decide you would rather opt out of this functionality on your Android phone, navigate to Settings, select Google then All Services and choose Privacy & Security. Once here, you need to select the "Phone number verification" page and de-select "Verify phone numbers automatically" to disable this feature.

title: New Instagam app on Apple TV brings reels, long-form video and live shows
author: mashable.com
content: We're less than a month away from the release of a new iteration of the Apple TV, packed with the kind of computing power once reserved for desktops, so it only makes sense that it should learn some new tricks.   Yesterday, we learned about one of those new tricks when  Instagram was re-listed on the Apple App Store  as available for iPhone, iPad,  and  Apple TV. But this isn't the first time Instagram has flirted with the big screen. Initial testing of the new form factor  began in late 2025 on Amazon Fire TVs and rolled out to Samsung TVs in mid-2026, so Apple is actually the last to adopt the new TV app. SEE ALSO: An AI image of Mia Goth sparks Instagram fan account controversy The most visible change as part of this new TV adoption is Instagram having to offer not only the portrait-style videos common to most phone and tablet designs but also horizontal, landscape videos to accommodate TV aspect ratios. As part of its migration to streaming services and smart TVs, Instagram is also exploring new video form factors , including longer-form video, episodic videos, live streaming, and even subscriptions, which would bring it into closer competition with YouTube, the internet's premier video content service.  Meta, parent company of Instagram, is betting that its famously addictive short-form video content will translate well to the big screen, where it can be enjoyed more communally, and it's working closely with creators to make the experience of uploading or streaming on Instagram as painless as possible.  It might seem like a risky bet, but if Meta can grab even a fraction of YouTube's massive audience , it will more than pay off.

title: The best comedies streaming on Netflix right now
author: mashable.com
content: Nothing feels as good as a deep, genuine laugh. It's an expression of joy! It's a workout. It's a sign that you're having a good time. Netflix has a dazzling selection of comedy movies that give you that good-time feeling on demand. Whether you're craving action-spiked shenanigans, quirky coming-of-age adventures, awkward humor, stranger-than-fiction silliness, madcap musical numbers, or crime with a spree of laughs, there's a perfect pick for you. And we've made singling it out all the easier by highlighting the most hilarious below. SEE ALSO: Best movies of 2026, and where to watch them now Here are the funniest movies now streaming on Netflix. 23. Cora Bora Megan Stalter stars in "Cora Bora." Credit: Brainstorm Media If Too Much has you craving more Megan Stalter, you'll want to catch up with this underseen gem. Directed by Hannah Pearl Utt, Cora Bora centers on the titular musician (played by Stalter), who has left Portland and her girlfriend (Jojo T. Gibbs) behind to pursue her dreams in L.A. The couple's open relationship allows each to explore other connections — or, in Cora’s case, endure an awkward one-night stand with a sexy Flat Earther (Thomas Mann). But when Cora begins to fear that her girlfriend is catching feelings for someone else, it prompts the chaotic bisexual into a hasty homecoming. In my review out of the film's SXSW premiere in 2023, I declared, " Cora Bora proves a sensational cringe comedy, spiked with wicked humor, skin-crawling awkward scenarios, and an ardent — if wounded — heart. Deftly dancing from brash jokes to tender dialogue, Stalter reveals a riveting range and stirring screen presence. Simply put, it’s easy to fall for Cora Bora. " — K.P. How to watch: Cora Bora is now streaming on Netflix. 22. Paddington in Peru Hugh Bonneville, Emily Mortimer, Imelda Staunton, Madeleine Harris, Samuel Joslin, and Ben Whishaw star as the Brown Family in "Paddington in Peru." Credit: Studio Canal / Peter Mountain We could all use some Paddington in our lives, so why not kick back and enjoy Paddington in Peru ? Sure, it's not the masterpiece that is Paddington 2 , but director Dougal Wilson still crafts a charming adventure in its own right in his directorial debut. SEE ALSO: 'Paddington in Peru' review: The movie we need right now This time around, Paddington (voiced by Ben Whishaw) is headed back to his homeland of deepest, darkest Peru, with the Brown family in tow. In his quest to find his missing Aunt Lucy, he'll cross paths with a high-energy, guitar-playing nun (Olivia Colman) and a cartoonish, disguise-loving boat captain (Antonio Banderas). Colman and Banderas elevate Paddington's journey from funny to downright outrageous, proving that there are few things more fun than watching seasoned performers let their freak flags fly. Check out their work and the rest of Paddington in Peru , and see why Mashable Entertainment Editor Kristy Puchko called it "the movie we need right now." — Belen Edwards, Entertainment Reporter How to watch: Paddington in Peru is now streaming on Netflix. 21. Nonnas Speaking of delicious, this comedy written by Liz Maccie and directed by her husband Stephen Chbosky will have you craving a home-cooked Italian meal. Inspired by the true story of the restaurant Enoteca Maria, Nonnas stars Vince Vaughn as an average Joe who channels his grief over losing his mother and grandmother into a tantalizing new venture. He uses his inheritance to build a new restaurant in Staten Island, and hires Italian grandmothers (or nonnas) to become the chefs using their family recipes. Personalities clash, but ultimately these strong-willed women come together to create something stupendous. It's a feel-good comedy full of love, joy, and laughs. * — K.P. How to watch: Nonnas is now streaming on Netflix. 20. Heart Eyes Credit: Christopher Moss Valentine's Day gets a horror-comedy makeover in Heart Eyes , from director Josh Ruben ( Werewolves Within ). The titular slasher only kills on Feb. 14, when they target happy couples in love. This year, the Heart Eyes killer has marketers Ally (Olivia Holt) and Jay (Mason Gooding) in their sights. There's just one problem: Ally and Jay aren't a couple, even though a coffee shop meet-cute and undeniable chemistry seem to suggest otherwise. Can these star-crossed acquaintances and definitely not lovers survive the night and convince the Heart Eyes Killer they're totally platonic? What follows is a cross between gory slasher and romantic comedy, and if you're a fan of both genres, chances are you'll be charmed by Heart Eyes . As Mashable contributor Kimber Myers wrote in her review, " Heart Eyes is a gory good time for those who are likely to swipe right on an off-kilter love story and a horror comedy." — B.E. How to watch: Heart Eyes is now streaming on Netflix. 19. Cunk on Life Comedian Diane Morgan has been gifting the world with her character of Philomena Cunk for a glorious decade and a half now. A dim-witted investigative journalist who butts heads with the real-world leading minds on each subject, Cunk proved to be a one-woman feast of absolute nonsense. The character Cunk started getting her own specials in 2016 with Cunk on Christmas , followed by Cunk on Britain and the epic globe-trotting mockumentary series Cunk on Earth ( also streaming on Netflix ). Morgan's expanded her reach all the way to Cunk on Life , her latest side-splitter that tries to uncover the very meaning of existence itself across its humble 71-minute runtime. Does Cunk succeed? Well, Cunk definitely thinks she does, every damn time. But if not, at least we'll get to hear some Technotronic in the process, dammit! — J.A.    How to watch: Cunk on Life is now streaming on Netflix . 18. Beverly Hills Cop: Axel F Credit: Netflix Eddie Murphy returns as wise-cracking Detroit police officer Axel Foley. 30 years after Beverly Hills Cop III , this sensational sequel sees Foley returning to Los Angeles to fight a new foe, reunite with old friends, and reconnect with his estranged daughter. SEE ALSO: 'Beverly Hills Cop: Axel F' review: Netflix's sequel shouldn't work and yet... Reprising their supporting roles are Beverly Hills Cop co-stars John Ashton, Judge Reinhold, Paul Reiser, and Bronson Pinchot. New to the crew is Taylour Paige as Axel's hard-headed daughter, Joseph Gordon-Levitt as a local ally, Nasim Pedrad as a flustered real estate agent, and Kevin Bacon as a smirking antagonist. The sparks will fly. The punchlines hit powerfully. The soundtrack is fire. And just like that, the heat is back on! — K.P. How to watch: Beverly Hills Cop: Axel F is now streaming on Netflix. 17. Between Two Ferns: The Movie Credit: Adam Rose / Netflix Zach Galifianakis' awkward celebrity interview web series Between Two Ferns might not seem like fodder for a full-length movie, but Between Two Ferns: The Movie goes double meta by presenting his success on Funny or Die as an insult to the actor's intention to host a "serious" interview show. Galifianakis the character sets off to correct the assumption that his original show is a joke by interviewing even more celebrities, like John Cho, Keanu Reeves , Tiffany Haddish, and more. — Alexis Nedd, Senior Entertainment Reporter How to watch: Between Two Ferns: The Movie is now streaming on Netflix. 16. Do Revenge Credit: Netflix Looking for a revenge flick that pays tribute to teen classics like Mean Girls , Heathers , Cruel Intentions , and more? Then check out Do Revenge , a dark comedy sure to join the canon of iconic high school movies. Students Drea (Camila Mendes) and Eleanor ( Maya Hawke ) couldn't be more different... apart from the fact that both have major bones to pick with people who ruined their reputations. They decide to team up and execute one another's revenge plans, which leads down a winding road of morally dubious choices, snappy one-liners, and excellent outfits. Mendes and Hawke have great chemistry, but it's Sophie Turner who damn near steals the show in a bit part that simply must be seen to be believed. * — B.E. How to watch: Do Revenge is now streaming on Netflix. SEE ALSO: Sophie Turner steals Netflix's 'Do Revenge' in 5 outrageous minutes 15. Always Be My Maybe Credit: Netflix What if the one who got away got a second chance? Back in the day, Sasha and Marcus were tight as a slap bracelet. But one fumbled night in a sweaty backseat seemed to shatter their future together. Fifteen years later, she's a world-renowned chef and he's — well — he's working for his dad's HVAC business and playing with his band on the side. Still, fate arranges for them to reconnect, which could mean Marcus (Randall Park) has a shot to show Sasha (Ali Wong) how he feels. Comedy ensues as the stakes get high when Keanu Reeves crashes the party, being all weird and hot and having the audacity to be Keanu Reeves ! This Nahnatchka Khan-helmed laffer also boasts appearances by James Saito, Charlyne Yi, Karan Soni, Daniel Dae Kim, and Michelle Buteau. * — K.P. How to watch: Always Be My Maybe is now streaming on Netflix. SEE ALSO: 20 best romantic comedies to fall in love with on Netflix 14. Dolemite Is My Name Credit: François Duhamel / Netflix Chronicling the true story of late comedian Rudy Ray Moore — also known as Dolemite — this Eddie Murphy vehicle is worth every minute of viewing. An outrageous showbiz comedy, Dolemite Is My Name is at once a poignant look at the life of an underdog and an unbelievably good time. With supporting performances by Da'Vine Joy Randolph , Wesley Snipes, Craig Robinson, and more, this biopic offers more beat-for-beat joy than many of its fictional counterparts. Sensational, aspirational, and electric: You'll love it. — Alison Foreman, Entertainment Reporter How to watch: Dolemite Is My Name is now streaming on Netflix. 13. The Polka King Credit: Netflix Sometimes true crime can lead to some pitch-perfect dark comedy. This is the case for this outrageous offering, which stars Jack Black as infamous scammer /local celebrity Jan Lewan. Black brings all the rock star panache you need to understand how Lewan could be so beguiling to the Pennsylvanian retirees who surrendered their savings to the self-proclaimed Polka King . Screenwriters Maya Forbes and Wallace Wolodarsky gave this story of fraud and showmanship shape. But they wisely trusted in the local flair of the terrific 2009 documentary The Man Who Would Be Polka King to provide some of the wildest lines of dialogue. Plucking directly from interviews with the friends, family, and victims of Jan Lewan, this comedy feels stranger than fiction but is jaw-droppingly real. Salty supporting turns from Jenny Slate, Jacki Weaver, and Jason Schwartzman bring added fun. * — K.P. How to watch: The Polka King is now streaming on Netflix. SEE ALSO: Love me like a Polka King 12. The Mitchells vs. The Machines Credit: Netflix Sony Pictures Animation has given audiences such daring and dynamic animated movies as Surf's Up, Hotel Transylvania, and Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse . This zany 2021 release centers on a family who's battling back the robo-apocalypse with togetherness, internet savviness, and a wall-eyed pug named Monchi (voiced by social media icon Doug the Pug). The Mitchells' adventure into chaos begins when daughter Katie (Abbi Jacobson) is poised to go off to college. Desperate for one last family-unifying road trip, her dad (Danny McBride) piles the whole family into his beater of a vehicle, unknowingly charting a fateful route into heroics. Co-directors Mike Rianda and Jeff Rowe infuse Katie's excitable perspective throughout the film by working in internet memes , social media-style reactions, and blitz of bonkers visuals. It’s a bold move that might alienate some viewers but has largely won the acclaim of critics and kiddos. * — K.P. How to watch: The Mitchells vs. The Machines is now streaming on Netflix . 11. Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery Credit: Netflix Writer/director Rian Johnson follows up his critically heralded whodunnit with a sequel that's even more explosive than Knives Out . Southern gentleman/detective Benoit Blanc (Daniel Craig) is back, drawling deductions and whipping out witticisms, much to the chagrin of a group of wealthy and conniving friends. It was supposed to be a murder mystery weekend where homicide was just a game. But when tech scion Miles Bron (Edward Norton) brings together his closest friends and worst enemy, real blood will be spilled, and the game is afoot! Joining in on the comically chaotic fun are Kate Hudson, Janelle Monáe, Dave Bautista, Kathryn Hahn, Leslie Odom Jr., and Jessica Henwick. — K.P. How to watch: Glass Onion is now streaming on Netflix. SEE ALSO: 5 movies like 'Knives Out' to scratch the funny murder mystery itch 10. The Forty-Year-Old Version Credit: Jeong Park / Netflix © 2020 The Forty-Year-Old Version isn’t just any film about a struggling New York artist, but one about a Black female playwright who’s continually held back from creating something authentic to her perspective. Radha Blank's autobiographical directorial debut, which she also wrote, produced, and stars in, is a searing, funny, and unabashedly honest look at the compromises Black creatives are pushed to make in a world dominated by whiteness. A teacher approaching her 40th birthday, Radha (Blank) gets the chance to produce one of her plays — only after she refuses to write a slave musical. But forced to change her vision to appease white audiences, Radha considers a totally different medium to express herself: becoming a rapper. The Forty-Year-Old Version may be one of the most slept-on Netflix originals, and it’s a shame we've yet to see another film from Blank since, itself an indictment of an industry that fails to continually platform raw and honest Black storytelling. * — Oliver Whitney, Contributing Writer How to watch: The Forty-Year-Old Version is now streaming on Netflix. 9. Vampires vs. the Bronx Credit: Netflix Want a movie that's got excitement, comedy, a scorching message about the evils of gentrification, and is a kid-friendly romp? Then take a bite out of Vampires vs. the Bronx . Oz Rodriguez's PG-13 horror-comedy centers on Afro-Latino teens who recognize that a flurry of missing person posters and an influx of rich white folks with tote bags means bad news for the neighborhood. Together, they team up Monster Squad- style to take down the bloodsuckers and save their community. With a sharp wit, a warm heart, a rich sense of atmosphere, and an equal appreciation for the Blade movies and '80s Amblin, Vampires vs. the Bronx is an easy watch full of rewards. * — K.P. How to watch: Vampires vs. the Bronx is now streaming on Netflix. 8. The Breaker Upperers This hidden gem comes from New Zealand, the fertile comedy ground that gave us Taika Waititi, Flight of the Conchords , and  What We Do in the Shadows .  Waititi collaborators Jackie van Beek, James Rolleston, and Jemaine Clement team up for a deeply quirky buddy comedy about two long-time besties with a bonkers — but brilliant — business model. Need someone to dump your partner so you can avoid a messy confrontation? Call on Jen and Mel (co-writers/co-directors/co-leads van Beek and Madeleine Sami). For a reasonable fee, these fearless Breaker Upperers will impersonate police officers, play pregnant, or even fake your death to help you ghost an ex. Whatever the shenanigans, van Beek and Sami sparkle. Booming with wild humor and big heart, this comedy is guaranteed to leave you cackling. * — K.P. Where to watch: The Breaker Upperers is now streaming on Netflix. 7. The Thursday Murder Club Celia Imrie, Helen Mirren, Naomi Ackie, Pierce Brosnan, and Sir Ben Kingsley in "The Thursday Murder Club." Credit: Giles Keyte / Netflix Sir Ben Kingsley, Helen Mirren, Pierce Brosnan, and Celia Imrie bring to life the brilliant pensioners at the heart of Richard Osman's best-selling novel The Thursday Murder Club. In the charming retirement village of Cooper's Chase, a club made up of a former M16 agent, a once-feared union activist, a wise therapist, and a cheerful retired nurse use their lifetimes of skills to crack cold cases. Hit Man Richard Linklater and Glen Powell reunite for Hit Man , a rom-com that is killer in all sense of the word. Wallace & Gromit: Vengeance Most Fowl Credit: Netflix Our pals Wallace the inventor and his loyal pup Gromit have been running around for nearly four cracking decades now, but their latest adventure (and only their second feature-length film, after 2005's The Curse of the Were-Rabbit ) proves they've lost not a whit of their vim and verve. Nominated for Best Animated Feature at the Oscars, Wallace & Gromit: Vengeance Most Fowl happily proves to be yet another gut-busting bit of British whimsy from Aardman Animation head Nick Park and his team of clay-playing creatives. Vengeance Most Fowl sees our cheese-loving duo facing down a familiar foe — the diabolical penguin mastermind Feathers McGraw, who was last seen being sent off to imprisonment in the City Zoo in the classic 1993 short The Wrong Trousers . Hacking into Wallace's latest invention, a garden gnome robot named Norbot that he's created to do all of the yard work, Feathers builds himself an army of killer gnomes all programmed to do his bidding. And he wants nothing more than to bid adieu to his nemesis Wallace! — J.A . How to watch: Wallace & Gromit: Vengeance Most Fowl is now streaming on Netflix . 4. Oh, Hi! Turns out, telling your girlfriend that post-coital, while handcuffed to a bed, isn't a great move! title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on October 25, 2026
author: mashable.com
content: It's the Full Moon tomorrow (or tonight, depending on your timezone), which means the Moon looks big and bright in the tonight. Hoping to do some Moon gazing? Here's what you should be able to see. What is today's Moon phase? As of Sunday, Oct. 25, NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Gibbous phase, with 99% of its surface visible. Tonight, without the use of visual aids you should be able to spot the Copernicus Crater, Tycho Crater, and the Mare Crisium. If you have binoculars you'll also see the Endymion Crater, the Alphonsus Crater, and the Mare Nectaris. Finally, if you have a telescope, you'll also see the Apollo 16 and 17 landing spots, and the Schiller Crater. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on October 25 or 26, depending on your timezone. What are Moon phases? The Moon takes around 29.5 days to travel around Earth, and its appearance changes throughout the month. As it moves around our planet, we see different amounts of its sunlit side, from a slim crescent to the quarter phases and eventually a Full Moon. It then begins the cycle again. As NASA explains, these phases are caused by the Moon's changing position relative to Earth and the Sun. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet. Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible. Waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere) Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit. Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

How to play Pips If you've ever played dominoes, you'll have a passing familiarity with how Pips is played. As we've shared in our previous hints stories for Pips, the tiles, like dominoes, are placed vertically or horizontally and connect with each other. The main difference between a traditional game of dominoes and Pips is the color-coded conditions you have to address. The touching tiles don't necessarily have to match. SEE ALSO: Wordle today: Answer, hints for October 25, 2026 The conditions you have to meet are specific to the color-coded spaces. For example, if it provides a single number, every side of a tile in that space must add up to the number provided. It is possible — and common — for only half a tile to be within a color-coded space. Here are common examples you'll run into across the difficulty levels: Number : All the pips in this space must add up to the number. Equal : Every domino half in this space must be the same number of pips. Not Equal : Every domino half in this space must have a completely different number of pips. Less than : Every domino half in this space must add up to less than the number. Greater than: Every domino half in this space must add up to more than the number. If an area does not have any color coding, it means there are no conditions on the portions of dominoes within those spaces. title: Elon Musk actually follows through on Grok AI adaptation of The Odyssey
author: mashable.com
content: Elon Musk doesn’t have a great track record of following through on his promises. According to MuskOmeter , a site that tracks the pledges Musk has made and whether he’s kept them, he’s at about a 24 percent hit rate. So it’s almost impressive that one of his sillier promises from this year actually came true. Late Friday afternoon, Musk shared the first of several planned episodes of an AI-generated version of Homer’s The Odyssey , made with Grok Imagine, the AI video generator from his company xAI. According to a post from the Grok Imagine account, the project is a collaboration between Wonder Studios and director Dev Walker. Both specialize in generative AI filmmaking. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. Musk first made the promise in July. As Mashable reported at the time , he posted on X that, before the year ended, Grok Imagine would make a full-length  Odyssey  movie that would be "historically accurate and true to the art of Homer." SEE ALSO: 'The Odyssey' is exposing some unexpected dating dealbreakers That was the culmination of months of Musk complaining about Christopher Nolan’s adaptation of The Odyssey . Much of the right-wing backlash to Nolan’s film was framed in terms of historical accuracy. The initial trailer sparked a little doubt about a faithful adaptation, as some took  issue with the film’s armor , calling it bland and closer to Roman than Greek. The bigger outrage came from the casting of Lupita Nyong’o as Helen of Troy and Elliot Page as Sinon. In February, Musk declared on X that Nolan had "lost his integrity" over it, as Mashable reported. Musk and others argued that a Black woman couldn’t play a character described as the most beautiful woman in the ancient world. Leave aside what that says about who gets to count as beautiful. Helen of Troy isn’t a real person. Troy was a real city , but historians still debate whether anything resembling the Trojan War ever happened. In Greek mythology, Helen herself is the daughter of Zeus and was hatched from an egg . "Historical accuracy" is doing a lot of heavy lifting here. Musk also took issue with Page's casting. In May, Musk reshared posts criticizing the casting , including some that misgendered the trans actor. Because Nolan’s cast list didn’t say who was playing whom, online conspiracy theories claimed Page would play Achilles. Instead, Page played Sinon, a character who originally appears in Virgil’s Aeneid , which is essentially Roman fan fiction of the Trojan War. With the casting details, Musk and right-leaning influencers predicted Nolan's adaptation would flop — " go woke, go broke. " Instead, The Odyssey opened to $124.5 million in July, a huge number for an R-rated, nearly three-hour film. IMAX 70mm screenings sold out weeks in advance, as Mashable previously reported. As of this writing, Nolan's film has grossed over $1.7 billion worldwide. Nolan, for his part, has been openly skeptical of generative AI. He told AFP earlier this year that the idea of it replacing human creativity is "a nonsense," according to The Guardian . Is Elon Musk's The Odyssey good? Musk's Grok-imagined version of Homer's tale is about what you'd expect. The first episode runs a little over seven minutes and covers the Greeks’ arrival at Troy. Every character is white. Visually, it has all the usual problems of generative AI video: unnaturally perfect teeth; the weightless, almost water-like hair texture; and the skin has an odd, smudgy quality that comes from the model not really understanding lighting or perspective. The backgrounds also suffer from something akin to texture pop-in, where video games load low-resolution textures before the detailed ones, so the screen isn't just black. As just a film to watch, the writing isn't all that great, and it's hard to keep up with all the characters as they look similar or look way too similar to real people. Is that not Kristofer Hivju? Credit: Grok Imagine / Wonder Studios / Mashable screenshot On top of that, in the entire seven-minute runtime, Odysseus is the only named character. Unless you've read The Odyssey fairly recently, you'd be confused about who some of the characters are — how is one supposed to know that one of those two men in the photo above is Palamedes? I sure didn't. As part of the promotion, Wonder Studios posted on X that "Homer didn’t have Grok… we do." True enough. Homer also told the story well enough that people are still adapting it nearly 3,000 years later, without any help from AI. Although Christopher Nolan’s  The Odyssey  is winding down its theater run, the critically acclaimed film is set to release digitally on Nov. 17. To tide you over, Wolfgang Petersen's Troy, starring Brad Pitt and Eric Bana, got a cultural re-evaluation thanks to the success of Nolan's film. It's human-made and currently holds a 3.5 average rating on Letterboxd.

title: Blocks latest AI model Dessa was trained entirely on human speech — and it shows
author: mashable.com
content: If interacting with Siri has been the extent of your experience "talking" to AI, you're in for a rude awakening. While Apple's voice assistant often fumbles basic commands and can take an unnaturally long time to process a request, the latest and greatest AI models are moving closer and closer to natural human speech. Case in point: Dessa, the brainchild of Jack Dorsey's Block, is allegedly the world's first full-duplex speech model , meaning it can listen to you  and  speak simultaneously, much like a real human does in the flow of normal conversation. In fact, that's Dessa's draw: it was trained entirely on human speech to make it as natural-sounding as possible. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. But these claims have to be heard to be appreciated, and Block's press release announcing Dessa shows just how far AI models have come to approximating the rhythm of natural human conversation.  SEE ALSO: Microsoft launches new MAI family of AI models for reasoning, voice, coding, and images In the second sample audio clip , for example, a real-life human and Dessa have an extended conversation about the movies of Christopher Nolan, and though the model does flex its knowledge at certain points, supplying a movie title, for example, it does so in a natural rather than robotic way, mirroring the tone of his human interlocutor while keeping up what, to human ears, sounds like a perfectly ordinary back-and-forth about Nolan's cinematic world.   In the third audio sample, Dessa spontaneously reacts to an unexpected prompt from the human ("Are you excited for our anniversary?") with genuine surprise and enthusiasm, complete with the conversation markers you would expect from a human being: audible gasps, a joyful enthusiasm that verges on tears, and even a difficulty finding the right words.  The final clip nixes human involvement entirely, featuring a conversation between ChatGPT and Dessa, and the contrast between the robotic, unnatural speech patterns of the ChatGPT agent and Dessa's prompts, interruptions, and puzzled questions perfectly illustrates how far Block has pushed its AI speech models.  Perhaps most impressive of all, Dessa seems to understand when a human speaking to it is being sarcastic, which requires a sophisticated understanding of both tone and its relationship to the content of speech that adult humans process effortlessly but that has historically stumped AI models (don't even think of speaking to Siri in a sarcastic tone).  According to the same press release, Block's motivation for developing Dessa is simple: "Speech is the most natural interface to any intelligence, super or otherwise, and today’s voice AI wastes it. It flattens what we say into text and can’t keep up with human timing. AI keeps gaining power and independence, and it’s still nearly deaf to the emotion in our voices. Imagine being in serious pain while a voice AI has no idea and just keeps going. That’s the safety problem. Dessa is a step toward fixing it." Leave aside the question of whether recognizing a tone of urgency, fear, or pain in a voice pattern is the same as  sympathizing  with the emotions behind those markers. But one should take a second to appreciate the complexity of training agentic AI to pick up on them in the first place. Wherever this leads us, Dessa is undoubtedly a major advancement in artificial intelligence and, more importantly, in bridging the gap between human communication and AI understanding.

title: Critical Musk documentary pulled from theatres after just two weeks
author: mashable.com
content: Despite its critical praise, Alex Gibney's Musk documentary about the world's richest man is ending its theatrical run after just two weeks, according to entertainment news site Showbiz411 . Upon its release on Oct. 9th, Musk was shown in just four theatres in two cities nationwide, but that number rose to over 450 by the second (and ultimately final) week of its theatrical run, though the total take, according to Gizmodo , was a paltry $571,902, making it "an unmitigated flop." But could there be something else at play here other than simple box office math?  Musk director, Gibney, is no stranger to tackling the rich and powerful in film, with previous credits including 2005's Enron: The Smartest Guys in the Room — about one of the largest corporate fraud cases in American history. Gibney then released Citizen K in 2019, exploring the alliance between Vladimir Putin and a Russian expat billionaire.  And prior to the film's release, SpaceXAI CEO Elon Musk himself publicly attacked both Gibney and the film, calling the director a " horrible human " after dismissing the documentary as an assembly of people with "an axe to grind." In the meantime, Musk's attorney Alex Spiro sent the production team a threatening legal letter , putting them "on formal legal notice" before the film had even been released.  Meanwhile, on Reddit, users are speculating about abrupt screening cancellations: " I hate to say it's a conspiracy, but what is it? " Inexplicably, TikTok also opted to disable the documentary's advertising account , allegedly for "political content" contrary to their use policies, but access was restored 48 hours later .    If you missed the abbreviated theatrical run and want to watch Musk yourself, it's now available for streaming on both Prime Video and Fandango.

title: The Knicks’ fake ring email is ticking off the internet
author: mashable.com
content: The NBA season has only just begun, but the New York Knicks are already embroiled in a PR nightmare after an email to staff to get a championship ring turned out to be an IT phishing test. On Tuesday, the defending champion Knicks played their first home game at Madison Square Garden since beating the San Antonio Spurs for their first NBA Finals win since the 1970s. As is custom, the first home game after a championship is when the team and fans get to watch the banner raised to the rafters and the presentation of their brand-new championship rings. According to reporting from The Athletic , based on conversations with seven league sources who spoke on condition of anonymity, many of the ring boxes handed out to coaching staff were empty. In fact, The Athletic could not even confirm whether head coach Mike Brown received his ring, receiving only this brief reply from a MSG Sports spokesperson: "We are not disclosing anything about the rings." SEE ALSO: Social media reacts to Knicks' storybook NBA Finals win It's possible, of course, that delays in the crafting of the rings or in the fitting of them necessitated the empty box move. Plus, there is precedent for coaching staff and front-office personnel having to wait longer for their rings. However, "many longtime employees at Madison Square Garden, including some who work in the Knicks’ business operations, will not receive rings at all," according to the insider sources who agreed to speak with The Athletic . Which is unusual, as the majority of team employees typically receive some form of ring in commemoration of the team's winning season. What's made the internet upset is a controversial IT trick played on the Madison Square Garden employees expecting a ring. According to The Athletic , in September, MSG staff received an email with the opening line "Congratulations, your Employee Championship Ring is here," followed by a prompt to choose their preferred style: Championship Gold or Garden Classic. Clicking through that link, however, did not bring employees to a jeweler's website. "Those who did click the link at the bottom of the message did not get to choose any jewelry; instead, they were forced to attend a mandatory cybersecurity class to help satisfy some of Dolan’s growing cybersecurity concerns," reported The Athletic .  Needless to say, when the internet caught wind of this, the roasting was severe and merciless. title: Sony WH-1000XM4C vs Bose QuietComfort (2nd gen): The battle of the mid-range headphones
author: mashable.com
content: Sony and Bose duke it out for the best mid-range headphone. Credit: Bethany Allard / Mashable Sony WH-1000XM4C vs. Bose QuietComfort (2nd gen): Specs Sony WH-1000XM4C specs Active noise cancellation: Yes Processor: QN1 for ANC Microphones: Four Equalizer: 10-band custom equalizer on companion app Spatial audio: Yes, but limited use Battery life: 27 hours Quick charge: Three-minute quick charge for one hour of playback Connection: Bluetooth 6.0 Multipoint: Connect up to two devices at once Weight: 0.61 pounds Colors: Black, lavender, platinum silver Bose QC (2nd gen) specs Active noise cancellation: Yes, with manual adjustment available Microphones: Six Lossless playback: Wired USB-C audio up to 24bit/48kHz Equalizer: Three-band custom equalizer Spatial audio: Bose TrueSpatial technology with Immersive Audio modes for Still, Motion, and Cinema Battery life: 24 hours per charge (18 hours with Immersive Audio) Quick charge: 15-minute charge for 2.5 hours of playback Connection: Bluetooth 5.4 Multipoint: Yes Weight: 0.5 pounds Colors: Black, white smoke, eucalyptus green*, dewdrop mint*, rosewood mauve* (*limited edition colors) Sony WH-1000XM4C vs. Bose QuietComfort (2nd gen): Sound quality The Bose QuietComfort (Gen 2) headphones come in black, white smoke, eucalyptus green, dewdrop mint, and rosewood mauve. Credit: Bethany Allard / Mashable The Sony WH-1000XM4Cs are available in black, lavender, and platinum silver. Credit: Bethany Allard / Mashable Sony headphones are known for their superior quality, and that trend holds true between these two headphones. Without any adjustments to the sound, the XM4C headphones produced a more nuanced and detailed sound profile with noticeably more clarity. The piano and vocals in Fiona Apple's rendition of "Why Try to Change Me Now" put me in a cozy jazz bar, while I found myself bumping the volume up on the Bose headphones to try to capture the same immersion. Speaking of immersion, Bose does have the advantage in offering spatial audio in the form of its proprietary Immersive Audio. While it's not the best spatial audio I've heard, it does help live performances and more soaring songs shine — Billy Joel's "New York State of Mind" was especially pleasing in this mode. Sony's equalizer... Credit: Screenshot / Sony versus Bose's. Credit: Screenshot / Bose Sony technically offers a spatial audio mode in the form of its 360 Reality Audio, but it's only functional with select apps (and none of the major music streaming ones). The lack of spatial audio, however, can be forgiven due to the excellent equalizer found on the companion app, which offers six presets, in addition to three custom settings. Users can also fine-tune their settings with a 10-band equalizer, compared to Bose's three-band equalizer and four presets. Ultimately, Sony provides a much more dynamic listening experience. SEE ALSO: The 10 best noise-cancelling headphones we use, love, and recommend Sony WH-1000XM4C vs. Bose QuietComfort (2nd gen): Active noise cancellation Where Sony generally takes the audio cake, Bose is known to be the master of ANC. While Sony's most recent flagship XM6 headphones have reversed that trend, Bose is back to taking the crown between these mid-range headphones. Sony's headphones use adaptive sound control and a four microphone system, compared to Bose's manually adjustable ANC and six microphone system. The result is slightly better ANC on the Bose headphones, with more flexibility in how much sound actually comes through. That said, Sony does offer an ambient reduction sound. In either case, you probably wouldn't be too mad to have either pair with you on an airplane or commute. Sony WH-1000XM4C vs. Bose QuietComfort (2nd gen): Design and comfort Bose has a fun party trick Sony can't quite match up to. Credit: Bethany Allard / Mashable The Bose headphones boast comfort in the name, and they live up to the expectations they set. They have a slightly looser fit than the Sonys, which also helps, but ultimately have more plush ear cushions. The cushions are also replaceable, which is useful for future-proofing. Don't get me wrong, the Sony XM4Cs are still plenty comfortable, but if you're a chronic headphones wearer, the Bose headphones may suit your needs better. The headphones fold up to roughly the same size. Credit: Bethany Allard / Mashable Bose relies on tactile controls, however. Credit: Bethany Allard / Mashable Travel-wise, both these headphones fold up to a similar compact position that makes them easy to pop into a bag. The biggest difference in their design is down to preference: the Bose QC rely solely on tactile controls (buttons and a power switch), while the Sony headphones use touch controls predominantly for playback, with the addition of a power button and ANC button. Sony WH-1000XM4C vs. Bose QuietComfort (2nd gen): Companion app I'd never recommend buying one pair of headphones over another based on their companion app, but because these headphones are still an investment, it's worth knowing the ins and outs of the experience. Bose's app layout leans more elegant, showing all the customization options on one screen, while Sony requires a scroll. The Sony companion app requires some scrolling to see all the options. Credit: Screenshot / Sony While Bose's has it all laid out. Credit: Screenshot / Bose They're relatively equal in terms of customization — where Sony headphones offer much more audio customization, Bose headphones offer more noise cancellation customization. Sony WH-1000XM4C vs. Bose QuietComfort (2nd gen): Battery life Both headphones have decent battery life. Credit: Bethany Allard / Mashable But Sony beats out Bose by three hours. Credit: Bethany Allard / Mashable While I was somewhat disappointed Sony cut the 30-hour battery life from the original XM4s to the 27 hours on the XM4C headphones, the 24-hour battery life on the Bose QuietComfort headphones puts the extra few hours into perspective. It's a decent amount of battery life in both cases, but the three-hour edge from the Sony headphones could be the difference between struggling on the last stretch of a long flight. title: Is Boox worth it? I tried Booktoks new favorite e-reader brand.
author: mashable.com
content: In our world of rising tech prices , when a new device hits the scene, the ultimate question is: is it worth it? If you're going to spend your money, you want it to be the best of the best. But the so-called best really depends on your priorities — do you want something that's the best value, best performance, or has the best features? As someone who spends nearly every day writing about e-readers , Boox devices have shaken things up. These E Ink tablets challenge what we previously thought an e-reader could be, with added features you won't find on a Kindle or Kobo . But are they worth it? Well, that depends on what you're looking for. Boox pricing: Is it more expensive than a Kindle? First things first, let's talk price. Boox e-readers are really E Ink tablets, which means they can do a lot more than Kindle or Kobo e-readers. But does that affect their price? Less so than you'd think. Especially with tech prices on the rise, e-reader prices have been evening out across the board. Generally, Boox e-readers are more expensive than both Kindle and Kobo devices, but not by much. The best way to compare prices is to look at each brand's 6-inch e-reader prices. The Kindle is cheapest at $149.99, the Kobo Clara BW is $159.99, while the Boox Go 6 is $199.99. Get a Boox if you want an e-reader that can do more Typically, on an e-reader you can access your library and all the books in it, but that's about all you can do. Boox e-readers do more. So while you might be paying a little more for a Boox than you would for a similar Kobo or Kindle e-reader, you're also getting far more features. All Boox e-readers besides the Picco are Android devices, meaning they have access to the Google Play Store. That allows you to download any app. Yes, that means Libby , Kindle, and Kobo, but it also means you can get virtually any other app on there. Use Libby and Kindle? Access them on one device with ABoox e-reader. Credit: Samantha Mangino / Mashable In perusing BookTok to see how Boox users maximize their e-readers, it's clear that Boox tablets are almost like distraction-free phones. You can download Goodreads and StoryGraph to update your reading progress or even your fitness tracker app, all the things you might want to check before bed. It just means not having to pull out your phone and instead staying on a more distraction-free tablet. But keep in mind, Boox devices are about as distraction-free as you make them. Since you can download any app, that also means you could get social media on there too. How does the Boox perform against Kindle and Kobo e-readers? The Boox Go 6 e-reader has solid performance but occasionally stalls out. Credit: Samantha Mangino / Mashable Kindle and Kobo devices are quick, but they're not as advanced as Boox e-readers. Credit: Samantha Mangino / Mashable While Boox devices are tablets, they're a little slower than other tablets . For example, the Boox Palma 2 has a Geekbench multi-core score of 1,872 compared to Apple's iPad, which scores 6,233. However, if you're comparing the processing power of a Boox to other e-readers, it'll seem on par. It has plenty of power to do what you need it to, like load books and turn pages. The only time Boox e-readers stalled out while I was testing them was when I was trying to turn a lot of pages in quick succession. Want more tech and digital culture news delivered to your inbox daily or sent straight to your device? Sign up for Mashable's Top Stories newsletter or get Mashable push alerts today. Skip it if you're a bath or beach reader If you live luxuriously and look forward to hours in the bathtub reading or taking your e-reader poolside, Boox e-readers are not for you. None of Boox's e-readers are submersible or have IPX waterproof ratings. Boox states that its Palma e-readers are water-repellent. Boox specifically notes on the Palma: "The water-repellent design protects against daily water exposure, including accidental spills, splashes, or light rain. It is not intended to be submerged in water, or exposed to high-pressure water, or other liquids. The water-repellent effect may decrease over time. Please note that it is not waterproof." So if you're reading around water, Boox e-readers aren't going to be worth it since you're so limited in where you can bring them. Is a Boox worth it? A Boox e-reader is worth the money, but is it right for you? Credit: Samantha Mangino / Mashable Boox e-readers are definitely worth the time and money, but who are they right for? Perhaps you're an e-reader user who is sick of being limited to one brand's ecosystem, or you want to buy a device that's more multi-purpose than a Kindle or Kobo. If you fall into either category, a Boox will be a great e-reader for you. When is a Boox not worth it? If you want an e-reader to take to the beach, skip it. But overall, Boox e-reader are solid, well-priced E Ink tablets that are definitely worth it for the right person. title: China is coming for the moon. NASAs answer: a faster, leaner plan
author: mashable.com
content: A faster, simpler plan can still put astronauts on the moon in 2028, despite a space rehearsal ahead of that landing running three months behind schedule, NASA leaders said Friday.  Administrator Jared Isaacman made the case at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, where crews have already started stacking the mega moon rocket for the expedited Artemis III mission. The two-week spaceflight around Earth would see four astronauts — Randy Bresnik, Andre Douglas, Frank Rubio, and Luca Parmitano — in the Orion spacecraft , connecting with two landers built by Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin and Elon Musk 's SpaceX in orbit.  Their new plan for the moon-landing mission, Artemis IV , scraps a distant orbit around the moon where the landers were once expected to pick up the crew, and it also cuts the number of rocket launches each landing needs. But NASA's timeline leaves almost no margin for error.  The stakes reach beyond science. Isaacman warned that NASA is in a new space race with China , which could land its own people on the moon within about three years.  "This is a story as much about their discipline, focus, and urgency, [as] it is about the weight of [NASA's] institutional inertia and displaced priorities and decades of decisions — some imposed upon us, and others of our own making — that have held America's space program back," Isaacman told reporters at a news conference.  SEE ALSO: Panel urges NASA to fetch Apollo 15 poop bags and hardware from moon The new plan to return to the moon depends on unproven technology. SpaceX's Starship lander burns so much fuel climbing to orbit that it can't reach the moon unless it fills up again in space. Other Starships would fly up as tankers and pump fuel into it , much like a fighter jet refueling in midair. Nobody has moved rocket fuel between spaceships on that scale.  SpaceX plans its first full attempt early next year, and that test should show how many tanker flights each moon trip takes. Once fueled, Starship would meet the astronauts near Earth and push their capsule to the moon. Starship only entered orbit for the first time last month. Blue Origin, on the other hand, skips the refueling but takes on a first of its own. It plans to launch three smaller spacecraft that work like tugboats. They would link up with the lander in orbit around Earth, then take turns hauling it to an easier lunar orbit than the one NASA originally conceived.  First, though, the company has to get flying again. Its New Glenn rocket hasn't launched since a catastrophic mishap in May that destroyed its launch pad.  Previously, NASA had chosen SpaceX's lander for its first two moon landings. Now the agency will keep both companies in the running before picking which one carries astronauts down first.  "Regardless of who goes first, both providers are planning for lunar landing missions in 2028," said Jeremy Parsons, NASA's Artemis program manager. The Artemis III mission is running about three months behind schedule, but NASA officials expect it to launch next year. Credit: NASA / Bill Stafford Want more science and tech news delivered straight to your inbox? Sign up for Mashable's Light Speed newsletter or get Mashable push alerts today. NASA attributes most of the Artemis III delay to late electronics parts for Blue Origin's lander. To claw back time, NASA has planted its own engineers inside suppliers' factories and requires daily progress reports from its major contractors. When a huge piece of Blue Origin's lander needed to cross the country fast, the agency borrowed a military cargo jet to fly it there, officials said. NASA also has started building more of its own hardware instead of outsourcing it to the private sector. A connection that feeds super-cold hydrogen into the Space Launch System rocket has had leaking issues in the past. The original fix would have taken years and tens of millions of dollars, Parsons said. NASA engineers redesigned and built a new one themselves for a fraction of the price in less than five months, he said. At a NASA center in Alabama, engineers also designed and built a part for the Artemis III rocket without hiring a contractor at all. That push comes from an unlikely source. The administrator is a tech billionaire, who made his fortune building a payments company . Business leaders usually argue that private companies beat the government on speed and cost. But when it comes to NASA, Isaacman argued nearly the opposite on Friday. He blamed bloated programs and a lobby of suppliers for slowing the agency down. The solution, he said, was more designing, welding, and machining performed in house.   "It's not entrepreneurial thinking or tech industry pixie dust or some new management philosophy," Isaacman said. "It's a playbook this agency knows really well — the same playbook that went from Apollo 7 splashdown to Apollo 11 in just nine months." NASA and Axiom Space are developing a pared-down Artemis IV spacesuit to speed up development. Credit: NASA / Bill Stafford To save time, NASA also has trimmed its own ambitions. NASA and its contractor, Axiom Space, are developing a pared-down spacesuit for the first short moonwalks that would weigh about 250 pounds, roughly half as much as the original. The agency also scrapped an expensive, delayed new top section for its rocket, the part that gives the capsule its final shove toward the moon, and picked a stretched version of one that United Launch Alliance already builds for its own rockets. Speed makes some people nervous, and with reason. In 1967, a fire during a launch pad test killed three Apollo astronauts. Isaacman and Amit Kshatriya, NASA's associate administrator, argued that moving fast doesn't mean cutting corners.  "Speed and rigor are not the same dial. They're just not," Kshatriya said. "We can dial them separately. Just because we go fast doesn't mean we're not doing the right things." All three rockets in NASA's plan head back to the launch pad within months. SpaceX could fly Starship again as soon as November, and Blue Origin hopes to return New Glenn to flight around the turn of the year. Before the close of 2026, NASA plans to load its own rocket with fuel at the launch pad.

title: Simone Biles sold her Texas home for under $1.25 million this month as she and Jonathan Owens move into custom mansion
author: Madz Dizon
content: Olympic gymnastics star Simone Biles has sold her Texas home after listing the property for $1.275 million, marking the end of a six-year chapter for the athlete and her husband, NFL player Jonathan Owens. The four-bedroom house in Spring, Texas, went under contract within days of hitting the market in September and officially closed on Oct. 15, 2026, according to Houston Business Journal . The final sale price was reported to be between $1.08 million and $1.24 million, below the property’s last asking price. Biles, 29, shared the news with fans through a TikTok video posted on Oct. 21. In the emotional clip, she walked through the nearly empty house and cried while talking about the memories she and Owens had made there. The sale comes after the couple completed their custom-built Texas mansion, a project they began planning in 2020 and started building in February 2022. The former home served as their living space while they waited for the new property to be finished. Now that the custom residence is complete, the couple has moved on from the Spring house as they adjust to Owens’ NFL career with the Indianapolis Colts. Although the property sold quickly, saying goodbye was not easy for Biles. In her TikTok video, recorded before the house was sold, the Olympic champion struggled to explain why leaving the place made her so emotional. “Why the [explicit] am I boohoo crying? [explicit]. This house will be on the market for the first time and I don’t know why I’m boohoo crying.” Biles explained that she had lived in the house for six years. During that time, she experienced happy moments and difficult ones, making the property an important part of her personal life. “I was here for six years, and I feel like there were just so many good memories, so many bad memories,” she continued. “But I feel like I grew up in this house. It’s made me a real adult, so I’m gonna miss it. Ugh, I didn’t think I’d be emotional about a house.” The video showed the house without most of its furniture, giving viewers a look at the space she was preparing to leave. Biles also showed the backyard, which includes a swimming pool. Despite her sadness, she shared a kind message for the home’s next owner. “Whoever buys this house, I hope it brings you as much joy as it did for me.” Biles later revealed that the sale happened faster than she expected. In the caption accompanying her TikTok video, she wrote: “The house sold in 4 days 😭. I was so excited to put in air fresheners for the potential buyers & showing Jonathan the last look. I just cried instead… anyone else? #emotionallyattached” Located in the gated Benders Landing Estates community in Spring, the property covers 3,998 square feet and sits on a lot of more than one acre. The four-bedroom, three-and-a-half-bathroom house was built in 2019. Biles purchased it in 2020 and it later became the couple’s home while their custom mansion was under construction. The property was listed for $1.275 million in September 2026. The house has several features designed for comfort, entertainment and everyday living. Its open layout connects the main living spaces, allowing natural light to enter through large openings that look out toward the backyard. The kitchen includes quartz countertops, a large waterfall-style island, modern appliances, custom cabinets, a wine wall and a hidden pantry. These features provide space for cooking and gathering with family and friends. The property also has two primary bedroom suites. The main suite includes a bathroom designed with a spa-like feel and two walk-in closets. The second suite sits behind double doors, offering another private sleeping area. Other indoor features include a media room, a separate study that can serve as a home office, and a sauna. The house also has a dedicated dog-washing station. Outside, a resort-style swimming pool serves as the main feature of the backyard. The pool has both heating and cooling systems, allowing the owners to adjust its temperature. A large patio surrounds the pool, creating room for outdoor meals and relaxation. The remaining space includes grass and landscaped areas. According to Homes of Celebs , the property also has an oversized three-car garage and a whole-home generator. The sale of the Spring home is closely tied to the couple’s long-awaited move into their custom-built Texas mansion. Biles and Owens began planning their new home in 2020. The design process took more than a year, and they later faced delays while waiting for approval from their homeowners association. Construction finally began in February 2022. What they initially expected to be a much shorter project took years to complete. The couple shared updates throughout the process, allowing fans to follow the home’s progress from the early building stages to the finished rooms. Biles announced that the mansion was complete in November 2025. After the construction work ended, the couple officially received their keys and prepared to move in. Reflecting on the long process, Biles previously wrote on Instagram: “Home building requires a lot of patience.” She also joked about how the original construction estimate had changed. “They lied when they said nine months to build!” The finished property features a custom design that reflects the couple’s preferences. Biles has shared glimpses of the house with her followers, including its kitchen, bedrooms, bathrooms, outdoor cooking area and swimming pool. In an interview with People in May 2025, she described how she and Owens worked together on the design. “I think we’ve done a good collab of what we wanted our house to look like.” The project became a major undertaking for the couple, who had to wait through design work, approvals and construction before they could settle into the finished home. Their new mansion is separate from the Spring property they recently sold. The former house served as a temporary home base during the years they spent waiting for the custom residence to be completed. The property sale also comes as Owens begins another chapter in his football career. The NFL safety signed a one-year contract with the Indianapolis Colts in March 2026 after previously playing for the Chicago Bears and other NFL teams. His move to Indianapolis has brought another change to the couple’s living arrangements. While maintaining their Texas home, Biles has also spent time in Indiana to support her husband during the football season. In September, Biles spoke about her plans to spend more time in Indianapolis. “I’ve been in Houston most of the time, so I’m going to officially move there [to Indianapolis] a little bit later,” Biles told Complex . She also spoke about what mattered most to her as Owens continued his career. “I’m just excited to watch my husband,” she said. “It doesn’t matter, as long as he’s safe and healthy and he’s having fun, then I don’t care.” For Biles, the Spring house was more than a property on the real estate market. She bought it in 2020, the same year she met Owens through the dating app Raya. They became engaged in February 2022 and married in April 2023. The house was therefore part of their lives before and during their marriage. It also remained their home while their custom-built mansion took shape. For Biles, the house may now belong to someone else, but the memories she made there remain part of her story. title: ‘Little People, Big World’ Star Amy Roloff’s Dad Dead at 97
author: Kayla Aldecoa
content: Little People, Big World stars are mourning the loss of Amy Roloff’s father, Gordon Knight. Amy and ex-husband Matt Roloff’s youngest son, Jacob Roloff, revealed the heartbreaking news on Monday, October 26. “My grandpa passed away 3 weeks ago. Haven’t necessarily slowed down enough to process that properly. I always hoped and looked forward to visiting him and my grandma in Michigan as a kid,” Jacob shared alongside a series of photos from his childhood in Michigan. “He may have intimidated me a bit, as grandpas can do, but he would smile and wink and you could feel softness.” Knight, who died at age 97 on October 5, shared four children with late wife Patricia Knight. “He was cleaning his muzzleloaders and driving his corvette 4 months ago,” Jacob added. “Going to miss him very very very much but I’m glad I found the time to go up and see him every summer in these last 4 years with Mateo, after far too long of a gap.” View this post on Instagram “I wish I asked him more questions, and for some reason particularly about his time in Korea, which he rarely mentioned,” he continued, referring to his grandfather’s time serving in the Korean War. “I enjoyed just sitting on the deck with him though. He saw a lot, an insane amount. Was able to vote for FDR, and ended up taking pictures of his great grandkids with an iPhone. Very admirable person who kept active, kept social, kept kind, kept reading, kept living.” Amy responded to her son, noting that she wished there were more opportunities to take Jacob and his siblings to visit her parents over the years. “I’m happy you had a chance to go and visit grandpa with me as an adult. I hope each one of you will have a special fond memory of him. 🙏🏻💙,” she wrote. According to his obituary, Knight was “known for his witty sense of humor as well as his ability to create, build, and survive.” View this post on Instagram He worked as a civil/structural engineer for Ford Motor Company for 30 years, and enjoyed participating in historical re-enactments in his retirement. The proud grandfather made occasional appearances on the family’s long-running TLC series.

title: 1975 Hit, Sung by Conway Twitty and His 16-Year-Old Daughter, Named One of the Best Age Gap Duets of the ‘70s
author: Gabriela Silva
content: Conway Twitty has made a name for himself for his hit country duets in his career, and in 1975, he allowed his teenage daughter, Joni Lee , to perform on a track that became a surprise hit on the charts. “Don’t Cry, Joni” has quit the backstory of how it was created, after some hesitation from Twitty. It’s one of the rare few tracks that he would release in his career without Loretta Lynn as his singing partner. Twitty was hesitant to let a 16-year-old Joni enter the music business, despite years of her trying to convince her father. The father and country singer wasn’t new to his children wanting to dabble in the music business. After two of his children, Kathy (aka “Jessica James”) and Mike (aka “Charlie Tango”), failed to make a hit, he wasn’t too keen on letting Joni also become a singer. Twitty ended up relenting to his daughter’s wishes and let her perform in the duet. “Don’t Cry, Joni” tells the story of a teenage Joni who falls in love with their 22-year-old neighbor, Jimmy. She asks Jimmy to wait for her until she’s old enough to marry, but he breaks her heart, telling her he cannot wait that long. He moves away to find the woman of his dreams and fails, realizing Joni was the perfect one all along. Jimmy returns home hoping to find Joni and ask her to marry him. To his surprise, Joni had fallen in love and married his best friend. There were never any details to suggest that the lyrics to the song were based on a true story, but Joni once revealed that her father had actually tricked her into appearing in the duet. “I had no idea I was going to be on the actual record,” she recalled to Billboard . “Dad kind of tricked me. He told me he was going to take my voice off of the track and replace it with a professional singer. When I went into the studio, my paper was shaking so badly from holding the paper to read the lyrics from.” Twitty’s other track “Touch The Hand” had become a success with radio jockeys, who soon flipped the record over and began playing “Don’t Cry, Joni.” To everyone’s surprise, the song hit the charts at No. 63 and No. 4 on the Billboard Country Singles chart. “I was going to college up in Virginia, and said ‘You’re not going to believe this. We have a hit record.’ I had no idea that my voice was still on the record. Being a kid, I started calling the radio stations asking them to play that new song by Conway Twitty and his daughter,” said Joni. Joni went on to continue her music career in the 1970s as Joni Penn. Her solo single “I’m Sorry Charlie” peaked at No. 16 on the Hot Country Songs chart. Grunge named the track as one of the best duets of the ’70s that had a sizable age gap between its singers. title: Matthew Perry Had 5 Half-Siblings: Meet His Family
author: Meredith Gordon
content: Nearly three years after Matthew Perry died at age 54, his family is sharing a more personal side of the Friends star in a new Netflix documentary . The One About Matthew Perry premieres October 27, 2026, one day before the third anniversary of his death on October 28, 2023. The three-part series features the first on-camera interview with Perry’s younger half-sister, Mia Perry Bowick , alongside accounts from two of his lifelong friends and never-before-seen family photos and videos. Perry had five half-siblings, and the documentary offers a rare glimpse of the family relationships that shaped his life beyond his iconic role as Chandler Bing. Matthew Perry’s Family: Parents, Stepfather and Five Half-Siblings View this post on Instagram Matthew Perry was born on August 19, 1969, to actor John Bennett Perry and Canadian journalist Suzanne Morrison . His parents separated before his first birthday, and he spent much of his childhood between Canada and California. His mother later married journalist Keith Morrison, best known for his work on Dateline NBC , who helped raise Matthew. Perry had five half-siblings through his parents’ later relationships and marriages. Four are from his mother’s side of the family, and one is from his father’s side. Caitlin Morrison: Perry’s maternal half-sister. Emily Morrison: Another maternal half-sister. William “Will” Morrison: Perry’s maternal half-brother. Madeline “Maddy” Morrison: His maternal half-sister, also known as Maddy. Mia Perry Bowick: Perry’s paternal half-sister, the daughter of John Bennett Perry and his second wife, Debbie Boyle. She is featured in the Netflix documentary, sharing personal memories of her brother. Although Perry became famous around the world for playing Chandler Bing, his family knew a side of him that audiences rarely saw. Mia’s participation offers a chance to hear directly from someone who shared a family bond with the actor. Related: Michael Bloomberg’s Childhood Visits to This Museum Inspired a Lifelong Love of Learning; Now He’s Giving $155 Million in Honor of His Parents Who Took Him There What Matthew Perry’s Sister Shares in the Netflix Documentary The One About Matthew Perry features the first on-camera interview with Mia Perry Bowick, along with accounts from Perry’s lifelong friends Roger Castillo and David Pressman . The series draws on family photos and videos that have not been seen publicly before, offering a more intimate look at the actor away from the spotlight. Bowick, a licensed psychotherapist, has said she hopes the documentary will help viewers see her brother as a whole person, rather than defining him solely by his most famous role or the personal challenges he faced. Her perspective adds a family dimension to the story of a performer whose life was often discussed in public. Did Matthew Perry Have a Wife or Children? Although Chandler Bing found his happy ending with Monica Geller, played by Courteney Cox , Perry never married and had no children. He had several high-profile relationships, including a romance with actress Julia Roberts in the 1990s. Perry was also engaged to literary manager Molly Hurwitz . The couple announced their separation in 2021. How Matthew Perry’s Family Is Honoring His Legacy Since Perry’s death on October 28, 2023, his family has helped keep his memory alive and supported efforts to raise awareness about addiction and recovery. His stepfather, Keith Morrison, and half-sister Caitlin have been involved in efforts connected to Perry’s legacy and addiction awareness. The new documentary adds to those efforts by sharing memories from the people who knew him long before he became a household name. For viewers who knew Perry primarily as the quick-witted Chandler Bing, these family stories offer a reminder that his life extended far beyond his most famous role.
