title: In 1927, Harry Lender bought a New Haven bagel bakery for $600; 69 years later, Kellogg paid $455 million for the business
author: Andrea Potenciano
content: Jewish baker Harry Lender worked in a small bakery in New Jersey and later decided to buy his own bakery in New Haven for $600 in 1927. Nearly seven decades later, Kellogg Co. purchased the family business from Kraft Foods for $455 million. Lender’s bakery was only 800 square feet, which he eventually named The New York Bagel Company. His shop specialized in New York-style bagels during a time when the product was heavily associated with the Jewish community. By 1934, Lender’s business had grown enough to warrant an increase in production. To that end, Lender bought a family house with a 1,200-square-foot garage. It was the former location of the Regna Italian Bread Bakery. His sons assisted with the bagel production, helping him for more than 30 years. The larger workspace supported the growth of the family’s business. Murray Lender of Lender’s Bagels displays a heart-shaped bagel. New York Daily News Archive / Getty Images As the demand for bagels continued to grow, the family looked for possible ways to increase production and distribute its products beyond the local market. In 1955, the Lenders began selling packaged bagels in supermarkets. Five years later, the company also started freezing bagels for delivery outside New Haven, increasing shelf life and enabling it to expand its customer reach nationwide, as reported by Baking Business . After Harry’s death in 1960, his sons Murray and Marvin took control and expanded production. By 1984, the family managed four factories that collectively produced more than 750 million bagels annually, according to Walk New Haven . The same year, Kraft Foods acquired the business from the Lender family. After 12 years, Kraft sold the company to Kellogg Co., per Supermarket News. The purchase broadened Kellogg’s breakfast-food portfolio, which includes Eggo waffles, Pop-Tarts, and Nutri-Grain bars. title: Taylor Swift Makes History as Youngest-Ever Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame Inductee
author: Aayush Sharma
content: The accolades just keep on coming for Taylor Swift. On Monday, October 26, the singer marked a major career milestone by being inducted into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame. By doing so, the 36-year-old musician became the youngest person ever to receive the award. While accepting the honor, she emphasized the role that the city’s songwriting community has played in shaping the artist she is today. She said (via Rolling Ston e) , “There is no music community like this music community. I know. I checked all the communities. There’s no one doing it.” During her speech, Swift opened up about the lessons she had picked up working with experienced songwriters in Nashville when she was a teenager, and stated that the relationships she had formed there enabled her to acquire the abilities that later allowed her to shift between different musical genres. “I was lucky enough to get a publishing deal with Sony Publishing when I was 14, and I just hit the ground running. I was like a sponge, and I have really curly hair, and it was yellow, so I kind of looked like a sponge too,” Swift noted. NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE – OCTOBER 26: (EDITORIAL USE ONLY. NO STANDALONE PUBLICATION USE (NO SPECIAL INTEREST OR SINGLE ARTIST PUBLICATION USE; NO BOOK USE)) (L-R) Brad Paisley, Taylor Swift and Lainey Wilson attend the 56th Nashville Songwriters Hall Of Fame Gala at Music City Center on October 26, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Kevin Mazur/Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for TAS) Swift said that from the moment she wrote her first song, it would be her passion even if it wasn’t her career. She also mentioned the people who guided her in those early years and said the songwriting community significantly shaped both her artistic skills and her personal growth. The Cardigan hitmaker added, “I’ve been very fortunate I’ve gotten to genre hop and travel the world and write with so many different people and in so many different ways. And the only reason that I’ve been able to have that kind of dexterity in my creative process is because of the fundamentals and the foundation that I learned here in Nashville.” Swift concluded her speech by saying that she feels grateful to be honored by her own and she would always remember this moment. “I will cherish it forever because Nashville is the place that honed and polished the thing about myself and the thing about my life that I am the most proud of and the most passionate about. So to be here with you and to be getting to have this moment, I am truly grateful, and it just feels like one of those amazing Nashville moments I’m going to revisit on a rainy day,” the musician concluded. The songwriter’s career actually started well before she began doing stadium concerts and releasing records that broke sales figures. She was born in Pennsylvania and began composing songs when she was a child, then moved to Hendersonville, Tennessee, with her family in 2004 in order to take advantage of the opportunities in Nashville. Her first album, which was titled the same as Taylor Swift , was released in October 2006 and included songs like “Tim McGraw” and “Teardrops on My Guitar”. The next album in 2008, Fearless , increased her popularity through the songs “Love Story” and “You Belong With Me”. The early successes she achieved in the country music field laid the foundation for the songwriting that Swift says enabled her to move on to pop and other musical genres in later years. title: ’90s Rock Legends Score Their 9th No. 1 Hit, 32 Years After Debuting With ‘The Blue Album’
author: DeAnna Janes
content: More than 30 years after helping define alternative rock, Weezer has another reason to celebrate. The band’s “ We Might as Well Be Strangers ,” featuring indie-rock group Wednesday , has climbed to No. 1 on Billboard ’s Alternative Airplay chart dated Oct. 31 , giving Weezer its ninth chart-topper . It’s a timely milestone for a band that has connected with new generations without abandoning the sound that made it famous. Weezer & Wednesday Top Alternative Airplay With ‘We Might as Well Be Strangers’ https://t.co/9NBFTan8VK — billboard charts (@billboardcharts) October 26, 2026 The song’s success also highlights an unexpected musical partnership. Weezer frontman Rivers Cuomo shares vocals with Wednesday’s Karly Hartzman , whose raw, conversational style gives the track a different texture from the band’s classic hits. 🎬 SIGN UP for Parade’s Daily newsletter to get the latest pop culture news & celebrity interviews delivered right to your inbox 🎬 How Weezer and Wednesday Came Together “We Might as Well Be Strangers” arrived in June as the second single from Weezer’s 20th studio album, The Gold Album . Rather than a brief guest cameo, the collaboration gives Hartzman a full verse, with her voice and Cuomo’s intertwining in the chorus. In an interview with Rolling Stone , Cuomo described how quickly the idea took shape. Hartzman sat down, pulled up a text file on her phone, and presented her idea while producer Kenneth Blume played the track. “She just pulled out some text file on her phone, and Kenny played the track, and she sang it to me,” Cuomo recalled. The song explores the emotional distance that can grow between people after a relationship breaks down, with Hartzman’s verse bringing a different perspective and creating a dialogue rather than a conventional guest appearance. Weezer Keeps Finding New Ways to Reach Fans Weezer emerged from Los Angeles in the early 1990s and broke through with its 1994 self-titled debut, better known as The Blue Album . Songs such as “ Buddy Holly ,” “ Undone – The Sweater Song ,” and “ Say It Ain’t So ” helped establish the band’s mix of catchy melodies, crunchy guitars, and self-conscious humor. But the group’s longevity hasn’t meant standing still. The Gold Album follows a long-running, color-themed album tradition, and the band reportedly emphasized live playing, with members responding to one another rather than relying on a rigid digital grid. Wednesday Brings a Different Indie-Rock Energy Wednesday , the North Carolina indie-rock band led by Hartzman, has earned attention for its blend of guitar-heavy rock, country influences, and vivid, often unsettling storytelling. Its sound differs sharply from Weezer’s bright power-pop hooks, making the collaboration feel like a meeting of musical generations rather than a simple nostalgia play. Now, with “ We Might as Well Be Strangers ” reaching No. 1 on the Alternative Airplay chart, the partnership has delivered a major milestone for both acts. For Weezer , it’s a ninth chart-topper more than three decades into its career; for Wednesday , it’s another opportunity to introduce its voice to a much broader audience. The result reminds that alternative rock’s past and present don’t have to compete. Sometimes, they can share a song and reach the top of the charts together . title: 1960s Carpenters Legend, Whose Solo Album Was Shelved for 16 Years, Named One of the Era’s Most Beautiful Voices
author: DeAnna Janes
content: Karen Carpenter is being celebrated once again for her extraordinary voice.  On Oct. 25 , Grunge included the Carpenters singer among the most beautiful female voices of the 1960s , with Elton John once calling her “one of the greatest voices of our life-time.”  But behind that unmistakable voice was a gifted musician who wanted to do more than repeat the formula that made her famous. View this post on Instagram In 1979 , while her brother and musical partner, Richard Carpenter , took a break from their career, Karen seized the opportunity to record a solo album. The project allowed her to explore a different sound, but it would remain unreleased for years, leaving fans to wonder what might have happened if she’d been given the chance to strike out on her own. 🎬 SIGN UP for Parade’s Daily newsletter to get the latest pop culture news & celebrity interviews delivered right to your inbox 🎬   Karen Carpenter Wanted to Find Her Own Sound The Carpenters became one of the biggest musical acts of the 1970s , known for polished arrangements and hits including “ Close to You ” and “ We’ve Only Just Begun .” Richard was the group’s principal musical architect, while Karen’s warm, remarkably controlled voice became its defining feature. When Richard entered rehab in 1979 , Karen decided she wouldn’t simply wait for the duo to resume. She traveled to New York to work with acclaimed producer Phil Ramone , with arrangements by musicians including Bob James . Instead of re-creating the Carpenters’ familiar soft-rock sound, the album ventured into disco, rock, and blues.  “She was beginning to free herself, but she was not free,” songwriter Tom Bahler said of Karen’s efforts to establish her independence, according to The Guardian .  The Album That Never Came Out During Her Lifetime Despite the ambition behind the project, the album didn’t receive the response Karen had hoped for. After its completion, the reaction from executives and others was lukewarm, and it was shelved in May 1980 . The decision meant that audiences never got to hear this different side of Karen while she was alive. She died in February 1983 , at age 32, from heart failure associated with anorexia nervosa. Her solo album finally appeared in 1996 , 13 years after her death, charting as high as No. 19 internationally. A Different Side of an Iconic Voice The album’s eventual release offered listeners a glimpse of an artist eager to stretch beyond the role that had made her a star. It didn’t erase the Carpenters’ legacy; it added another dimension to it. Karen remains best remembered for the tenderness and precision of her singing. But her solo work also leaves behind a tantalizing question: What else might she have accomplished if she’d had more time—and more opportunities—to define her career on her own terms? Whatever the answer, one thing’s certian: It would have sounded beautiful. Related: 1982 Ballad, Which Knocked Kenny Rogers From No. 1, Named One of Soft Rock’s Greatest One-Hit Wonders

title: Morrissey Upped the Sad Factor on This 1985 Smiths Song Now Ranked the Best Alternative Song of the Decade
author: Meredith Gordon
content: There are few bands that define the ’80s alternative sound like The Smiths, who paired Johnny Marr’s stunning arrangements with Morrissey’s yearning lyrics about longing, romantic devotion and wanting to belong. Few songs capture the decade’s ethos like “There Is a Light That Never Goes Out.” Now, a new ranking names it the best alternative song of the 1980s. Released on the band’s 1986 album The Queen Is Dead , the song captures Marr and Morrissey at their best. “This is the whole package Smiths-wise in a single song, and maybe a little more, since there are small amounts of warmth here that shine through,” Collider shares, before pointing to the tune’s dark, funny and cynical lyrics (would it be a Smiths song without a dose of cynicism?). The contrast between the beautiful, almost lilting music and the dark humor of the lyrics is what makes the song so distinctive. Few bands of the era could make the morbid seem almost beautiful quite like The Smiths. Here, they do just that. Related: Your Favorite College Rock Band of the 1980s Was Formed at the University of Georgia and Just Beat The Cure and The Smiths for No. 1 Why the Song Still Resonates “There Is a Light That Never Goes Out” captures the intense emotions of young adulthood: the feeling of being an outsider while searching for connection, and the belief that the right person can make the rest of the world all but disappear. Its combination of romantic longing and Morrissey’s undeniable wit has helped make it one of the band’s signature songs. The track regularly appears on critics’ best-of lists and topped NME readers’ 2011 poll of the band’s greatest songs. Its latest accolade underscores The Smiths’ lasting influence on British indie music, which can be heard in the work of artists such as Oasis and the Stone Roses. title: Walter Koenig Was Disappointed With This ‘Star Trek’ Film for One Specific Reason
author: Nicole Moore
content: While late actor Walter Koenig , who died on October 25 at the age of 90, took pride in his Star Trek role as Pavel Chekov, he wasn’t too happy about one of the franchise’s films. In a 2025 interview on That’s Classic , Koenig, who began playing Chekov during the second season of Star Trek: The Original Series , said he felt disappointed in the 1991 film, Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country . He said he was unhappy about the movie’s lack of recognition for the Star Trek: TOS secondary characters, like Chekov, Montgomery “Scotty” Scott ( James Doohan ), Nyota Uhura ( Nichelle Nichols ), and Hikaru Sulu ( George Takei ). “I was very upset with Star Trek VI , not because it wasn’t a good script. It was a good script. It was intelligently written and well performed, etc., but I felt that the subordinate characters were given a short shrift. And we’ve been with Star Trek , I mean, I’ve been with it since 1967. George and Nichelle and Jimmy had been with it since 1966,” said the actor. “And I thought there should have been a scene for each of us that acknowledged, you know, our endurance and our loyalty and our continuity being part of all this.” He clarified that he “was never concerned that [his] part wasn’t big enough” as Chekov in the Star Trek franchise. Rather, he believed Chekov, Uhura, Sulu, and Scotty deserved to be treated as “three-dimensional” characters in the final film that focused on the Star Trek: TOS crew. In addition, Koenig admitted that he didn’t hide his disappointment about Star Trek: TOS . “I was disappointed, very disappointed, and I kind of overreacted. That’s who I am, and so I saw articles about our complaining, complaining about me complaining, that I should feel just so lucky to be a part of this, that I had no right to feel umbrage,” said Koenig. “I’m who I am. I wasn’t a happy camper. I was pleased that the movie was good, you know, that everybody did a good job, who had a role to play. That was worthwhile, but, yeah, I was disappointed.”

title: ’80s Rock Legends Spent More Than $1 Million Making Their Biggest Album, ‘4’—And Nearly Fell Apart in the Process
author: DeAnna Janes
content: For Foreigner, October 1981 was a pretty good time to be a rock star. The band’s fourth album, aptly titled 4 , was still riding high on the charts, sitting at No. 2 on Billboard ’s rock albums chart for the week ending Oct. 31 , 45 years ago. Packed with enduring hits including “ Urgent ,” “ Juke Box Hero ,” and “ Waiting for a Girl Like You ,” the record would become one of the group’s signature achievements. View this post on Instagram 🎬 SIGN UP for Parade’s Daily newsletter to get the latest pop culture news & celebrity interviews delivered right to your inbox 🎬 But behind those arena-ready anthems was a far less glamorous story.​ Foreigner spent more than $1 million making 4 , endured months of grueling studio sessions, and watched relationships strain under the pressure. The album that helped define the band’s sound nearly pushed its creators to the breaking point. Foreigner’s Million-Dollar Gamble Released on July 2, 1981 , 4 followed the band’s 1979 album, Head Games . Guitarist Mick Jones and singer Lou Gramm wanted to take Foreigner in a fresh direction, and producer Robert John “Mutt” Lange , who would later become famous for his work with Def Leppard , helped shape the record. Lange was a perfectionist, and Jones was hardly one to settle for less. Their shared determination led to painstaking work on songs and sounds, but it also made the sessions extraordinarily expensive. In a 2026 retrospective for Classic Rock , bassist Rick Wills recalled the mounting financial pressure. “We’d spent over a million dollars in recording costs,” he said, describing pressure from the record company, management, and the band itself. The group’s manager, Bud Prager , repeatedly had to seek additional advances from Atlantic Records to keep paying for studio time. As Wills explained, once they had invested so much, turning back wasn’t really an option. They would need to sell an enormous number of records to make the gamble pay off. 9 Months of Perfectionism … and Exhaustion The recording process stretched across much of a year, moving from Atlantic Studios to New York’s Electric Lady Studios . The band and Lange worked through long nights, continually refining arrangements and performances. They didn’t always agree. Jones later described himself and Lange as “two goats”—both stubborn, both unwilling to back down. The producer’s intense dedication could be difficult, but it also pushed the material toward the sound Jones had envisioned. The sessions even brought in a then-little-known English keyboard player, Thomas Dolby , whose contributions helped shape the album. Soul musician Junior Walker gave “ Urgent ” its distinctive saxophone solo, after Jones invited him to the studio after seeing him perform nearby. The Risk That Became a Rock Classic Eventually, the work paid off. 4 spent 10 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 , sold more than six million copies in the U.S., and produced six singles, according to Classic Rock . “Urgent” reached No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100, while “Waiting for a Girl Like You” climbed to No. 2. Related: ’70s Rock Band Delivers Soulful Performance of Longest-Running No. 2 Hit in Rock History Looking back, Jones acknowledged that the price wasn’t only financial. “Relationships got strained during that album,” he said. “Domestic situations got out of control.” Still, he considers 4 his favorite Foreigner album, calling it the culmination of what the band had been building toward. He said the process was “long, grueling, and costly.” For fans, the result was a collection of songs that helped define early-’80s rock. For the musicians who made it, the record was proof that sometimes a classic comes at a staggering cost. title: In 1922, Charles H. ‘Chuck’ Taylor walked into Converse complaining of sore feet; 81 years later, Nike bought the company for $305 million
author: Jacqueline Burt Cote
content: When 47-year-old footwear manufacturing manager Marquis Converse founded the Converse Rubber Shoe Company in Malden, Mass., in February 1908, nobody ever could have predicted that the brand would end up manufacturing one of the most iconic sneakers in history. In fact, the first type of shoe made by the company were galoshes. Then, in 1917, the company designed a canvas basketball shoe with a rubber sole called the All Star…and changed history forever. Actually, the history of mass-produced basketball shoes really changed a few years later. In 1922, former professional basketball player Charles H. “Chuck” Taylor started working for Converse as a sneaker salesman and marketer. Taylor, who was also a player and coach for the company’s industrial basketball team, the “Converse All-Stars,” suffered from sore feet and helped redesign the All Star to be more comfortable. Taylor’s input, as well as his success promoting the All Star at touring clinics, was held in such high esteem that the company added his name to the ankle patch in 1934. The decades that followed saw the All Star grow in popularity and cultural relevance alike. By 2008, an estimated 800 million pairs had been sold, with more than 60 percent of Americans owning a pair of Chuck Taylor All Stars during their lifetime. NBA Photos / Getty Images “They have a unique style, but are still classical,” said Hal Peterson, author of Chucks!: The Phenomenon of Converse: Chuck Taylor All Stars . “They are also very retro and comfortable, and appeal to many different groups because of the variations possible with canvas uppers.” Chucks became a footwear mainstay for all kinds of celebrities, from rock stars like the Ramones and Kurt Cobain to athletes including Larry Bird and Magic Johnson , both of whom starred in a famous Converse ad campaign in the ’80s. Unfortunately, in the mid-80s, Nike offered Jordan more money than Converse, leading to the birth of the Air Jordan franchise in 1985. Air Jordans exploded in popularity over the next decade and beyond; in 2007, the Jordan brand grossed approximately $800 million. Converse couldn’t quite compete, and the company’s stock value fell to 20 cents per share before it filed for bankruptcy in 2001. Of course, that wasn’t the end of Chucks: Nike bought the company for $305 million in 2003. Almost a century after the Converse Rubber Shoe Company was founded, the Converse All Star remains one of the best-selling basketball shoes in the world. title: In 1982, the Red Hot Chili Peppers’ First Show Consisted of 1 Song for a Tiny Crowd; 44 Years Later, Their Music Catalog Is Worth More Than $300 Million
author: DeAnna Janes
content: The Red Hot Chili Peppers recently returned to the stage for a special October performance, reminding fans that even one of rock’s most successful bands still has deep roots in the Los Angeles music scene. On Oct. 17 , the group headlined a benefit celebrating the Silverlake Conservatory of Music ‘s 25th anniversary, the nonprofit school co-founded by bassist Flea . The band even dusted off songs it hadn’t played live in more than 25 years. View this post on Instagram It was a fitting occasion for a group whose own story began on a much smaller stage. 🎬 SIGN UP for Parade’s Daily newsletter to get the latest pop culture news & celebrity interviews delivered right to your inbox 🎬 When the band played its first show in December 1982 , fewer than 50 people showed up, with the musicians performing just one song. More than four decades later, however, their recorded-music catalog sold for a reported $300 million-plus . The Red Hot Chili Peppers Started With Just 1 Song Before they became the Red Hot Chili Peppers, Anthony Kiedis , Flea , guitarist Hillel Slovak, and drummer Jack Irons came together for what was supposed to be a one-off performance at a Hollywood club. Their friend Gary Allen needed an opening act for his EP release party, and the group agreed to play. But, they had barely rehearsed. Still, Flea had a bass line, Kiedis had a poem, and they performed “ Out in L.A. ” In a 1990 interview with SPIN , Flea recalled the unlikely beginning, saying, “We had one song, and we did it, and people went wild.” The response encouraged them to keep going. Their next performance featured two songs, and the band began building a following in Los Angeles. So, even though the first show was hardly a sign of the global success to come, it marked the beginning of a career that would span generations. From Tiny Crowds to a $300 Million Catalog The band’s breakthrough arrived with 1991 ’s Blood Sugar Sex Magik , which featured hits including “ Under the Bridge ” and “Give It Away .” Later albums, including Californication , helped cement the Chili Peppers as one of the era’s most commercially successful rock acts. In May 2026 , the group sold its recorded-music catalog to Warner Music Group in a deal reportedly worth more than $300 million . The package included 13 studio albums and reportedly generated around $26 million annually.​ The transaction followed an earlier sale of the band’s publishing rights, underscoring just how valuable its decades of music had become. Flea’s Other Legacy Is Helping Young Musicians The October benefit also highlighted a different part of the band’s legacy. Flea co-founded the Silverlake Conservatory of Music in 2001 to expand access to music education, including scholarships for students whose families cannot afford lessons. The school now serves more than 1,000 students each week. So when the Chili Peppers took the stage earlier this month, they weren’t simply revisiting old songs. They were supporting a community built around the same art form that brought four young musicians together for a one-song performance in 1982 . Fewer than 50 people witnessed that first show. Today, the band’s music is worth hundreds of millions, with its influence reaching far beyond the stage. And that is a red-hot legacy. title: Jay-Z Is Headlining the 2027 Super Bowl Halftime Show, and the Announcement Is a Full-Circle Moment
author: Kait Hanson
content: Jay-Z has spent years helping decide who takes the Super Bowl halftime stage, and now, he’s taking it himself. The rapper has officially been announced as the headliner for the 2027 Apple Music Super Bowl Halftime Show. The NFL, Roc Nation and Apple Music announced the news on Monday, October 26, during ESPN’s Monday Night Football broadcast featuring the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys . “GOAT’s out of the bag,” Roc Nation teased in a social media post announcing the news. View this post on Instagram The big game is scheduled for February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. “From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl halftime stage, this has been a journey,” Jay-Z said in a statement to People . “Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world’s biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true.” The announcement marks a notable turn for the 56-year-old artist. Since 2019, Jay-Z and his entertainment company, Roc Nation, have partnered with the NFL to help oversee the league’s live music entertainment, including selecting and producing the Super Bowl halftime show. In other words, the man who has helped decide who gets the coveted halftime slot will now be taking the spotlight himself. The announcement comes after weeks of speculation that Jay-Z would take the stage himself and during a significant stretch for the Grammy-winning rapper. Jay-Z has been celebrating the anniversaries of two landmark albums, his 1996 debut, Reasonable Doubt , and 2001’s The Blueprint . He also recently released the eight-part HBO docuseries JAŸ-Z in 8 , which explores his music and career. Jay-Z will follow Bad Bunny, who headlined the 2026 Super Bowl halftime show, which drew 128.2 million viewers and earned a record nine Emmy nominations.

title: Willem Dafoe Explains Why He Prefers Movies Over TV Shows
author: Aayush Sharma
content: Willem Dafoe is considered to be one of the most versatile actors working in the industry right now and has spent his career taking on some of the most demanding roles in Hollywood. However, it seems he is not particularly enamored with the streaming TV phenomenon. The acclaimed actor has made it clear that there is a reason why he chooses movies over television and explained that the work required of an actor in a feature film is of a different order. Moreover, he noted the film format provides the audience with a more focused experience. Speaking in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter India , Dafoe opens up about his dedication to film and his qualms about long-form narrative. He does admit that TV series have their place but maintains that he is far more interested in the cinema and the possibilities it affords. For him, the primary concern is that the length of the TV format gives the actor so much time to develop a character that the performance can end up being less urgent. He feels a film has to be more focused in that it has a much shorter time in which to make its impact. “The point is I’m not that attracted to doing a series. Many people like them, but I think they don’t hold your feet to the fire. You have a long time to reveal (something), which may be a good thing, but it takes away a certain kind of discipline in what you’re doing,” Dafoe noted during the interview. The 71-year-old actor also referenced the bond that forms between the viewer and a character over the course of multiple episodes. Consequently, the actor has a real appreciation for the cinema experience of going to the movies in the theater where you’ve got a bunch of strangers all sharing the same story. For Dafoe that shared experience between the performer and the audience is something that you simply can’t quite get by watching it at home. He added, “The theatrical experience is very important, and it’s why I maintain my involvement in theater on stage as well, because I think the personal encounter, the meeting of public and performer live, and also in an intimate setting is so important. I think, ironically, being in a theater with a bunch of strangers watching a light on a screen is more intimate than being at home, comfortable, watching it on… a TV of whatever size.” Dafoe’s reservations about TV go even further in terms of how some series are made. With different directors potentially working on different episodes you can see how difficult it can be to maintain a consistent creative vision. He likes to work on projects where one director is in charge and the cast and crew all work together to achieve that director’s vision. title: At 14, Warren Buffett spent $1,200 of his paper route money on a 40-acre farm; 82 years later, he’s giving away nearly his entire $145 billion fortune
author: Andrea Reiher
content: In 1944, Warren Buffett was 14 years old and already thinking about what to do with the money he’d earned delivering newspapers. According to Forbes , the future billionaire saved about $1,200 from his paper route and other childhood ventures when he made a remarkably grown-up purchase: 40 acres of Nebraska farmland. It was an early investment for the Omaha native, who would go on to become one of the world’s richest people and one of its most prominent philanthropists. Buffett’s fascination with business began even earlier. He purchased his first stock at age 11. As a boy, he also sold chewing gum, Coca-Cola and magazines door-to-door before taking on newspaper routes. By his teens, Buffett was delivering hundreds of newspapers a day. The work was lucrative enough that he filed his first tax return at 13, famously claiming a deduction for the bicycle and watch he used on his route. The following year, he put some of his savings into something considerably larger. Buffett paid about $1,200 for 40 acres of farmland in Nebraska and arranged for a tenant farmer to work the property, according to accounts of his early life. Rather than simply spending his newspaper earnings, the teenager had turned them into an asset capable of producing more income. It was a remarkably early glimpse of the investing philosophy that would eventually make Buffett a household name. Buffett went on to study at the University of Nebraska before earning a master’s degree in economics from Columbia University, where he studied under famed value investor Benjamin Graham . In the decades that followed, Buffett transformed Berkshire Hathaway from a struggling textile company into a massive conglomerate with holdings and investments spanning insurance, railroads, energy, manufacturing and some of America’s most recognizable companies. His investing success earned him the nickname the “Oracle of Omaha” and built a fortune Forbes estimates at roughly $145 billion. But Buffett has spent years making plans for that fortune to eventually leave his hands. In 2006, Buffett announced that he would gradually give away the overwhelming majority of his Berkshire Hathaway shares to philanthropic foundations. Four years later, Buffett joined Bill and Melinda French Gates in launching the Giving Pledge, an effort encouraging the world’s wealthiest people to commit the majority of their fortunes to charitable causes. Buffett went considerably further than the pledge’s basic requirement. “More than 99% of my wealth will go to philanthropy during my lifetime or at death,” Buffett wrote in his Giving Pledge letter. He has already donated tens of billions of dollars worth of Berkshire Hathaway shares over the past two decades, making him one of the largest individual charitable donors in history. In recent years, Buffett has also laid out what will happen to his remaining wealth after his death. His three children will oversee a charitable trust tasked with distributing the money, with Buffett making clear that he does not intend to create a multigenerational dynasty from his fortune. It’s an extraordinary trajectory for money that started accumulating one newspaper at a time. At 14, Buffett took $1,200 he’d earned and saved and turned it into 40 acres of farmland. More than eight decades later, after turning those early instincts into one of the world’s largest fortunes, he’s preparing to send nearly all of it back out the door. title: In the 1970s, He Became a Fan Favorite on ‘Captain Kangarooo’ Wearing a Suit That Showed His Organs—50 Years Later, Here’s What Happened to Slim Goodbody
author: Christina Izzo
content: Some kids’ TV show hosts become household names across geography and generations: Mister Rogers , Mrs. Rachel , Bill Nye and the like. But other children’s entertainment personalities haven’t been as enduring in the public consciousness and instead exist in a sort of time capsule of viewers’ childhood memories. One such blast-from-the-past TV educator is John Burstein , better known to kids of the 1970s and ’80s as Slim Goodbody, a.k.a. “The Superhero of Health.” Costumed in a skintight, flesh-colored unitard decorated with biologically accurate organs, muscles, and skeletal structures, Mr. Goodbody taught youngsters about human anatomy, healthy nutrition, personal hygiene and exercise routines via songs, dances, skits and more. And while members of Generation X no doubt remember Slim Goodbody from his days on CBS and PBS, younger TV viewers might not be as familiar with Burstein’s signature character, especially after all these decades. Here’s what to know about Slim Goodbody and what John Burstein is up to these days. 🎬  SIGN UP for Parade’s Daily newsletter to get the latest pop culture news & celebrity interviews delivered right to your inbox  🎬  John Burstein as “Slim Goodbody” with puppet, Inspector Thiamin, on “Captain Kangaro.” CBS/Getty Images Who was Slim Goodbody? Slim Goodbody is an original character created and performed by actor-educator John Burstein. The performer adopted the alter ego while working at The Floating Hospital in his native New York in the mid-’70s; he wrote original songs and short skits about anatomy, digestion, and the inner workings of the human body to entertain the hospital’s disadvantaged children. “I came in, and I sang a couple of [songs], and somebody said, ‘You know what would be really good? You ought sell them to Sesame Street. ’ Then I said, ‘Gee, maybe I could sell myself to Sesame Street . What would that be, if I could do that? And it would be a custom character,” Burstein explained Goodbody’s genesis to the Bangor Daily News . “So I went to this funky loft on 14th Street and said, ‘I got this idea, and I want to do this sort of thing that looks like the body, but I don’t want it to be Gray’s Anatomy . I want it to be more superhero. So we sat down, and we marked some stuff up, and she built this costume for me.” Burstein then took the character to television, booking regular guest spots and cameo appearances before securing his very own television series, Inside Story , on PBS in 1980. Related: The Highest-Rated Episode of ‘Mister Rogers’ Neighborhood’ Was the Last One Ever Actor-educator John Burstein, in costume as ‘Slim Goodbody,’ in New York 1981. Brownie Harris/Corbis/Getty Images What show was Slim Goodbody on? In the early days of Burstein’s TV career, he appeared as Mr. Goodbody on daytime programs like The Today Show and Good Morning America . Between 1978 and 1981, he began guest-starring twice a week on the beloved CBS children’s series Captain Kangaroo, appearing opposite host Bob Keeshan in education segments like “The Adventures of Slim Goodbody in Nutri-City”. “[Producer Jim Hirschfeld] sent his production team to watch my show in New Jersey, and they really, really liked it,” Burstein recalled to The Hollywood Reporter about scoring the regular CBS gig. “And they say to me, ‘You are going to be on Captain Kangaroo .’” He later added: “ Captain Kangaroo gave me the credibility that enabled my whole career to flow. I just got a royalty check today from Discovery streaming for stuff I did 35 years ago.” After the popularity of his Captain Kangaroo cameos, Burstein spun his character off into his own educational series on PBS: The Inside Story with Slim Goodbody premiered in 1980 and soon became the station’s second-highest-rated program. Related: ’90s Kids Lock In, Bill Nye And Steve From ‘Blue’s Clues’ Gave An Interview Together Bob Keeshan and John Burstein on “Captain Kangaroo.” CBS When did Slim Goodbody end? Well, Slim Goodbody never really ended. The CBS educational television series The Inside Story with Slim Goodbody ended in the early 1980s. Still, John Burstein kept the character going both on-screen and off-screen for decades to follow, including Nickelodeon programs , educational shorts, health books, live appearances and more. Related: Ms. Rachel Is Taking Her Viral Toddler Hits Off-Screen in a Huge New Release John Burstein in “Well, Well, Well With Slim Goodbody” PBS Where is Slim Goodbody now? John Burstein, the man behind the Slim Goodbody persona, is now 76 years old. He lives with his wife, Chrissy, in a lakeside home in Lincolnville, Maine; they have two sons, Devin and Luke. Burstein has been appearing and educating as Mr. Goodbody for the better part of five decades, though these days, he’s better known online as “Grandpa Goodbody.” He continues to share educational health content for young viewers on his Instagram and YouTube channels, including short videos detailing everything from fine motor skills to easy magic tricks to the American political system . Nearly 50 years after creating Slim Goodbody, the performer has reflected on the legacy of the character and the impact he had on young people’s lives. “Slim lives on because it’s also iconic, the character in the suit, and people remember it from their childhood,” Burstein told the Bangor Daily News in 2020. “I don’t believe it when people say to me, ‘Oh, you made such a difference, you’re why I’m a doctor.’ Pfft, yeah, right. But to know that you’ve had a positive effect on people, for whatever small little bit, that feels very satisfying to me.”  Next, Whatever Happened To Steve From ‘Blue’s Clues’?

title: Jeff Bezos founded Amazon in his garage in 1994; 24 years later, he pledged $2 billion through his Day One Fund to help homeless families
author: Geca Flores
content: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos solidified his legacy in e-commerce after founding the tech and retail giant in 1994. What started in a humble garage in Bellevue, Washington, grew into one of the world’s largest online marketplaces. As the company grew into an e-commerce giant, Bezos also turned his attention to philanthropy, announcing a $2 billion commitment through the Bezos Day One Fund. With the early 1990s ushering in a transformative era for modern technology and commerce, he recognized the internet’s potential to reshape the way people shop. The Princeton University alum left his high-paying job on Wall Street and moved across the country in 1994 to start Cadabra, Inc., a startup he operated from the garage of his rental home in Bellevue, Washington. The company eventually became Amazon. Jeff Bezos, founder of Amazon, speaks on stage during the Italian Tech Week 2025. Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images “The wake-up call was finding this startling statistic that web usage in the spring of 1994 was growing at 2,300 percent a year,” the now-billionaire recalled, as cited by the Academy of Achievement, adding, “You know, things just don’t grow that fast. It’s highly unusual, and that started me thinking, ‘What kind of business plan might make sense in the context of that growth?’” Starting with just a vision and a unique business idea, Amazon officially launched on the World Wide Web in 1995 as an online bookstore.  Bezos worked alongside his then-wife, MacKenzie Scott, with the early operation involving tasks such as packing and shipping orders. View this post on Instagram The first book Amazon sold was Fluid Concepts and Creative Analogies: Computer Models of the Fundamental Mechanisms of Thought by Douglas Hofstadter. Within months of launching its website, Amazon had hired its first employee, Shel Kaphan, and was reportedly generating $20,000 in sales per week and was selling books across the United States and in 45 foreign countries. In 1997, Amazon went public through an initial public offering (IPO), setting its share price at $18. This allowed public investors to buy ownership stakes in the company. At the time, financial experts were unsure whether Amazon could survive competition from established retailers that were beginning to sell products online, according to Biography. However, the Bezos-led company continued to expand and established itself as a major force in e-commerce. From selling books to developing its cloud computing business, launching its Kindle e-reader and introducing Alexa and Echo smart devices, Amazon continued to diversify its offerings. Despite its commercial success, the company also became involved in philanthropy. In 2018, Bezos, then the world’s richest person and centi-billionaire, announced the creation of the Bezos Day One Fund, a philanthropic initiative designed to support homeless families and improve access to early childhood education through creating a network of tuition-free preschools in underserved communities. In a post on Twitter , now known as X, Bezos pledged an initial $2 billion from his personal wealth to support the initiative. The fund has awarded grants to charitable organizations since its launch. title: 1966 Hit, Ranked Among ‘Best Garage Rock Songs of All Time,’ Was Written by a 25-Year-Old Bricklayer
author: Jacqueline Burt Cote
content: If there’s one thing you can say about the Troggs, it’s that the ’60s rockers were pretty great at coming up with catchy tunes. Sure, “Wild Thing” was their biggest hit (not to mention one of the most popular singles of the era), but that wasn’t their only infectious anthem. Released as a single in 1966, “With a Girl Like You” went to the top of the charts in the U.K. and blew up in Europe. And while it wasn’t as popular in the U.S. as “Wild Thing,” released earlier that year, it peaked at #29 on the Billboard Hot 100 and remains a critical and fan-favorite decades later. In 2014, Paste ranked “With a Girl Like You” at #20 on their list of the “50 Best Garage Rock Songs of All Time,” with music writer Bonnie Stiernberg praising the track’s “simple romanticism,” noting, “there’s a reason this song gets a lot of play at weddings.” Not bad for a tune written by the Troggs’ lead vocalist Reg Presley when he was just a 25-year-old bricklayer. “I started writing on the building site when I was a bricklayer,” Presley told Stuart Maconie on BBC Radio 2 , adding, “We needed songs and I was bricklaying.” Though it was released after “Wild Thing,” the songs were recorded in the same session, according to 1,000 UK Number One Hits . As Presley explained, the part of the song that really gets stuck in your head (“ba ba ba ba ba, ba ba ba ba ba”) was inspired by the Beach Boys hit “Barbara Ann.” “We recorded it at the same time as ‘Wild Thing’ and either of them could have been released first,” Presley recalled. “I liked the way The Beach Boys were going ‘Ba-ba-ba-Barbara Ann’ and it was lovely to do something like that in ‘With a Girl Like You.’ We nearly had a trumpet playing it, but it sounded better when we sang it.” The Troggs didn’t have much time to make magic happen in the studio, but as it turned out, they didn’t need it. “In 45 minutes we had to get our gear in the studio, do the two songs and get out, because it was the end of his orchestra session and he left us only 45 minutes,” Presley said. “I mean our first album only took two and a quarter hours, how do you do that?” he continued with a laugh. “It almost takes that to play it.” One thing’s for sure: Just a few hours in the studio ensured that Presley’s bricklaying days were over for good. title: Alicia Keys and Swizz Beatz Have a Monthly Date Rule After 16 Years of Marriage—No Matter Where They Are in the World
author: Sam Sears
content: If you’re in a serious relationship, you know getting a date on the calendar can be a negotiation all its own.  Alicia Keys  and  Swizz Beatz  have already settled theirs. After 16 years of marriage, the singer and music producer still make time for a romantic outing every month—even when getting there involves more than a drive across town. In Keys’ November cover story for  Vogue Italia , published Oct. 26 , Beatz explained that wherever work takes him, he makes a point of showing up for their evening together. “No matter where I am in the world, I know I have to be there that evening,” he said, according to  People ’s translation of the interview . Apparently, being out of town doesn’t get him a rain check. Related: 2009 No. 1 Hit Became This Generation’s ‘New York, New York’—But Frank Sinatra Wasn’t the Inspiration One of those dates came with a particularly memorable setting: Razor House , the striking property in San Diego, California’s ritzy La Jolla beach hamlet, that the couple eventually purchased and renamed Dreamland. Beatz told  Vogue Italia  that the house had been his computer screensaver for eight years. When the opportunity arose, he arranged for a chef to prepare an evening there with Keys. Dinner with a view is one thing. Moving in afterward is another. The couple  married in July 2010  and share sons Egypt and Genesis. Their approach to staying close also extends to how they handle disagreements once date night is over. In a  March 2025 interview with  Us Weekly , Beatz said they disagree but avoid yelling at each other, crediting communication with helping them work through their differences. “When you yell at each other, no one is really listening anyway. Nothing gets solved in each other’s yelling,” he told the outlet. Related: Hip-Hop Pioneer That Megan Thee Stallion Credits as an Inspiration Announces Final Album: ‘This Is It’ He also emphasized that marriage doesn’t mean owning another person, describing both himself and Keys as independent people who choose to come together. Now, they’re bringing that partnership into a new project. The  Vogue Italia  interview introduces  Lovers Rose , their forthcoming joint album, with seven tracks drawing on R&B, Chicano soul and Latin musical traditions. That adds another shared commitment to the calendar. Their monthly date, however, already has its slot.

title: Former Miss Switzerland Accuses Donald Trump of Rape in Report Linking President to Jeffrey Epstein
author: Aayush Sharma
content: Former Miss Switzerland Beatrice Keul has accused President Donald Trump of raping her at the Plaza Hotel in New York City in November 1993, according to a new report from Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee looking into Trump’s alleged links to Jeffrey Epstein’s sex trafficking enterprise. The report, cited by People , claims that Keul was 24 at the time and worked as a model and in the financial services sector in Switzerland. She was recruited by Jill Harth to take part in the Donald J. Trump American Dream Pageant which took place in Atlantic City and New York in November 1993. At a press luncheon at the Plaza Hotel (which Trump owned at the time) he allegedly spoke to Keul and offered to help her get a US visa and get into NYU. Epstein came along afterwards and made the same offer to her, plus invited her to a party at Mar-a-Lago. The report claims that a Trump representative later invited Keul to meet him in a hotel suite. Believing the meeting could help her career and education, she accepted. However, things took a horrifying turn once she entered the suite. Keul alleges that Trump grabbed her from behind and raped her, leaving her with injuries. Consequently, the report also says that Trump subsequently asked her to remain silent, telling her, “The show must go on.” Keul returned to Switzerland after the pageant and declined to participate in another Trump-sponsored competition in Hawaii several weeks later, according to the report. The White House has denied all the allegations leveled at Trump, and he has not been charged with any crime in connection with the incident. In a statement given to People , White House spokesperson Lauren Bis shot down Keul’s allegations and called the report “politically motivated.” “None of these allegations are true. This ‘report’ is nothing more than a desperate attempt by crazed Democrats to distract Americans from the surging Republican momentum driven by President Trump’s historic achievements. The President kicked Jeffrey Epstein out of his club at Mar-a-Lago because he was a creep, and he has been fully exonerated of anything related to Epstein,” the spokesperson said in the statement. The report also refers to other allegations relating to Trump and Epstein (the 1997 sexual assault suit filed by Harth being one example). It makes reference to the alleged promises made to Keul and to the accounts of various women who have described how Epstein would use the promise of education and career opportunities as a means of recruiting and controlling his victims. This is not the first time Trump has been the subject of such allegations. In 2023 a civil jury found him liable in the case of the sexual abuse of writer E. Jean Carroll and the defamation of her. Trump denied any wrongdoing in that case. If you or someone you know has been a victim of sexual assault, help is available 24 hours a day through RAINN ‘s National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-4673. title: How Many ‘Powerless’ Books Are There? The Complete Lauren Roberts Reading Order
author: D. Schaller, Parade AI Desk, Larry Slawson
content: Lauren Roberts ’ Powerless series combines young adult fantasy, forbidden romance and a kingdom divided by supernatural abilities. The story follows Paedyn Gray, an ordinary girl forced to survive in a society that prizes magical power, and Kai Azer, a prince whose responsibilities put him on a collision course with her. Since the first novel arrived in 2023, the series has become a global bestseller, with Roberts’ books selling more than 5 million copies worldwide, according to publisher Simon & Schuster . The Powerless series includes three main novels and two companion novellas that expand the world of Ilya through other characters’ perspectives. Keep reading for a guide to all five books and the order in which to read them. Related: How To Read All of Colleen Hoover’s Books in Order All the Powerless Books in Order, Including the Novellas The main trilogy follows Paedyn and Kai’s story, while the two novellas offer additional perspectives on events in the series. Powerful takes place during Powerless , and Fearful unfolds during Fearless . Read the books in this chronological order: Powerless (2023) Powerful (2024) Reckless (2024) Fearless (2025) Fearful (2025) Powerless Simon & Schuster In Ilya , a mysterious Plague changed society by leaving some survivors with supernatural abilities. These gifted people, known as Elites, hold power over those born without abilities, called Ordinaries. Under the king’s rule, being an Ordinary is a dangerous secret to keep, and Paedyn Gray has learned to survive by stealing and staying out of sight. To avoid detection, Paedyn pretends to be a Psychic , an Elite who can read minds. Her sharp instincts help her maintain the lie until an unexpected encounter with a prince puts her in the public eye. Chosen to compete in the Purging Trials, a perilous test of Elite abilities, Paedyn must conceal the truth about herself while navigating a competition that could cost her life. Related: How To Read All of Kristin Hannah’s Books in Order—Including the Firefly Lane Series! Powerful Simon & Schuster Adena has spent years surviving in Loot alongside her best friend, Paedyn . But when Paedyn is taken away to compete in the Purging Trials, Adena is left to make her own way in the slums. Her attempt to steal from a market leads to an encounter with Mak, a mysterious man who intervenes to save her. Mak has secrets of his own, and the two form an unlikely partnership as they set out to reach their loved ones before the trials begin. Their journey takes them beyond the familiar streets of Loot and tests how much they are willing to trust each other. Set during Powerless , this novella follows Adena as she faces danger and the possibility of a connection she never expected. Related: How To Read All of Freida McFadden’s Books in Order Reckless Simon & Schuster Ilya is thrown into upheaval after Paedyn Gray survives the Purging Trials and kills the king, setting a Resistance in motion. Now she is fleeing the kingdom’s authorities, including Kai Azer, the prince she once hoped would protect her. Kai has become the kingdom’s Enforcer under his brother Kitt, who now sits on the throne. He is tasked with tracking Paedyn down and bringing her back, even as his feelings complicate his duty. His search carries him through the dangerous Scorches and into Dor, a city where Elites have no place. There, the rules that have shaped Kai’s life begin to shift as he closes in on Paedyn. Related: How To Read All of Abby Jimenez’s Books in Order Fearless Simon & Schuster After everything that has driven them apart, Paedyn and Kai find themselves back in Ilya, facing an uncertain future. Paedyn must make a choice that will shape her own fate and affect the people around her. As the struggle over the kingdom’s future intensifies, Paedyn and Kai must confront the competing demands of love and loyalty. The final book in the main trilogy brings their story to a decisive moment, with Paedyn’s next move carrying consequences far beyond her own life. Fearful Simon & Schuster During the events of Fearless , Mara returns to Ilya, a kingdom caught in a struggle for the throne. Known as Death and connected to the realm called the Mors, she has reason to take an interest in King Kitt Azer, particularly after he makes a decision that could change his future. Mara watches Kitt and the people living within the castle as she tries to understand the king and what might await him. Her time at court challenges her outlook as she grapples with the pull of love, revenge and ambition. This companion novella explores Ilya’s conflict through the eyes of a figure whose connection to death gives her a different perspective on the lives at stake. How To Read the Powerless Books in Chronological Order Follow the story in this order: Powerless — Start with Paedyn and Kai and learn how Ilya’s unequal society works. Powerful — Read Adena’s companion story, which unfolds alongside Powerless . Reckless — Continue with the second novel in the main trilogy. Fearless — Finish Paedyn and Kai’s central story. Fearful — End with Mara’s companion novella, which takes place during Fearless . Reading the books this way introduces the setting and characters before expanding into the companion stories. Although the novellas focus on different characters, they add context to the larger series and offer more time in the kingdom of Ilya. Related: How Many Andy Weir Books Are There? title: Alan Alda Was Discouraged From Writing This ‘M*A*S*H’ Episode
author: Nicole Moore
content: Alan Alda , who famously starred as Captain Hawkeye Pierce in M*A*S*H , also served as one of the directors and writers for the 11-season series. During a 2000 interview for the Television Academy Foundation , Alda noted that he had penned the script for Season 5, Episode 8 (“Dear Sigmund”), which focused on psychiatrist Dr. Sidney Freedman ( Allan Arbus ) grappling with depression. Alda, who described the episode as “one of [his] favorites,” revealed that the show’s executive producer, Gene Reynolds , wasn’t too keen on his idea for “Dear Sigmund.” “It was a difficult show to get Gene to agree to let me do this idea for the story about the psychiatrist becoming depressed and to get out of his depression, he writes a secret letter to Sigmund Freud, and I mean, in his imagination. Freud is of course dead by this time for several decades,” said Alda, now 90, during the 2000 interview. “Gene said, ‘No, this is a mistake. Don’t do this. Because if you ask an actor to play depressed, it’ll be depressing for the audience.'” Alda said he pivoted accordingly and made sure that Sidney hid his depressive state in the season 5 episode. “I took that to heart, and I went even more for what I had a sense I could do. But it really confirmed this for me and made me go more in this direction, which was that the guy is fighting his depression and, on the surface, seems cheerful. But he’s got a lid on it and is trying to hold it down, and that helped make that work,” said Alda. Alan Alda Discussed His Emmy for Writing an Episode From the Seventh Season of ‘M*A*S*H’ In the Television Academy Foundation interview, Alda referenced that his script for M*A*S*H Season 7, Episode 17 (“Inga”) won him the Emmy for Outstanding Writing in a Comedy Series in 1979. He said he was thrilled to be recognized for his writing, as he wasn’t sure if he was actually being rewarded for his talent when he took home the Emmys for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series and Actor of the Year in a Series in 1974. “To get an award for acting, and you don’t really know how much of it is because you’re cute or because you’re on a popular show. But if you get an award for writing, the chances are much higher, I think, that it’s because you did good work, and work that’s hard to do,” said Alda. While receiving his 1979 Emmy Award , Alda shared that he had long-time dreams of being a writer. “It has been many years since I’ve been trying to be good at being a writer, since I was a little kid. I think, as a matter of fact, I wanted to be a writer from the time I was eight years old, and I wanted to be an actor from the time I was nine,” said Alda during his acceptance speech. “So it’s been a very long time. And this really, really pleases me enormously and encourages me enormously. I accept this as encouragement from you, and I will really continue to do my best to get better.”

title: Neil Young Sues Donald Trump Again, Seeking $10 Million Over ‘Rockin’ in the Free World’
author: Erica Loop
content: Neil Young just sued Donald Trump’s political action committee, Trump 47, for $10 million over alleged copyright infringement for the use of “Rockin’ in the Free World.” The recent complaint states, “Rockin’ in the Free World is a blistering anthem that contrasts the hollow promises of American political rhetoric with the harsh realities faced by the poor, homeless and forgotten.” It continues, painting a harsh contrast between Young’s song and Trump’s intentions. “The lyrics paint vivid street-level portraits — a mother discarding her baby. Addicts lost in despair, garbage piling in the shadows of prosperity — while the repeated chorus delivers a savage irony, celebrating freedom that clearly isn’t shared by all. In short, the Song is the opposite of everything that Donald J. Trump stands for.” The current suit stems from the use of the song during Trump’s Youngstown, Ohio rally on October 12, 2026. According to the complaint, Trump’s political action committee does not and did not “have a license or Young’s permission to play the Song at any public political event.”  If this suit seems familiar, it is. This is the second time Young has filed a complaint over unlicensed appropriation of the hit 1989 song. And that’s another fact that the current lawsuit includes.  In August of 2020, Young sued Trump’s campaign for repeated unlicensed use of “Rockin’ in the Free World” and “Devil’s Sidewalk” at multiple rallies and political events. The following December, The Guardian reported that Young had voluntarily dismissed the case himself “with prejudice” in the New York court. At the time, neither Young nor Trump revealed the details of the dismissal. But, according to the new complaint, “Donald J. Trump for President, Inc. asserted no defense and immediately settled after it was served, promising that it would never use ‘Rockin’ in the Free World’ without a license and permission from Young.” While Young is one of only a few musicians to actually sue Trump or his political committees and campaigns (the estate of Isaac Hayes and Jack White previously filed lawsuits), plenty of other celebs have criticized the President for unauthorized use of their music. Celine Dion , Rihanna , Pharrell Williams , The Rolling Stones, Zara Larsson , Beyoncé , Sabrina Carpenter , Olivia Rodrigo , Ariana Grande , Taylor Swift , and Katy Perry have all publicly denounced Trump, his administration, or his campaign for using their hits.

title: These Unhinged Halloween Cake Designs From 1990s Betty Crocker Cookbooks Have to Be Seen to Be Believed
author: Julie Andrews, MS, RDN, CD, FAND
content: Halloween desserts have come a long way, from elaborate bakery creations to picture-perfect treats all over social media. But long before Instagram and Pinterest made over-the-top baking projects go viral, home cooks had another source of inspiration: Betty Crocker cookbooks . The beloved kitchen brand has spent generations helping families bring fun, approachable recipes to their tables, and its novelty cakes deserve a little extra attention when spooky season rolls around. Vintage Betty Crocker recipes had a special knack for turning ordinary cakes into something extraordinary. A standard boxed cake mix could become a grinning jack-o’-lantern, a creepy-crawly creature or a wicked witch with a crooked hat. With a little frosting, some colorful candies and a healthy dose of imagination, home bakers could create desserts that doubled as the centerpiece of a Halloween party . 😋😋 SIGN UP to get delicious recipes, handy kitchen hacks & more in our daily Pop Kitchen newsletter 🍳 🍔 The 1990s were a particularly fun era for these kinds of playful, kitschy designs. Recipe collections from the decade and later Betty Crocker cookbooks helped keep these imaginative baking projects in circulation, even when some ideas had roots in earlier decades. The results weren’t necessarily polished or minimalist, but that was part of their charm. These cakes were meant to make people laugh, surprise party guests and give kids something exciting to look forward to after dinner. The Most Unhinged Halloween Cakes From 1990s Betty Crocker From the ’90s-era Betty Crocker cookbooks, we think these three designs in particular stand out for their wonderfully over-the-top personalities: a pumpkin face cake, a creeping centipede cake and a wicked witch cake. Each transforms familiar ingredients into a Halloween showstopper, proving that a memorable dessert doesn’t have to come from a professional bakery. And honestly, a little retro weirdness might be exactly what your Halloween party needs this year. Read on for images of these fun Halloween cakes, plus how to make them yourself for spooky season this year. 1. Pumpkin Face Cake Courtesy Julie Andrews A jack-o’-lantern is a Halloween classic, but why stop at carving a pumpkin when you can turn a cake into one? Betty Crocker’s Pumpkin Face Cake recipe takes the familiar orange Halloween icon and gives it an edible makeover. The idea is simple, colorful and delightfully nostalgic: create a pumpkin-shaped cake, cover it in orange frosting and give it a face that can be anything from cheerful to downright mischievous. The finished cake is a fun alternative to a traditional sheet cake, especially for a Halloween party or a family baking afternoon. Its appeal lies in the recognizable pumpkin shape and expressive features, which can be customized to suit the occasion . Go for a classic toothy grin, a goofy smile or a more sinister expression if you want to lean into the spooky theme. To make this festive pumpkin cake, originally from the Betty Crocker Cookbook For Boys and Girls , you’ll need two boxes of devil’s food cake mix (or another flavor you prefer), along with the water, vegetable oil and eggs listed on the packages. You’ll also need two jars of vanilla frosting, yellow and red food coloring, black licorice and candy corn. Preheat the oven to 325 degrees, and grease and flour a two-quart round casserole dish or a 2 1/2-quart oven-safe bowl. Mix one box of cake batter according to the package instructions, pour it into the prepared dish and bake for 65 to 75 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Let the cake rest for 15 minutes before carefully removing it from the dish and transferring it to a cooling rack with the rounded side facing up. Allow it to cool completely, then repeat the process with the second cake . Once both cakes have cooled, trim a small amount from the top of each one to create flat surfaces that will fit together when stacked. To assemble the pumpkin, combine the vanilla frosting with approximately nine drops of yellow food coloring and six drops of red food coloring, adjusting as needed to achieve an orange shade. Place one cake rounded-side down on a serving plate and spread about two-thirds of a cup of frosting over its flat surface. Position the second cake on top with its rounded side facing upward to create the pumpkin shape. Apply a thin coat of orange frosting over the entire cake to trap loose crumbs, then chill it in the refrigerator or freezer for 30 to 60 minutes. Once the crumb coat has firmed up, cover the cake with the remaining frosting. Finally, cut the facial features from your black licorice sticks, and assemble the pieces into the eyes and nose. For the mouth, use the candy corn and arrange them on the frosted cake to give your pumpkin its own spooky jack-o’-lantern personality. Related: The Secret Way To Make Frozen Pie Crust 10x Better, According to Pastry Experts 2. Creeping Centipede Cake Courtesy Julie Andrews If a pumpkin cake is a Halloween staple, the creeping centipede cake is its delightfully bizarre cousin. This design takes a chocolate cake and transforms it into a long, winding creature with plenty of legs, antennae and a face. This dessert might make guests do a double take before realizing that the creepy crawler is actually something sweet. To make this spooky caterpillar cake from the Betty Crocker Halloween Cookbook , gather one box of chocolate fudge cake mix with pudding, plus the water, vegetable oil and eggs specified on the package. You’ll also need a jar of creamy white frosting, green food coloring, one coconut- and marshmallow -coated chocolate snack cake with a creamy center, black pull-apart licorice twists and small chocolate candies. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees and grease a 12-cup fluted tube pan. Prepare the cake batter according to the package directions, pour it into the pan and bake as instructed. Let the cake cool in the pan for 10 minutes before carefully turning it out onto a cooling rack to cool completely. Once cooled, slice the cake vertically into two equal halves. Arrange the pieces on a serving tray with their cut sides positioned to form a long, curved S shape, creating the body of your caterpillar. Mix the green food coloring into the white frosting until you achieve a vivid green shade. Position the chocolate snack cake at one end of the body to serve as the head, using a little frosting to secure it in place if needed. Spread the remaining green frosting over the cake to cover the body and head. Cut the licorice twists into short segments and press them into both sides of the cake to form the legs. Add two longer licorice pieces to the head for antennae. Finish decorating your creepy-crawly creation with small candies and pieces of licorice to make the eyes, nose, eyebrows and mouth. For an extra Halloween touch, sprinkle crushed chocolate cookies around the base of the cake to resemble dirt, giving your edible caterpillar a fun, spooky setting. The result is a Halloween centerpiece that looks like it might crawl right off the serving platter. Kids who love creepy-crawly creatures will likely get a kick out of it, while anyone with a serious bug phobia may prefer to admire it from a safe distance. Related: A Professional Chef Says These 3 ‘Old-Fashioned’ Desserts From the 1940s Are the Definition of Nostalgia 3. Wicked Witch Cake Courtesy Julie Andrews A witch is practically a Halloween mascot, so it makes sense that Betty Crocker gave her the cake treatment too. This wicked witch cake takes a simple yellow cake and turns it into a green-faced character complete with a pointed hat, dark hair and a candy-decorated expression. It’s part dessert, part edible Halloween illustration. Unlike the centipede, which relies on the cake’s shape to create its character, this design uses a rectangular sheet cake as a canvas. Green frosting provides the background, while a waffle cone becomes the witch’s hat. Black decorating icing creates the hat and hair, and colorful gumdrops become the facial features. Candy corn adds a final toothy touch. To make this Halloween witch cake from the Betty Crocker Halloween Cookbook , you’ll need one box of yellow cake mix with pudding, along with the water, vegetable oil and eggs listed on the package. You’ll also need multicolored Halloween sprinkles, one container of vanilla frosting, green food coloring, one waffle cone, black decorating icing, assorted large gumdrops and three pieces of candy corn. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees. Grease the bottom of a 13-by-9-inch cake pan, then prepare the cake batter according to the package directions. Gently fold in the Halloween sprinkles, pour the batter into the prepared pan and bake as directed. Allow the cake to cool completely before decorating. Mix green food coloring into the frosting until you reach your desired shade, then spread it evenly across the top of the cake. Position the waffle cone at an angle near the upper center to create the witch’s pointed hat. Use a toothpick to lightly trace an oval outline beneath the hat for the witch’s face. Add a few extra drops of green food coloring to the frosting around the face, being careful to keep the outlined area clear. Gently swirl the added color with a knife to create a fun, mottled effect. With the black decorating icing, draw the witch’s hat and brim, then add strands of hair around the face. Pipe a small section of icing below the face to suggest a cape. For the finishing touches, cut and shape the gumdrops into facial features, including the eyes, eyebrows, nose and mouth. Use additional gumdrop pieces to make a buckle for the witch’s hat and buttons down her cape. Arrange the three pieces of candy corn along the mouth to resemble pointy teeth, giving your colorful Halloween cake a playful, slightly spooky finish. The final look is wonderfully theatrical, especially if you give the witch an exaggerated expression. You could make her look grumpy, mischievous or downright wicked. Either way, she’s guaranteed to stand out on a Halloween dessert table. Related: 5 Discontinued Fall Grocery Items We’d Pay an Embarrassing Amount of Money to Taste Again How to Recreate These Vintage Halloween Cakes Today PuiStocker65 / Getty Images The beauty of these retro designs is that you don’t need professional decorating skills or a pantry full of specialty ingredients to pull them off. Boxed cake mixes, ready-made frosting and familiar candies do most of the heavy lifting, making these projects approachable for busy families and casual bakers. Start by choosing the cake that best fits your comfort level. The pumpkin face cake is a natural choice if you want a recognizable Halloween classic, while the wicked witch cake offers plenty of room for creative decorating. The centipede is the most sculptural of the three, but its curved body is easier to assemble than it looks once the cake has cooled and been cut into sections. A few modern shortcuts can make the process even easier. Use a piping bag or a resealable bag with a small corner snipped off to apply decorating icing more neatly. Set out bowls of gumdrops , licorice, candy corn and other decorations so kids can help design the faces. If you’re baking with younger children, handle the cake cutting and assembly yourself, then let them take charge of the frosting and candy details. It’s also worth remembering that these designs are supposed to be fun, not flawless. Don’t worry if the centipede has uneven legs or the witch’s hat leans a little too far to one side. Those imperfections are part of the appeal, and they make each cake feel like a homemade creation. For the most nostalgic presentation, serve your cake on a simple platter and let the colorful decorations do the talking. You could even make all three for a retro Halloween dessert spread, with the pumpkin providing the classic option, the centipede adding a creepy-crawly surprise and the witch bringing a little storybook magic to the table. Decades after these kinds of novelty cakes captured home bakers’ imaginations, their appeal hasn’t disappeared. They remind us that holiday baking can be about more than perfect frosting or picture-worthy slices. Related: I’m a Professional Chef, and This Retro Slow-Cooker Meal Is My Go-to Every Fall

title: In 1973, KISS earned $50 playing its first show to fewer than 10 people in Queens; 51 years later, the band sold its songs and name for over $300 million
author: Nina Derwin
content: On Jan. 30, 1973, four young musicians took the stage at a small club in Queens, New York, for a concert that would hardly qualify as a promising debut. The audience consisted of fewer than 10 people, and the band walked away with just $50 for the night’s performance. The group was Kiss, and that nearly empty room at the Popcorn Club, later known as Coventry, marked the beginning of one of rock music’s most successful careers. Fifty-one years later, in 2024, Kiss sold its music catalog, name and likeness rights to Swedish entertainment company Pophouse Entertainment in a deal reportedly worth more than $300 million. The contrast between those two milestones is extraordinary, especially considering how uncertain the band’s future looked in its earliest days. The original lineup consisted of Gene Simmons, Paul Stanley, Ace Frehley and Peter Criss. Simmons and Stanley had previously played together in a group called Wicked Lester before recruiting Frehley and Criss to form a new band with much bigger ambitions. Their first booking came after Simmons contacted the Popcorn Club and arranged a three-night engagement for $150. “We gave our picture to the club, and by this time we had decided to be reborn as Kiss, thanks in part to Epic’s decision to drop Wicked Lester,” Simmons shared in his memoir Kiss and Make-Up . “I remember very clearly when our picture went up on the outside of this club, Ace took a marker and wrote our new name right on the picture. The way he drew it was pretty crude, but it resembled our logo, with the two S ‘s like lightning bolts at the end of the word. It didn’t make much difference for the show, which had a crowd of maybe three people: Peter’s wife, Lydia, a girl named Jan who I was seeing, and Jan’s friend.” Even the band’s famous image was still a work in progress. The elaborate face paint, towering platform boots, and extravagant costumes that would eventually make Kiss instantly recognizable had yet to fully take shape. But the music was already there. “We played like the place was packed, and afterward I realized that this band was the band,” Criss later recalled. “I was so proud of the guys. We were all drenched in sweat, and we had given the performance of our lives for four people.” Early performances featured songs including “Deuce,” “Black Diamond” and “Watchin’ You,” all of which would become important parts of the band’s early catalog. In February 1974, Kiss released its self-titled debut album, followed by Hotter Than Hell later that year. The band’s commercial breakthrough arrived with 1975’s Alive! , a live album that captured the energy of its increasingly elaborate performances. Its success helped propel Kiss into the mainstream, setting the stage for hits including “Rock and Roll All Nite,” “Detroit Rock City” and “Beth.” Over the following decades, the band became famous for much more than its music. Its elaborate stage productions, distinctive makeup and extensive merchandise turned the band into a global entertainment brand. After completing its farewell tour in December 2023, the group announced another major milestone. In April 2024, Kiss reached an agreement with Pophouse Entertainment to sell its music catalog, master recordings, publishing rights and rights to its name and likenesses for more than $300 million. The deal also opened the door for new projects, including a planned biopic and digital avatar performances designed to introduce Kiss to future generations. For a band that began its career playing to a handful of people in a Queens nightclub, the sale represented an extraordinary transformation. “We’re involved together in the future,” Simmons told Music Radar of the Pophouse deal. “So there’s gonna be a motion picture, which is being cast now, and there’s gonna be – I don’t know – cartoon shows, theme park, you name it, it’s all coming up. So it’s gonna be bigger and better than you’ve ever heard, including the avatar show. But that also means that Kiss can’t play live without Pophouse’s permission because they own the makeup and everything.” What started with a $50 paycheck had become a multimillion-dollar legacy, ensuring that the music and unmistakable image of Kiss could live on long after its final concert.
