title: I Tried Making an Old-Fashioned Apple Brown Betty—and I Don’t Know Why It Ever Went Out of Style
author: Jeanette Donnarumma
content: Fall baking season is in full swing, and while I love a classic apple pie or apple crisp , I’m always looking for new ways to use one of my favorite seasonal ingredients…especially when my kids demanded we get TWO bags of apples while apple picking. So when an old-fashioned apple dessert popped up in my Instagram feed, I was immediately intrigued. It had everything I love about fall baking, warm cinnamon , tender apples and a buttery, golden topping, but with one surprising ingredient I never would have thought to use. Meet (or re-meet!) Apple Brown Betty . If you’ve never heard of it, you’re not alone. This vintage American dessert is made by layering fresh apples with toasted and hand ripped breadcrumbs, brown sugar and warm spices, then baking everything together until the apples are tender and the topping is golden. Think of it as apple crisp’s wonderfully nostalgic cousin, with a few clever shortcuts. And this recipe has some serious history! Variations of Brown Betty date back to the 1800s, long before it became the kind of economical, pantry-friendly dessert that made so much sense during the Depression era . It’s a perfect example of how home cooks could turn the simplest ingredients into something really special and make an entire dessert out of what you already have on hand. I saw this Old Time Hawkey video on my Instagram feed and had to give this a try. If you’re familiar with his videos, you know exactly what I mean when I say they’re almost hypnotically soothing. Everything feels a little slower, a little quieter and very cozy . Watching him make this old-fashioned Apple Brown Betty, I had a feeling that whatever was coming out of that oven was going to be just as comforting as the video itself. So I had to give this one a try. And the finished dish has me wondering why this dessert ever went out of style. Related: A Professional Chef Says These 3 ‘Old-Fashioned’ Desserts From the 1940s Are the Definition of Nostalgia Why I Swapped My Go-To Apple Crisp for an Old-Fashioned Brown Betty Courtesy Jeanette Donnarumma Apple crisp has always been my go-to easy fall dessert. You get all those wonderful apple pie flavors without having to deal with making a pie crust, and it’s practically begging for a scoop of vanilla ice cream. But what immediately caught my attention about Apple Brown Betty was how incredibly practical it is. Instead of making a traditional crumb topping with flour, oats and butter , this recipe uses something almost everyone has sitting in their kitchen: bread . View this post on Instagram That’s it! Regular sandwich bread that you can turn into crumbs and layer with apples, butter, sugar and spices. I love a recipe that makes good use of what you already have, especially when it helps use up something that might otherwise go to waste. Have a few slices of white bread left in the bag? Perfect. A loaf that’s starting to get a little stale? Even better. Apple Brown Betty vs. Apple Crisp: What’s the Difference? Courtesy Jeanette Donnarumma At first glance, Apple Brown Betty and apple crisp look pretty similar. Both feature tender baked apples , warm spices and a buttery topping, but there’s one major difference. Apple crisp traditionally has a streusel-like topping made with flour , butter, sugar and often rolled oats. That mixture gets scattered over the apples, creating a crunchy, crumbly layer as it bakes. Apple Brown Betty uses breadcrumbs or small pieces of bread instead of the traditional crisp topping. The breadcrumbs are often layered between the apples, not just scattered over the top. As the dessert bakes, some of the bread soaks up the buttery apple juices while the top becomes beautifully golden and slightly crisp. The result is something that lands between an apple crisp and a cozy baked bread pudding. You get soft, cinnamon -spiced apples with bits of buttery, toasted bread throughout. And because everything is layered together, you get a little of that delicious crumb mixture in practically every bite. Related: We Asked 3 Chefs How To Make Frozen Butternut Squash Taste Better—and They All Agreed on This One Trick The Secret to the Best Betty: Your Bread Matters Courtesy Jeanette Donnarumma Here’s where I think the beauty of this recipe really shines: You don’t need fancy bread to make a delicious Apple Brown Betty. Of course, you could use brioche if you happen to have some. Its rich, buttery texture would make the finished dessert feel a little more indulgent. But I really love the idea of using plain old white sandwich bread . Related: 30 Creative Ways to Savor Pumpkin Seeds That Go Beyond Simply Roasting Them Choosing the Right Loaf Courtesy Jeanette Donnarumma White sandwich bread is inexpensive, it’s something most families already have around, and it’s such a smart way to give those last few slices a second life. And it truly does; the bread keeps this really unique chewy texture that is unlike any other apple dessert I’ve ever had. Slightly stale bread is especially useful because it can absorb the melted butter and apple juices without immediately turning to mush. If your bread is very fresh, you can let it dry out a little before turning it into crumbs. One tip: You want breadcrumbs with some texture, not the super-fine, powdery kind you buy for coating chicken cutlets. Those slightly coarse, irregular crumbs give you little crispy bits throughout the dessert. I used my fingers to achieve this, so the crumbs didn’t get too small. Related: 50 Savory Pumpkin Recipes That Will Keep You Comforted and Happy All Season Long The Best Apples to Balance the Sweetness Courtesy Jeanette Donnarumma Since this dessert gets plenty of sweetness from the brown sugar, I recommend using an apple with a little tartness to balance everything out. Granny Smith apples are a great option. They hold their shape nicely during baking, and their tart flavor keeps the finished dessert from becoming overly sweet. I’m sure Honeycrisp or Pink Lady apples would also be great too. If I’m being honest, I just used what my kids picked off the trees! How to Make Apple Brown Betty (Step-by-Step) Courtesy Jeanette Donnarumma The beauty of this old-fashioned Apple Brown Betty recipe is just how simple the process is. There’s no dough to roll out, no complicated topping to prepare and no special baking skills required. Step 1: Prepare the apples and toast bread. Peel, core and slice your apples into fairly even pieces so they cook at the same rate. Lightly toast five slices of white bread. Courtesy Jeanette Donnarumma Step 2: Melt butter and rip bread into crumbs . Combine melted butter with breadcrumbs, brown sugar , cinnamon, nutmeg and salt. Mix together. Courtesy Jeanette Donnarumma Step 3: Layer the dessert. In a buttered baking dish, layer half the apples and half the brown sugar breadcrumb mixture. Layer another round of apples and breadcrumbs. Step 4: Combine vanilla and apple cider . Pour it over the dessert, making sure to get it around the sides and over the top. Courtesy Jeanette Donnarumma Step 5: Cover and bake until golden. Bake for 40 minutes, uncover and bake another 20 minutes. The apples should be soft and fragrant and the top should be golden brown. Courtesy Jeanette Donnarumma Step 6: Let it rest before serving. Give the dessert a few minutes to settle after removing it from the oven. This allows the juices to thicken slightly, and it’s much easier to scoop. Courtesy Jeanette Donnarumma Step 7: Top with ice cream. And enjoy! The whole process is refreshingly uncomplicated, which is probably why this dessert was such a staple in home kitchens for generations. Related: Pillsbury’s Iconic Shape Cookies Have Been a Fall Favorite for Decades—Here’s the Surprising Story Behind Them Serving Suggestion: Bring on the Ice Cream! Courtesy Jeanette Donnarumma Could you eat Apple Brown Betty straight out of the baking dish with a spoon? Absolutely and I wouldn’t blame you one bit. But if you’re going to make this cozy fall dessert, I think there’s one thing that makes it even better: a big scoop of vanilla ice cream. The contrast between the warm, cinnamon-spiced apples and the cold, creamy ice cream is just about perfect. As the ice cream starts melting into those buttery breadcrumbs, it creates its own delicious sauce. For something a little more traditional, you could serve it with lightly sweetened whipped cream , a drizzle of heavy cream or even old-fashioned hard sauce, which is a sweet, buttery dessert sauce sometimes flavored with rum or brandy. It’s also a wonderful dessert to make when you have company because you can serve it right from the baking dish. No fancy plating required. I love testing vintage recipes because they remind me that good food doesn’t always need to be complicated, expensive, or made with a long list of ingredients. Sometimes it’s just apples, bread, butter and a little brown sugar. And after making this old-fashioned Apple Brown Betty, I think this fall dessert throwback deserves a permanent spot back in the rotation. Related: I Baked Lucille Ball’s Forgotten 1950s ‘Apple John’ Recipe—and It Might Be Better Than Traditional Apple Pie

title: Red Bull’s New Winter Edition Energy Drink Is Bringing an Unexpected Flavor to the Party
author: Julie Andrews, MS, RDN, CD, FAND
content: Red Bull is giving fans another reason to get excited about seasonal sips, and this time, it’s going a little nutty. The energy drink brand has built plenty of buzz around its limited-edition flavors , turning each seasonal release into a chance to try something new. But its latest winter offering might be one of its most unexpected combinations yet. Meet the Red Bull Winter Edition Pistachio & Berries , a new flavor that pairs a subtle nutty taste with a fruity hint. The limited-time drink officially launched today, Oct. 26, and its unique profile is already getting people talking online. 😋😋 SIGN UP to get delicious recipes, handy kitchen hacks & more in our daily Pop Kitchen newsletter 🍳 🍔 Red Bull Reveals Its 2026 Winter Edition: Pistachio Berry According to Red Bull , the flavor features a bright blend of berries, a hint of caramel and a smooth finish. The cans also get a seasonal makeover in a distinctive pistachio -green shade, so they should stand out in the energy drink aisle. Shoppers can look for 8.4-ounce and 12-ounce individual cans, as well as 12-ounce four-packs, at retailers nationwide while supplies last. The new flavor is also featured in Red Bull’s seasonal Advent Calendar . Related: This ‘Superior’ Scalp Shampoo Is Winning Over Customers With Thinning Hair Red Bull Fans Have Mixed Feelings About the New Flavor As soon as Red Bull shared the announcement on TikTok , fans began weighing in on the unusual flavor pairing. Some were ready to crown it a new favorite before even cracking open a can. “This is my NEW top favorite i love it!” one enthusiastic commenter wrote. Another fan seemed intrigued enough to give it a shot, commenting, “PISTACHIO 🤔 okay you convinced me… I’ll try it.” Of course, not everyone is ready to trade their old favorites for a pistachio-inspired drink. Some fans used the announcement as an opportunity to campaign for the return of a beloved seasonal flavor . “PLEASE BRING BACK FESTIVE ARCTIC BERRY PLEASE I’LL DO ANYTHING,” one commenter pleaded. And then there were the skeptics who weren’t exactly sold on the new combination . “Nah bro that winter is terrible,” another person declared. With reactions ranging from instant enthusiasm to outright rejection, Red Bull’s latest flavor is already sparking plenty of debate. Pistachio and berries might sound like an unexpected pairing for an energy drink , but curious fans will have the chance to decide for themselves. title: ‘Star Trek’ Star Walter Koenig Revealed the Surprising Way The Monkees’ Davy Jones Inspired His Character
author: Erica Loop
content: Legendary Star Trek actor Walter Koenig died at his home in Los Angeles at the age of 90. And while he’s now known as the iconic Russian navigator Ensign Chekov on the beloved series, Koenig didn’t join the cast until the second season.  Why did the powers that be at Star Trek bring in Koenig? According to the actor, they needed a new cast member who the younger audience would appreciate. And that’s why “Chekov” originally had a different name. “I think his name was Jones. And I think, you know, when I think back in retrospect, why they called him Jones even though he was going to be a Russian was because the whole idea was inspired by Davy Jones of The Monkees,” explained Koenig in a 2019 interview for the Television Academy Foundation archive.  Walter Koenig in ‘Star Trek.’ Photo: CBS Photo Archive / Getty Images CBS Photo Archive / Getty Images Koenig continued, “They were looking for an actor or a personality that would appeal to the same demographic that Davy Jones did. Kids eight to 14 years old. And indeed, my mail was from people who were eight to 14 years old.” What kind of mail did the then-new Star Trek star get? Koenig revealed the overall theme of his fan letters: “You know, ‘I think you’re groovy,’ you know, ‘I love your hair.’ Which was a wig, by the way. I got hundreds and hundreds of letters.” The actor was so popular with the tween and teen set that, as he shared, “I actually, at one point, was getting the third most mail after Bill and Leonard. What a novelty. What an interesting novelty to get these big canvas bags of mail. Initially, I read it all. After a while, I couldn’t. But for a while I read it all. There was never any antagonistic or hostile mail about the fact that I was playing a Russian.” Even though Star Trek originally aired at the height of the Cold War, Koenig’s fans didn’t seem to connect his character’s background with the political climate. But as it turns out, there was a very good reason. He explained, “Because these were all kids. And you know, they didn’t really know too much about the Cold War. They were just interested that they found the character appealing.”  Decades later, Koenig was still entertaining fans around the world. Following his death, the actor’s talent agent Zachery McGinnis told NBC News in a statement, “Today we mourn the passing of Walter Koenig, whose talent, warmth, and unforgettable performances left a lasting mark on generations of fans around the world. Walter helped inspire audiences with his optimism, humor, and adventurous spirit,” adding, “Beyond Star Trek , his long and distinguished career showcased his versatility as an actor and his genuine love for his craft.”

title: Is Meghan Markle Moving To Melbourne? Her New MasterChef Gig Might Indicate Her Presence Down Under
author: Rebekah Manibog
content: Clutch your crown and aprons, 'cos Junior MasterChef Australia is officially copping a revival, with Duchess of Sussex, Meghan Markle , signing on as co-host. And with that kind of royal-tea , that leaves us with one question: Will Markle be moving to Melbourne for the new show?  Yep, you read that right. After appearing as a guest judge on MasterChef Australia 2026 , Markle will be making a bigger splash on the culinary cook-off show with the revival of its incredibly wholesome spin-off, Junior MasterChef Australia, as a co-host alongside series favourite and Gold Logie nominee, Poh Ling Yeow .  Culinary icons. (Image source: Network 10 / MasterChef Australia)   “I had an incredible time with the whole team at MasterChef this past April, so when they approached me to come back and work with this young group of talent, it was an easy yes,” Markle shared in a statement, per the Sydney Morning Herald .  “I love cooking with my own kids, so seeing what these young stars create in the kitchen is going to be a lot of fun. I can’t wait to see what they cook up!” Alongside the announcement, which was made during Network 10's Upfronts event on Tuesday, Yeow said the upcoming reunion “would be a real treat” following their “lovely time” filming for the OG MasterChef back in April.  “The much-loved series will see Poh Ling Yeow joined by special guest Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, as they help guide the next generation of young culinary talent,” a Network 10 spokesperson shared, per 9News .  “An entrepreneur, actress, humanitarian and passionate home cook, Emmy-nominated Meghan previously joined the MasterChef Australia kitchen as a guest judge in 2026. Now, she returns to work alongside Poh and meet the young contestants as they embark on their own culinary journeys.” So, does this mean Meghan Markle will become a temporary Melburnian?  While details surrounding the revival have remained hush-hush, publications have reported that filming is expected to take place in Melbourne — with Secret Melbourne claiming production will take place at Melbourne Showgrounds — once the next season of MasterChef Australia has wrapped in May.  The SMH also reported that production is expected “to take about two to three weeks to film”, which could indicate a short stay for the Duchess.  But for now, the status of whether or not Markle will be coming Down Under for the entirety of filming has remained a secret. It's also unknown whether or not her husband, Prince Harry , or their two children, Prince Archie and Prince Lilibet , will also be Down Under with her.  Me and my bestie when we WFH. title: Jack Antonoff Slams Ed Sheeran For His Loop Tour Controversy: 'Stand The F*ck Up'
author: Rebekah Manibog
content: Producer and musician Jack Antonoff has completely popped off at Ed Sheeran , telling the artist to “stand the f*ck up” following the controversy surrounding his Loop Tour, support act Macklemore and his support for Palestine. In a recent interview with The Guardian , Antonoff vented about Sheeran's recent controversy, in which his support act, Macklemore, was removed from his tour after sharing pro-Palestine messages during his set.  “ [Ed Sheeran] missed a massive, beautiful opportunity there: just cancel the whole fucking tour, then play for free outside each venue, raise a bunch of money, rather than let a fucking billionaire tell you what to do,” Antonoff told the publication.  Antonoff, who is Jewish, has received criticism for expressing solidarity with Palestinians. (Image source: Getty Images)  What happened between Macklemore and Ed Sheeran during the Loop Tour?  Macklemore — who's been vocal about his political beliefs through songs like “Same Love” and “Hind's Hall” — was removed from the US leg of Sheeran's Loop Tour after criticism of his on-stage pro-Palestinian messages back in September.  The rapper confirmed his removal from the tour on Instagram, revealing the decision happened after a “difficult conversation" with Sheeran before focusing his post on the genocide taking place in Palestine. “We have careers, money, opportunities, safety and audiences around the world,” he wrote. “Whatever consequences any of us face for what we say, we get to go home to our families. “The victims are the Palestinian people. The men, women and children who have been killed, starved, displaced and forced to live through unimaginable violence." “My message is for peace." (Image: Kristy Sparow/Getty Images) Robert Kraft, who owns Gillette Stadium and the New England Patriots, confirmed he didn't want Macklemore performing at his venue, and the decision was based on the artist's recent actions and material used on stage that had been "deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community”. In a September 8 post, Macklemore clarified that his pro-Palestine stance wasn't an attack on Jewish people.  “To all of my Jewish brothers and sisters: criticism of Israel, criticism of apartheid, being against genocide in no way is a criticism of you,” he wrote on X.  “My message is for peace; love for all human beings to be treated with dignity, respect, and equality.” Jack Antonoff says Loop Tour controversy inspired him to speak out more  While Antonoff — who's Jewish — has expressed solidarity with Palestinians, and has received backlash for doing so, he says the Sheeran and Macklemore controversy has made him feel “way more emboldened to say it now, because it’s not in any way a strange, uncomfortable, or controversial thing to say, it’s a deeply human thing to say. If you think it is [controversial] you’re lost in some other sauce that is so crazy".  “They’re going to let some fucking promoter tell me what I can say? Don’t book me. I’ll play for free outside.”  “The reason it’s not an anomaly or niche issue is that we all live in a world where billionaires are constantly telling us what to do. So stand the fuck up," he continued.  Shortly after Macklemore was dropped, all of Sheeran's remaining openers — which included Aaron Rowe , Finneas and Lukas Graham — and his touring band, Beoga , quit the show in solidarity with the rapper.  Following the mass exodus, Sheeran addressed the controversy on stage in Philadelphia , telling the audience, “I never wanted to be an activist musician, but this has put me in the middle of an important and passionate argument about free speech and the most complex political issue on the planet.”

title: G Flip & Chrishell Stause Announce Split: ‘I Will Always Love Her’
author: Lauren McNamara
content: Aussie Musician G Flip and Selling Sunset star Chrishell Stause have announced they are breaking up after more than four years together. Love is truly dead.  The pair confirmed the news in separate statements shared on social media on Monday, with both expressing their continued love for one another. “After four + years Chrishell and I are no longer together,” G Flip wrote on Instagram. “I will always love her, we will always share a special connection and I cherish our memories together deeply.” The Melbourne-born singer and drummer went on to ask fans for privacy as they navigate the separation. “My head and heart are feeling very heavy right now and I’m not able to talk but I want to thank you all for your support and appreciate you respecting our privacy at this difficult time," they said. Stause, meanwhile, addressed the split in an emotional video shared with her Instagram followers, revealing that the pair had agreed to handle their separation with love and respect.  “I have a pretty humbling update to share with you guys. G and I are no longer together,” she began.  “We have agreed to treat this public separation with love and respect for each other. That’s not hard for me because I am in love with this person, and I don’t have all the information or the reasons.” The reality television star became visibly emotional as she reflected on the end of their relationship, admitting that she was struggling to come to terms with the separation.  “I feel like a little bit of a failure,” she said. “There’s nothing you could say about me that would be worse than what I say to myself. I just have to kind of heal and figure this out. It’s hard. It’s painful.” Despite the heartbreak, Stause reflected positively on their time together, acknowledging that the relationship had simply reached a different conclusion than she had anticipated.  “I had an amazing over four years with G. Maybe that’s not a miss, you know. Maybe it’s just coming to terms with it being a different ending than you had imagined," she said. “I will always love G, and I don’t ever really see that changing. This sucks, but everyone deserves to be happy and I wish that for both of us.” G Flip and Stause first went public with their relationship in May 2022, when the reality star revealed their romance during a reunion episode of Netflix’s Selling Sunset . The pair had previously connected through G Flip’s music video for “Get Me Outta Here”, in which Stause appeared. In May 2023, the couple celebrated their relationship with an intimate wedding ceremony in Las Vegas , before going on to hold additional celebrations with family and friends, including a ceremony in Australia. They later made a tradition of celebrating their relationship with further wedding ceremonies, including a medieval-themed celebration in Los Angeles in July 2025. Their 2023 wedding. (Image: Instagram) Throughout their relationship, the pair frequently spoke publicly about their love for one another, as well as their hopes of starting a family. In a 2025 interview with PEOPLE , G Flip opened up about the emotional challenges of their IVF journey, describing the experience as one marked by periods of hope and disappointment. Neither has publicly stated the reason for their separation. This article is from Rolling Stone AU .

title: Sound The Alarm: Viral Beauty Brand Touchland Has Landed At Sephora Australia
author: Bree Grant
content: If the sanitisers of the early 2020s left you with lingering sensory PTSD, you’re not alone. For years, we’ve watched the TikTok girlies became utterly feral for the aesthetic mist, left to rely on friends returning from the US to bring us back a bottle. Well, the travel tax is officially over, Touchland has officially landed Down Under, launching at Sephora.   Founded in 2018 by Andrea Lisbona , the cult brand basically flipped functional hygiene into a status-symbol accessory. Instead of a gloopy pump bottle that leaks through your tote lining, you get an ultra-fine, fast-absorbing mist spiked with skincare heroes like Aloe Vera and Radish Root Ferment. It hydrates, skips the tacky residue, and genuinely looks chic sitting next to your lip oil and keys on an iced-matcha run. You'll be able to secure the product that launched a thousand TikTok hauls, the OG Power Mist Hydrating Hand Sanitiser ($18) in eight different scents, including Beach Coco, Wild Watermelon, Vanilla Blossom, Berry Bliss, Rainwater, Pure Lavender, Blue Sandalwood and Mango Passion.  Touchland isn’t just keeping your hands germ-free anymore; they’ve branched out into lightweight body and hair scents. Absolutely not.  If history has taught us anything about viral US beauty launches, we’d recommend getting in early before the shelves are completely wiped.  You can shop Touchland here .

title: We Tried The Internet’s Favourite Shampoo & Conditioner Combos For Curly Hair – Here Are The Ones That Are Worth It
author: Bree Grant
content: If you’ve been blessed with curly hair , you already know what a mission it is to find a shampoo and conditioner combo that plays well with you hair.   Finding the right balance between moisture, curl definition, and scalp cleanliness is a full-time job. As someone who has wrangled her curls for 30+ years, I can confidently say that I've tested dozens of formulas (and paid the frizzy consequences) and I might finally be onto something.  To save your hair (and your bank account), I've pulled together the best I've found, so far. Whether you’ve got soft type two waves, juicy type three ringlets, or lush type four coils, here are the absolute best shampoos and conditioners for curly hair available in Australia right now. Best Overall: Briogeo Don't Despair, Repair! Super Moisture Shampoo & Conditioner (Image: Briogeo) Best For: Type 2 – 3 Curls needing damage repair and intense hydration Key Ingredients: Rosehip oil, algae extract, B-vitamins Sulphate & Silicone Free? Yes Price: $64 each Why It Made The Cut If your curls are feeling stressed from heat, bleaching, or general life, Briogeo’s Don’t Despair, Repair! range is the ultimate reset button. The shampoo cleanses without stripping away essential moisture, while the conditioner provides incredible slip, making detangling in the shower effortless. It strikes the sweet spot between heavy hydration and lightweight bounce, so your ringlets stay juicy without getting weighed down. Best Budget Pick: SheaMoisture Coconut & Hibiscus Curl & Shine (Image: SheaMoisture) Best For: Thick Type 3 – 4 Curls wanting high shine on a budget. Key Ingredients: Coconut oil, hibiscus flower, silk protein. Sulphate & Silicone Free? Yes. Price: $23.50 each Why It Made The Cut A classic for a reason, SheaMoisture delivers salon-level results at drugstore prices. This line is rich, thick, and smells like a tropical holiday.  Because it’s packed with rich shea butter and coconut oil, it’s ideal if your curls suffer from chronic dryness. (IYKYK!) A little goes a long way, but if you have finer hair, start with a small amount to avoid build-up. Best For Coils & Kinks: Bread Beauty Supply Hair Wash Gentle Cream Cleanser (Image: Bread) Best For: Type 3C to 4C Coils needing an ultra-gentle, non-stripping wash. Key Ingredients: Argan oil, aloe vera juice, lemon tea tree oil. Sulphate & Silicone Free? Yes. Price: $21 (for the 100ml) Why It Made The Cut Australian-owned brand BREAD revolutionised wash days for textured hair. Their Hair Wash isn’t a traditional lathering shampoo — it’s a hybrid co-wash that cleanses like a mild shampoo while conditioning like a mask. I know what you're thinking, “not a two-in-one!!” but this one's different and quite possibly the only exception we will ever make.  It leaves coils feeling bouncy, pillow-soft, and completely clean without stripping it. Pair it with their Hair-Mask Cream Conditioner for maximum moisture retention.  Best Luxury Shampoo + Conditioner: Kérastase Curl Manifesto  (Image: Kérastase) Best For: All curl types looking for high-end definition and frizz control. Key Ingredients: Manuka honey, ceramides. Sulphate & Silicone Free? Sulphate-free, contains water-soluble silicones. Price: From $64 Why It Made The Cut If you feel like splurging, Kérastase’s Curl Manifesto is where you wanna spend your money. The formula infuses Manuka honey directly into the hair shaft, locking in moisture to fight humidity before you even step out of the shower.  It has a rich, creamy lather that smells like high-end perfume, leaving curls soft, defined, and remarkably frizz-free.  My Personal Favourite: ORI Lab by NAK Hair Curl (Image: Bree Grant) Best For: Type 2 – 3 curls Key Ingredients: Niacinamide, Hyaluronic Acid, Marshmallow Root, Flannel Flower, and Hydrolyzed Rice Protein. Sulphate & Silicone Free? Yes — completely silicone-free, sulphate-free, vegan, and packaged in 100% recycled bottles. Price: $42.95 each Why It Made The Cut Honestly, this set is my favourite at the moment by far. The conditioner is where the magic happens, it doesn't leave my hair feeling too clean (IYKYK), frizzy or fluffy. Instead, because it relies on rice protein rather than heavy silicones, it helps clump curls together and builds bounce. Plus, the marshmallow root extract and flannel flower, it gives ridiculous slip to untangle stubborn knots with just your fingers in the shower.  How To Choose The Right Formula For Your Curls Know Your Curl Type: Finer waves (Type 2) need lightweight lotion-like conditioners, while tight coils (Type 4) thrive on thick, butter-based formulas containing shea or cocoa butter. Watch For Sulphates: Harsh sulphates (like Sodium Lauryl Sulphate) strip away the natural oils that curly hair relies on for shape and shine. Always opt for gentle, sulphate-free cleansers. Focus On The Scalp First: Shampoo is for your scalp; conditioner is for your lengths. Massage your cleanser into the roots to clear product build-up without drying out your ends. How often should you wash curly hair? Honestly, this one feels personal. I do a full hair wash every two weeks, and condition the ends as needed, but most curly types thrive on washing one to two times a week. Over-washing strips natural oils, causing dryness and frizz. If you work out often, try rinsing with warm water and conditioner in between wash days.  Do I really need a sulphate-free shampoo? Yes. Because natural sebum from your scalp has a harder time travelling down a spiral hair shaft than straight hair, curls are naturally drier. Sulphates strip that essential moisture away quickly. What is the difference between a co-wash and a shampoo? A co-wash (conditioning wash) cleanses using gentle moisturisers rather than sudsing surfactants. It's ideal for dry, coily hair types that need frequent moisture refreshes without stripping the scalp. Anyway, that's all for now. If I try something else that blows my curls back, I'll let you know. Happy wash day!

title: Bring The Holiday To You: How To Bring The Himalayas To You This Holiday Season
author: Saacha Neilson
content: In partnership with Hikers and foodies alike have been making pilgrimages to the Himalayas for decades. Whether for the physical challenge or the momos, the appeal of the mountain range and the five countries through which it sprawls is intoxicating for many.  I would travel many moons for these bad boys. (Image source: Getty) The one struggle I’ve personally found is that it’s quite far away. If it were next door, I’m sure I would’ve climbed Everest by now, but as fate would have it, it’s a hop, skip, and a massive jump from Australia.  So I’ve figured out how you can get all that Himalayan goodness right at home, so you can get all the props of some huge hike without having to actually freeze on the side of a mountain… unless you’re into that sort of thing.  A hiker's paradise  Obviously, the Himalayas have some decent hikes. Dare I say, given it’s the most famous mountain range in the world, climbers are probably quite fond of it.  But don’t you worry! Here in Australia, we have some cracking alternatives that you can huff and puff up without the huge airfare.  If you’re going for height, Mount Kosciuszko is our tallest mountain. Located in the Snowy Mountains of NSW, its peak sits at 2,228 metres, typically taking about six hours to reach the top. Now, while it is still a great deal shorter than Mount Everest (8,848 metres), Kosciuszko does reach some of the smaller foothills in the Himalayas; it's good practice.  Me and my bestie after leaving the house. (Image source: Getty) If you’re after length over height, look no further than Tasmania’s Overland Track. The six-day, one-way track covers 65km, with side treks leading up Tassie’s biggest mountain (1,617 metres) and about every terrain you can imagine. While it’s definitely different to treks you might do in the Himalayas, it is one of Australia’s most iconic walks and isn’t that what this is all about?   Curries, momo and more The Himalayas lie across five countries: China, Nepal, Pakistan, Bhutan, and India. This means the food coming out of the Himalayas is not only a combination of flavour profiles from all of these countries, but it’s bloody delicious.  To find some Himalayan food in Australia, you’ve got a couple of great options. You can focus on one of these cuisines, such as Apa's Canteen, a Bhutanese eatery on Melbourne’s Collins St.  For authentic Nepalese food, look no further than one of Falcha’s Sydney locations. For an Indian meal, you could even mix it up a little and try Melbourne’s infamous Diamond Indian and Hungarian restaurant in Clifton Hill — a confusing combination if ever I've seen one.  The final summit. (Image credit: Getty) Of course, the easiest way to transport yourself to the top of a Himalayan peak is with  Kettle Ridge Cut Himalayan Pink Salt chips .  Now, I personally will be favouring the food portion of this homebound holiday but if you hikers fancy a longer journey, I wish you the best of luck. Melbourne and Sydney, we have something extra special in store to celebrate summiting this delicious snack, but you'll have to stay tuned to find out.

title: A New TV Series Is Finally Giving Us The Origin Of Friday The 13th's Jason Voorhees
author: Saacha Neilson
content: In partnership with Slasher movies are some of the best in the biz. They’re quick (sexy) and dominated by a terrifying killer, often with zaddy energy. Since October is obviously the time for scary viewings, we usually see a bunch of second-, third-, or fourth-gen slasher flicks, but this time, rather than doling out another sequel, one franchise is finally telling us how the slashing started. Stan's Crystal Lake is a  Friday The 13th prequel series that’s actually telling us how Jason Voorhees became the camp slasher. And in terms of backstories, it beats any sob story I’ve heard. Who Is Jason Voorhees You don't know THE Jason? (Image credit: Glee) He’s the serial killer in a hockey mask who’s wandered around the Crystal Lake camp since the 80s. For non-horror fans, he typically wears a mask and kills any teens hanging out lakeside. What they may be getting up to by that lake is none of my business (though I will watch it). While his mum kicked off the killing spree in the OG 1980 film Friday The 13th , Jason quickly picked up the mantle and went on to star in 11 more films across the franchise, including my personal favourite  Friday the 13th Part VIII: Jason Takes Manhattan . Fun fact, he also beat Freddy Krueger in the 2003 crossover  Freddy Vs Jason , which should tell you a thing or two about his fighting prowess.  What does Crystal Lake reveal about Jason Voorhees Beyond getting the full backstory of why Jason's face looks the way it does, we get a much deeper understanding of Jason’s fascination with Crystal Lake. Having grown up by the lake, much of his trauma is tied to the location, and so, the logical next step is to kill people nearby. We also knew from the first film that Jason had “drowned” in the lake, but this time, we get to see what life was like before and exactly what went down that day.  That had to hurt. (Image credit: Stan) Interestingly, while the show may talk about Jason’s background, we spend most of our time with his mum. Played by  Freaks And Geeks  icon Linda Cardellini, Pamela Voorhees is the doting mother who goes on quite the journey through these eight episodes.  I don’t want to give any spoilers but let's just say Jason's bloodlust may run in the family.  Diva is down. (Image Credit: Stan) It’s a bizarrely emotional tale for a slasher setting, as you see the lengths a mother will go to for her son. Given it’s an A24 production, it’s hardly surprising that we’re getting emotional depth alongside the gore. Each bit of violence is underpinned by a sincere character struggle and a single-minded devotion to family. Oh, and it’s set in the 70s, so expect amazing fashion and interior design you could never afford.  Dare I say, bring back high-waisted jeans. (Image credit: Stan) Ready for a fright? Every episode is now streaming on Stan from October 15.

title: 'The Hot Wiggle' AKA John Pearce Has Revealed His Wildest Fan Encounters & Y'all Are Messy
author: Lachlan Guertin
content: John Pearce is very aware that fans refer to him as “the hot Wiggle” , and he's fully embracing it. Since he  joined the children’s group in 2021  and adopted the moniker “Big Strong John”, fans of all ages have screamed his name at concerts, commented on his social media “thirst traps” and approached him in public. The intense amount of attention would be a lot for any regular person to handle, but the entertainer is no stranger to fandom culture. Pearce was famously a member of the dance group Justice Crew from 2009 to 2020, with the group winning Australia’s Got Talent in 2010, releasing a string of chart-topping singles and opening for artists like Pitbull , Janet Jackson and One Direction on tour. Reflecting on his wild career trajectory, Pearce told PEDESTRIAN.TV that the opportunity to join The Wiggles came at a crossroads in his life when he was unsure about his future, and he had no idea how people would react to the transition. “When I posted that first video online of me going from my Justice Crew self to what I've become now, Big Strong John, that kind of took off, and it's been really great,” he shared. “Especially when I had a bit of imposter syndrome joining, it was the last thing on my mind that the mums and dads and uncles and aunties were really going to go to town on the comments.” Wildest fan experiences When comparing the two fandoms, Pearce admitted that they’re “completely different” because The Wiggles supporters are “a lot more tame than the young teeny boppers” that followed him across the country during the Justice Crew era — although there’s definitely a crossover. “A lot of those teenagers at the time are having their own kids and bringing their kids to Wiggle shows, and I do get pulled over quite regularly saying, ‘I’m a massive fan of Justice Crew, thanks for now entertaining my child’, and it’s a full circle moment for their family, which is really cool,” he said. “You don't really get bothered as much as if you're spotted in public. Parents are tired, they’re exhausted, they’re not going to want to scream and get photos and all that sort of stuff.” It’s a far cry from the early 2010s when Aussie fans would do anything — and we mean anything — to meet their idols. “You'd always get the fans that were really over the top that book a flight and sit next to you on the plane, and you'd wonder how they got that seat, things like that,” he recalled, quickly adding that it was “always fun” and he never found it “creepy” or “stalkery”. “We did have a few people get a few tattoos of our signatures in Justice Crew days. I don't know why, but they’re obviously big fans, big supporters. And now in The Wiggles, you get posters made by little children, and that's always really nice and wholesome, and we always do appreciate that.” Justice Crew won Australia’s Got Talent in 2010 and competed on America's Got Talent: The Champions in 2019. (Credit: NBC) After countless live shows, world tours and thirst traps, Pearce recently celebrated five years with The Wiggles — and he has no plans to wrap up anytime soon. “Touring is fun, filming is fun and obviously, most importantly, making families and children happy all around the world is very rewarding, and I'm very grateful to be a part of the team,” he remarked. “Time flies, and I'll do it for another 20 years, or however long they want me there.” He's also fully embracing his surprising status as a sex symbol by starring in a new MILKRUN ad, which shows him using the on-demand grocery and essentials delivery service because he can't leave the house without being swarmed by fans. “I thought, what a fun way to bring light to what's been happening — the crazy phenomenon, is what I call it — when I joined the Wiggles,” he said. “It’s the last thing I ever expected to get that kind of response, and it's been fun.”

title: Are Dating Apps Ruining Romance? We Spoke To The Singles In Our Area
author: Saacha Neilson
content: Romance in the modern age has become dependent on dating apps. There’s your classic Tinder, Hinge, Feeld (if you’re looking for something a little more open), and Bumble if you're looking for women to make the first move — though that novelty is long gone.  Apparently, more than a  third of Gen Z Aussies have used dating apps, and  ANU research found that between 20 and 40 per cent of relationships started on the apps — a better success rate than anyone would have expected. Unfortunately, research has also found that relationships that kick off thanks to a swipe often experience a lower intensity of love . Ouch. And despite the hopeless romantics or horny individuals who may be using dating apps in good faith, for a number of us the process can boil down to four little words: “I hate it here.”  So why are we all committing to this charade if we're really just after a little chemistry? I couldn’t help but wonder (read in a Carrie Bradshaw voice): are dating apps doing us dirty?   To understand the attitudes of those actually using them, I embarked on an investigation. What do people think our screens are doing to romance?  Boots on the ground. (Image Credit: My Hinge) Casting the virtual net far and wide (you would not believe my age range and radius), I created a profile and waited for the results to roll in. Let me tell you, if you ever want to give your profile a boost, tell them you’re writing an article.  Your girl really was open to all. (Image credit: My settings) “The apps are a lot like social media,” one Hinge user wrote, “In the sense that I can get absorbed just looking at how others present themselves on the internet and forget why I’m there.”  They've got a point. (Image Credit: Hinge) The overwhelming sentiment was that people weren’t being intentional with their dating. “I think it possibly makes dating too disposable,” one response read. Another even went so far as to say, “I wish phones were banned.”  Of the 25 strangers who sent through their thoughts on the topic, 22 of them felt negatively about the apps we were communicating on.  Bring back daring. (Image credit: Hinge) How widespread is this, though? Could I have just found a group of uniquely cynical singles?  If you ask Crush Club creator Izzy Burns — whose Melbourne speed-dating events are drawing in droves of desperate singles — dating apps are the issue. “I think that dating apps have soured romance and genuine connection,” she told PEDESTRIAN.TV. “They give people the illusion of having endless options, resulting in a bunch of noncommittal, low-effort users.”  I often compare dating to Lord Of The Rings. (Image credit: Feeld) When it comes to the general sentiment of the singles walking through her doors, whose ages range from 18 to 40, she’s noted a complete shift away from the apps. “Most people are either bored of them and looking to try something new, or completely fed up and have deleted or paused their profiles,” she explained.  “Even outside of the events, I rarely have conversations with people who enjoy using the apps.”  The need for connection away from screens seems to have spread to the business side of intimacy. It's even been a driving force behind Love Honey’s Down & Dirty campaign. For every per cent of screen time you cut while away with your partner, you get that percentage knocked off the price of your stay at an Into The Wild cabin.  But how have we gotten to this point, where we have to encourage presence with one another?  Ate with that. (Image credit: Feeld) According to sexologist  Christina Rafe , while we’ve gained access to singles in our area, we’ve lost the art of interacting with them.  “Dating apps aren't inherently the problem,” she told P.TV. “But when we start seeing people as disposable, we lose the humanness that is required to encourage curiosity and build meaningful relationships.” This seems to be the general sentiment. (Image credit: Hinge) According to Rafe, the apps' constant cycling of new dating options “creates the illusion of endless choice”, where they’ll find “either your perfect match, or just one swipe away from the ‘perfect’ one.” She maintains, however, that there is both a yearning and opportunity for those app-trapped baddies to regain a little intimacy.  “After years of situationships, mixed signals and game-playing, people are increasingly drawn to folks who are upfront about their feelings and intentions,” she explained, pointing to pop-culture relationships such as   Off Campus ’ Hannah and Garrett as indicators of what people are actually looking for. Or, as she puts it, the “emotion smut” we’re consuming to compensate for the emotionally honest relationships we’re after.  To find real-time romance, Rafe says you simply need to look past the “dating app filters and icks” and instead head into the real world.  So, while you all may wish to keep those apps in your back pocket, it seems the experts are saying it’s time to get out there. Guess I’ll be seeing you at a Crush Club soon.

title: Big Brother Australia Host Mel Tracina Says She Already Knows Who Could Win The New Season
author: Lachlan Guertin
content: Big Brother Australia host Mel Tracina is fairly confident she knows who fans will be voting for on the upcoming season of the reality show, despite the fact that none of the contestants has even been announced yet. The radio presenter and Cheap Seats cultural commentator told PEDESTRIAN.TV ahead of next week’s premiere that she’s seen everyone’s audition tapes and has already worked out who the fan favourites and ‘villains’ of the season will be — but she’s not giving anything away just yet. “I feel like I already know who could win. Just based on, I want to say likability, but also probably layers,” she teased. “When you have an audition tape, you can find out a little bit more about someone because they're more forthcoming and explaining their life, right? But when they enter the house, it might be something that slowly comes out as the time progresses.” Big Brother Australia returns next week. (Credit: Channel 10) Mel recalls seeing 2025 housemate (and eventual runner-up) Emily Dale ’s audition tape and thinking that she could go all the way on the show — “when she came second I was like, ‘go me!’, but I can’t bet because that’s insider trading” — but she’s also aware that the contestants’ personal journeys on the show impact their chances of winning. “I feel like what Coco [ Beeby ] showed in that kind of first week of being in the house without her clothes and then forming this relationship with Bruce [ Dunne ] and being really vulnerable about missing her kids and being someone that was really loyal to her friends and sticking up for people in the house, that kind of arc of just watching her develop is why people voted her to win,” she shared. New changes to Big Brother 2026 After a successful reboot on Channel 10 last season, Big Brother is returning bigger and better than ever. Not only will the series have a longer run with even more housemates than last year, but it will also be filmed in Brisbane for the very first time with a brand new house. “I've seen the plans, and I know we are very much leaning into the Brisvegas feel. There is a stylistic choice that Big Brother has gone with, which is luminous luxury spectacle,” Mel described. “It's like sculptural architecture, rich textures, bougie lighting, and there's going to be more cameras and more microphones, which is so good.” Mel is also making some changes within her role and deciding to be an “admin girl” this time around to better prepare for her interviews with the housemates. “I've decided this year I need to take notes,” she declared. “So much happens, and there are so many iconic lines or moments or interactions between housemates, and I feel like my brain can't always hold on to them, and so I think I want to be better at taking notes this season, so that way I can really remember the housemates' time in the house.” The new season premieres Monday, October 26, at 7:30pm on 10, so stay tuned for all the inevitable drama, tension and awkwardness that comes from a group of strangers living under one roof for our entertainment.

title: Heated Rivalry Is Coming To Cinemas For Marathon Screenings If You Wanna Be Horny In Public
author: Lachlan Guertin
content: It's time to go back to the cottage . As we patiently wait for Heated Rivalry season two to be released, the hit Canadian romantic drama is heading to the big screen. Madman Entertainment has announced a one-day theatrical marathon of the critically acclaimed series for select Australian cinemas on December 5.  The special five-hour event will see all six episodes of the show’s first season screened back-to-back, with an intermission between episodes three and four for you to take a break from all that yearning. Tickets are on sale now at select cinemas across Australia, so tell your friends — or go alone if that's more your thing. Heated Rivalry is heading to the big screen. (Credit: HBO Max) Heated Rivalry season two details For the uninitiated, Heated Rivalry follows hockey players Shane Hollander ( Hudson Williams ) and Ilya Rozanov ( Connor Storrie ) as they navigate a years-long journey of love, denial, and self-discovery. The series was created by Jacob Tierney and is based on Rachel Reid 's bestselling novels. Production on season two began filming earlier this year and is set to premiere in April 2027, so the countdown is on. It's already been confirmed that the second season will adapt Reid's novel The Long Game , which picks up three years after the events of Heated Rivalry . Williams and Storrie hinted in HBO Max’s announcement video in December that season two will be “hotter, wetter, longer” — as if you needed any more convincing to tune in. “Start reading The Long Game if you wanna spoil it for yourself,” Storrie said.

title: Nine Responds To Police Investigation Following MAFS Groom’s Reported Complaint
author: Simran Pasricha
content: Content warning: This article discusses alleged image-based abuse.  NSW Police have confirmed an investigation into a report of “inappropriate content being shared”, following allegations that producers on the upcoming season of Married At First Sight (MAFS) shared a participant’s private material with his on-screen bride. “On Monday 24 August 2026, officers attached to South Sydney Police Area Command commenced an investigation following a report of inappropriate content being shared,” a NSW Police spokesperson told PEDESTRIAN.TV . “Following inquiries, the matter will be referred to WA Police Force.” It is unknown whether filming was halted because of this matter. (Image: 9Now) According to TV Blackbox , a male participant filming the 2027 season lodged a formal police complaint after producers allegedly shared personal material involving him and an ex-girlfriend with his bride. The publication linked the complaint to an alleged breach of NSW’s image-based abuse laws. Police have not confirmed what the content was or which potential offences are being investigated. Nine acknowledged the investigation when contacted by P.TV , directing questions to the show’s production company. “We are aware of a police investigation involving EndemolShine Australia and all enquiries should be directed to them," they wrote. While NSW Police intends to refer the matter interstate, WA Police told P.TV it had not yet received the referral at the time of writing. “We understand NSW Police intend to refer a matter to the WA Police Force; however, the referral has not yet been received," they wrote. “As such, we are unable to confirm any details at this stage." Neither force has explained the reason for the referral.  The Australian allegations come after a separate BBC Panorama investigation into MAFS UK aired in May. Two female participants alleged they had been raped by their on-screen husbands, while a third woman alleged a non-consensual sex act. The men involved denied the allegations. In July, the BBC reported that an unnamed UK cast member had been arrested on suspicion of rape and released on bail while inquiries continued. Following the BBC investigation, former Australian participant Tahnee Cook spoke to ABC’s 7.30 about feeling pressure to progress intimacy during her time on the show. “Given the nature of the show, you do feel the pressure to … progress quite quickly in the relationship, whether that is intimacy, whether that is connecting with that person,” she said. Nine and EndemolShine Australia told the ABC that participation in Intimacy Week was voluntary and participants were not expected to do anything they were uncomfortable with.  PEDESTRIAN.TV has reached out to EndemolShine for comment. Recording, sharing, or threatening to share an intimate image without consent is a criminal offence across much of Australia. If you'd like to report image based abuse to police or get help removing an intimate image from social media, reach out to the Australian eSafety Commissioner here . If you'd like to speak to someone about image based abuse, please call the 1800RESPECT hotline on 1800 737 732 or chat online . Under 25? You can reach Kids Helpline at 1800 55 1800 or chat online .

title: Channel 7 Has Announced The New Hosts For I'm A Celebrity 2027 & It's... Unexpected
author: Lachlan Guertin
content: Three months after it was announced that I’m A Celebrity… Get Me Out Of Here! would be returning in 2027 on a brand new network , Channel 7 has finally revealed who will be heading to the jungle to host the reality show. It was confirmed at the network’s 2027 Upfront Event on Thursday that longtime host Julia Morris and Aussie heartthrob Robert Irwin will be replaced by Ricki-Lee and Jim Jefferies for the show’s 13th season — which is quite the unexpected pair. “Raining Diamonds” hitmaker Ricki-Lee currently hosts Australian Idol on Channel 7 and presents Nova 96.9 Breakfast, while her comedian co-host has hosted The 1% Club Australia since its launch in 2023. The new season will feature an all-new cast of celebrities in the South African jungle, with the network promising “fresh twists” and “series firsts”. TBC what type of animal testicles the contestants will be eating. Ricki-Lee and Jim Jefferies are hosting I’m A Celebrity in 2027. (Credit: Instagram @therickilee / Channel 7) Ricki-Lee said in a statement that she “couldn’t be more excited” to be heading to South Africa to host “one of the most iconic shows in the world”. “I’m such a massive fan and it’s a huge honour. And to be doing it alongside the incredible Jim Jefferies makes it even better!” she said. “For years I’ve watched on from the comfort of my couch and now I get to experience it up close and personal — while standing comfortably off to the side with Jim. Watching our favourite celebrities squirm their way through some absolutely horrific challenges is gonna be a wild ride.” Jefferies also shared that he immediately said yes when offered the role, adding: "When Seven asked if I’d like to spend weeks in the African jungle watching celebrities eat strange things and embarrass themselves on national television, I couldn't say yes fast enough. It sounds like my ideal holiday.” Robert Irwin and Julia Morris have been replaced. (Credit: Channel 10)  Julia Morris reacts to new I'm A Celebrity hosts Following the announcement, outgoing host Julia Morris shared an Instagram post sending her well wishes to Ricki-Lee and Jefferies ahead of the new series. “These two absolutely glorious humans are off to the job of a lifetime. The ceremonial Knobkerrie is in the best of hands,” she wrote. “Love you both & can’t even BELIEVE the high levels of fun you are about to have! South Africa, up around Limpopo… is paradise. Chookas for a brilliant series. Let’s go!” While the TV veteran turned comments off on her post, the official Channel 7 post has been flooded with comments from fans lamenting Morris' exit — including a former I’m A Celebrity contestant. “Ngl there's no I'm A Celeb without Julia Morris in my eyes (I'm biased) but happy for this new era best of luck to them!” UK content creator and 2025 participant Max Balegde replied. “Julia Morris was the only reason I stayed watching this show for so long!” another fan commented, while someone else said, “The magic of this show was always Julia! Won’t be watching with these two hosting”. Others also criticised the fact that neither Ricki-Lee nor Jefferies have experience working with animals, unlike Irwin or former host Chris Brown . Channel 10 says goodbye to I’m A Celebrity Channel 10 confirmed in May that they had made the decision to “rest” I’m A Celebrity in 2027 and “focus on offering our audience a range of content on all platforms”. “We look forward to working with Julia Morris and Robert Irwin on other projects,” a spokesperson added. Irwin has since been announced as host of Australian Ninja Warrior alongside Georgie Tunny and Beau Ryan in 2027, while Morris currently appears on the ABC series Class Clowns .

title: MAFS’ Sam Stanton & Abbie Chatfield Have Slammed Filip Gregov’s ‘Manosphere-Adjacent’ Videos
author: Lachlan Guertin
content: Married At First Sight ( MAFS ) groom Sam Stanton has teamed up with Abbie Chatfield to call out his former co-star Filip Gregov after he shared a series of bizarre posts about the supposed “war on men”. Filip — who reportedly broke up with his fiancée Stella Mickunaite over the phone in July after falling in love on this year’s season of the reality show — has posted a string of controversial videos in recent weeks complaining about men having to help around the house and being “controlled”. “The most dangerous kind of man is one that can’t be controlled, that stands up for what he believes in, that means what he says, says what he means, and that is very intentional and not scattered,” he said. “There is a war on men — their attention, their sexual attention, their financial direction, where they fit into relationships, what their place is, everything. There’s a war on that.” Filip and Stella were this year's golden couple on MAFS. (Credit: Channel 9) Sam Stanton and Abbie Chatfield call out Filip Gregov Abbie Chatfield called out Filip’s “manosphere-adjacent” content on this week’s episode of her podcast It’s A Lot alongside his MAFS co-star Sam, who admitted he was recently blocked by the life coach on Instagram after sharing a post questioning why straight men are “so disrespectful to the gender they’re supposedly attracted to”. The pair specifically analysed one of Filip’s recent videos where he shared the criticism he gives female clients who want to find a partner: “You’re kind of showing a bit too much body over here, you’re following too many guys, you have very suggestive photos, you’re travelling all the time.” Sam pointed out the hypocrisy in his statement because Filip always shares shirtless photos on Instagram, and said he gets really “frustrated” and “upset” by this type of content. “I’m so disappointed that he’s spreading this message because it’s just so damaging, and I’m at a loss for words,” Sam said. “It’s encouraging women, in my opinion, to minimise themselves in an effort to get a man,” Abbie added. “Even to the point of not travelling… To say that travelling is a negative thing implies that having a big life is a negative thing and having a full life is a negative thing.” Elsewhere in the podcast, Abbie and Sam called out the “double standards” in Filip stating that men should “max out their lifestyle” by going jet skiing, cycling or running and “document it to a really high degree” on social media, while women should change their lifestyle to appeal to a man. “How could he sit there and say those things and not know that he’s literally told girls not to do that? That’s what really gets me, like is he just talking in circles?” Sam remarked. The podcast episode comes shortly after Filip’s ex Stella posted a now-deleted video saying his content left her feeling “humiliated”. “When I said I felt humiliated, I meant how confronting it is to hear views I deeply disagree with from someone I once loved and imagined a future with,” she told Woman’s Day . “My impression is that, somewhere along the way, he absorbed messages that encourage men to see women as a threat. I find that deeply sad, because those messages can push people away from the connection they want and sabotage relationships. That is how the ‘male loneliness epidemic’ begins.” Filip responds to online commentary In response to the recent commentary surrounding his online content, Filip simply told PEDESTRIAN.TV that he’s “moved on with [his] life”. “I wish people all the best and encourage them to go live their lives,” he said.  Well, that’s that then.
