title: Tennessee paid $1M for lethal injection drugs; concerns rising about past botched executions
author: Catherine Sweeney
content: Several new details about Tennessee’s recent executions came to light this week, including the price of the drugs and issues with executions leading up to Christa Pike’s catastrophic failed one . The state has paid more than a million dollars for lethal injection drugs since 2023, The Tennessean reports . Secrecy laws shield nearly every detail except for the dollar figure. So it’s unclear how many doses were purchased or where corrections officials bought the drugs. It’s also unclear where the drugs were created. There are two options . The first, by a pharmaceutical company in a commercial facility, which requires the medications to be diverted out of the tightly regulated monitoring system for controlled substances. Or, it could have been mixed at a compounding pharmacy. Those are labs that undergo more lenient inspections than other pharmacies and make copies of commercial drugs, which are not regulated by the Food and Drug Administration. Defense attorneys for death row inmates filed a motion with the Davidson County court on Thursday that details problems in each of the executions initiated under the 2025 lethal injection protocol. Those attorneys filed a lawsuit arguing that the new protocol was unconstitutional shortly after it was made public last year . The state has been fighting to get the case dismissed. One of the state’s arguments has been that concerns about misadministration were speculative. Defense attorneys say that it is no longer speculation. Two of the failed execution attempts, including Christa Pike’s , have drawn international attention to their problems. But even injections that did end in death had complications. For example, the department put Bryon Black to death in August 2025 . But EKG strips later showed his heart was beating steadily for several minutes after the doctor pronounced him dead. It’s unknown when he actually died. The motion filed this week is asking the court to let attorneys re-write their complaint. That way, it can incorporate facts from the long list of troubled executions under the new protocol. The state, meanwhile, is arguing the case should be thrown out because of a law change at the statehouse this year. In 2018, lawmakers made it easier for residents to sue the state government. Specifically, it let people to challenge laws before they’re harmed by them, instead of making them wait until they could prove they’ve already been harmed. Defense attorneys say the botched executions show harm. The legal team for Pike is undergoing a similar process. They filed a lawsuit arguing the protocol was illegal back in January. Similarly, it raised concerns about how Pike’s rights might be violated by the process. Now, they want to submit an updated complaint that explains the harm she experienced in her execution. Her team and the state are fighting about the timeline on that. Pike’s lawyers say re-writing the complaint will take months. Attorneys representing the Department of Correction want the cutoff to be Nov. 8 — 30 days from when Pike was released from the hospital. The issue was scheduled for a hearing on Friday, but the judge canceled it and said she would consider the issues without an oral argument.

title: The Boring Company is digging under Music City Center. Greater sinkhole, pollution risks lie ahead
author: Caroline Eggers
content: The Boring Company drilled near the Music City Center this week, suggesting the company has completed up to a tenth of its route between downtown and the airport. But trickier terrain lies ahead as the tunnel extends underneath Nashville, according to a new report commissioned by the Southern Environmental Law Center. Sinkholes, tunnel flooding and groundwater pollution from legacy industries are all potential risks as the project digs into Nashville’s limestone, according to the report. “It can be machines that get stuck. It can be sinkholes forming on the surface. Huge inflows of water,” said SELC attorney Trey Bussey. Nashville contains four layers of limestone between downtown and the airport along the company’s planned route of parallel tunnels: in order from highest to lowest, Leipers-Catheys, Bigby-Cannon, Hermitage and Carters. Courtesy Chris Groves/Western Kentucky University Nashville has four layers of limestone underground along the Boring Company’s planned route between downtown and the airport. The Leipers-Catheys, Bigby-Cannon, and Carters are relatively pure limestone layers of rock — and the more limestone, the more soluble the rock. They contain conduits, caves, and other karst features that have been enlarged by dissolution as groundwater moves through the soluble limestone. “These conditions create potentially severe karst-related tunneling challenges,” says the report by Chris Groves, a professor of hydrogeology at Western Kentucky University. It references projects by other companies in karst terrain that have resulted in “massive water or mud inflow and flooding, sinkholes and ground subsidence above the tunneling, and machine entrapment.” Without preparing for potential karst challenges, the report points to research referencing worst-case scenarios of “heavy casualties,” “serious economic losses” and “construction cessation.” The tunnel will go through ‘problematic’ limestone The Boring Company’s plan is to stay in the Hermitage Formation, which is a layer of limestone that’s mixed with tougher, less soluble minerals. But the Hermitage layer is completely eroded in some areas. The tunnel will be forced to go through the Carters Formation underneath Browns Creek, Mill Creek and the Cumberland River. “The Carters Limestone in this area has the most intense karst development and will likely be the most problematic to tunnel through,” the report says. Several mapped caves are located in the Carters within two miles of the tunnel route. One void, called Pulley Cave, has a passage measuring 30 by 40 feet, according to Tennessee Cave Survey data. Courtesy Chris Groves/Western Kentucky University The Boring Company plans to primarily drill through the Hermitage foundation, which is a less “pure” and thus less soluble level of limestone, but that layer has completely eroded away in some areas along the company’s planned tunnel route. Before tunneling, the Boring Company published an environmental assessment of its plan at the end of last year. In the 150-page document, less than 10 pages directly addressed water, safety or geology . The assessment solely references studies published between 1958 and 1990. The Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation chose not to require a permit due to this self-funded report. “The environmental info provided by the company was simply not serious,” said Nashville Councilmember Clay Capp, who read the new report. “That goes to show what this project is: an inside deal for favored billionaires who want to ignore the normal rules.” Capp suggested it was not too late to cancel the project. An additional geotechnical challenge could emerge if the company requires blasting. While limestone is considered, geologically, “easy to scratch,” and thus easy to cut through, some areas may have a mixture of particularly tough minerals. If the company blasts those areas, it could lead to fractures in the surrounding limestone and potential sinkholes. Sinkholes are not uncommon on construction sites in the region . But public awareness may be limited , as developers are not required to disclose incidents to the public, Jason Polk, a karst expert and professor of geoscience at WKU who was not involved in the report, told WPLN last year. Where is the Boring Company now? The Boring Company began tunneling underneath Nashville in February. The company has announced multiple projects, but it has only started tunnel construction on the route between downtown and the airport. This week, Boring planned to dig a pothole on 8th Avenue next to the Music City Center to “expose and verify utilities,” according to a ticket published on Tennessee811, a database for all digging activities. The center is located about one mile from the state parking lot where the project began. The pothole location represents where the tunnel will turn from 8th Avenue onto Lafayette Street. In eight months, the company has potentially completed as much as 10% of the parallel, one-way tunnel system’s roughly 9.5-mile length. It is unclear how much progress the company has made on both tunnels of the system. Since August, the company’s machines reached “a big milestone of both Prufrock-MB1 and Prufrock-MB2 tunneling at the same time,” the company wrote in a blog post on Oct. 1. The speed of tunneling does not appear to match the company’s estimated date of completion. When first announcing the project, the company said the tunnel would be operational by late 2026. Officials later adjusted that timeline to early 2027. The Boring Company did not respond to questions from WPLN about the report, its current digging location or its timeline for project completion. The Boring Company may encounter decades-old pollution The Boring Company may have been able to stay within the Hermitage Formation thus far, but it will very likely encounter karst features in the second half of its route. Along the way, the tunnel may pass properties that currently or historically used hazardous chemicals such as fuel stations, dry cleaners, auto shops and other industries. The Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation, or TDEC, has listed dozens of underground storage tanks for oil along the roads and mapped several dozen remediation sites. Roughly three miles from the Music City Center, the company could come into contamination near the former Aladdin Industries on Murfreesboro Pike. The company manufactured vacuum bottles, insulated trays and lamp mantles between 1949 and 2002. TDEC documented soil, groundwater and soil gas contamination by the carcinogen trichlorethylene, hazardous solvents, metals like arsenic, cadmium and lead, and a radioactive isotope of thorium, according to the report. Courtesy Chris Groves/Western Kentucky University The Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation has information on dozens of known or suspected hazardous waste sites along the Boring Company’s planned tunnel route between downtown and the airport. If the project runs through contaminated soil or groundwater, there is a risk that the contamination could spread. “Because of the karst features, groundwater can move in new and unpredictable ways if there are changes in the geology,” said Bussey, the attorney. Serious questions remain unanswered about the project and how the company will prepare for risks and handle complications, from potential pollution spread to fractured limestone, he said. “What happens if a tunneling machine gets stuck under Mill Creek?” Bussey said. “What happens if there’s a sinkhole on downtown streets that undermines the structural integrity of the buildings along the route? Who pays to fix those issues?”

title: The late Country Music Hall of Famer John Anderson was a singular voice
author: Jewly Hight
content: The widely admired country neotraditionalist John Anderson has passed at the age of 71 . Anderson was proud of the fact that he worked on the roof of the Grand Ole Opry House long before he was invited to grace its stage. Not just because it made for a good story, but because it spoke to the type of country artist he was: one who fashioned his thoroughly down-to-earth, blue-collar sensibilities into enduringly vital music. Anderson had done his share of rocking during his rural Florida youth, but he was also an admirer of honky-tonk’s great expressive voices. Lefty Frizzell. George Jones. Merle Haggard. And when Anderson began to score his own hits in the early 1980s, it wasn’t by aiming for what was popular at the time, but embracing his thrilling idiosyncrasies as a singer. Thanks to the often rollicking, mischievous songs he selected and the gutsy way he dug into the melodies’ bluesy bends, his music was instantly recognizable. Even when Anderson evolved from a country hitmaker into an elder statesman and slowed his touring, he still followed his gut. After a mysterious health condition caused him sudden and catastrophic hearing loss for which he sought successful treatment at Vanderbilt, he made one last deeply felt album and conveyed his gratitude to his doctors by playing a benefit show at the Ryman Auditorium. John Anderson sings for the doctors who gave him his music back In recognition of the mark he’d made, Anderson received what he considered the ultimate honor in 2024: induction into the Country Music Hall of Fame . “It’s a long, long road from Apopka, Florida, to standing right here on this stage,” he reflected during his acceptance speech. “But I must say … I got to choose my own way. And I said I wouldn’t really trade with anyone, because it was my way.” And we can surely hear that in the music Anderson left behind.

title: At Tennessee District 5 forum, Hatcher rescinds debate promise
author: Marianna Bacallao
content: Tennesseans will not see a debate between any of the state’s Democratic and Republican candidates for Congress. GOP District 5 nominee Charlie Hatcher told reporters that he won’t debate his Democratic opponent after all. The dairy farmer and former Tennessee agriculture commissioner had initially told the Williamson Scene that he was “committed to debating.” Now, he said he won’t go head-to-head with his Democratic opponent, Columbia Mayor Chaz Molder. “We got 13 days left, and every minute’s accounted for,” Hatcher said. In a red state like Tennessee, the Republican strategy has been to avoid debates . U.S. Sen. Marsha Blackburn has refused to debate in the primary and general elections for Tennessee governor. Tennessee’s 5th Congressional District is shaping up to be a much more competitive race. This election will be the first test of the new District 5 map since state lawmakers redrew the boundaries at the behest of President Donald Trump in May. While the Cook Political Report still rates the district as “Solidly Republican,” an energized Democratic base and an unpopular war in Iran could make for tighter results than expected. Hatcher has done something no other Republican running for Congress has done — share the stage with his Democratic opponent. He told reporters he’s “satisfied” with candidate forums. Unlike a debate, he and Molder cannot address each other or respond to the other’s answers. Marianna Bacallao WPLN News Tennessee District 5 Democratic candidate Chaz Molder (left), independent candidate Micheál O’Leary (middle) and GOP candidate Charlie Hatcher participate in a candidate forum in Spring Hill, Tenn. on Oct. 21, 2026. At their last candidate forum in Spring Hill Wednesday night, the pair disagreed on the economic success of the Trump administration’s tariffs. “Tennessee soybean farmers lost over $110 million last year as a result of bad trade and tariff policies … I was speaking to a local CEO of a company that employs about 300 people. He told me that he has to create a separate profit and loss statement that depends on whether the tariffs stick,” Molder said. “That’s a problem. That creates uncertainty.” Marianna Bacallao WPLN News Democratic Columbia Mayor Chaz Molder addresses the crowd at a Spring Hill candidate forum on Oct. 21, 2026. Hatcher said tariffs can help prioritize American production when they’re placed on the right industry, like dairy farming. “Tariffs are a tool. They can be used effectively, sometimes badly. And the first ones that take the brunt of it are farmers. But with the use of tariffs, (Trump) brought some of these countries to the table that were taking advantage of us and made very effective trade deals,” Hatcher said. When asked about the impact of tariffs on soybean farmers, Hatcher told WPLN News that he knows what soybean farmers want. “They want fair-balance trade, and they want international trade,” Hatcher said. “They want a farm bill. We can’t even get a farm bill passed.” Hatcher previously made an appearance at President Donald Trump’s rally in Clarksville on Oct. 10, where he stressed patience with the economy. “I know we are facing fierce economic headwinds. Just give it a little time. We’ll get that taken care of,” Hatcher said. He shared a booth that day with current District 5 Congressman Andy Ogles, who Hatcher defeated in the August primaries . Both Hatcher and Molder criticized Ogles’ lack of presence in the district and pledged to be more accessible to constituents. Early voting runs through Oct. 29. Election Day is Nov. 3.

title: At Michelin Guide’s Nashville ceremony, a local Mexican restaurant earns a new honor
author: Alexis Marshall
content: Chefs and restauranteurs from across the American South gathered in Nashville Wednesday night for the second-annual Michelin Guide ceremony. This is the fateful night when restaurant teams learn if they’ve earned, retained — or lost — their coveted stars from the world-renowned travel guide. Michelin debuted its American South guide last year , awarding one star each to three Nashville restaurants: Locust, Bastion and The Catbird Seat, all part of the Strategic Hospitality group. Wednesday’s ceremony revealed that all three held onto their stars. The Michelin Guide also recognized Nashville Mexican restaurant Maíz de la Vida for its high-quality cooking and great value for money with the Bib Gourmand distinction. It’s an honor shared by: St. Vito Focacceria Peninsula Uzbegim S.S. Gai Kisser Redheaded Stranger Sho Pizza Bar In an Instagram post, Maíz de la Vida thanked its workers, guests, and the farmers who supply its ingredients, including the restaurant’s namesake: maize. “We’ll keep doing what we love: cooking with heirloom corn, nixtamal, and the flavors that connect us to home,” the post read. View this post on Instagram And three restaurants in the city are newly recommended by the Michelin Guide: 5 th & Taylor, Junior and Present Tense. They don’t get a bib or stars, but even receiving a nod from the guide carries its own cachet. Last year’s Michelin recommended restaurants include: Audrey Arnold’s Country Kitchen Bad Idea Café Roze Folk Hattie B’s Iggy’s International Market January Rolf and Daughters, Shotgun Willie’s Tailor Explore the Michelin Guide’s full Nashville restaurant list.

author: Jay Hilotin
content: Houthi official says Egypt's military support for Saudi declaration of war A Houthi official said Tuesday that the Egyptian parliament's decision to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia to defend against the Iran-backed group's attacks was a declaration of war. "Egypt and its parliament declared support for what is called the defence of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and in doing so, it declares war against the Republic of Yemen," said Mohammed Ali al-Houthi, a member of the Houthis' political bureau, in a Telegram post. US updates Saudi travel alert as Riyadh airport resumes limited international flights The US Mission in Saudi Arabia has renewed its warning over airport security and flight disruptions following Houthi attacks on the kingdom. In an October 27 security alert, the mission said Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport had partially reopened on October 23 for domestic flights and some international services operated by national carriers. Some flights normally based in Riyadh are operating from Prince Naif bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Qassim. Jeddah and Dammam airports remain operational, although delays and cancellations continue. The mission also reiterated that the US State Department ordered non-emergency government employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia effective October 23. US government personnel require special authorisation to use Saudi airports. Travellers have been urged to exercise extreme caution and check flight status directly with airlines and airports. Security Alert: U.S. Mission Saudi Arabia (October 27, 2026) Effective October 23, 2026, the Department of State ordered non-emergency U.S. government employees and U.S. government employee family members to leave Saudi Arabia due to safety risks. Some 7.3 million people are eligible to vote, with the last polls to be published showing Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, running neck and neck with his main centrist rival Gadi Eisenkot. Most polling stations will close at 10:00 pm (2000 GMT). Saudi coalition intercepts four Houthi drones targeting southern region The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed four drones launched by Yemen's Houthi militia towards Saudi Arabia's southern region. Coalition spokesman Major General Turki Al-Malki confirmed the interceptions. Saudi air defences intercept three Houthi ballistic missiles targeting Eastern Region The Saudi-led coalition said its air defences intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles launched by Yemen's Houthi militia towards Saudi Arabia's Eastern Region. Coalition spokesman Major General Turki Al-Malki confirmed the interceptions. Oman urges Gulf security pact including Iran Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi urged a Gulf security framework including Iran and a non-aggression pact among the region’s eight states, the Foreign Ministry said Monday. Speaking at Cambridge University’s Girton College, he called for “a new regional security structure” designed and implemented locally, saying reliance on external powers had lasted too long. Excluding Iran would make any framework inherently unstable, he said. “It’s not a matter of whether you’re friendly or hostile to Iran,” Albusaidi said. “A Non-Aggression Pact between all eight states should be the goal,” he added, referring to the six Gulf Cooperation Council members, Iraq and Iran. 'Entering new path could be considered': Iran tells US, insists on 7 conditions for new talks Washington must fulfill seven conditions before Tehran considers negotiations, an Iranian official said on Monday, warning against a temporary deal followed by renewed military action or pressure. Ali Bagheri Kani, deputy for foreign policy and international security at the Supreme National Security Council secretariat, spoke to state television after Mecca Pact talks involving Iran, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan in Tehran. “If the United States fulfills them, then entering a new path could be considered,” he said. Bagheri Kani suggested Washington might pursue a short-term agreement to claim a political victory before the November 3 midterm elections, then resume military operations or increase pressure. He said countries had proposed shortening Iran’s seven-day implementation period. “Today, at the meeting, Mr. Rezaei said that if the issue is the number of days, we could accept five days or even four days,” he said, referring to council secretary Mohsen Rezaei. “But the important point is that these seven conditions must be fulfilled,” he added. “We have no doubt whatsoever that these seven conditions must be fulfilled. Once that happens, we will decide what to do next.” Syria shuts main border crossing Tuesday with Jordan after strikes Syria said it was closing its main border crossing in the country's south with Jordan on Tuesday after deadly strikes that Amman said came in retaliation for a jihadist attack on a church last week. Syria's border and customs authority announced the closure of the Nassib border crossing, known as Jaber on the Jordanian side, "due to the current circumstances", and suspended all "passenger and commercial traffic in both directions". Syria says death toll in Jordan strikes rises to 8 Syria said the death toll in Monday's strikes in its south had risen to eight, as Jordan said it had targeted "terrorist organisations" after a deadly jihadist attack on a church. Health officials said "hospitals in Daraa province have received eight victims, including an elderly man and three children", in addition to four wounded, raising an earlier toll of five dead. Syria says Jordan did not coordinate before strikes Syria's government said Monday that Jordan did not coordinate with it before launching deadly strikes on the country's south in retaliation for a deadly jihadist attack on a church last week. A Syrian government statement carried by state news agency SANA said "no prior coordination with the Syrian side was carried out concerning the military operation" by Jordan, adding authorities were investigating the strikes and discussing them with Amman while stressing the need for joint security coordination in border areas. Syria says five civilians killed in Jordanian strikes Syria said five civilians were killed on Monday by Jordanian strikes on the country's south that Amman's military said targeted "terrorist organisations" in retaliation for a deadly jihadist attack on a church last week. Syrian state news agency SANA, quoting a health official in Daraa province, said "five civilian victims including women and children fell in Jordanian airstrikes on several locations in Daraa province". Iran says agreed with Mecca pact countries security must come from region Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian (R) and National Security Council head Mohsen Rezaei (L) Iran said it had agreed with three countries party to the Mecca defence pact, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan, that regional security should be ensured by countries in the region itself and not by foreign actors. "The outcomes we agreed on were that security in the region where we live should be endogenous, meaning it should be achieved by the countries themselves, and that we must prevent any kind of foreign intervention in this region," Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei said after the meeting. Iran hails ‘very good’ talks with Mecca Pact nations Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian and National Security Council head Mohsen Rezaei during their meeting with Saudi Arabia's Defence Minister, Pakistan's army chief, and Turkey's intelligence chief in Tehran on October 26, 2026. Iran's security chief said Monday he held "very good discussions" with the three member countries of the Mecca defence pact, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, after their first meeting in capital Tehran. "Very good discussions took place between us," Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, told state television after the meeting with top officials from the three countries. "I feel that a new atmosphere is emerging in the region... I sensed a very positive atmosphere in the discussions among the gentlemen." The Israeli foreign ministry said on X that the investigators' finding "is not a human rights report but a propaganda document detached from reality, aimed at undermining Israel's right to self-defense, delegitimising the Jewish state, and legitimising terrorism against its citizens". title: Ronaldo makes Portugal preliminary squad for next round of internationals
author: Robert Ilsley
content: Dubai: Cristiano Ronaldo has been named in Portugal’s preliminary squad for their upcoming Nations League fixtures, despite reports of a strained relationship with head coach Jorge Jesus following the forward’s departure from the national team camp during the previous international break. The Al-Nassr captain has been included on Portugal’s provisional list for the November international window, alongside club teammates Joao Felix and Samu Costa. His inclusion comes after an incident in September raised questions over his international future. Ronaldo was reportedly unhappy after being left on the bench for Portugal’s match against Norway in Oslo, with tensions escalating before he left the squad ahead of the fixture against Denmark. The dispute between Cristiano Ronaldo and Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus centred on broken promises over Ronaldo’s playing time. The 41-year-old’s presence on the preliminary list suggests he remains in contention for selection, although the final squad is yet to be confirmed. Portugal are scheduled to face Denmark in Braga before travelling to Cardiff to play Wales in their final Nations League Group A4 matches. According to Portuguese media reports, the final squad announcement is expected on Friday, November 6. Suspension nearing its end Ronaldo’s potential return has also been helped by the timing of his disciplinary punishment. The Portuguese Football Federation’s Disciplinary Council handed the forward a 30-day suspension following the incident, with the sanction due to expire on October 30. That would leave him eligible for selection ahead of Portugal’s November fixtures, although his inclusion in the preliminary squad does not guarantee a place in the final team. Chasing more international records Despite the reported tensions, Ronaldo remains one of the most decorated players in Portugal’s history. Ronaldo is Portugal's all-time top scorer and appearance maker He holds the record for international appearances, with 234 caps, and has scored 146 goals for his country. His achievements include captaining Portugal to their first major international trophy at Euro 2016, as well as winning the Nations League in 2019 and 2025. Portugal maintain perfect record Portugal have made an impressive start to their Nations League campaign, winning all four group matches to collect 12 points and secure early qualification for the quarter-finals. Their results include a 1-0 victory over Wales, a 4-2 win against Denmark and two 2-1 victories over Norway. Ronaldo’s possible return would provide another major talking point ahead of the final fixtures, as Portugal look to maintain their momentum in the competition. title: Not even 3, this Karnataka girl can play 12 taals on tabla
author: Devadasan K P
content: Dubai: A two-year-and-10-month-old girl from Karnataka has captured attention online after earning a place in the India Book of Records for reciting and playing 12 taals on the tabla. Swarshri Hegde, from Honnavara in Uttara Kannada district, has impressed social media users with her musical ability at an age when most children are just beginning to explore the world. A video of her performance, shared on X, has gone viral, drawing praise from viewers amazed by her ability to combine rhythmic recitation with tabla playing. Her name is Swarshri Hegde she is 2 years 10 months old. But at this little age only she has made into India Book of Records for reciting,playing 12 taals in Tabala. She is from Honnavara Uttara Kannada Karnataka. Congratulations to little Swarshri pic.twitter.com/U5TjJKT35N — Adarsh Hegde (@adarshahgd) October 24, 2026 In Indian classical music, a taal is a rhythmic cycle that provides the structure for a musical performance. Reciting a taal involves vocalizing its bols —syllables representing different percussion strokes—while playing it on the tabla requires rhythm, coordination, and controlled hand movements. Mastering multiple rhythmic patterns takes practice and concentration, making Swarshri’s reported achievement particularly remarkable given that she is not yet three years old. Social media applauds young talent The video has prompted an outpouring of appreciation, with users celebrating the young musician and her achievement. One user described it as a proud moment for Uttara Kannada. At the same time, another invoked Goddess Saraswati, the Hindu deity associated with knowledge, music, and the arts, to express admiration for the child. Another commenter praised Swarshri as a gifted child and remarked on her name. One viewer described the performance as unbelievable, comparing the toddler to a little goddess playing the tabla and reciting musical syllables. Another commenter joked that she must have started practicing in her mother’s womb. The response highlights the fascination with a young child showing musical skills that typically take sustained practice to develop. Swarshri’s achievement has drawn fresh attention to her early musical abilities, and her performance has won admiration from viewers across social media. title: iPhone Duo screen cracks: Why do foldable displays fail at the fold?
author: Lakshana N Palat
content: A foldable screen almost never fails at random: When it breaks, it breaks along the fold, because that is the one strip of the phone asked to do something glass normally cannot. That is why the early iPhone Duo reports look so alike. Apple’s first foldable went on sale on October 23 at $1,999 (Dh8499 in UAE) and up. Within days, owners were posting photos of inner screens cracked along the center line of the hinge. On October 26, Apple said it was aware of an issue on 'a small number' of units and told affected owners to contact AppleCare for a replacement. It did not say what causes it. If you have never owned a foldable, here's what is actually inside that bending screen, why the fold is the weak point, and what the hinge has to get right. It also covers what is known, and not yet known, about the Duo. iPhone Duo crackgate: Apple breaks silence on screen cracks, offers replacements Are iPhone Duo screens really cracking? Fake photos cloud ‘Crackgate’ as real cases emerge Glass that bends Glass can bend if it is thin enough. The trick behind every modern foldable is not a new kind of glass but glass made extraordinarily thin. A window pane snaps when you bend it because its outer surface is pulled apart. The thicker the sheet, the harder that outer surface is stretched for a given curve. Make the sheet thin, and the same curve barely stretches it. As Northwestern materials scientist John Rogers put it to The New York Times, thickness governs how stiff something is against bending. How thin? A human hair is roughly 50 to 100 micrometres across. The glass layer in the iPhone Duo is reportedly under 30 micrometres. Samsung describes its own ultra-thin glass, or UTG, as about a third the thickness of a hair. The trade-off is built in. Corning, the US glass company best known for the Gorilla Glass on many phone screens, also makes bendable glass for foldables. Its patent filings note that glass around 75 micrometres or thinner bends tightly but resists punctures poorly. Glass thicker than about 125 micrometres resists punctures well but can only bend to a radius of about 30 mm. A foldable display needs a bend radius of about 10 mm or less. So the glass at the fold is as thin as engineers dare, and everything around it exists to protect it. A screen made of layers The inner screen is not one sheet. It is a sandwich of thin layers glued together, and each has a different job. iFixit counted about 10 layers in the iPhone Duo’s inner display. Samsung’s support pages describe a simpler version of the same basic stack, from the top down: Protective film: a replaceable top sheet that takes everyday scratches and pressure. Protective layer: sits on the glass, absorbs impacts and holds pieces together if the glass breaks. Ultra-thin glass: gives a flat, glass-like surface and stiffens the stack. OLED panel: the layer that actually makes the picture, with each pixel producing its own light. The layers are bonded with optically clear adhesives, as The Star had once explained. Those glues matter more than they sound. When the stack bends, the outer layers travel a slightly longer path than the inner ones, and the adhesive has to let them slide a little without peeling apart. The top layers are part of the structure, not decoration. In 2019, several Galaxy Fold review units failed after reviewers peeled off what looked like a screen protector, but was a layer Samsung never meant to be removed. The Duo has its own wrinkle: it is the only foldable with a matte screen, and iFixit found its nano-texture coating comes off easily. Until the coating is replaced, the display is more exposed. Stretch and squeeze Every time you bend something, one side gets pulled apart and the other side gets pushed together. Glass handles being pushed together very well. It handles being pulled apart badly, so cracks start on the side that gets stretched. Corning describes folded glass as being squeezed on one side and pulled on the other at the same moment. Somewhere in the middle runs a line that is neither stretched nor squeezed. Engineers call it the neutral plane. How hard the outer side gets stretched comes down to two things: how thick the layer is and how tight the bend is. A thicker sheet gets stretched more, and so does a sheet bent more tightly. Corning’s patent filings describe exactly this trade-off. Picture a thick rubber eraser. Bend it, and you can see the outside surface stretch while the inside bunches up. Bend a thin rubber band into the same curve and it barely changes. That is why foldable glass is made so thin, and why the hinge works so hard to keep the curve gentle. Engineers use that calm middle line to protect the most delicate part. They arrange the layers so the OLED pixels sit on or near it, which means the part that makes the picture barely feels the fold. This matters because the seals that keep moisture out of the OLED are thin and brittle. It is a fine balance. If one layer comes out a little thicker or stiffer than planned, that middle line can shift, and the delicate parts start to feel the strain. Glass makers add one more trick. They treat the glass so its surface is already slightly squeezed before it ever bends. A fold has to undo that squeeze before the surface actually starts to stretch. Tiny flaws, big cracks Glass rarely breaks because the whole sheet is too weak. It breaks because a microscopic flaw on the stretched surface becomes the starting point of a crack. Every real glass surface carries tiny scratches and nicks, some far smaller than a micrometre. Under bending, stress concentrates at the tip of each one. Corning’s patents describe the danger in two forms: instant failure, or a slower fatigue failure where a flaw grows a little with each cycle until it runs. Glass has a fracture toughness of roughly 0.7 MPa√m, and the same filings put the threshold for slow growth under repeated loading at about 0.2 MPa√m. That is why a phone can survive many folds and then crack on an ordinary one. Manufacturers fight this in three ways: Smaller flaws: Corning’s designs aim to keep surface flaws around 5 micrometres or smaller, and in some cases under half a micrometre. Clean edges and surfaces: Samsung says a smoothly cut edge is vital and that it polishes UTG to remove imperfections. A compressed skin: if flaws stay inside the layer that ion exchange has put into compression, they are held shut and do not grow. The environment also plays a part. Research presented to the Society for Information Display notes that crack growth in UTG under repeated loading behaves much like it does in thick glass, with temperature and humidity affecting how fast a crack spreads. The hinge decides the bend The glass only survives if the hinge never lets it bend tighter than it was designed for. The hinge is not just a pivot. It sets the exact shape the screen takes every time you close the phone. A hinge that pinches the screen into a sharp fold concentrates all the bending stress along one narrow line, according to an analysis of foldable creases published by SoftwareSeni. Most modern foldables instead use a waterdrop or teardrop hinge, and repair specialist iFixit’s teardown of the iPhone Duo, as reported by Tom’s Guide, shows Apple chose the same design. When the phone closes, the screen curls into a teardrop-shaped loop inside the hinge rather than being folded flat at one point. Think of folding paper flat versus rolling it around a pencil: same material, very different stress. Even a well-designed hinge leaves a mark. Folding the same strip of screen thousands of times creates the familiar crease, and lab measurements show it deepens with repeated folding and with time spent folded. A crease is cosmetic. A crack is what happens when the screen is forced into a shape the hinge was supposed to prevent. Pressure points: when something pushes from below Many of the most sudden fold failures are not caused by the bending alone. They come from a hard point pressing into the screen at the fold: a grain of grit, a hinge part in the wrong place, or a finger or object on the outside. A screen stack a fraction of a millimetre thick has almost no stiffness of its own. Push a small, hard point into it while it is flexing, and the stress at that spot can far exceed what the bend alone produces. Samsung’s own care guidance tells owners to avoid pressing on the fold or closing the phone on cards, keys, sand or metal dust. It also warns that a crack in the UTG can spread and show up as a white line. The industry learned this publicly in 2019. Several Samsung Galaxy Fold review units broke within days. iFixit traced one likely cause to a gap of about 7 mm near the hinge that let debris slip beneath the screen. The Verge’s unit developed a bulge from a trapped particle before its pixels died. Samsung delayed the launch and, according to Yonhap, closed the gap near the hinge before shipping. Dust is still hard to keep out. A water and dust rating such as IP68 does not mean a hinge is sealed against fine grit. In iFixit’s fluorescent-powder test, particles still got into the iPhone Duo’s hinge, though less than in the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Pixel 11 Pro Fold. What this means for the iPhone Duo The Duo’s failures fit the pressure-point pattern, but the cause is not confirmed. Apple has not explained it, and the leading theory comes from a teardown, not from failed phones. What owners describe is consistent. Cracks appear at the same spot along the fold, often with a stuck feeling or a popping noise just before, and frequently a line of bright pixels. One Australian owner said his phone cracked within about six hours and fewer than 20 openings. Apple says the problem tends to show up soon after purchase. iFixit built a 3D model of the hinge from teardown footage, patents and CT scans, then compared it with where screens are failing. Its main suspect is a center support bar that may not drop far enough as the phone folds. That would create a pressure hotspot between the underside of the screen and the hinge. Grit in the hinge is a second possibility. Three cautions apply: iFixit itself says none of its theories are confirmed. It named three possible mechanisms, and many headlines overstated what it found. Not every “crack” may be broken glass. iFixit noted that a wiring fault can produce the same look. There is no failure rate. No repair, teardown or service data yet shows how many units are affected, so any percentage quoted now is a guess. A widely shared CT-scan theory was based on an intact review unit, not a failed phone. If you are new to foldables A foldable screen is tougher than it looks when it folds normally, and far more fragile than a regular phone screen against pressure at the fold. Treat it that way. Keep the fold clean. Never close the phone on anything, including grit, a card or a key. Samsung’s guidance applies to any foldable. Don’t press on the crease. Avoid pens, nails and hard tapping on the inner screen, especially along the fold. Leave the factory layers alone. The top film is part of the screen, not a disposable protector. Removing it can damage the panel. Expect a crease. A faint line at the fold is normal. A sudden bright line, a crunching sound or a stiff spot when folding is not. Know your window. Apple says Duo owners with a damaged inner display should contact AppleCare for a replacement, and no AppleCare+ plan is needed. Carrier buyers should go to AppleCare directly, and launch buyers have a two-week return window. title: DIP IPO: How UAE residents can apply, from just Dh5,000
author: Stacy Pereira
content: STOCK DIP / Dubai Investments Park Dubai: UAE residents can apply for DIP Holding’s initial public offering from today, October 27, with as little as Dh5,000. The offer is open for subscription and will closes on November 3. The price range has been fixed at Dh1.10 to Dh1.15 per share. Although a book-building process will fix the final price, due on November 4. Public tranche allocations follow on November 10. Anyone who receives fewer shares than requested gets the balance refunded. Trading is expected to begin on or around November 11. Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here. How can a UAE resident apply? The Dh5,000 minimum applies to the public tranche, which covers individuals and anyone holding a valid Dubai Financial Market (DFM) investor number, known as an NIN. Further investments go up in multiples of Dh1,000. There is no maximum. At the top of the price range, Dh1.15 per share, Dh5,000 buys about 4,348 shares. Successful subscribers are guaranteed at least 2,000 shares. Other groups of investors face different thresholds. Eligible Dubai Investments employees can start bidding for the IPO at just Dh1,000, while eligible shareholders need Dh5,000. Professional or institutional investors must commit at least Dh1 million. Where to apply? Applicants can use the DFM IPO subscription platform, the DFM mobile app or the DFM iVESTOR application. Individuals need their NIN and a valid passport or Emirates ID. Electronic channels run their own identity checks. After choosing a platform, investors enter the NIN, select the DIP Holding offering and provide banking details. Some payment methods shut before the November 3 deadline. Also since the public tranche is small and holds only 5 per cent of the offer, or 86,762,165 shares, allocations may fall short of requests, so early applications are safer. First dividend due April DIP Holding expects to pay Dh725 million for 2027, implying a yield of 7.27 to 7.60 per cent across the range. The first payout of Dh350 million , due in April 2027, covers the whole of the second half of 2026. Shareholders who join through the IPO therefore collect a full half-year. The company has not guaranteed these payments, which depend on board recommendation, shareholder approval and distributable reserves. Dubai Investments PJSC is selling 1,735,243,300 existing shares, equal to 20 per cent of DIP Holding. The offering is worth Dh1.9 billion to Dh2 billion . It is the UAE’s first IPO this year. DIP Holding owns the company that operates Dubai Investments Park, a 23 million square metre estate. title: Dubai's new World Trade Centre bridge: Roads connected, travel times and benefits
author: Zainab Husain
content: Dubai: If you regularly drive through the Dubai World Trade Centre area, you have probably noticed the extensive roadworks around one of the city's busiest intersections. While work continues on nearby roads, motorists will soon see the benefits of a major upgrade. From Friday, October 30, Dubai's Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) will open the final bridge of the Dh696-million-plus World Trade Centre Roundabout Development Project , designed to cut journey times, ease congestion and improve connections between some of Dubai's busiest roads. Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here. Where is Dubai's new bridge located? The new bridge is located at the World Trade Centre Roundabout , a major intersection connecting Sheikh Zayed Road with five key streets: Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Street Sheikh Rashid Street 2nd December Street Za'abeel Palace Street Al Majlis Street The intersection is a key route for motorists travelling between Dubai World Trade Centre, Downtown Dubai, Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC) , Deira and surrounding neighbourhoods. Which roads does the new bridge connect? The 1,000-metre (1km), two-lane bridge connects Al Majlis Street to 2nd December Street. It can accommodate approximately 3,000 vehicles per hour and is designed to provide a smoother, more direct route between the two streets. The bridge is the fifth and final structure to open under the World Trade Centre Roundabout Development Project , completing a network of five bridges spanning a combined 5km. Ongoing work for the World Trade Centre Roundabout Development Project. How much time will motorists save? For motorists regularly using the intersection, the biggest benefit will be shorter journeys and fewer delays. According to RTA, the improvements will: Cut travel time from Al Majlis Street to 2nd December Street from six minutes to just one minute. Reduce average delays at the intersection from 12 minutes to 90 seconds. Improve traffic flow between Sheikh Zayed Road, Al Mustaqbal Street, Sheikh Rashid Street and surrounding roads. The new bridges will also help reduce the need for motorists to navigate the former roundabout, allowing traffic to move more freely along major routes. What has changed at World Trade Centre Roundabout? The development involved transforming the former roundabout into a ground-level intersection and constructing five bridges to improve traffic movement in different directions. Apart from the final bridge opening on October 30, the project includes: Sheikh Zayed Road to Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Street: A 1km, two-lane bridge towards Deira, accommodating 3,000 vehicles per hour. Sheikh Rashid Street to 2nd December Street: Two bridges providing two lanes in each direction, spanning a combined 2km and accommodating up to 6,000 vehicles per hour. Al Majlis Street to 2nd December Street: Two bridges spanning a combined 2km, including the final bridge opening on Friday, with a capacity of approximately 6,000 vehicles per hour. Dubai RTA opens new DWTC bridge, cutting travel time from 10 minutes to 2 Dubai RTA opens new bridge cutting travel time from 6 minutes to 1 minute at World Trade Centre Roundabout Major traffic relief: RTA opens new bridges easing congestion across central Dubai Which Dubai roads and neighbourhoods will benefit? The improvements will benefit motorists travelling between: Jumeirah Al Satwa Dubai World Trade Centre DIFC Deira Neighbourhoods expected to benefit include Za'abeel, Al Satwa, Al Karama, Al Jafiliya and Al Makhoul. According to RTA, the project is expected to serve more than 500,000 residents and visitors , including commuters and people attending exhibitions and events at Dubai World Trade Centre. Why are roadworks still continuing nearby? Although the World Trade Centre Roundabout Development Project will be completed with Friday's bridge opening, another major road upgrade is still under way nearby. The Al Mustaqbal Street Development Project extends from the intersection with Za'abeel Palace Street to Financial Centre Street. The project includes: Widening Al Mustaqbal Street from three to four lanes in each direction. Constructing bridges and tunnels spanning a combined 1.5km. Increasing the road's capacity by 33 per cent. Reducing journey times from 13 minutes to six minutes. When will the remaining roadworks be completed? The Al Mustaqbal Street Development Project is scheduled for completion in 2027 . Once finished, it will complement the new World Trade Centre bridges, providing better connectivity between Dubai's business districts and surrounding residential areas while helping the road network accommodate future traffic growth. title: Amy Jackson on Dubai's charm: A city of endless fun for families and boundless ambition for creators
author: Manjusha Radhakrishnan
content: Dubai: For British actress and model Amy Jackson , Dubai isn't just another glamorous destination on the international celebrity circuit. It's a city she keeps returning to, both for work and family holidays. And the reason is refreshingly simple: Dubai never gets boring. "It just keeps changing and getting better and better. So every time is like a new experience, but it's built on tradition. It's built on a beautiful culture," Jackson said in an interview during her visit to Beautyworld Middle East in Dubai. Amy Jackson and Ed Westwick The actress, who has built a career spanning modelling, Indian cinema, fashion and beauty, is particularly taken by the city's infectious ambition. "I love the fact that it's an ever-growing society. It feels massively metropolitan," she said. But beyond its skyscrapers and opportunities, it's the people who make the difference. "I think it's the warmth of the people here. Everybody is very inspired, and they're very motivated." For Jackson, Dubai's appeal extends well beyond professional engagements. The city has become a favourite family holiday destination, thanks to its convenience and endless entertainment options. "But every holiday we get, we are like, okay, kids, Dubai. We're like, yes, because it is just so easy, so straightforward, and fun," she said. "There's always something new for the kids to do, and keeping them entertained, and also taking care of the adults at the same time. There's something for everyone, everyone, which I love." Jackson also believes Dubai's entrepreneurial energy makes it a natural playground for beauty brands, fashion entrepreneurs and content creators. "I think it's the people who are living here and wanting more and being inquisitive and curious, and wanting to push the boundaries and see what they can do and see what they create," she said. Her appearance at Beautyworld Middle East reinforced her belief that the beauty industry is no longer simply about selling products. It's about building communities and making consumers feel part of something bigger. "The brands that are doing very well are the brands that involve the community," she said, pointing to interactive campaigns, workshops and immersive experiences as examples. For Jackson, beauty has always been deeply personal. Growing up in Liverpool, she was surrounded by women who celebrated individuality through makeup, skincare, hair and nails. "It's a form of self-expression and self-worth," she said. That philosophy has followed her through modelling, acting and collaborations with major beauty brands, including L'Oréal, Armani, YSL and Prada. Ultimately, she believes beauty should be about enjoyment rather than rigid rules. "I've always had that mindset that it's about feeling good and having fun," she said. And perhaps that's precisely why Dubai resonates with her: a city where reinvention, ambition and having fun seem to go hand in hand. title: Forget the Ballon d'Or, Bukayo Saka won the biggest award of the night
author: Shamseer Mohammed
content: Bukayo Saka wins the award that celebrates football beyond trophies For me, Bukayo Saka won one of the most meaningful awards of the night at the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony in London. The Arsenal and England star received the Socrates Award, recognising his incredible humanitarian work. Now, I am not saying the Ballon d'Or or any of the other awards are less meaningful. They recognise years of hard work, dedication and extraordinary achievements on the football pitch. But the introduction of the Socrates Award has been a fantastic addition to the ceremony. Because football is not just about goals, assists and trophies. It is also about the difference these footballers can make in people's lives. And Saka is a wonderful example of that. Speaking at the ceremony, the 25 year old explained how he works alongside his family and the charity BigShoe to help children who are less fortunate. "I work a lot with my family and the charity called BigShoe. We try to do our best to help children who don't have the same opportunities or capabilities we have." Changing lives beyond football In 2022, Saka helped fund 120 surgeries for children in Kano, Nigeria, where his parents are originally from. He later supported medical treatment for another 100 children across Rwanda, Kenya and Tanzania. He also helped provide accommodation for 26 families affected by the devastating earthquakes in Türkiye in 2023. But one of the most touching moments of the ceremony came when Saka shared the story of Biringiro, a 14 year old boy from Rwanda. The youngster had been losing his eyesight and was struggling to read at school or even play with his friends. Thanks to BigShoe, he received the treatment he needed and can now see clearly again. And guess what? He now dreams of becoming an English teacher. Just imagine that. A child who was struggling to see the blackboard can now dream of standing in front of one as a teacher. That is the kind of impact footballers can have beyond the pitch. Supporters of Brazil's President and Workers' Party (PT) presidential candidate Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva hold a banner featuring Lula in the state of Sao Paulo, Brazil, on October 25, 2026, during the presidential runoff election. The Socrates connection with Lula There is another beautiful story behind this award. It is named after legendary Brazilian footballer Sócrates, who was not just a wonderful midfielder but also a doctor, a political activist and a passionate advocate for democracy. During Brazil's military dictatorship, Socrates played an important role in the Corinthians Democracy movement, which promoted democratic decision making within the club. He was also a friend and political ally of Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, the leftist leader who later became president of Brazil. Both were involved in Brazil's democracy movement during the 1980s. And here comes quite a coincidence. On Sunday, October 25, Lula was re-elected president of Brazil for a fourth term, defeating Flavio Bolsonaro. Just a day later, Saka received an award named after Socrates, the footballer who once stood alongside Lula in Brazil's fight for democracy. Socrates passed away in 2011, but his legacy continues through an award that celebrates footballers who make a difference in society. Quite a coincidence, isn't it? More than just football Footballers deserve recognition for their achievements on the pitch. Winning the Ballon d'Or, the Kopa Trophy or any other major individual honour is something special. But recognising their contributions to society is equally important. An award that celebrates someone for helping others has a special place of its own. And that is why I believe the Socrates Award has been one of the best additions to the Ballon d'Or ceremony. It reminds us that footballers can be heroes not just for what they do with a ball at their feet, but also for what they do with the opportunities their success gives them. Well deserved, Bukayo Saka! title: ‘Running saved my life’: Alex Bowman’s story behind 100km Dubai run
author: Robert Ilsley
content: Dubai Fitness Challenge returns this weekend, inviting residents and visitors to embrace an active lifestyle as the city prepares for a month of free fitness activities, community events and sporting challenges. Launched in 2017 by His Highness Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence, the initiative encourages everyone to complete 30 minutes of physical activity every day for 30 days. Now celebrating its 10th edition, the challenge has attracted more than 16 million participants. Running from October 31 to November 29, this year's event will transform Dubai into a fitness hub, with three Fitness Villages, 34 Community Fitness Hubs and thousands of free classes available to the public. Among the most inspiring stories to emerge from the initiative is that of Alex Bowman, who will mark the opening day by attempting to run 100km across 10 of Dubai's most iconic landmarks. The Dubai Fitness Challenge ambassador will set off on Saturday October 31, with his route showcasing the city's landmarks. "I'm excited to take on this challenge through Dubai, especially knowing the community can be part of the journey,” said the Dubai resident. The runner has covered 168km in 24 hours, completed 12 marathons since taking up running four years ago and recorded a personal-best marathon time of 2:44. Despite those achievements, Bowman knows the distance will present its own difficulties. "People sometimes assume that because you've run 100km before, it somehow becomes easier, it doesn't,” explained Bowman. “Every distance deserves respect, regardless of how many times you've covered it. “There will inevitably be moments when things get difficult. But that's also what excites me, those moments where you have to dig a little deeper, trust yourself and keep moving forward." Bowman hopes the run will become a collective effort rather than simply a personal endurance test, inviting members of the public to accompany him along any part of the route. He said: "This challenge isn't just about me running 100km. It's about bringing people together through movement and showing what's possible when we support one another. “Whether someone wants to run a few kilometres alongside me, join for a longer section or simply come out and cheer, every bit of support will mean something." "You don't need to run 100km to be part of a 100km challenge. Run your distance, whatever that looks like." Running with a purpose Behind Bowman's achievements is a personal story that reflects the importance of physical activity beyond competition and performance. His introduction to running came during a difficult period following the loss of his father, shortly after he became a father himself. What began as a way to cope with grief eventually became a central part of his life. "Running came into my life completely by accident,” said Bowman. “I had been searching for a positive way to deal with personal pain after losing my father. I didn't start running to become an athlete. I started running for my mind, and that's always remained my biggest motivation." "Running genuinely saved my life. It gave me structure, purpose and a way to work through things I didn't always know how to deal with." The story also resonates with the theme of the UAE's Year of Family, under which this year's Dubai Fitness Challenge is taking place. For Bowman, the initiative's appeal lies in its ability to encourage people to get active without placing pressure on them to achieve a particular result. "It removes the idea that fitness has to be about competition, ability or achieving a particular result. “Instead, it encourages everyone to get moving, regardless of where they're starting from. I always say that you don't have to be an athlete to inspire someone. Anyone can influence anyone." Proud to represent Dubai Fitness Challenge Bowman was named among the fitness ambassadors representing the landmark 10th edition, a role he views as an opportunity to encourage others to discover the benefits of exercise. "I genuinely couldn't be prouder,” added Bowman. “For me, being an ambassador isn't just about representing an initiative - it's about representing something I wholeheartedly believe in. "The energy around Dubai Fitness Challenge is incredible. Seeing an entire city come together, supporting and motivating one another through movement, is something really special. “If my story encourages just one person to start, to keep going or to believe in themselves a little more, then I've done something worthwhile." As Dubai Fitness Challenge celebrates its 10th edition, the initiative continues to promote the idea that small, consistent steps towards an active lifestyle can make a difference. With free classes, community activities and opportunities for people of all fitness levels, the city-wide event aims to make movement part of everyday life. Residents and visitors can register for Dubai Fitness Challenge 2026 at www.dubaifitnesschallenge.com . title: ‘Take extreme caution’: US Embassy warns Americans flying from Saudi Arabia
author: Surabhi Vasundharadevi
content: Dubai: The US Embassy in Riyadh has issued a security alert, saying the State Department ordered non-emergency US government employees and their family members to leave Saudi Arabia due to safety risks, effective October 23. In the alert posted on X on Tuesday, the embassy said Iranian-backed Houthis have carried out hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure. These attacks have resulted in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions, and the embassy warned the situation could escalate rapidly beyond the immediate area. Following recent missile and drone attacks on airports in the Kingdom, US government employees in Saudi Arabia now need special authorisation from the Chief of Mission to use any airport in the country. According to the embassy, King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh partially reopened on October 23 for domestic flights and some international flights operated by national carriers. A limited number of flights normally based in Riyadh are operating from Prince Naif bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Qassim. King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam are both operating, but with some delays and cancellations. The embassy warned US citizens to be aware of possible attacks on airports, airspace closures, flight cancellations and travel disruptions. It urged them to take extreme caution if they choose to use airports in Saudi Arabia, and to check their flight status directly with their airline and the airport.

title: Free Nakheel Palm Run returns to Palm Jumeirah on Nov 14 with 3km, 5km and 10km races
author: Areeba Hashmi
content: Dubai:  Runners will take over Palm Jumeirah's Crescent next month as the Nakheel Palm Run returns on Saturday, November 14. Organised by Nakheel, part of Dubai Holding Real Estate, with events company Race ME, the community run offers three distances, 3km, 5km and 10km, along a route with views of the Arabian Gulf and the Dubai skyline. When: Saturday, November 14, from 5.30am Where: Palm Jumeirah Boardwalk, Palm Jumeirah, Dubai Price: Free Three distances to choose from The run caters to everyone from first-timers to experienced runners. According to Race ME, the distances and start times are: 10km Challenge, ages 13 and above, at 6.30am 5km Speed Run, ages 13 and above, at 7.30am 3km Family Fun Run, ages three and above, at 8am The race village and registration open at 5.30am. Prize-giving begins at 8.30am, and the morning wraps up with closing remarks at 11am. All participants will receive a commemorative race T-shirt. Finishers will also get an official medal and a digital certificate. Who can take part The two longer races are open to runners aged 13 and above, so younger children will need to sign up for the 3km Family Fun Run. That race is open to anyone aged three and above, which means parents can run alongside their children. Music and family activities Big Rossi will host this year's event. The race village will have music, family entertainment and community activities, giving runners and supporters a place to gather before and after their races. Part of the Dubai Fitness Challenge The run takes place during this year's  Dubai Fitness Challenge , which runs from October 31 to November 29. The citywide initiative asks residents and visitors to commit to 30 minutes of activity every day for 30 days. The month also includes community favourites such as Dubai Run, Dubai Ride, Dubai Stand Up Paddle and Dubai Yoga, along with Fitness Villages and Fitness Hubs across the city. How the race has changed The Nakheel Palm Run was  first held in 2023 , when 1,790 runners took part, including people of determination. That first edition offered longer distances. Runners aged over 16 could choose between 21.1km, 10km and 5km, while a 1km course was set aside for children aged four to 15. The route took in the Crescent, the semi-circular road that forms the outer edge of Palm Jumeirah, as well as the running track in Al Ittihad Park. This year's programme has no half marathon. Instead of the 1km children's race, there is a 3km family run, and the minimum age for the 5km and 10km races is 13. Getting there There is no parking at the venue. Race ME advises runners to park at Nakheel Mall and take the Palm Monorail, with a round-trip monorail ticket included in each runner's entry. Monorail tickets for spectators can be added during registration. Details on collecting race packs will be emailed to registered participants closer to the event. How to register Registration is open through Premier Online booking platform. Organisers say the race sells out every year, and runners are advised to check category eligibility and race-day arrangements before booking. title: India-China visa update: What changes for Indian passport holders?
author: Lekshmy Pavithran
content: STOCK VISA / Travel / Holiday Indian travellers planning a trip to China will need to follow a revised visa application process from October 26, as Chinese diplomatic missions take over applications previously handled by visa application centres in New Delhi, Mumbai and Kolkata. Under the new system, applicants must complete an online application and receive approval for their documents before submitting their passports and supporting papers to the designated Chinese embassy or consulate. The change affects tourists, business travellers and people seeking consular legalisation of documents. Applicants will also need to check which diplomatic mission handles applications from their state. Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here. What is changing from October 26? According to a notice issued by the Chinese Embassy in India on October 22: Visa application centres will stop accepting new applications: The centres in New Delhi, Mumbai and Kolkata will no longer accept new Chinese visa and consular legalisation applications from October 26. Applications will be handled directly : The Chinese Embassy in New Delhi and the Consulate General in Mumbai will process applications under the revised arrangements. Kolkata applicants will be redirected : Applications from the Kolkata consular jurisdiction will temporarily be handled by the Chinese Embassy in New Delhi. Existing applicants can collect documents : People who have already submitted applications can collect their processed documents from the existing centres until noon on October 30, 2026. Which Chinese mission should you apply to? Your place of residence determines where you should submit your visa application. The revised arrangements divide applications between the Chinese Embassy in New Delhi and the Consulate General in Mumbai. Maharashtra and Karnataka : Apply through the Chinese Consulate General in Mumbai. West Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha and Chhattisgarh : Apply through the Chinese Embassy in New Delhi under the temporary arrangement. All other Indian states and Union Territories : Apply through the Chinese Embassy in New Delhi. For consular legalisation, the relevant jurisdiction is determined by where the documents were issued. Applicants should check the embassy’s latest instructions before proceeding. How to apply for visa under the new system Travellers must complete the online review process before submitting their passports and supporting documents in person. Complete the online application : Fill in the visa application form through the official Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa application portal. Upload supporting documents : Submit the required documents for online review. Wait for approval : Do not proceed to the in-person submission stage until the online review has been approved. Submit your passport and documents : After receiving the approval email, submit your passport, application form and relevant supporting papers to the designated embassy or consulate within 30 days. The online review stage may add to the overall processing time, so travellers should plan ahead. Will Chinese visa applications cost less? The revised system removes visa application centre service fees for eligible online applications submitted after the announced deadline. Online applications submitted after 5pm on October 23, 2026, will not attract the visa application centre service fee, according to the published notice. Service fees already paid for applications submitted before the deadline will not be refunded. Visa fees charged by Chinese authorities are separate and may still apply. Applicants should check the relevant diplomatic mission’s fee schedule and payment instructions before submitting their documents. Chinese visa fees for Indian passport holders The reduced visa fee schedule for Indian passport holders remains in effect until December 31, 2026. The listed fees are: Single-entry visa : ₹2,900 Double-entry visa : ₹4,400 Multiple-entry visa valid for six months : ₹5,900 Multiple-entry visa valid for one year or longer : ₹8,800 Group visa : ₹1,800 per applicant Additional charges apply for faster processing. Express processing, which takes two to three working days, costs an extra ₹1,800, while urgent processing attracts an additional ₹2,700. Payments must follow the relevant mission’s instructions. The published guidance specifies bank-printed demand drafts, with the applicant’s full name, collection slip number and contact number written on the reverse. Visa fees are payable when collecting the passport. Fingerprints: Who is exempt? Under a temporary arrangement running until December 31, 2026, applicants for short-term visas for stays of up to 180 days are generally exempt from fingerprint collection. However, the exemption does not cover every visa category. Applicants for certain long-term study, work and family reunion visas may still need to provide fingerprints in person. Check the requirements for your specific visa before booking an appointment or travelling to submit documents. Photo and document requirements Applicants should carefully check their documents before uploading them to avoid delays. Visa photographs must measure 33mm × 48mm and have a white background. The commonly used Schengen visa photo size of 35mm × 45mm does not meet the stated Chinese visa photo requirement. Tourist visa applicants should check the embassy’s financial-document requirements. The guidance supplied for this process specifies bank statements covering the previous six months, showing a consistent average monthly balance of at least ₹1 lakh, or an eligible deposit certificate for a similar amount held for at least three months. Requirements can vary by visa category, so applicants should consult the latest official checklist. How early should you apply? Standard processing takes about four working days after the application is submitted, but the mandatory online review can add to the overall waiting period. Travellers are advised to begin the process four to six weeks before departure, allowing time to correct document issues and complete the required steps. The revised arrangements apply to travel to mainland China. Hong Kong and Macao have separate entry and visa procedures, so travellers heading to either destination should check the applicable rules separately. Before applying: Check the latest notices from the Chinese Embassy in India or the relevant Chinese consulate for current procedures, jurisdiction, fees and document requirements. title: Mary Kom says Priyanka Chopra's biopic showed 'only 10 per cent' of her struggle, rules out sequel
author: Lakshana N Palat
content: 1.1391386-1839783341 When Mary Kom, starring Priyanka Chopra came out in 2014, it was celebrated as a landmark sports biopic. Twelve years later, Kom feels the film, as substantial as it was, barely scratched the surface. In an interview, after her eviction from the Salman Khan-hosted Bigg Boss 20 on Saturday, the boxing champion was blunt about how her life had been portrayed on screen. “The biopic was not real. I felt some parts of the story were not real. Only 10 percent of my struggle and hard work was shown in it,” she told Indian Express, adding that only her book shows the full picture. Nick Jonas offers glimpse into life with Priyanka Chopra, hugs daughter Malti Marie backstage Kareena Kapoor turns 46: Priyanka Chopra says ‘No one like you’, Soha Ali Khan sends her back to the 80s A celebrated film, a disappointed subject The film was directed by Omung Kumar and produced by Sanjay Leela Bhansali, with Priyanka Chopra in the lead role. It traced Kom’s journey from a village in Manipur to international boxing rings. Along the way it covered her marriage to Onler Kom, her comeback after becoming a mother, and her battles with a sports system that offered women boxers little backing. Chopra’s physical preparation for the part drew wide praise. The film was a commercial hit and won the National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment. It was also unusual for its time: a big-budget Hindi biopic about a female athlete who was still competing. When it released, Kom was a five-time world champion and had won bronze at the 2012 London Olympics. Kom says the real account of her life is in Unbreakable , her autobiography. She has no interest in a follow-up film. Between the movie and the book, she feels her story has already been told, and the public knows it well enough. As for what comes next, she said she hopes for a peaceful and happy future. Asked whether there might be room for love in her life, she said that is a decision she will make on her own terms. Showing the 'real' Mary Kom The same wish to be seen accurately is what drew her to Bigg Boss 20. Kom said she had followed the show for years and wanted to try the format herself. She also wanted viewers to see her as a mother and an everyday person, not only an athlete, and to prove wrong those who assumed she couldn’t cook or manage a home. She maintained that she was herself throughout, saying no one could fake their personality for seven weeks. Her stay in the house had its difficulties. After a strong start, she struggled with the strategic side of the game and mostly kept out of fights, which led to criticism that she wasn’t contributing enough. Kom said the language barrier hurt her: her limited Hindi sometimes made her statements sound wrong, and she felt some contestants exploited that. She described feeling disrespected at times, including during an argument with Uditi and a remark by Mahhi that upset her. In the end, she said, she understood that provoking others was part of the game, and she chose not to play it that way. Her exit from the show also comes as her ex-husband has reportedly filed a defamation suit against her. title: UAE oil spill: Beach clean-up update and advice for residents
author: Devadasan K P
content: Dubai: UAE authorities continue coordinated efforts to contain an oil spill affecting the coastline of Umm Al Quwain, with specialised teams carrying out clean-up operations, environmental assessments, and coastal monitoring to protect the marine environment. The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) said its technical monitoring and environmental assessment system detected marine pollution caused by an oil spill from a tanker. The incident has affected Umm Al Quwain’s beaches, while the ministry confirmed that unusual odours reported by residents in Sharjah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain pose no health risks. The response involves coordination between federal and local authorities, with teams working to contain the pollution, cordon off affected areas and carry out clean-up and remediation operations. Coordinated response to protect the coastline Umm Al Quwain has temporarily closed its beaches and coastal areas as a precaution. At the same time, technical teams assess the extent of the pollution and determine the measures needed to protect public safety and marine habitats.
