The precautionary measures aim to safeguard residents and visitors while assessments and containment operations continue. Umm Al Quwain Municipality has also been conducting field operations to monitor affected locations, support clean-up work and limit the impact on coastal ecosystems. Monitoring and public safety remain priorities The ministry has urged fishermen and other sea users to follow official instructions and avoid fishing in affected areas. Residents and visitors have also been advised to stay away from closed beaches and coastal areas until authorities announce that they can reopen. The UAE’s response includes ongoing coastal surveys and environmental assessments to establish the extent of the pollution and guide further action. Authorities have urged the public to follow official channels for updates and avoid circulating unverified information. What residents need to know The ministry has confirmed that the odours reported in Sharjah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain pose no health risks. However, the temporary beach closures remain in place as a precaution while environmental assessments and clean-up operations continue. No reopening dates have been confirmed for the affected beaches. Authorities continue to focus on containing the pollution, limiting its environmental impact and protecting the UAE’s coastline and marine environment. The latest reports available on October 27 indicate that satellite imagery showed the oil slick widening offshore on October 24, underscoring the importance of continued containment and monitoring. title: Shah Rukh Khan channels his inner deadly romantic in new ‘King’ poster, complete with guns and roses
author: Manjusha Radhakrishnan
content: Dubai: Who says romance is dead? Certainly not Shah Rukh Khan, who seems determined to prove that you can be a gun-toting assassin and a hopeless romantic at the same time. The Bollywood superstar unveiled a striking new poster from his much-anticipated action thriller King on Tuesday, October 27, giving fans another glimpse of his rugged, dangerous avatar. Dressed in a fitted leather trench coat, plunging black shirt, with a gun in his hand and a thorny rose stem clenched between his teeth, Khan strides towards the camera against a fiery backdrop. Think guns, roses and a generous helping of Bollywood swagger. The accompanying caption only adds to the intrigue. “Aaj phir yaad aaya... Qaatil nahi… Aashiq hoon…” (Today I remembered again… I'm not a killer, I'm a lover), reads the post. It's a cheeky reminder that even when Khan is playing a potentially lethal character, his romantic hero persona is never too far away. Directed by Siddharth Anand, King marks the filmmaker's reunion with Khan following their 2023 blockbuster Pathaan , which cemented the actor's spectacular return to action cinema. The film also stars his daughter Suhana Khan, alongside Deepika Padukone and Abhishek Bachchan in pivotal roles. Jaideep Ahlawat, Abhay Verma and Arshad Warsi round out the ensemble. Based on a story by Sujoy Ghosh, who was initially attached to direct, the screenplay has been written by Anand, Ghosh, Suresh Nair and Sagar Pandya, with dialogues by Abbas Tyrewala. Produced by Red Chillies Entertainment and Marflix Pictures, King has already generated considerable buzz through its teaser and dialogue promo. And judging by this latest poster, Khan isn't abandoning his romantic roots. He's simply giving them a dangerous makeover. title: Philippines e-Visa in Dubai: Everything you need to know
author: Tricia Gajitos
content: philippine consulate Dubai: Foreign nationals living in the UAE who need a visa to visit the Philippines can now apply through a new electronic visa (e-Visa) service launched by the Philippine Consulate General in Dubai, making it easier to plan holidays, business trips, and other short visits. The consulate has begun issuing e-Visas on October 26, following a two-week beta-testing period. The service covers eligible applications for tourism, business, conferences, medical treatment, and other short-term visits, removing the need for applicants to appear in person as part of the standard application process. Ambrosio Brian Enciso III, consul general of the Philippines in Dubai and the Northern Emirates, has noted that the launch was part of the Philippine government’s wider efforts to modernise public services. Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here. “We hope that the system will make travel to the Philippines faster and more accessible, especially for those who want to travel to the Philippines purely for tourism,” remarked Enciso during a press briefing at the consulate on October 26. The Philippine e-Visa system was soft-launched by the Department of Foreign Affairs in August 2023 and has since expanded to selected diplomatic missions worldwide. The Philippine Embassy in Abu Dhabi has started issuing e-Visas in March last year, with Dubai now joining the programme. Philippine consul general Ambrosio Brian Enciso III Personal appearance no longer required The new service has been intended to make the Philippines more accessible to eligible foreign nationals living in the UAE, particularly those planning short holidays. The Philippines requires citizens of 37 countries to obtain an entry visa before travelling. At the Dubai consulate, applicants commonly include nationals of Bangladesh, India, Iran, Iraq, Egypt, Lebanon, Palestine, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Sudan, Syria, Ukraine, and Yemen. “The requirements are the same but we took one important thing out which is the personal appearance, which was a hindrance to a lot of people,” shared Enciso. He has bared that Dubai’s international population presented an opportunity to attract more visitors to the Philippines, particularly as social media has helped bring the destination to the attention of younger travellers. “If you want to see the Philippines for a few days, this is a very good option. And options are important.” Visa validity, fees, and processing times The online system covers eligible 9(a) temporary visitor visas for tourism, business, conferences, medical treatment, and other short-term purposes. The e-Visa is valid for seven up to 59 days, depending on the applicant’s nationality and travel requirements. Visas issued through the official electronic platform are non-extendable and non-convertible. A single-entry visa costs Dh260 and generally takes seven to 12 working days to process. A six-month multiple-entry visa costs Dh420, while a one-year multiple-entry visa costs Dh580. Processing for multiple-entry visas takes between 15 and 40 working days. The approval for multiple-entry visas still comes from Manila, and processing times depend on the relevant authorities. The consulate will continue issuing conventional sticker visas alongside the e-Visa system. Travellers who need a visa category or arrangement not covered by the electronic service may still need to use the existing application process. Documents and requirements remain unchanged Although applications can now be submitted online, the consulate has retained the existing documentation requirements. Applicants must provide a recent identification photograph, a passport valid for more than one year, and a valid UAE residence visa. An original no-objection certificate bearing a wet stamp is also required. Tourist applicants must submit three months of bank statements with a wet or digital stamp, showing a maintained balance of more than Dh5,000 each month. A tentative return flight booking and hotel reservation are required. Alternatively, applicants may provide a letter from a legal Filipino relative, together with the relative’s identification and signature. Business applicants must submit a notarised invitation letter from the Philippines and identification bearing the relevant signature. Where applicable, proof of Filipino family ties, such as a marriage or birth certificate and the relative’s identification, must also be provided. Applicants must include details of previous Philippine visas, where applicable, and their travel history covering the past two years. The consulate has advised applicants to ensure that their documents are complete and accurate before submission, as the introduction of the online platform does not remove the existing assessment process. Applications will still be reviewed by officials Enciso has stressed that the e-Visa system would not result in automatic approvals. “The visa processing system will rely still on the visa processing that we have done, the system in place is still the same. We will evaluate the documents as they are submitted to us,” stated Enciso. Answering a question from Gulf News about the security of personal information submitted through the online platform, the consul general has mentioned that it is protected by security protocols similar to those used for passport applications. On the possibility of applicants providing false information, Enciso has emphasised that there was an expectation that applicants would not misrepresent themselves. He has warned that misrepresentation could lead to removal or blacklisting. Consul Paola Belle Ebora and consul general Ambrosio Brian Enciso III answering questions from the media An e-Visa does not guarantee entry Holding a Philippine visa does not automatically guarantee admission into the country. “The principle involved here is the possession of a Philippine entry visa does not guarantee entry into the country,” explained Enciso. Consul Paola Belle Ebora has pointed out that the Bureau of Immigration is responsible for safeguarding the country’s borders. Consul Paola Belle Ebora “Maybe a concern would be what if this person should not be entering the Philippines? In that matter, it’s the Bureau of Immigration that safeguards our borders,” said Ebora. Enciso has hoped that future developments would allow for more systems to capture biometric information and improve integration with the systems of other countries. e-Travel registration remains mandatory Travellers heading to the Philippines must also complete registration through the Philippine e-Travel system within 72 hours before arrival. Registration is free of charge and is separate from the visa application. Travellers should complete the process before departure to help avoid delays or issues during border checks. The e-Visa simplifies the visa application process but does not replace other travel requirements. Visa-free entry for Indian and Chinese nationals Indian nationals have been eligible for visa-free entry to the Philippines for tourism or business for up to 14 days since June 2025. The stay is non-extendable and non-convertible. Indian nationals travelling for longer stays, study, employment, or transit must still obtain the appropriate visa before travelling. On the other hand, Chinese nationals have also been eligible for visa-free entry for tourism or business for up to 14 days since January this year. The stay is non-extendable and non-convertible, and entry under this arrangement is restricted to Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Manila and Mactan-Cebu International Airport in Cebu. Travellers should confirm the requirements applicable to their nationality and purpose of travel before booking flights. The launch of the e-Visa service gives eligible UAE residents a more convenient way to apply for Philippine visas, while keeping the existing documentation requirements, application assessments, and immigration safeguards in place. title: Graeme McDowell becomes latest major winner to quit Liv Golf
author: Robert Ilsley
content: Dubai: Northern Ireland's Graeme McDowell has become the latest major champion to announce his exit from LIV Golf. The 2010 US Open champion confirmed on Monday that he had "decided not to pursue" LIV 2.0, the revamped version of the breakaway circuit scheduled to launch in 2027. McDowell follows major winners Jon Rahm and Louis Oosthuizen in confirming their departures. His fellow Northern Irishman Tom McKibbin also announced last week that he would leave LIV to return to the DP World Tour. England's Tyrrell Hatton and Ian Poulter have also departed the league. LIV Golf's future was thrown into uncertainty in April when Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its financial support after investing more than $5 billion (£3.8bn). The league subsequently filed for bankruptcy protection in the United States last month. The circuit has since secured the possibility of $300 million (£224m) in financing from BC Partners Credit as it attempts to push ahead with LIV 2.0, although only a small number of players have committed to the new project so far. Former world number four McDowell joined LIV when the Saudi-backed competition launched in 2022, attracted by its lucrative financial backing. The 11-time DP World Tour winner's best result on the circuit was a tie for second at the Virginia event in June 2025. "I've decided not to pursue LIV 2.0," said McDowell, a four-time Ryder Cup player. "I'm grateful for the opportunity I've had over the last four years and want to thank everyone who has been part of that journey. "I look forward to the next chapter in my career." title: Kylian Mbappe loses two major sponsors over 'dictator' meme controversy
author: Abdul Bari Khan
content: Dubai: Kylian Mbappe has lost commercial partnerships with two major Chinese brands after a video circulated online in which the France captain appeared to joke about former Chinese leader Mao Zedong. Sports drinks maker Dongpeng and dairy giant Mengniu announced on October 27 that they were ending their collaborations with the Real Madrid forward, citing remarks they said offended Chinese people. “Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments,” Dongpeng said in a statement, confirming the immediate termination of its partnership with the 27-year-old. Mengniu issued a similar statement, saying it would also end its cooperation with Mbappe and would not tolerate words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people. The controversy followed the circulation of a video in which Mbappe reportedly described an internet meme featuring his face superimposed on that of “some guy – I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. The remark appeared to refer to Mao, who led China for decades and died in 1976. Bottles of Dongpeng Beverage Group's "Bushuila" electrolyte drink featuring French football star Kylian Mbappe on the packaging are displayed at a convenience store in Beijing on October 27, 2026. The authenticity of the video could not immediately be verified according to AFP Fact Check. The episode has triggered strong reactions on Chinese social media, with Dongpeng’s decision becoming a trending topic on Weibo. Some users called for the company to remove Mbappe’s image from its products. Mbappe had previously addressed memes portraying him as a historical dictator, telling French newspaper L’Equipe in September that comparisons with figures responsible for mass suffering were not funny. The French star had enjoyed considerable popularity in China, where fans nicknamed him “guigui”, meaning turtle, because of a Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles meme. The dictator memes are another category with which fans troll Mbappe, citing his alleged strong demands within the club as a connection. The controversy comes a day after Mbappe missed out to England striker Harry Kane in the Ballon d’Or race, losing the prestigious individual award to the Bayern Munich forward.

title: Beyond Property: Dubai forum to explore where UAE wealth is heading in 2027
author: A Gulf News Report
content: For years, property has been the default route to wealth for many UAE residents. A growing number of investors are now weighing what else their money could do . US and global equities, fixed income, technology and alternative assets are drawing more attention from professionals, entrepreneurs and investors who want to diversify and build resilience, even as real estate remains a cornerstone of wealth in the country. The phone in the pocket is a big part of that story. More than 60 per cent of UAE consumers actively use digital financial platforms, and 70 per cent to 75 per cent of investors now prefer mobile-first, digital investment solutions, according to 2026 figures published by trading platform Dealing. Appetite is holding up too. In eToro’s UAE Retail Investor Beat survey of 1,000 residents, conducted in August 2026, 71 per cent of retail investors said they plan to invest more over the next 12 months. That shift is the focus of Beyond Property: Where to Invest and Grow Your Wealth in 2027 , presented by Gulf News in association with CUSP Wealth . The event takes place from 10am to 1pm on October 29 at the Conference Hall, Gulf News, DIP 2, Dubai. The forum is aimed at digitally savvy UAE residents who are already investing or are ready to take their next step. Speakers will look at where investors are putting their money, why they are diversifying and what to weigh when assessing different opportunities. Topics include US and global equities, Shariah-compliant and conventional options, fixed income, technology and alternative assets, as well as diversification, risk, liquidity, valuations and market volatility. “The UAE is entering a new chapter of wealth building. Looking to 2027 and beyond, I believe we’ll see more investors diversifying beyond property into global markets, more demand for Shariah-compliant investments, and AI becoming part of everyday investing, with human guidance still central to big decisions,” said Ramesh Murthy, Senior Executive Officer, CUSP Wealth. “The biggest shift is that serious investing is becoming accessible to everyone. I hope attendees leave with a clearer picture of where wealth is heading, and the confidence to plan for it themselves.” The event opens with a keynote on the outlook for 2027, followed by a panel on where the next investment opportunity lies, covering the opportunities and risks across asset classes and the role of diversification in long-term wealth strategies. A spotlight session will turn to practical steps for building a portfolio in 2027, including how to set goals, time horizons and risk appetite. A presentation will then look at how technology and wider market access are changing the way people build and manage wealth. The morning closes with a live audience Q&A, followed by lunch and networking.

title: Diwali 2026 guide in Dubai: Where to shop, what to buy and how to not overspend
author: Lakshana N Palat
content: Diwali lands on Sunday 8 November this year. That means a weekend Lakshmi Puja and about ten days to sort your gold, your glitter and your gulab jamun. In the UAE, Diwali starts long before the first diya is lit. Bur Dubai’s lanes fill with the sights of lehenges, the Gold Souk queues stretch past sunset on Dhanteras, and Karama’s sweet shops run their kitchens around the clock. So, regardless, of whether you’re shopping for the in-laws, the office or yourself, here is where to go, what to buy and what to simply order from the sofa. The dates that run the show Dhanteras, Friday, November 6, the big gold-buying day. The puja window in Dubai is roughly 6.06pm to 8.03pm. Diwali (Lakshmi Puja), Sunday November 8, diyas lit, sweets out, best outfit on. Govardhan Puja, Monday November 9 Bhai Dooj, Tuesday November 10: a day earlier than India this year, so sibling gifts are due sooner. Diwali at Global Village: 600-drone show, first baithak and a five-day mela Diwali 2026 in the UAE: Festivals, temples and where to celebrate Diwali isn’t a UAE public holiday. With Lakshmi Puja on a Sunday, though, nobody needs a fake dentist appointment this year. Meena Bazaar: For the outfit, the lights and the vibe Bur Dubai’s 'Little India' runs mostly along one lane between Al Fahidi Street and Khalid Bin Al Waleed Road. It has been the community’s shopping hub since the 1970s, and in Diwali week it’s just a lot of fun to walk through. The outfit: lehengas, salwar suits, kurtis, sherwanis, kurta pyjamas and tiny party-wear for kids. Fabric and a tailor: pick a length, get measured, then pray. Tailors are swamped, so go this week, not next. Decor: clay diyas, string lights, torans and rangoli colours, all cheaper than at the mall. A snack break: Kailash Parbat and Royal Sweets are right there for chaat and mithai. The souks: Gold, spice and everything nice Deira Gold Souk is the Dhanteras main event. Gold prices have been worth watching this year, so check the day’s rate before you go. If a big set is off the cards, a small coin or a light 18K or 22K piece keeps the tradition alive without flattening your wallet. Check the hallmark, and ask for the making charge separately. Compare the day’s per-gram rate before you fall for a “free gift”. If you’re going on November 6, expect evening queues around the puja window. Deira Spice Souk is a short walk away, and it’s where gift baskets get built: dry fruits, saffron, cardamom and nuts by the scoop. You pay about half the price of a ready-made hamper and get twice the bragging rights. Bur Dubai Souk is across the Creek by abra. It has lamps, fabrics and festive bits if Meena Bazaar runs out of diyas (it won’t). Mithai: Karama is your sugar district Sweet shop sales can increase at Diwali, and premium boxes can run to Dh400 a kilo. Pre-order by phone to skip the queue. Bikanervala (Karama, Al Barsha and more): kaju katli, Mysore pak, gift boxes Puranmal (Karama): khajur barfi, Karachi halwa Shree Gangour Sweets (Oud Metha / Karama): kesariya jalebi, stuffed gulab jamun Chappan Bhog (Karama): Rasgulla, ras malai Royal Sweets (Meena Bazaar): grab-and-go boxes while you shop Some things are worth the souk trip. Fairy lights are not, so order these online: Lights in bulk: LED string lights, curtain lights and battery tea-lights, which are safer with kids and curtains. Rangoli kits: stencils and colour packs, so your doorstep design doesn’t depend on your art skills. Puja basics: brass thalis, incense, kalash sets and ready-made puja kits. Corporate gifting: dry-fruit hampers and gift boxes delivered straight to the office. Gift ideas, anyone? This one is for the person who already has three boxes of kaju katli. The Belgian chocolatier Godiva has wrapped Diwali in fuchsia, teal and gold, with stars, flowers and glowing diyas on every box. When: 26 October to 9 November Where: GODIVA boutiques across the UAE Diwali Chocolate Chest Box, Dh999: the showpiece, with 70 pralines and truffles plus 144 Napolitains Ultimate Gift Box (40 pcs), Dh429: the greatest hits, with pralines, ganaches, truffles, biscuits and carrés Royal Box (45 pcs), Dh415: 15 pralines and 30 carrés, in brown, navy or red Gold Box (24 pcs), Dh249: the classic, with pralines, ganaches and truffles in milk, dark and white Napolitain Gift Box (88 pcs), Dh199: individually wrapped milk, hazelnut milk and dark Napolitain Gift Box (48 pcs), Dh129: same, smaller Below Dh,1000 gifts that you can consider Best Speaker: JBL Flip 6 Portable Speaker It’s small but loud, with bold JBL Pro Sound and deep bass. It’s IP67 waterproof and lasts 12 hours on a charge via USB-C, so it can play from diya-lighting to dance floor. Best Lighting: Philips Hue Indoor 6-Foot Smart LED Light Strip It glows in festive colours or calm single shades, controlled by app or voice (Alexa, Google Assistant, Apple HomeKit). It’s instant Diwali ambiance with no ladder required. Best Gift Basket: Spa Luxetique Lavender Spa Gift Basket It packs 15 pampering goodies, including soaps, shampoo bars, scrubs and a dry hair cap. Self-care, but make it festive. Best for Hosts: LILKUISYN 4pc Acacia Resin Wood Coaster Set These are acacia wood coasters with a pop of blue resin, and the base doubles as a napkin holder. They’re pretty, practical and ready for a house full of chai cups. Best for the table: French Rose Series Dinnerware Set It has delicate florals and a timeless finish, and it’s sturdy enough for every festive feast to come. It’s a gift for the loved one who notices the plates before the food. How to Diwali without draining the bank Make a list, and check it twice. Write down who’s getting what before you set foot in Meena Bazaar. Wandering in without a plan is how you come home with three lehengas and no diyas. Go small on gold. Tradition says buy gold on Dhanteras. It doesn’t say buy a necklace. A small coin or a light 18K piece counts, and your bank balance will thank you on Monday. Build your own hamper. A scoop of dry fruits from the Spice Souk, a box of mithai and a ribbon cost far less than a ready-made basket. You also get to call it “handpicked.” Buy the boring stuff online. Fairy lights, rangoli kits and tea-lights don’t need a trip across town. Order them early from Amazon.ae and save the petrol and the parking rage. Split the big gifts. Pool with siblings for the parents’ present. One great gift beats four average ones, and nobody has to explain the matching scented candles. Skip the last-minute panic. Prices, queues and stress all peak in the final 48 hours. Shop this week and you’ll pay less and keep your sanity. Set a sweets budget, then add 10%. Let’s be honest, you’re going to buy one more box of kaju katli. Plan for it. That’s the list. Your outfit is at the tailor, your sweets are pre-ordered and your fairy lights are already tangled in a box somewhere. All that’s left is to light the diyas, dodge the “so when are you getting married?” questions, and eat one more laddoo than you planned. Happy Diwali! title: Paws on the trail: How UAE residents are hiking with their dogs this winter
author: Areeba Hashmi
content: Dubai: For Vishaal S Shah, the start of the cooler months means getting back on the trails with his two dogs, Simba and Kiko. "Every year we count down to the cooler season because of what it brings, adventures in the mountains and wadis with the two of them," he said. With hiking season back in the UAE, residents are lacing up their boots, packing extra water and heading for the trails with their dogs. For many of them, it has changed far more than their weekend plans. Vishaal S Shah with Simba and Kiko More than a walk around the block Yvonne, founder of Doggie Adventures UAE and co-founder of dog hiking group Leash Explorer UAE, believes dogs genuinely need to get outdoors. "Getting out of the house with your dog for outdoor adventures is not just a luxury outing for your dog, it's a necessity for their health," she said. "A walk in your neighbourhood with your dog is nice, but does your dog get enough mental enrichment from those walks?" On the trails, she said, dogs take in a mix of new experiences. "New smells, different kinds of grounds under their paws, meeting other dogs and humans. We basically focus on what makes dogs thrive and happy while spending quality time with our furry best friends and enjoying the beautiful nature you have in this country." Yvonne, founder of Doggie Adventures UAE and co-founder of dog hiking group Leash Explorer UAE 'We learned it the hard way' Ukrainian expat Veronika Konkovska has lived in the UAE for 11 years. She hiked often before she started bringing along her Japanese Spitz, Sugar, who is now six and a half and began hiking at one and a half. "Hiking with a pet requires more preparation and actually basic awareness, which I was lacking when we started," she said. At first, Veronika took Sugar on hikes with friends who didn't have dogs. Sugar kept stopping to sniff around, and Veronika kept falling behind the group. Sugar would also eat small stones, drink from ponds and even pick up thorns, so each hike was followed by difficult recovery days. "We needed more breaks, structure and confidence for both of us," she said. "We learned it the hard way." Veronika Konkovska with her Japanese Spitz, Sugar. Things changed when they followed a neighbour in Jumeirah Lake Towers and her two rescue dogs to a beginners' group hike. "It helped a lot, introducing structure, bringing awareness and building our confidence, adding on to our bond and providing great ground for socialisation," Veronika said. Sugar used to bark a lot at goats and camels on the trail. After a group hike to the Hidden Oasis in Ras Al Khaimah two years ago, the organisers recommended training to help her around wild animals, and the pair have kept at it ever since. Sugar on a hike 'My dogs pulled me out of that' Vishaal has two dogs: Simba, a five-year-old cream toy poodle, and Kiko, a three-year-old cockapoo. The Kenyan expat has lived in the UAE for two decades. "I have lived in the UAE for 20 years, but I have seen more of this country in the last five than in all the years before, and that is entirely because of my dogs," he said. The dogs changed more than his weekends. "We all get so busy with daily life, chasing work, deadlines and things we think we need. My dogs pulled me out of that. They pushed me to change my lifestyle. Health became a priority, routine became non-negotiable, and early mornings stopped being a struggle because they are waiting at the door, ready to go." "Out on a trail with them, everything else falls away. Watching them discover a new place, checking back on me, looking out for each other, you realise the connection is completely real." Before he joined a group, he said, hiking with dogs felt like guesswork. He wasn't sure which trails allowed dogs, how hot the rocks got, how much water to carry or what to do if something went wrong. Hiking with others has also brought new friendships. Vishaal S Shah with Simba and Kiko "Along the way we have met people from so many cultures and nationalities, people our paths might never have crossed otherwise, and they have become friends, almost a second family, all brought together by our dogs," he said. "Because in the end, it is not where you walk, it is who you walk with." A vet's view Sarah Ramsey, a British veterinary surgeon who lives in Dubai, hikes with Rocket, a two-year-old Maltese and American Cocker Spaniel cross. "He's a little dog with a big personality and absolutely loves getting outdoors and exploring," she said. "It's a lovely way to escape the city, get some exercise and spend quality time together." She said the heat is the biggest challenge, and finding suitable dog-friendly routes can be tricky, particularly with a smaller dog. Rocket at the summit "As a veterinary surgeon and dog owner, my biggest advice is to plan your hikes around your dog's abilities rather than your own. Don't underestimate little dogs, though. They can be surprisingly adventurous," she said. "Always carry plenty of water, take regular breaks, watch for signs of overheating and check their paws, especially on rocky terrain." "I love seeing him explore, sniff everything and have his own little adventures. He might be small, but he's a brilliant hiking companion." Getting your dog ready for the season After the long summer break, Yvonne said, dogs need time to build up again. "After a long summer break, we need to not only dust off our own hiking boots but also toughen the paw pads of our doggies to avoid any split paws during the hike," she said. "Walking in your neighbourhood is not the same as walking a rocky path on the mountains. We can also not expect our dogs to do a 10km hike all of a sudden, so we need to build up their endurance a bit." She also stresses packing enough water. "Keep in mind that you will drink around half a litre per hour and your dog a quarter of a litre per hour," she said. Timing meals matters too. Yvonne advises leaving enough time between a meal and a hike to avoid bloat, a condition in which a dog's stomach can twist. Vishaal's checklist is similar. "Go early, carry plenty of water for your dog, check paws at every break, and choose routes that suit your dog's size and fitness," he said. Rocket and Nata hiking Heading out on your own Not everyone wants to join a group. For those exploring independently, Yvonne recommends sticking to official dog-friendly hiking trails and using a long leash. "Have your dog on a long leash so he or she has the freedom to explore but can't run away in case a natural instinct kicks in by wanting to chase wildlife, and have a GPS tracker on your dog just in case," she said. Staying on the path matters too. Hussain Darwish, who has been hiking with dogs in the UAE for more than 15 years,  told Gulf News last year  that pets should be kept on marked trails and that owners should always clean up after their dogs. Vishaal's main advice is simple. "Most of all, just start. Your dog has been waiting for this adventure longer than you have." title: Netanyahu's future on the line as Israel votes today: What you need to know
author: Jay Hilotin
content: FILE - People walk past a Likud party campaign billboard featuring Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu alongside opposition party leaders and bearing the Hebrew slogan "Right or Palestine," ahead of Israel's general election, in Beni Brak, Israel, Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026. (AP Photo/Oded Balilty, File) Israelis vote on Tuesday (Oct. 27, 2026), from 7am.  About 7.3 million people are eligible to cast their ballots to pick the next government. The vote is widely seen as a verdict on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. It's a pivotal election: the first chance of the Israeli electorate to hold leaders accountable for the security failures around the October 7, 2023 attacks , to decide who leads the state through its regional conflicts, and to weigh in on the contentious issue of military service. Arab capitals, both those that normalised ties with Israel and those that haven’t, are treating the vote as a critical decision point. Here's a look at the basics and major parties/candidates in Israel's election Tuesday (Oct. 27, 2026). Get it: Fast, verified news for FREE ... download the Gulf News app — simply click here The basics Type of government: Israel is a parliamentary democracy.  Knesset : Voters elect the 120-seat Knesset (the unicameral national legislature/parliament) of the State of Israel) located in Jerusalem.  The prime minister: The PM is head of government, and is the person who can build a majority coalition.  The president: Currently Isaac Herzog, is head of state and largely ceremonial but plays a key role in choosing who tries to form a government. Israel to give verdict on Netanyahu in pivotal election. A deeply divided Israel will head to the polls on Tuesday for the first time since Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack, with voters delivering their verdict on veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the country's… pic.twitter.com/BMG9C7Gmtc — AFP News Agency (@AFP) October 27, 2026 When it was founded: Israel declared independence on May 14, 1948. Basic Laws: Israel has no single written Constitution. It operates under a flexible constitutional framework, similar to countries like the UK and New Zealand. Its system relies on a collection of core constitutional statutes known as the Basic Laws ( Chukei Yesod ), alongside judicial precedence and fundamental legal principles. Voters wait in a queue to cast their ballots at a polling station in Jerusalem on October 27, 2026, on the day of Israel's legislative election. How often does Israel vote? The Knesset normally serves a four-year term , but early elections are common when coalitions collapse.  Between 2019 and 2022, Israel held five elections because parties repeatedly failed to form stable governments.  This Knesset formally dissolved on July 17, 2026. Total number of registered voters eligible to vote in the Israeli elections on Tuesday (Oct. 27, 2026) 7.3 million Thirty-six (36) parties are running, but most won’t clear the 3.25% threshold.  Election Day Timeline 7 am (Jerusalem time): Most polling stations open nationwide (5:00am GMT | 9am UAE) 8 am: Special polling stations open in smaller communities, hospitals, prisons and care homes. Through the day: Turnout figures come out at regular intervals, and leaders cast their ballots. 8 pm: Special polling stations close. 10 pm: Main polling stations close, and anyone already in line can still vote.  Exit polls: TV networks release exit polls, which are projections and can differ significantly from actual results. Overnight: Votes are counted and preliminary results emerge.  Nov. 4, 2026: Official results are due by November 4, and the deadline for appeals is November 18. A woman waits before casting her ballot to vote at a polling station in the Arab-Israeli town of Umm al-Fahm on October 27, 2026, on the day of Israel's legislative election. Arab Members in the Knesset In the 25th Knesset, 13 Arab members currently serve in the 120-seat parliament. Arab residents and citizens in Israel are estimated at 2.17 million , making up about 21.7% of the country's total population, Jewish Virtual Library data show. The Arab representation includes members of Muslim, Christian, and Druze communities. These members represent both independent, Arab-majority political factions and broader cross-party lists: Ra'am (United Arab List): 5 seats (led by Mansour Abbas ) Hadash–Ta'al: 5 seats (led by Ayman Odeh and Ahmad Tibi) Zionist / Mainstream Parties: 3 seats (representing Likud, Yesh Atid, and Yisrael Beiteinu) Israel's outgoing government (clockwise from top left): Benjamin Netanyahu (Prime Minister and Likud leader), Bezalel Smotrich (Finance Minister and Religious Zionism leader), Itamar Ben-Gvir (National Security Minister and Otzma Yehudit leader), Avigdor Liberman (Leader of Yisrael Beiteinu), Yitzhak Goldknopf (Leader of United Torah Judaism, UTJ), and Yair Lapid (Leader of the opposition Yesh Atid Party). The Role of Israeli Arabs in the Knesset Historically, Arab political parties operated primarily in the political opposition, acting as advocates for Arab minority rights rather than governing partners. However, their role has evolved substantially. For example, Arab Members of the Knesset (MKs) advocate for municipal funding, infrastructure improvements, civil rights, combating organised crime in Arab towns, and ending housing discrimination. They also serve as a vocal platform opposing policies toward Palestinians in the occupied territories. Mansour Abbas, head of Israel's conservative Islamic Raam party, meets his supporters during a campaign rally in the Arab-Israeli village of Abu Gosh on October 21, 2026. Who's running this time Likud (Benjamin Netanyahu): The main right-wing party. Netanyahu, 77, is seeking a seventh term. Yashar (Gadi Eisenkot): A centrist party and Netanyahu’s main challenger. Eisenkot is a former military chief of staff who quit the war cabinet in June 2024. Together/B’Yachad (Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid): A joint list of two former prime ministers, generally polling third. Far-right and religious allies of Netanyahu: Otzma Yehudit (Itamar Ben-Gvir), Religious Zionism (Bezalel Smotrich), and the ultra-Orthodox Shas and United Torah Judaism. Others: The Democrats, Yisrael Beytenu, and the Arab-led parties, including the Joint List and Ra’am. What the polls show so far A 10-poll average has Likud and Yashar tied at 22 seats, with Together at 13.  Netanyahu’s bloc polls at 49 to 55 seats, short of the 61 needed. The opposition bloc sits at 54 to 56, and Eisenkot led Likud in eight of nine final polls.  Polling is banned from Friday until election day. Why it matters Accountability : Opposition voters rank the October 7 failure first at 28%, per CNN. Netanyahu rejects responsibility and points to gains against Iran’s proxies. The draft : Opposition parties are campaigning on getting ultra-Orthodox Jews to serve, which Netanyahu has resisted to keep his religious allies. Per Channel 12, voters rank the economy first at 21%, then the draft at 17%, October 7 at 14% and the Iran war at 10%. War and diplomacy : Netanyahu argues Israel’s campaigns in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran aren’t finished. Netanyahu’s legal troubles : He is on trial for corruption, which he denies, has asked President Herzog for a pardon, and faces an ICC warrant over Gaza. Arab turnout : It was 53.2% in 2022, versus 70.6% overall. Higher turnout would likely add seats to parties that won’t sit with Netanyahu.  The Palestinian statehood : The issue looms little in the campaign, since most Jewish-majority parties, including the leading challengers, reject it. What's next Not final tonight: Election results won’t automatically determine the next prime minister, and coalition talks can take weeks or months. Herzog’s role: Once results are confirmed, he will task a member of parliament, usually the leader seen as best able to win parliamentary support, with forming a government.  Minority government: A minority government is possible with enough backing. Kingmakers: Without a majority, Eisenkot would need the Haredi or Arab parties, and neither is an easy fit. Stalemate risk: If no coalition can form a majority, Israel could face another election, with Netanyahu leading a caretaker government in the meantime. NPR notes that would leave him in power with full authority, including on decisions like going to war. title: Virat Kohli shares heartfelt message to Harry Kane on Ballon d'Or win
author: Abdul Bari Khan
content: Dubai: Virat Kohli has sent a heartfelt message to Harry Kane after the England captain won the 2026 Ballon d’Or, celebrating the Bayern Munich striker’s achievement and the hard work behind his success. Kohli took to social media to congratulate his friend, praising the 33-year-old for his resilience and conduct throughout his career. “Harry my friend, you deserve every bit of this award for your resilience, hard work and honesty with which you’ve carried yourself through all these years playing football at the top,” Kohli wrote on X. “Really happy for you. God bless you and your family. They must all be very proud of you as you would be of your own journey. My best wishes always. Congratulations,” he added. The message reflects the bond between two of the biggest names in their respective sports, who have exchanged public praise over the years. England and Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane kisses the trophy on stage after receiving the Ballon d'Or award for the best male footballer during the 2026 Ballon d'Or France Football award ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London on October 26, 2026. Their connection dates to 2016, when Kane praised Kohli after the Indian batter’s match-winning innings against Australia in the T20 World Cup. Kohli scored an unbeaten 82 off 51 balls in India’s quarter-final victory, prompting Kane to hail his performance on social media. The pair eventually met at Lord’s in London in May 2019, sharing photographs and exchanging messages of mutual respect. Kane has now added football’s most prestigious individual honour to his achievements after a prolific 2025-26 campaign. He scored 73 goals for club and country, helping Bayern Munich retain the Bundesliga title as part of a domestic treble. The England striker finished ahead of Kylian Mbappe and Barcelona teenager Lamine Yamal to claim the award, becoming the first Englishman to win the men’s Ballon d’Or since Michael Owen in 2001.

title: The numbers behind Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or winning season
author: Robert Ilsley
content: Dubai: Harry Kane earnt football’s most illustrious individual prize on Monday night when he was awarded the 2026 Ballon d’Or. The England captain’s extraordinary numbers for Bayern Munich and his country saw him beat Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to the award. The 33-year-old finished the 2025/26 campaign with 73 goals in 65 appearances for club and country, helping the striker become the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001. Only Lionel Messi scored more goals in a Ballon d’Or-winning season than Harry Kane. The numbers behind his award-winning season: 61 goals for Bayern Munich Kane scored 61 goals in all competitions for Bayern, 19 more than any other player at a club in Europe’s top five leagues. It was the most prolific campaign of his club career, surpassing his previous best of 44 goals during his debut season in Germany in 2023/24. Even removing his 17 penalty goals, Kane’s tally of 44 non-penalty goals was higher than the total scored by any other player in Europe’s top five leagues. 36 Bundesliga goals Kane finished as the Bundesliga’s leading scorer for the third consecutive season, becoming only the second player in the competition’s history to win the Golden Boot in three successive campaigns, after Robert Lewandowski. The Englishman has scored 102 Bundesliga goals for Bayern Munich in 101 games. His 36 goals were the third-highest individual tally in a Bundesliga season, behind Lewandowski’s record of 41 in 2020/21 and Gerd Muller’s 40 in 1971/72. 14 Champions League goals Kane also delivered on European football’s biggest club stage, scoring 14 goals in the Champions League as Bayern reached the semi-finals. It was his highest return in a single Champions League campaign and left him just one goal behind Kylian Mbappe in the competition’s scoring charts. He also recorded five hat-tricks across all competitions for Bayern, more than any other player at a club in Europe’s top five leagues. 12 goals for England Kane’s international contribution further strengthened his Ballon d’Or credentials, with 12 goals for England during the award’s assessment period. Harry Kane is England’s all-time leading World Cup goalscorer, ahead of Gary Lineker’s 10. Six came at the 2026 World Cup, where he overtook Gary Lineker to become England’s outright leading scorer in the tournament’s history, taking his total to 14 goals. He also became the first England men’s player to score at five different major international tournaments. Three trophies and a historic award Kane’s goals helped Bayern secure a domestic treble, winning the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup before retaining the Bundesliga title and adding the DFB-Pokal to their honours. The Champions League semi-final run and England’s World Cup campaign added further weight to his case, while his individual numbers placed him among the outstanding performers of the season. After years of prolific scoring without the biggest team honours, Kane has now combined individual excellence with silverware and football’s most coveted individual recognition. title: Instagram tests 90-minute videos in bid to challenge YouTube
author: Nathaniel Lacsina
content: Why Instagram is testing hiding your like count Instagram is testing a new video format that lets selected creators upload videos up to 90 minutes long, marking a significant shift for a platform best known for short Reels. The Meta-owned app announced the initiative, called Features, on Monday, October 26, as it looks to attract creators who currently publish longer content on YouTube. Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here. Instagram head Adam Mosseri and vice-president of product Tessa Lyons outlined the plans in a video announcement. The test is already underway with some creators in Brazil and is expanding to a small group in the United States. What are Instagram Features? Unlike Reels, which are primarily designed for short, vertical videos, Features will support longer videos in a horizontal format. Instagram is targeting content such as podcasts, interviews, comedy specials and other programmes that viewers might prefer to watch in full. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Adam Mosseri (@mosseri) For example, a creator could publish a complete podcast episode as a Feature and share shorter highlights through Reels. Those clips could then direct viewers to the full-length video without leaving Instagram. The company is testing a tool called Clips as Reels to connect the two formats. Why is Instagram introducing longer videos? The move puts Instagram in more direct competition with YouTube, where creators regularly publish lengthy videos and earn advertising revenue. Mosseri acknowledged that he had previously opposed longer videos on Instagram because he was concerned they could reduce interactions between friends. Instagram now lets you put someone else's post on your profile grid He now believes short and long videos can work together, with Reels helping people discover longer programmes. Instagram has also been expanding its TV apps, letting users watch content on larger screens rather than only on their phones. Will Instagram pay creators like YouTube? That remains a major unanswered question. YouTube shares advertising revenue with eligible creators through its Partner Program, making long-form videos an important income source for many channels. Instagram has not announced a comparable revenue-sharing programme for Features. A Meta spokesperson told TechCrunch that the company is exploring ways for creators to earn money through brands, fans and Instagram itself. Instagram can now edit your Reels in under 10 seconds — but there's a surprise For now, the test involves a limited group of creators rather than a general invitation to upload longer videos. What else is changing? Instagram is also experimenting with several related features. One would allow creators to organise connected Reels into a series, making it easier for viewers to follow episodes in order. Another aims to help users discover live videos from accounts they may not already follow. The company is also developing its television experience to support more than short Reels. When will 90-minute videos be available? Instagram has not announced a worldwide release date for Features. Testing is currently limited to selected creators in Brazil and the United States. Instagram has not confirmed a timetable for when creators in the UAE or other countries can upload 90-minute videos. Instagram previously experimented with longer videos through IGTV, which launched in 2018 and was discontinued in 2022. The new test represents another attempt to make longer videos part of the main Instagram experience. title: UAE family disputes: Father ordered to support daughter, 37, as lawyer reveals unusual cases
author: Aghaddir Ali
content: Sharjah: Family disputes over money, inheritance, maintenance and the care of elderly parents can escalate into police complaints and court proceedings when they involve alleged abuse, financial exploitation or violations of individual rights, a UAE lawyer has warned. Speaking on Sharjah TV’s Qadiya Lil Hiwar, which means in English “An issue for discussion” , lawyer and legal consultant Aisha Rashid Al Tunaiji discussed cases involving an elderly father allegedly denied access to his pension, a 37-year-old unmarried woman whose father was ordered to support her, and a wife seeking Dh500 a month from her higher-earning husband. Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here. The discussion also covered property transfers, inheritance disagreements, online earnings, domestic violence and neglect of vulnerable parents. Al Tunaiji said the law protects individual rights and regulates responsibilities, but not every family disagreement requires legal action. Dialogue should come first wherever possible, although alleged abuse and financial exploitation may warrant intervention. Family disputes over money, care and inheritance can lead to legal action in the UAE. WhatsApp rows can trigger police complaints Family WhatsApp messages can lead to formal complaints when remarks are interpreted as insults, verbal abuse or defamation. Al Tunaiji described arguments that escalated until one party approached a police station. ironic comments and provocative posts can intensify tensions, sometimes with the aim of settling a personal score rather than seeking compensation. Social media has also created disputes among families who publish videos featuring their children or generate income through shared accounts. In one case, a father managed family accounts and finances, including online earnings, while his children reportedly felt their contributions were not adequately recognised. Similar conflicts arise between couples who disagree over earnings, account ownership or financial management. Al Tunaiji urged families to establish clear arrangements and keep records to reduce misunderstandings. Elderly parents allegedly denied financial support Al Tunaiji recounted a case in which her side sought financial support for a father while his children simultaneously pursued a claim seeking support from him. The children were employed and receiving salaries, raising questions about their ability to contribute towards their father's living expenses. In another case, an elderly father received a pension but his children allegedly prevented him from accessing the money. The concern was whether he was being deprived of income belonging to him. She contrasted these cases with a son who voluntarily gave his mother money whenever he visited. The mother explained that the payments were gifts, highlighting how financial contributions can express affection as well as meet practical needs. Al Tunaiji also referred to cases in which elderly parents were reportedly left in rooms without adequate care or access to water. Such circumstances raise serious concerns when vulnerable people depend on relatives for daily assistance. Whether children can be legally required to support parents depends on the applicable law and the financial circumstances of those involved. Court ordered father to support daughter, 37 Al Tunaiji cited a case involving an unmarried 37-year-old woman whose father was ordered by a court to continue supporting her until she obtained employment and could support herself, or until marriage changed the relevant support circumstances. Other cases involved adults in their twenties and thirties who remained dependent on parents because of health problems or difficulties finding work. The parent's financial means and the child's circumstances must be considered. Expenses such as transport and social activities may arise in maintenance disputes, but do not automatically establish entitlement to a particular amount. The cases do not mean every adult child is automatically entitled to support. Al Tunaiji also described a working wife who earned more than her husband but wanted him to contribute Dh500 monthly towards her expenses. He questioned why he should pay when she earned more. She said the issue involved marital financial responsibilities as well as the emotional significance of a contribution. The legal position depends on the applicable law and circumstances, not the salary difference alone. Property transfers and inheritance disputes Al Tunaiji described a mother with several sons and a younger daughter who registered her house in the daughter's name because they were particularly close. The arrangement later became a source of concern as family tensions developed. The case highlighted the risks of transferring valuable assets based on emotional closeness or expectations of future care. Parents may find themselves vulnerable if they lose control of property needed for their security in old age. In another case, family members initially appeared to agree on an arrangement involving family property. After one or two court sessions, disagreements emerged over management and whether everyone was satisfied. Al Tunaiji said distributing property during a parent's lifetime does not necessarily prevent future disputes. She also welcomed specialised judicial arrangements in the UAE for inheritance matters, particularly where estates involve multiple heirs, substantial assets or children from different marriages. Neglect, violence and legal responsibility The programme examined uquq al walidayn , a term associated with disobediene towards or mistreatment of parents. Al Tunaiji stressed that failing to visit or telephone a parent regularly does not automatically constitute a legal offence. The situation may be different when conduct involves threats, verbal abuse, physical assault, financial exploitation or misuse of a parent's property. Depending on the facts, personal status legislation, domestic violence protections, criminal law or civil and commercial law may apply. Family violence, she said, can also be psychological or economic. She cited hurtful remarks by parents towards children and by children towards parents, as well as cases in which family members allegedly controlled another person's money. She recalled a child telling his mother he would beat her when he grew up, as he had seen his father do. The example illustrated how witnessing domestic violence can influence children's behaviour. By contrast, she described a mother who raised her children through years of marital difficulties before separating from their father after they had grown up and married. Despite the separation, the children wanted their father involved in their marriage and engagement occasions. Al Tunaiji noted that the mother had not turned them against him. Courts must protect vulnerable parents When a parent is bedridden, unconscious, seriously ill or unable to manage their affairs, relatives may need legal authority to handle financial or administrative matters. Al Tunaiji stressed that old age or physical weakness alone does not establish incapacity. Courts may need medical assessments and other evidence before deciding whether intervention is justified. She also referred to a commercial dispute involving a son and a company-related claim for money, and a separate dispute between two merchant brothers involving alleged misconduct, family members and hospital and medical reports. The precise allegations and outcomes were unclear in the programme. Such cases illustrate how business disagreements and personal grievances can become closely linked in court. Al Tunaiji said mediation or assistance from trusted relatives may help resolve disputes, but reconciliation must not pressure victims to tolerate abuse or surrender their rights. Dialogue can prevent family conflict Al Tunaiji cautioned against treating parenthood as a transaction in which children must repay every sacrifice. Referring to the importance of honouring parents in the Quran, she urged families to teach respect and appreciation from an early age. She also said women who choose not to remarry after separation to raise their children should be respected, but remaining unmarried should not be treated as a universal requirement of motherhood. Such sacrifices should remain voluntary. She urged people to develop social awareness, respect personal boundaries, consider others’ feelings and take responsibility for their own mistakes. Her message was that preserving family ties should not come at the expense of individual rights, just as defending those rights should not turn every disagreement into a bitter legal battle. While the law offers protection when rights are violated, mutual respect and a willingness to resolve differences remain essential to maintaining healthy family relationships. title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's younger brother smashes 14 fours in century

title: Israel continues genocide in Gaza despite ceasefire, UN-commissioned experts say
author: AP
content: Jerusalem: A ceasefire agreement in Gaza has not stopped what a group of independent experts commissioned by the UN say is genocide carried out by Israel in the territory, the team said in a new report. They also accused Israeli forces of crimes against humanity, including torture and rape, in the West Bank. In response, Israel's mission in Geneva called for the commission's dissolution and said on X the report marked an example of the body's “misinformation campaign to demonize the state of Israel and portray its very existence as criminal." Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here. Israel has long criticized the commission's output and denied accusations of genocide in Gaza and sexual assault by its forces. The Associated Press could not independently corroborate multiple graphic accounts described in the report of sexual assaults by prison guards and soldiers on Palestinian detainees since October 2023. In one, female guards strip-searched a pregnant Palestinian. In another, guards beat a detainee and hurled sexist slurs while denying her access to the toilet and sanitary pads. The findings by the Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, which seeks to document in minute detail the allegations and evidence of crimes to bolster accountability for perpetrators, could be used by prosecutors at the International Criminal Court or in other jurisdictions to try to bring justice to victims and their relatives. The report Monday said Israel was “continuing to commit genocidal acts with the genocidal intent to destroy, in whole or in part, the Palestinians in Gaza.” Much of the harm has come from Israel’s expansion deeper into Gaza during the ceasefire period, the report says. Since October 2025, when the ceasefire was signed, Israeli forces have gone from controlling 53% of Gaza to at least 60%, the commission said. A winter storm chills Gaza and floods tent camps, exposing aid failures In that time, Israeli fire across the advancing front has killed at least 196 Palestinians – including 18 women, 32 boys and 11 girls, the commission said. The report also accused Israeli soldiers and prison guards of war crimes and crimes against humanity in the West Bank, including extermination, torture, rape and other forms of sexual violence and persecution against civilians. The commission said that it had recently documented six cases where Israeli guards were sexually violent toward male detainees from Gaza in the Sde Teiman military prison. The ceasefire scaled down a devastating war started by the Hamas-led attacks on Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, when the militants killed 1,200 people and took 251 hostages. Israel responded with a campaign that has killed over 74,000 Palestinians, according to Gaza's Health Ministry. title: Macklemore Free Palestine concert: Mark Ruffalo, Cynthia Nixon and more join Dublin kick-off
author: Lakshana N Palat
content: Mark Ruffalo, Cynthia Nixon, Ilana Glazer and Natasha Rothwell lent their star power to Macklemore on Monday night (October 26), appearing remotely as the rapper launched his three-date Free Palestine benefit series before a sold-out crowd at Dublin’s 3Arena. Strokes frontman Julian Casablancas also checked in from afar, while Game of Thrones star Liam Cunningham was there in person, taking the stage as one of the evening’s featured speakers. Macklemore calls for 'free Palestine' at first show since Ed Sheeran tour exit Macklemore announces his own Free Palestine tour: 'I didn't need 10 shows from Ed. I needed two' The music matched the celebrity turnout. Hozier and Kneecap headlined a long list of guest performers that also included Irish folk group Beoga, singer-songwriter Lina Makoul, Dead Prez’s M1 and DJ Habibeats. Psychotherapist and activist Nadia Greenspan and artist-organizer Samir Eskanda joined Cunningham among the night’s speakers. Where the proceeds go Organisers say money raised across the run will support groups delivering humanitarian aid, healthcare, schooling and advocacy for Palestinians. Live Nation’s September announcement listed Anera, Medical Aid for Palestinians, the Palestine Children’s Relief Fund, Jewish Voice for Peace and UNRWA USA among the recipients. How it started The benefit series traces back to September, when Macklemore left the North American stretch of Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour without warning. At a MetLife Stadium show, he had shouted “Free Palestine” and expressed solidarity with people in Gaza and the West Bank. He later claimed New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft lobbied to have him dropped. Kraft acknowledged he had blocked the rapper from performing at Gillette Stadium, pointing to those remarks and accusing him of a longer pattern of antisemitic statements and imagery. Sheeran distanced himself from the call, saying it came from his promoter. Other openers walked away from the tour in protest, including Beoga, who had been sharing the stage with Sheeran nightly before joining Macklemore in Dublin. The rapper has committed the full $1 million he netted from the Sheeran dates to Palestinian relief organizations. Back on stage The Dublin show followed Macklemore’s return to performing on October 22 at Colorado’s Red Rocks Amphitheatre, his first concert since the split. Across 17 songs, he repeated his call for Palestinian freedom and also addressed crises in Sudan, Congo, Lebanon and Haiti, along with those affected by U.S. immigration enforcement. The tour heads next to Paris’ Accor Arena on Thursday (October 29) before closing at London’s OVO Arena Wembley on Friday (October 30). Both remaining shows, like Dublin, are sold out. title: Nazriya faces online trolling after Dubai appearance with Suriya, sparking debate on moral policing
author: Manjusha Radhakrishnan
content: Dubai: South Indian actress Nazriya is facing mixed reactions on social media over an outfit she wore at a promotional event in Dubai, as she prepares to return to Tamil cinema after more than a decade. The actress appeared in an olive-green, off-the-shoulder gown at the event in Dubai for Scene , an upcoming Tamil film starring Suriya and directed by Jithu Madhavan. Images of her appearance prompted strong reactions online, with some users questioning her choice of clothing while others defended her against the criticism. The episode highlights the scrutiny female actors can face over their clothing at public events, even as they promote their latest work. The incident also highlights the double standards often encountered by female actors, who are expected to maintain a particular public image while simultaneously facing pressure to embrace contemporary fashion. Nazriya is also married to actor Fahadh Faasil, making the scrutiny more intense. The episode reflects a broader pattern in celebrity culture, where women’s public appearances frequently become flashpoints for debates about modesty, tradition and individual freedom. The controversy has once again raised a central question: why do women’s fashion choices continue to invite judgments about their morality, even when they are attending professional events? Interestingly, this controversy has also revived discussion of an earlier dispute involving Nazriya and the 2013 Tamil film Naiyaandi , starring Dhanush. At the time, Nazriya alleged that an intimate scene involving a body double had been filmed without her permission. The film's director, A Sarkunam, disputed her account, saying that a double had been used with her consent for a shot in the song Inidhu Inidhu . Nazriya later said she had watched the film and was satisfied that the disputed footage had not been used. The distinction, however, is between a woman choosing what to wear and an intimate scene allegedly being filmed using a body double without her consent. While Nazriya's outfit at the Dubai event was her own choice, the earlier dispute involving Dhanush's film Naiyaandi centred on her allegation that footage had been shot without her permission — highlighting the difference between personal freedom and consent. When ordering through food delivery platforms, such as Deliveroo , Keeta , noon or other food delivery apps, you may encounter several additional charges. 1. Delivery fees This is the amount charged to deliver your order. The fee may vary depending on the restaurant's distance, your delivery location and whether your order qualifies for free delivery. 2. Service or convenience fees Some platforms charge an additional service or convenience fee on top of the food and delivery costs. These are separate charges associated with using the platform or processing the order. 3. Small-order fees Ordering just one item? You may be charged extra if your basket falls below a minimum order value set by the restaurant or platform. This is sometimes called a small-order surcharge. 4. Higher menu prices The price of a meal on a delivery app may differ from what you would pay directly at the restaurant. Some restaurants set higher prices on third-party platforms to account for commissions and other operating costs. This means your order could cost more even before delivery and service fees are added. 5. Optional tips Some apps allow customers to add a tip for the delivery rider. This is optional and should not be confused with mandatory delivery or service charges. What are Dubai's rules on food delivery charges? In 2025, the Dubai Corporation for Consumer Protection and Fair Trade (DCCPFT) introduced guidelines for online food delivery platforms under Circular No. 2 of 2025, in line with Dubai Law No. 5 of 2023 . The guidelines aim to improve pricing transparency, protect consumers and promote fair practices between delivery platforms and restaurants. What must food delivery apps show before checkout? Under the guidelines, platforms should provide an itemised breakdown of charges before customers confirm their orders, including: Food costs: The price of items set by the restaurant. Delivery fees: Including whether charges vary by location or other factors. Service or convenience fees: Any additional platform charges, with an explanation of what they cover. Taxes: Applicable taxes, including VAT. The guidelines also state that undisclosed charges cannot be added after payment. Consumers should be informed of service fees, surcharges and pricing changes before completing an order. A typical food order at checkout on a delivery app should transparently display the additional charges. An example of how a food order checkout page on a delivery app should typically look, with all additional charges clearly itemised. What about discounts and free delivery offers? Promotional offers should also be transparent. For example, cashback offers or discounts that can only be used on future orders should clearly explain their conditions and expiry dates. The guidelines also prohibit unfairly passing the costs of customer subscription programmes, including free or discounted delivery schemes, on to restaurants. Do delivery riders receive the full tip? Under Dubai's guidelines, delivery personnel must receive 100 per cent of gratuities paid by customers. Charged an unexpected fee? Here's what you can do If you notice misleading or undisclosed charges, such as unexpected delivery surcharges, service fees or subscription-related costs, you can raise a complaint with the delivery platform. Under the guidelines, platforms should: Acknowledge the complaint within three working days . Resolve the issue within seven working days , including providing a refund where warranted. How to file a consumer complaint in Dubai for overpricing, defective products or poor service How to avoid paying more on your next food order A few simple checks can help you avoid unexpected costs: Compare the final total: Don't rely only on the advertised meal price. Check the amount payable before confirming. Check minimum-order requirements: A small order may attract an additional surcharge. Read promotional terms: Free delivery does not necessarily mean there are no service fees. Compare restaurant prices: Check whether ordering directly from the restaurant offers better value. Review optional extras: Check whether tips or other optional charges have been added to your basket. The key is to check the complete price breakdown before paying, rather than relying on the initial price displayed in the app. UAE fuel prices rise: Will rising costs make deliveries more expensive? title: Hrithik Roshan is lucky to have Saba Azad, says Sussanne Khan: ‘She is an amazing human being'
author: Lakshana N Palat
content: More than a decade after her marriage to Hrithik Roshan ended, Sussanne Khan says the family they built has landed somewhere rare: everyone, on every side, is content. In a recent interview with the interior designer spoke warmly about her partner Arslan Goni, about Hrithik’s girlfriend Saba Azad, and about the co-parenting bond that has held steady through it all. Jailer 2 first reviews: Rajinikanth brings the whistles as Tiger Pandian, Hrithik Roshan makes a splash Praise for her ex-husband’s partner Rather than keeping her distance from Hrithik’s new relationship, Sussanne went out of her way to praise the actor he is now with. “I must say that even Hrithik’s partner, Saba, is an incredible girl and an amazing human being. I think he is very lucky to have found her. All of us are feeling happy and secure in our relationships now,” she told Times of India. On divorce and alimony The calm that both sides describe today was hard-won. Sussanne’s sister Farah recently looked back on the couple’s 2013 announcement and the uproar that followed, in a conversation with journalist Vickey Lalwani on his YouTube channel. “Everyone was in shock. There was a lot of hue and cry. There were a lot of opinions which people had about their personal life, but I think they both handled it all beautifully. It was amicable,” she said. Farah also took aim at one of the most persistent rumours about the split: that Sussanne received Rs 400 crore in alimony. “I feel sick at the bottom of my heart when I see people online saying that Rs 400 crore was paid and Sussanne got richer,” she said. She argued that the story makes little sense given how close Sussanne remains to her former in-laws, Pinkie and Rakesh Roshan. “They love her. I think she conducted herself in a very sophisticated manner. She is not a gold-digger. It didn’t work out for them, but you don’t need to blow up your marriage for the sake of the press. There was no alimony in this. It’s incorrect and completely bad.” According to Farah, the settlement narrative has lingered for years despite being untrue, and Sussanne never sought to profit from the separation. ‘I don’t care what people think of me’ Farah revealed she had often pushed her sister to set the record straight, but Sussanne chose to stay silent. “I told her, ‘Why don’t you deny all this?’ She said, ‘I don’t care what people think of me, Farah’. I think we are all like that. I do whatever I want. Unless you bring some value into my life, what I do shouldn’t matter to you, and what you think of me shouldn’t matter to me.” Finding love again The current stability has also given Sussanne room to rebuild her own life. She said she met Arslan at a time when she had lost faith in relationships, and that he brought love and companionship back. “I am very lucky to have met him. He is an incredible man and he completes my heart,” she said, adding that the two came into each other’s lives when they both truly needed it. “Whatever the tide throws in, we have got each other. That is the main thing," she told Times of India. title: US lawmakers warn banks, ports against Russian diesel as Trump defends energy dealings with Moscow
author: IANS
content: Washington: A bipartisan group of US lawmakers has warned the chief executives of major American banks, port authorities and fuel distributors that importing Russian diesel could expose them to criminal and civil liability, as President Donald Trump defended his energy dealings with Moscow. The letters were sent on Saturday by Senators Jeanne Shaheen, Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, Ron Wyden, Sheldon Whitehouse, Chris Coons, Elizabeth Warren and Republican Thom Tillis, along with Congressman Gregory W. Meeks, Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee. The Senate Foreign Relations Committee released them on Monday. Get it: Fast, verified news for FREE ... download the Gulf News app — simply click here “Any importation of Russian diesel into the US raises significant legal questions and may be subject to legal action, as well as congressional investigations. Companies that import products in violation of US law may expose themselves to both criminal and civil liability,” the lawmakers wrote. The letters went to the CEOs of JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citigroup, Wells Fargo Bank, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, and to the heads of the port authorities of Houston, Corpus Christi and Beaumont in Texas and of New York/New Jersey. The lawmakers cited Trump’s October 9 announcement and the Treasury Department’s General License 135. They said the Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act of 2022 generally bars Russian energy imports unless the President certifies to Congress that Russia has ceased hostilities in Ukraine. “Granting Moscow the ability to freely sell Russian diesel in global markets damages America’s security interests and is a betrayal of the people of Ukraine,” they wrote. According to the release, public reporting and vessel tracking data show ships carrying Russian diesel are on track to reach Beaumont and New York/New Jersey as soon as the end of this month. The lawmakers asked the companies to preserve all related records and to confirm by October 28. Separately, House Judiciary Committee Ranking Member Jamie Raskin has written to the oil industry warning against the arrangement, Politico reported. Trump, speaking to reporters on Sunday before boarding Air Force One, defended the move. “The only deal we made with Russia, frankly, they released oil into the world,” he said. He added, “we’re not gonna be hostage with the oil industry.” He also referred to special envoy Steve Witkoff’s trip to Moscow. The diesel issue is being watched closely in New Delhi. India became one of the largest buyers of Russian crude after the Ukraine war began, and US policy on Russian energy has been a sore point in the ongoing India-US trade negotiations. Washington had earlier imposed additional tariffs on India over its Russian oil purchases.
