title: Game PC Ringan Terbaik untuk Laptop Spek Rendah
author: GameDex
content: Punya laptop dengan spesifikasi pas-pasan bukan berarti harus berhenti bermain game. Memang, laptop dengan prosesor lama, RAM terbatas, atau tanpa kartu grafis dedicated mungkin kesulitan menjalankan game AAA terbaru. Namun, ada begitu banyak game PC ringan yang tetap menawarkan gameplay seru, cerita menarik, dan pengalaman bermain yang menghibur. Bahkan, beberapa game yang tergolong ringan justru mampu memberikan pengalaman bermain yang tidak kalah menyenangkan dibandingkan game dengan grafis super realistis. Alasannya sederhana: keseruan sebuah game tidak hanya ditentukan oleh kualitas grafis . Game seperti Stardew Valley , Terraria , Undertale , Portal 2 , hingga Left 4 Dead 2 memiliki konsep dan gameplay yang kuat sehingga masih menarik dimainkan meskipun perangkat yang digunakan bukan PC gaming kelas atas. Masalahnya, memilih game untuk laptop spesifikasi rendah terkadang tidak semudah kelihatannya. Label “ringan” bisa memiliki arti berbeda tergantung perangkat. Game yang lancar di laptop dengan RAM 8 GB belum tentu nyaman dimainkan pada laptop dengan RAM 4 GB. Begitu juga dengan penggunaan prosesor dan integrated graphics. Karena itu, artikel ini akan membahas rekomendasi game PC ringan terbaik untuk laptop kentang , lengkap dengan alasan mengapa game tersebut layak dimainkan, jenis gameplay, serta tips agar performanya tetap optimal. Apa yang Dimaksud dengan Game PC Ringan? Sebelum masuk ke daftar rekomendasi, kita perlu memahami terlebih dahulu arti game PC ringan. Secara sederhana, game PC ringan adalah game yang tidak membutuhkan spesifikasi hardware tinggi untuk dapat dimainkan dengan nyaman. Biasanya game seperti ini memiliki kebutuhan prosesor, RAM, GPU, dan kapasitas penyimpanan yang relatif rendah dibandingkan game AAA modern. Namun, “ringan” bukan berarti gamenya jelek atau sederhana. Ada game ringan yang memiliki: Cerita sangat kuat. Gameplay mendalam. Dunia yang luas. Mode multiplayer. Sistem crafting. Strategi kompleks. Replayability tinggi. Dengan kata lain, sebuah game tidak harus memiliki grafis realistis untuk menjadi game yang bagus. Cara Menentukan Game yang Cocok untuk Laptop Kentang Sebelum mengunduh game, sebaiknya perhatikan beberapa komponen utama pada laptop. 1. RAM RAM berfungsi sebagai ruang kerja sementara bagi sistem dan aplikasi. Laptop dengan RAM 4 GB tentu memiliki keterbatasan dibandingkan laptop dengan RAM 8 GB atau 16 GB. Jika laptop Anda hanya memiliki RAM 4 GB, sebaiknya prioritaskan game yang memang memiliki kebutuhan memori rendah. Untuk laptop lama, menutup aplikasi seperti browser dengan banyak tab, Discord, atau aplikasi lain sebelum bermain juga dapat membantu mengurangi penggunaan RAM. 2. Prosesor CPU bertanggung jawab menangani banyak proses dalam game. Game 2D atau game indie sederhana biasanya tidak terlalu membebani prosesor dibandingkan game open-world modern dengan simulasi dunia yang kompleks. 3. GPU GPU merupakan salah satu komponen paling penting untuk game yang memiliki grafis berat. Laptop tanpa GPU dedicated masih bisa memainkan banyak game. Integrated graphics modern maupun integrated graphics generasi lama mampu menjalankan sejumlah game ringan, terutama jika pengaturan grafis diturunkan. 4. Penyimpanan Game ringan biasanya memiliki ukuran instalasi yang jauh lebih kecil daripada game AAA. Ini menjadi keuntungan bagi pengguna laptop dengan SSD atau HDD berkapasitas terbatas. Rekomendasi Game PC Ringan Terbaik Berikut beberapa game yang menarik untuk dicoba jika Anda menggunakan laptop dengan spesifikasi rendah. 1. Stardew Valley Stardew Valley merupakan salah satu game ringan yang sangat populer di kalangan pemain PC. Konsepnya sederhana: Anda mewarisi sebuah perkebunan dan memulai kehidupan baru di sebuah desa. Namun, gameplay-nya jauh lebih dalam daripada sekadar bertani. Anda bisa: Menanam berbagai tanaman. Memelihara hewan. Memancing. Menambang. Berteman dengan penduduk desa. Menikah. Menjelajahi area baru. Mengembangkan perkebunan. Menyelesaikan berbagai misi. Keunggulan terbesar Stardew Valley adalah kebebasan bermain. Tidak ada kewajiban untuk terus mengejar progres dengan cepat. Jika hari ini ingin bertani, silakan bertani. Kalau ingin memancing, Anda bisa menghabiskan satu hari penuh di dekat sungai. Cocok untuk: pemain yang menyukai game santai, farming, eksplorasi, dan simulasi kehidupan. 2. Terraria Terraria adalah game 2D sandbox yang terlihat sederhana tetapi memiliki konten sangat dalam. Anda akan masuk ke dunia yang bisa dieksplorasi, ditambang, dan dibangun sesuai keinginan. Salah satu daya tarik Terraria adalah kombinasi antara: Eksplorasi + crafting + survival + combat + building. Anda bisa menggali tanah untuk mencari material, membuat senjata, membangun rumah, menemukan item langka, dan menghadapi berbagai boss. Walaupun menggunakan grafis 2D, jumlah konten di dalamnya sangat banyak. Bagi laptop kentang, Terraria merupakan salah satu pilihan yang menarik karena fokus utamanya bukan pada visual realistis. Cocok untuk: pemain yang menyukai Minecraft tetapi ingin pengalaman 2D dengan sistem boss dan crafting yang kuat. 3. Undertale Undertale membuktikan bahwa game tidak membutuhkan grafis realistis untuk menghasilkan cerita yang berkesan. Game RPG ini memiliki tampilan sederhana dan gaya visual retro. Namun, kekuatan utamanya terletak pada: Cerita. Karakter. Dialog. Humor. Musik. Sistem pertarungan. Pilihan pemain. Menariknya, cara Anda memperlakukan karakter tertentu dapat memengaruhi perjalanan permainan. Karena kebutuhan hardware-nya sangat rendah dibandingkan game modern, Undertale menjadi pilihan yang sangat cocok untuk PC atau laptop spesifikasi rendah . Jika Anda lebih mementingkan cerita daripada grafis, game ini patut masuk daftar prioritas. 4. Portal 2 Portal 2 adalah game puzzle dari Valve yang terkenal karena mekanisme portalnya yang unik. Anda menggunakan portal untuk berpindah tempat, memecahkan puzzle, dan melewati berbagai ruangan. Semakin jauh permainan berjalan, puzzle menjadi semakin kompleks. Hal yang membuat Portal 2 menarik adalah game ini tidak hanya menguji refleks, tetapi juga kemampuan berpikir. Anda mungkin akan menemukan sebuah ruangan dan berpikir: “Bagaimana caranya saya bisa sampai ke sana?” Kemudian Anda mulai memperhatikan posisi portal, momentum, tombol, laser, dan berbagai elemen lingkungan. Game ini juga memiliki mode co-op yang memungkinkan dua pemain bekerja sama menyelesaikan puzzle. Cocok untuk: pemain yang suka puzzle, humor, cerita, dan gameplay yang mengandalkan logika. 5. Left 4 Dead 2 Left 4 Dead 2 merupakan salah satu game FPS lama yang masih menarik dimainkan hingga sekarang. Game ini menempatkan Anda bersama kelompok survivor yang harus bertahan dari serangan zombie. Ada beberapa hal yang membuat Left 4 Dead 2 tetap menarik: Gameplay cepat. Banyak jenis zombie. Beragam senjata. Mode co-op. Campaign yang dapat dimainkan berulang kali. Sistem AI Director yang membuat jalannya permainan terasa dinamis. Dibandingkan banyak FPS modern, kebutuhan hardware Left 4 Dead 2 relatif ringan. Jika Anda memiliki laptop lama tetapi ingin memainkan FPS bersama teman, game ini bisa menjadi pilihan menarik. 6. Hotline Miami Hotline Miami memiliki visual pixel-art dan gameplay yang sangat cepat. Dari tampilannya, game ini terlihat sederhana. Namun jangan tertipu. Permainannya membutuhkan: Refleks cepat. Strategi. Pengamatan. Timing. Kemampuan mengulang level setelah gagal. Anda dapat menggunakan berbagai senjata dan memanfaatkan lingkungan untuk mengalahkan musuh. Salah satu karakteristik game ini adalah tingkat kesulitan yang cukup menantang. Anda mungkin berkali-kali gagal pada satu ruangan sebelum akhirnya menemukan strategi yang tepat. Bagi pengguna laptop kentang yang menyukai game action, Hotline Miami sangat menarik untuk dicoba. 7. Papers, Please Papers, Please adalah game unik yang menempatkan Anda sebagai petugas pemeriksaan imigrasi di sebuah negara fiksi. Tugas Anda tampak sederhana: memeriksa dokumen orang yang ingin masuk. Namun, semakin jauh permainan berlangsung, semakin kompleks keputusan yang harus diambil. Anda harus memeriksa: Paspor. Nama. Tanggal. Dokumen pendukung. Masa berlaku. Identitas. Informasi yang tidak konsisten. Keputusan Anda dapat memengaruhi kehidupan karakter dan kondisi keluarga Anda dalam game. Game ini cocok bagi pengguna laptop spesifikasi rendah yang ingin mencoba sesuatu yang berbeda dari FPS atau game action biasa. 8. FTL: Faster Than Light FTL: Faster Than Light merupakan game strategi dengan konsep luar angkasa. Anda mengendalikan sebuah kapal dan harus membawa informasi penting melewati berbagai wilayah sebelum dikejar musuh. Di sepanjang perjalanan, Anda harus membuat keputusan. Misalnya: Apakah harus bertarung? Apakah sebaiknya kabur? Sistem kapal mana yang harus diperbaiki? Awak kapal mana yang harus ditempatkan? Apakah sumber daya sebaiknya digunakan sekarang atau disimpan? Karena setiap perjalanan dapat menghasilkan situasi berbeda, game ini memiliki replayability tinggi. Cocok untuk: pemain yang suka strategi dan game dengan keputusan yang memiliki konsekuensi. 9. Among Us Among Us menjadi salah satu game multiplayer yang sangat populer karena konsepnya sederhana tetapi mampu menghasilkan situasi lucu dan menegangkan. Para pemain harus menyelesaikan tugas di dalam sebuah map, sementara beberapa pemain memiliki peran sebagai Impostor. Masalahnya, Anda tidak tahu siapa yang berbohong. Inilah yang membuat permainan menjadi menarik. Kadang pemain yang paling banyak berbicara justru bukan Impostor. Sebaliknya, pemain yang diam bisa saja menjadi pelaku sebenarnya. Game seperti ini cocok untuk laptop kentang karena kebutuhan grafisnya relatif sederhana. Yang lebih penting adalah koneksi internet yang stabil jika Anda ingin bermain secara online. 10. Brawlhalla Brawlhalla merupakan game fighting platform yang dapat dimainkan secara kompetitif maupun santai. Konsep dasarnya mudah dipahami: pilih karakter, masuk arena, lalu kalahkan lawan. Namun, semakin serius Anda bermain, semakin terasa pentingnya: Timing. Positioning. Dodge. Combo. Penguasaan karakter. Prediksi gerakan lawan. Bagi pemain laptop rendah yang ingin memainkan game multiplayer kompetitif, Brawlhalla layak dicoba. 11. Minecraft Minecraft memang dikenal sebagai game sandbox dengan dunia yang sangat luas, tetapi versi PC-nya dapat dikonfigurasi agar lebih ramah terhadap perangkat dengan spesifikasi terbatas. Minecraft memiliki banyak aktivitas: Mining. Building. Farming. Exploration. Crafting. Survival. Multiplayer. Jika laptop Anda kurang bertenaga, beberapa pengaturan seperti render distance dan graphics settings dapat diturunkan. Namun, performa Minecraft sangat bergantung pada versi, konfigurasi, mod, jumlah objek di dunia, dan spesifikasi perangkat. Jadi, jangan langsung berasumsi bahwa semua laptop kentang akan mendapatkan FPS yang sama. 12. Don’t Starve Don’t Starve merupakan game survival dengan gaya visual yang unik. Anda harus bertahan hidup di dunia yang penuh bahaya. Untuk bertahan, Anda perlu mengumpulkan sumber daya, membuat alat, membangun tempat perlindungan, dan memperhatikan kebutuhan karakter. Salah satu tantangan menarik dalam game ini adalah Anda tidak hanya perlu menjaga kesehatan, tetapi juga harus memperhatikan berbagai aspek survival. Jika Anda suka game yang memberikan tantangan dan tidak terlalu banyak menuntun pemain, Don’t Starve bisa menjadi pilihan. 13. Cuphead Cuphead memiliki gaya visual yang terinspirasi dari animasi kartun klasik. Game ini terlihat lucu dan penuh warna, tetapi tingkat kesulitannya cukup tinggi. Sebagian besar tantangan berfokus pada pertarungan boss. Anda harus menghafalkan pola serangan, menghindari proyektil, dan menemukan celah untuk menyerang. Bagi pemain yang suka tantangan, Cuphead dapat menjadi pilihan menarik. Namun, dibandingkan game 2D yang lebih sederhana, kebutuhan hardware dan performanya tetap perlu disesuaikan dengan kemampuan laptop Anda. Cara Membuat Game Lebih Lancar di Laptop Spesifikasi Rendah Memilih game ringan saja belum tentu cukup. Anda juga dapat melakukan beberapa optimasi sederhana. Turunkan resolusi Jika game terasa berat, turunkan resolusi dari misalnya 1920×1080 ke resolusi yang lebih rendah. Semakin sedikit piksel yang harus diproses GPU, semakin ringan beban rendering. Gunakan pengaturan grafis rendah Prioritaskan pengaturan berikut: Shadow Quality. Texture Quality. Effects. View Distance. Anti-Aliasing. Ambient Occlusion. Shadow dan efek visual tertentu dapat memberikan beban cukup besar pada GPU. Tutup aplikasi di background Sebelum bermain, tutup aplikasi yang tidak diperlukan. Browser dengan puluhan tab dapat menggunakan RAM dalam jumlah cukup besar. Jika RAM laptop terbatas, hal ini bisa menyebabkan game terasa lebih lambat atau mengalami stuttering. Gunakan mode performa Pada laptop Windows, pastikan perangkat menggunakan mode daya yang sesuai ketika sedang bermain. Namun, perhatikan suhu perangkat karena mode performa dapat meningkatkan konsumsi daya dan panas. Bagaimana Memilih Game Berdasarkan Spesifikasi Laptop? Tidak semua laptop kentang memiliki kemampuan yang sama. Sebagai gambaran umum: Laptop sangat lama Jika perangkat Anda menggunakan prosesor lama dan RAM terbatas, prioritaskan: Undertale Terraria Papers, Please FTL Hotline Miami Stardew Valley Laptop kelas entry-level Jika perangkat sedikit lebih baru dan memiliki integrated graphics yang lebih baik, pilihan Anda menjadi lebih luas. Anda bisa mencoba: Stardew Valley Terraria Portal 2 Left 4 Dead 2 Among Us Brawlhalla Don’t Starve Laptop dengan integrated graphics yang relatif modern Jika perangkat Anda memiliki CPU generasi lebih baru dan integrated graphics yang cukup baik, Anda dapat mencoba game yang lebih menuntut dengan pengaturan grafis rendah. Tetap periksa system requirements resmi setiap game sebelum menginstalnya karena performa aktual dapat berbeda antara satu laptop dan laptop lainnya. Game Ringan Tidak Berarti Membosankan Salah satu kesalahpahaman terbesar tentang game ringan adalah anggapan bahwa game tersebut pasti membosankan. Padahal, banyak game ringan justru memiliki gameplay yang lebih kreatif dibandingkan game dengan anggaran besar. Game AAA mungkin menawarkan: Grafis 4K + ray tracing + dunia luas. Sementara game indie mungkin menawarkan: Konsep unik + cerita kuat + gameplay inovatif. Keduanya memiliki kelebihan masing-masing. Karena itu, jika laptop Anda tidak mampu menjalankan game terbaru, jangan melihatnya sebagai sebuah kekurangan. Justru ada kesempatan untuk menemukan banyak game klasik dan indie berkualitas yang mungkin sebelumnya tidak pernah Anda coba. Rekomendasi Berdasarkan Genre Agar lebih mudah memilih, berikut kategorinya. Untuk game santai: Stardew Valley Don’t Starve Untuk RPG: Undertale Terraria Untuk FPS: Left 4 Dead 2 Untuk puzzle: Portal 2 Papers, Please Untuk strategi: FTL: Faster Than Light Untuk multiplayer: Among Us Brawlhalla Left 4 Dead 2 Untuk game action: Hotline Miami Cuphead FAQ Game PC Ringan Apa game PC ringan terbaik untuk laptop kentang? Tidak ada satu game yang paling cocok untuk semua laptop. Namun, Stardew Valley, Terraria, Undertale, Papers, Please, FTL, dan Hotline Miami merupakan beberapa pilihan yang menarik karena gameplay-nya kuat dan kebutuhan hardware-nya relatif rendah. Apakah laptop tanpa VGA bisa digunakan untuk bermain game? Bisa. Laptop tanpa GPU dedicated tetap memiliki integrated graphics pada banyak konfigurasi. Banyak game ringan dapat dimainkan menggunakan integrated graphics, meskipun tingkat performanya bergantung pada model CPU, GPU terintegrasi, RAM, dan pengaturan game. Apakah RAM 4 GB cukup untuk bermain game PC ringan? Untuk sejumlah game ringan, RAM 4 GB masih dapat digunakan. Namun, pengalaman bermain bisa lebih terbatas karena sistem operasi dan aplikasi background juga menggunakan RAM. Jika memungkinkan, RAM yang lebih besar akan memberikan ruang lebih luas untuk multitasking dan game yang lebih berat. Bagaimana cara mengetahui laptop kuat menjalankan sebuah game? Periksa minimum system requirements dan recommended system requirements dari game tersebut. Bandingkan CPU, GPU, RAM, dan ruang penyimpanan yang dibutuhkan dengan spesifikasi laptop Anda. Perlu diingat bahwa memenuhi spesifikasi minimum tidak selalu berarti game akan berjalan pada FPS tinggi. Kesimpulan Memiliki laptop spesifikasi rendah bukan berarti pilihan game Anda terbatas. Justru ada banyak game PC ringan terbaik yang menawarkan pengalaman bermain luar biasa tanpa membutuhkan GPU mahal. Jika Anda menyukai game santai, Stardew Valley bisa menjadi pilihan. Jika ingin eksplorasi dan crafting, Terraria sangat menarik. Untuk cerita dan RPG, Undertale layak dicoba. Sementara itu, Portal 2 cocok bagi penggemar puzzle dan Left 4 Dead 2 dapat menjadi pilihan bagi Anda yang ingin bermain FPS bersama teman. Kuncinya bukan hanya mencari game dengan grafis sederhana, tetapi memilih game yang sesuai dengan kemampuan perangkat dan preferensi bermain Anda. Sebelum menginstal game, selalu periksa spesifikasi minimum, sesuaikan pengaturan grafis, dan jangan ragu menggunakan resolusi lebih rendah jika performa belum optimal. Jadi, daripada laptop kentang hanya dipakai untuk browsing dan menonton video, kenapa tidak mulai menjelajahi game-game ringan yang seru? Pilih satu game dari daftar di atas, instal, dan temukan sendiri mana yang paling cocok dengan perangkat serta gaya bermain Anda. title: Bulls overwhelmed by Celtics as defense remains an ongoing issue
author: Joe Cowley
content: <p>BOSTON — There have been flashes of good play from this new group of Bulls, moments where the front office could say, ‘‘OK, we have something here.’’</p><p>There just haven’t been a lot of them.</p><p>And there were even fewer Monday night.</p><p>Similar to what happened in the season opener Wednesday in Toronto, the young Bulls (1-3) simply couldn’t compete for more than a few minutes here and there with the established Celtics, ultimately falling 134-99 in a game that was well out of hand by the third quarter, when a halftime deficit of 12 points grew to a laughable 30. The Celtics outscored the Bulls 39-21 in the quarter behind 19 points from sharpshooter <b>Payton Pritchard</b>.</p><p>The damage didn’t only come from the outside. The Celtics also outscored the Bulls 46-30 in the paint and outrebounded them 54-40, including 19 offensive boards.</p><p>That’s what irked coach <b>Tiago Splitter </b>the most, among a list of disappointments.</p><p>‘‘We knew that was a very good team shooting the three-ball, but when you give them second and third chances, it’s impossible,’’ Splitter said. ‘‘The biggest reason [for the loss] is we’ve got to rebound the ball better. We’ve got to take care of the ball and shoot the ball better, as well.’’</p><p>The defense, including the rebounding, was expected to be better this season.</p><p>‘‘We can be really good defensively,’’ forward <b>Matas Buzelis </b>said. ‘‘Just thinking, me, <b>Caleb</b> [<b>Wilson</b>], [<b>Jalen Smith</b>], [<b>Nic</b>] <b>Claxton</b>, <b>Lenny</b> [<b>Miller</b>] — we’re all really athletic, long, so we have all the tools. It’s just the process of getting that understanding of what position we’re in, how to attack the offense, how to get back. . . . It’s like telepathic, honestly. Sometimes you can’t explain basketball. Something happens, and you know where to be at.</p><p>‘‘Like, I knew last year I could be really, really aggressive being low man with <b>Isaac</b> [<b>Okoro</b>] because he would scramble, so you knew where to go. So it takes some time.’’</p><h3>Nic of time?</h3><p>The Bulls could have used a certain 6-11 big man to help deal with the Celtics’ <b>Mitchell Robinson</b> and <b>Neemias Queta</b>. Claxton, who’s out with a strained left hamstring, continues to move closer to a return.</p><p>‘‘He’s getting better,’’ Splitter said. ‘‘[On Monday morning], he did a good workout on the court, not with the team yet. We’re looking to increase those practice, individual workouts at the start of next week and hopefully get him with the group soon.’’</p><p>The Celtics were the latest opponent to exploit the Bulls’ lack of size, beating them up 30-19 on the glass in the first half. That was coming off the Bulls’ loss to the Wizards on Saturday in which they were outrebounded 48-44.</p><h3>Fix the hitch</h3><h3></h3><p>Miller, a forward in his fourth NBA season, has proved to be an efficient scorer overall, but the Bulls think there’s an entirely different gear for him in becoming a better three-point shooter. He has a hitch in his shot that the coaching staff is working on making a bit smoother.</p><p>‘‘It’s not something that is easy to change, especially when you have that habit,’’ Splitter said. ‘‘But [we’re] just trying to get smoother and make him feel comfortable. At the end of the day, you’ve got to make shots. It doesn’t matter how it looks, right? We’re putting a lot of effort into all the guys and shooting. It’s part of the development with this team that everybody becomes a better shooter.’’</p><p>Miller is shooting 25% from three-point range this season after shooting 35.6% in 27 games with the Bulls last season.</p>

title: Man shot during argument in West Englewood
author: Sun-Times Wire
content: <p>A man has been hospitalized after he was shot during an argument in West Englewood Monday evening, according to Chicago police.</p><p>The man, 38, was arguing with another man in the street in the 2000 block of West 68th Place at 5:30 p.m. when the other man shot him in his leg and abdomen, police said. The wounded man was taken to Christ Medical Center in serious condition.</p><p>No one is in custody.</p>

title: A forgettable start for the Bulls' Matas Buzelis as he finds his way
author: Joe Cowley
content: <p>BOSTON — It’s easy to forget that Bulls forward Matas Buzelis has a 40-point game on his résumé. Forty-one points, actually, on a 16-for-28 shooting night against the Warriors in March.</p><p>It’s easier to forget that during that same month, in his second NBA season, he averaged 20.7 points, 7.1 rebounds and 1.8 blocks over 14 games.</p><p>Is this season starting the way he’d like it to? Not even close. But the notion he’s somehow regressing or isn’t a true foundational piece in the Bulls’ latest rebuild left him shaking his head with a laugh Monday.</p><p>“We have Norm [Powell], Caleb [Wilson], both ultra-aggressive, so you’ve got to figure out the right time to shoot,” Buzelis said before the Bulls (1-3) fell hard in a 134-99 loss to the Celtics at TD Garden. “Not just me — all of us. That’s why we all watched film together [Sunday], players only, trying to figure out how things need to work.</p><p>“Once we figure out our spots, where we want to go, and then everyone figures out what they’re going to shoot, the shots they’re going to take, it will be easier to understand the game. Right now, how we’re shooting is like freestyle. We really don’t know what we have to get into or what sets we have to be aggressive in. But I know this group is very passionate about basketball and what we have to do to get there, how we can compete every night, [to] be the best team we can be.”</p><p>How does Buzelis (11 points Monday) see himself fitting into the equation specifically?</p><p>“What do people think — you’re going to come in and get buckets right away?” he said. “It’s a process. I’ve been working really hard, worked hard this summer, so all I need to really do is get out there and trust my skills. I’m still trying to figure out where I can hunt my shots at, where I can be aggressive. And once that happens, we’ll be just fine, all of us.”</p><p>“All of us” is a focal point for him this season: Getting together for extra film sessions. Talking it out. Getting on the same page.</p><p>That cohesiveness also falls on first-year Bulls coach Tiago Splitter. It’s great that Wilson, the No. 4 overall draft pick, dropped 30 points on the Wizards in his first home game Saturday — but it came in a loss. Splitter knows Wilson is a huge piece in what the Bulls hope to achieve, but he’s not the only one. His philosophy is making sure Buzelis and Wilson develop at the same time.</p><p>“Play the right basketball,” Splitter said. “Coach them, teach them. Be on it when it’s needed. I think that’s how you build a team — you build winners.</p><p>“I don’t think there’s any secret there. It’s not just ‘Let them play.’ You have to coach them where to be, how to do it. . . . It’s a balance, also, where you play random basketball and sometimes you call a play for one of those guys. So, it’s a balance for sure.”</p><p>Buzelis is on board — he just wants to make sure he’s on the floor to help make it happen. That wasn’t the case last Friday night, when he was benched for the entire fourth quarter of the Bulls’ victory over the Bucks.</p><p>“If we see [forward] Lenny [Miller] is playing better than me, creating more advantages, you play him,” Buzelis said. “As a competitor, of course I’m a little annoyed, I want to be out there. But I also have a responsibility to show that I belong out there, that I belong on the court at the end of a game. That’s on me to play hard, create problems for the opposing team. That’s my responsibility.”</p>

title: Feds say Quincy man mailed letters containing white powder to members of Illinois congressional delegation
author: Misha Manjuran Oberoi
content: <p>A 36-year-old Quincy man is accused of mailing letters containing white powder to four members of Congress from Illinois, including a senator and three House members, according to a criminal complaint filed in the U.S. District Court Monday.</p><p>Matthew Unglesbee faces charges of mailing threatening communications, false information and hoaxes, according to the complaint filed in the Central District of Illinois.</p><p>The letters contained a white granular substance and handwritten messages, including “HA HA” and “HAH enjoy the gift,” according to an FBI affidavit. Preliminary testing did not detect chemical or biological toxins in the substance.</p><p>During an interview with FBI agents Sunday, Unglesbee allegedly admitted mailing the four letters. He told investigators the substance was salt and said he used it because it resembled anthrax, according to the affidavit. Unglesbee said he knew the powder would be taken seriously and would have “hazmat come in white suits.” He claimed he was joking, but acknowledged recipients could perceive the letters as dangerous.</p><p>The letters were postmarked in Springfield on Oct. 19. While searching Unglesbee's home, investigators also found an empty, unmailed envelope addressed to a congressional office in Washington, D.C.</p><p>The complaint does not identify the four congressional recipients by name. Several <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/10/16/schneider-quigleys-offices-receive-suspicious-letters-amid-pre-election-threats" >Illinois lawmakers have publicly reported receiving suspicious mail</a> in recent weeks, including Democratic Reps. Mike Quigley, Brad Schneider and Jan Schakowsky. Quigley and Schakowsky each reported another letter last week.</p><p>Sen. Tammy Duckworth's office also confirmed receiving two suspicious letters in the mail in recent weeks. The letters were mailed to Duckworth's Chicago office.</p><p>It has not been confirmed that all of those incidents are connected to the case against Unglesbee, though in a statement to the Sun-Times, Quigley said he was “relieved to learn” an arrest had been made in connection with one of two suspicious mailings sent to his Chicago office.</p><p>“This individual, and whoever is responsible for the other suspicious mail received around the country, must be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law,” Quigley said in a statement. He also thanked the Chicago Fire Department’s hazardous materials unit for responding to both incidents.</p><p>Schakowsky released a statement Monday afternoon saying she was aware of reports of someone being arrested in connection with the letter sent to her Skokie office last week. She also expressed gratitude to the law enforcement officers "who acted quickly and decisively to help ensure the safety of me and my staff and are working to hold those responsible accountable."</p><p>Schneider’s office issued a statement last Wednesday saying it had received another piece of suspicious mail at his Lincolnshire office. Schneider thanked law enforcement agencies for their response and investigation, according to his office’s public statement.</p><p>The investigation continues.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/10/21/2-chicago-area-members-of-congress-receive-another-suspicious-package" >2 Chicago area members of Congress again received ‘suspicious’ packages</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

title: Last mayoral candidates file signatures for 2027 ballot
author: David Struett
content: <p>Thirteen candidates will vie for the right to deny <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/09/13/chicago-mayor-brandon-johnson-announcement-reelection-bid-2027" >Brandon Johnson</a> a second term and become Chicago’s 58th mayor, but only if they can survive cutthroat petition challenges that could narrow the field considerably.</p><p>Joining the mayoral field on the final day of filing were: retiring Illinois Comptroller Susana Mendoza with a self-reported 26,000 signatures; cardiologist and political newcomer Lisa Nee with what she says are 31,000 signatures; Cook County Board of Review Commissioner George Cardenas with a self-reported 31,500 signatures; and Cook County Treasurer Maria Pappas with what she said is "slightly shy of" 40,000 signatures.</p><p>Also joining the mayoral field on the final day of filing were attorney William Quinlan, businessman Joe Holberg, conservative Danielle Carter-Walters and former real estate developer Zoe Ma.</p><p>Five candidates filed their nominating petitions on the<a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/19/mayor-race-candidates-stacks-nominating-petitions-chicago-board-of-elections" > first day of filing:</a> Illinois Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias; lobbyist John Kelly; former Chicago Housing Authority Chair Matthew Brewer; U.S. Rep. Mike Quigley and millionaire businessman and perennial political candidate Willie Wilson.</p><p>That brings the total number of mayoral candidates to 14 — but that is likely to change.</p><p>Campaign managers and veteran political operatives said they expect the crowded mayoral field to shrink substantially as candidates closely scrutinize each other's nominating petitions to make certain they have the required 12,500 valid signatures to remain on the ballot.</p><p>No one will be immune from those challenges no matter how it looks, or whom it might knock off the ballot. That includes Johnson, who skipped opening day, and therefore, the lottery for the top spot on the ballot. He said he filed 33,000 signatures Friday.</p><p>That’s a relatively low number for an incumbent mayor. Richard M. Daley, Chicago’s longest-serving mayor, once filed more than 100,000 signatures with the help of the once-powerful Democratic ward organizations filled with city workers.</p><p>“I’m looking at everybody — particularly the African American ones,” Wilson told the Chicago Sun-Times. “And if somebody do challenge me, I’m very confident that we’re OK. But that’s up to them if they want to spend the money.”</p><p>Asked whether he believes Johnson will have a problem making the ballot, Wilson said, “He’s the mayor. He’s been through this before. He ought to have his stuff in order, I would think."</p><p>The challenge period begins Tuesday and ends Nov. 2. The adjudication of challenges will continue until Dec. 17, when the final mayoral ballot if certified.</p><p>“I know for a fact that different people have pulled Dr. Wilson’s petitions and are going through them line-to-line," said former state Sen. Ricky Hendon, who is handling petition challenges for Wilson. "The only thing I can guarantee is they can’t get him because we did the work, went down to the Board of Elections and verified the signatures before we filed them. Some campaigns did not do that."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-fb0000" appear shaky.</p><p>Former President Barack Obama launched his political career by knocking incumbent state Sen. Alice Palmer off the ballot.</p><p>“Everybody has to do the work to get on the ballot. If you don’t have the signatures, that’s a problem. … That’s why they have the challenge process. Everyone is gonna be held to that scrutiny," Jubeh said.</p><p>Veteran political operative Victor Reyes, advising the Nee campaign, expects Giannoulias to concentrate his challenges on Quigley and others with the greatest potential to draw votes along the “vote-rich” north lakefront.</p><p>That’s where Johnson sealed his 2023 mayoral victory, and where the 2027 election is expected to be decided once again.</p><p>“You do everything you can to structure the race regardless of how they beat you up” for being the big-bucks candidate who “compromises democracy,” said Reyes.</p><p>Kelly is likely to challenge Mendoza, who is targeting the same conservative voters in Northwest and Southwest Side wards that are home to scores of police officers and firefighters. And Mendoza is likely to challenge Cardenas, the only other Hispanic in the race.</p><p>Giannoulias could challenge Kelly and Mendoza, as well as Pappas, a fellow Greek-American with whom he has a long-standing rivalry. </p><p>"He’s going for a first-round win and, with all of that money, he has the resources and the ability" to narrow the field enough to improve his chances, Reyes said.</p><p>Pappas filed her petitions wearing a shirt reading, "No biceps, just brains," a veiled jab at Giannoulias that she said "speaks for itself."</p><p>That was a reference to what she told the Sun-Times about Giannoulias the day candidates began circulating nominating petitions. “If you want to be mayor of the city of Chicago, your IQ has to be higher than your body temperature. … That’s what’s going to be required in the mayor’s race."</p><p>Pappas and Cardenas were among five candidates filing within an hour of the deadline on Monday, thereby entering a lottery for the coveted last spot on the ballot. The others were Holberg, who said he gathered 32,000 signatures; Carter-Walters, who said she had 13,000 signatures; and Ma with a self-reported 17,000 signatures.</p>

title: Illinois joins 19 other states in FTC lawsuit accusing Dollar General of false price advertising
author: Sun-Times Wire
content: <p>Illinois joined a coalition of states and Federal Trade Commission in suing Dollar General, accusing the discount chain of charging more at the checkout counter than prices advertised online.</p><p>The lawsuit alleges the company “generated millions of dollars by regularly and repeatedly charging shoppers more at the register than the prices it advertises,” in violation of both federal and state laws regarding consumer fraud, according to a statement from Illinois Attorney General Kwame Raoul.</p><p>“Overcharging for products at a time when many basic necessities have become less affordable harms vulnerable families and consumers,” Raoul said.</p><p>Dollar General didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.</p><p>In two instances detailed in court documents, Illinois consumers were charged $0.75 to $1.78 more than was advertised online. Examples from other states allege the company charged more than four dollars above the listed price and didn’t honor coupons.</p><p>“Whatever the register rings up, that will be the price, and we can’t give you [a] discount,” an Illinois Dollar General store manager is alleged to have told a customer upset about the price differences in April 2024, per the lawsuit.</p><p>An FTC investigator who went undercover to make purchases at one location found the screens displaying the prices as items were rung up faced only the employee; in other cases, those screens were broken, according to the lawsuit.</p><p>Joining Illinois in the lawsuit are the attorneys general of Alabama, Arizona, Arkansas, California, Connecticut, Florida, Iowa, Kansas, Louisiana, Michigan, Mississippi, Nebraska, New Jersey, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Tennessee, Utah and Wisconsin.</p>

title: Amtrak's Bridgeport railyard to get environmental review after community pressure
author: Violet Miller
content: <p>Amtrak’s new maintenance facility in Bridgeport will undergo a federal environmental review after community pushback over the project initially being allowed to move forward without one, according to the Federal Railroad Administration.</p><p>The agency’s dashboard for the project lists Oct. 8 as the start date of the environmental review, which it also said is expected to be complete by year's end.</p><p>The review will trigger a 30-day public comment period, and the federal agency said it will hold at least two public meetings on the project, though details on those have yet to be released.</p><p>Amtrak initially had received more than $600 million and a “<a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/what-to-know-chicago-white-sox-stadium-proposal-justin-ishbia" target="_blank" ><u>categorical exclusion</u></a>” from the federal government for the project, which allowed it to move forward without a full environmental assessment or an environmental impact statement “unless there are extraordinary circumstances.”</p><p>But the federal agency changed its tune after Amtrak said it planned to use some of the funds for the $915 million project to repair 17 viaducts “supporting the Canal Street Yard.”</p><p>“After reviewing this modified project scope, FRA has decided to prepare an environmental assessment, through a process that will include public comment, for the Proposed Action,” the agency said on its <a class="Link" href="https://www.permits.performance.gov/permitting-project/dot-projects/midwest-maintenance-facilities" target="_blank" ><u>website for the project</u></a>.</p><p>It comes after <a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/environment/2026/10/16/amtrak-bridgeport-chinatown-justin-ishbia-white-sox" target="_blank" ><u>months of public outcry from local residents</u></a> who worry the new facility could pose health hazards and generate smells and sounds that could tank property values. An initial review from the FRA determined the project would have a minimal noise, air quality and groundwater impact on the surrounding community.</p><p>Also behind neighbors' ire: The move comes hand-in-hand with <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2025/06/05/jerry-reinsdorf-justin-ishbia-reach-long-term-agreement-that-establishes-a-framework-for-transition" target="_blank" ><u>potential future White Sox owner</u></a> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2025/06/06/justin-ishbia-white-sox-jerry-reinsdorf-ownership-winnetka" target="_blank" ><u>Justin Ishbia</u></a>’s companies helping to finance Amtrak’s move while purchasing the existing rail facility, which it wants to develop as a site for a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/05/new-sox-park-future-owner-announces-proposal-for-riverside-stadium-at-the-railyards" target="_blank" ><u>proposed new stadium</u></a> for the South Side team.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/what-to-know-chicago-white-sox-stadium-proposal-justin-ishbia" >What to know about the Chicago White Sox stadium proposal</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2026/10/07/amtrak-bridgeport-rail-yard-white-sox-ishbia" >City Council grills Amtrak over proposed Bridgeport rail yard</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/environment/2026/10/16/amtrak-bridgeport-chinatown-justin-ishbia-white-sox" >Bridgeport, Chinatown residents tell us what they think about Amtrak rail yard development plans</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>In a joint statement Monday, Ishbia’s company, Canal Edge, and Amtrak said they welcomed the “opportunity for additional review, dialogue and feedback.”</p><p>“We believe a deeper public review process will better help stakeholders understand the need for a new facility and associated viaduct repair work as well as the environmental impact of the project,” the companies said.</p><p>Ald. Nicole Lee (11th), whose ward encompasses the proposed maintenance facility, said a 24/7 rail maintenance operation in the middle of a residential neighborhood “should have been an immediate nonstarter,” and that the fight against the new railyard would continue. Both of the state's U.S. senators, Democrats Tammy Duckworth and Dick Durbin, called for transparency for the environmental review, but applauded the move as progress.</p><p>“We should not have had to scream, fight and pound on the doors of power just to get the basic transparency about the environmental effects this plan could have on our residents,” Lee said in a statement. “No matter what this environmental study produces, our concerns about noise pollution, economic impact and other issues remain unaddressed.”</p><p>Hannah Dembosky, founder of the Bridgeport Environmentalists, said she and other residents are still pushing for a more detailed Environmental Impact Statement. Dembosky is concerned the Trump administration’s history of flouting environmental concerns will carry through the Amtrak project’s two-month assessment.</p><p>She said she hopes for an independent review of the findings. The Rail Passengers Association, a rail travel advocacy group based in Washington, D.C., said it plans such a review, in addition to conducting its <a class="Link" href="http://www.railpassengers.org/canalyardsurvey" target="_blank" ><u>own community survey</u></a>.</p><p>“I am concerned that under the Trump administration, this environmental assessment could just be used to silence community members if it's done behind closed doors,” said Dembosky, a Bridgeport resident. “Having this next to so many homes, residences and schools, it'll be important to have detailed and accurate information.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-100000" title: Top mayoral aides defend Mayor Johnson's tax-heavy $17.6B budget
author: Fran Spielman
content: <p>Top mayoral aides on Monday began their defense of Mayor Brandon Johnson’s tax-heavy <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2026/10/20/mayor-brandon-johnson-failed-corporate-head-tax-resurrected-proposed-budget" >$17.6 billion budget</a> and acknowledged they have no Plan B if, as expected, the failed corporate head tax is shot down again.</p><p></p><p>One year after a 31-member coalition of conservative and moderate alderpersons rejected the mayor’s corporate head tax, 29 alderpersons have vowed to do the same with Johnson’s newest attempt. </p><p>They will be joined by business leaders, who are also determined to block the third and biggest increase yet involving a Chicago tax on equipment rentals and cloud computing. The current tax already is the highest of its type in the nation.</p><p>Against that backdrop, Johnson’s finance team began trying to sell a tax-the-rich budget that includes $664.2 million in new and increased taxes and $119.8 million in spending cuts. The trimming is even less, given that up to $68 million of that spending is being shifted from the city’s corporate fund to enterprise funds.</p><p>“This budget is quote, unquote 'balanced’ with more than $5 in new revenue for every one dollar saved,” said Ald. Brendan Reilly (42nd). “Why is the administration choosing taxing over managing its expenses?”</p><p>Acting Budget Director Jonathan Ernst said cost-cutting in Johnson’s first three budgets produced “nearly three-quarters of a billion dollars” in savings. “Those reductions continue this year. We’re adding another $120 million,” Ernst said.</p><p>Reilly was not appeased, lashing out at newly appointed Chief Financial Officer Ashlee Gabrysch, a former senior director and mid-central regional manager at Fitch, the Wall Street rating agency that in February dropped Chicago’s bond rating to three notches above junk. </p><p>“This budget repeats every one of those problems listed by Fitch ratings where you once worked,” Reilly said. “We have at least $155.6 million in one-time money, $480 million in new borrowing for settlements, (a) $882 million structural gap and a jobs tax that a majority of this City Council rejected once already.”</p><p>Ald. Anthony Beale (9th) demanded to know why the head tax was even presented to the Council “knowing you had 29 aldermen who wouldn’t support it.”</p><p>“What’s Plan B if the head tax doesn’t pass?” Beale asked Ernst.</p><p> “Work with the City Council.," Ernst replied. "We presented you with our plan.”</p><p>Ald. Nicole Lee (11th), who helped lead last year’s unprecedented budget rebellion, homed in on Johnson’s proposal to raise by 33% the tax on equipment rentals, software and cloud computing.</p><p>“This is just an insane amount to increase the PPLT,” Lee said of the personal property lease transaction tax.</p><p>Lee said a promise was built into the management ordinance tied to the city’s 2026 budget that promised not to raise the so-called “cloud tax” for two years.</p><p>“What happened to the freeze, guys?” she asked.</p><p>Ernst said the two-year freeze was stricken from the management ordinance because the cloud tax has over-performed, and the city could not resist the temptation to take even greater advantage of what has become a cash cow.</p><p>“This is where the economy is moving toward, away from areas that we typically tax," Ernst said. "We need to evolve with that or else we don’t end up getting the structural fixes that we need.” </p><p>Johnson's decision to freeze hundreds of police vacancies and civilianize more than 130 more police jobs was another flash point on the first day of budget hearings. So was the mayor's plan to borrow $480 million over what Gabrysch described as five to seven years to cover settlements tied to allegations of police abuse. </p><p>The mayor recently used his fourth veto to block an ordinance that would have required a three-fifths Council vote to approve future borrowing. City Comptroller Michael Belsky denied continued borrowing to cover operating costs would trigger another drop in the city's bond rating.</p><p>"These are things that happened years ago, that are now coming home to roost," Belsky said.</p><p>"We don't want this liability. Nobody does. But the best way to deal with it without crowding out a lot of services at that larger number and affecting the quality of life in Chicago — the only option you have is to finance ... as short as possible and you hope that, going into the future, these things dissipate so you don't have to face that floating liability every year."</p><p>Finance Chair Ald. Pat Dowell (3rd) also made it clear she and her colleagues would not allow Johnson to use the $75 million up-front payment they negotiated with Stonepeak Partners to be used toward the advanced pension payment. They want the $75 million to be an extra payment to chip away at the city's $36 billion pension crisis. That negotiation paved the way for <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2026/09/29/city-council-parking-meters-deal-compromise-stonepeak-partners" >Stonepeak’s acquisition</a> of the city's parking meters. </p>

title: CPD probing its potential misuse of outside agencies' license plate reader systems
author: Violet Miller
content: <p>The Chicago Police Department is conducting an audit to determine whether cops abused their access to other law enforcement agencies’ license plate reader systems.</p><p>The audit comes with a slew of immediate and proposed policy changes to the way Chicago police officers are allowed to access license plate reader data.</p><p>The department said it has immediately reduced access to outside license plate reader systems to only those whose “position and job duties” require access.</p><p>Each of the department’s five bureaus also will be required to designate someone to oversee the use of license plate reader systems, not only those owned by the department, but also those owned by outside agencies.</p><p>Among the proposed changes, the department said it will make login information for the system non-transferable — meaning only one department member can use their log-in credentials — and require that a "legitimate law enforcement purpose” be documented for every query.</p><p>Additionally, monthly audits of searches would be conducted and the Office of Public Safety Administration would be tasked with processing requests by officers for access to outside license plate reader systems.</p><p>The proposal also outlines potential penalties for violations of the department’s directive, which range from suspension from use of the license plate reader search systems to referral for prosecution.</p><p>The department didn’t respond to questions about what initiated the audit or when the subsequent audits would be completed, but said in an earlier statement that the technology plays a “vital role” in homicide, shooting and missing persons cases.</p><p>Mayor Brandon Johnson's office declined to comment.</p><p>A <a class="Link" href="https://www.chicagopolice.org/policy-review/cpd-automated-license-plate-reader-alpr-systems/" target="_blank" ><u>draft</u></a> of the department’s new policy regarding license plate reader use is <a class="Link" href="https://www.chicagopolice.org/policy-review/cpd-automated-license-plate-reader-alpr-systems/" target="_blank" ><u>open for public comment</u></a> through Nov. 12. The department said it will “review the additional feedback received to guide future revisions to the draft” before finalizing the directives.</p><p>The police department is the latest local law enforcement agency to announce internal inquiries into possible abuses of license plate reader technology amid public outcry against surveillance technology company Flock Safety.</p><p>Earlier this month, a former Joliet police lieutenant was hit with felony charges for alleged misuse of Flock technology. It is the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/09/01/illinois-cities-halt-flock-use-suspend-officers-and-review-policy-amid-alleged-improper-use" target="_blank" ><u>third known case this year of a Will County law enforcement officer being accused of misusing the database</u></a> that tracks millions of drivers’ real-time locations.</p><p>Officers from <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/10/06/former-itasca-west-chicago-police-officers-charged-over-alleged-misuse-of-flock-cameras" target="_blank" ><u>Itasca</u></a>, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/10/06/former-itasca-west-chicago-police-officers-charged-over-alleged-misuse-of-flock-cameras" target="_blank" ><u>West Chicago</u></a>, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/08/27/flock-license-plate-reader-alpr-chicago-suburb" target="_blank" ><u>Prairie Grove</u></a> and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/08/27/flock-license-plate-reader-alpr-chicago-suburb" target="_blank" ><u>Kenosha County, Wisconsin</u></a><u>,</u> have all been hit with felony charges after their alleged misuse of the cameras and databases. The Will County sheriff’s office and Channahon Police Department <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/09/01/illinois-cities-halt-flock-use-suspend-officers-and-review-policy-amid-alleged-improper-use" target="_blank" ><u>have also suspended officers</u></a> pending investigations into the searches.</p><p>On Nov. 12, the Will County Board <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/10/07/former-joliet-police-officer-charged-over-alleged-flock-camera-misuse" target="_blank" ><u>is set to consider</u></a> an ordinance to ban automated license plate reader cameras on county property. That's the same day public comment closes for the updated Chicago Police Department directive.</p>

title: Por miedo a ICE, algunos inmigrantes de Chicago cambian su trabajo y vida diaria a horas nocturnas
author: Alma Campos
content: <p>Antes de salir de su casa, incluso para ir a lavar la ropa a una lavandería cercana, Gustavo Domínguez reza. Le pide a Dios que lo deje regresar a casa sano y salvo.</p><p>Era de noche cuando Domínguez, de 49 años de edad, y su esposa Patricia Dávila, de 67, cargaron sus bolsas de ropa en la cajuela y salieron. Domínguez no tiene estatus legal. Su esposa tiene autorización de trabajo y dice que solicitó asilo tras huir de amenazas en México.</p><p>Ahora esperan hasta la noche para lavar la ropa y hacer compras. Tienen miedo de toparse con agentes del Servicio de Inmigración y Control de Aduanas (ICE) durante el día.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-fe0000" name="module-fe0000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>En la lavandería, Domínguez descarga apresuradamente las bolsas. Dávila ayuda y habla mientras trabaja. Dávila ha notado que ahora mucha más gente viene a lavar por la noche.</p><p>“Ahorita vas a ver que más tarde empieza a llegar más gente”, dice Dávila.</p><p>Una vez puesta la lavadora, la pareja sale a comprar en un supermercado cercano mientras la oscuridad se instala en el vecindario.</p><p>Adentro, piñatas cuelgan del techo. Ollas gigantes de tamales ocupan una repisa alta junto a unas hieleras. Cada uno empuja un carrito, cubriendo distintas partes de la tienda para terminar las compras más rápido.</p><p>Dávila dice que a menudo ve a jóvenes en videollamadas con sus madres, mostrando productos y preguntando qué marca comprar.</p><p>Hay “tanto miedo que mandan a los muchachos a hacer las compras”, afirma.</p><p>Casi un año después de que el Operativo Midway Blitz terminara oficialmente, los inmigrantes en Chicago siguen cambiando sus horarios de trabajo y haciendo las diligencias cotidianas en las horas nocturnas o antes del amanecer por miedo a ser arrestados o detenidos por ICE.</p><p>Trabajadores describieron comprar insumos para vender antes del amanecer, trabajar de noche, hacer compras nocturnas y reducir las salidas de sus casas. Algunos todavía trabajan de día porque dependen de esos ingresos, pero cambian sus horarios cuando pueden. Ese cambio ha significado una pérdida de ingresos y la ansiedad constante sigue afectando la salud mental y las relaciones.</p><h3>‘Gente de la noche’</h3><p>Desde comienzos de 2026 hasta la primera semana de agosto, ICE realizó 1,560 arrestos en el Condado de Cook, según un análisis del Chicago Sun-Times y WBEZ de datos de detenciones de ICE obtenidos por el Deportation Data Project. Grupos legales y comunitarios han documentado encuentros en cortes, escuelas y supermercados, y dicen que los operativos se han vuelto menos publicitados pero siguen ocurriendo como parte de la campaña de deportaciones masivas en curso de la administración de Trump.</p><p>“Nos estamos convirtiendo en gente de la noche”, dice Baltazar Enríquez, presidente del Concilio Comunitario de La Villita. “Ahora hacemos las cosas de noche”.</p><p>Enríquez dice conocer a muchos inmigrantes que adoptaron el turno nocturno como forma de intentar evitar encuentros con ICE. Una madre le dijo que le cuesta dormir después de trabajar de noche. Todavía tiene que alistar a sus hijos por la mañana cuando llega a casa. Él recordó que ella describía periodos de solo dos o tres horas de descanso, tomando siestas cuando podía.</p><p>“Me están saliendo ojeras” le dijo, según Enríquez.</p><p>Rosemary Magaña, terapeuta y directora de programas de la Coalición por la Salud Mental de los Inmigrantes, dice que las rutinas nocturnas pueden costarle a la gente las conexiones sociales que les ayudan a sobrellevar la situación. Las visitas, las salidas de fin de semana y las reuniones desaparecen.</p><p>Magaña ha sentido esa vigilancia en carne propia. Durante los primeros días de Midway Blitz, regresaba de llevar a su hijo a la escuela y pasaba el tiempo mirando coches e imaginando qué haría si los agentes los paraban. Una vez, dice, su cuello se puso tan rígido que no podía moverlo.</p><h3>Los agentes impulsaron la nueva rutina nocturna</h3><p>Dávila dice que sus nuevas rutinas nocturnas comenzaron después de que vieron a agentes de inmigración detener gente cerca de su casa. En un incidente el otoño pasado, los agentes pasaron cerca de sus ventanas mientras una niña en una patineta les advertía a los vecinos que no salieran. Los agentes la derribaron de la patineta, según Domínguez, quien dice que escuchó fuertes estallidos y que cayeron botes de gas lacrimógeno detrás de su casa y frente a la de un vecino.</p><p>Domínguez cubrió las ventanas con cobijas. Cerraron las puertas con llave y apagaron las luces. Temía que los agentes entraran. Entre septiembre y parte de octubre de 2025, intentaron quedarse en casa. Durante aproximadamente un mes, una amiga con estatus legal llevaba a Patricia a lavar la ropa y a comprar. Gustavo siguió yendo a trabajar, pero dejó de manejar.</p><p>Durante esos primeros meses de Midway Blitz, pagó viajes en Uber al trabajo, a veces acostándose en el asiento trasero. Domínguez trabaja en un almacén y carga camiones. Cuando su turno terminaba, esperaba horas a que un compañero lo llevara a casa. Otro Uber costaba demasiado.</p><p>Se puso ansioso y perdió peso, quizá entre 10 y 20 libras, dice Patricia. Se preocupa por él.</p><p>Dávila huyó de amenazas de muerte en México después de denunciar abusos sexuales a niñas y ayudar a personas a escapar de la violencia. En 2010, dos de sus sobrinos fueron asesinados en una masacre estudiantil. Ahora teme quedarse en Chicago y regresar a México.</p><p>“Estoy en medio de dos fuegos”, dice.</p><p>Aun así, atribuye a su participación en organizaciones comunitarias el haberle dado cierto sentido de protección cuando todo se vuelve abrumador.</p><p>Pero ve a su esposo batallando más con el miedo, todavía ansioso y enojado por lo que presenciaron el otoño pasado.</p><p>Gustavo tiene una camiseta de un equipo deportivo de Estados Unidos que ya no puede ponerse.</p><p>“La admiración que yo sentía por este país se ha convertido en un desprecio”, dice.</p><p>Habla de ver a padres maltratados por agentes delante de sus hijos, del dolor que los niños podrían llevar mucho tiempo después de una detención.</p><p>“Eres su héroe, ¿y te tratan así?” dice. “Lo que quieren es arrancarte la dignidad”.</p><p>Además de la ansiedad, hay presiones económicas. La pareja ha apartado suficiente dinero para pagar aproximadamente dos meses de renta en caso de que uno de los dos sea detenido.</p><p>Antes iban al centro comercial por ropa y otras cosas que necesitaban, dice Patricia. Ahora pide más por internet, comprando ropa en el sitio Shein y artículos del hogar y personales por Amazon. Comprar así puede salir más caro, afirma. Extraña encontrar ofertas en persona.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-2f6339" sueño</h3><p>En el sistema hospitalario Cook County Health, el psiquiatra Dr. Hugo Solari escucha a diario a pacientes que viven con miedo a ICE.</p><p>“Todos los días, en la consulta, oigo a pacientes hablar de cómo tuvieron que adaptar sus vidas para evitar encontrarse con ICE”, dice Solari.</p><p>Algunos piden citas por telemedicina o recetas por correo. Otros posponen la atención preventiva por temor a salir de casa.</p><p>El estrés también interrumpe el sueño. La ansiedad dificulta dormir y la falta de sueño profundiza la ansiedad. Para pacientes que trasladan sus actividades a la noche, conseguir sueño suficiente y regular puede volverse aún más difícil. Con el tiempo, dice Solari, el estrés crónico y el sueño interrumpido pueden afectar la salud física además de la mental.</p><h3>Mover el trabajo a la noche</h3><p>Imelda, una cuidadora de niños que no tiene estatus legal, ahora sólo acepta trabajos de niñera por la noche. Imelda es un apodo. El Sun-Times no usa su nombre real porque ella teme la deportación.</p><p>Se siente muy orgullosa de su trabajo, enseñar a los niños a tratar a los demás. Disfruta especialmente cuidar a menores de 3 años.</p><p>“Me gusta sembrarles empatía, respeto, por todas las personas”, dice.</p><p>Cuando comenzaron los operativos de inmigración el otoño pasado, Imelda cuidaba a una niña. Aún la llevaba a museos, parques y la biblioteca, vigilando por agentes en el camino. Niñeras se llamaban entre sí para avisarse sobre agentes adonde llevaban a los niños, pidiendo a sus compañeras evitar esas áreas y cuidarse.</p><p>Pero en el trabajo, Imelda trató de no mostrar su miedo.</p><p>“Y con todo el cuerpo temblando tenía que ser profesional en mi trabajo”, dice.</p><p>Le contó a la madre de la niña lo asustada que se sentía. Su empleadora cambió la organización de su trabajo. La familia también le ofreció refugio a ella y su familia en su casa. La oferta la hizo sentir valorada y cuidada.</p><p>La recordó a Ana Frank.</p><p>Ese trabajo terminó cuando la niña empezó la escuela. Ahora, Imelda acepta cuidados esporádicos por la noche, ayudando a los niños con la cena, el baño, los libros y la hora de dormir. El trabajo la mantiene dentro de casa, pero trabaja apenas unas dos veces al mes.</p><p>Imelda se consideraba alguien a quien los demás podían recurrir. A través de su voluntariado en derechos laborales, representa a la gente y alza la voz por ellos. Entre sus compañeras, ella es la que canta, baila y trata de relajar a todos. Pero últimamente se sorprende de su propio miedo, de lo difícil que le resulta salir de casa.</p><p>Pero ni siquiera quedarse en casa apaga el miedo.</p><p>Los pasos arriba le hacen pensar que los agentes han entrado al edificio. Se imagina a alguien dejándolos entrar. Considera dónde podría esconderse. Afuera, estudia los coches que pasan por si podrían pertenecer a agentes de inmigración.</p><p>Magaña, la terapeuta, dice que la ansiedad prolongada puede cambiar lo que la gente espera del mundo. Anticipan peligro y dudan de que las circunstancias vayan a mejorar. Ella lo describe como trauma sistémico, que alcanza más allá de quienes son detenidos directamente.</p><p>“No tiene que pasarte a ti para que te traumatice”, dice.</p><p>Imelda trata de mantenerse fuerte por sus hijos y asegurarles que no pasará nada. Pero ellos también tienen miedo, dice. Las salidas al parque y el tiempo de juego al aire libre se han vuelto menos frecuentes. Le preocupa que los niños asuman preocupaciones por la comida y la renta cuando deberían poder concentrarse en sus estudios.</p><p>“Todo esto va a tener consecuencias y yo lo estoy viendo más en Tomó asiento mientras otros vendedores iban llegando.</p><p>Flores ha vendido comida desde un carrito por unos 16 años. Prepara vasos de mango, sandía, piña y pepino antes de salir con raspados, frituras y chicharrones.</p><p>Tiene licencia para vender y paga impuestos, dice. Tiene licencia de conducir desde hace más de 14 años sin accidentes ni revocaciones.</p><p>“Estoy tratando de hacer todo correcto”, dice.</p><p>Aun así, los reportes de acciones de inmigración en su vecindario a menudo lo mantienen sin vender. Se queda en casa un día, a veces otro, perdiendo ingresos.</p><p>Evitar trabajar de día por completo significaría renunciar al negocio que ha construido durante años. En cambio, cambia las partes del día que puede. Solía comprar la despensa alrededor de las 7 a.m. Ahora hace las compras a las 5, antes del amanecer, con la esperanza de evitar un encuentro. Sigue vendiendo durante el día, pero menos horas.</p><p>Algunos vendedores prefieren trabajar cerca unos de otros para poder ayudarse y intercambiar avisos, dice. Donde él vende, solo hay otro vendedor cerca.</p><p>Para Flores, mover sus horas de venta a la noche traería un riesgo distinto. Teme los asaltos y evita quedarse afuera después de oscurecer.</p><p>“Nos tenemos que cuidar de ICE y también nos tenemos que cuidar de los robos”, dice.</p><p>Cuando ve que se hace de noche, se va.</p><p>“Le doy gracias a Dios y lo que se vendió, se vendió, y vámonos”, afirma.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a
