title: From Classroom to Community: How Advanced Education Skills Could Shape Tasmania’s Next Generation of Leaders
author: busselton
content: Great educational leadership starts with understanding what happens in the classroom. But moving into leadership means looking beyond your own classroom, and instead, thinking about the education community. And while your knowledge and experience as a teacher provide a strong foundation, educational leadership calls for a different skill set. It involves understanding people, systems, change, and the broader community surrounding a school. For Tasmanian educators considering their next step, developing these skills can open up new ways to contribute, influence and lead.   What Does Tasmania’s Education Sector Need From Its Next Generation of Leaders? The next generation of education leaders will need to do more than manage people and make decisions. They will need to understand the people behind those decisions. Schools bring together students, teachers, families, support staff and community organisations. Good leadership means listening, communicating and bringing people together around shared goals. Strong communication is one of the most important leadership skills you can develop. Leadership often requires tough conversations, whether you’re discussing change, supporting team members, or building mutual understanding. Key leadership strengths include: Strategic thinking , so you can look beyond immediate problems and consider longer-term priorities. Communication and collaboration, so you can build productive relationships. Adaptability, particularly as technology, teaching practices and community expectations change. Evidence-informed decision-making, so choices are based on more than instinct or tradition. People leadership, including mentoring, supporting and developing others. These skills can help educators move from responding to challenges to helping develop the direction of their education community.   Beyond the Classroom: Building Skills for Tasmania’s Changing Education Landscape Leadership begins when you start seeing the bigger picture. A classroom teacher naturally focuses on students, learning and the daily demands of teaching. An education leader needs to take into account how those experiences connect with the wider school and community. That might mean contributing to curriculum planning, supporting student wellbeing, working with community groups or helping colleagues adapt to new approaches. The ability to connect classroom experience to broader educational issues is becoming increasingly important. Technology is one example. Leaders need to think beyond using new tools and consider their effects on teaching, learning, professional development, student engagement and relationships. The same applies to student wellbeing, inclusion and community engagement. No one person can solve these issues alone. For educators preparing for leadership, it can help to develop skills in areas such as: Using evidence well, without getting buried in spreadsheets Leading professional learning, so it feels useful and connected Supporting inclusion, especially for students with complex needs Working with families, not just contacting them when something goes wrong Managing change, while keeping staff trust intact You don’t have to master every detail. The aim is to expand your outlook in a way that complements the practical skills you’re already developing.   How Further Study Can Help Tasmanian Educators Take the Next Step Sometimes the next stage of your career requires you to step back from the classroom and look at education from a different angle. Postgraduate learning can help you test those ideas, sharpen them and place them alongside research. A Masters in Education will help Tasmanian educators deepen their expertise in leadership, policy, research, curriculum, wellbeing, and school improvement. The value is not just in the qualification. It is in the thinking habits you develop along the way. You learn to question assumptions, read evidence more critically and understand why some changes take root while others fade after a term. Further study also helps if you are considering roles beyond the classroom, like: Assistant principal or principal pathways Instructional leadership or curriculum roles Wellbeing, inclusion or learning support leadership Education policy, project or system-level work Professional learning and mentoring roles Community and partnership-focused positions For busy teachers, study needs to feel relevant. The best learning connects back to real school issues, the kind you can picture clearly because you have lived them. – Tasmania’s next education leaders are already working in its classrooms, staffrooms and school communities. They are the people who notice what needs to change and care enough to act.   Taking the next step does not mean becoming someone different. It means building on the skills you already use every day, then adding broader knowledge, confidence and perspective.   With the right support, Tasmanian educators can lead in ways that are practical, thoughtful and deeply connected to community. //This content is provided by a third party The post From Classroom to Community: How Advanced Education Skills Could Shape Tasmania’s Next Generation of Leaders appeared first on Busselton .

title: Top 10 Car Accident Lawyers Gold Coast
author: busselton
content: Involved in a Gold Coast car accident and dealing with injuries, medical appointments, time away from work, vehicle issues and pressure from insurers, all while trying to understand whether you can make a compensation claim. In Queensland, people injured in road accidents may be able to claim compensation through the Compulsory Third Party (CTP) insurance scheme. However, every claim is different. Liability, the nature of your injuries, medical evidence, insurance details and important legal deadlines can all affect your options. We have compared 10 car accident lawyers servicing the Gold Coast. We considered their advertised experience with motor vehicle accident claims, no-win, no-fee options, specialist focus, local accessibility, and free consultation availability. This guide helps you create a shortlist before arranging independent legal advice.   1. Splatt Lawyers Gold Coast Based in Southport, Splatt Lawyers Gold Coast personal injury law firm that assists local residents with car accident and motor vehicle compensation claims. Kerry Splatt, a Queensland Law Society Accredited Specialist in Personal Injury Law, leads the firm. From Pimpama to Tweed Heads, the team advises people injured in car, motorcycle, truck, bicycle, pedestrian, public transport, taxi, Uber, rideshare, e-bike, and e-scooter accidents. This broad focus on road accidents (and whiplash claims) can be useful when an accident involves more than a standard car-to-car collision. Splatt Lawyers promotes a 100% no-win, no-fee service with no upfront legal fees. The firm also offers free initial advice to help injured people understand whether they may have a claim, what evidence they may need and what compensation categories could apply. The firm may be particularly suitable for serious or complicated claims involving chronic pain, long-term treatment, significant income loss or catastrophic injuries. Pros: Queensland Law Society Accredited Specialist leadership for complex personal injury matters Advertises a 100% no-win, no-fee arrangement with no upfront costs Handles a wide range of road accident claims, including motorcycles, trucks, pedestrians and rideshare accidents Free initial advice for clients who want to assess their legal options They can make home and hospital visits for those who can’t travel Cons: Queensland-focused practice cannot help with legal issues in other Australian states   2. The Car Accident Compensation Lawyers QLD The Car Accident Compensation Lawyers QLD is a Queensland-focused firm that handles motor vehicle accident and road injury claims. It serves people across Queensland, including Gold Coast drivers, passengers, motorcyclists, pedestrians, and cyclists. The firm works under the guidance of a Queensland Accredited Specialist in Personal Injury Law and focuses on making the CTP claim process easier to understand. Clients can arrange a free consultation to discuss their accident, injuries and potential eligibility for compensation. Its team assists with car accident claims, motorcycle accidents, truck crashes, pedestrian injuries, bicycle accidents, rideshare incidents and insurance claim disputes. The firm advertises transparent legal costs and a no-win, no-fee arrangement with no upfront charges. Pros: Specialist focus on Queensland car and road accident compensation claims Free consultation and advertised no-win, no-fee arrangement Assistance with CTP claims, insurance disputes, serious injuries and multiple accident types Accredited Specialist guidance for personal injury matters Cons: Specialist motor vehicle injury focus may not suit clients needing extensive advice in other legal areas   3. Attwood Marshall Lawyers Attwood Marshall Lawyers is a long-established Australian law firm with several Gold Coast office locations. Its personal injury team assists clients with motor vehicle accident claims, workplace injuries, public liability matters, superannuation claims and Total and Permanent Disability (TPD) claims. The firm offers free no-obligation consultations and promotes no-win, no-fee representation for eligible compensation claims. Pros: Free no-obligation consultations and no-win, no-fee options Can assist with related compensation, TPD and superannuation matters Home visits may be available for seriously injured clients Cons: Broad personal injury focus may place less emphasis on car accident claims Clients should ask about the specific Queensland CTP experience of their assigned lawyer   4. Lifestyle Injury Lawyers Lifestyle Injury Lawyers is a Gold Coast-based compensation law practice that assists people injured in motor vehicle accidents. The firm handles CTP claims for eligible clients and offers a free assessment for people seeking early advice after a crash. The practice promotes a no-win, no-fee model and takes an integrated approach that combines compensation assistance with rehabilitation support. This may appeal to injured people managing treatment, recovery, and a legal claim at the same time. Pros: Gold Coast-based compensation law practice Advertises no-win, no-fee representation for eligible CTP claims Free assessments for potential motor vehicle accident claims Integrated treatment and rehabilitation-focused approach Cons: Clients should clarify whether they can choose their own treating practitioners The integrated care model may not be necessary for people seeking only legal claim management   5. Main Lawyers Main Lawyers provides Gold Coast legal advice for motor vehicle accident injuries and insurance disputes. The firm helps clients understand the early stages of a car accident compensation claim. The team offers free initial consultations, enabling injured people to discuss their circumstances before deciding whether to engage a lawyer. Pros: Free initial consultations for Gold Coast car accident matters Assistance with personal injury issues Suitable for clients dealing with accident-related legal concerns Cons: Broader insurance and personal injury focus rather than exclusive CTP specialisation Confirm whether medical-report costs and other disbursements are included in any fee arrangement   6. Ramsden Lawyers Ramsden Lawyers is a Gold Coast law firm that provides advice on compensation matters, including claims for people injured in car accidents. The firm offers a free initial consultation and can explain the process of making a claim against the CTP insurer of an at-fault vehicle. The team assists clients who have suffered injuries in road accidents and need guidance about compensation. Local access can help Gold Coast residents who prefer speaking with a lawyer in person. Pros: Gold Coast-based firm with compensation law services Free initial consultation for prospective clients Local option for people who prefer face-to-face appointments Cons: Compensation law is one part of a wider legal service offering Clients should confirm the experience of the lawyer assigned to their motor vehicle accident claim   7. Smith’s Lawyers Smith’s Lawyers is a Queensland personal injury firm servicing Gold Coast clients. It assists with car and road injury claims, workplace injuries, public liability claims and TPD matters. The firm promotes a “No Fee” arrangement and offers free initial advice for people considering a compensation claim. Its team can assist with insurer communication, claim documentation, evidence gathering and settlement negotiations. Smith’s Lawyers may suit clients seeking a personal injury-focused firm that can also assist if a car accident has affected their capacity to work or has triggered a potential TPD claim. Pros: Personal injury-focused practice with Gold Coast access Advertises a no-win, no-fee arrangement and free initial advice Assistance with insurer communication, evidence and settlement negotiations Cons: Clients needing broader legal services may need a separate law firm Ask exactly which disbursements are included under the no-win, no-fee agreement   8. Travis Schultz & Partners Travis Schultz & Partners is a Queensland compensation law firm with a Gold Coast office in Southport. The firm assists people pursuing personal injury claims arising from car accidents. The team offers free case reviews and no-win, no-fee arrangements for eligible matters. Its general compensation focus may help clients with mild injuries and claims involving financial loss. Pros: Dedicated Queensland compensation-law practice Gold Coast office in Southport Free case reviews and no-win, no-fee options Cons: Popular specialist practices may have variable appointment availability Clients should ask which lawyer will oversee their claim and who will be their usual contact   9. East Coast Injury Lawyers East Coast Injury Lawyers is a personal injury law firm servicing Gold Coast and Queensland clients. It assists people injured in motor vehicle accidents and offers free consultations to discuss the claims process. The firm promotes a no-win, no-fee guarantee and can assist with relevant documentation, accident information and the process of lodging a CTP claim. Pros: Personal injury-focused practice servicing the Gold Coast Free consultations and advertised no-win, no-fee representation Assistance with CTP claim documentation and road accident evidence Cons: Fewer locations than some larger Queensland and national firms Ask about after-hours contact options and expected communication frequency   10. Murphy’s Law Accident Lawyers Murphy’s Law Accident Lawyers provides Queensland personal injury advice for people injured in road accidents and matters involving medical negligence. The firm has a Gold Coast presence and offers free initial advice to help people understand their potential rights after an accident. The team promotes no-win, no-fee accident claim assistance and compensation options. Pros: Free initial advice for road accident and personal injury claims Advertises no-win, no-fee accident claim assistance Gold Coast access for local clients Can assist with several related types of personal injury matters Cons: Broader personal injury practice rather than an exclusively car accident-focused firm Confirm whether your claim will be managed by the Gold Coast team or another Queensland office   What To Expect During A Free Car Accident Lawyer Consultation Most Gold Coast car accident lawyers offer a free initial consultation. This appointment allows you to explain what happened, understand your potential options and decide whether the firm is a good fit before signing a costs agreement. During the consultation, the lawyer will usually ask about: The date, place and circumstances of the accident The vehicles and people involved Whether police attended or an incident report was made Your injuries, symptoms and medical treatment Time missed from work or changes to your ability to earn an income The at-fault vehicle’s registration and CTP insurer, if known Any communication you have received from an insurer The lawyer should explain whether you may have a claim, what evidence may be needed, the likely next steps and how legal costs will work. A free consultation does not usually oblige you to proceed with that firm.   How Long Do You Have To Make A Car Accident Claim In Queensland? Time limits for Queensland car accident claims can be strict. In many cases, a Notice of Accident Claim Form must be given to the relevant CTP insurer within nine months of the accident or within one month of first consulting a lawyer, whichever occurs earlier. Different rules may apply if the responsible vehicle cannot be identified, such as after a hit-and-run accident. In these matters, an earlier notice period may apply. Court proceedings generally need to begin within three years, although exceptions can exist depending on the circumstances. The safest approach is to seek legal advice as soon as possible after an accident. Early advice can help preserve evidence, identify the relevant insurer and avoid missing important deadlines.   What Can You Claim Compensation For? If you were injured in a car accident caused wholly or partly by another person, you may be able to make a CTP claim. The compensation available depends on the facts of the accident, the medical evidence, your recovery and the impact of the injury on your life. Depending on your situation, a claim may include compensation for: Medical, hospital and rehabilitation costs Past and future loss of income Reduced future earning capacity Pain and suffering Paid care and assistance Care provided by family members, where legal requirements are met Travel expenses associated with treatment Loss of enjoyment of life No lawyer can guarantee a compensation amount at the beginning of a claim. A realistic assessment should be based on evidence, including medical records, employment information and the circumstances of the accident.   How To Choose The Right Car Accident Lawyer The best car accident lawyer for you may not be the largest firm or the one with the loudest advertising. Consider the following factors before making a decision: Specialist accreditation: Ask whether a Queensland Law Society Accredited Specialist in Personal Injury Law will supervise your claim. Relevant experience: Choose a firm experienced with your type of accident, whether it involved a car, motorcycle, truck, pedestrian, cyclist, rideshare vehicle or unidentified driver. Fee transparency: Ask what the no-win, no-fee arrangement covers and whether you may be responsible for disbursements such as medical reports, expert evidence or court fees. File management: Find out who will handle your matter day to day and whether you can speak directly with the lawyer responsible for the claim. Communication: Ask how often you will receive updates and how quickly the firm normally responds to calls and emails. Convenience: Consider office location, online appointment availability and whether home or hospital visits are offered. Costs agreement: Read the entire agreement before signing. Ask for clarification in writing if any term is unclear.   Final Thoughts The right Gold Coast car accident lawyer should have relevant Queensland CTP experience, clearly explain costs and make you feel informed throughout the claims process. Use this list as a starting point, then speak with two or three firms before choosing representation. Comparing consultations can help you assess communication style, relevant experience and the practical details of each firm’s fee agreement. Most importantly, do not delay seeking advice after an accident. Prompt action can help you protect evidence, identify the correct insurer and understand the deadlines that may apply to your claim. //This content is provided by a third party The post Top 10 Car Accident Lawyers Gold Coast appeared first on Busselton .

title: Is It Time to Refinance? How an Australian Home Loan Broker Can Help You Find a Better Deal
author: busselton
content: I clearly remember the first time I really looked at my home loan after settling into my property. I’d been making repayments on autopilot, assuming that just because everything was running smoothly, there wasn’t much to think about. Then, I started wondering whether the loan I’d chosen years earlier was still the right fit. Interest rates had changed, my financial circumstances had shifted, and there were plenty of new loan options I hadn’t considered. It made me realise how easy it became to overlook one of the biggest financial commitments I’ve ever made. For me, that’s why checking my mortgage every few years makes sense. Sometimes, a closer look can reveal opportunities I didn’t even know were there. The Mortgage You Took Out Five Years Ago? It Might Not Fit Your Life Today A lot can change in five years. When I first took out my home loan, I was making decisions based on my current income and expenses, as well as the financial goals I had at the time. Fast forward a few years, and my circumstances might look completely different. Maybe (hopefully) my income has increased, or I’ve finally settled down and started a little family of my own (which, although it’s a gift, comes with so many extra expenses ), or perhaps I’ve gone ahead and built up equity in my property. That being said, even the smallest life changes, whether they’re the purposeful decisions we make to get closer to our goals, or unexpected plot twists that ambush us out of nowhere, can make us question whether that mortgage we signed up for years ago is still pulling its weight. Australia’s Mortgage Market Is Changing. Is Your Rate Keeping Up? Keeping an eye on your mortgage rate is a bit like checking the price of groceries. We might not notice small changes straight away, but they can really start to add up over time. Australia’s home loan market is constantly shifting, with lenders adjusting rates, introducing new products and competing for borrowers. That means the rate I locked in a few years ago might not look quite as attractive today. Despite that, it’s important not to get too distracted by a shiny headline rate. A loan that looks cheaper at first glance might come with higher fees or lack features we actually rely on, such as an offset account or redraw facility. That’s why comparing the bigger picture makes much more sense than chasing the lowest number. Doing a quick mortgage review, whether that’s on your own or with the help of a refinance home loan broker like the professionals at Orange Home Loans, can help work out whether your current loan is still competitive, or if it’s time to see what else is out there. What a Broker Sees When They Look at Your Home Loan Over time, I’ve realised that looking at my home loan on my own can be a little like trying to read a restaurant menu without my glasses. I can see the numbers, but I’m not always sure what I’m actually looking at. That’s where a mortgage broker can add some useful perspective. Rather than focusing only on my interest rate, a broker can look at the bigger picture, including my loan balance, repayments, income, expenses, existing debts, loan features and future goals. Thanks to their expertise, a broker can put my current mortgage under the microscope, compare it with what’s out there, and see if there’s a better match hiding in the fine print. When it comes to my home loan, ultimately, I’ve come to realise that like many other things in my life, it also deserves a little attention every now and then, rather than being left to quietly run in the background. Life changes, lender offers change, and the Aussie mortgage market certainly doesn’t sit still. That’s why regularly reviewing my home loan rate, fees, loan features, as well as my financial goals, can help me work out whether my current loan is still pulling its weight. After all, financial peace of mind isn’t about finding the perfect answer. It’s about being willing to ask whether that answer still fits the life I’m building. //SPONSORED CONTENT The post Is It Time to Refinance? How an Australian Home Loan Broker Can Help You Find a Better Deal appeared first on Busselton .

title: The Best Skincare Treatments of 2026
author: busselton
content: In 2026, the almost universally unattainable Glass Skin aesthetic is out . Skincare is entering a new era, where science-based treatments are replacing social media hype. Rather than blindly following TikTok trends and Instagram fads that would have us jump on the bandwagon of ‘viral’ products with questionable effectiveness, Australian skincare enthusiasts are becoming increasingly selective about the treatment recommendations they trust. Today, Australian beauty lovers are learning to understand our own skin types and what suits us best, embracing tailored treatments that help us each achieve our healthiest complexions yet. With advanced methodologies becoming ever-more accessible in Australia, we’re seeing a new wave of treatments hit our shores. But which are the best skincare treatments of 2026? Healthy Skin is The New Status Symbol Just like ‘ old money ’, healthy skin never goes out of style. In a bold beauty move that’s seeing us shift away from past ideals of heavily filtered faces, impossibly smooth cheeks and blurred complexions, today’s new status symbol is a healthy, glowing skin barrier that shines without full-coverage foundation. Of course, this shift towards naturally healthy-looking skin does mean that we are more reliant than ever before on science-backed skincare that delivers proven results. But with top-tier treatments becoming increasingly accessible, the question on every Australian’s lips is which facial rejuvenation ritual to invest in first. For many Australians, investing in our skin has become more than just a nice-to-have, and we’re seeing the true value of this investment. Skincare is now, for many of us, a non-negotiable step in our self-care routines, and the benefits pay off. A healthy skin barrier, increased collagen production, and higher skin cell regeneration are essential elements of a glowing complexion, helping us achieve that lit-from-within radiance many Australians are striving to attain today. And the best way to get that glow? Many of us are choosing to support our at-home skincare routines with expert application of advanced treatments, the likes of which are heralding a new era of skincare in Australia. Australian Skincare Has Entered a New Era Skincare treatments have come a long way from the days of cheap apricot face scrubs and detergent-like cleansers grabbed from supermarket shelves. These days, almost all of us have a dedicated skincare routine, and we’re leaning into a new era of advanced treatment methods to care for our complexions. Our skincare needs are becoming more complex, especially as we learn more about what it actually takes to care for our skin. Many of us are reaching for better quality skincare products to incorporate into our at-home routines. We’re also looking for ways to supplement our self-care, often outsourcing to skincare experts like aestheticians who deliver professional treatments that combine advanced technology with customised treatment plans. Enter: personalised skincare solutions tailored to our specific skin concerns, whether that’s pigmentation, acne scarring, fine lines, or uneven skin texture. But regardless of whether we would benefit most from laser resurfacing or more medical-grade procedures, there’s no doubt that these types of treatments are now more accessible than ever for many Australians. title: How Busselton Graduates Can Stand Out in a Competitive Job Market
author: busselton
content: Graduating from university is always an exciting milestone. However, entering the job market can feel daunting. That’s certainly the case in a regional area like Busselton. Employers are increasingly seeking candidates who are not only qualified but also proactive and professional. That means standing out from the crowd requires more than simply a degree. Fortunately, there are various practical strategies graduates can use to make a strong impression. Here’s how to secure the role you want. Build a Professional, Adaptive Resume Your resume is typically the first impression you’ll have on a potential employer. For Busselton graduates, it’s important to highlight your academic achievements. That’s clear. Yet there should also be a focus on work experience, internships, and volunteer roles when applicable. You should adapt each resume to the specific role you’re applying for, using keywords from job descriptions and emphasising skills relevant to the position. Yes, this requires more effort than simply firing out a load of cookie-cutter applications. It also makes your application stand out from the crowd. Develop Relevant Skills Through Internships and Volunteering As touched on in the previous section, it’s wise to demonstrate initiative through the likes of internships and volunteering . Not only does it add depth to your resume, but it also assists in gaining practical skills and expanding your network. Even short-term experiences in small businesses or local community organisations can supply valuable hands-on experience. Oh, and highlighting these experiences during interviews signals your commitment and adaptability, qualities highly prized in competitive job markets. Network Strategically Within the Region Networking is essential for regional graduates. To do this successfully, take the initiative and attend local business events and university career fairs whenever possible. Establishing relationships with professionals in your field can unlock doors to opportunities not advertised publicly. LinkedIn is also an effective tool for connecting with local and southwest professionals. Remember, even small interactions, like speaking to a local business owner about industry trends, can result in referrals or advice to give you a competitive edge. Present Yourself Professionally in Every Interaction Professionalism goes beyond your resume. Every interaction, from interviews to networking events, reflects on your personal brand. Think about dressing appropriately and communicating clearly. You should also demonstrate enthusiasm for the role and organisation. One practical tip for recent graduates is to keep polished, organised documentation. For example, having copies of certificates and a thesis bound neatly can convey attention to detail, as well as pride in your achievements. Thesis binding might seem like a small step. However, presenting your academic work professionally signals that you take quality seriously. That’s a trait employers notice. Showcase Your Digital Presence and Work Portfolio In today’s job market, you can significantly improve your chances of landing a role with a strong, professional online presence. Start by creating a LinkedIn profile that highlights your education, experience, and skills. If relevant, you should include an online portfolio showcasing projects and presentations. Employers increasingly use digital tools to screen candidates. Because of this, ensuring your online presence is professional and up to date can help you stand out. title: Kids race added to Cape to Cape
author: Nicky Lefebvre
content: Cape to Cape MTB, Australia’s largest and most popular mountain bike stage race is getting even bigger with the addition of Cape Kids, a kids ride and community event to start the 2025 edition, Wednesday 15 October in Margaret River. Taking place the day before the official start of the four day event, Cape Kids in the heart of Margaret River township will bring kids and the local community closer to the race than ever before. Designed to provide the local community an opportunity to get involved in the event and for kids of all ages the chance to ride on a closed course similar to Cape to Cape MTB. Held at Nippers Oval, the fun starts at 3.00pm before the kids ride rolls out from 4pm. To be as inclusive as possible, there will be rides for those under 10, 10-13 and 14+. All participants in Cape Kids will receive a C2C race plate to display proudly on their bikes and a participant medal. Beyond the event itself, Cape Kids is giving back to the South West community, with part proceeds supporting the Margaret River Off Road Cycling Association (MRORCA) who are long-time Cape to Cape MTB supporters through volunteering, trail building, and maintenance – and Perth Children’s Hospital Foundation (PCHF), which helps more than 10,000 children from regional WA access world-class care at Perth Children’s Hospital every year. As part of the festival some of the best mountain bikers in the country including defending champion and former Australian Champion Cameron Ivory, Oceania Mountain Bike Marathon Champion Brent Rees, former winner Izzy Flint, 2025 Australian Champion Sam Fox and local rising star Connor Wright, will be on hand with advice and to inspire a new generation of mountain bikers. “The South West and Margeret River have been supporters and hosts of Cape to Cape MTB for close to 20 years and the launch of Cape Kids will bring the local community even closer to the event,” Cape to Cape MTB Co-owner and Race Director Bill Hayes said. “Cape to Cape MTB has always been a community event and we know there are lots of kids out on the trails and we wanted to provide an opportunity for them to join in with the event. We hope to see many of them go on to ride the event in the coming years. “Having some of Australia’s best mountain bikers there to chat and sign autographs is sure to inspire the next generation and encourage more people to get out on the trails in a beautiful part of the world with some of the best trails around. “We are proud Cape Kids will further support the local MTB community and MRORCA and Perth Children’s Hospital Foundation with the important work they do.” Shire of Augusta Margaret River President Julia Jean-Rice said the event would be a great way to start the Cape to Cape MTB. “Mountain biking is part of our identity – from our unique trails to the passionate riders who call this place home,” she said. “The new kids-focused event in the heart of Margaret River will give children the chance to be a part of this iconic event, while also creating a welcoming space for families to connect, participate, and celebrate the sport and the outdoor lifestyle we all love. “Events like these build community, inspire healthy lifestyles, and ensure our major events continue to grow in ways that benefit everyone.” Perth Children’s Hospital Foundation CEO Carrick Robinson said, “We’re honoured to team up with Cape to Cape MTB, an iconic WA race that shares the Foundation’s unwavering commitment to pushing for the very best for our state and its people. “The launch of the inaugural Cape Kids race makes this partnership even more meaningful considering the growing number of South West children who rely on PCH each year for specialist care. “By riding and raising funds, participants will make a direct impact on the lives of WA’s sickest kids. From Margaret River to Broome, whenever a child needs expert paediatric care, it’s PCH that families turn to – WA’s leading centre for excellence in children’s health.” Entries for the Kids Ride are open at capetocapemtb.com The post Kids race added to Cape to Cape appeared first on Busselton .

title: Observatory closed for essential upgrades
author: Edward Scown
content: Busselton Jetty has announced its Underwater Observatory (UWO) will be closed from Monday, 28 July to Friday, 5 September to undergo a major accessibility-focused upgrade, including the installation of a brand-new lift system. Operations Manager Amy Gornall said the upgrades were “more than a maintenance project”. “We’re ensuring the Busselton Jetty experience continues to evolve and remain accessible to everyone for generations to come.” After more than two decades of service, the current lift will be replaced to ensure all visitors – regardless of mobility – can safely access the Observatory’s immersive seafloor experience. While the UWO is closed, the Jetty team is encouraging visitors to explore the newly launched Discovery Express, a bundled experience which includes a return trip on the Rio Tinto Solar Express Train and entry to the Marine Discovery Centre (MDC). “The MDC is a fully interactive, all weather, family-friendly exhibit space offering hands-on marine science and storytelling about the ocean’s wonders.” The lift installation is expected to take up to six weeks, but a Jetty spokesperson said progress will be monitored closely, and the UWO will be reopened earlier if possible. “UWO bookings have been temporarily paused to allow the project to proceed smoothly, though guests booking the Return Train during this time can register their interest in UWO should an early reopening occur.” Progress updates will be made through the Busselton Jetty’s social media channels. For more info or to book visit www.busseltonjetty.com.au The post Observatory closed for essential upgrades appeared first on Busselton .

title: ‘Over 60, still surfing strong’: Wain wins again
author: Edward Scown
content: Yallingup’s Richard Wain has claimed the Over-60 Men’s SUP title at the 2025 WA SUP Championships, held in Geraldton over the weekend. Competitors from across WA took on solid 2 to 3 foot surf in the battle for coveted State Titles and qualification spots for the 2025 Australian SUP Titles to be held at Phillip Island in October. Wain narrowly defeated Tim Calder (Exmouth), who later returned the favour by winning the Over-60 Men’s 9ft SUP, after locking in an excellent 8.00 in the dying minutes. “Over 60 and still surfing strong, that says it all,” Wain said after the win. “It’s just insanely good that we’ve still got guys surfing at a good level so to come away with the win, justifies all the effort and time put into the sport. “It’s incredibly competitive, but also a laugh and a celebration of the sport. “The older we get, the more we value weekends like these.” Meanwhile, Calder said it was nice to finish on a high note. “I used to live in Dunsborough and surf with Richard nearly every day, so I’ve known him for 30 years. He goes hard, he’s got his head in the game,” he laughed. The post ‘Over 60, still surfing strong’: Wain wins again appeared first on Busselton .

title: Sport and inclusion expert takes on role
author: Edward Scown
content: The City of Busselton’s new Sports Inclusion Coach says she is looking forward to driving greater inclusivity in local sport and promoting accessible and inclusive sporting opportunities across the community. Gemma Harrison was appointed to the role after the City partnered with Sport4All in 2024, in a jointly funded three year agreement to ensure everyone can enjoy the benefits of sport. The award-winning national program was brought to life through a collaboration between the Australian Government, the Australian Sports Commission and the former Australian of the year, Dylan Alcott AO’s consultancy, Get Skilled Access. “This role is an incredibly powerful opportunity that combines my two greatest professional passions – sport and inclusion,” Gemma said. “Collaboratively we can make a real difference by removing barriers and building a welcoming, inclusive environment for all.” Boasting a distinguished career in national and state-level sport development, including time at the Australian Sports Commission and the WA Football Commission, Gemma’s background as a registered teacher and work in the disability sector underscores her passion for inclusive learning environments. She is also a proud beach-lover, surfer, jet skier and hockey player, often spotted enjoying life with her partner, two children and two spirited dachshunds. “We’re truly excited to have Gemma onboard,” Mayor Phill Cronin said. “Through the Sport4All initiative, Gemma will lead efforts to provide resources, guidance and training that embraces diversity and creates opportunities for people with disability to participate and thrive.” The City said it would host an Inclusion Forum later this year, in collaboration with Sport4All, and local and state organisations. To get involved visit www.busselton.wa.gov.au The post Sport and inclusion expert takes on role appeared first on Busselton .

title: City of Busselton chief announces resignation
author: Edward Scown
content: City of Busselton Chief Executive Officer Tony Nottle announced his resignation on Monday, saying he planned to focus on interests outside of local government. Promoted from the position of Director Finance and Corporate Services in 2022, Mr Nottle said it had been “a real privilege” to take on the role. Mayor Phill Cronin said Council would discuss Acting CEO arrangements and commence recruitment for a permanent chief executive. “Tony has been on the journey with us at a senior level for many years and has been instrumental in delivery of a range of successful projects and initiatives,” he said. “As CEO, Tony has successfully led the organisation through a period of change, including recruitment of a new Executive Leadership Team following a major realignment of organisational portfolios. “He has consistently provided strong support and guidance to the Council on strategic and governance matters, and we have all appreciated his dedication and commitment… On behalf of the Elected Members, I wish Tony and his family all the very best for the future and their next chapter.” The post City of Busselton chief announces resignation appeared first on Busselton .

title: Airport artwork tells story of culture and country
author: Edward Scown
content: A new artwork at the Busselton Margaret River Airport is giving passengers leaving the region a fond farewell with a touch of local culture. Unveiled last week at the Busselton Margaret River Airport’s Departures Terminal, the Aboriginal artwork is the result of a collaborative project made possible through $50,000 in funding from Tourism WA, under Jina- Western Australia’s Aboriginal Tourism Action Plan. Named ‘Keyap Boodja’ Water Country , the final piece showcases modern contemporary Noongar artist, Melissa Riley and Project Manager, Sam Tago, whose design reflects the region’s cultural richness and deep connection to water and land. Four respected Aboriginal women – Sandra Hill, Amanda Bell, Tahn Donovan and Thelma Harris – oversaw the selection of the piece. “I am truly privileged to be given this opportunity to express my culture through art,” Melissa Riley said. “My artwork allows me to continue to tell stories being passed down to me from my family.” She said her interpretation of ‘Keyap Boodja’ gave her the chance to have her story shared by people far and wide. “Reflecting nature in my works is an important reminder that we are obligated to share and care for nature as it continues to provide for us in many ways. “The opportunity to showcase my artwork will keep our stories alive.” The City of Busselton worked with the Karri Karrak Aboriginal Corporation to ensure the project remained “culturally respectful and community-driven”. “This artwork marks a significant moment in the City’s ongoing journey of reconciliation, recognising the strong connection between Aboriginal culture and Country,” Mayor Phill Cronin said. “We are proud to have been able to unveil this incredible mural as we continue to walk together and achieve projects we can be proud of, in line with our Reconciliation Action Plan. “This piece doesn’t just brighten the airport space, it tells a story,” he said. “It represents our deep ties to Country and culture and leaves a lasting impression on both locals and visitors alike. “This project is a testament to what can be achieved collaboratively and I applaud all those involved.” The post Airport artwork tells story of culture and country appeared first on Busselton .

title: Busselton marks 70 years with win over Lions
author: busselton
content: Busselton celebrated their 70th anniversary after defeating Harvey Brunswick Leschenault at Sir Stewart Bovell Park on Saturday afternoon, in the opening game of round sixteen. The match was supposed to be played in heavy rain, but it never rained all day, with a healthy crowd watching the top five contest. Busselton started strong, kicking the opening three goals of the match, with Jozef Parkinson kicking the opening major after four minutes, followed by a goal to Ethan Bowman and Ryan Ekert, who marked strongly all day. Parkinson on the run. Images by Sharyn Newlands. The Lions started to get back into the contest, but kicked four behinds, and as is always the way, the ball went to the other end, landed in the hands of Ben Ganzer, who kicked the Magpies fourth goal. Taine Williams kicked the Lions opening goal after the quarter time siren with Busselton leading by three goals. Ekert and Aidan Austen started to dominate in the forward line, both kicking goals early in the the second quarter to open at thirty three point lead. Goals to John Manuel and Taine Williams mid quarter narrowed the margin, but a late goal to Tony Notte gave the home side a 29 point lead at half time. The Magpies blew the game open in the third term kicking three consecutive goals to lead by a game high forty four points. Busselton took down HBL on Saturday, in front of a healthy hometown crowd. Images by Sharyn Newlands. Some individual brilliance from Jarrod Humphries who snapped a goal from 40m gave the Lions their only goal of the term. Images by Sharyn Newlands. Busselton dominated scoring and possession in the final term, restricting the Lions to one goal kicked by Cruz McCagh. Ryan Ekert put an explanation mark on the contest when he kicked his fifth, with the final margin 57 points. Ben Ganzer and Tony Notte played well for Busselton, while Ekert’s five goals was also impressive. The win sets up a top of the table showdown with South Bunbury at Hands Oval, while the Lions now fall into the clutches of Donnybrook and Carey Park, and will face Dunsborough, in Dunsborough next Sunday. title: UP economist questions purpose of BIR’s QR registration badge
author: Newsbytes.PH
content: University of the Philippines economics professor Cielo Magno has questioned the purpose of the Bureau of Internal Revenue’s (BIR) mandatory QR-coded Registration Seal Badge, arguing that the requirement adds administrative burdens without clear evidence that it would improve tax compliance or revenue collection. Magno welcomed the BIR’s decision to suspend the requirement under Revenue Memorandum Circular (RMC) No. 38-2026 until further notice, but said the policy lacked a clearly established public benefit. “I support efforts to broaden the tax base, improve tax compliance, and ensure that businesses and individuals earning income through digital platforms pay the correct taxes. But regulations should serve a clear public purpose, and their benefits should justify the costs they impose on taxpayers,” said Magno, a former undersecretary of the Department of Budget and Management. She argued that verifying taxpayer registration does not necessarily establish compliance with tax obligations, noting that the BIR already maintains registration records and has mechanisms to verify taxpayer status. Electronic marketplaces and digital financial service providers are also subject to withholding and information-reporting requirements for certain transactions, she added. “What additional tax administration problem does mandatory public posting solve? What evidence is there that it will improve revenue collection?” said Magno, who has also announced her intention to run as senator in the 2028 elections. Without clear answers, she warned that the requirement could add another layer of bureaucracy rather than improve tax administration. Magno also raised concerns that additional administrative requirements, uncertainty, and potential penalties could discourage microentrepreneurs, freelancers, and content creators from registering their businesses, particularly those with modest or irregular incomes. “Instead of encouraging people to enter the formal economy, we risk giving them more reasons to remain outside it,” she said. Sen. Bam Aquino also welcomed the suspension, calling on the BIR to continue listening to taxpayers and ease the burden of doing business, particularly for small entrepreneurs and online sellers. “ Maraming salamat, BIR, s a pagsuspinde ng Registration Seal Badge. Patuloy nating pakinggan ang hinaing ng ating kababayan at pagaanin ang pagnenegosyo, lalo na para sa maliliit na negosyant e, content creator, at online seller,” Aquino said. Magno’s criticism comes as the Philippine economy faces slower growth. Gross domestic product expanded by 2.3% in the second quarter of 2026, while the digital economy contributed P2.74 trillion, equivalent to 9.8% of GDP, in 2025. Magno said the government should reduce unnecessary barriers to entrepreneurship and economic activity rather than introduce requirements whose economic and fiscal benefits have not been established. She also flagged privacy and taxpayer-protection concerns, saying publicly accessible verification systems should not expose personal information unnecessarily. Although replacing the public display of the full Certificate of Registration with a badge was an improvement, unclear rules and inconsistent enforcement could create opportunities for harassment, arbitrary penalties, and extortion, she said. Magno further questioned the imposition of penalties for noncompliance when the relationship between displaying the badge and paying the correct taxes had not been established. “We should not impose additional obligations on taxpayers merely because technology makes them possible. Digitalization must solve problems, not create new ones,” she said. She said tax administration should instead be assessed through measurable outcomes, including increased voluntary registration, accurate income reporting, improved revenue collection, lower compliance costs, and greater taxpayer trust. “Displaying QR codes online does not improve tax administration,” Magno said. title: Groups urge balance between child online safety and digital rights
author: Jinji Quiambao
content: Two proposed measures to protect Filipino children online should adopt risk-based safeguards without unnecessarily restricting privacy, freedom of expression, and access to digital services, according to a law firm and a digital advocacy group. Gorriceta Africa Cauton & Saavedra and GoDigital Philippines raised the concerns during a policy forum on Oct. 22 at Manila House in Taguig City, where government officials, technology industry representatives, and legal experts discussed two pending measures: House Bill No. 11566, or the Safe Kids Act, and Senate Bill No. 2424, or the Smart Kids Act. The proposed bills seek to address risks faced by minors in digital environments, including questions about age restrictions, platform accountability, regulatory enforcement, and access to online services. The groups said safeguards should reflect how children actually use digital platforms rather than impose broad restrictions that could limit legitimate online activities. They also called for age-verification mechanisms that do not unnecessarily intrude on privacy, as well as proportionate restrictions that protect children without limiting access to information or creating unnecessary barriers to the Philippine digital market. The responsibilities of technology companies, their compliance obligations, and the enforcement of new requirements should also be clearly defined, they said. Stakeholders should be given sufficient time to adjust to new regulations. Mark S. Gorriceta, managing partner of Gorriceta Africa Cauton & Saavedra and chairman of GoDigital Philippines, said legislation should consider how safeguards would work in practice and their potential effects on users’ rights. “Protecting children online is a responsibility we all share. But effective legislation requires careful consideration of how safeguards will work in practice, who will be responsible for implementing them, and how we can protect children without unnecessarily restricting freedom of expression, privacy, and access to information. The goal should be policies that are clear, proportionate, and workable,” Gorriceta said. In a separate presentation examining the proposed measures, Gorriceta also stressed that legislation alone would not guarantee effective implementation. “A simple law is not the same as effective enforcement, and age limits raise freedom-of-speech and information issues. Process matters as much as policy,” he said. The presentation identified risk-based age restrictions, privacy safeguards, proportionate regulation, and sufficient implementation time as key considerations in developing child online safety rules. CICC executive director Aboy Paraiso The forum also featured Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) executive director and undersecretary Renato “Aboy” Paraiso, who delivered the government’s perspective on cybersecurity, cybercrime prevention, and the protection of Internet users. Meanwhile, Kankan Ramos, chief operating officer of InvictusPH, presented an industry perspective on the proposed legislation and its potential implications for digital services. The event concluded with an open forum involving Gorriceta lawyers Micaela Kristina V. Galvez and Luis Teodoro B. Pascua where participants discussed legal, regulatory, and operational concerns surrounding the bills. title: BIR suspends online registration seal badge requirement
author: Newsbytes.PH
content: The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) suspended on Monday, Oct. 26, the mandatory online posting of its Registration Seal Badge until further notice, following data privacy concerns raised by online sellers, content creators, and lawmakers. Revenue Memorandum Circular (RMC) No. 113-2026, dated Oct. 26, also suspends the Oct. 31 compliance deadline. The circular covers the requirement introduced under RMC No. 38-2026 and supplemented by RMC Nos. 64-2026 and 99-2026. BIR commissioner Charlito Martin R. Mendoza said the suspension would allow the agency to review the implementation of the requirement and address privacy and technical concerns. “When BIR issued RMC 38-2026 last April 29, 2026, the Seal Badge was introduced as an alternative to posting the full Certificate of Registration (COR) online, as required under Revenue Regulations Nos. 7-2024 and 15-2024, issued pursuant to the Ease of Paying Taxes Act,” Mendoza said in a statement. “We recognize that protecting personal information online presents different and more complex challenges than displaying a COR at a physical business establishment.” The BIR said it will work with the National Privacy Commission (NPC) and consult affected taxpayers and other stakeholders as it reviews the requirement. Taxpayers who have already obtained their Registration Seal Badges may continue displaying them voluntarily. No penalties will be imposed solely for failure to display the badge while the suspension is in effect. The circular does not set a new compliance deadline. The suspension follows calls from Senators Bam Aquino and Pia Cayetano for the BIR to pause the requirement ahead of the Oct. 31 deadline. Aquino has urged the agency to defer implementation and listen to concerns from online sellers and content creators. “ Hiling natin sa BIR: ipagpaliban muna ang Registration Seal Badge requirement. P akinggan muna natin ang hinaing ng mga online sellers at content creators,” Aquino said. Cayetano raised concerns that the badge’s embedded QR code could expose personal information, including taxpayers’ full legal names. She said she had brought the issue to the NPC and called for the agencies concerned to resolve the data protection issues before the deadline. Under RMC No. 38-2026, the badge was introduced as an alternative to publicly displaying a full Certificate of Registration on websites, e-commerce platforms, and business-related social media accounts. The measure covers online sellers, e-commerce merchants, digital service providers, freelancers, vloggers, content creators, and influencers. The BIR had previously extended the deadline to Oct. 31 under RMC No. 99-2026. The badge was intended to allow customers and other parties to verify a taxpayer’s registration through a QR code without requiring the full registration document to be posted publicly. However, concerns emerged over the personal information that could be accessed through the verification system. title: Digital channels dominate overseas remittances to PH — study
author: Jinji Quiambao
content: Digital banking and mobile wallets are becoming common channels for international money transfers among Filipinos, but high fees and security concerns continue to affect adoption, according to Visa’s Money Travels 2026 report. The study found that 45% of Filipino respondents received money from overseas in the past 12 months, the highest proportion among six Asia-Pacific markets surveyed. About 72% of respondents said they send or receive money internationally several times a year, while 35% do so at least monthly. Remittances primarily support household expenses, with 34% citing daily necessities as a reason for international transfers. Other reasons included family obligations (33%), holiday gifts (30%), and emergency expenses (25%). The United States accounted for 36% of inbound remittance activity reported by respondents, followed by Canada at 13%, Australia at 9%, Saudi Arabia at 8%, and Japan at 7%. Online banking and bank mobile apps were the most commonly used channels, accounting for 44% of reported transfers. Mobile wallets and remittance apps each accounted for 28%, while 19% of respondents used physical money transfer agents or stores. Speed was a key factor in choosing digital services. Among mobile wallet users, 44% reported near-instant access to transferred funds, compared with 31% of those using direct bank transfers and 18% of those making in-person transactions. However, 37% cited high fees as a problem with digital transfers. Technical difficulties and exchange rate issues were each reported by 15% of respondents. The report also found that awareness of stablecoins is growing in the Philippines, although actual use remains limited. Stablecoins are cryptocurrencies designed to maintain a relatively stable value against an asset such as the US dollar. About 42% of Filipino respondents said they had heard of stablecoins, but only 2% of remittance users had used them. Trust levels remained significantly lower for stablecoin transfers than for conventional methods. Only 38% expressed trust in stablecoin transfers, compared with 81% for cash remittances and 79% for digital remittances. Another 79% said they wanted more education on how stablecoins work. Visa is expanding its money movement services through Visa Direct and developing stablecoin-based payment capabilities to address delays in conventional cross-border transfers. Visa Direct allows banks, fintech firms, and businesses to send funds to cards, bank accounts, and digital wallets across more than 195 countries and territories. The service supports over 150 currencies and 18 billion endpoints worldwide, according to the company. Visa is also developing a system that would allow businesses to use stablecoins instead of traditional currencies to pre-fund Visa Direct payouts. The company said the approach could make funds available within minutes rather than days. Other initiatives include near-instant stablecoin payouts for consumers, freelancers, and content creators, as well as seven-day settlement capabilities for banks and fintech firms. Visa launched stablecoin settlement in the United States in 2025 after earlier pilot programs. The company has not specified a rollout schedule for the Philippines. Visa Philippines country manager Jeffrey Navarro said the company would continue working with regulators, banks, and fintech partners to improve the speed, security, and accessibility of money transfers. The study, conducted by Morning Consult, surveyed more than 45,000 respondents across 20 markets, including 3,101 adults in the Philippines. title: Report: Pinoys warm to AI customer service but demand transparency
author: Jinji Quiambao
content: Filipino consumers are becoming more receptive to artificial intelligence (AI) in customer service, with 64% reporting a more positive attitude toward the technology than two years ago, according to a Genesys report. The figure exceeds the Asia-Pacific (APAC) average of 56% and the global average of 50%, based on the latest “State of Customer Experience” report. Among Filipino respondents whose attitudes toward AI improved, 35% attributed the change to positive experiences with AI-powered customer service. However, poor service continues to affect consumer spending and business loyalty. The report found that 91% of Filipino consumers had reduced their spending or stopped doing business with a company because of unsatisfactory customer service, compared with 86% across Asia Pacific. The findings suggest that while consumers are increasingly willing to use AI, businesses still need to deliver satisfactory service to retain customers. About 84% of Filipino respondents expect AI to improve customer service quality and speed over the next two to three years. Another 78% said they do not mind whether a human agent or AI resolves their concerns, provided the issue is addressed quickly and completely. Meanwhile, 73% said virtual agents or chatbots have made it easier to resolve issues independently. Despite growing acceptance, consumers want greater transparency about the use of AI and how their information is handled. Nearly all Filipino respondents, or 98%, said they want to know when they are interacting with AI, while 62% believe companies should disclose AI-powered interactions. The report also found that 58% want greater control over their personal data, while only 45% are comfortable allowing AI to make decisions on their behalf. Personalized service remains another factor influencing customer loyalty. If assured of personalized experiences, 91% of Filipino respondents said they would likely recommend a company, 87% would make repeat purchases, and 85% would buy additional products or services. On the business side, 62% of Philippine customer experience (CX) leaders plan to deploy AI-powered tools to assist employees over the next two years. This compares with 55% across APAC and 47% globally. Philippine organizations also expect to allocate an average of 32% of their CX budgets to AI-powered technologies over the next 12 months. Meanwhile, 49% of local CX leaders expect agentic or semi-autonomous AI to play a greater role in managing customer experiences. However, only 37% anticipate autonomous AI agents performing this function within three years. “Customers increasingly expect organizations to understand their needs, maintain context and deliver seamless, personalized experiences,” said Mao Gen Foo, vice president for Genesys Asia. “For businesses, the opportunity is to move beyond isolated AI automation toward agentic orchestration – coordinating AI, people, data and systems around customer intent,” he added. The report surveyed 5,811 consumers and 1,560 CX and business leaders across more than 20 countries, including the Philippines, in March and April 2026. title: Cybersecurity summit spotlights public-private push vs digital threats
author: Newsbytes.PH
content: I AM SECURE 2026 wrapped up its ISOGx Season 4 Conference, Cybersecurity Soluation Pitch and Exhibition on October 1 at SMX Convention Center Aura in Bonifacio Global City, Taguig, drawing cybersecurity executives, government officials,    The event, themed “Soaring High: Future-Ready in the Age of Intelligent Threats,” centered on strengthening public-private alliances and advancing practical, scalable cybersecurity strategies. ISOG president Chito Jacinto cited Philippine Statistics Authority data showing about 24.28 million Filipino ICT-device users experienced at least one cybersecurity incident in 2024, with only 1.9 percent reporting incidents to authorities. He also pointed to the World Economic Forum’s Global Cybersecurity Outlook 2026, which identified artificial intelligence as a major driver of cybersecurity transformation and stressed preparations for longer-term developments including quantum computing. Jacinto underscored shared responsibility among government, enterprise, technology providers and cybersecurity professionals in protecting the country’s digital infrastructure. ISOG vice president Alvin Punsalan reaffirmed the organization’s mission to develop information security professionals through continuous learning, knowledge exchange, mentorship and industry collaboration. The executive panel “A Unified Front: Securing the Nation Against Evolving Cyber Threats” featured Jacinto; Usec. Rodil Aniban, Officer-in-Charge of the Office of the Undersecretary for Cybersecurity at the Department of Information and Communications Technology; Rojun Valaquio Hosillos, Director IV of the Cybercrime Investigation Office at the Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center; and PLT Justin Butz Fetalino, Chief of the Information and Communications Technology Management Section at the Philippine National Police Anti-Cybercrime Group. Moderated by Patricia Bermudez-Hizon, it focused on cross-sector coordination, cyber defense readiness and collective responses to emerging digital threats. The Cybersecurity Solution Pitch, themed “Securing Digital Ecosystems Through Scalable and Practical Cybersecurity Solutions,” featured plenary presentations from F5 through Westcon, Rapid7, NMI, ViewQwest, Infoblox, Sophos through WSI, Datadog through Netsec, TrendAI through VST-ECS, Forcepoint, Exabeam, Varonis through Westcon, Fortinet through VST-ECS and Arcon. Gold breakout sessions featured Gigamon through MSecurity and MEC, Menlo through Netsec and VST-ECS, Abnormal AI through Netsec and BeyondTrust through Westcon, with Cyble through ABPSecurite as exhibitor. The Cyber Caravan gathered representatives of the defense sector, law enforcement, government cybersecurity agencies and professional organizations, with presenters from the Armed Forces of the Philippines, PNP-ACG, the National Computer Emergency Response Team under the DICT Cybersecurity Bureau, Pag-IBIG Fund, the Cybersecurity Council of the Philippines, ISACA Manila Chapter and the ACFE Philippines Chapter. In her closing remarks, XMS Chief Executive Officer Xialeemar Valdeavilla, I AM SECURE’s strategic partner, reflected on the platform’s eight-year journey since 2018, saying “a successful business event becomes a platform for an industry” of connecting cybersecurity professionals, government agencies, technology companies and business leaders. title: Dongfeng rolls out electric SUV in PH at P1.398 million
author: Newsbytes.PH
content: Dongfeng Motors Philippines has launched the Mage EV, an electric SUV with a claimed driving range of 530 kilometers, priced at P1.398 million. The 530-kilometer range and P1.398-million price are key selling points for buyers considering an electric SUV. Actual range and charging times may vary depending on driving conditions, battery state, and charging equipment. The launch was attended by representatives of Dongfeng Motors Philippines and Tara Global Technology, along with automotive media and other industry stakeholders. The Mage EV joins Dongfeng’s Philippine lineup of electrified and fuel-efficient vehicles, which includes the Vigo EV, Nammi EV, and Huge Hybrid. title: Social engineering drives 39% of PH banking fraud — BPI
author: Jinji Quiambao
content: Social engineering scams account for 39% of fraudulent transactions and 36% of fraud-related losses in the Philippine banking industry, with fraudsters increasingly relying on deception to trick customers into transferring money or revealing sensitive information, according to the Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI). Citing year-to-date industry data during Cybersecurity Awareness Month 2026, BPI said voice phishing, or vishing, accounted for 21.3% of reported fraud incidents. Malware and rogue applications represented 7.5%, followed by SMS phishing, or smishing, at 3%, and email phishing at 2%. The figures point to the growing use of social engineering, in which scammers impersonate legitimate institutions or create a sense of urgency to persuade victims to disclose confidential information or authorize financial transactions. BPI also flagged so-called authorized scams, in which victims are manipulated into transferring money themselves. Impersonation scams accounted for 10.3% of reported incidents, followed by investment scams at 2.7% and romance scams at 0.6%. Emerging threats include artificial intelligence-assisted scams, deepfake impersonation, synthetic identities, and targeted fraud that uses personal information to make fraudulent communications more convincing. The risks come as more Filipinos conduct banking transactions digitally. BPI has 10 million digital banking users, and more than half of its retail payment transactions are conducted through digital channels. Its platforms have facilitated more than 377 million transactions. BPI said it is strengthening fraud monitoring, authentication, and account protection through additional security technologies. One measure is Mobile Key Authentication, which replaces SMS-based one-time passwords with authentication tied to a trusted device and secured by a PIN or biometric verification. The BPI app also imposes mandatory cool-off periods for certain high-risk account changes, giving customers time to identify and report potentially unauthorized activity. Other safeguards include integrity checks that restrict access from rooted devices and certain VPN-enabled environments, as well as masked recipient names for transfers between BPI accounts. The bank also warned customers against installing malicious Android application packages, or APKs, disguised as delivery notifications, government forms, and promotional offers. Lost or stolen phones pose another risk because physical SIM cards can be transferred to other devices to intercept authentication codes. BPI advised customers to enable SIM locks, consider switching to eSIMs, and secure their phones with strong passcodes and biometric authentication. The bank is also working with the Philippine National Police Anti-Cybercrime Group and the Department of Information and Communications Technology on cybersecurity awareness and efforts to combat online fraud. BPI said it is implementing safeguards under Republic Act No. 12010, or the Anti-Financial Account Scamming Act, which addresses financial account scams and related offenses. “Cybersecurity is not about responding to threats after they happen. It requires financial institutions to anticipate risks, continuously strengthen their defenses, and work together with the broader ecosystem to address fraud,” said Jon Paz, BPI head of enterprise information security and fraud risk management. title: Asia loses $136.5 billion to scams, study finds
author: Edu Lopez
content: An estimated $136.5 billion was lost to scams across Asia, with 71% of adults surveyed reporting exposure to fraud in the past year, according to a new regional study by the Global Anti-Scam Alliance (GASA) and Gogolook, the developer of caller identification app Whoscall. The “State of Scams in Asia 2026” report surveyed 17,460 adults across 13 Asian markets and found that 62% of respondents who encountered a scam interacted with it. Of those who engaged with scammers, 26% suffered financial losses. Among victims who lost money, 51% said they had been scammed more than once. Phone calls were the most common channel through which respondents encountered scams, cited by 56%, followed by text messages at 50% and instant messaging apps at 40%. Shopping fraud, investment schemes, and fake employment offers were among the most common types of scams. Although 66% of respondents said they were confident they could recognize scams, many still interacted with suspicious communications. “One of the most striking findings is the gap between confidence and behavior,” said Brian D. Hanley, director of GASA’s Asia-Pacific chapter. “This shows why education is important but cannot be our only line of defense. We also need stronger safeguards that protect people throughout the scam journey.” The impact of scams extended beyond financial losses. Among respondents who lost money, 77% experienced at least one emotional impact, 72% reported negative effects on their mental well-being, and 58% said the losses disrupted their everyday finances. Despite 85% of victims reporting their experiences, recovery and reimbursement remained difficult and inconsistent, the report found. The study also identified growing challenges for telecommunications providers as scammers adapt to security measures such as SIM registration and identity verification. “Phone and text message scams remain a major challenge across Asia. In Thailand, Malaysia, Vietnam, and Indonesia, more than six in ten respondents encountered scam calls,” said Jeff Kuo, CEO of Gogolook. “As scammers use AI-generated voices and increasingly convincing scripts, identifying suspicious numbers and warning users before they engage becomes even more important. Whoscall’s observations also suggest that scammers are adapting to tighter SIM registration and identity checks by using international and satellite numbers, making continued cross-market information sharing essential.” The survey found substantial public support for measures that would allow financial institutions and technology providers to intervene before victims lose money. About 71% of respondents supported allowing banks to block high-value transactions without prior customer permission when fraud is suspected. Another 69% backed empowering telecommunications operators and messaging apps to block malicious calls and messages proactively. title: Senators seek BIR pause on registration badge over privacy concerns
author: Newsbytes.PH
content: Senators Bam Aquino and Pia Cayetano have called on the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) to address data privacy concerns raised by online sellers and digital content creators over its registration seal badge requirement ahead of the Oct. 31, 2026 compliance deadline. Aquino urged the BIR to defer implementation while authorities review complaints from affected sellers and creators. “ Hiling natin sa BIR: ipagpaliban muna ang Registration Seal Badge requirement. Pakinggan muna natin ang hinaing ng mga online sellers at content creators,” Aquino said. Cayetano said online sellers and digital content creators were concerned that the badge’s embedded QR code could expose personal information, including their full legal names. She said she had brought the issue to the National Privacy Commission (NPC), whose budget she is handling in the Senate. “Given the October 31, 2026 implementation date, I trust that the concerned agencies can work together to immediately address and resolve the data protection concerns raised by our online sellers and influencers, balancing tax compliance with individual privacy,” Cayetano said. Under Revenue Memorandum Circular No. 38-2026, the BIR Registration Seal Badge is required for online sellers, e-commerce merchants, digital service providers, freelancers, vloggers, content creators, and influencers. The badge replaces the need to publicly display a full Certificate of Registration (COR) online, which contains tax registration details. The measure is intended to limit the public exposure of sensitive tax information while allowing businesses and individuals to display proof of BIR registration. The compliance deadline has been extended to Oct. 31, 2026. Generating the badge is free. However, taxpayers who need to update their registration details online must pay a P30 documentary stamp tax (DST), according to published guidance on the requirement.
