title: BU’s AI leaders weigh in on Healey’s AI regulations as lawmakers debate bill
author: By Nate Williams
content: A Massachusetts economic development bill, which could set precedent for artificial intelligence regulation, sits before a legislative committee for reconciliation after differing versions were passed by the state House and Senate. The Center for Computing and Data Sciences at Boston University. A bill proposed by Gov. Healey would require major AI models to get evaluated by third parties at least three times a year. (EMERSON LIHN/ DFP PHOTOGRAPHER) In September, Gov. Maura Healey called on the state legislature to require independent evaluations of the most powerful AI models under the Mass Wins Act . Major AI developers, like OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta, would be required to pay independent experts to evaluate their models at least three times a year for risks of catastrophic harm. If enacted, Massachusetts will be the first state to allow third parties to look into the technology. States like California, Illinois and New York only require AI developers to publish their own plan for managing catastrophic risks. Junior Denali Schlesinger, president of Boston University’s AI Society, said Healey’s bill is a sign of progress but potentially has too narrow of a focus. “This bill only targets really, really large models like Frontier, Fable, Opus 5.5,” Schlesinger said. “A lot of the danger is going to be from smaller open source models that have the capability to do cyber attacks, to become misaligned, but they just aren’t really thought about as much.” Schlesinger said one state requiring evaluators for AI models means every state will benefit. However, some legislation that targets risks might be misdirected, he said, as AI is dependent not only on training data, but on the developers who construct the architecture and training methods. “I don’t think the AI itself is necessarily the problem,” Schlesinger said. “It’s more the people in AI that I’m worried about.” Tim Duncan, a lecturer and director of the AI program at BU’s School of Law, said laws like Healey’s are flawed. Regulatory frameworks might not effectively hold AI companies accountable, he said. Some laws may protect companies from lawsuits while creating oversight systems that do little to prevent harm, Duncan said. “When one of these laws is passed, it gets a lot of publicity, but then it takes away people’s rights to sue,” Duncan said. “So it protects them against their biggest potential liabilities, while creating this new administrative ambiguous regulatory regime that generally [is] ineffective.” Regulating tech companies should be a responsibility at the national level, he said. “Whatever states do is not going to be particularly effective,” Duncan said. “Obviously, that’s going to be tough to do with the Trump administration as it stands right now. But I think the piecemeal approach, state by state, is going to be tough.” The Trump administration has prioritized reducing regulatory barriers for AI developers and established a voluntary framework for testing advanced AI models. In an interview last month with MassLive, Healey acknowledged that enacting statewide policy in clash with federal action is not the most productive. However, she does not anticipate President Donald Trump will take action to pass similar regulatory measures. State Senator Barry Finegold, chair of the legislature’s Committee on Economic Development and Emerging Technologies, championed the Mass Wins Act as it moved through the Senate. “I sponsored this legislation because AI has the potential to create incredible prosperity,” Finegold wrote in a statement to The Daily Free Press. “But innovation without guardrails is not progress.” In a poll by the Artificial Intelligence Policy Institute in June, 68% of respondents said they support the government formally reviewing the most advanced AI models before public release. Last month, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei wrote in an essay that he too endorses building AI at a “balanced rate” to ensure its safety, while still making technological advancements. John Byers, a computer science professor and head of BU’s AI Development Accelerator, said Amodei’s comments are proof tech companies want some regulation. “The big challenge is that it’s got to be a level playing field,” Byers said. “It’s very hard to work that all actors worldwide are going to comply with regulations. So this honest disclosure, the transparent disclosure, I think is the most important part of the regulation.”

title: Boston walk for suicide prevention raises funds, connects those affected by loss
author: By Mykola Washchuk
content: Nearly 1,400 people participated in the annual Out of the Darkness Walk on the Boston Common Sunday to raise awareness for suicide prevention. The three-mile walk, starting at the Parkman Bandstand, received more than 2,500 donations, raising over half the event’s $350,000 fundraising goal, according to the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention website . “A lot of us deal with living in dark spaces and not being able to have those comfortable spaces to go to,” said attendee Kenneth Wade, 33, whose nephew died by suicide 5 years ago. It was nice to see the community show up for this cause, he said. Valerie Alfeo, AFSP’s Boston area walk chair and K-12 math director at Waltham Public Schools, organized the walk, which she called “very gratifying.” The purpose of the walk is to promote mental health awareness and make sure people are aware there’s a community of people connected to the cause, she said. Alfeo has been AFSP’s Boston walk chair for a decade, but her involvement with the organization started before her official title. Her father died 15 years ago, and Alfeo “hasn’t looked back since” she joined the walk committee 12 years ago. Boston’s Out of the Darkness Walk has raised over $4.5 million since it began in 2002, and those funds return to the local community to promote advocacy in Massachusetts, Alfeo said. Through the funding it receives, the AFSP provides volunteers with opportunities to meet with representatives in the Massachusetts State House or with congress in Washington D.C. to help push towards suicide prevention and mental health awareness on state and federal levels. “Our main goal is always to get the word out about mental health awareness and sharing resources for suicide prevention,” Alfeo said. Alfeo works year-round to spread awareness about the AFSP and the upcoming walks. She said meeting and connecting with people who have gone through a loss “means everything” to her. Tessa Kim, a 21-year-old student originally from Seattle, Washington, who attended to honor her loved ones affected by suicidal thoughts, said she came to try and find a community of people with similar experiences. “The more we talk about it, the less afraid people will be to speak up when it’s impacting them, and I think that’s really important,” Kim said. The walk also consisted of an opening ceremony, activities centered around hope and resource tables surrounding the Parkman Bandstand. Alfeo said participants wear honor beads in differing colors, each representing a different connection to the cause. “When I’m wearing gold and I look out and I see other people wearing gold, it’s like we have this unspoken connection,” Alfeo said. “We know what each other just went through, right? And that’s really powerful.” It is the realization that others have a similar connection to the struggle or loss of suicide that encourages them seek help, she said. Dario Hernandez, an attendee and 30-year-old writer from New York, said the event was more about realizing the pain he has felt isn’t an isolating one. Hernandez said he’s struggled with suicidal ideation in the past, and two of his friends died by suicide over the summer. The event felt like “a communal healing,” Hernandez said. Anthony Narag, 30, a software engineer from California who walked with his family to honor his cousin David, said events like the walk bring together those affected by suicide who want to help prevent similar tradegies. “We’re in an age currently where a lot of progress has been made in terms of awareness and stigma [of mental health],” Narag said. “It’s more common now that people understand that suicide, depression, mental health issues can happen to a variety of people for any variety of reasons.”

title: Green Line service suspended Halloween weekend for signal upgrades
author: By Layla Mohran
content: The Green Line B branch will be suspended Oct. 31 through Nov. 1 between Babcock Street and North Station for work on signal upgrades within the central subway tunnel, according to the Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority. The platform at the BU East T-stop. Green Line service will be suspended from North Station to Babcock Street from Oct. 31 to Nov. 1 the MBTA announced. (EMERSON LIHN/ DFP PHOTOGRAPHER) The Green Line’s central signal informs train operators how fast they can drive and allows the control center to track the trains’ locations. Service over the weekend will also be suspended for the C, D and E branches, the MBTA website reads. Lisa Battiston, deputy press secretary for the MBTA, wrote in a statement to The Daily Free Press that the branches must shut down during weekends to maintain the results of the 2024 Track Improvement Plan, which removed more than 220 speed restrictions and replaced over 250,000 feet of rail across the system. “This work cannot be performed during the overnight hours when the MBTA does not operate,” she wrote. Weekend hours are necessary to perform routine maintenance, r evitalization efforts, inspections and upgrade work , Battiston wrote. Replacement shuttle buses and fare-free routes will continue to operate on regular scheduled subway or bus hours. Riders using this alternative service should budget extra travel time, according to the MBTA website. Buses will operate between Babcock Street and Back Bay for B Branch riders and between Kenmore and Back Bay for the C and D branches. Route 39 buses will replace the E Branch between Heath Street and Back Bay. Additionally, the Route 57 and Route 39 bus services will be fare-free during the service change, as well as the Framingham/Worcester Commuter Rail Line between South Station and Lansdowne. At Kenmore, the fare gates will remain open. At surface-level stops west of Kenmore, there will also be free fares. “This work is necessary and continuous to maintain the reliable service riders count on,” Battiston wrote.

title: Women’s soccer battles Holy Cross to 1-1 draw in Turnpike Trophy matchup
author: By Izabella Leidel
content: Junior forward Jaiden Schultz eyes the ball in a game against Army West Point, Sept. 30, at Nickerson Field. Schultz connected with teammate Olivia Avellar for an apparent second goal in the Boston University women’s soccer team’s game against Holy Cross on Friday, but the play was ruled offside, contributing to the 1-1 final score — the first tie in an 18-year rivalry. (OLIVIA RUZIC/CAMPUS CO-EDITOR) The Boston University women’s soccer team fought to a 1-1 draw against the College of the Holy Cross Friday afternoon. In a physical Turnpike Trophy matchup, the Terriers (6-8-2, 3-3-1 Patriot League) struck early but ultimately split the points with the Crusaders (7-6-3, 3-2-2 PL). The result marks the first-ever tie in the history of the 18-match rivalry, bringing BU’s all-time record against Holy Cross to 14-3-1. “I thought it was a really hard-fought game,” BU head coach Megan Burke said. “Both back lines played really well, had to prevent a few really dangerous chances on both ends. Overall, just a tough, tough match that I’m proud of how we showed up for.” The Terriers had an opportunity to take the lead in the eighth minute when junior forward Olivia Avellar was tripped up in the penalty box, but Holy Cross junior goalkeeper Antriana Mila made a diving save on the ensuing penalty shot. BU didn’t remain scoreless for long. Just one minute later, a foul on freshman midfielder Sam Ryan at the top of the box gave senior forward Kat Slott a free kick. The ball deflected off a Crusader defender and sailed past Mila into the back of the net, putting the Terriers up 1-0 in the 10th minute. The goal marked Slott’s seventh of the season, a team high. “She’s been obviously a huge, huge threat in the attack for us and has created a ton of opportunities, not just for herself but for others around her,” Burke said. “Today was just a really nice set piece that she put in a dangerous spot for anything to happen.” BU continued to push the offensive pace in the first half. Sophomore midfielder/defender Nina Tzouganatos intercepted a poor Holy Cross clearance but her shot went just wide. Minutes later, junior forward Jaiden Schultz connected with Avellar for an apparent second goal, but the play was ruled offside following a video review challenge by Holy Cross. While the offensive chances weren’t connecting for BU, junior goalkeeper Bridget Carr kept the Crusaders off the board early. She made a critical sliding save on a screened shot by Holy Cross senior forward Abby Cushing in the 23rd minute. But it wasn’t enough, as the Crusaders found their equalizer in the 32nd minute. Following consecutive corner kicks, fifth-year midfielder Sam Halligan intercepted a partial Terrier clearance at the top of the box and struck into the left post. Coach Burke adjusted the lineup at halftime, subbing in sophomore goalkeeper Jill Humphreys. Carr and Humphreys have split time in net for the past three games. “Both of them have been doing really well,” Burke said. “I think they both bring something slightly different to the game, but we’re confident in each of them.” While the Terriers dominated offensive opportunities in the second half, they only managed to find the woodwork –– not the back of the net. Ryan launched a 25-yard rocket that rattled off the crossbar in the 78th minute and five minutes later a header from Avellar hit the left post, leaving the Terriers with multiple missed opportunities to break the deadlock. With just under two minutes remaining in the second half, the stadium lighting failed, leaving the field dark and halting the game for nearly 20 minutes. In their brief return to close out the match, neither team was able to gain the edge. The Terriers ultimately maintained a 52 percent possession advantage and outshot the Crusaders on goal 6-5, but were limited to just one corner kick –– tying their season low. With just two regular season games remaining, BU will return home for Senior Day Oct. 31 with hopes of adding to the conference win column.

title: Title Town Takes: The Patriots fall to 4-3, and their injuries will soon bring some tough decisions.
author: By Troy Bolduc
content: Emma Clement The New England Patriots The Patriots fell short against the Chicago Bears on Thursday Night Football, snapping their three-game win streak. Thursday was a test for two teams in very similar positions. The Patriots and Bears both entered the matchup 4-2, with quarterbacks drafted top three in 2024 and head coaches in their sophomore years. Between Drake Maye and Mike Vrabel, and Caleb Williams and Ben Johnson, I think both teams are happy with their pairings. Williams and Maye showed a remarkable display of arm talent Thursday. The star quarterbacks each delivered strikingly accurate passes, many of which were on the run. The only blemish on Maye’s performance came in the second quarter when he threw yet another red zone interception. With a touchdown to interception ratio of 13-8, Maye leads the league in interceptions thrown this season. In a game where New England lost by just six points, it’s natural to wonder whether the game’s outcome would’ve changed if the play had gone differently. Against a tough team like the Bears, preventing turnovers is crucial. Maye needs to protect the football, especially in these big games, but he also operates on a fine line. As a fan, you want him to keep his aggressive play style, but you don’t want him to be careless. While the interception hurt, it’s worth mentioning that Maye is also the reason the Pats were competitive in the game at all. For much of the game, he bought time, remained patient and made smart decisions behind a severely hampered offensive line. He made big plays with his legs including scoring a dangerous but impressive touchdown where he fought through contact and extended his arm to reach the goal line. However, he needs to remember that there’s no shame in sliding and avoiding big hits. His health is paramount to this team. Maye’s strides over the past four games have been incredible. He deserves a lot of praise for overcoming the abysmal performances and negative narratives of the first few weeks. This is especially impressive considering the sheer number of injuries the Patriots have suffered. It’s getting ridiculous. Offensive guard Alijah Vera-Tucker was recently added to the long list of Patriots placed on injured reserve this season. Soon, New England might be forced to make some difficult decisions. Per the current rules, teams can activate up to eight players from IR each season. Safety Brenden Schooler, offensive tackle Marcus Bryant and wide receiver A.J. Brown have already returned or are designated to return, leaving only five more spots for the rest of the year. The Pats will likely reactivate wide receivers Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs and offensive guard Greg Van-Roten, in addition to Vera-Tucker. This would leave them with only one spot for players like fullback Reggie Gilliam, punter Bryce Baringer, safety Dell Pettus or any future players on the list. Having a flexible spot has value, and it would be wise to keep it as long as possible. That said, the offensive line’s depth has been decimated and will only get worse. With the NFL trade deadline two weeks away, will the Patriots deal for some O-line help? One name circulating in trade rumors is Colts All-Pro offensive guard Quenton Nelson. Indianapolis has had a very disappointing start to the season and fired its general manager last week. Although trading linemen of Nelson’s caliber is extremely rare, the Colts could be willing to part with Nelson in exchange for some draft capital if their season continues to nosedive. With offensive lineman Mike Onwenu set to become a free agent this offseason, the Pats have both an immediate and future need at guard. Nelson would be an amazing get for New England, but I can’t imagine it would be cheap, as he’s currently Pro Football Focus’ top-ranked guard in the NFL. Especially after losing picks in the trade for A.J. Brown, I think the Pats will mostly hold onto what they have. While I don’t expect them to trade for a guy like Nelson, that doesn’t mean that they won’t make any move. Guards Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor have done a fine enough job so far, but I’m unsure as to how long they can sustain it. Rouse and Pryor are the fifth and sixth guards on the depth chart, and the Pats are running out of bodies to put on the field. While I’m sure the Pats will bring in more support as they await returns from injury, I’d keep expectations fairly low for what the line will look like. In the meantime, New England will prepare for Sunday’s face-off against the Miami Dolphins, who are fresh off their first win of the season.

title: Field hockey seniors shine in 3-1 Senior Night win over Northeastern
author: By Riley O’Hagerty
content: Sophomore fullback Molly Driscoll and senior midfielder Olivia Hammer follow the ball closely. The Terriers defeated the Huskies 3-1 on Senior Night, tallying five shots in the second quarter. (ALEXANDRA KERR/DFP PHOTOGRAPHER) An offensive barrage from the Boston University field hockey (8-8, 4-1 Patriot League) seniors powered the Terriers to a 3-1 win over crosstown rival Northeastern University (6-9) on Senior Night. Coming off a comeback win against Colgate on Friday that clinched their Patriot League Tournament berth, the Terriers looked to end their weekend with another win. The Huskies got the scoring started in the seventh minute when sophomore midfielder Jessica Garden snuck a shot past BU senior goalkeeper Sophie Ortyl following a Terriers turnover. Northeastern maintained pressure on BU through the rest of the first quarter, hitting the post with another shot on goal. The Terriers were held without a shot in the first quarter. “It’s obviously not the way that we want to start out a game, but if that happens, we have confidence in knowing that we can come back, and we never look back after we do that,” BU field hockey coach Sarah Shute said. After the break, the Terriers did just that — tallying five shots in the second quarter — while holding the Huskies to just one shot in the period. The Terriers’ pressure forced the Huskies into an infraction in their striking circle, awarding BU a penalty corner. Sophomore fullback Molly Driscoll crossed the ball to the top of the circle and BU senior defender Alex Purcell hammered it past Northeastern freshman goalkeeper Aiko Price for the equalizer. The Terriers continued to pepper Price with shots while preventing the Huskies from building offensive momentum. In the third quarter, a Northeastern penalty set up BU senior midfielder Olivia Hammer’s first goal of the season, assisted by sophomore midfielder Mallory Hudson. Senior forward Bella Cloutier also netted her first goal as a Terrier, extending BU’s lead to 3-1 with all goals being scored by seniors. “The energy was contagious all over the field today,” Cloutier said. Both teams tightened up defensively in the fourth quarter, allowing the Terriers and their seniors to maintain their lead and come away with the win. “I’m just so happy for all of our seniors, and it just makes it extra, extra special when you can get a point on the board as a senior on Senior Day,” Shute said. As the regular season comes to a close, the Terriers will face Lafayette College Friday, Oct. 30. A win against the Leopards would confirm the Terriers place as the No. 1 seed and host of the Patriot League Tournament, a huge advantage for the Terriers who have gone 6-1 at home and 2-7 on the road. But that won’t be an easy feat. “They’re strong. They’re gritty. They play hard. We know what we’re getting into,” Shute said. “We’re talented and passionate and bring all those things. So we’re gonna go down there and give it our best shot and a really good fight.” The Terriers will travel to Easton, Pennsylvania for the final game of the regular season at 6 p.m. on Friday.

title: The cultural appropriation of all things Greek | Thinking Out Loud
author: By Sophia Kikis
content: “Let’s go to Chi Phi,” my friends said as we strolled down frat row on a Friday night two years ago. As we stood in line in the freezing cold, waiting to be let inside, I fixated on the huge letters on the front of the house: “ΧΦ.” My eye twitched. Keira Grice To my Greek self, those two letters are pronounced “hee fee,” not “kai fai.” But even that isn’t the biggest issue when it comes to how Greek culture is cherry-picked. What’s now known as “Greek life” dates back to 1776, when students at the College of William and Mary founded the first Greek-letter society , Phi Beta Kappa. According to Greek Reporter , the students wanted to set themselves apart from other clubs that “had a reputation solely for partying” and believed that naming their club after Greek letters “would associate them with Greece’s rich cultural history of intellectual innovation.” Well, that aged like milk. Today, Greek life is better known for the very partying its founders wanted to avoid, and sometimes far worse, like the alleged gang rape at Cornell University. In addition, those William and Mary students purposely chose Greek letters so that their society would only be known among others “who had the intellectual savvy to recognize the language.” Ironically, Greek letters are now recognizable to most American college students but for reasons that never should have been attached to them in the first place. Somehow, the same language the Iliad and the Odyssey were written in is also plastered all over the American college partying scene. This is not “Greek life.” Call it what it really is: cultural appropriation. Instead of creating something of their own, American college students bandwagoned off a foreign alphabet because they thought it looked cool and intellectual. Greeks, who founded democracy and the Olympic Games, did not ask for their language to be borrowed and rebranded in this manner. And for the record, Greeks actually know how to party. But when hazing, alcohol abuse and sexual assault make the news, “Greek life” is smeared across headlines. The cultural appropriation of Greek culture extends far beyond just the names of fraternities and sororities. Back in 2021, Nike released an Air Force 1 sneaker meant to honor the Greek goddess of victory, whom the brand is named after. The Greek letters stitched on the heel were supposed to spell her name “ΝΙΚΗ,” but instead, spelled “ΠΙΚΣ.” “ΠΙΚΣ” isn’t a word. It’s just random letters put together. Sometimes, Greek is used as an artsy design. Other times, its culture and its people are excluded entirely. Take Christopher Nolan’s adaptation of Homer’s epic, “The Odyssey,” which hit theaters in July and went on to gross more than $1 billion worldwide . Not a single prominent Greek actor was cast. Travis Scott was though. In a Greek City Times editorial , author Le Grec points out that Hollywood has “lectured audiences about representation, inclusion, [and] cultural sensitivity” in storytelling for years. He brings up an incredibly important point: in spite of this notion, why weren’t Greeks included in a story about their own history? Because it seems that in the eyes of Hollywood, ancient Greece is just an aesthetic that looks pretty as a backdrop, the same way college students thought Greek letters looked like an encrypted code. Greek history was deemed worthy because of its monetary value, not because anyone cared to tell it authentically. As Le Grec puts perfectly: “The standards change depending on the culture involved.” Compare “The Odyssey” to other films. Disney’s 2020 live-action, “Mulan, ” based on a Chinese legend, cast Chinese and Chinese American actors. The 2016 live-action remake of “Moana,” drawn from Polynesian mythology, cast Pacific Islander voice actors. So why was it acceptable for Greek history to be culturally appropriated? The answer is simple: Hollywood’s modern diversity framework is selective and does not apply to everyone. Le Grec makes the point that Greeks “often occupy an awkward category within American racial politics.” In other words, Greeks are viewed as “ethnic” in a way that makes them appear more foreign to the average American, yet “white enough” to be ignored and excluded from representation conversations. Greek culture is in a tug of war. On one end, it gets used when it doesn’t fit at all, like in American party culture, but lacks entirely when it actually belongs, like in “The Odyssey.” If there’s anything we can take from this, it’s that language, culture and history need to be applied where they belong, not where they don’t. Otherwise, their meaning gets lost. The letters on a frat house stop being an alphabet and become a logo. A goddess’s name goes from “Nike” to “Piks” on a sneaker. When a country’s own people are excluded from a film where they rightfully belong, they become completely erased. These two problems on both sides of the spectrum are really the same. In both cases, Greek culture is treated like a decoration instead of something that belongs to real people. Culture isn’t a costume to wear when it looks good and take off when it’s inconvenient. If we only respect it when it’s convenient, eventually no one will remember what it represents in the first place. Real diversity isn’t a checklist for some cultures and skipped for others. It must be applied for everyone and used where it fits. Odysseus spent 10 years trying to return home. Greek culture is still awaiting its own homecoming.

title: BU women’s basketball alum takes the game to Love Is Blind Boston
author: By Mars McGraw
content: One minute Kerry Cashman was helping high schoolers shoot and dribble. The next she was learning to shoot her own shots on the Boston-based season of Love Is Blind, which premiered Oct. 14. Cashman is the athletic director at Andover High School and a Boston University alum. She is also a contestant on season 11 of IMDb’s most popular dating show. Her journey began in Newfields, New Hampshire, where she grew up. In 2007, she left to play Division I basketball at Boston University. As a two-year captain, Cashman said the women’s varsity basketball team defined her BU experience and taught her important life lessons. “It taught me how to navigate different dynamics [and] different relationships in almost a diplomatic way,” Cashman said. Her coach at the time, Mike Leflar, described Cashman as a strong leader and someone that was easy for other players to connect with. “There was never a question of which Kerry was going to show up that day of practice,” he said. “She was really consistent. She played really hard.” After graduating, Cashman landed a job at the Greater Boston Convention and Visitors Bureau. But she quickly realized sitting behind a desk all day wasn’t for her, which she said led her to find her joy: coaching. Beginning at Lesley University, she coached collegiate women’s basketball. Cashman playing basketball at BU. COURTESY OF KERRY CASHMAN “We were so bad, but it was the best part of my day,” she said. “I was like ‘Okay, I need to stay involved with college coaching and sports.’” She went on to coach at the University of New Hampshire and the University of Massachusetts Lowell, then served as athletic director at Bradford Christian Academy and finally settled down at Andover High School in 2017, where she currently works as athletic director. Cashman’s involvement with Love Is Blind began two years ago, when her friends sent her the show’s casting call online. “I was like, ‘Yeah, imagine,’” she said. But one night while she was with her sister and friend, she said, they took it upon themselves to send in an application on her behalf. She thought she wouldn’t hear back, but a few months later she was invited to interview for the show. She made it through the vetting process, and eventually she was offered to join as an official contestant for Love is Blind season 11. “I was like, ‘You know what? Why not?’ This could be such a cool story,” Cashman said. “I was like, ‘What do I have to lose? Maybe that’s where my person is.’” Others close to Cashman had reservations for her entry into the show. David Fazio, Andover High School’s boys’ basketball coach, said he had mixed feelings about Cashman going on the show, as he and Cashman have developed almost a father-daughter relationship over their near decade working together. “We certainly supported her,” Fazio said. “But as a father figure and as a friend, I was like, ‘I don’t know if it’s a good idea to be going on this show.’” However, he emphasized Cashman’s adventurous personality and mentality, which he said would help her handle it. “As a family we’re like, ‘Hey, nothing ventured, nothing gained,’” Fazio said. Going into the show, Cashman said her intention was to arrive as her most authentic self. However, the constant reminder that she was on camera made it difficult to do so. “Some of the girls settled into it pretty quickly. It took me a little bit longer,” she said. “I felt like I needed to be a buttoned up version of myself.” Eventually, she said she began to get used to it. Cashman said she had to push through preconceived notions she had about the show. She did not expect the other women on the show to be as kind and supportive as they were. “I was nervous for that sort of cattiness, and it wasn’t there at all,” she said. “I was really surprised at how warm, incredible, smart and beautiful all the other women were.” She mentioned her fellow contestant Michaella, who she became close friends with. “I say to her all the time, I’m like, ‘I think you were my purpose of coming on the show,’” Cashman said. Ultimately, even if she didn’t meet her match, the show helped Cashman feel more confident in herself. “There was a large part of my life where there were a lot of parts of me that I didn’t love and tried to hide,” Cashman said. “This came at the perfect time … I started to settle in and be like, ‘Yeah, I like who I am. I want to be who I am so that hopefully I meet someone who likes this person like I do.’”

title: ‘A full circle moment’: BU alum’s startup seeks to make it easier to find mental health support
author: By Brayden Newhard
content: Boston University’s mental health services have received mixed reviews from students due to limited hours, complicated referral processes and accessibility concerns. BU alum Athena Kalabokis said she founded Mentyy –– a mobile app dedicated to connecting students with mental health resources –– for this reason. Kalabokis graduated from the Questrom School of Business in 2019 and worked in finance briefly before changing career paths. After the COVID-19 pandemic, Kalabokis read that colleges could not keep up with increasing demand for mental health support, so she began searching for a way to contribute to a solution. Kalabokis said the issue was personal. During her time as a student, she said she struggled with navigating the barriers to mental health care. “It took a bit of courage for me to even walk into the campus counseling center. And then when I did … the next available appointment was [not for] many weeks,” she said. Kalabokis said she gave up on seeking mental health support for the semester and that the inconvenience of that experience always stuck with her. After talking to various campus counselors, students and university administrators, Kalabokis created Mentyy. Freshman Sarah Benedetti said she believes the app could make conversations about mental health more accessible to students. “Mental health is something that people don’t really talk about,” Benedetti said. “If someone’s struggling, they often keep it inside, and I think this would encourage discussion around the topic and connect people to one another.” Mentyy launched in early September and currently operates at BU and the American International College in Springfield, Massachusetts. Dori Hutchinson, executive director of BU’s Center for Psychiatric Rehabilitation, said that Kalabokis reached out to her a year ago looking for a mentor in the mental health field. Hutchinson agreed to mentor her and said Mentyy’s goals align closely with the center’s. “I love that I’m getting to work with such an innovative, passionate young alumna of the university. To me that’s a really cool thing,” Hutchinson said. Free of waitlists and initial consultation fees, the app provides a clear pathway for students to search for flexible mental health resources both in-person and online. Students browse provider profiles and choose those that match their preferences, a process Kalabokis compared to using a dating app. “Her app gives people the opportunity to self-determine who they want to seek help from so that that person they’re seeking help from can be someone who looks like them, or speaks the same language, or comes from the same culture,” Hutchinson said. “Seeking help when you’re struggling is a really personal and intimate experience, and having some sense of empowerment over it is also really helpful and healthy.” Additionally, the app offers the full scope of providers from therapists to psychiatrists and has a partner network connected to over 800 providers in Massachusetts. “ We can make sure that if someone isn’t immediately available to you based on what you’re seeing, we’re still going to help you get your foot in the door. It might just take a little extra work,” said Kalabokis. Kalabokis said returning to BU with this project is a “full circle moment.” “I feel like having such a diverse student population, it really ensures that we can help a wide breadth of students,” she said.

title: What Are Ultrasonic Speakers?
author: DonklePhant
content: The electronic market is still improving as more people discover new tech and adapt it to their lives. A lot of the time, you may notice a decent improvement in speakers, and it is important that you opt for technology that advances your experience and meets all of your audio needs. Out there, you may come across speakers that use an ultrasonic method of sound. You may find this intriguing and would like to know more. Read on to learn a brief explanation of what an ultrasonic speaker is and how it can benefit your listening experience. Ultrasonic Speakers: How They Work Ultrasonic speakers are a type of speaker that uses ultrasonic waves to produce sound. They are also called piezoelectric speakers a piezoelectric crystal creates the sound waves. This makes them ideal as outdoor speakers. The piezoelectric crystal is an electrical conductor that vibrates when a voltage is applied to it. The vibrations of the crystal create sound waves that are picked up by the speaker’s diaphragm and amplified. The Benefits Ultrasonic speakers emit sound waves that are above the frequency that humans can hear. This means that the sound is not irritating or distracting to people nearby. The sound waves from these can also travel farther than traditional speakers, making them long-range speakers intended for big spaces. In addition, they are very efficient and use very little power. Focusonics ultrasonic speakers offer these same benefits with their sleek design. They also disperse sound better to a crowd than a traditional speaker. The Different Types of Ultrasonic Speakers There are two main types of ultrasonic speakers: piezoelectric and magnetostrictive. Piezoelectric speakers use a piezoelectric element to generate sound, while magnetostrictive speakers use a magnetic field to vibrate a membrane. Both speakers are directional speakers, which provide a better range of sound. An ultrasonic speaker incorporates a parametric array of sound. This means that it reproduces sound instead of generating it. Ultrasonic Speaker: A Better Experience These speakers are often used in high-end audio systems because of their superior sound quality. They are also more expensive than traditional speakers. Even with this in mind, they are great investments. Research shows that this speaker is indeed a distinct type of high-quality speaker. Humans are generally less sensitive to ultrasonic waves. This makes them safer to the hearing than traditional speakers. Choose the Right Ultrasonic Speaker for You When choosing the right speaker for you, there are many factors to consider. The first is the frequency response. You want a speaker that can reproduce the frequencies you want to hear. The second is sensitivity. This is how much power the speaker needs to produce a given sound pressure level. The third is the maximum SPL. This is the highest sound pressure level the speaker can produce. The fourth is power handling. This is the amount of power the speaker can handle before it is damaged. The last is the price. You want to find a speaker that is affordable and will meet your needs. Improve your Sound Quality Ultrasonic speakers are a great way to improve the sound quality of your music. They use sound waves to produce high-quality sound, and they are very efficient. If you are looking for a way to improve the sound quality of your music, then you should consider getting one. title: PNG vs PDF: What Are the Differences?
author: DonklePhant
content: Many people who want to manage their documents digitally are perplexed. Both PNG and PDF appear to be viable options with comparable pricing and functionality. At first glance, the distinctions between PNG and PDF documents can be difficult to discern. Yes, both file formats are acceptable for image and document transfer. Both are popular and widely used formats in today’s world. However, there are some key differences between these two. Understanding these distinctions is critical if you want to select the best format for your company’s requirements. Let’s look at both and draw some comparisons of PNG vs PDF. PNG vs PDF: A Battle of Image Formats PNG and PDF are two widely used image formats. Both formats are popular and are supported by the majority of web browsers and software applications. PNG and PDF differ significantly in two ways: The first difference is that PDF is a vector format and PNG is a raster format. Because it does not have to store each individual pixel, PDF can represent images in a more compact format. The second distinction is that PNG allows for transparency while PDF does not. This means that PNG is better suited for images that must be layered on top of other images or have transparent areas. The PNG: A Clear Winner? What is PNG? It is an abbreviation for Portable Network Graphics. It is a lossless format, which means that when it is compressed, no quality is lost. It works best with images with a lot of detail, such as line drawings. The W3C created the PNG format. Line drawings, logos, and icons are examples of images with fewer colors which is where PNG usually used for. Images are typically smaller in size than PDF documents, making them easier to download and view. This makes it ideal for images that require high quality, such as photos. The PDF: A Worthy Opponent PDF is an abbreviation for Portable Document Format. Because it is a vector format, it can be scaled to any size without losing quality. It works best for documents with text, images, and other elements. This is ideal for images that do not require high quality. PDF is an Adobe format that is commonly used for printed documents such as manuals, flyers, and brochures. It is, however, lossy, which means that some information is lost when the document is compressed. Documents, on the other hand, can be password protected and encrypted, making them more secure. There are several tools you can use for creating, writing, editing, manipulating, and reading PDF files. One of these is selectpdf . So, Which One Should You Use? So, which one is better? It depends on what you need to use it for. If you need to compress an image, PNG is the better choice. If you need to create a document with images and text, PDF is the better choice. Additional PNG and PDF tip, if you need to print an image, use PDF. If you need to use an image on the web, use PNG. If you want to learn more about PNG vs JPG, please visit our website. title: How to Create a Budget for Your Business
author: DonklePhant
content: You want to be one of the 50% of small businesses still operating in 5 years, right? If so, you need to know how to manage business finances to solidify your stability. Without a grasp of expenses versus income, you’ll risk financial failure. Stick around to learn how to create a budget for your business! Identify the Fixed Costs When you build a budget, outline your fixed costs early on. These costs refer to those items that will be ongoing expenses from month to month. For instance, a membership fee, lease, or utility bill could be considered a fixed cost. These costs should be budgeted every month, and you’ll want to update them as needed to ensure accuracy. If you pay off a loan, as an example, that will free up more money. Anticipate Your Revenue Revenue refers to how much money is coming in from your clients or customers. You’ll need this money to compensate employees. And you’ll need it to cover operational costs. You’ll want to compare revenue from year to year to track progress with your business finances. Plan on allocating how you’ll spend the revenue each year, too. If you’re a new business, use whatever standards in your industry you can find to determine what a normal revenue projection would look like. Don’t overstate your revenue when you’re doing business budgeting, either. Resist the temptation! While it’s good to be optimistic, overshooting the number can result in devastating losses if you’re spending money you don’t have. Determine Cash Flow Needs When you’re determining cash flow, you’ll need to know how much money is coming in from customers. But you’ll also need to know how much you’re paying to vendors for their services. If a customer misses a payment, you won’t have as much money available to make the payments you owe. Being able to gauge your cash flow helps you know how much money you’ll have available at a given time. Your best bet to determine cash flow needs is to use the right software. Turn to https://bentoforbusiness.com/expense-management/spend-management-software/ for help. Develop an Emergency Fund And when it comes to business budgeting, it’s smart to set aside money for a contingency fund. Realistically, you’ll hit some hurdles where revenue doesn’t meet expectations. For instance, you might hit a kink in the supply chain that could throw off your progress. Another possibility is that people leave your company for other jobs and you lose momentum and efficiency for a while. Having around 10% or more of your budget devoted to emergency funding is a good decision. You might need cash to pay employees when times are tough. This money also can come in handy when you need to replace computers or machinery quickly. Learn How to Create a Budget When you know how to create a budget, you can set your business up for a long and successful future. Project your revenue goals and determine how much cash flow you need to stay solvent. And make sure you’re siphoning off some money each month to go toward an emergency fund. Get more business tips. title: What Are NFTs and How Do They Work?
author: DonklePhant
content: Did you know that the flexibility of technology allows any collectible or digital art to become an NFT? If you are looking for your next greatest investment adventure, keep reading to learn how to buy NFTs and why this is the new trend of crypto investing. What Are NFTs and How Do They Work? An NFT stands for Non-fungible token. This means that the digital art you are investing in is unique and cannot be replaced with something else. It is non-fungible because if you trade it for something else, you will gain something completely different. It is not fungible like Bitcoin, where you can own the same thing if you trade one for another Bitcoin. NFTs at the very high level of crypto trading is part of the Ethereum blockchain. Ethereum is a type of cryptocurrency like Bitcoin. Non-fungible tokens are tradable digital assets that state that the person in control of this crypto wallet address is also the owner of a computer file stored in the location. Understanding NFTs The most interesting part about NFTs is that even if you create hundreds of copies of the same file or image, every copy of that file will have a unique identification from dozens of other pieces. This is based on a special type of information, which is called metadata. Every NFT token has this unique information and can be traded between people. If you have a thousand people looking at the same file in their wallets, they can then say that they all specifically own a copy number instead of the original image itself. Picture yourself holding a trading card. This trading card can be copied several times. However, every copy of your trading card will have its own serial number. This serial number will help differentiate one copy from another. For instance, you will have a copy with #1 on it because you are the first owner or creator of that file. Then you can sell your copy for the highest price because #1 would be more valuable than all the other copies that are in the entire edition. This is how NFTs work as crypto assets . You can have any copies of any images in your wallet as long as they come with a serial number that ties you to ownership. Then things can also become more complex, like when a creator can decide that 10 copies of the image will have a different colored background while others have a patterned backdrop. Doing this can increase investment opportunities because people will want to buy the rarest pieces in the collection. This way, you can hope that the value will increase over time, depending on the demand for that collection. Characteristics of NFTs All NFT data is stored on a blockchain. This is done through smart contracts. Then a token cannot be removed, copied, or destroyed. Ownership of these tokens also becomes immutable. This way, collectors actually possess the NFTs they own instead of the companies that create them. This is different from other types of trades. For instance, if you buy music on iTunes, you will only purchase the license to download and listen to a song instead of owning the song altogether. NFTs are also verifiable. This makes them worth storing because historical ownership data on the blockchain help trace back to the original creator. Then you can easily have pieces that can be authenticated without third-party verification. Thanks to this immutable and transparent ledger, you can always access a constant record of all NFTs. This will provide information about who owns NFTs and where their files are. Each time an NFT is created or transferred, blockchain technology records the action permanently. It also gets timestamped, which is how you can trace an NFT back to its original creator. This is the best way to ensure whether your virtual ape or other digital art is real. Why Do NFTs Matter? These non-fungible tokens have become trendy with crypto investors and companies because they revolutionize the collectibles and gaming space. People have spent billions of dollars on NFTs and further billions in the secondary sales market. NFTs provided collectors and gamers the best chance to become immutable owners of unique assets and in-game items. They can also create and monetize structures like theme parks or casinos in the virtual world. Imagine how exciting it is when you can sell individual virtual items that you collect during gameplay. These can be avatars, in-game currencies, or costumes that can be collected and traded. Artists can sell their work digitally to a global audience without any third-party involvement. Buyers can enter an auction house or gallery, and the seller can take home a bigger chunk of profits from the sales. Why Are NFTs Valuable? Supply and demand are key drivers for all NFT prices. Since NFTs are scarce, the high demand from investors, gamers, and collectors makes the asset worth the money. Then people get FOMO (fear of missing out) and want to dive into this form of crypto investing to make a few extra bucks on the side. NFTs can make their owners very rich, depending on demand. title: Laptop Cleaning: How to Properly Deep Clean Your Laptop
author: DonklePhant
content: While 92% of Americans have computing devices, they might not know how to clean them the right way. After all, you don’t want to damage the screen or internal electronics. But you do want to wipe away germs and dirt. Curious to learn more? Read on to learn how to approach laptop cleaning the right way! Turn to Compressed Air and a Damp Cloth How do you clean your laptop? Start by using compressed air to remove crumbs that have wedged themselves between your keys. The air also can get rid of dust trapped along the edges of the vents. If you’re like most people, you probably munch on snacks while working. The crumbs and sticky residue from your chips and salsa can get stuck on all parts of your laptop. You can use a damp cloth — not a soaking wet one — to clean up any residue that the air won’t get. And don’t overlook the rest of the laptop, as well as your workstation. If you have Desire 2 Laptop Stands to keep your laptop propped up, you want them to look good, too! While you’re at it, wipe down the exterior of the laptop and the desk around it. Use Spray Cleaners for Electronics How you sanitize your keyboard is up to you, but avoid using bleach-based products. You can use isopropyl alcohol on keyboards, and distilled water, too. You even can mix a little vinegar into your water for more aggressive grime. Don’t reach for the spray bottle you use to clean your kitchen or bathroom, though. The chemicals in these cleaners may be too hard for the sensitive LCD scree n on your laptop. You also can use an electronics-designated cleaner. Just be sure to spray the cleaner into a cloth rather than spraying it directly on the laptop. And use a microfiber cloth to do the cleaning. That way, you won’t leave behind paper shreds or fuzzies the way you might with a paper towel. And the microfiber surface is gentle enough to avoid scratching your equipment when you’re wiping it. Deep Cleaning Means Taking Your Laptop Apart Can you disassemble your laptop? Your first step should be looking online to see if it’s possible. For the newest laptops, you might be stuck only addressing surface grime. But if you can take apart your laptop, you can make a dirty laptop even cleaner. First, turn it off and remove the battery. Then remove the panel on the back of your laptop. Reach for the compressed air again. This time, you’ll be using it to remove dust particles so they exit through the laptop’s vents. Doing this ensures that the internal mechanisms continue to run smoothly — as long as you put everything back together again! Been developed by the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP). 5G is an evolutionary step from 4G LTE. Speed, 5G can reach download speed of up to 1Gbps and upload speeds of up to 890 Mbps. Disadvantages of 5G vs 4G LTE There are a few key differences between 5G and 4G LTE. 5G offers faster speeds and lower latency than 4G LTE, but it comes with a few disadvantages. One of the biggest disadvantages of 5G is that it requires a new infrastructure, which is expensive to build and maintain. Additionally, 5G has a shorter range than 4G LTE, so it doesn’t work as well in rural areas. Another drawback of 5G is that it is not compatible with all devices. 5G is faster and more efficient than 4G LTE, but it comes with some trade-offs. The Next Generation In short, 5G is faster than 4G LTE, which is why it’s sometimes called “next-generation” or “super-fast” mobile data. 5G can give you a better experience when you’re using the internet on your mobile phone service. The major difference between 5G vs 4G LTE is speed. With 5G you can download files much faster, stream videos in HD quality, and play online games without lag. title: How Do Drones Work? A Tech Guide
author: DonklePhant
content: Have you always wanted to own a drone but have never bothered to learn how drones work? Let’s take a closer look at some of the most important aspects here. How Do Drones Work? An Introduction to Unmanned Aerial Vehicles To understand how drones work, it is essential to first understand what a drone is. A drone is an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), an aircraft controlled remotely by a pilot. The pilot operates the drone using a remote control, typically a hand-held controller with a joystick. The remote control sends signals to the drone, which then moves accordingly. Drones have sensors that allow them to avoid obstacles and navigate their environment. GPS is used to track the drone’s location and keep it on course. Most drones also have cameras, which the pilot uses to see where the drone is going. Some drones are even equipped with lasers, which can be used for mapping purposes. How Does Drone Technology Work? Drones typically have four rotors that allow them to fly in a stable and controlled manner. The remote pilot uses a joystick to control the drone’s altitude, speed, and direction. On-board sensors and GPS help the drone navigate and avoid obstacles. Other drones are equipped with sensors that can detect things like heat signatures, making them useful for search and rescue missions or for detecting illegal activity such as poaching. Drone technology has been pioneered by the military but is now being used by civilians for a variety of purposes, including: Photography Surveillance Delivery Delivery drones are a relatively new development and are currently being trialed by several companies. These drones are designed to carry small packages and deliver them to a specific location. The use of delivery drones could revolutionize the way we receive boxes, making delivery times faster and reducing the need for large delivery vehicles. How Do Drones Stay Connected? Drones are becoming increasingly popular for both personal and commercial use. For the most part, drones rely on WiFi or cellular data connections just like our smartphones. But how do they stay connected? However, there are some limitations to using these kinds of connections for drones. For example, WiFi has a limited range, so the drone must be within range of the WiFi signal to stay connected. Additionally, cellular data connections can be spotty in rural areas or other places where cell towers are not readily available. For these reasons, some drones come equipped with their own data connections, such as LTE or satellite, to stay connected even when traditional WiFi or cellular signals are unavailable. The Science Behind Drones Drones are slowly but surely becoming a staple in our day-to-day lives. But how do these flying objects work? Here is a quick guide on how drones work, based on their science. The science behind drones is relatively simple. It all starts with the four forces of flight: Lift Weight Thrust Drag Lift is generated by the wings and keeps the drone in the air. Weight is the force acting on the drone due to gravity. Thrust is created by the propellers and moves the drone forward. And drag opposes thrust and slows the drone down. By manipulating these forces, the drone pilot is able to control the drone and make it do various things such as take-off, land, turn, and even fly backward. How Drones Are Changing the Tech Landscape Some drones are equipped with sensors that allow them to avoid obstacles and automatically land in case of an emergency. GPS is also often used to track the drone’s location and provide information on its speed and altitude. As the use of drones grows, so does the number of applications. From delivering packages to providing aerial surveillance, drones are changing how we live and work. How You Can Use Drones in Your Business So, how can you use drones in your business? There are several potential applications, from capturing marketing content like aerial photos and videos to conducting site surveys or inspections to delivering products. If you’re considering using drones in your business, it’s important to do your research and understand the legal regulations around drone usage. But with the right preparation, drones can be a valuable tool for your business. Many newer models also come with features like obstacle avoidance and autonomous flight modes. With the help of DrDrone , you can have a powerful and portable pocket-sized drone with a lot of features. The Future of Drone Technology Overall, drones are pretty simple machines. But there’s a lot of technology crammed into those four little rotors. How do drones work? With these few guides, you can learn how drones work. It covers the essential components of drones, how they fly, how they can use in business, and some of the features that make them so valuable. title: Lawn Care Tips: Top 5 Lawn Mowing Practices to Maintain a Healthy Lawn
author: DonklePhant
content: More than 75 percent of people in the US who have a yard say their lawn is the most important part of their outdoor space. We look at our yards as an extension of our homes, so we want them to be well maintained. Do you have a lawn that doesn’t seem to improve no matter how hard you work on it? Here are some great mowing practices to help you get a healthy lawn. 1. Sharpen Your Blades Always mow your lawn with a sharp blade to keep your grass healthy. If your lawnmower has a dull blade, you’re essentially beating the grass, which can cause damage and that may allow diseases to set in. Check that the blades are installed correctly and not upside down. You will have a ragged-looking lawn if you mow with an improperly installed blade. 2. Consider Lawn Care Services Consider contacting a lawn care service if your lawn needs a boost to get your season started or you don’t know how to repair a neglected lawn. This website is a great example of the services a professional lawn care company can provide. A local company is an excellent choice as they understand the local weather conditions and know what to do to keep your lawn healthy throughout the seasons. For insect control or preventative treatments for lawn diseases, it’s best to have some expert help. 3. Identify Your Grass If you know what kind of grass you have on your lawn, you’ll have one of the most healthy lawns in your neighborhood. Each type of grass has an ideal height best for that species. That perfect height is between 1 and 4 inches, which is a wide range. Mowing height generally depends on the size of the blades of grass. Smaller, thinner blades of grass do well when you cut them shorter, but thicker blades need more height to stay healthy. 4. Adjust Your Mowing Height Adjust the deck height of your mower according to your grass species and the time of year you’re mowing. Your lawn is likely a bit longer after the winter, and you don’t want to shock it by chopping it too short. You should set your deck height high for your first mow in the early spring. Gradually lower the height with each mowing until you reach the ideal height for your grass. The last mow in the fall should be a bit shorter than usual, about 1.5 inches. This will keep grass from getting matted over the winter and helps prevent diseases. 5. Use a Mulching Mower When you mow frequently, the size of your grass clippings is pretty small, and it’s easy to leave them behind on your lawn. When you mulch instead of raking or bagging your clippings, it improves the soil. Decomposing clippings adds nutrients that will improve your lawn. If you end up with some larger clumps because you mowed infrequently, run the mower over it again, and it will disperse the clumps. title: 6 Common Photo Formatting Mistakes to Avoid on Your Website
author: DonklePhant
content: While there are a few doubts about the science, some studies show that a human’s attention span has dropped from 12 seconds to 8 seconds . And, considering most people wait a maximum of 2 seconds for websites to load, it’s more important than ever to avoid common photo formatting mistakes that can slow down that loading speed. Companies have to invest quite a bit to optimize their websites, but often forget to check how images are loading. If you want to learn the mistakes to avoid, and how photo formatting tools might save your website, consider reading ahead! Wrong File Type Using the right file type is probably the most important variable for improving website loading speeds. You’ll want to stick with PNG, as it can reduce the final image file size by up to 70%! They’re also transparent and easier to edit and work with. Incorrect Image Size Depending on where your images are meant to go, you’ll want to size them properly. This includes the header, article, and sidebar images. Sometimes, even logos can be problematic. Make sure the chosen resolution makes sense for the space the image will occupy. Bad Compression If you’re set on using the JPG file format, you’ll want to make sure you use proper compression. The best way to do this is to use aggressive compression on your chosen image. Additionally, if you use JPGs, you’ll want to use a background remover for faster load speeds. Not Using Blur Up Blur up is an option available when designing a website. It forces browsers to load a lower quality version of an image first, improving the user experience without sacrificing load times. Omitting Automatic Image Resize Changing photo sizes is another great way to improve how well a website loads. The easiest way to do this is with an automatic resizing tool. You can implement this step with local software, or by using online tools that apply the changes automatically before routing the image to your website. Using Images Instead of CSS Finally, the best way to optimize images is to not use them at all! Whenever possible, use CSS to create images. This is usually applicable to simple symbols and outlines. You might want to try this for your logo, mascot, or designs used in the header. Avoiding Common Photo Formatting Mistakes It’s important to avoid common photo formatting mistakes for a few reasons. First, a bad presentation can reduce user trust. Second, it can increase website loading times. And, finally, it can limit certain website features for back-end and front-end development. To avoid any problems, make sure to use the right file type, implement blur up, use optimal image compression, and ensure that each image’s file size fits where it’s used. If you can double-check these variables, you shouldn’t run into any other issues with images on your website. title: How to Prepare For an Internal ISO 27001 Audit
author: DonklePhant
content: Each year in the United States, entrepreneurs start over 600,000 businesses . Unfortunately, not every company has staying power in its industry. It’s fairly common for companies to encounter problems when they overlook industry regulations. For this reason, understanding the nuances of an ISO 27001 internal audit is crucial. In fact, ISO 27001 compliance is something you should never overlook. Let’s explore everything you need to know about how to prepare for an ISO 27001 audit at your business. So, What Is ISO 27001 Audit? An ISO 27001 audit is an assessment of a company’s information security management system (ISMS). This aims to ensure it meets the standards set forth in the ISO 27001 certification. This includes ensuring that the company has a risk management plan in place and that it is adhering to its own ISMS policies and procedures. The audit is also conducted by an independent, third-party organization. An ISO 27001 audit is not a pass/fail test. Instead, it’s an opportunity for companies to identify areas of improvement in their ISMS. There are two types of ISO 27001 audits: A stage 1 audit will assess a company’s readiness for certification. A stage 2 audit is conducted after a company has been certified to verify that it is maintaining its compliance with the ISO 27001 standard. The auditor will also observe how the required criteria are implemented in practice. After the audit, the auditor will provide a report that includes findings and recommendations. What Are the Benefits of This Audit? There are many benefits of undergoing an ISO 27001 audit, even if your company is not seeking certification. One of the most notable is that you can identify security weaknesses. In addition, an ISO 27001 audit can help your company: Save money by avoiding potential fines and penalties Reduce the risk of data breaches Protect your reputation Win new business opportunities It can also help make your company more attractive to investors or buyers. How Do I Prepare For an ISO 27001 Audit? The best way to prepare for an ISO 27001 audit is to have a well-documented ISMS. This includes having policies and procedures in place that meet the requirements of the standard. In addition, you should designate a team of employees who are responsible for managing the ISMS. These employees should be trained on ISO 27001 and the audit process. You should also create an audit plan that outlines the steps you will take to prepare for the audit. This plan should be reviewed and updated on a regular basis. Finally, you should conduct internal audits to identify any weaknesses in your ISMS. Preparing For an ISO 27001 Audit Is Easier Than It Seems Although you might expect it to be difficult, this process is straightforward. title: How to Identify and Prevent 5 Common Lawn Weeds in Utah
author: DonklePhant
content: It can be frustrating when your beautiful lawn is overtaken by undesirable grass. Unexpected weather variations, some underlying issues with your yard, or implementing new soils can lead to a prolific amount of lawn weeds. This article will discuss common lawn weeds in Utah and ways you can prevent them from taking over your lawn. Read on to make sure your lawn remains weed-free and attractive. 1. Dandelions Dandelions are a common weed in Utah. They can be identified by their bright yellow flowers and long, slender leaves. They are often found in lawns, gardens, and parks. Dandelions are not harmful to humans or animals, but they can be a nuisance. If you want to get rid of dandelions, you can pull them up by the root or dig them up with a shovel. You can also use a weed killer , but be careful not to damage other plants. 2. Crabgrass Crabgrass is a type of annual grass that germinates in early spring and grows. It has a shallow root system and thick, coarse leaves. The best way to prevent crabgrass is to make sure your lawn is healthy and thick. This will crowd out crabgrass and make it easier to control. Mowing your lawn regularly will also help to prevent crabgrass. If you do have crabgrass, you can spot treat it with a herbicide. 3. Nutsedge If you have ever seen a lawn with yellow patches, it’s likely due to nutsedge. Nutsedge is a weed that is common in Utah lawns. It is identified by its yellow-green color and its triangular shape. Nutsedge can be prevented by mowing your lawn often and removing any dead leaves or debris. 4. White clover White clover is a common weed in Utah lawns. It is a low-growing plant with small white flowers. The leaves are often three-lobed and the plant can spread. White clover is difficult to control once it becomes established. The best way to prevent it from invading your lawn is to keep a thick, healthy grass stand. This will prevent the white clover from getting a foothold. If you already have white clover on your lawn, the best way to control it is to mow it often. This will prevent it from flowering and spreading. 5. Common Mullein Common mullein (Verbascum thapsus) is a common weed in Utah lawns, gardens, and agricultural areas. It is a biennial plant that grows from a rosette of basal leaves in its first year to a tall stalk with yellow flowers in its second year. Common mullein is a problem in Utah’s lawns, gardens, and agricultural areas due to its ability to spread fast and outcompete other plants. The best way to control common mullein is to prevent it from establishing itself in the first place. This can be done by removing seeds and rosettes from the area, and by keeping the area clear of mullein seedlings. If common mullein does establish in an area, it can be controlled by mowing, herbicides, and other methods. title: 7 Security Measures You Can Take to Protect Your Business
author: DonklePhant
content: Did you know that each year over 300,000 robberies occur? These unfortunate incidents can happen to anyone. But, all too often unsecured businesses tend to be the target. If your business has recently been robbed, or you’re just worried about the possibility, you’re likely looking into security options. That’s why we made this article. In it, we’ll be going over seven of the best security measures you can take to protect your business. That way, you can sleep easy knowing it’s safe. Let’s get started! 1. Perform a Risk Assessment When thinking about security measures it’s always a good idea to perform a risk assessment first. Without one of these, you’re just shooting in the dark in terms of security improvements. An honest assessment of risks helps you learn which security measures you have in your place that currently work. However, more importantly, it allows you to identify weak spots in your security. Maybe your aisle arrangement is prone to shoplifter blind spots. Or, perhaps one of your backdoor’s lock systems is easy to break into. Without knowing where the problem lies, you won’t know where to begin with security measures for your business. So, consider hiring a professional security company to perform a risk assessment. That way, you can prioritize areas that are your biggest current threat. 2. Install an Alarm System Thieves hate attention. And, few things are going to draw attention more quickly than a good alarm system. Modern-day systems can even immediately alert the police if you don’t enter a code. At the very least you want a basic system that’s been installed by a professional. This will let you know when someone enters the business without permission. However, depending on the type of business you are you might want a more advanced alarm system. For example, let’s say you’re a retail business. Shoplifters could be costing you hundreds or even thousands of dollars. In these cases, you’ll want to get a specific alarm system that detects when unpaid items are leaving your store. When you get an alarm system make sure that you get it regularly tested. The last thing you want to do is spend a lot of money on security only for it not to work. 3. Hire Security Not every business will require on-site security guards. But, there are some situations where it’s called for to protect your company. One example is if you have expensive inventory on-site that you’re worried about. You should also consider them if you’ve experienced a lot of break-ins recently. Nothing dissuades criminals like an in-person physical presence. Just make sure you choose a security guard company that properly trains their employees. You don’t want anyone getting hurt, even if they’re trespassing. 4. Set-Up Cameras Security cameras are a bit of a no-brainer for business owners worried about company protection. For one thing, they record any theft as it’s occurring. Whether it’s an active robbery in the middle of the day or trespassing after hours, the cameras will catch it. This will then help the police or public identify the criminal. Once they’re apprehended you have one less criminal to worry about breaking in. But, catching thieves isn’t the only thing that these cameras do. Their mere presence is often enough to dissuade criminals. Typically, thieves will case an area before they rob it. They do this to look for weak security points. And, if they see cameras it’s usually enough to convince them the business isn’t worth their time. Security cameras are also good for insurance purposes. It will make the claims process a lot easier if you get robbed. 5. Train Your Employees One major security weak point could be your employees. They might be doing things like leaving doors unlocked when they leave, inviting people into the building, or engaging in risky cyber behavior on company property. You should lay out strict security guidelines in terms of securing the property when they leave, as well as securing their own devices. Send out a company-wide email, or print off reminders. That way, everyone is on the same page when it comes to business protection. 6. Security Window Films When people think of commercial window films they mainly think of cooling. These films block out UV rays which can make rooms much cooler. However, this is far from the only benefit they provide. Security window films provide a good degree of privacy by blocking out visibility from busy streets. And these types of commercial security window films even come with shatter-proof capabilities. So, if anyone does try to enter by breaking a window, they won’t have any luck. 7. Don’t Forget About IT Security In the past business owners only had to worry about physical crime happening around their commercial property. Sadly, that’s no longer the case. These days, cybercrime has never been higher. For some businesses, IT security might not be at the top of the list. And that’s fine if you don’t rely on technology much for your day-to-day operations. A little common sense and cybersecurity software should keep you safe. But, if your employees access company information on their devices, or you have your own server, you need IT security. If you have a small business, the best way to do this is to outsource your digital data protection. Just make sure you pick a dependable company that can advise you on the best cybersecurity methods for your needs. Appreciate Learning How to Protect Your Business? Keep Reading We hope these safety tips helped you learn some security measures that will protect your business. There’s only one thing worse than being robbed and that’s being robbed again. So, don’t wait around for this to happen. Take your business security seriously and learn from past mistakes. Did you learn something from this article? title: Top Tips For Conducting a Successful Live Cell Imaging Experiment
author: DonklePhant
content: Live cell imaging offers an unprecedentedly clear look at fast-paced biological processes. Thanks to recent advances in technology, it’s becoming more and more popular. But it isn’t infallible, and it’s always most effective when researchers are prepared. Without preparation, researchers using live cell imaging techniques risk losing data and generating misleading results. Most importantly, though, they also risk wasting precious time. Read on, and we’ll help you make sure your research produces results you know you can trust. Maintain the Right Environment Before you start to conduct your research, make sure you’ve created the right environmental conditions for your samples. The conditions you need will depend on the samples you are using, so make sure you know what you need before you start! You need to make sure that you have the right temperature, humidity and gas levels. If you don’t get the conditions right, your cells will weaken. This will make it harder for you to get accurate data from your experiment. You can use an incubator or chamber to maintain stable environmental conditions. You should also consider using air conditioning or dehumidifiers to keep the room temperature and humidity at a stable level during your experiment. Avoid Contamination Any live cell imaging experiment needs to take precautions against cross-culture contamination. Cross-culture contamination can happen when foreign cells are introduced to the cells you want to observe. This usually happens via unclean equipment. Before you start your experiment, make sure to sterilize any pipettes and open devices . This will minimize the risk of outside cells finding their way into your experiment, potentially jeopardizing your results. You should also try to move your cell as little as possible during the experiment. The more you move it, the greater the risk of contamination. Prevent Phototoxicity During live cell imaging, you’ll need to use a light source to get clear images of your cell samples. But too much light exposure can cause phototoxicity in your cells. Phototoxicity can cause cell damage or even cell death, putting your experiment at risk. It can also cause cells to behave in unusual ways, which may give you less useful results. Ultraviolet light is phototoxic, so you should avoid UV light sources if you can. Turning off the light source when not capturing images can also reduce cell exposure to light. And as a rule, it’s best to make sure you have the most advanced imaging tools available. They’re built to prevent phototoxicity and give you more reliable data. Success in Live Cell Imaging Live cell imaging is at the forefront of cell research in almost every scientific field. With the right tools and the right preparation, you can conduct research at the cutting edge of cellular biology. Who knows what biological processes your work will uncover?
