title: Obi: Expect no blame game from us, we’ll deliver measurable results from day one
author: Adesuwa Tsan
content: …says 20 percent credit will be given to small businesses …elections will be won at polling booths, not courts – Campaign council From Adesuwa Tsan, Abuja Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has pledged an uncompromising war against corruption, promising emergency measures to tackle insecurity, hunger, unemployment and the country’s electricity crisis if elected president in 2027. Obi, who is seeking the presidency with Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso as his running mate, said Nigerians would no longer have to contend with a government that blames previous administrations for its failures, insisting that the purpose of governance is to solve problems and improve living conditions. Speaking at a dinner in Abuja on Monday to mark the inauguration of the party’s National Presidential Campaign Council, unveiling of its national secretariat and presentation of certificates of return to candidates, Obi promised measurable improvements in governance from the first day of an NDC administration. “The purpose of governance is to solve problems, not to blame people. Kwankwaso and I will not blame anybody. We will create that new Nigeria that is possible,” he declared. The former Anambra State governor said the country’s economic and security challenges required a fundamental change in leadership and the management of public resources, arguing that increased government revenue and borrowing had not translated into improved living conditions for Nigerians. He challenged the administration of President Bola Tinubu to account for its spending, alleging that capital expenditure under the 2023, 2024 and 2025 budgets remained below 20 per cent and that contractors were experiencing payment difficulties. “We must stop people from stealing public money. We must use public money for the public good. And that will be seen, it will be shown,” Obi said. He insisted that public officeholders must be held accountable for the management of public funds, adding that anyone found culpable of corruption must answer in accordance with the law. “We don’t want you to hire us to tell you about our problem. It’s only in Nigeria that you hire people, and they start reminding you of what happened in the past. No, we don’t want you to hire us to tell you about our problem. We want you to hire us to improve from today,” he said. Obi also promised to declare an emergency in the security sector, arguing that the president must demonstrate direct leadership in responding to attacks, kidnappings and other threats to lives and property. “If they say there is a problem in Jos, he will go to Jos,” he said, adding that he would visit communities affected by insecurity, including those in Plateau, Benue, Zamfara, Sokoto and Borno states. Furthermore, he promised an agricultural emergency, particularly in northern Nigeria, where insecurity has disrupted farming and restricted the use of productive land. “We have vast land in the north. When we secure the north, our farmers must go back and produce what we eat and what we use for our industries,” he said. The NDC candidate linked improved security and agricultural production to food availability, lower prices, job creation and industrial development, insisting that Nigeria must move away from an economy driven by consumption and borrowing to one anchored on production. On education, Obi expressed concern over the number of out-of-school children, saying the country could not achieve sustainable development without investing in human capital. “We must create a society where a child of nobody will be somebody without knowing anybody,” he said. In healthcare, he renewed his pledge to establish a functional primary healthcare centre in every ward within two years of assuming office, while promising emergency interventions in electricity generation, transmission and distribution. “We will declare emergency on generation, transmission, and distribution,” he said, describing reliable electricity as essential to industrial growth, job creation and lower operating costs for businesses. Obi also promised to improve access to credit for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), saying the businesses, despite numbering more than 40 million, received less than five per cent of bank lending. He said an NDC government would ensure that more than 20 per cent of credit went to small businesses, alongside tax holidays and other incentives to stimulate production and employment. “We will put a mark to it. We will ensure that over 20% of credits will go to small businesses. We will support them,” he said. The former governor criticised what he described as excessive foreign trips by Tinubu, arguing that the president should devote more attention to domestic challenges and spend time with communities grappling with insecurity. He also urged political actors to refrain from intimidating NDC supporters and other participants in lawful political activities, insisting that the 2027 elections should be contested on the basis of ideas rather than violence. “Humility and civility are not weaknesses. It is a virtue. Good behaviour is not a weakness. It is a virtue,” Obi said. “The revolution that is coming is a revolution of the ballot,” he declared, urging Nigerians to defend electoral integrity and demand free, fair and credible elections. Meanwhile, Chairman of the NDC Campaign Advisory Council, BD Lawal, warned against electoral violence and attempts to manipulate the 2027 election, declaring that the party would not tolerate attacks on its supporters. Lawal, who spoke at the inauguration of the party’s election committees, urged members to monitor the voting and collation processes to ensure that results were properly counted, recorded and announced. “This election will be won and lost at the polling booths, not the courts,” he said. Earlier, NDC national chairman, Senator Moses Cleopas, charged candidates to regard their nominations as a responsibility to the electorate, warning that the party would not tolerate unfulfilled promises. “If we fail to bring water for you in two years, if we open our mouths to say, vote for us again, please don’t vote for us,” he said. The party also unveiled its national secretariat at 393 Etang Obuli Crescent, Jabi, Abuja, which is expected to serve as its administrative headquarters and campaign coordination centre ahead of the 2027 general elections. title: 2027: INEC announces online access to preliminary voters’ register
author: Lawrence Agbo
content: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has announced plans to publish the preliminary register of voters for the 2027 general elections on its website, allowing Nigerians to access the document online. The commission said the decision followed concerns raised by citizens and other stakeholders about the need to make the register available electronically in addition to the physical display previously conducted at Registration Areas. In a statement issued on Monday, INEC said the move was intended to improve public access to the register and strengthen confidence in the electoral process. “Accordingly, and in furtherance of its commitment to transparency, accessibility and public confidence in the electoral process, the Commission has decided to make available on its online platform https://display.inecnigeria.org the same Preliminary Register of Voters earlier displayed at the Registration Areas,” the statement said. The commission added that the online publication would complement the physical exercise and enable more Nigerians to examine the preliminary register. “This additional measure complements the physical display already undertaken and is intended to facilitate wider public access to the register,” it stated. The statement was signed by Mohammed Kudu Haruna, chairman of INEC’s Information and Voter Education Committee (IVEC). INEC said it was continuing to process claims and objections arising from the preliminary register exercise in line with the Electoral Act, 2026. The commission explained that the process would precede the certification and publication of the final register of voters, scheduled for December 15, 2026. It also acknowledged the interest shown by Nigerians and other stakeholders in the exercise, reaffirming its commitment to transparency and accountability. “The Commission appreciates the continued interest and constructive engagement of Nigerians and stakeholders and reiterates its commitment to transparency, accountability and the faithful implementation of the Electoral Act, 2026 in delivering credible elections,” the statement added. title: $1t economy: RMRDC DG hinges actualisation on processing local resources
author: Romanus Ugwu
content: …Urges Obi to consider joining APC to actualise presidential ambition The Director-General of Raw Materials Research and Development Council (RMRDC), Nnanyelugo Ike-Muonso, has stated that Nigeria’s ambition of building a $1 trillion economy would depend substantially on the ability to process local resources, strengthen manufacturing and reduce dependence on imported industrial inputs. Ike-Muonso equally appealed to the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, to shelve his ambition for next year’s presidential election, and consider joining the All Progressives Congress (APC) to actualise his ambition of presiding over the country. He further argued that the debate ahead of 2027 should extend beyond individual ambitions to include an assessment of the policies and programmes needed to diversify the economy, create jobs and strengthen domestic production. The DG also claimed that Tinubu administration’s Renewed Hope Agenda had created a policy framework within which institutions such as the RMRDC could advance local raw-material development, industrialisation, import substitution and value addition. The Council, according to him, was pursuing initiatives aimed at moving Nigeria away from the export of unprocessed commodities towards a production-based economy capable of creating jobs, attracting investment and strengthening domestic manufacturing. Among its policy proposals is a legislative framework intended to require at least 30 per cent value addition to raw materials before export, a measure designed to encourage domestic processing and ensure that more of the economic benefits from Nigeria’s natural resources remain within the country. Speaking at an interactive session with newsmen in Abuja, he expressed concerns that Obi participating in next year’s presidential election might divide the vote to guarantee a southern candidate winning the election and truncating the principle of power rotation between the North and South, which has shaped Nigeria’s political calculations since the return to democracy in 1999. While urging Obi to consider joining APC, the RMRDC Chief Executive Officer argued that engagement within the ruling party could provide the needed opportunity to contribute to policy debates, understand its governance structures and participate in the development programmes implemented by ruling party-controlled states. “Presidential ambition must be balanced with the larger interests of national unity, political stability and the need to sustain policies that can transform the economy. “Nigeria has developed a political tradition of power rotation between the North and South, and respecting that understanding can help strengthen confidence among the country’s diverse political constituencies,” he said. “Peter Obi has built a political following and brought issues of public expenditure, accountability and economic management into the national conversation. Those issues deserve sustained engagement. But political leadership also requires strategic decisions about when to contest, when to collaborate and how best to contribute to national development,” he said. Speaking further, he said that: “The opportunity before Nigeria is to move beyond exporting raw commodities and build an economy in which our natural resources support local factories, generate employment and create wealth within our communities,” he said. He said that the RMRDC is also promoting the identification and development of raw-material resources across the country’s 774 Local Government Areas (LGAs) to encourage investment in processing facilities and industrial clusters. Its initiatives include strengthening access to raw-material information for manufacturers and investors, promoting research commercialisation and encouraging collaboration between universities, research institutions and private-sector operators. The Council’s Research and Demonstration Plant Complex and other research-industry initiatives are intended to help translate scientific discoveries and indigenous technologies into commercially viable products. Ike-Muonso said these interventions were particularly important for small and medium-scale enterprises, which require reliable access to local industrial inputs, appropriate technologies and investment opportunities to expand production. He maintained that infrastructure development across the South-East could complement the Council’s industrialisation agenda by improving the movement of raw materials, finished products and agricultural produce. Among the major federal road projects in the region are the Enugu–Onitsha and Enugu–Port Harcourt expressways, the Enugu–Abakaliki road and access roads connecting the Second Niger Bridge. The projects are intended to improve connectivity between the South-East and neighbouring regions, reduce transportation difficulties and facilitate access to markets. In Enugu State, projects highlighted during a Federal Government inspection in June 2026 included the Enugu International Specialist Hospital, the Abakpa Junction flyover interchange, the dualisation of the Enugu International Airport Road and the reconstruction of sections of major federal road corridors. The state government also showcased its Smart Green Schools initiative and a tractor assembly plant as part of its broader development programme. In Ebonyi State, projects inspected included sections of the Trans-Sahara Superhighway, the Ndi-Egbe Bridge linking Ebonyi with Cross River State, rural roads, educational facilities and housing initiatives. In Abia State, the projects highlighted included the Ohafia–Umuahia Federal Road, sections of the Enugu–Port Harcourt Expressway and the state-funded Umuahia–Uzuakoli–Akara–Ohafia Road. In Imo State, projects highlighted in July 2026 included the Okigwe–Owerri Road, the Owerri–Obowo–Umuahia Road and improvements to Sam Mbakwe International Cargo Airport, alongside interventions in education and healthcare. The projects involve different funding and implementation arrangements, with responsibilities shared between federal and state governments. Their expected benefits include improved transportation, stronger commercial links and increased opportunities for investment. Ike-Muonso said the ultimate test of governance was whether public policies translated into measurable improvements in people’s lives through employment, better public services, lower business costs and increased productive capacity. title: Amnesty condemns brutal killing of Islamic cleric in Katsina
author: John Ogunsemore
content: Amnesty International has strongly condemned the brutal killing of renowned Islamic preacher, Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka in Katsina State . In a Monday statement posted on Facebook , Amnesty said the cleric was killed by gunmen on motorbikes as he stepped out of his house in Dutsin-Ma to go for his usual evening preaching. “The Nigerian authorities must immediately and effectively investigate the incident and ensure that those suspected of being responsible are brought to justice,” Amnesty said. The organisation described Sheik Masussuka as a preacher who consistently used his preaching to promote cooperation, peaceful coexistence, interfaith dialogue and understanding among Muslim faithful, adding that he was notable for preaching against violent extremism and radicalisation. “The late Islamic cleric faced threats to life and intimidation — all through his life,” Amnesty added. Meanwhile, the killing has been confirmed by the Katsina State Police Command. Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) of the command, DSP Abubakar Sadiq Aliyu, said the attack occurred at about 7:30 pm on Monday, October 26, in front of the scholar’s residence in Dutsin-Ma, when two armed men on a motorcycle opened fire. The police said Masussuka and his friend, Adamu Abubakar, sustained fatal gunshot injuries and were pronounced dead at the hospital. Commissioner of Police, CP Ali Umar Fage, announced an investigation into the incident, ordering the deployment of tactical and operational teams to track down the fleeing suspects. Governor Dikko Umaru Radda has also condemned the killing, describing Masussuka as a voice for peaceful coexistence and interfaith harmony. title: Burna Boy makes history as first Nigerian artiste to present Ballon d’Or award
author: Seyi Babalola
content: Grammy-winning Nigerian singer Damini Ebunoluwa Ogulu, popularly known as Burna Boy, has become the first Nigerian artiste to present an award at the Ballon d’Or ceremony. The singer, popularly known for his hit song Last Last, presented the 2026 Sócrates Award to Arsenal forward Bukayo Saka at the London Palladium on Monday, October 26. The ceremony marked the 70th edition of the Ballon d’Or awards and the first time the event was held in London. Organisers moved the ceremony to mark 70 years since England’s Stanley Matthews won the inaugural award in 1956. Before presenting the award, Burna Boy spoke about his football academy in Nigeria and its aim of supporting the game at home. “Something I started a few years ago, just to support the football culture back home. Hopefully, inshallah, one day I’ll come back here to see one of my people getting an award in Ballon d’Or,” he said. The Sócrates Award recognises footballers who use their influence to support humanitarian causes. Saka, who represents England and has Nigerian heritage, received the honour for his charitable work with BigShoe. The organisation supports medical treatment for children, including operations in Nigeria. Burna Boy’s appearance at the ceremony came a day after his halftime performance at the NFL Paris game. title: Nigerians borrow to eat as food costs swallow 120% of income – Oyedele
author: Goli Innocent
content: The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has disclosed that some Nigerian households spend as much as 120 per cent of their income on food, forcing many to borrow money or depend on relatives to survive. Oyedele, who spoke at Chatham House in London, said a government survey revealed that food costs had exceeded the total income of some households, highlighting the severity of the country’s cost-of-living crisis. “In fact, there was a survey we did that shows that up to 120 per cent of household income is spent on food. “Like, how do you spend 120 per cent of your income? You borrow food before the end of the month,” he said. The minister said Nigeria’s poverty rate remained above 50 per cent despite an unemployment rate of about five per cent, warning that low unemployment figures did not reflect the financial struggles of millions of Nigerians who have jobs but cannot afford basic necessities. “That tells you something. As a policymaker, you don’t sit back and say we don’t have unemployment. You have working poor,” he said. Oyedele attributed the pressure on household budgets to persistently high food prices, noting that food inflation was not easing as quickly as the headline inflation rate. He said food inflation stood at 19.6 per cent in September, adding that the cost of essential items such as tomatoes, garri and beans remained a major concern for households. “Headline inflation is falling faster than the price of a basket of tomatoes, gari, and beans. And this widens inequality,” he said. The minister added: “Macroeconomic stability means little to a mother who still cannot afford food.” Oyedele identified low agricultural productivity, seasonal farming, post-harvest losses, inadequate storage facilities, high transportation costs and insecurity in farming communities as major factors driving food prices upwards. He cited the loss of as much as 60 per cent of tomatoes after harvest as an example of the challenges confronting Nigeria’s agricultural sector. According to him, the government is investing in agricultural technology, irrigation systems to support year-round farming, improved storage facilities and access to finance for smallholder farmers to increase food production and reduce waste. He also said the administration was providing direct assistance through a cash transfer programme that had reached more than 10 million households. “In the short term, the administration is providing direct support through a cash transfer programme that has reached more than 10 million households. Payments are made digitally and beneficiaries are verified with National Identification Numbers to reduce leakage,” he said. The minister further argued that Nigeria’s household economic challenges were rooted in structural weaknesses rather than fuel taxation, stating that the country had no taxes on fuel. He said the government was prioritising agriculture and non-tradable services, which together employ 81.4 per cent of working Nigerians. Oyedele explained that the aim was to grow these sectors faster than the overall economy, raise household incomes and gradually reduce dependence on government cash transfers. His remarks highlight the growing challenge facing policymakers as millions of Nigerians struggle to meet basic food needs despite efforts to stabilise the economy and improve agricultural production. title: 14 Chinese, Nigerian arrested over illegal lithium processing in Ogun
author: John Ogunsemore
content: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has arrested 14 Chinese nationals and one Nigerian over illegal lithium processing in Ogun State . In a Monday statement, the EFCC said operatives of its Lagos Zonal Directorate 2 arrested the suspects at four illegal lithium processing plants in the Ogere area. They were arrested on Friday, October 23, following credible intelligence and surveillance, the anti-graft commission said. Operatives recovered bags of lithium rocks, 18 mobile devices, four computer laptops, two decoders, a television remote control, and a trailer truck from the suspects. The EFCC said the suspects would be charged to court upon conclusion of investigations. title: 2027: Obi Urges Civility, Warns Against Harassment of Supporters
author: Lawrence Agbo
content: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has cautioned against the harassment of his supporters, insisting that good behaviour and peaceful conduct should not be mistaken for weakness. Obi made the remarks amid political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections, appealing to those targeting his supporters to embrace civility and respect the rights of Nigerians who want to express their political preferences. He said people supporting his political movement should be allowed to participate in the democratic process without intimidation. “For those harassing our supporters, innocent Nigerians who want food, humility and civility are not weaknesses. They are virtues. Nobody has the monopoly of rascality,” Obi said. The former Anambra State governor further urged political actors to conduct themselves responsibly, warning that peaceful behaviour should not be interpreted as an inability to respond to provocation. “Good behaviour is not weakness; it is a virtue. I am warning and pleading with everybody. Enough is enough,” he said. Obi’s comments come as political parties and their supporters intensify activities ahead of the 2027 elections, with political exchanges and competition over public support expected to feature prominently in the coming months. title: Troops destroy ISWAP enclave, neutralise 16 terrorists
author: John Ogunsemore
content: The Joint Task Force (North East), Operation Hadin Kai, has destroyed ISWAP enclaves and neutralised 16 terrorists in the Lake Chad Basin . According to a Monday statement by the Acting Military Information Officer, Captain Mohammed Goni, the operation followed intelligence on the presence of key terrorist leaders and fighters. He disclosed that the coordinated air and artillery strikes were conducted on three suspected terrorist locations in the Tunbunma area of South Lake Chad between 1:00 am and 2:00 am on Monday. The JTF spokesman said Battle Damage Assessment indicated that 16 suspected Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters were neutralised across the targeted locations. Among those reportedly killed were Abu Zubiru, an Arab national, and two associates, Baana Nglewa and Jindullah Sadiq, alongside other fighters. Additionally, Abu Saleem, identified as the Wali of Tunbunma, sustained severe injuries alongside seven others. Operation Hafin Kai reaffirmed that there is no hiding place for terrorists and remains committed to restoring peace and normalcy while conducting intelligence-led operations in the North East. Members of the public were encouraged to provide timely and credible information to security agencies to support ongoing counter-terrorism operations. title: 2027: Obi tells Tinubu to go home, questions capacity to govern
author: Lawrence Agbo
content: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has called on President Bola Tinubu to leave office, questioning whether the President has the energy and capacity required to address Nigeria’s challenges. Obi argued that the country needs a president who is consistently available to respond to emergencies and visit communities affected by insecurity, rather than leaving citizens to face crises without visible leadership. He made the remarks while criticising the government’s handling of Nigeria’s security challenges and calling for a more active approach to governance ahead of the 2027 general elections. “We need him to go home because Nigeria cannot be governed by his energy. Nigeria needs a president who will be available and be there at any location in the country that has a problem,” Obi said. He cited the abduction of large numbers of people as an example of the security challenges he believes require a more direct response from the country’s leadership. “We cannot be in government, and 600 people will be kidnapped and taken into the bush; we will go into that bush with them,” he added. The former Anambra State governor also challenged Nigerians who believe they have the competence and energy to serve to join the political contest, saying leadership requires consistent engagement with the country’s problems. “If you have competence and energy to serve, come and campaign,” Obi said. He further argued that Nigeria could no longer afford leaders who were unavailable when citizens needed them. “We can no longer accept people who are elected and not available. The president of Nigeria must be available at all times and must tour all over Nigeria,” he said. Obi’s comments come as political parties prepare for the 2027 elections, with security, economic hardship and leadership capacity expected to remain key issues in the contest. title: Minor delays coming along Troutdale’s Buxton Road
author: Christopher Keizur
content: Beginning next week folks should expect some minor delays along South Buxton Road, in Troutdale, as Multnomah County road crews begin installing new curb ramps at a trio of intersections. The project will be at Buxton and: Southwest Second Street Southeast Third Street Southwest Fourth Street The plan is for the work to be completed in December, pending weather. The cost for Buxton Road is about $600,000, and comes from Multnomah County’s road funds. There will be delays during daytime weekday hours. Flaggers may be on site directing traffic. Expect signs and barriers as well providing direction for pedestrian detours. Access to local businesses and residential traffic will be maintained throughout the project. Construction hours will also be scheduled to minimize impacts on the nearby Troutdale Elementary School. All of this is part of the County’s Americans with Disabilities Act Transition Plan. Early projects installed new ramps at Northeast Halsey Street and Northeast Market Drive; Northeast Halsey Street and Northeast 230th Court; and 24697 S.E. Stark Street.

title: Letter to the editor | Metzger: Bassett is the type of person you want in the state legislature
author: none
content: Bassett is the type of person you want in the state legislature I filled out my ballot yesterday. As is the case most years, I voted for strangers. I made my best guess on who I think would represent me well. Except this year, someone I know is running for office. I know Nicole Bassett as a small business owner. I met her at her factory and I met the people working the jobs she was creating by repairing clothes that otherwise would have been sent to landfills. She saw a wasteful, broken economic model and instead of complaining about it, she went to work fixing it. It was incredibly inspirational. (Her dog bit my foot, but to be fair, she had warned me that he bites.) When I voted yesterday, I relied on others who vouched for people on the ballot. I can vouch for Nicole. She is exactly the type of person you want representing you in Salem. Vote for Nicole Bassett for District 26 State Senator. Eliot Metzger Clackamas

title: Pair arrested in brazen series of Happy Valley funeral home burglaries
author: Christopher Keizur
content: Two men are in custody after a series of brazen, repeated burglaries at a Happy Valley funeral home. Eliah Leslie Wright, 42, of Eagle Creek, and Robert Eugene Hillis, 30, of Happy Valley, are in custody on charges related to the burglaries. They are being held at the Clackamas County Jail. Wright faces aggravated theft, first-degree theft, two counts of burglary, two counts of possession of a stolen vehicle, and unauthorized use of a motor vehicle. Hillis faces aggravated theft, first-degree theft, two counts of burglary, two counts of possession of a stolen vehicle, unauthorized use of a motor vehicle, and possession of methamphetamine. The investigation into the pair is ongoing. Police also want to return the copper tubing to its rightful owner. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Clackamas County Sheriff’s Office Tip Line at 503-723-4949 or online at: clackcosheriff.us/submitATip . Reference Case # 26-019918. Burglaries On Thursday, Oct. 8, two suspects, accompanied by a dog that ran loose at the crime scene, broke into a shop at Lincoln Memorial Park and Funeral Home, 11801 S.E. Mt. Scott Blvd., in Happy Valley. They made three criminal trips to the funeral home between 1 and 3 a.m., all caught on surveillance footage. First, the two suspects arrived in a white Chevy truck. They broke the shop locks, loaded the truck with power tools, hitched a trailer belonging to the funeral home, and drove away. A short time later, the suspects returned to load more tools into a different trailer they stole and drove away again. They returned a third time, broke into a box containing the keys to a 2025 Ford Transit van and a dump truck, and stole the van. The stolen trailers are valued at $4,000, and the thieves stole an estimated $50,000 worth of tools. One week later, on Thursday, Oct. 15, the thieves struck the same funeral home again. Around 1 a.m., the pair returned to Lincoln Memorial in a different vehicle (an unplated mid-2000s Dodge Durango) with the same dog. This time, after cutting a gate chain, they entered the funeral home’s equipment storage area, stole tools, left for 30 minutes, returned to steal another trailer ($3,200 value) and loaded a John Deere side-by-side utility vehicle ($27,000 value). They eventually left at 1:55 a.m. Arrests At 4:18 a.m. Friday, Oct. 16, a sergeant with the Happy Valley Police Department was patrolling Southeast Vradenburg Road near Southeast 162nd Avenue when he came across an unoccupied white 1995 Chevy truck on the shoulder. Attached was one of the funeral home’s trailers. As he was investigating, a man (Wright) arrived driving an SUV. He walked over and identified himself as the truck’s owner. In addition to the stolen trailer, he had an arrest warrant for first-degree aggravated theft out of Multnomah County. Police said Wright was wearing a mask around his head like a hat at the time of his arrest. Investigators found long-handled bolt cutters and a spool of copper tubing in the truck bed, believed to be stolen. Later that afternoon, around 3 p.m., a second man (Hillis) pulled up to the parked truck on a Honda motorcycle (later found to have an expired registration, no insurance, and no license). Hillis told deputies he was there to get his wallet from the truck. Based on the investigation, deputies also took Hillis into custody. During booking, a plastic bag with meth was found in his back pocket.

title: Debra Jean “Debbie” Ferguson
author: none
content: April 27, 1952 — July 20, 2026 – Beloved wife, best friend, mother, grandmother and great grandmother. Debbie passed away on July 20, 2026 due to advanced pulmonary fibrosis. Her husband Doug and her daughters Tammy (Newcomb) and Lori (Lei) were by her side when she died. During her life she enjoyed many varied activities, among them fishing, camping, hiking, her flower garden, especially her roses and activities with many friends. She also adored and spoiled her dogs, who also adored her. She worked from an early age, starting as a sewing machine operator in the Jantzen production department and finishing her career there after 32 years as the head of the Human Resources department for the sewing factory. After Jantzen moved their production overseas she attended Clackamas Community College, earning an Associates degree in Office Management. She then worked for 2 years at City Sign in Portland and then moved to U.S. Meat and Restaurant Supply in Sandy where she worked for another 12 years before retiring. She is survived by her husband of 43 years, Doug, daughters Tammy and Lori, 6 grandchildren and 14 great grandchildren. Rest in peace, Debra! You left us way too soon.

title: Letter to the editor | Pickett: Al-jaouni will serve Gresham well
author: none
content: As someone who spends a lot of time working alongside people from every walk of life, I’ve come to appreciate leaders who lead with humility, compassion, and a genuine desire to understand others. That’s one of the things I admire most about Joshua Al-jaouni. He is genuinely curious about people and their experiences. He asks thoughtful questions, seeks to understand different perspectives, and takes the time to learn about the challenges and opportunities facing our community. His life experiences have given him a perspective that isn’t always represented in local government. He understands that people come from different backgrounds, face different obstacles, and need different kinds of support to thrive. He approaches issues with empathy and a willingness to learn. I’ve seen firsthand his compassion for people and his commitment to building strong community connections. He believes meaningful progress happens when we bring people together, listen to one another, and work toward shared goals. Joshua brings a thoughtful, collaborative, and servant-hearted approach to leadership. He is committed to helping Gresham be a place where everyone has the opportunity to succeed. He will serve Gresham well, and I’m proud to support Joshua! Andrea Pickett Boring

title: Certification questions arise in Clackamas County sheriff race
author: Christopher Keizur
content: One issue that has come up in the race for Clackamas County Sheriff is the candidates’ eligibility. Specifically, voters are concerned that Interim Sheriff James Rhodes would need to step away from the role for a period of time — if they select him — to get recertified. Rhodes is running against Undersheriff Brad O’Neil to replace Sheriff Angela Brandenburg, who retired earlier this year. Whoever is elected will face serious budget woes for the sheriff’s office. Some have voiced concerns that Rhodes will have an additional distraction. He worked 26 years for the CCSO before retiring in 2021. During that time, his basic police certification lapsed. A person who does not have that must go through the Oregon Department of Public Safety Standards and Training process within the first year of taking office. O’Neil has worked for the CCSO since 1999, with the last two years as an undersheriff. His certification is current. Recertification A law enforcement certification can lapse or expire. It lapses when an officer is separated from their certifiable position for a consecutive period greater than three months. That means they must go through certain requirements to reactivate certification. Certification expires after five years. In both cases, officers must undergo a background investigation, psychological evaluation, fingerprinting, a medical examination, first aid and adult/child CPR certification, completion of the Field Training Manual, signing a code of ethics, and submission of an application for certification. If one year has passed, the person in question must complete eight hours of Firearms or Use of Force Training within 30 days. If two and a half years have passed, a Police Career Officer Development course must be completed. This consists of an 80-hour (two-week) self-study. If more than five years have passed, the 640-hour (16-week) Basic Police training course at the Oregon Public Safety Academy in Salem must be completed. That runs from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday-Friday. Most students stay in the campus dormitory for the duration of the course. “If they are not certified within one year after taking office, the county governing body must declare the office of sheriff vacant,” said a spokesperson with the Department of Public Safety Standards and Training. “These rules apply to all officers with lapsed or expired certifications and are universal across all positions and ranks, from line officers to sheriffs, chiefs, or other command staff.” During public events, Rhodes has stated he is confident only the shorter self-study will be needed. He plans to go through that process after the upcoming levy campaign this spring. Levy, budget issues Clackamas County is planning another Public Safety Levy for the May 2027 election after Measure 3-633 failed in the May 2026 primary with about 62% “No.” The levy first passed in 2006 and funds about 17% of Sheriff’s Office services — patrol deputies, drug enforcement, detectives, and jail staff. The failure ran counter to the trend, after voters have backed the levy three times since its inception. The current levy expires at the end of the year. If that funding isn’t replaced, it would mean losing an estimated 92 positions — about a third of the jail staff and half of patrol. That kind of result would be “catastrophic,” both Rhodes and O’Neil have said.

title: Downtown Gresham’s Wisenheimer Books is a page-turner
author: Christopher Keizur
content: A new independent bookstore has opened on a prominent corner in Downtown Gresham, creating a haven for readers who love to get lost in books. Wisenheimer Books, 10 N.W. Third St., is a true passion project for owner Anna Palmquist. “I’ve always wanted to own a bookstore and be an artist ever since I was a little kid,” she said. “At 55 I decided to start making art; at 60 this place came available.” “I knew I would regret it if I didn’t do this,” Palmquist added. The shop opened Friday, Oct. 9. That was slightly earlier than planned, but so many people were excitedly coming to the door that Palmquist decided to jump in with both feet. “The store is a work in progress. I am always adding new things, and rotating makers and artists,” Palmquist said. “Don’t feel like you have to buy, just come say, ‘Hi’ whenever you like.” The response has been slightly overwhelming, in the best way. So many books were sold in the first couple of days that Palmquist had to raid her own personal collection just to keep things stocked. “People have been unbelievably nice and positive,” Palmquist said. “They walk in and are so excited. People keep telling me they ‘love the vibe.’ They love the offerings, the community, the colors.” Wisenheimer Books has all sorts of genres of books. They carry classics and “banned books,” literary and general fiction, ghost stories and mysteries, poetry and philosophy, non-fiction and cookbooks, art-related books, and sci-fi, horror, and fantasy. “I pick things up that I think people will be interested in,” Palmquist said. Of the books, about 90% are used. On her off days, Palmquist scours the region for new additions. She has a real eye for finding treasures, cultivated by a lifelong passion for reading, two years running on an online shop, and a book nook at the Troutdale Art Center. “People are loving the book choices. I’m flattered but tired because I am searching everywhere for more books,” Palmquist said with a laugh. “For me, it’s quality over quantity.” While the books are in the spotlight, Wisenheimer Books offers many other eclectic things to discover. Palmquist has curated a collection of items from friends, family, and fellow artists in East Multnomah County. Candles, soaps, and lotions are made by a woman who raises Nigerian dwarf goats in East County. Mugs that are engraved at home by one of her neighbors. Handcrafted cards, including some made by her granddaughter. Artwork on the walls by five different folks (there are more walls she is excited to fill). There are records, including some produced by the guys at Gresham Midschool . Around the shop are Dimepiece Rub from Gresham’s Sanguiche sandwich shop . The t-shirts are screen-printed a few blocks away in Downtown. There are puzzles and knickknacks. One of the most popular items flying off the shelves is “Dragon Journals,” which have a satisfying heft and an outer cover that feels like metal scales. “I wanted to be part of the community and help other local makers,” Palmquist said. “We need businesses and people to support each other.” Wisenheimer Books Where: 10 N.W. Third St., in Downtown Gresham Hours: 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. Wed.-Sat., Noon to 5 p.m. Sun. Facebook: Wisenheimer Books Instagram: @wisenheimerbooks

title: Letter to the editor | Reynolds: Brad O’Neil for Clackamas County Sheriff
author: none
content: I’ve had the pleasure of meeting Brad O’Neil several times and been impressed by his experience, credentials, and integrity. At a time when Clackamas County faces serious public safety and budget challenges, O’Neil is the right choice to lead our Sheriff’s Office. It is concerning that O’Neil’s opponent was recently appointed sheriff by the Board of County Commissioners without public input and is not currently certified as an Oregon police officer – a requirement for the position. To become certified, he’ll need four months of training from the state licensing body, followed by field training. The Sheriff’s department faces a budget crisis, with potential layoffs and cuts to critical public safety services. The first 100 days are crucial to the county’s budget cycle planning. We need a sheriff ready to lead immediately, not one completing required certification. O’Neil brings over 27 years of service with the Clackamas County Sheriff’s Office, strong credentials, and a proven ability to build relationships and work collaboratively. title: No evidence voting machines are purposely ‘flipping’ votes, it’s usually user error and can be fixed
author: Loreben Tuquero
content: Claims about voting machines swapping or “flipping” voters’ choices are again going viral as early voting continues during the 2026 midterm elections. The claims have surfaced in multiple states. “There is a very disturbing trend being seen in early voting,” read a Facebook post from the liberal group “The Other 98%.” “Texas, Florida, Tennessee, Ohio are reporting difficulties getting the machines to accept Democratic votes. The machines change them back to Republican unless the voter persists, pressing several times to get the correct vote to go through.” Similar claims also circulated on X and TikTok . Vote flipping or swapping claims have become a recurring theme since the 2020 election, but there is no evidence of voting machines deliberately designed with such flaws or that it is happening on a wide scale. Election officials have said it often is attributable to user error on touch screens. Tennessee, Texas voters’ concerns likely related to user error or screen calibration Dolly Parton’s sister Stella Parton posted Oct. 21 on Facebook that she voted at Hermitage Library in Nashville and her ballot “kept flipping to the wrong candidate.” “I had to go back three times and correct my vote because it kept defaulting to Marsha Blackburn,” she said . WSMV-TV reported that some Tennessee voters picked a candidate on the voting machine and saw a different candidate selected on the screen. They voted in Franklin, Spring Hill or Nolensville, all in Williamson County. Similar complaints were reported in Madison County . Tennessee Coordinator of Elections Mark Goins told WSMV that it “appears to be a voter error,” and could have happened because of an unintended touch on the screen. He said voting equipment is tested before elections. Voters were advised that styluses are available by request to help with the touch screens. The Tennessee Secretary of State told news outlets that among around 400,000 voters who have cast their ballots, the office has received one complaint of that nature. In Texas, KSAT-TV reported that in Bexar County, three voters said voting machines changed or removed their choices. They were able to check their ballots before finalizing them. Michele Carew, Bexar County Elections Administrator, said in a press release, “Reports of mismatched selections are almost always due to user touchscreen sensitivity, not machine malfunction. Touchscreens require a firm, direct tap, and poll workers are trained to assist as needed.” She said the county tests machines for security and accuracy, and voting machines are never connected to the internet. One man in Kendall County said on social media that his mother-in-law had tapped on Democratic candidates but the machine repeatedly switched her choice to Republican candidates. Alicia Pierce, Texas Assistant Secretary of State for Communications, said she is unaware of anyone reporting such issues. Pierce said during this election, Texas is not using machines that directly store voting selections in computer memory, except in rare cases such as to accommodate voters with disabilities. The counties with reported issues use machines that generate a paper ballot and do not store voters’ selections. “Any machines must produce a human-readable paper ballot that a voter can review before casting. We encourage all voters to review their choices before finally casting their ballot,” she said. Williamson County, Davidson County and Madison County in Tennessee , where issues were reported, and Bexar County, Williamson County and Kendall County in Texas use the ExpressVote machines, manufactured by ES&S. ES&S spokesperson Katina Granger told PolitiFact the company has not received widespread reports from election officials about voting technology issues.“Most commonly, reported instances stem from a voter not touching the text box in the correct place. They can touch anywhere inside the large box containing the candidate’s name,” she said. Old videos resurface on social media As new claims are surfacing, old video is being misleadingly reshared, too. An X video posted Oct. 23 shows a person tapping the box next to one candidate, but the screen marking the candidate above. “Can you say national emergency?” the caption reads. “Electronic voting machine will not let voter select the Republican candidate that they want to vote for and automatically selects the Democrat candidate instead.” That video is from 2019 . The people on screen are Tate Reeves and Bill Waller Jr., who were then primary candidates for the Republican nomination for Mississippi governor. PolitiFact explained that video in 2019, too. Another video posted Oct. 22 shows a voting machine not accurately marking the candidate the person is selecting. Other X posts reshared it too as if it’s happening now. But the video is from 2018 , not the 2026 midterm election. The candidates on the screen are Jim Baird and Tobi Beck, who ran for U.S. House in Indiana. What voters should know about touch screen voting Issues involving incorrect choices on a touch screen are “rare,” Granger said. “Statewide and local officials have both repeatedly affirmed that nearly every case comes back to the screen calibration on older touchscreen machines, not a change to anyone’s vote,” Kristin Miles, president of the Texas Association of County Election Officials, said in a statement to PolitiFact. If you encounter an issue with your ballot, you can ask a poll worker for help before casting your vote. Granger and election officials encouraged voters to verify their choices before casting their ballots. There are multiple opportunities to review your vote. Voting selections are displayed on the voting machine screen, on a review screen at the end of the voting session and on a paper ballot generated by the system to confirm your choices. If your printed ballot does not reflect your desired choices, you may notify a poll worker. “There is no scenario in which a voter would be forced to cast a ballot that they believe did not reflect their intentions,” Granger said.

title: At Ohio rally, Barack Obama says told-you-so on his approach to Iran nuclear policy
author: Josie Hollingsworth
content: In some of his highest-profile remarks about President Donald Trump’s decision to launch the Iran war, former President Barack Obama lamented Trump’s decision to exit the 2015 deal Obama negotiated with Iran while speaking at an Oct. 24 campaign rally for Ohio’s Democratic slate, gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton and U.S. Senate candidate Sherrod Brown. During the Cleveland event, speaking about the Iran war, Obama said. “The original rationale was we’re going to go in there and get them to give up their nuclear program, their nuclear weapons. Now, the thing was, Iran didn’t have nuclear weapons because I had put a deal in place that everybody acknowledges kept them from getting nukes, and I didn’t have to fire a missile to do it. I just had to engage in diplomacy. He pulled out of it, starts this war.” Obama’s interpretation of the Iran deal is shared by many specialists. Obama had campaigned on a promise to ensure that Iran did not obtain a nuclear weapon. The negotiated agreement was signed in 2015 by the United States and Iran as well as China, Russia, France, Germany and the United Kingdom. Under the deal, Iran agreed to refrain from pursuing nuclear weapons and to allow continuous monitoring of its compliance in exchange for relief from economic sanctions. Different parts of the agreement were scheduled to last between 10 and 25 years; some elements were to last indefinitely. Obama officials hoped for future renegotiations. Iran agreed to relinquish 97% of its enriched uranium stockpile and 70% of its centrifuges, which are machines used to enrich uranium. It also agreed to stop plutonium production and to dismantle a plutonium reactor. If Iran broke any of these pledges, the other signatories would be able to reimpose sanctions, a process known as a “snapback” provision. Over the 28 months the deal was in effect, the International Atomic Energy Agency said it found Iran committed no violations, aside from some minor infractions that were addressed. In 2018, Trump pulled the U.S. out of the deal. The U.S. then imposed economic sanctions on Iran , and Iran reduced its compliance with the deal, including curbing compliance with international inspectors. title: Fact-checking Trump, Donalds and Moody as they rally voters in Fort Myers, Florida
author: Samantha Putterman
content: With 11 days until the election, President Donald Trump headlined a rally at Florida Gulf Coast University’s campus in Fort Myers to boost Republican candidates on the ballot. Republican incumbent U.S. Sen. Ashley Moody and Republican gubernatorial candidate U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds spoke in Donalds’ home district ahead of the president and painted their Democratic opponents — state Rep. Angie Nixon and David Jolly, respectively, as extreme. Trump said Democrats chose “the most extreme anti-American radicals ever to seek office,” but, he said, “This is the free state of Florida, where people come to escape communists and not to elect them.” We fact-checked some of their claims. RELATED: What Trump’s communism claims miss about Democrats and democratic socialists Trump: Jolly is “pledging to turn Florida into a sanctuary state.” The term “sanctuary” typically is used to describe jurisdictions that limit cooperation with federal immigration enforcement authorities. Jolly says he wouldn’t require statewide 287(g) agreements that mandate local police participation with federal Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations. But he’s open to local officials implementing them. In a February interview with Spectrum News, Jolly said local-federal police cooperation should be suspended while ICE agents use masks and until “we know that individual due process is being protected for everybody.” Around 347 state and local agencies in Florida have signed these agreements, the most of any state. Jolly also has said that local police should focus resources on community safety rather than immigration sweeps. His platform supports giving people a pathway to legal status and work permits for immigrants in the country illegally who have been longterm residents. Donalds: “Ten years ago (Jolly) said that he wanted to see the end of Roe v. Wade, as a Republican. But today as a Democrat, he says he wants to bring Roe v. Wade back.” This is accurate, and Jolly has acknowledged it. Jolly was a Republican when he served in the U.S. House from 2014 to 2017, then became an independent and eventually a Democrat in 2025 Jolly opposed Roe v. Wade as a Republican and aligned with anti-abortion policies . Today, Jolly says he supports Roe. v. Wade and wants to codify into law Roe’s standard of abortion access up to fetal viability — the point of gestation when the fetus can survive outside the womb. The U.S. Supreme Court overturned Roe in 2022, and Florida currently has a 6-week abortion ban . Jolly has said his views on abortion have evolved since his time in Congress and that he previously conflated his personal faith teachings with his political stance. Moody: Nixon “signs up to defund the police, kneecap our military, abolish prisons, let noncitizens vote, do away with our borders.” This is misleading. Moody was alluding to Nixon joining the Democratic Socialists of America, an organization, not a political party. The organization has not endorsed Nixon. While Moody accurately describes the DSA platform , Nixon said she doesn’t align with everything the organization stands for. “I don’t fully align with anybody’s full platform 100%, not even the Democratic Party,” Nixon told WLRN in August. Nixon’s campaign has told PolitiFact she supports public safety, addressing the root causes of crime, and securing the U.S. border while also establishing clear pathways to citizenship and rebuilding immigration enforcement. Nixon said she doesn’t support abolishing all prisons, but wants to end for-profit prisons. Nixon opposes the U.S. war with Iran, and favors diplomacy for conflict resolution. She has advocated for heavier scrutiny of the defense budget. Nixon’s campaign said she “supports the right of every eligible American citizen to vote.” She does not call for allowing noncitizen voting. Donalds: When Jolly was a Republican, he “said that he was a staunch defender of the Second Amendment. But now as a Democrat, he’s somebody who rants and raves about ‘who cares about the Second Amendment.’” Jolly’s shift on gun control is accurate. The quote Donalds referenced followed a mass shooting in Maine three years ago. In Congress, Jolly typically aligned with the Republican Party on bills favoring firearm access. Since leaving the party, Jolly has criticized the GOP stance on firearms while saying he supports the Second Amendment. Donalds’ reference to Jolly saying “who cares about the Second Amendment” stems from an October 2023 MSNBC clip where Jolly criticized American gun culture. “You can say I don’t agree with the Second Amendment. Maybe I don’t, I don’t care,” Jolly said. “…We have to crush the culture of guns in the United States.” The Oct. 25, 2023, interview followed a mass shooting in Lewiston, Maine , where a gunman killed 18 people at a bowling alley and restaurant. Jolly’s 2026 campaign stance calls for stricter firearm regulations, including banning the sale of new assault weapons, requiring universal background checks and strengthening gun storage mandates and training requirements. title: Santa Claus or Tony Soprano? Trump’s midterm ‘goodies’ are conditioned on GOP control
author: Amy Sherman
content: President Donald Trump is crisscrossing the country in campaign mode like a Republican Santa Claus, pulling out promised “goodies” for voters — a manufacturing facility here, a military academy there and $5,000 checks. There’s just one condition: Voters have to keep Republicans in control of Congress for the final two years of his second term. As he visits red states, some with tossup races that will determine congressional control, Trump has said he will deliver healthcare settlement money to veterans and a Space Academy. He said he would send hurricane relief money to North Carolina if the Republican wins, before adding he was “joking.” At an Oct. 19 Kansas rally , he said if voters want low-cost diesel fuel, they must vote for the Republicans running for governor and U.S. Senate. “You have to do it,” Trump said. “And some more goodies. You know, I always heard that when you’re president, you have a little bit of an advantage and I sort of see why now, actually.” Trump’s blunt transactional style sets him apart from other presidents. “Presidents routinely promise that if their party retains control of Congress, they will enact programs that benefit a particular constituency or interest group. That’s normal politics,” John Pitney, a Claremont McKenna College American politics professor, said. “Trump is different. He suggested — and sometimes said outright — that he will personally grant benefits only if he gets an election result he wants.” Here’s what Trump has promised voters ahead of the Nov. 3 midterms. THE MAGA-METER : How PolitiFact is tracking Trump’s second-term campaign promises An ethanol waiver in Kansas At the Kansas rally , Trump praised U.S. Sen. Roger Marshall, the Republican seeking re-election against Democratic challenger Adam Hamilton, and tied the contest to gasoline prices. In an effort to address high costs at the pump, the Environmental Protection Agency in March issued a temporary emergency fuel waiver to allow nationwide sales of gasoline with a 15% ethanol blend to be sold starting in May. Known as E15, it is slightly cheaper than conventional gasoline but is usually prohibited in the summer because of concerns that it adds smog in high temperatures. “I also gave Kansas a waiver to sell E15 all year round. And with Roger Marshall in the Senate, we will make year-round E15 permanent,” Trump said. “But if Adam Hamilton is in, I’m not doing it. That’s it. I’m only doing it for him.” Pitney said that kind of statement may not be illegal but “bears some resemblance to bribery or even extortion.” He added, “ Other presidents have tried to model themselves on Washington or Lincoln. Trump is the first to model himself on Tony Soprano.” The E15 waiver was neither exclusively for Kansas nor unique to the Trump administration. Summertime waivers have become common, including during the Biden administration . The waiver lowers posted prices at the pump slightly, said Kenneth Gillingham, a Yale energy and environmental economist. “However, it comes at a cost of lowering fuel economy, so the savings generally cancel out or come close to canceling out.” A space academy in Ohio During one of many Ohio rallies to promote U.S. Sen. Jon Husted’s re-election and Vivek Ramaswamy’s bid for governor, Trump said a new Space Academy could land in Ohio. The Trump administration wants to break ground on the astronaut and scientist training school by 2027 , with a permanent location completed by 2031. “And every other state wants it. So many states want it,” Trump said Oct. 3 . “And I have no doubt that as the birthplace of aviation and the home of the Wright brothers, if we win the midterms, Ohio will be very, very strongly considered.” In August, Trump issued a proclamation calling for a commission to provide a report in late December about establishing the academy and a process to select the location. Several states including Texas, Florida and Ohio are expected to submit bids by Nov. 16 . $100 million taxpayer investment in Kentucky manufacturing facility During an Oct. 17 Kentucky rally , Trump announced another project he said hinged on the Republican, Andy Barr, winning the U.S. Senate against Democrat Charles Booker. Trump said the Defense Department will invest $100 million in Antheia’s drug manufacturing facility in Winchester, Kentucky. “But you have to win, Andy, otherwise forget it,” Trump said. The next day, Antheia announced it had received a commitment from the Defense Department for a direct, long-term loan of up to $80 million. “The conditional loan commitment specifies additional steps Antheia must complete before financial close, including satisfying various financial, legal, technical, investment, due diligence, and other requirements,” Antheia wrote. The company’s announcement did not list Republicans winning office as a condition. Speeding up North Carolina settlement and disaster relief claims Trump said keeping Republican majorities would help people seeking financial help for illnesses linked to contaminated water at Camp Lejeune, a North Carolina Marine Corps base. “If we win the House and the Senate I am directing the Department of Justice to settle all remaining legitimate claims as soon as possible and get it off the books and get it finished,” Trump said Oct. 20 at the Pitt-Greenville Airport. “If we don’t win, there’s no money,” Trump said. “If we do win, you’re getting it.” A 2022 federal law allows people to file a claim if they lived or worked at the military base between 1953 and 1987 and became ill after exposure to dangerous chemicals. The Justice Department announced in September it had paid out $879 million so far, but a backlog remains . Democratic Gov. Josh Stein responded on X , “Real leaders fight for the people, not for power. To condition doing the right thing by sick North Carolinians on who wins the election is foul.” Trump said at a September rally that he would send more Hurricane Helene aid to North Carolina only if Republican Michael Whatley wins the U.S. Senate over former Democratic Gov. Roy Cooper. Then he said he was “kidding.” Trump’s promises “can make voters want to do what he says, so they can get the money, or it can make voters want to do the opposite, because they don’t like being threatened,” Whitney Ross Manzo, a Meredith College political science professor, said. But she said only people who already support him believe him, so it’s unlikely to make much of an impact. Payments for Americans Since September, Trump has said every adult U.S. citizen will receive a $5,000 payment if Republicans win control of the House and Senate. On top of the steep demands of fulfilling such a costly promise, Trump has added an impossible condition: “You have to spend the money in the United States of America.” The payout would require congressional approval and could cost more than $1 trillion. “Promises of direct cash payments within a month of an election are a new precedent in the modern presidency,” said Thomas C. Sutton, Baldwin Wallace University political science professor emeritus. An October NBC poll found most adults don’t believe the payment will materialize. About 14% said they “definitely” or “probably” expect to receive such a check if the GOP keeps control of Congress, while 71% said they “definitely” or “probably” won’t get one. Trump has already flashed some money sent to certain groups ahead of the election , such as a $90 payment to certain enrollees in Medicare Part B and $500 per person for some Affordable Care Act enrollees. Political scientists pointed to Trump’s record level disapproval ratings and Democrats’ competitiveness in red states as signs that a strategy of promised “goodies” may not work. “If for nothing else, Trump has a real credibility problem and it seems most people don’t believe him,” said Chapman University political science professor Lori Cox Han. PolitiFact Chief Correspondent Louis Jacobson and Staff Writer Loreben Tuquero contributed to this article. title: Actress Christina Applegate was misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis. How often does that happen?
author: Madison Czopek
content: Actress Christina Applegate was diagnosed with the neurological condition multiple sclerosis more than five years ago. “It was my answer to everything that was going on,” she said. Applegate embraced the MS community. She began speaking about her experience on her podcast MeSsy with actress Jamie-Lynn Sigler, who has MS, and became a prominent voice in the multiple sclerosis community. So when Applegate’s doctor recently came to her and said, “Congratulations, you don’t have MS,” she recounted , speaking through tears: “I was like not happy at all.” She described feeling lost after learning that she’d been misdiagnosed. “I’m back at square one,” Applegate said , despite having what she described as “every single symptom” of MS including tingling, pain, tremors, incontinence, fatigue, intolerance to heat and cold, knee buckling and leg weakness and losing her ability to walk. “I’m still dealing with all of those symptoms,” Applegate said in an Oct. 20 podcast episode. “And now here I am without a name.” Misdiagnosis isn’t particularly rare when it comes to multiple sclerosis. Here’s what research tells us about the prevalence of erroneous MS diagnoses and how it can happen. What is multiple sclerosis? Multiple sclerosis, sometimes shortened to MS, is a central nervous system disease that disrupts the brain and the rest of the body’s information exchange . It occurs when the immune system attacks and destroys myelin, the protective protein and fatty substance that surrounds and protects nerve fibers. This forms scar tissue called sclerosis , plaques or lesions. MS looks different for each person. Symptoms can include numbness, pain, tingling, shaking, paralysis, partial or complete vision loss, mobility issues, coordination and balance issues, fatigue, weakness, memory trouble, mood changes and bladder and bowel problems. The disease has no known cure. The National Multiple Sclerosis Society said about 1 million people in the U.S. live with MS. How is MS diagnosed? Doctors don’t perform one single test to diagnose multiple sclerosis. In isolation, no symptoms, or specific test results can prove the condition is MS. Instead, doctors work to rule out other conditions that might explain a patient’s symptoms while looking for evidence that supports a multiple sclerosis diagnosis. Doctors typically look for evidence of damage in the brain, spinal cord or optic nerve. If damage is found in multiple places, doctors might also try to confirm that the damage happened at different times or search for lesions with MS-specific features or certain proteins in the spinal fluid, the National Multiple Sclerosis Society said . “It’s a list of criteria,” Dr. Marwa Kaisey, a neurologist who treats and researches MS, told Applegate on MeSsy. “There’s room for error there,” because assessing criteria can be subjective and because the list can change over time, so doctors have to stay on top of developments. “The symptoms of MS — like tingling in your feet or numbness in your feet, for example, fatigue, brain fog — are very common in other things that are not MS,” Kaisey said. Distinguishing “MS from its mimics can be challenging.” Even doctors with good intentions who have closely examined someone’s case can get the diagnosis wrong, she said. Dr. Michael Kornberg, an associate professor of neurology at Johns Hopkins University, told NPR that an MS diagnosis is reached after analyzing a patient’s various symptoms. Christina Applegate, left, and her daughter Sadie Grace LeNoble arrive at the 29th annual Screen Actors Guild Awards on Sunday, Feb. 26, 2023, at the Fairmont Century Plaza in Los Angeles. (AP) How often is multiple sclerosis misdiagnosed? MS researchers are very familiar with misdiagnoses. Some studies have found about 5% of patients were misdiagnosed, while others have placed that number as high as 36% . A 2024 analysis pooled six studies and found that among 1,621 patients diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, 15% did not actually have it. In a 2019 study , Kaisey and her coauthors found that in one year, roughly 18% of 241 people with established MS diagnoses who were referred to academic multiple sclerosis centers in Los Angeles had been misdiagnosed with the disease. “When you really look at why they’d been misdiagnosed or what they had in common, most of them had some form of white matter spots on their MRI, some sort of lesions,” Kaisey said. The issue was that those lesions were caused by something other than MS. In that study, most of the people who were misdiagnosed actually had migraine , a neurological disease that causes intense headaches and other symptoms. Misdiagnosis concerns drove MS researchers to seek signs that distinguish MRI white spots caused by MS from white spots with other causes. One emerging method involves looking for something called the central vein sign in individual lesions, because that can help distinguish MS from other conditions that mimic it. The approach was incorporated into diagnostic criteria released in 2025 , but not all hospitals are able to check for this sign, Kaisey said. It looks for “little blood vessels sitting in the middle of these white spots or lesions” — their presence signals multiple sclerosis more clearly than white spots alone because that’s how MS creates its lesions, Kaisey said. People can also be misdiagnosed with some other condition before they are diagnosed with MS. One 2017 survey found that approximately 42% of people had initially been misdiagnosed with conditions such as depression, migraine and fibromyalgia . What happened in Applegate’s case? Applegate recalled some of the test results that seemed to support the initial, now inaccurate multiple sclerosis diagnosis, including a brain MRI that showed white lesions and a lumbar puncture test that came back positive for oligoclonal bands, or antibodies found in the cerebrospinal fluid. Kaisey said from what she had learned about Applegate’s case, it sounded possible her lesions didn’t meet the criteria for the central vein sign. As for the lumbar puncture, normal results would return one or no oligoclonal bands in a patient’s cerebrospinal fluid. Applegate said her test showed “three bands,” which is considered a positive test that signals inflammation in the central nervous system. “Over 90% of people with MS are positive for this test,” Kaisey said. “But other things can cause it, it’s not just positive for MS. Anything that’s causing inflammation in the central nervous system would give you a positive result.” What comes next for someone who was misdiagnosed with MS? Once the misdiagnosis has been identified, the next step is beginning the search for a new clinical explanation, Kaisey said. Such errors can also bring harm. The diagnosis often becomes part of someone’s identity and community, and something their support network relies on, she said. Years of multiple sclerosis treatment can be extremely expensive . If someone’s disability paperwork is tied to the diagnosis, there can be financial consequences. “You’ve been told you have this thing for many years,” Kaisey said. “To suddenly take that away, I think it is earth shattering. It’s life changing in a huge way.” Often, doctors also don’t readily have another explanation, which can leave patients at a loss. “We’re just starting from scratch, basically,” Applegate said, explaining that her doctor was beginning with blood tests to check for rheumatoid arthritis. Testing for other rarer “cousins” of multiple sclerosis might also be in order, and blood tests exist for some of those, Kaisey said. Cheryl Herbert, a National Organization for Rare Disorders spokesperson, said Applegate’s experience reflects the challenges many people with rare diseases face. Getting an accurate diagnosis can take on average five or more years, Herbert said, “often involving multiple specialists, uncertainty and missed opportunities for earlier intervention.” PolitiFact Staff Researcher Caryn Baird and PolitiFact Digital Research Analyst Erin Jones contributed to this report.
