title: Most People Only Use 10% of AI — Here’s What That’s Costing Your Business
author: Garry Pickles
content: There’s a growing gap online. Not between people who use AI and people who don’t. That gap is closing fast. The real divide now is between those who know how to use AI properly and those who are just scratching the surface. Most business owners fall into the second group. They open ChatGPT , type a quick question, get an answer, maybe copy and paste it into an email or blog post, then move on. Useful? Yes. Transformational? Not even close. That’s about 10% of what these systems can actually do. Social media is where the gap becomes obvious, most people use AI to write a post or a caption, something quick and passable, that is surface level, at a more advanced level AI becomes a thinking partner behind your content, shaping positioning, refining tone, stress-testing ideas and sharpening how a message lands before it ever goes live, it becomes the difference between posting for the sake of it and posting with intent, the people getting real traction are not just asking for a tweet, they are quietly using AI to structure arguments, pressure-test narratives and tighten delivery so every line does a job, from the outside it just looks like clarity, consistency and timing, but underneath there is a system doing the heavy lifting, and that is where the real advantage sits The Illusion of “Using AI” Using AI at a basic level feels productive. You get quick wins. Faster replies. Some content. A bit of convenience. But here’s the problem. If everyone is doing the same thing, then nobody is gaining an advantage. You’re not using AI strategically. You’re just using it casually. It’s the difference between owning a set of golf clubs and actually knowing how to read the wind, judge distance, pick the right club under pressure, and execute. Anyone can swing. Very few can play. What Advanced AI Use Actually Looks Like When you move beyond the basics, AI stops being a tool and starts becoming a system. Instead of one-off prompts, you build structured workflows. Instead of asking questions, you design outcomes. Instead of generic outputs, you create highly targeted assets that are aligned with your business goals. Here’s what that looks like in practice: Turning AI into a content engine that produces SEO-focused pages at scale Training it to match your brand voice so everything sounds consistent Using it to analyse competitors and identify gaps in your market Building conversion-focused sales copy that’s tested and refined Creating repeatable frameworks for Social Media, emails, landing pages, and ads At this level, AI isn’t saving you time. It’s actively driving growth. Why Most People Never Get There It’s not a tech problem. It’s a thinking problem. Most users treat AI like a search engine. Type something in, get something out. But high-level use requires a different mindset. You need to: Break problems down into components Give precise instructions Iterate and refine outputs Understand what “good” actually looks like in your industry That’s where experience comes in. After 25 years in internet marketing, the difference is clear. The people who win online are not the ones with the most tools. They’re the ones who know how to use them properly. AI just amplifies that gap. The Real Opportunity Right Now We’re in a window where AI capability is high but user understanding is still low. That creates leverage. If you learn how to use these systems properly now, you’re not just keeping up. You’re pulling ahead. Because while others are generating generic blog posts and basic replies, you’re building structured systems that produce better content, better messaging, and better results. Final Thought AI isn’t magic. It’s a multiplier. If you use it casually, you get casual results. If you use it strategically, it becomes one of the most powerful growth tools available today. Most people are operating at 10%. The question is simple. Do you want to be one of them, or do you want to understand what the other 90% looks like? title: Do you really understand your online growth?
author: Garry Pickles
content: Many businesses do not invest in online growth like they expect it to perform. They fund it like a final gamble. Last in line for budget, first in line to be cut. They give it six months, watch the money go out, and obsess over the reserved spend instead of the actual mechanics of what is or is not working. Very little attention goes into improving the pages, tightening the conversion path, tracking lead quality, or fixing weak points. So the budget runs down, the doubts grow, and online gets blamed, when in reality it was never properly managed to succeed in the first place. A lot of companies treat online growth as the very last place to put money. It sits at the back of the queue. They will fund vans, tools, stock, wages, signage, almost anything else first, then give online marketing a small six-month window as a last resort. But the focus is often not on whether it is actually working, or how to make it work better. The focus is on the budget they set aside at the start. Once that pot is gone, they decide “online did not work” without ever really testing, improving, refining, or understanding what was failing. In other words, they are not managing it to succeed. They are managing it to expire. I’m going to say something most people in this space avoid saying. After working with thousands of UK businesses across trades, retail, services and everything in between, around 95% do not actually understand what is happening with their online growth. Not in a real, measurable way. Only a small fraction, maybe 5%, can clearly explain where their leads come from, what converts, what does not, and what they are truly paying for each enquiry. Everyone else thinks they know. That is the dangerous part. Because on the surface, everything looks fine. Enquiries come in. Reports get sent. Rankings get mentioned. Charts go up and to the right. But when you slow it down and ask basic questions, the cracks show immediately: Where exactly did your last 10 leads come from? Which pages are generating revenue, not just traffic? What is your true cost per enquiry, not a rough guess? What would break first if your main traffic source dropped tomorrow? Most business owners pause. Hesitate. Or answer in vague terms. And that should worry you. Because it means decisions are being made without clarity. And in many cases, without control. Now add this layer on top. A surprising number of businesses are not even working with their current provider because they proved themselves. They are there because: They were recommended by someone. They knew a friend. They came in at the right time. Not because they were rigorously tested. Not because they demonstrated clear, repeatable results. Just… because they were there. And once they are in, they stay. Not because performance is obvious, but because questioning it feels awkward. Changing it feels risky. And most people assume “it must be working” because something is happening. But “something happening” is not the same as understanding what is happening. And it is definitely not the same as control. We see this constantly: • Businesses paying monthly with no clear attribution • Websites that look professional but quietly leak enquiries • Rankings that impress on paper but do not translate into customers • Campaigns that cannot be properly explained, only described It creates a false sense of security. Activity without certainty. Movement without direction. And over time, that adds up to wasted money that nobody can quite pinpoint. The problem is not effort. It is not even intent. It is that most businesses cannot see the full picture. And if you cannot see it, you cannot question it. If you cannot question it, you cannot fix it. So here is the uncomfortable question: Are you genuinely in control of your online growth, or are you trusting a system you have never properly verified? If you are honest, there is probably at least a small doubt. And that doubt is usually there for a reason. Because the businesses that truly understand their setup do not hesitate when asked. They know their numbers. They know their sources. They know what would happen if something changed. They are the 5%. Everyone else is operating on trust. And trust without visibility is where most of the waste hides. If you want a clear, straight breakdown of what is really going on in your setup, just reply with: CHECK MY SETUP No jargon. No fluff. Just what is working, what is not, and what you cannot currently see. title: Why Small Businesses Stall Online — And How to Break the Cycle
author: Garry Pickles
content: If you strip it back, most small business marketing problems come down to three blunt realities. They don’t spend enough. They don’t take internet marketing seriously enough to commit to a defined budget. They don’t know what to do. And they don’t know who to trust to do it. That combination is not just inefficient. It’s corrosive. It creates a slow bleed of time, money and missed opportunity that compounds month after month. Let’s break it down properly. 1. Underinvestment: Treating Marketing Like an Optional Extra Most small businesses still approach marketing casually. No fixed budget. No long-term commitment. Just “we’ll see how it goes this month.” That mindset is the first failure point. In 2026, you do not have optional exposure online. You have one dominant gateway: Google . Google controls the majority of search intent. When someone types “roof repair near me” or “forklift trucks for sale,” they are not browsing randomly. They are expressing intent to buy. If you are not visible there, you do not exist in that moment. This is not opinion. It is market structure. And yet many businesses still allocate inconsistent, reactive budgets. £200 one month, nothing the next. That is not strategy. That is drift. A useful benchmark is this: Established business → 5%–10% of revenue on marketing New or rebuilding online presence → closer to 15%–20% in year one That first-year push builds the asset. Pages, rankings, data, conversion flow. Without it, you stay invisible. Invisible businesses don’t grow. 2. Lack of Direction: Activity Without a System The second issue is confusion. Business owners know they need “SEO” or “Google Ads” but cannot define what that actually looks like in execution. So they drift between tactics. A bit of social media. A few ads. A website tweak. Nothing connects. This is where most budgets get quietly wasted. Effective online marketing is structured: Build 30 targeted service/location pages per month Run Google Ads with a defined cost-per-acquisition (CPA) Track every enquiry properly (calls, forms, sales) Improve conversion rates over time This is a system. Traffic → leads → data → optimisation. Without a system, you are not marketing. You are experimenting without feedback. 3. Supplier Selection: Hiring Blind The third issue is who they choose to execute. Most small businesses pick based on price, personality or promises. That is not a recruitment process. That is guesswork. A proper selection framework should include: Education of the consultant Do they understand how search engines rank, how auctions price clicks, how conversion rates are improved? Can they explain it clearly? Years of experience Experience reduces waste. Someone who has managed budgets, scaled campaigns and handled failures will move faster and make fewer costly mistakes. State of the agency This is critical. Large agencies often carry high overheads , multiple layers and diluted responsibility Smaller, lean operators tend to offer direct one-to-one guidance , faster execution and clearer accountability You are not hiring a logo. You are hiring thinking. And beyond that, you must demand structure: What is being built each month? What is the CPA target? What defines success? What is the 12-month roadmap? If those answers are vague, the outcome will be too. The Compounding Effect: Why This Combination Kills Growth These problems reinforce each other. No budget → weak execution Weak execution → poor results Poor results → loss of confidence Loss of confidence → reduced spend It loops. Meanwhile, competitors who take it seriously build momentum. More pages. Better rankings. Lower acquisition costs. Stronger positioning. They are not guessing. They are operating a system. The Shift: Accept the Reality and Build the Asset The key shift is simple. Stop treating online marketing as optional. Start treating it as infrastructure. Because in 2026, with Google acting as the primary gateway to demand, you do not have a choice. You either show up where buyers are searching, or you don’t get considered. The businesses that win do this: Commit to a defined budget Build a structured system Hire with clear criteria Track cost per acquisition Scale what works Over 12 months, that creates an asset: Hundreds of targeted pages Predictable lead flow Measurable acquisition costs A platform that can scale Final Thought Small business failure online is rarely complicated. It is usually a refusal to commit properly. No budget discipline. No system. No hiring filter. In a world where Google controls demand, that approach is no longer survivable. Take it seriously, or accept being invisible. The post Why Small Businesses Stall Online — And How to Break the Cycle appeared first on Online Media Direct .

title: Top 10 Niche Product Business Ideas for an Online Business in 2026
author: Garry Pickles
content: In 2026, the smartest online businesses in the UK will not be the biggest. They will be the most focused. At Online Media Direct, we think the era of the generic ecommerce store is fading. The UK online market is still substantial, with online sales accounting for 28.3% of total retail sales in December 2025, but broad categories are crowded, expensive to advertise in, and difficult to rank for organically. The better play is to go narrower, build around a clear audience, and become known for solving one problem well. Wider UK trend signals back that up too: gardening remains mainstream, pet ownership is high, equestrian participation has grown, and Britain’s car parc is getting older. All of that creates openings for specialist product businesses rather than bland general stores. Here are ten niche product business ideas that look especially strong for 2026. 1. White-label functional mushroom products Functional mushroom products are still niche enough to feel specialist, but broad enough to build a real brand around. This is not about trying to become the next giant supplement company. It is about going after a narrower angle: lion’s mane coffee sachets, evening wind-down blends, desk-drawer focus drops, or wellness gift sets designed for a very specific type of customer. The attraction here is branding. A generic supplement store is forgettable. A focused mushroom brand with a clear identity, tight packaging, a simple hero product range, and strong educational content is a different proposition entirely. It also lends itself well to subscriptions, repeat orders, and bundle offers. The key is discipline. Keep the range tight, make the proposition simple, and avoid drifting into vague “we sell wellness stuff” territory. Niche wins when the customer instantly understands what you are for. Wholesale suppliers: The Fungi Folks — white-label and private-label functional mushroom extracts. Rocket Science Nutrition — UK mushroom supplement manufacturer. Supplement Factory UK — private-label and bespoke supplement manufacturing. 2. Home mushroom grow kits This is one of the most content-friendly product niches on the list. Mushroom grow kits are visual, giftable, beginner-friendly, and perfect for short-form video. They also sit in a wider UK gardening culture that remains huge. The RHS says around 41 million people in the UK garden at least once a month, which gives this kind of product a large adjacent audience without making it feel mass-market. What makes this niche attractive is the angle. You are not selling “gardening products”. You are selling a countertop growing experience. Oyster mushroom kits for flats, starter kits for foodies, children’s grow-at-home boxes, refill packs, and seasonal gift bundles all make sense here. This is also a great niche for organic traffic. A small website can build authority with guides like how to grow oyster mushrooms indoors, how long mushroom kits last, or best mushroom kits for beginners in the UK. That is exactly the kind of focused search demand smaller ecommerce brands can still compete for. Wholesale suppliers: Martian Mushrooms — bulk Lion’s Mane grow kits in UK pack sizes. Spore Supplies — wholesale all-in-one mushroom grow kits. Mushroom Box — UK supplier offering trade terms for stores and garden centres. 3. Horse calmer, gut and recovery supplements Equestrian is a proper niche. It has a passionate customer base, clear problems to solve, and an audience that values specialist knowledge. UK Pet Food’s latest validated figures show around 700,000 horses and ponies kept as pets in the UK, while British Equestrian says federation memberships rose by 11.7% between 2023 and 2024. That is not a mass-market category. It is a specialist market with signs of active engagement. The mistake would be going too broad. “Horse supplements” is still too vague. The better move is to niche down further. Nervous horse calmer bundles. Travel and event-day digestive support. Winter recovery packs. Older horse joint and gut routines. Pony club starter kits. The narrower the use case, the stronger the positioning. This sort of niche also rewards trust. If you build useful content, testimonials, and a clean product structure, it is much easier to stand out than in a general pet category. Wholesale suppliers: Brinicombe Equine — trade enquiry page for equine supplements. AR Wholesale — UK pet and equestrian wholesaler. Henry Cole & Co — animal feed and supplements for the equine and smallholder trade. 4. Backyard chicken care kits Backyard poultry is one of those overlooked UK niches that many people ignore simply because it feels too specific. That is exactly why it is interesting. UK Pet Food’s figures show around 1.3 million domestic fowl kept as pets in the UK. That is more than enough scale for a focused online store. The smart version of this business is not “sell random poultry accessories”. It is to package products around clear needs. A red mite defence kit. A winter hen health box. A first-time chicken keeper starter bundle. A moulting support pack. A coop hygiene essentials set. Those are much easier to market than a loose catalogue of feeders and supplements. It also gives you obvious content angles. First-time owners always search for checklists, seasonal advice, common mistakes, and simple buying guides. That creates a natural bridge between ecommerce and SEO. Wholesale suppliers: Dalton Supplies — poultry equipment supplier with trade accounts. Trilanco — wholesaler covering animal health, agricultural and smallholding products. Copdock Mill — pet and feed wholesaler serving poultry among other sectors. 5. Older-car headlight and trim restoration kits Britain’s ageing vehicle parc makes this one especially attractive in 2026. According to the SMMT, the average age of a car on the road is now 9.5 years, and 43.4% of the total parc has been in use for more than a decade. That creates a large pool of cars with faded plastics, cloudy headlights, dull trim, and tired-looking finishes. This niche works because the promise is obvious. Make an older car look better without a bodyshop bill. That is simple, visual, and easy to demonstrate with before-and-after content. The strongest angle is to stay narrow. Headlight restoration kits. Black trim revival bundles. Older-car cosmetic refresh packs. MOT-prep appearance kits. You are not trying to compete with giant detailing brands across every product category. You are owning one outcome. Wholesale suppliers: Gold Label Car Care — trade accounts for UK detailers and restoration products. JRP Distribution — B2B automotive distributor carrying headlight restoration kits. EZ Car Care — manufacturer-led trade and wholesale partnerships. 6. Allotment seedling protection bundles This is a smart spin-off from the broader gardening space. Instead of trying to sell generic tools or seeds, focus on one very specific problem: protecting young plants. That could mean fleece, mini hoops, clips, netting, slug barriers, labels, seedling trays, and simple seasonal starter packs. The appeal is clarity. Gardeners and growers do not want a thousand products. They want the right bundle at the right time of year. The wider gardening market is large enough to support micro-niches like this, especially when the offer is practical and seasonal. This kind of niche also suits content-led ecommerce beautifully. Spring planting checklists, slug protection guides, or what to cover seedlings with in the UK are all highly relevant search topics. Wholesale suppliers: Creation Horticulture — trade crop-protection netting and fabrics. Gardening Naturally — trade account for resellers of natural gardening products. Dejex Supplies — specialist commercial horticultural supplies for growers and retailers. 7. Wildlife garden starter kits Another strong 2026 idea is the wildlife garden niche. Instead of selling general garden décor, build products around attracting birds, pollinators, or hedgehogs. Think starter bundles for new wildlife gardeners, pollinator-friendly planting packs, bird feeding kits, or beginner habitat boxes. The beauty of this niche is emotional appeal. People like buying products that feel useful, visible, and positive. It also sits naturally inside the same wider gardening culture the RHS describes as part of everyday life for millions across the UK. This is also excellent for branding. A wildlife garden brand can look warm, purposeful, and distinct, rather than like another forgettable ecommerce catalogue. Wholesale suppliers: CJ Wildlife Trade — wildlife care manufacturer and distributor trade range. Wildlife World Trade — trade site for wildlife habitat and garden wildlife products. Woodlodge — wildlife care range with trade support for garden retail. 8. Cold-water swim recovery kits Cold-water swimming has created a very particular kind of customer. They do not just want a towel. They want a kit. Changing mat, oversized poncho, flask-friendly accessories, dry bag, recovery socks, waterproof pouch, and warm-up add-ons. That is why this niche is interesting. The customer identity is already there. Your job is to package around it. Starter bundles for beginners, winter swim kits, gift boxes, or recovery kits for regular sea dippers all make sense. It is also social-media friendly. Lifestyle niches with a recognisable ritual often outperform “practical” categories because people like showing the experience, not just the product. Cold pods are another smart add-on within this niche because they give customers a lower-cost, lower-commitment way into cold-water recovery than a full hard-shell plunge setup. Portable pod-style ice baths are built around quick setup, compact storage, easy drainage and home or garden use, which makes them a strong entry-level product for beginners, gift buyers, and fitness-led ecommerce brands looking for a simpler product line. Supplier links: RuggaRobe — bespoke custom changing robes with MOQ-based supply. B S Suthi & Bros — UK changing robe manufacturer. DRYBONES — bespoke corporate, club and school changing robes. Outdoorliving – Cold pods suppliers 9. Campervan storage and blackout bundles Campervan owners are another niche audience with strong identity and very specific needs. A general travel accessories shop will struggle. A focused brand selling privacy screens, storage organisers, compact kitchen add-ons, cable tidy packs, and overnight comfort bundles has a much clearer proposition. What makes this good for ecommerce is the bundling potential. You are not relying on one product. You can create themed packs for weekends away, stealth camping, van organisation, or rainy-weather comfort. That immediately increases average order value. This niche also rewards instructional content. Setup guides, packing tips, van storage ideas, and checklist pages are the sort of content that can drive long-tail traffic without needing a huge domain. Wholesale suppliers: Wholesale Van Accessories — trade-only pricing for van conversion businesses. Trade Glass UK — van and campervan curtains for multiple vehicle types. Clearcut Campervan Design — wholesale account for campervan parts and accessories. 10. Fermentation and home-preserving kits Fermentation is still niche enough to avoid the mainstream race to the bottom, but broad enough to build a recognisable product range around. Kombucha kits, kimchi starter packs, hot sauce fermentation sets, jar bundles, labels, weights, and beginner guides all fit neatly into one brand. This is a strong niche because it combines hobby, food, gifting, and repeat purchase. Once someone gets started, they often come back for ingredients, accessories, replacements, and upgrades. That is exactly the kind of customer behaviour an online business wants. It is also a natural content play. Beginner mistakes, how-to guides, recipe content, and product demos all help reduce the trust barrier for first-time buyers. Wholesale suppliers: Wares of Knutsford — wholesale and bulk glass jars with lids. Jars & Bottles — trade cases and wholesale pallets for jars and closures. Jam Jar Shop — artisan trade packs for wholesale jar orders. Final thoughts The best niche product businesses in 2026 will not win by trying to sell everything. They will win by being specific. That means a clear audience, a visible problem, a tight product range, and content that actually matches what people are searching for. In our view, the strongest ideas are usually the ones that sit at the intersection of hobby, habit, identity, and repeat purchase. That is why categories like mushroom kits, equestrian supplements, backyard chicken care, and older-car restoration stand out more than another generic home or lifestyle store. The broader UK backdrop still supports focused ecommerce plays, with online retail retaining a major share of sales and clear enthusiast markets visible in gardening, pets, equestrian participation, and older vehicles. If you are starting an online business this year, go narrower than feels comfortable. That is usually where the real opportunity begins. title: The next 90 days in Internet marketing (2 March to 31 May 2026)
author: admin
content: What’s changing in SEO, WordPress, WooCommerce and Google Ads and what to do about it The next 90 days will reward boring competence. Clean tracking. Fast pages. Safe updates. Content built for the surfaces that are actually sending traffic. If your marketing has felt “soft” lately, it’s usually not a creativity problem, it’s a measurement and platform-change problem. That’s the theme from March through May 2026. Four moving parts are colliding at once: WordPress core is about to move with WordPress 7.0 scheduled for 9 April 2026 and it introduces changes that can affect how the editor renders and how plugins interact with admin screens. WooCommerce is about to move with WooCommerce 10.6 scheduled for 10 March 2026 and it includes performance and block refinements plus specific behaviour changes like default lazy-loading in Product Image blocks. Google’s discovery and SERP layouts are shifting . Google launched a February 2026 Discover core update on 5 February 2026 and confirmed rollout completion on 27 February 2026 . In parallel, Google is preparing EU search-result experiments that may change how visibility is distributed in certain verticals, especially travel and hospitality style queries. Paid media measurement is still being rebuilt around consent and first-party data , while Google is also pulling creator marketing deeper into the Ads product with Creator Partnerships Hub and Partnership ads. So what do you do with that? This article is a practical plan you can run across your marketing stack in the next 90 days. If you only do one thing, do this: treat March as “measurement and performance month” then treat April as “platform updates month” then treat May as “distribution month” (SEO surfaces, creators and diversification). That sequencing reduces risk and it keeps you shipping. March 2026: fix measurement first so every click counts If your tracking is wrong, you can’t trust the campaign data and you can’t trust the automated bidding. The result is the worst kind of waste: you pay for traffic, then you pay again to “learn” from noisy data. 1) Consent Mode is now operational, not optional For UK and EU businesses, you need a consent signal that is consistent and testable. Google’s own Consent Mode reference spells out consent types such as ad_storage , analytics_storage , ad_user_data and ad_personalization . Importantly, Google explicitly ties ad_user_data to measurement use cases like enhanced conversions and tag-based conversion tracking. What to do this week (two-hour audit): Open Tag Assistant and confirm consent states change correctly on accept and reject. Google’s verification guidance literally tells you what parameters to check. Ensure the default consent state is set, then updated after a user choice (Google’s developer guide is clear on the “default then update” model). Check for double-tagging: GA4, Ads and GTM misfires are common after “quick fixes”. What success looks like by end of March: Your conversion numbers won’t necessarily go up overnight, but they stop behaving like a random number generator. Your “top campaigns” don’t change every day and smart bidding stops oscillating. 2) Enhanced Conversions is the fastest win for lead gen and ecommerce measurement Enhanced Conversions uses hashed first-party data from conversion pages to improve conversion measurement accuracy. Google describes it as capturing hashed, user-provided customer data and matching it in a privacy-safe way. Where this matters most: Lead gen forms (trades, B2B services, local service businesses) Checkout completion (WooCommerce stores) Any account where “conversion loss” has been creeping up What to do this week: Implement Enhanced Conversions on the conversion page templates (thank-you pages, lead form confirmations). Confirm your data collection is minimal and relevant. You are not trying to hoover up everything, you are trying to restore measurement and maintain compliance. Run a controlled before/after comparison over 14 days with identical budgets, then check conversion modelling stability. If you run Google Ads in 2026 without Enhanced Conversions and a correct consent implementation, you’re flying with instruments that flicker. 3) Landing pages: speed and clarity beat gimmicks in March Before you scale spend or content, get your money page experience tight: One page, one job (call, quote request, add to cart) Remove friction (forms that feel like a tax return) Prioritise Core Web Vitals type basics: image sizing, caching, lazy-loading, preloading critical assets This sets you up for April’s WordPress and WooCommerce changes without chaos. Late March into April 2026: build the paid creative pipeline, then test creator-led ads Google is not hiding the direction of travel: creator marketing is being productised inside Ads. 4) Creator Partnerships Hub and Partnership ads are becoming a serious lever Google calls Creator Partnerships Hub “a new central place in Google Ads” for managing creator collaborations, including discovery, reporting across paid and organic and creator search and outreach. Partnership ads powered by BrandConnect let advertisers promote YouTube creator videos in ad campaigns. This matters for two reasons: It reduces the friction of creator outreach and measurement It makes creator content a scalable performance channel instead of a messy PR exercise What to do in April (two-stage test): Stage 1 (7 days): Run a small creator-style creative test without creators. Film “creator format” assets yourself: face-to-camera, product or service demonstration, before/after, FAQs, short proofs. Stage 2 (14 days): If Stage 1 beats your baseline CPA or ROAS, run a Partnership ads test with a local creator or niche creator that matches your customer profile. How to choose creators in a UK SME context: Location relevance beats fame for local services Demonstration beats vibe for ecommerce Trust cues beat polish (show the work, show the process, show outcomes) You’re not paying for celebrity. You’re buying credibility at scale. April 2026: platform updates month (WordPress 7.0 and WooCommerce 10.6) April is where good businesses quietly win because they update safely while competitors break things. 5) WordPress 7.0 is scheduled for 9 April 2026. Treat it as a project, not a button WordPress.org’s own Beta 2 post states the scheduled final release date for WordPress 7.0 is 9 April 2026 and it highlights a new Connectors UI for managing external AI connections in wp-admin. There is also a documented change around the editor: WordPress core has a post on “Iframed editor changes in WordPress 7.0” and notes that editors have been iframed already while the post editor is part of this shift. What to do before you update: Clone production to staging Update plugins and themes in staging first Click through every revenue path: contact forms, checkout, email confirmations, analytics events Specifically test any custom admin UI your site relies on (page builders, custom metaboxes, bespoke blocks) Why the Connectors UI matters even if you “don’t use AI”: Anything that centralises external connections becomes a governance surface. You want to know what is connected, who can connect things and where the logs are. Even if you never touch it, your stack should be auditable. 6) WooCommerce 10.6 is scheduled for 10 March 2026. If you haven’t done it yet, don’t delay WooCommerce’s developer update confirms 10 March 2026 as the final release date. There are also specific performance-related behaviour changes like product images in the Product Image block being lazy-loaded by default starting with WooCommerce 10.6. Lazy-loading is usually positive but it can change how images appear during loading states, it can affect LCP measurement and it can expose theme quirks. So test it. WooCommerce 10.6 checklist for store owners: Checkout blocks and payment gateways: test 5 full orders end-to-end in staging Shipping rules: edge cases (postcode restrictions, free shipping thresholds) Product pages: image galleries, zoom, variation switching Tracking: GA4 purchase events, Ads conversion tags, server-side events if used Performance: compare product page load and LCP before and after If your WooCommerce store makes money every day, treat upgrades like you’d treat changing the till system in a busy shop. Rehearse it. May 2026: SEO distribution shifts (Discover, EU SERP changes and what it means for you) May is where you stop pretending “SEO” means ten blue links only. It doesn’t. 7) Google Discover is in play and it just had a confirmed update Google’s Search Central blog announced the February 2026 Discover core update on 5 February 2026 . Industry tracking and reporting also notes it completed rollout on 27 February 2026 . What this changes for content planning: Discover rewards compelling topics and packaging, not just keyword targeting Consistency matters. One good article is not a strategy Relevance and local expertise are increasingly important in how content performs in these surfaces (and clickbait is a long-term loser) Practical Discover-ready content moves for UK businesses: Build a “90-day newsroom” for your niche: weekly commentary posts tied to customer questions, prices, regulations, seasonal demand Use real photos where possible (job photos, product shots, behind the scenes). Keep them sharp and well framed Put your best proof above the fold: outcomes, timelines, case studies, constraints, what you do and what you refuse to do Refresh top performers: update the date, add new sections, add new FAQs, improve images, fix internal links Discover is not something you “do once”. It is a publishing habit. 8) EU SERP layout changes are a reminder to diversify Reuters reports Google plans to test search result changes in Europe under DMA pressure, including giving more visibility to rival vertical services especially for “hotels, flights and restaurants” style queries. The Verge summarises the same direction of travel: more prominence for rivals and phased rollout across Europe. Even if you are not a travel business, the lesson is bigger: layout changes can move your clicks without your rankings changing . So May is diversification month. Diversification moves that actually help: Build an email list that is not rented attention Strengthen brand search demand (content and social that makes people search your name) Use YouTube and short video for “how it works” content (then repurpose into ads) Build local citations and review velocity for local service queries Create comparison pages and alternatives pages where appropriate (high-intent pages) The goal is simple: no single Google surface should be able to wipe out your pipeline overnight. Security and resilience: the quiet multiplier across the whole quarter Updates bring benefits and risk, and attackers love slow-moving sites. A recent example: Patchstack reported an SQL injection vulnerability in the “Quiz and Survey Master (QSM)” plugin affecting 40k+ sites and advised updating to a fixed version. You don’t need to run that plugin to learn the lesson. The lesson is that WordPress sites are ecosystems of third-party code. If you want growth, you need a minimum viable security routine. Minimum viable security routine (set it and keep it): Weekly updates on staging, monthly on production (or faster if critical) Remove unused plugins and themes Enforce least-privilege user roles Use reputable security monitoring and alerts Keep backups and practise restore Security is not a fear story, it is how you avoid losing a month of marketing progress to a preventable incident. The 90-day scoreboard: what to track weekly If you want to know whether the plan is working, track a short set of metrics weekly: Leads or orders (the real number) Cost per lead or cost per acquisition (by campaign type) Conversion rate (sitewide and on the main money pages) “Tracked conversions” vs “actual outcomes” gap (CRM or order records) Top landing pages by revenue contribution Search Console: clicks and impressions for your top topics Site performance: LCP and page speed on your top pages If any of these lines drift, you act fast. The point of weekly tracking is not reporting, it’s correction. A clean 90-day action plan you can follow If you want the simplest version, here it is: Week 1–2 (March): Consent Mode audit, Enhanced Conversions, landing page friction fixes. Week 3–4 (late March): Creative refresh, creator-format tests, rebuild your offer pages. Week 5–6 (April): WordPress 7.0 staging rehearsal, WooCommerce 10.6 checks and performance review. Week 7–9 (May): Discover-ready publishing cadence, refresh top pages, improve internal linking and media. Week 10–12 (late May): Diversification sprint: email capture, YouTube pipeline, local SEO reinforcement, creator partnership pilot. If you want Online Media Direct to run this for you A sensible “done with you” stack for the quarter looks like: Tracking and consent implementation audit, then Enhanced Conversions rollout WordPress 7.0 and WooCommerce 10.6 staging rehearsal with a pass/fail report A 12-week SEO and Discover content plan with internal links mapped to revenue pages A Google Ads creative refresh and a creator partnership pilot with strict measurement If you want, paste your main service pages and your primary conversion action (calls, quote forms or checkout) and I’ll tailor this plan to your exact site structure and niche. title: Take your website to the GYM
author: Garry Pickles
content: When did you last improve your website? Let’s take your website to the gym Quick question, when was the last time you made a meaningful improvement to your website or online setup? Most small businesses treat their website like a sign above the door, set it up once and hope it keeps working, the problem is your competitors keep upgrading while Google keeps changing and customer expectations keep rising. Your website is an asset you own Your website is the only “lead platform” you fully control. You own the domain, the pages, the content, the tracking, the conversion path and the data. Compare that to third-party lead sources. Trade directories, lead sellers and “request a quote” platforms can be useful, but you do not control the rules, you do not own the audience and you can lose the tap overnight. Worse, you can end up paying for 2nd-hand, 4th-hand, 6th-hand leads that have been sold to multiple businesses, price-shopped into the ground and stripped of urgency. Quick question, when was your last website upgrade? Direct leads are different. They come to you first, they are higher intent and they usually convert better because you are not one of five quotes in a race to the bottom. The uncomfortable truth If you have never experienced a regular flow of direct leads from your website, you have to ask: Is your online presence being actively improved, or just passively “maintained”? A website that gets results is not “done”. It is trained. It gets stronger through small, consistent upgrades. Why your site isn’t producing direct leads (yet) A simple self-audit (2 minutes) When was the last time you: Added a new piece of content that answers a real customer question Improved a key page to convert better (clear offer, proof, strong call-to-action) Tightened up your enquiry flow (forms, click-to-call, WhatsApp, booking, follow-up) Built trust signals (reviews, case studies, before/after, accreditations, guarantees) Checked mobile speed and usability (most leads now start on phones) Confirmed tracking is correct (so you know what is working and what is leaking) If the honest answer is “not sure” or “a long time ago”, that alone explains why direct leads feel inconsistent. What “direct lead growth” actually looks like. At Online Media Direct Ltd we put your website on a practical growth program, the goal is simple: Generate a reliable flow of direct enquiries from your own online asset. That typically means: Content growth: new pages and FAQs that match what people search for in your area Conversion upgrades: clearer messaging, stronger CTAs, better layout and trust proof Local visibility: improvements that help you show up for local searches consistently Measurement: tracking and reporting so decisions are based on numbers not guesses Compounding: monthly improvements that stack up over time Think of it like taking your website to the gym. You do not “train” once. You train consistently and the results compound. Your website should be getting stronger every month If you want a quick win Reply to this email with GYM and I’ll run a quick website fitness check and send back: The top 3 improvements that will move enquiries fastest The biggest lead leak we can fix immediately A simple plan for building a steady flow of direct leads. author: Jake Winfrey

title: Local attorney Sara Baker released from custody as judge reinstates pretrial bond
author: Patrick Camp
content: Local attorney Sara Baker has once again been released from jail after a judge determined her prior bond conditions had not been violated last week. Baker was arrested in November 2025 and charged with conspiracy to commit murder stemming from allegations that she had mixed Fentanyl into her husband’s food and/or drinks on three separate occasions between September 4 and September 20, 2025. Baker was released on a $400,000 bond with orders not to contact her husband or to intervene in his medical care. In July, prosecutors claimed Baker had violated those provisions by requesting that one of the caregivers retrieve an empty prescription medication bottle from the home that was later returned and placed in a safe. When the Cullman City Police Department searched the home, they discovered just over 12 grams of a “purple-tinted powder substance” inside the bottle, which court documents indicate to be Fetanyl. Walker County Circuit Judge Gregory Williams — who was appointed to hear the case — ordered that Baker be returned to jail. “The continued release of the Defendant poses a risk to public safety and no set conditions will reasonably assure compliance with the Court’s Orders regarding the Defendant’s bond,” Williams wrote in his July order. Last week, on Oct. 21, Williams walked back his previous opinion and ordered that Baker’s pretrial bond be reinstated and that she be released from custody with additional conditions. In addition to Baker’s previous release conditions she must now pay for an electronic monitoring system and neither she nor any third party acting on her behalf may contact, come within 400 feet or deliver any materials, food, property, etc. to her husband. The Alabama State Bar suspended Baker’s license in 2025.

title: Cullman City BOE recognizes student’s advocacy work for dyslexia awareness
author: Patrick Camp
content: Cullman High School Junior Lily Shadeck was recognized by the Cullman City Board of Education on Tuesday, Oct. 20, for her already flourishing advocacy work to raise dyslexia awareness. Shadeck is well aware that something as simple as reading a page from a book can be a tremendous challenge for someone with dyslexia. While she may not be affected by the condition herself, her twin brother Michael is, and she said watching his strength and determination to face challenges she would never know, inspired her to help other dyslexic children. This is why Shadeck wrote “The Dynamic Duo and the Mix-up Magic,” a children’s story reflecting her and Michael’s own experience as siblings learning about dyslexia together and discovering that learning differently doesn’t mean learning less. On Tuesday, Oct. 20, Shadeck announced that the Cullman City Schools Education Foundation had donated 75 copies of her book and that one would be placed in every elementary classroom in the district. Shadek also founded, and plays an active role in, the Mythbusters Dyslexia Foundation to raise funding to provide families access to dyslexia testing. “One of my biggest goals is to place 500 books in classrooms across Alabama to encourage kindness, acceptance and confidence,” Shadek said. In other business the board: — Approved the job description for an American Sign Language Interpreter. — Approved a yearbook purchase agreement with Walsworth Yearbooks. — Approved the Clear Path for Veterans Operation Socrates Partnership Plan. — Approved for the Cullman Middle School FFA Chapter to travel to Indianapolis, Indiana to attend the 99th National FFA Convention. — Accepted the resignation of Syvella Dillingham as an instructional assistant. — Approved the conditional employment of the following personnel: – Emily Coffman, Instructional assistant. – Heather Floyd, Permanent substitute. – Jillian LeCroy, Licensed practical nurse. – Pamela Rauch, Cullman High School custodian.

title: PREP FOOTBALL: Vinemont downs Susan Moore to clinch playoff berth
author: Jake Winfrey
content: Joshua Rhodes threw a touchdown pass to Travis Speer with 4:17 remaining, Brennan Marlow recorded a late interception, and Vinemont knocked off Susan Moore 12-7 on Friday night to earn a playoff berth for the seventh consecutive year under head coach Stephen Robinson. With the win, the Eagles finished the regular season at 6-4 overall and 4-3 in Class 3A, Region 6 play. “Backs against the wall two weeks in a row, and these kids found a way,” Robinson said. “We had some mistakes tonight, but we did what we had to do. The defense had a big goal-line stand, and the offense scored when it had to late. Really proud of them.” Rhodes ran for a long touchdown on the first play of the game, but Susan Moore led 7-6 at halftime. Late in the third quarter, Speer came through with a clutch interception to end a scoring threat by the Bulldogs. Vinemont eventually took the lead and then held on for the win. The Eagles are off next week before hitting the road for a first-round playoff game in November. “We’ll enjoy this one and get rested up before playing another one,” Robinson said.

title: PREP ROUNDUP: Cold Springs, Cullman, Good Hope record blowout wins
author: Jake Winfrey
content: See a recap of Friday’s local games below. Class 2A, Region 5 Cold Springs 52, Carbon Hill 6 The Eagles dominated the Bulldogs from start to finish on Friday night. Brandon Chasteen threw two touchdown passes to Eli Voce and rushed for another score. Blake Phillips (twice), Jordan Garmon and Cooper Johnson each provided touchdown runs as well. Latham Shuford, meanwhile, added a scoop-and-score on defense. Cold Springs (8-1, 6-1) wraps up its regular season next week with a home game against Tanner. Class 5A, Region 5 Cullman 42, Jackson-Olin 13 The Bearcats snapped a five-game skid with a strong showing against the Mustangs on Friday night. Colt Colvard, Parker Smith and John Mark Stephens each had rushing touchdowns for Cullman in the win. Smith also threw a touchdown pass to Landon Pitts. Defensively, Hank Helms and Grayson Gay each had pick-sixes to account for the Black and Gold’s first two scores. Cullman (3-6, 2-5) wraps up its regular season next week with a road game against West Morgan. Class 4A, Region 8 Good Hope 42, Hayden 7 The Raiders rolled to a victory over the Wildcats on Friday night. Parker Johnson ran for two touchdowns and threw another to Kayden Collins. Ayden Young also caught a touchdown pass — from Web Buchanan — and Karson Hollis added two scoring runs. Good Hope (7-2, 6-1) wraps up its regular season next week with a road game against Scottsboro. Class 3A, Region 6 Oneonta 62, Hanceville 0 The Bulldogs had no answers for the No. 5 Redskins on Friday night. Hanceville (0-9, 0-7) wraps up its regular season next week with a road game against Elkmont. Class 3A, Region 6 Etowah 43, Holly Pond 12 The Broncos couldn’t keep pace with the Blue Devils on Friday night. Kort Freeman had a touchdown run, and Grayson Baggett threw another to Braxton Rice. Holly Pond (2-7, 1-6) wraps up its regular season next week with a road game against Falkville. Class 4A, Region 7 Deshler 41, West Point 14 Max Patterson threw a pair of touchdown passes to Bryant Moon in Friday night’s loss to the No. 8 Tigers. West Point finishes the regular season 0-10 overall and 0-7 in region play.

title: PREP FOOTBALL: No. 2 Addison rolls past No. 7 Hackleburg to claim region title
author: Jake Winfrey
content: Addison is back on top. Not that it ever really departed. The No. 2 Bulldogs punctuated a perfect regular season on Friday night, defeating No. 7 Hackleburg 33-7 to earn the Class 1A, Region 7 title for a second consecutive year. “Hats off to Hackleburg — they came out and hit us in the mouth,” Addison coach Mark Hastings said. “We also made some small mistakes that turned into big mistakes early, but we got those corrected at halftime. I think we played a lot better defensively after they scored, too, which ended up being the key to the game.” Judah Wilkins rushed for a pair of first-half touchdowns to give Addison a 14-7 lead at intermission. In the third quarter, Elijah Roberts connected with Zane Smith for a touchdown strike. The two later added scoring runs for the Bulldogs, who closed the game with 33 unanswered points. Defensively, Roberts, Scout Flynn, Ben Bridges and Michael Lee each recorded interceptions. For the regular season, Addison outscored its opponents 484-26. The Bulldogs will have next week off before hosting a first-round playoff game in November. “I think we can make a run,” Hastings said. “We’ve got some really good players, but tonight was a wake-up call. I’ve got to get them ready to play because there are a lot of good teams in the North.”

title: PREP VOLLEYBALL: Addison wins North Super Regional title; Cold Springs, West Point also advance to state tournament
author: Jake Winfrey
content: Addison won the Class 1A North Super Regional title on Friday, while Cold Springs and West Point also clinched state tournament berths this week. See a recap below. Class 1A No. 2 Addison defeated top-ranked Meek in five sets (25-22, 23-25, 25-13, 13-25, 15-12) to take home the top prize. The Bulldogs also defeated No. 4 Spring Garden (25-11, 25-13, 25-22) and Wadley (25-8., 25-7, 25-20) at the Finley Center in Hoover. Addison (31-12) will open play at the state tournament against Washington County. The match is scheduled for Tuesday, Oct. 27 at noon. Class 2A Cold Springs defeated J.B. Pennington (25-18, 25-13, 25-16) to advance to the state tournament. The No. 10 Eagles later fell to No. 1 Fyffe (25-20, 25-17, 25-14) before beating Pisgah in five sets (25-21, 19-25, 28-26, 19-25, 22-22) at the Finley Center in Hoover. Cold Springs (17-21) will open play at the state tournament against No. 5 Ariton. The match is scheduled for Wednesday, Oct. 28 at 1:30 p.m. Class 4A West Point defeated Sylacauga in five sets (25-19, 25-13, 23-25, 14-25, 15-8) to advance to the state tournament. The No. 7 Warriors later fell to top-ranked Guntersville (25-21, 25-18, 25-11) before beating Moody in five sets (20-25, 29-27, 14-25, 25-17, 15-12) at the Finley Center in Hoover. title: Wallace State sets fall enrollment record, surpassing 7,100 students
author: Staff reports
content: Wallace State Community College has set another fall enrollment record, surpassing 7,100 students for the first time in the college’s history. As of Wednesday, Oct. 21, enrollment for the Fall 2026 semester stood at 7,141 students, an increase of 155 students over Fall 2025 enrollment of 6,986. The milestone, a fourth straight fall increase, represents growth of nearly 20 percent since Fall 2022, when enrollment stood at 5,966 students. “The record enrollment, combined with our recognition as an Aspen Prize finalist, reflects the exceptional work being done across campus to help students start early, start right, finish, and succeed,” said Wallace State President Dr. Vicki P. Karolewics. “We are honored that more students than ever are choosing Wallace State as the place to begin or advance their educational journey.” Wallace State continues to expand educational opportunities in response to student needs and regional workforce demands. New and expanded offerings include evening nursing classes, additional nursing opportunities at the Oneonta campus, a new Speech-Language Pathologist Assistant program, the only associate-degree program of its kind in Alabama, more dual enrollment opportunities, new workforce credit-to-college credit pathways, and the new Winston County Learning Center in Arley. The college is also establishing new and expanded program opportunities in other high-demand healthcare and technical fields, strengthening transfer pathways, and enhancing advising and student support services to help students achieve their educational and career goals. These initiatives reflect Wallace State’s commitment to providing affordable, accessible pathways to high-demand careers, family-sustaining wages, and continued educational advancement. Wallace State is a finalist for the 2027 Aspen Prize for Community College Excellence, one of the nation’s most prestigious recognitions of community college achievement. The college was also a finalist in 2025, earning the Rising Star Award and recognition as one of the nation’s top three community colleges. Wallace State has been selected to compete for the Aspen Prize seven times, reflecting its sustained commitment to student success and excellence in higher education. Registration for the Spring 2027 semester is underway, with classes beginning Jan. 8 for the regular term and Mini Term I, and March 8 for Mini Term II. For more information, contact Lion Central at 256.352.8236 or visit wallacestate.edu.

title: Cullman Tree Commission prepares for 2026 Festival of Trees
author: Staff reports
content: Christmas may still be a couple of months away, but the City of Cullman Tree Commission is already making plans for one of the community’s annual holiday traditions, the Festival of Trees. During its Oct. 20 meeting, the Commission discussed preparations for the 2026 event, which will once again feature Christmas trees decorated by students from local public and private schools, along with the Cullman County Public Library. The decorated trees will be displayed in the foyer of the Cullman Wellness & Aquatics Center (CWAC), where residents and visitors can enjoy them free of charge during regular operating hours. Participating schools and the library will decorate their trees Dec. 2–3, with judging scheduled for 1 p.m. on Dec. 3. The Festival of Trees opening ceremony will follow at 5 p.m. The decorated trees will remain on public display from Dec. 4 through Dec. 27, giving residents and visitors an opportunity to enjoy the students’ creativity and holiday spirit. Commission members are reaching out to participating schools and coordinating the details that help bring the event together each year. Commission member Jason Fowler confirmed that local Boy Scouts will assist with setting up and taking down the display. In other business, the Commission discussed upcoming grant opportunities, plans for the Arbor Day Poster Contest, and the Dec. 2 deadline for submitting the City’s Tree City USA and Growth Award applications. Members also discussed opportunities for additional training and professional guidance from arborists. The Commission scheduled an additional meeting for Monday, Nov. 16, 2026, at 10 a.m., as preparations for the Festival of Trees continue. The Festival of Trees is free and open to the public during CWAC’s regular operating hours.

title: St. Vincent DePaul Holiday Food Bank receives donation
author: Staff reports
content: Sacred Heart Catholic Church’s annual “Christmas in September” sale, which features gently used donations of holiday decorations, raised $7,800 for the St. Vincent DePaul Holiday Food Bank, and will provide holiday meals for those in need. The sale is sponsored by the Sacred Heart Altar Society and the Knights of Columbus Council 1484.

title: City Council approves controversial farm land lease agreements
author: Brett Briscoe
content: COLDWATER, MI (WTVB) – The Coldwater City Council Monday night approved five lease agreements for City owned farm ground with three of the leases going to the highest bidders from the original process that was brought forward at the September 14, meeting those properties are located on North Willowbrook Road, Angola Road and Butters Ave. The process became muddied at that September 14 meeting when Brian Sexton of Sexton Farms who has two of the current lease agreement spoke before council and challenged the bidding process causing council to to choose different path for the two largest tracts on Newton Road and West Chicago Street , deciding to pause the standard five-year award process despite receiving higher bids from Matthew Avery and Mark Barone. Sexton claimed in the past, the current land operators of the farm ground were given the option to match a higher bid, saying his farm had invested thousands of dollars in the Newton Road and West Chicago street properties to make the land farmable. Council then entertained a proposal to extend the Sexton Farm leases for a year to allow city staff time to re-word and update the lease agreement contracts. That process did not sit well with Mark Barone of Barone farms who had the highest bid for leasing the 72 plus acers on West Chicago Street document.createElement('audio'); https://media-cdn.socastsrm.com/wordpress/wp-content/blogs.dir/2484/files/2026/10/barone-lease.wav Barone also challenged the claims made by Sexton Farms at the previous meeting https://media-cdn.socastsrm.com/wordpress/wp-content/blogs.dir/2484/files/2026/10/barone-cut-two.wav In the end Council voted 6-3 to extend the leases by Sexton Farms for a year with the no votes coming from council members Rissman, Johnson and Knaack.

title: NBA roundup: Cavs rally from 15 down, hand Wolves first loss in OT
author: Syndicated Content
content: By Field Level Media Oct 27 (Field Level Media) – Donovan Mitchell hit a tiebreaking midrange jumper with 48 seconds left in overtime as the host Cleveland Cavaliers rallied from a 15-point deficit to defeat the previously unbeaten Minnesota Timberwolves 127-125 on Monday night. Timberwolves superstar Anthony Edwards missed a wide-open 3-pointer with 3.9 seconds remaining that could have tied the game. Peyton Watson grabbed the rebound and made two free throws to push Cleveland’s lead to 127-122. Mitchell finished with 26 points and seven assists, while James Harden had 19 points and nine assists for the Cavaliers, who ​improved to 2-1. Evan Mobley added 18 points and 10 rebounds, and rookie Meleek Thomas scored 16 off the bench in his NBA debut. Edwards connected on a 3-pointer at the buzzer to finish ‌with a season-high 47 points, his seventh career regular-season game with at least Jaden McDaniels had 14 points and Rudy Gobert collected 20 rebounds and LaMelo Ball had 11 points and seven turnovers. Warriors 134, Nuggets 114 Steph Curry hit all eight of his field-goal attempts and scored 17 of his 24 points in the third quarter, leading visiting Golden State over Denver for its first win of the season. Curry made a trio of 3-pointers and all five of his free-throw attempts to complete his perfect night. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg scored a career-high 31 points and added 12 rebounds, Brandin Podziemski scored 18 points, Gui Santos contributed 13 and Al Horford had 11 for Golden State. DeMar DeRozan scored a team-high 21 points, Nikola Jokic finished with 19 points and 11 assists, Jamal Murray also had ‌19 points ​and Bryce Hopkins added 13 points for Denver, which played the final 8:34 without Aaron Gordon after the forward was hit with two technicals. Bucks 110, ⁠Pacers 102 Tyler Herro compiled 23 points, 10 rebounds and seven assists ⁠as Milwaukee notched the first win of the Taylor Jenkins era, defeating visiting Indiana. Ryan Rollins added 19, Kyle Kuzma had 17 and Kel’el Ware paired 16 points with 14 rebounds as Milwaukee avoided its first 0-4 start to a season since 1976-77, 50 years ago. Tyrese Haliburton posted 22 points and nine assists for Indiana, while Pascal Siakam chalked up 20 points, 13 boards and six assists. Mavericks 113, Heat 109 Reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg returned from a one-game absence to score 29 points and dish 11 assists as visiting Dallas defeated Miami. Flagg, who sat out Saturday due to a left shoulder injury, added six ​rebounds against the Heat. He shot 12 of 23 overall and 2 of 8 on 3-point attempts. Kyrie Irving, who was rested in Dallas’ previous game, posted 18 points, six rebounds and six assists. Giannis Antetokounmpo posted his first triple-double for the Heat — 29 points, 15 rebounds and 11 assists — but Miami fell to 0-4 on the season. Besides Antetokounmpo’s contributions, Miami got 21 points from Davion Mitchell. All-Star center Bam Adebayo was held to eight ⁠points and eight rebounds. Celtics 134, Bulls 99 Payton Pritchard came off the bench to score a game-high 28 points to lead Boston to ⁠a victory over visiting Chicago. Pritchard made 7 of 10 shots from behind the 3-point arc. Jayson Tatum added 23 points, seven rebounds and six assists for Boston, ​which made 21 of its 44 3-point attempts and had a 54-40 edge in rebounds. Norman Powell led the Bulls with 20 points. Caleb Wilson tossed in 17, and Josh Giddey and Matas Buzelis each finished with 11. Leonard Miller ​had nine points and nine rebounds. Thunder 125, Suns 114 Ajay Mitchell scored 30 to lead Oklahoma City to a home win over Phoenix a day after losing a pair of ‌starters to long-term injuries. Oklahoma City was playing its first game since Jalen Williams suffered a fractured fibula and a dislocated left ankle in the closing minutes of a win over the Clippers. Earlier in that game, Cason Wallace suffered a torn labrum. Both will require surgery and will be out long term. In the win over Phoenix, Alex Caruso left after turning his right ankle. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 26 points on 11-of-18 shooting and Isaiah Hartenstein had 15 points and 13 rebounds. Phoenix’s Devin Booker had scored a combined 66 points over the first two games but finished with just three points on 1-of-7 shooting. Jalen Green led the Suns with 20 points while Dillon Brooks added 19. Rockets ⁠120, Hawks 110 Alperen Sengun scored a game-high 29 points, Jabari Smith Jr. added a double- double and Houston Rockets remained unbeaten by beating visiting Atlanta. Sengun added nine rebounds and nine assists to pace a balanced attack. Smith paired 16 points with 12 rebounds, while Kevin Durant added 22 points and nine boards. Tari Eason and Reed Sheppard scored 13 points apiece off the bench. Jalen Johnson paced the Hawks with 21 points and nine rebounds while ⁠CJ McCollum added 20 points and four 3-pointers. The Hawks dropped back-to-back games against ‌the Rockets. Grizzlies 110, Jazz 105 Ty Jerome scored eight of his 15 points in the final six minutes — including two clutch free throws with 11.6 seconds remaining — to ⁠lead Memphis to a victory over host Utah. The Grizzlies won their fourth straight game to open the season for only the second time in franchise history. ​Meanwhile, Utah lost ‌two starters in the first half. Jaren Jackson Jr., the former Grizzlies star, injured his right knee in the second quarter and did not return. Lauri ​Markkanen injured his right ⁠wrist early in the first quarter and did not return. Cedric Coward had 16 points and 11 rebounds, Jaylen Wells added 14 points and Cam Boozer and Jerami Grant each scored 13 for Memphis. Keyonte George had 26 points for the Jazz and Ace Bailey contributed 17 points and 10 boards. Mo Bamba added 14 points and seven rebounds off the bench. Hornets 110, Wizards 103 Brandon Miller scored a career-high 39 points and Charlotte held off visiting Washington for their first back-to-back wins of the young season. Miller made 15 of 28 shots from the field, including five 3-pointers. Naz Reid added 18 points and 12 rebounds for Charlotte, while Grayson Allen scored 15 off the bench, including seven from the free-throw line. Moussa Diabate chipped in 11 points and 17 rebounds. Anthony Davis scored 29 points and grabbed 10 rebounds for the Wizards, hitting three of Washington’s nine 3-point attempts. Trae Young added 22 points and 10 assists, Kyshawn George posted 20 ​points and Alex Sarr had 12 points. (–Field Level Media)

title: Meghan to join Australia’s Junior MasterChef next year

title: India’s Cipla misses quarterly profit view on muted US sales
author: Syndicated Content
content: Oct 27 (Reuters) – Cipla, India’s third-largest drugmaker by revenue, missed second-quarter profit estimates on Tuesday, as muted sales of generic Revlimid ​and stiff competition weighed on its US ‌business. The company’s consolidated net profit fell to 8.78 billion rupees ($92.2 million) in the quarter ended September 30, from 13.51 billion rupees a year ago. Analysts, on average, had expected ‌profit ​to fall to 9.42 billion ⁠rupees, according to data ⁠compiled by LSEG. Cipla is facing mounting pressure in its key US market as sales of generic Revlimid – Bristol-Myer Squibb’s blood cancer drug – continue to ​taper amid rising competition, increasing its dependence on India where sustained growth in chronic therapies ⁠and newer launches are ⁠helping offset the drag. The company is ​also banking on obesity drug, Yurpeak, to support growth ​as weakness in the US business weighs ‌on overall momentum. Yurpeak is Cipla’s brand of Eli Lilly’s tirzepatide, which it sells in India under a partnership with Lilly.Revenue from its India ⁠business rose 12%, while North America revenue decreased 19% during the quarter. Revenue from operations fell 2.4% to 74.04 ⁠billion rupees during ‌the quarter, partly due to ⁠a reclassification from April 1, 2026, ​that now ‌presents certain marketing and promotional expenses ​as a ⁠reduction from revenue rather than under other expenses, with no impact on profit or cash flows. India and North America together contribute about two-thirds of Cipla’s revenue. (Reporting by Kashish Tandon in Bengaluru; Editing by ​Jochelle Mendonca)

title: Attackers kill 60 people in Ethiopia’s conflict-hit Oromiya region, Orthodox church says
author: Syndicated Content
content: NAIROBI, Oct 27 (Reuters) – At least 60 people were killed in two separate attacks in Ethiopia’s conflict-hit Oromiya region in the ​past week, the Ethiopian Orthodox Church said. Church ‌authorities said the dead were all Christians, but did not go into details on how they died or who was behind the attacks. The Oromiya regional government and ‌a ​source linked to a rebel ⁠alliance fighting government forces ⁠in the northern Tigray region traded blame for the attacks. The Holy Synod of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church said 14 believers were killed ​in Merti Woreda on October 20 and 46 in Sherka Woreda on October 24. More ⁠than 20 homes were also ⁠burned and more than 20 people ​hospitalised with severe injuries, the church’s statement, issued ​on Monday, added. The regional government said the rebel ‌alliance launched the attacks to try to spark religious conflict, without providing evidence. The source linked to the rebel alliance said the Oromiya regional ⁠government had carried out the killings, citing conversations with two local residents. The Oromo Liberation Army rebel group, which ⁠the regional ‌government has blamed for previous attacks ⁠on Orthodox Christians, did not immediately ​respond ‌to a request for comment. The OLA ​is one ⁠of seven armed groups that announced last month that they had formed an alliance aimed at overthrowing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government. (Reporting by Nairobi newsroom;Writing by Vincent Mumo Nzilani;Editing by Alexander Winning and ​Andrew Heavens)

title: Caviar, champagne and a Porsche ride as aviation widens its class divide
author: Syndicated Content
content: By Alessandro Parodi and Joanna Plucinska ROISSY-EN-FRANCE, France, Oct 27 (Reuters) – A sleek black Porsche Cayenne glides across the tarmac at Charles de Gaulle airport in Paris as it delivers the elite passengers many airlines are seeking to court to an Air France Boeing 777 jet. The sharpened focus on the world’s wealthiest is an industry reaction to a surge in fuel prices that has squeezed margins and led to fare increases that have deterred the ​more cost-conscious economy passengers. Air France, which says its “La Première”, or first-class, fares rank among the industry’s most expensive, is seeking to stand apart by spending €1 ‌billion ($1 billion) on upgrading its services. In addition to the private car to the plane, Première class customers get their own entrance at the airport, discrete security checks, a lounge with a spa and caviar and champagne while they wait. On board, they can spend their flight in a private suite, wearing designer pyjamas and eating food designed by Michelin-star chefs. “We really wanted to move upmarket,” Air France’s Executive Vice President Customer Fabien Pelous told Reuters on board the plane. “Over the past five years, we have created this new cabin and we have paid attention to every detail to push it to the maximum of the expectations ‌of ​our customers,” Pelous said. “We wanted to create the space like in a private jet.” Apart from the €1 billion investment in lounges, ⁠cabins and improved WiFi over a five-year period, ⁠he said Air France was spending another €1 billion a year as part on its annual fleet renewal costs. SOCIETY’S WIDENING DIVIDE The widening gap between the experience of elite airline passengers and those flying economy reflects society as a whole. The surge in fuel costs, linked to the US-Israeli war with Iran, and an attendant rise in inflation has helped to spark social unrest over the cost of living in some countries, including France. It coincides with an artificial intelligence-led surge in stock markets and ​the creation of a new super-rich class. Aviation analyst John Strickland said airlines were willing to reduce the overall number of seats in order to increase their premium sector, which he said had grown substantially. “It’s understandable why airlines are investing in that, changing their cabin configurations with lower overall seats,” he said. Industry body the International Air Transport Association ⁠in a report in June found that overall growth in travel was slowing, with passenger traffic, across ⁠all classes, expected to increase by only 2.1% this year, compared with 5.3% last year. Air France does not break out separate figures ​for its highest class, but said the combined first and business-class sector grew by 28.1% in 2025 and 26.9% in 2024, while economy revenue stagnated. Its first-class flights start at just ​below $14,000 for a Paris-New York return ticket, which the company says offers a unique experience. “We did invest a lot of money both on ‌the ground and in the air,” Chief Executive Ben Smith told Reuters in an interview. “This particular cabin or class is unmatched.” The Skytrax World Airline Awards, one of the best-known airline rankings, this year named Air France the world’s best first-class airline. THE ADVANTAGE OF ANONYMITY The amount of space and resources allocated to each first-class passenger means they have a heavy carbon footprint, although lighter than if they travelled in a private jet. Air France says its services can also be preferable for showbiz stars and other VIP travellers because they provide anonymity ⁠whereas private jets, which owners have to register, can be tracked on aviation surveillance websites. Other airlines are also seeking to increase their luxury appeal. In Asia, Air India has rolled out new cabins on some international routes, while IAG-owned British Airways earlier this month said it was revamping its A380 fleet to reduce the overall number of seats and increase ⁠the focus on premium customers. Roberto Alvo, the chief executive of LATAM ‌Airlines Group, said this month he believed airlines with robust premium offerings would emerge the strongest from the current economic ⁠turmoil, which he predicted would lead to some consolidation. In the US, traditionally low-fare airlines such as Southwest, Frontier, JetBlue and ​Allegiant are moving upmarket. Delta ‌Air Lines has also said it is targeting the upper end of what is known as a “K-shaped economy”, in ​which sections of the ⁠population are becoming richer and others — the downward arm of the K — are becoming poorer. Air France’s Pelous acknowledged that even some of the rich could start to worry more about cost as the war in Iran, which began at the end of February, continues to drive energy prices, but he said the company would not change its luxury strategy. The price of jet fuel, which accounts for 30% to 40% of airlines’ expenses, has more than doubled since the start of the year. “The first impact of this war is a huge increase in the cost of petrol that definitely affects us,” Pelous said. “But despite this complicated context, we want to maintain our strategy to move upmarket.” ($1 = 0.8905 euros) (Additional reporting by Abhijith Ganapavaram and Allison Lampert; ​Editing by Adam Jourdan and Barbara Lewis)

title: Elsa Hosk is Back in Her Angel Wings!
author: Echo Lawrence
content: Elsa Hosk knows a thing or two about making an entrance at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show. The Swedish supermodel returned to the famous runway in Los Angeles on Sunday night, bringing back the kind of Angel energy that helped make her one of the brand’s most recognizable faces. Elsa has a memorable place in Victoria’s Secret history. Back in 2018, she wore the brand’s iconic Fantasy Bra, a jaw-dropping creation that turned her into the center of attention thanks to its spectacular display of diamonds. This year, that honor went to Kylie Jenner, who made her own runway debut wearing a new Fantasy Bra reportedly valued at $50 million. So while Kylie got to be the woman wearing the diamonds this time around, Elsa was back doing what she does best: looking like she was born to walk in lingerie and wings. Elsa has been a fan favorite for years, and seeing her back on the runway was another highlight for longtime followers of the brand. Some models make a great impression for a season; others become part of the show’s history. Elsa is firmly in the second category. title: Rosie Huntington-Whiteley Is Back in Her Angel Wings After 16 Years!

content: Rosie Huntington-Whiteley is proof that some things really do get better with age. The British model returned to the Victoria’s Secret runway in Los Angeles on Sunday night, marking 20 years since her first time on the iconic runway. Rosie first walked for the lingerie brand back in 2006, when she was just 19 years old. She went on to become one of Victoria’s Secret’s best-known Angels before moving on to other projects, including beauty, her own business ventures and having babies with Jason Statham. title: Kylie Jenner Walks the Victoria’s Secret Runway in a $50 Million Diamond Bra!
author: Echo Lawrence
content: Kylie Jenner has found a way to make the rest of us feel broke while wearing underwear. Kylie hit the runway wearing the brand’s legendary Fantasy Bra, a diamond-covered creation valued at a ridiculous $50 million. title: Victoria’s Secret Just Rejected Romee Strijd and Frida Aasen!
author: Echo Lawrence
content: Well, Victoria’s Secret, we have some questions. Two of the hottest models to ever grace the lingerie brand’s runway have reportedly been left out of this year’s Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show, and we’re struggling to understand the logic here. Romee Strijd and Frida Aasen have both confirmed they won’t be walking this year’s show after going through casting in New York City a few weeks ago. Romee, a former Victoria’s Secret Angel who walked the show from 2014 to 2018, opened up about the rejection in a series of candid TikTok videos. Frida also confirmed she didn’t make the lineup. @romeestrijd ♬ original sound – romee strijd @romeestrijd ♬ original sound – romee strijd Romee explained that she had spent the summer training and preparing for a potential return to the runway after having two children. She traveled to NYC for casting in September, then spent weeks waiting for an answer. Eventually, she was told she wouldn’t be part of the show, with the explanation that the team didn’t think she’d fit this year’s lineup. She said the experience made her feel unsupported by her agency and suggested she probably wouldn’t audition for the show again. That’s a pretty disappointing ending for someone who helped make the brand’s runway so memorable. And then there’s Frida Aasen, another stunning model who would have looked right at home in those wings. We’re not saying Victoria’s Secret has to bring back every familiar face, but good luck finding two hotter women to walk that runway this year… Victoria’s Secret has been trying to reinvent its fashion show and appeal to a new generation, but surely there’s room for established Angels who already know how to deliver the fantasy. We can only imagine what kind of trolls VS has replaced these two angels with this year.
