title: How Molly Ringwald is Using Her 'Gen X Poster Girl' Status to Raise Awareness
author: Nealy Simms
content: Although we’ve bid farewell to side ponytails, power suits and popped-up collars, one ‘ 80s icon is looking to remind the generation that grew up beside her that their health matters just as much as nostalgia. After years of playing characters who helped define an era of teen angst, Molly Ringwald , 58, is using her voice for a new cause, partnering with Pfizer and its VaxAssist platform to raise awareness of pneumococcal pneumonia and remind Gen X they shouldn’t play hooky on visiting their doctor’s office. “One thing that really struck me was the fact that after the age of 50, we are six times more likely to contract pneumococcal pneumonia,” Ringwald exclusively told Us about the prominence of the illness. “I felt as the ultimate Gen X poster girl, it was a good idea to use my platform to just let other people know that this vaccine is available, that it can help save your life.” But the conversation around health isn’t one the actress is reserving for audiences who watched her navigate the growing pains of adolescence on screen (including the occasional Saturday detentions and juvenile love triangles). Ringwald says she has plenty of “frank” conversations with her own children. “I’m just really straight with them. I think you know they have agency over themselves and their bodies, and we talk about everything from vaccines to sunscreen to anything for their health,” she told Us . “It’s their health, it’s their bodies and their futures, and I think they care about it just like I care about my health and my future.” The mother of three — daughter Mathilda, 22, and 17-year-old twins Adele and Roman, whom she shares with her husband, Panio Gianopoulos — admits that although she doesn’t revisit the coming-of-age classics on her own, she has introduced her children to the films that made her a household name. “I don’t actually have cable, so anything that I watch is a choice,” she candidly shared. “And the only time that I’ve really watched the John Hughes movies was when I watched them with my kids, and that was a choice.” As the actress prepares to play Van Palmer’s mother in the Paramount+ series Yellowjackets , Ringwald says her character, Vicky, is much more “flawed” than the poignant parent she played in the past to Shailene Woodley in The Secret Life of an American Teenager or KJ Apa in Riverdale. Darko Sikman/Paramount+ “I was already a fan of the show,” she said, recalling a chance encounter with a cast member at the Sundance Film Festival that led to her receiving a role. “I think it has a lot of great actors in it and it’s fun watching women my age being fierce and bad and naughty. I love it.” Beyond her return to TV, the actress also revealed she isn’t done writing her own story. As for what else is in the works, Ringwald says she’s currently penning a memoir called The Paris Years , which she says will take readers down memory lane and chronicle her years in France during her 20s and says directing is something she’s “always wanted to do.” “I spent sort of coming of age in Paris because I kind of came of age a little bit later because I was working when I was a teenager. So the 20s were really when I kind of came of age,” she told Us , adding she plans to begin writing and directing once her book is finished.

title: Why Aldi Grocery Dupes Are Getting So Much Attention From Shoppers
author: Ashley Lynch
content: You know that moment in the cookie aisle when your kid grabs the blue Oreo package and you glance at the price tag. Then you spot the store-brand version a shelf over for a couple of dollars less and wonder if anybody would actually notice the difference. Grocery dupes are built on that trade-off, and more families are leaning on them to keep weekly carts affordable without yanking favorite snacks out of the lineup. Store-brand lookalikes are having a moment, and Aldi is at the center of a lot of the chatter online. What Are Grocery Dupes and How Do They Work? Grocery dupes are products shoppers put side by side with recognizable name-brand foods, comparing taste, look, ingredients and the overall experience of eating them. They turn up in cookies, candy, chips, sauces and frozen meals, which is why the idea has caught on with families trying to stretch a weekly budget. A lot of grocery dupes are private-label items sold under a retailer’s own brand. Not every store-brand product counts, though. Some are their own thing and were never designed to mimic a specific national-brand snack. Nicole Kidman’s Burgundy Bag Is Giving Quiet Luxury — Get the Designer Look for Just $30 Which Aldi Dupes Are Shoppers Talking About? Walk down an Aldi aisle and a few products come up over and over in the dupe conversation. Benton’s Original Chocolate Sandwich Creme Cookies are a popular Oreo alternative. A Simply Recipes blind taste test flagged noticeable differences between the two, and the reviewer still preferred Oreos in the end. Allrecipes’ roundup of Aldi copycats calls out Clancy’s Original Potato Chips as a Lay’s alternative and Choceur Peanut Butter Cups as a stand-in for Reese’s. The same roundup points to Benton’s Peanut Butter Filled Cookies as a swap for Girl Scout Tagalongs, so the dupe idea even stretches to specialty treats you can only get a few weeks a year. A dupe doesn’t have to taste identical to earn a spot in your cart. Sometimes families end up liking the alternative better. How Shoppers Are Comparing Dupes Online Social media and online shopping groups are doing a lot of the heavy lifting. Reddit threads, TikTok videos and taste-test posts give parents a place to compare notes and vouch for the swaps that actually hold up at snack time. Allrecipes points to Reddit discussions where shoppers line up store-brand chips, cookies and candy against the national favorites. The same report mentions a shopper who ran a blind taste test of Aldi’s L’oven bagels against Thomas’ bagels and ended up preferring the Aldi version. These conversations focus on texture, flavor and value, so you get more to go on than a sticker shock comparison before taking a chance on something new. Why Store Brands Are Growing Store-brand products are posting record numbers right now. According to the Private Label Manufacturers Association’s 2026 report , U.S. store-brand sales hit a record $282.8 billion in 2025 and grew faster than national-brand sales. The association’s store-brand research also points to improving quality and value as reasons shoppers are reaching for retailer-owned products. That growth doesn’t prove dupe culture is driving the shift. It does show that more shoppers are willing to try something besides the familiar label. What Grocery Dupes Mean for Name Brands Brand loyalty is still real, and plenty of parents keep buying the same cereal, cracker or cookie they grew up on. But Retail Brew’s reporting on private-label growth shows retailer-owned products are winning shoppers over on quality as well as price. A good grocery dupe can nudge families to toss a few more store-brand picks in the cart next time. Cheaper doesn’t always mean better, and not every store-brand item is a copycat. Still, the growing habit of comparing an Aldi cookie with the one on the next shelf suggests familiar packaging isn’t the only thing deciding what ends up in the family basket anymore.

title: Dad Arrested After Dropping Baby Off at Grandparents House With 'Peeling' Skin
author: Katherine Schaffstall
content: A North Carolina father was arrested after he allegedly burned his 7-week-old baby with hot bath water before dropping the child off at his grandparents’ home while the infant’s skin was “peeling” off. Jaylen Walker has been charged with felony child abuse after his son allegedly suffered second- and third-degree “burns” to his body “from hot water” during an incident on Wednesday, October 21, according to court documents viewed by Law & Crime . “On or about the date of offense shown and in the county named above the defendant unlawfully, willfully, and feloniously did intentionally inflict serious bodily injury … on [the child],” an arrest warrant stated. “The defendant was the child’s parent.” Prosecutors claim that after Walker, 22, allegedly burnt his child while giving him a bath, he called his son’s grandparents and explained the alleged situation. Walker allegedly told them that he tried to apply Vaseline to the child’s body as his skin kept peeling away, according to WGHP . Prosecutors added that he later dropped the child off with his grandparents. Mother Burned Son, 6, and Made Him Stand Outside in the Cold as Punishment Walker then allegedly told the child’s mother about the burns, at which point she urged him to seek emergency help. The woman was not home at the time of the incident because she was at work. “She was in constant contact with the father, advising him he needed to call 911 and that she was on her way,” a prosecutor claimed during Walker’s first court appearance on Friday, October 23. The child’s mother ultimately called 911 to report the burns, and Greensboro police and emergency crews were dispatched to an apartment complex around 4:30 p.m. on Wednesday. EMS personnel were already at the scene by the time the officers arrived. The baby was taken to the hospital for treatment, where doctors reportedly discovered that he had healing rib fractures in addition to the burns. Prosecutors said during the hearing that officers could not locate Walker for several hours after the incident, and he was eventually found at a local grocery store. He was then taken into custody around 1 a.m. on Thursday, October 22. Man Arrested After Allegedly Throwing Hot Soup on Baby, Assaulting Woman Meanwhile, Walker’s defense argued that he had no criminal record and that there was no evidence to indicate that he intentionally hurt his son. Walker has since been denied bond. He’s scheduled to return to court on Wednesday, November 25. It’s not currently clear if Walker has entered a plea, and an attorney was not immediately able to be contacted. The investigation into the case remains ongoing. If you or someone you know is experiencing child abuse, call or text Child Help Hotline at 1-800-422-4453.

title: Convicted Killer at Large After Escaping From Prison by Slipping Through Fence
author: Julia Marnin
content: A man convicted of murder is at large after he escaped a Tennessee prison where he’s been serving a life sentence, authorities said. Jacob Allen Morley escaped the Northwest Correctional Complex in Lake County the evening of Sunday, October 25, according to the Tennessee Department of Correction . He’s wanted by the department and the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation. Morley, 28, “should be considered dangerous,” the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation said in a Monday, October 26, Facebook post . He’s been added to the state’s most wanted list. Morley is described as 6 feet tall, weighing around 240 to 270 pounds, with green eyes and brown hair. Man Accused of Kidnapping and Killing 7-Year-Old Girl Nearly 30 Years Ago Officials are calling on the public’s help in locating him. “Residents in the area are asked to check home security and doorbell cameras, trail and hunting cameras, and other surveillance systems for possible sightings or activity,” the Tennessee Department of Correction said in an update shared to Facebook on Monday. “Anyone who sees Morley or has information about his whereabouts should not approach him,” the department warned. Morley was sentenced to life in prison after he was convicted of first-degree murder, aggravated burglary, tampering with evidence, evading arrest and vandalism in connection with the death of Cody Birchfield, according to authorities. Birchfield was considered missing until his body was found buried below Morley’s home in March 2022, WJHL-TV reported. The Carter County Sheriff’s Office started investigating Birchfield’s disappearance in February 2022 following the last sighting of him in Elizabethton, according to The Tennessean . Tennessee Sex Offender Receives Record-Breaking 438-Year Prison Sentence Morley was found guilty of murder in Birchfield’s death in February 2025, before he was sentenced in the case in June 2025, per the TV station. Morley allegedly escaped the Northwest Correctional Complex, which has the capacity to house up to 1,776 male inmates, by slipping through a fence, according to the Associated Press . As of Monday, investigators “have searched and cleared buildings and structures in the surrounding area, and the Tennessee Highway Patrol has deployed aviation assets and state troopers to assist with the search,” the Tennessee Department of Correction said. Authorities are offering $2,500 for information leading to Morley’s arrest and urge anyone who sees Morley to call 911 or the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation at 1-800-TBI-FIND.

title: SZA Debuts Her First VANS Collaboration With VANSZA Drop 1
author: Keenan Higgins
content: India Sleem/Yudo Kurita/VANS The anticipation has been building to see what SZA would bring to the table after being appointed Artistic Director for VANS. After fronting the brand’s “Off the Wall” campaign for Spring 2026 earlier this year, the record-breaking R&B queen is officially ready to unveil her first collaborative collection. Who’s ready for some VANSZA! RELATED: SZA Shines For Vans In Spring 2026 “Off the Wall” Campaign Featured in a lookbook that captures the essence of SZA — a collision of nature, creativity and self-expression — the collection is highlighted by her iterations of the Knu Skool Mule and Authentic Kickdown. Both silhouettes incorporate motifs that put you in the mind of the music video for her GRAMMY-nominated single, “Good Days,” with the latter infusing custom artwork by Sage Adams. Photographer India Sleem pairs a classic California backdrop with product and landscape photography courtesy of Yudo Kurita to create imagery that accentuates the collection itself. Butterflies, duck camo, bug life and creatures of the sea pair perfectly over a range of hoodies, checkered print, shorts, sweats, denim and other streetwear essentials. VANSZA Drop 1 really comes together to tell the story of why a collaboration of this nature makes so much sense. With the Authentic Kickdown for example, the collapsible heel is directly influenced by the way she treated her kicks growing up. She states in the press release , “My mom has been telling me, ‘Please stop stepping on the back of your shoes’ my whole life. She hates it. So I put the design aspect in my shoes.” It’s these personal anecdotes that give the collection as a whole an eclectic vibe that only SZA could spin. You can expect the VANSZA Drop 1 collection to officially launch on October 22, 2026, both online and at VANS retail locations. SZA herself will make special appearances at Vans Glendale Galleria in California on October 17 and Foot Locker at Freehold Raceway Mall in New Jersey on October 21. title: ‘Feel The Rhythm! Feel The Rhyme!’ Where Is The Cast Of ‘Cool Runnings’ Now?
author: Shannon Dawson
content: Source: Michael Loccisano/ Arturo Holmes If you grew up watching Cool Runnings , chances are you still remember the Jamaican bobsled team that proved you don’t need snow, fancy equipment or years of experience to chase an Olympic dream. Released in 1993, the beloved sports comedy brought plenty of laughs, unforgettable characters and an inspiring message about determination, teamwork and believing in yourself. So, where is the cast of Cool Runnings now? Well, let’s catch you up to speed about the film first. Loosely based on the real-life Jamaican bobsled team’s journey to the 1988 Winter Olympics in Calgary, Canada, the Disney classic followed Derice Bannock, Sanka Coffie, Yul Brenner and Junior Bevil as they traded the tropical heat of Jamaica for the freezing temperatures of the bobsled track. With the help of their unconventional coach, Irving “Irv” Blitzer, the unlikely underdogs faced skepticism, financial challenges and plenty of spills along the way. More than three decades later, the film remains a fan favorite. But what happened to the actors who brought these memorable characters to life? From starring in hit television shows to releasing new music and taking on fresh film projects, here’s where the cast of Cool Runnings is today. Leon Robinson as Derice Bannoc k Leon Robinson, who played team captain Derice Bannock, continued building an impressive career in entertainment long after Cool Runnings crossed the finish line. Robinson went on to appear in several memorable films, including the basketball drama Above the Rim , alongside Tupac Shakur, as well as The Five Heartbeats and The Temptations . His career has also included music, with Robinson performing alongside his band, Leon & The Peoples, which is preparing to release new music. He has also continued working in film. In September, Robinson unveiled Wildcards , a gritty courtroom thriller exploring what happens on the road to justice. He stars as Greg Sims, an undefeated veteran defense attorney with a 20-year unblemished record. From the bobsled track to the courtroom, Robinson clearly hasn’t slowed down. Hit the flip to see what the rest of the cast of Cool Runnings are doing today.

author: Walter Gainer II
content: Hosted by Brian “Boss” Valmond, the popular true-crime series explores the lives, crimes, and cultural influence of some of the most notorious figures in American history   The Urban One Podcast Network is proud to welcome the Infamy podcast, created and hosted by media entrepreneur, writer, and storyteller Brian “Boss” Valmond, to its growing portfolio of compelling audio content.  Known for its cinematic storytelling and rigorous historical research, Infamy is a scripted narrative true-crime series that explores the lives, crimes, and cultural impact of some of the most notorious figures in American history. Through a distinctive blend of investigative reporting, archival material, immersive sound design, and narrative storytelling, the series explores the intersections of organized crime, street culture, hip-hop, race, and American history.  Each episode takes listeners beyond the headlines and folklore, providing deeper context on the individuals, organizations, and cultural movements that have helped shape American society.  Valmond’s work has earned recognition for its ability to connect crime stories with broader conversations around history, identity, and culture. Through his company, ValTown, Brian has cultivated an audience of more than 400,000 followers across social platforms while expanding into publishing, documentary filmmaking, television, and original digital storytelling. His work has also been featured by major media outlets, including The New York Times .  “I’m incredibly excited to continue this journey of storytelling by joining the Urban One Podcast Network team with Infamy” said Brian Valmond. “These stories are important and I’m honored to be a part of a company who embodies black culture and prioritizes our stories.”  Infamy is more than a crime podcast. It tells stories of power, survival, culture, identity, and the ways certain individuals and communities have influenced American history.  “Brian is a dynamic storyteller with a clear vision and a passion for uncovering overlooked narratives. We’re thrilled to add Infamy to our lineup and look forward to growing the brand alongside him.” — Dre Smith, Sr. Director of Podcast Operations. New episodes from the upcoming season of the Infamy podcast are available across the Urban One Podcast Network and wherever podcasts are available.  For more information about the Urban One Podcast Network, visit www.urban1podcasts.com and listen to Infamy today on Spotify , Apple Podcasts , and all major podcast platforms.

title: Congratulations! Nivea Reveals Her Cancer Is Now In Remission: ‘I Couldn’t Believe It!’
author: Shannon Dawson
content: Source: Prince Williams / Getty Nivea , the 2000s R&B goddess responsible for hits like “Laundromat” and “Don’t Mess With My Man,” is on the mend after a scary diagnosis of chronic myeloid leukemia — also known as CML – in early 2026. During an Oct. 7 appearance on The Tamron Hall Show, the 44-year-old revealed that her battle with the blood cancer was in remission thanks to a groundbreaking clinical trial administered by her doctor, Colin Vale. “I couldn’t believe it because this happened to me this year, only a few months ago,” she said in disbelief. Nivea found out about her diagnosis shortly after discovering a painful “knot” on her side. Nivea is taking an FDA-approved targeted treatment to fight her CML. The singer said she’s grateful to have taken part in Vale’s clinical trial, where she is receiving an FDA-approved targeted treatment. She takes two pills once a day, preferably at the same time each day.  Dr. Colin Vale — who was also present for the interview — explained that to understand how chronic myeloid leukemia develops, it helps to think of the bone marrow as the body’s blood-cell factory. Normally, the bone marrow produces the right amount of blood cells to meet the body’s needs. But in CML, a genetic change involving chromosomes 9 and 22 causes abnormal cells to develop and multiply uncontrollably, disrupting the normal production of blood cells. “So the way that we treat this type of blood cancer is with a targeted therapy, where we can precisely focus on the abnormal signaling in the bone marrow to stop the growth of the cancer cells,” he explained.  Nivea said that while she’s happy her leukemia is now in remission, she still has a long recovery road ahead.   “It has been an adjustment, the symptoms. I’m tired a lot. I have other issues —  bleeding,” she revealed. “I found out I have fibroids, but I’m still on the better side. I’m not complaining…the medicine has definitely helped.” Nivea is making new music and gave a sneak peek of her new song “Ferris Wheel.” With a bill of new health, Nivea said she’s been pouring energy into new music and her passion for audio engineering. The Grammy-nominated singer has enrolled in night school to study the field. “I’ve always wanted to be an audio engineer. I believe I have engineer ears. I’m in love with sound in general in so many different ways,” she gushed.  Source: Paras Griffin / Getty She’s also started taking vocal training to learn some “tricks and tools” to be better at her craft. Later on in the episode, the star gave the audience a sneak peek of her new song, “Ferris Wheel,” her first single in 20 years.  Throughout her difficult health journey, Nivea said she has been grateful to have a strong support system by her side. That includes the father of her children, super-producer The-Dream, as well as Lil Wayne. “I’ve been very much supported,” she said, noting that The-Dream and his wife even came to visit her while she was in the hospital. Congrats to Nivea! RELATED CONTENT: Nivea Reveals Leukemia Diagnosis At 44, Says She’s Taking It ‘Day By Day’

title: Bre Tiesi Says She’ll Leave Nick Cannon If He Has Another Baby, Blasts His Five Other Baby Mamas As ‘Insecure’—’We Are Not The Same’
author: Danielle Canada
content: Source: Jerritt Clark / Gett Bre Tiesi may be one of six women who share children with prolific procreator Nick Cannon, but the Selling Sunset star insists she’s in a league of her own. During a candid appearance on Angela Yee’s Lip Service podcast , Bre blasted Cannon’s other baby mamas as “insecure,” revealed why baby No. 13 could cause the end of their relationship, and detailed the difficulties of filming his forthcoming Netflix series, which she called the “worst thing” she’s ever done. On Wednesday’s episode of Lip Service , Angela brought up Nick Cannon’s previous description of Bre Tiesi as his “twin flame,” noting that while the entertainer insists he doesn’t have a favorite among his children’s mothers, he’s acknowledged that Bre understands him better than the others. Bre agreed. “Yeah, we’re very, very similar,” she said. “And I think that, like, I really accept this crazy lifestyle, even though people think that I don’t.” The reality star who shares a 4-year-old son, Legendary Love, with the father of 12, has repeatedly defended their relationship against criticism, maintaining that their arrangement allows her to preserve her independence while building a life with someone she loves. She emphasized that, when asked on the podcast whether she thought she’d wind up with Nick long-term. “He is my partner. I think he is my life partner. I genuinely love this man,” she said. We have a great relationship. I love our family regardless of everything else.” But while Bre has embraced Nick’s sprawling family tree, she said on Lip Service that she’s drawing the line at adding another branch. “I only have like one deal breaker. One. And if it ever happens, then I might be out,” she said. “If he has another baby.” She added that, considering that Nick has12 children across six households, he’s already stretched thin, and Bre doesn’t believe another child would make things any easier. “There’s only so much time in a day. There’s so many kids. There’s so much going on,” she explained. “You got the Brady Bunch. We’re not doing 13!” Bre Tiesi Says Filming Nick Cannon’s Netflix Series Was The ‘Worst Thing’ She’s Ever Done Bre’s candid comments come as Nick prepares to pull back the curtain on his unconventional family dynamics in an upcoming Netflix docuseries featuring several of his children’s mothers—minus Mariah Carey, as confirmed by Bre on Lip Service . Source: Earl Gibson III / Getty The project is expected to offer a closer look at how Nick navigates fatherhood across multiple households, but Bre admitted that she wasn’t exactly jumping at the opportunity to participate. When Angela questioned Bre’s decision to put her relationship with Nick on display, the Selling Sunset star clarified that participating wasn’t exactly her choice. “No, I didn’t really agree to this. I was forced,” Bre said. She explained that participating felt like a lose-lose situation, because although she wanted to protect her privacy, she also worried that declining to appear would leave room for others to shape the narrative surrounding her relationship. “Personally, I felt like it was a lose-lose,” she explained. “If I didn’t do it, I’m allowing a space for another narrative to be created that isn’t mine.” She continued, “We’re very private, so I think actually seeing the interaction is a big deal,” she said, noting that viewers will get a rare glimpse of their relationship and how they raise Legendary together. Still, Bre questioned whether inviting cameras into an already heavily scrutinized family arrangement was worth the additional attention. “It’s something that’s so scrutinized that people have so many opinions,” she explained. “I’m like, why are we giving people more? I don’t want to do this.” And while she’s accustomed to Nick having relationships with other women, actually witnessing those interactions presented an entirely different challenge. “I’ve never had to watch his interactions with anyone else,” Bre admitted. “Do you say all the same things? Is it insert bitch here? I don’t know.” Making matters even more nerve-racking, Bre revealed that she hasn’t been allowed to preview the finished series. “I’ll be watching with everybody else, and they don’t want to show me, which makes me even more nervous,” she said. As for her overall experience filming the project, Bre didn’t mince words, calling it the “worst thing” she’s ever done and joking that she’d rather go to jail or return to the grueling reality competition Special Forces than do it again.

title: The Biggest Sneakerheads Of The Black Sitcom Universe
author: Keenan Higgins
content: Ron Galella / Getty We’re currently at a point in pop culture where interest in Black sitcoms are at an all-time high. From A Different World getting a revival series on Netflix that continues the legacy of Hillman College to Martin receiving a sitcom spinoff with The Varnell Hill Show streaming on Paramount+, some of our favorite fictional stars are making comebacks like they never left. The influence has even manifested in other ways as well, like 27-year-old NBA star Ja Morant launching a “Halloween” colorway for his Nike Ja 4 signature sneaker inspired by one of the most hilarious episodes of Martin . RELATED: Gotta Be The Shoes: Coolest Celebrity Sneaker Collaborations Lifted from the Season 5 episode “Boo’s in the House” that aired on Halloween night in 1996, the shoe’s design cleverly reworks the shirt Martin wore for his Ike Turner costume. The eclectic mix of red, black and white does a great job at channeling the fit, and it even comes with a red bow accent to match the scarf around Martin’s neck in the episode. Even though the current Portland Trail Blazers point guard wasn’t even born until two years after the show’s epic five-season run came to an end, his fandom is a testament to the generational power of syndication and the fact that sitcoms like Martin have extreme replay value. It’s even arguable that many who aren’t even born yet will one day discover the show and become fans just like the rest of us. The connection between sneaker culture and sitcoms, particularly ones with a predominately Black cast and audience, is stronger than some might be aware of. Many lead stars of hit primetime shows made it a mission to throw on a fresh pair of kicks in order to relate deeper to viewers while also giving their character a piece of their own personality. In addition Marty-Mar, you also had Will Smith giving us grails on The Fresh Prince Of Bel-Air , the combined steez of Dwayne Wayne and Ron Johnson on A Different World , Eddie Winslow staying loyal to his Air Jordan 3s on Family Matters and the late Malcolm Jamal Warner making a style icon out of Theo Huxtable on The Cosby Show . They are amongst a niche group of fictional sneakerheads who inspired a generation with their flair for footwear. We’d like to believe that somewhere in the Black sitcom universe, they’re all still keeping it fresh, fly and funny. From Jordans and Reebok Pumps to Air Force 1s and classic adidas, these characters reflected the close relationship between Black youth culture, hip-hop, basketball, and fashion. In that sense, the fictional Black sitcom sneakerhead isn’t simply someone who wears cool shoes—they represent the evolving influence of sneaker culture within our culture. Keep scrolling for a look at the premiere sneakerheads in the Black sitcom universe, and let us know if we’re missing any: Dwayne Wayne and Ron Johnson, A Different World

title: Kim Fields Regine-ly Reacts To Audaciously Ashy Abyss Dwellers Calling The Living Single Cast ‘Unattractive’
author: Danielle Canada
content: Theeeeee audacity! That’s what Living Single fans (like us!) are saying after an audaciously ashy, abyss-dwelling group of mouth breathers had the nerve to dub the cast of the beloved ’90s sitcom “unattractive.” Now, the uproar has gotten so loud that one of the show’s stars has entered the chat. Source: Gilbert Flores / Getty Earlier this week, the hosts of The Views From The 7 podcast sparked backlash after a convo they had about Living Single went viral across Black social media. Source: Vinnie Zuffante / Getty “No one watched Living Single and said they are attractive,” one of the men said. “You didn’t say they was ugly, but nobody say they was attractive. “They weren’t Girlfriends,” added another. Another one on the panel also called out Maxine Shaw’s “Mystikal braids” as the group wondered how men were choosing to date the character played by Erika Alexander. As you can imagine, the group has been dragged across Al Gore’s Internet as people came to the defense of the Queen, Kim Fields , Kim Coles and Erika Alexander . HelloBeautiful reports that one Reddit commenter described the cast on the beloved sitcom as “real everyday people,” adding that their relatability was likely part of the show’s appeal. Others immediately started naming their favorites, with Maxine, Regine, and Khadijah getting love throughout the discussion. KevOnStage also joined the online conversation, and in his comments, Kim Fields, who portrayed Regine Hunter on the Fox sitcom, weighed in. “Da Fuq?!” she wrote, much to the delight of fellow commenters who wondered where the group garnered the audacity to weigh in on anyone’s looks. As you can imagine, these “podcasters” have been getting draaaaaaaagged within an inch of their musty microphones. See some reactions below.

title: What Happened To The Cast Of ‘The Parent ‘Hood’?
author: Shannon Dawson
content: Photo courtesy of IMbD. The Cast of ‘The Parent ‘Hood.’ If you grew up watching ’90s television, chances are the Peterson family felt a little like your own extended family, only with better one-liners. The Parent ‘Hood debuted on The WB in January 1995 and quickly became one of the network’s signature family sitcoms. The series followed Robert and Jerri Peterson as they tried to raise four children in their Manhattan brownstone while juggling work, school, relationships and all the chaos that comes with parenting. The show ran for five seasons and 90 episodes before saying goodbye in 1999.   So where is the cast of The Parent ‘Hood today and the memorable neighbors who kept the household interesting? As it turns out, the cast took some very different paths after leaving the Peterson brownstone. Let’s find out together. Robert Townsend — Robert Peterson Of course, there was Robert Peterson, the well-meaning but sometimes hilariously exasperated dad played by Robert Townsend. Townsend was much more than the star of the show. He was also a co-creator, filmmaker, writer and producer, and his career behind the camera has remained just as busy as his career in front of it. The man behind Hollywood Shuffle and The Five Heartbeats has continued directing and acting well into the 2020s. More recently, Townsend appeared as Emmanuel Adamu on FX’s The Bear and has directed episodes of The Chi , according to his website. He also directed multiple episodes of Poppa’s House in 2024 and 2025, as well as episodes of Power Book IV: Force .  So, while Robert Peterson may have spent his sitcom years trying to keep his kids in line, Townsend has spent the decades since helping shape stories from behind the camera. Not a bad second act.

title: Where Are They Now?: The Cast Of ‘Family Matters’
author: Shannon Dawson
content: Source: Derek White/Noam Galai/Derek Whitevia Getty Images. If you grew up watching ABC’s TGIF lineup, chances are the Winslow family felt like extended family. From Carl Winslow’s legendary patience to Laura’s teenage drama and Steve Urkel’s unforgettable “Did I do that?”, Family Matters became one of the defining sitcoms of the 1990s. The show debuted in 1989, ran for nine seasons, and eventually moved from ABC to CBS for its final season in 1998. Nearly three decades later, the cast has taken some very different paths. So, where is the cast of Family Matters today, you ask? Where is the cast of Family Matters ? Jaleel White Source: Noam Galai / Getty At the center of the Urkel phenomenon is Jaleel White, who turned what was supposed to be a one-off guest appearance into one of television’s most recognizable characters. White’s hilarious character Steve Urkel became a centerpiece of the series, as well as his smooth-talking alter ego Stefan Urquelle. With his nerdy demeanor and hilarious laugh filled with snorts, fans loved watching Urkel whip up odd science experiments and try to win over the heart of Laura Winslow despite her frequent rejections. After the show ended, White has continued working in Hollywood long after leaving the Winslow household, appearing in movies and television, competing on Dancing with the Stars , and taking on hosting duties for the game show Flip Side . He has also appeared in projects including Netflix’s Hustle and Disney+’s Star Wars: Skeleton Crew . And yes, White has even found a way to bring a little Urkel energy into the business world with his own cannabis brand, ItsPurpl.

title: 25 Black Coming-Of-Age Movies That Define the Culture
author: Global Grind Staff
content: Source: Michael Ochs Archives / Getty Black coming-of-age movies have always been about more than growing up. They are about figuring out who you are while navigating family, friendship, first love, heartbreak, identity, culture and everything happening around you. Check out these 25 Black coming-of-age movies that define the culture. For generations, these movies have given us characters who felt familiar. We saw ourselves in the kids trying to make sense of the world, the teenagers chasing their dreams, the friends trying to stay connected and the young adults realizing that growing up does not come with an instruction manual. Some made us laugh. Others broke our hearts. A few did both in the same movie.  Publications like Essence and Collider shared the films that told these stories.  From the streets of Brooklyn and Chicago to the neighborhoods of Los Angeles and Atlanta, these stories have captured Black childhood, adolescence and young adulthood in ways that Hollywood did not always make room for. They gave us iconic soundtracks, unforgettable characters, quotable moments and snapshots of Black life that became part of the culture. Whether you grew up watching these movies with your family, caught them on late-night television or discovered them years later, their impact is hard to deny. So, from HBCU campuses and summer vacations to first crushes, family drama, and figuring out your purpose, scroll below for 25 Black coming-of-age movies that define the culture.

title: The Cast Of ‘Rosewood:’ Where Are They Now?
author: Shannon Dawson
content: Source: Photos by Robin L Marshall/Paras Griffin/JC Olivera/Getty Images. Remember the star-studded cast of Rosewood , the stylish Fox crime drama that mixed murder mysteries, Miami sunshine and plenty of chemistry between its two leading detectives? If you need a refresher, the series followed Dr. Beaumont Rosewood Jr ., a brilliant private pathologist who could uncover clues from a body that everyone else had missed. With his high-tech lab, larger-than-life personality and relentless optimism, Rosewood became an unlikely crime-solving partner to tough Miami detective Annalise Villa. The show ran for two seasons from 2015 to 2017, but its cast certainly didn’t disappear when the cameras stopped rolling. In fact, many of the stars went on to some pretty big projects. So, what are the familiar faces of Rosewood doing now? Here’s what we know. Morris Chestnut — Dr. Beaumont Rosewood Jr. Source: Jon Kopaloff / Getty Morris Chestnut was the heart of the series, playing the charismatic pathologist who could crack a case while keeping everyone entertained. Rosewood was confident, charming and determined to enjoy life to the fullest, even while dealing with a serious heart condition. Since leaving the show, Chestnut has continued to build an impressive television résumé. He has taken on major dramatic roles, including appearances in Reasonable Doubt , while also stepping into the lead role of Dr. John Watson in the CBS series Watson , a modern take on the famous Sherlock Holmes universe. And acting isn’t his only venture. Chestnut has also branched out into business, including co-founding the spirits company Sable Bourbon alongside fellow Hollywood star Taye Diggs. Not bad for the guy who spent Rosewood solving murders between trips to the lab and flirting with his detective partner!

title: 12 Best Characters From Chappelle’s Show
author: Davonta Herring
content: Source: Jeff Kravitz / Getty There are comedy shows that are funny in their moment, and then there are shows that permanently change the language of pop culture. Chappelle’s Show firmly belongs in the second category. When Dave Chappelle and Neal Brennan’s sketch series premiered on Comedy Central on January 22, 2003, it mixed celebrity parody, racial satire, Hip-Hop culture and completely ridiculous premises in a way television had rarely seen before. The series also helped transform Chappelle from a respected stand-up comic and familiar movie face into one of comedy’s biggest names. More importantly, its best sketches refused to choose between being smart and being absurd. Chappelle could use one character to dissect racism and another to spend five minutes screaming three words at strangers, and somehow both could become classics. That versatility gave Chappelle’s Show a ridiculous bench of memorable characters. Some appeared repeatedly, others only needed one legendary sketch, and a few were Chappelle’s exaggerated versions of real celebrities. More than two decades later, people are still quoting them. Here are 10 of the best. Clayton Bigsby Introducing Clayton Bigsby in the very first episode told viewers immediately that Chappelle’s Show was willing to go places most television comedies would not. Chappelle played a blind Black man raised to believe he was white who becomes a committed white supremacist, turning an outrageous premise into a sharp satire about how racism is learned.

title: 15 ‘Love Jones’ Movie Quotes That Still Say So Much About Black Love
author: Global Grind Staff
content: Source: Archive Photos / Getty Some movies give us romance. Love Jones gave Black love a language. Check out 15 Love Jones movie quotes that still say so much about Black love inside.  Released in 1997, the Larenz Tate and Nia Long classic captured the complicated space between attraction, friendship, vulnerability, timing, and the terrifying possibility of actually falling for somebody. Set against Chicago’s poetry and jazz scene, Love Jones let its characters talk about love with humor, honesty, sensuality, and plenty of Black cultural flavor. Nearly three decades later, the movie’s words still hit. From Darius Lovehall trying to explain why love can feel urgent to Nina Mosley questioning whether years together are enough, these moments remind us that Black love has always been about more than getting together. Sometimes it is about figuring out whether two people can grow together, whether timing really matters, and whether the possibility of love is worth taking the risk. As documented by IMDB’s collection of Love Jones quotes and Poem of Quotes’ film archive, scroll down for 15 lines that still say plenty about Black love. 15 Love Jones Movie Quotes  1. “Romance is about the possibility of the thing.” Darius understood that romance is not just about having someone. It is about remaining curious about what could happen next. 2. “This here, right now, at this very moment, is all that matters to me. I love you.” Sometimes love makes everything feel urgent. 3. “Why is everything so urgent with you?” Nina reminds us that not everybody moves through love at the same speed. 4. “Until the next time became the right time.” Timing can change everything when two people genuinely want each other. 5. “You’d be surprised how far it can get ya.” Darius had faith in persistence, even when romance got complicated. 6. “I gather up each sound you left behind and stretch them on our bed.” Nina’s poetry turns longing into something tangible and intimate. 7. “All we have, Marvin, is all these years. And it’s just not enough anymore.” Love and history do not automatically guarantee that a relationship still works. 8. “Poetry is the possibility of language.” Sometimes feelings become clearer when ordinary conversation is not enough. 9. “The point is… I don’t know the point, alright?” Even poets can be completely confused about love. 10. “Masterpiece of MINIMALISM.” Because sometimes the best description of your life is simply that you are figuring it out. 11. “I need some food that had parents, man.” Darius also understood that compatibility includes the little things, including what is actually on the dinner table. 12. “No, you need a personality to get women.” Sheila was not letting Hollywood get away with thinking confidence was enough. 13. “Try a breath mint and a visa.” Savon’s response remains one of the movie’s funniest reminders that dating requires more than talking. 14. “Who am I? I’ll be whoever you say.” Darius’s flirtation showed the theatrical, poetic side of Black desire. 15. “Is that all right?” After all the poetry, confidence, and desire, Darius still asks for permission. That question captures something essential about intimacy: attraction can be loud, but connection still requires an answer. RELATED: Where Are They Now? The Cast Of ‘You Got Served’

title: Where Are They Now? The Cast Of ‘You Got Served’
author: Shannon Dawson
content: Source: Vivien Killilea/Rodin Eckenroth/Gregg DeGuire/Getty. It has been 22 years since You Got Served hit U.S. theaters on January 30, 2004, and somehow, the movie’s dance battles still live rent-free in the memories of an entire generation. Long before viral dance challenges and TikTok choreography, You Got Served turned the underground dance scene into a full-blown cinematic event. With a young, star-studded cast, jaw-dropping choreography and enough dramatic dance battles to keep viewers on the edge of their seats, the film became much more than just another early-2000s dance movie. So, where is the cast of You Got Served now, you ask? Before we jump into it. Let’s unpack this incredible film.  What was You Got Served about? Directed by Chris Stokes, the 2004 drama follows best friends David and Elgin, played by Omarion and Marques Houston, who lead a talented street dance crew in Los Angeles. Their big dream? To open their own dance and recording studio. Of course, things don’t exactly go according to plan. In true movie fashion, the pair need money to make their dream a reality, so they enter an underground dance competition where serious cash — and serious bragging rights — are on the line. But when betrayal, rivalry and a devastating loss threaten to tear the crew apart, David and Elgin find themselves on opposite sides of a friendship that once seemed unbreakable. Eventually, the dancers put their differences aside, create a new style and reunite for one last shot at proving they are the best on the streets. And audiences absolutely ate it up. The movie became a cultural phenomenon, particularly among young fans who didn’t just watch the dance battles — they wanted to recreate them. Omarion reflected on the movie’s impact in a 2014 interview with Billboard , recalling just how far the phenomenon had spread: “I remember, in the first week that it came out, we got reports that people were actually battling in the theaters,” he recalled. “It became more than just a movie — it became a part of culture. And that’s like… you can’t ask for anything more. People always ask me if I’m going to do another dance movie, and it’s hard to say if I would ever do another dance movie, because, really, that was like the top of the top for me.” It was an award-winning movie, too! At the 2004 American Choreography Awards, You Got Served won for Outstanding Achievement in Choreography – Feature Film. The award was shared by choreographers Dave Scott, Shane Sparks and Robert Hoffman, who also played rival dancer Max. The film also picked up notable nominations at the 2004 MTV Movie Awards, including Best Dance Sequence for Omarion and Marques Houston and Breakout Male Performance for Omarion. Twenty-two years later, the cast has taken some very different paths. So where are they now, you ask? Let’s take a look. Where is the cast of You Got Served now? Omarion Omarion, who played David, continued building a successful career as a solo R&B singer and touring artist, releasing albums including O and 21 . He also continued acting, appearing in projects including Somebody Help Me and The Proud Family Movie , while later returning to the spotlight through reality television and touring. His career has remained closely tied to R&B and the legacy of B2K.

title: Alicia Keys’ Top Songs: 25 Hits That Made Her A Music Icon
author: Shannon Dawson
content: Source: getty / Getty Alicia Keys didn’t just arrive on the R&B scene in 2001; she practically kicked the door down, sat at a piano, and started singing like she’d been doing it for 40 years. From breathtaking piano ballads to hip-hop collaborations and giant New York anthems, these songs are not only beloved fan favorites, but they also helped Alicia Keys blossom from a promising young pianist into a global superstar. Here are 25 of Alicia Keys’ top songs that you need to bump right now. 25. “Girlfriend” — Songs in A Minor (2001) Before the inspirational anthems and giant ballads, Alicia could bring the attitude. “Girlfriend” showed off the sassier side of her debut and proved she wasn’t simply a piano-playing balladeer. 24. “Unbreakable” — Unplugged (2005) Warm, optimistic and wonderfully understated, “Unbreakable” off of the singer’s 2005 live album Unplugged , showed Alicia’s ability to make a positive message feel personal rather than preachy. 23. “Superwoman” — As I Am (2007) The cape was optional; the vocals were not. “Superwoman” became one of Alicia’s signature empowerment songs and perfectly captured her inspirational side. Alicia’s ability to turn vulnerability into strength is one of her greatest trademarks, and “Superwoman” might be the clearest example. Empowering and downright infectious, it’s the musical equivalent of putting your hands on your hips and saying, “I’ve got this.” “Superwoman” won Best Female R&B Vocal Performance in 2009. 22. “Teenage Love Affair” — As I Am (2007) Sweet, flirtatious and packed with retro soul vibes, this was Alicia having some fun. The throwback sound made it one of the lighter—and catchier—moments of the As I Am era. 21. “Karma” — The Diary of Alicia Keys (2003) Alicia gets her revenge—and makes it funky. “Karma” showed that the woman behind “Fallin’” could turn up the attitude and bring some serious rhythmic energy. 20. “Try Sleeping with a Broken Heart” — The Element of Freedom (2009) This is for the Alicia Keys super fans. Dark, atmospheric and emotionally wrecked in the best possible way. “Try Sleeping with a Broken Heart” showed Alicia continuing to evolve beyond the traditional piano-ballad formula.

title: Where Are They Now?: What Happened To Kyle Barker From ‘Living Single’ ?
author: Shannon Dawson
content: Source: Nykieria Chaney / Getty If you watched Living Single back in the ’90s, chances are T.C. Carson’s Kyle Barker had a special place in your TV-loving heart. The hit sitcom premiered in 1993 and went on to deliver five seasons of laughs, friendship, romance and plenty of unforgettable moments before wrapping up in 1998. Carson, an actor and accomplished voice-over artist, joined the beloved ensemble as Kyle Barker — a polished, successful Wall Street accountant and executive whose intelligence, confidence and undeniable charm made him one of the show’s standout characters. But fans were shocked to see the beloved character leave after the Season 5 premiere, leaving many to wonder what happened to Kyle Barker? Creating the Man Behind Kyle Barker. Kyle wasn’t just another slick sitcom bachelor. He represented a successful Black professional who was deeply connected to his culture, valued his relationships and could hold his own in both the boardroom and the living room. And Carson was intentional about creating that image. During a 2020 interview with Hype+ , Carson opened up about the inspiration behind Kyle Barker and explained that the character was actually a combination of people he knew in real life. “Kyle is a combination of a few friends of mine, my dad, [a] doctor friend of mine, a lawyer friend of mine, a social worker friend of mine,” he explained. “I pulled from all those people to create who he was. I thought it was very important for us to see a young Black man that was successful in his business that was very connected to his heritage and his culture that [he] treated women a certain way and that [he] treated his friends and his family a certain way. I hope that came off through that character.” Clearly, Carson wanted Kyle to be more than a handsome guy in a nice suit. He wanted viewers to see a multidimensional Black man who could be successful professionally while remaining grounded in his family, friendships, culture and relationships. Mission accomplished. But just as fans were getting comfortable with Kyle, something happened that left many viewers wondering: Where did Kyle Barker go? Read more after the flip to find out.

title: Black 90s Cartoon Characters Who Helped Shape Our Vision Of The World
author: Davonta Herring
content: Source: Pressmaster / Getty Long before social media became part of everyday life, television was one of the biggest windows children had into the world. The cartoons we rushed home to watch, woke up early on Saturday mornings for or caught before school weren’t just entertainment. Whether we realized it at the time or not, they introduced us to different people, places, problems and possibilities. That representation could carry even more weight for Black children . There was something different about turning on the television and seeing a kid with brown skin, braids, a high-top fade or a family that reminded you of your own. Those characters didn’t have to announce that they were Black every episode. Sometimes simply getting to be the smart kid, the cool kid, the superhero or the voice of reason was powerful enough. And the best characters went even further. They taught us to protect the environment, believe in ourselves, ask questions, navigate predominantly white spaces, stand up to bullies, and be comfortable with what made us different. Decades later, many of the lessons have stuck with the same generation that first learned them sitting in front of the TV. Here are some of the Black cartoon characters from the 1990s who helped shape the way we see ourselves — and the world around us. Kwame — Captain Planet and the Planeteers Kwame wasn’t simply another member of the Planeteers; he was frequently the group’s calm, grounded voice and unofficial leader. Hailing from Africa and wielding the power of Earth, he was introduced as someone deeply connected to conservation and protecting living things, while LeVar Burton’s unmistakable voice gave him even more presence. The series itself was built around teaching kids about pollution, deforestation and other environmental issues, meaning a Black character was helping lead a generation through some of its earliest lessons about taking care of the planet.

title: The Best HBCU Movies & TV Shows To Watch
author: Global Grind Staff
content: Source: Netflix / Netflix Hillman College is calling, and class is officially back in session. The release of the sequel series of A Different World debuts this month, and it inspired our list of the best HBCU movies and TV shows to watch. Check it out inside.  Just in time for homecoming season, A Different World is getting a whole new generation of students. The highly anticipated sequel series premieres on Netflix Sep. 24. The series brings viewers back to the fictional HBCU Hillman College through the eyes of Deborah Wayne — the daughter of beloved alumni Dwayne Wayne and Whitley Gilbert. Several original cast members are returning, with Debbie Allen back behind the scenes as executive producer and director. Before you head back to the yard, it is time to brush up on your HBCU screen education. Essence shared a roundup of HBCU movie and TV show favorites ahead of Beyoncé’s iconic Homecoming drop on Netflix. From legendary marching bands and Greek life to Black love, campus politics, friendship, activism and finding yourself, these movies and television shows capture different pieces of the HBCU experience. As Essence points out in its homecoming watch list, titles like Drumline , Stomp the Yard , School Daze and A Different World have helped bring the energy of Black college culture to audiences everywhere. And as Bustle previously highlighted, the HBCU stories on screen offer more than entertainment. They give viewers a window into traditions like stepping, marching band culture, Greek life and the everyday experiences of Black college students. So grab your snacks, call your homecoming crew and press play.

title: The Black Comedians Who Made History On ‘SNL’
author: Shannon Dawson
content: Source: Dimitrios Kambouris / Getty For more than five decades, Saturday Night Live has been one of television’s biggest comedy launching pads, and some of its funniest, most memorable performers have been Black comedians. From Garrett Morris breaking barriers in the very first season of the hit comedy-sketch series to Kenan Thompson becoming the longest-serving cast member in the show’s history, Black comedians have brought unforgettable characters, spot-on impressions and plenty of chaos to Studio 8H, where SNL has been filmed for decades. As we gear up for the beloved show to head into its 52nd season on Sept. 26, let’s take a trip through SNL history and revisit the Black comedians who helped make the iconic sketch show what it is today. Garrett Morris Broke the Ice. Source: John Nacion / Getty When Saturday Night Live premiered in 1975, Garrett Morris made history as the show’s first Black cast member. Morris spent five seasons on the series and became known for characters and sketches that showcased his versatility as a singer, actor and comedian. His casting opened the door for generations of Black performers who would follow. Yvonne Hudson and Danitra Vance Changed the Game. In 1980, Yvonne Hudson became the first Black female performer on SNL . Initially appearing as an uncredited extra, Hudson’s presence marked an important moment for the show’s representation. A few years later, Danitra Vance took another historic step. During the 1985–86 season, Vance became the first Black woman to serve as a repertory, or main, cast member. Her run was brief, but her place in SNL history was significant. Hit the flip to see a few more Black people who have left a mark on Saturday Night Live.

title: Why Your Laptop Fan Is So Loud and How to Fix It
author: GBM Staff
content: Your laptop used to be relatively quiet. Now, every time you open a few browser tabs or start working, it sounds like a tiny airplane preparing for takeoff. A loud laptop fan isn’t always a sign that something is broken. Fans help prevent overheating, and they naturally spin faster when your computer is working harder. But if your laptop fan is constantly running, suddenly much louder than usual or making strange noises, there may be something worth fixing. Here are 10 things to check before assuming you need a new laptop. 1. Check What’s Running in the Background One of the most common reasons a laptop fan gets loud is that something is using too much processing power. You might have dozens of browser tabs open, an application updating in the background or a program that isn’t responding properly. Even if you’re not actively doing much, your laptop might be. On Windows Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager. Click Processes. Select the CPU column to sort applications by processor usage. Look for programs using unusually high amounts of CPU. If you recognize an application you don’t need, close it normally. Avoid ending unfamiliar system processes just because they’re using resources. On a Mac Open Activity Monitor. Click the CPU tab. Sort by % CPU. Look for applications using unusually high processing power. Quit unnecessary applications and see whether the fan quiets down. If the fan gets quieter after closing a particular program, you’ve found a likely cause. 2. Stop Using Your Laptop on Soft Surfaces Your bed, couch and favorite blanket might be comfortable for you, but they aren’t necessarily comfortable for your laptop. Many laptops use vents along the bottom, sides or back to move air through the computer. Placing your laptop on a pillow, blanket or other soft surface can block airflow. That forces the cooling system to work harder. Try moving your laptop onto a hard, flat surface like a desk or table. If you frequently use your laptop on the couch or in bed, consider a lap desk that provides a stable surface without blocking ventilation. 3. Clean Dust From the Vents Over time, dust and lint can accumulate around your laptop’s cooling vents. When airflow becomes restricted, internal temperatures can rise and the fan may need to work harder. Turn off your laptop, unplug it and inspect the vents. If you see visible dust, gently remove it using a soft brush or follow your manufacturer’s cleaning instructions. Avoid inserting objects into the vents or forcing compressed air into the computer without checking the manufacturer’s guidance. Some laptops have delicate internal fans that can be damaged by improper cleaning. If your laptop is several years old and has never been cleaned internally, accumulated dust could be contributing to the problem. 4. Restart Your Laptop Yes, the classic restart. It’s recommended so often because temporary software problems really can cause excessive processor usage. A background task might be stuck, an application might have developed a memory leak or your operating system may simply need a fresh start. Save your work, restart the laptop and give it a few minutes to settle. If the fan immediately becomes loud again, move on to the other troubleshooting steps. 5. Close Unnecessary Browser Tabs Web browsers can consume a surprising amount of system resources. Streaming video, animated advertisements, web applications and poorly optimized websites can all increase processor usage. Having 30 tabs open doesn’t automatically mean your laptop will overheat, but certain websites can place a substantial load on your computer. Close tabs you’re no longer using. If you use Chrome or Edge, check whether the browser’s memory-saving or energy-saving features are enabled. You can also test whether one particular website causes the fan to speed up. If the laptop becomes noticeably quieter after closing your browser, it’s worth investigating extensions and active tabs. 6. Check for Software Updates An outdated operating system, driver or application can sometimes cause performance problems that increase fan activity. Check for available updates. Windows Open Settings > Windows Update. Install relevant updates and restart when prompted. Mac Open System Settings > General > Software Update. Install available updates. Keep in mind that fans may temporarily run faster while updates are installing, files are being indexed or other maintenance tasks are taking place. If the fan is loud immediately after a major update, give the computer some time to finish its background work. 7. Change Your Power Settings Many laptops offer different performance modes. Higher-performance settings may allow the processor to use more power, generate more heat and trigger faster fan speeds. If you don’t need maximum performance, switching to a more balanced mode may help. Windows Open Settings > System > Power & battery. Look for Power mode and select Balanced or another lower-power option available on your device. Mac On supported Mac laptops, Low Power Mode can reduce energy usage and may help reduce heat generation. Open System Settings > Battery and review the available energy settings. Not every laptop offers the same controls, and some manufacturers include their own thermal or fan-management utilities. 8. Check the Room Temperature Your laptop’s cooling system has to work with the air around it. If you’re using your computer outside on a hot day, near a sunny window or in a room without adequate ventilation, the fan may need to work harder. Move the laptop into a cooler environment and keep it out of direct sunlight. Make sure there’s enough open space around its vents. Avoid putting the laptop in a refrigerator or freezer to cool it down. Rapid temperature changes and condensation can damage electronics. 9. Disconnect Unnecessary Accessories External monitors, USB devices and other accessories can increase a laptop’s workload or power consumption. For example, driving multiple high-resolution displays may require additional graphics processing. If your laptop fan becomes noticeably louder when connected to a docking station or external monitor, try disconnecting those accessories temporarily. Then reconnect them one at a time. This can help determine whether the additional workload is contributing to the noise. 10. Consider a Hardware Problem If you’ve tried the simpler fixes and your laptop fan is still unusually loud, the problem may be physical. Possible causes include accumulated internal dust, a failing fan, worn bearings or a cooling system that isn’t working properly. A fan that makes grinding, rattling or clicking noises is especially concerning. Those sounds are different from the normal rushing-air noise of a fan spinning quickly. If you suspect a hardware problem, stop using the laptop for demanding tasks and contact the manufacturer or a qualified repair technician. Opening the laptop yourself may not be advisable, especially if it’s under warranty. Why Is My Laptop Fan Loud When I’m Not Doing Anything? This is one of the most confusing situations. Your laptop is sitting on the desk with no obvious applications running, yet the fan is working overtime. The explanation is often background activity. Your computer might be downloading updates, syncing cloud files, scanning for malware, indexing documents or performing other maintenance tasks. Open Task Manager on Windows or Activity Monitor on macOS to check CPU usage. If the fan settles down after a few minutes, the behavior may be normal. If it continues for hours, investigate which process is responsible. Why Is My Laptop Fan So Loud While Charging? Some laptops allow higher performance when connected to external power. Charging can also generate additional heat. Depending on your laptop’s design and settings, this may cause the fan to run faster. If the fan becomes loud only when charging, check your power mode and make sure the laptop has adequate ventilation. However, if the charger, battery area or laptop becomes unusually hot, disconnect it and have the equipment inspected. Is a Loud Laptop Fan Bad? Not necessarily. A fan that gets louder during gaming, video editing, large downloads or other demanding activities is often doing exactly what it’s supposed to do. The more important questions are whether the behavior is new, whether the laptop is overheating and whether the fan sounds mechanically damaged. Normal fan noise usually sounds like rushing air. Grinding, clicking, scraping or rattling can indicate a problem that deserves attention. How to Tell If Your Laptop Is Overheating A loud fan alone doesn’t prove that your laptop is overheating. But watch for other warning signs: The laptop becomes unusually hot to the touch. Applications slow down dramatically. The computer unexpectedly shuts down or restarts. You receive temperature warnings. The fan runs at maximum speed even during light use. If your laptop is shutting down unexpectedly or displaying overheating warnings, stop demanding tasks and address the cooling issue before continuing. Should You Buy a Laptop Cooling Pad? A cooling pad may help some laptops, particularly models with air intakes on the bottom. However, results vary depending on the laptop’s design and how its cooling system works. A simple laptop stand can also improve airflow by lifting the computer off the desk. Before buying anything, try using the laptop on a hard, flat surface and checking for software or dust-related problems. A cooling pad won’t fix a failing internal fan or a serious hardware issue. When Is It Time for a New Laptop? A loud fan doesn’t automatically mean your laptop is finished. If the problem is caused by software, blocked vents or a relatively inexpensive fan replacement, fixing it may be worthwhile. But if your computer is older, frequently overheats, struggles with everyday tasks and needs multiple repairs, replacement might make more sense. The key is figuring out whether you’re dealing with a cooling problem or a laptop that’s simply struggling to handle your workload. FAQ Why Is My Laptop Fan Suddenly So Loud? A sudden increase in fan noise may be caused by high CPU usage, background updates, blocked airflow, dust buildup or changes in performance settings. Is It Normal for a Laptop Fan to Run Constantly? Some laptops run their fans frequently, especially under heavier workloads. However, a fan running at maximum speed continuously during light use may indicate a software or cooling problem. How Do I Make My Laptop Fan Quieter? Close unnecessary applications, check CPU usage, improve ventilation, clean accessible vents safely and review your power settings. Can Dust Make a Laptop Fan Loud? Yes. Dust can restrict airflow and cause the cooling system to work harder. Heavy buildup can also contribute to overheating. Should I Worry If My Laptop Fan Is Making a Grinding Noise? Yes. Grinding, scraping or rattling can indicate a mechanical problem with the fan. Have the laptop inspected before the cooling system fails. The Bottom Line If your laptop fan is loud, start by checking what’s running in the background and making sure the computer has enough airflow. Many fan problems can be improved without replacing hardware. But if the noise is accompanied by overheating, unexpected shutdowns or grinding sounds, it’s worth having the laptop professionally inspected. A little fan noise is normal. A laptop that sounds like it’s trying to leave the runway every time you open your email deserves some attention. This article may contain affiliate links.
