title: 15 Best Restaurants In Provincetown Massachusetts
author: Nicole Schneeberger
content: Provincetown, or “P-Town,” is rightfully known as the welcoming, warm, and vibrant Northern tip of the Cape. With a beautiful downtown centered around the famous Commercial Street, endless water views, shops, and a gorgeous boardwalk. Provincetown has proven to be one of the most idyllic and charming spots for people that live here and tourists alike to explore and enjoy everything there is to do . It also happens to be a culinary hotspot filled with restaurants serving a diverse range of cuisine, most of which feature picturesque bay views! Check out this list below to find your next Provincetown dining experience!  1. Victor’s Address : 175 Bradford Street Ext, Provincetown, MA 02657 Victor’s restaurant is an amazing spot serving “New American” cuisine and specialty cocktails in an elegant, cottage-style environment. Victor’s is open seven days a week for happy hour from 3 to 5 p.m., dinner, and Sunday brunch. The place itself is incredibly airy and light, with white tablecloths inside and tons of outdoor tables. There is also comfy outdoor furniture surrounding a beautiful fire pit. I’ve also noticed how attentive the staff is–they always seem to remember the faces of returning customers and are very welcoming and friendly!  The restaurant offers shareable plates that are all extremely thoughtful in their construction and flavor. If you decide to attend happy hour, you’ll be offered refreshing drinks like the white cosmo or spicy cucumber margarita, and an assortment of raw bar items like oysters and shrimp. Additionally, the raw bar menu has tasty choices like chicken wings, fries, and burger sliders. The restaurant also provides specials and sometimes even has something called “Sushi Tuesday.” You can check out their Facebook to see if it’s something they are currently offering!  Looking at the shareable plates, there are so many good choices for every craving! For those wanting veggies, the stuffed mushrooms are amazing, and the vegetable spring rolls are bright and enticing. For seafood, the tuna tartare and grilled halibut tacos are absolutely delicious. I also suggest trying the house-made empanadas which can be made with either chicken or mushrooms.  For dessert, the homemade beignets with fresh seasonal fruit are a must-try!  Definitely make a reservation if you plan to eat at Victor’s for dinner. It truly is a wonderful all-around experience for anyone lucky enough to dine there!  2. Fanizzi’s Restaurant Address : 539 Commercial St, Provincetown, MA 02657 Fannizi’s Restaurant serves up Italian and American seafood cuisine right along the water. They serve lunch, dinner, and a Sunday brunch all-you-can-eat buffet from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. This restaurant is a personal favorite of many of my family members, and it’s not difficult to tell why. The beautiful bay views and window-lined dining room contribute to the sophisticated yet relaxing atmosphere perfect for a sunset meal. The alluring cozy bar has continuing sea views and is a great place to enjoy a cocktail or appetizer.  If you do decide to try an appetizer, there are a great deal of options! If you want seafood, the crab cakes are flavorful and the chowder is creamy and rich. If you want something vegetable-based, the stuffed artichokes and buffalo cauliflower are both quite yummy. I also loved the curried chicken salad and the burnt ends are crispy and moist. What’s more, there are classic appetizers like loaded nachos and homemade onion strings!  The entree portion of the menu offers a diverse selection of dishes. For seafood, I recommend the cucumber dill salmon or the salmon burger, both of which are super fresh and zesty with flavor. The cajun seafood alfredo is also tasty and perfect for anyone wanting a little pasta with their seafood! Moreover, the restaurant has lots of hearty classics, like “Mom’s Best Meatloaf,” chicken or eggplant parmesan, or boneless Southern-fried chicken.  The burger menu at Fanizzi’s is also quite impressive. The “Fanizzi’s Favorite,” in particular is very popular and comes with cheddar, bacon, and veggies–and is served on an English muffin. You can also enjoy a turkey or veggie burger as an alternative! There is also a great kid’s menu available to those 12 and under.  Call Fanizzi’s to make a reservation and don’t miss their early-bird special from 4:30 to 5:30 p.m. daily! 3. The Lobster Pot Address : 321 Commercial St, Provincetown, MA 02657 The Lobster Pot is an iconic Provincetown establishment that is well-known and very loved by its patrons. Easily spotted by its distinctive neon sign, the Lobster Pot offers seafood classics with beautiful bay views and plenty of refreshing drinks. The inside of the place is filled with beachy decor, tons of tables, and a huge lobster tank. In addition to the waterfront dining rooms, there is an outdoor deck and the restaurant’s “Top of the Pot” is a gorgeous spot to grab a mocktail or signature cocktail while overlooking the harbor. In my opinion, you can’t go wrong with their bloody mary (they make the mix!) or one of the non-alcoholic chilled lemonade coolers!  The menu at The Lobster Pot is quite extensive, featuring seafood, many Portuguese specialties, salads, and raw bar items. In addition to the classic raw bar items, for appetizers, the clam chowder is delicious and can even be served in a bread bowl. The menu also has a wide selection of bouillabaisses or traditional seafood stews. You can also order a variety of fishes, whether you want tuna, salmon, halibut, or swordfish–all of which can be prepared either blackened or grilled and come with your choice of sauce. I always recommend going with blackened fish, and the Lobster Pot does not disappoint; the fish is filled with flavor and cooked to perfection.  As expected due to the name, The Lobster Pot has a huge lobster menu, featuring various forms of preparations. Your lobster can be pan-roasted, stuffed, or boiled. You can also order the “clam bake” which comes with your choice of soup, corn on the cob, red potatoes, and a whole lobster cooked to your liking. Moreover, you can try their unique lobster Reuben or lobster mac and cheese.  If you aren’t in the mood for seafood, the menu offers steaks, baked chicken, and vegetarian choices, like the pasta primavera and fresh veggie sandwich. There is also a plethora of gluten-free options, which are highlighted on the menu. Lastly, there is a great kid’s menu, so if you’re looking for a family-friendly spot, this restaurant is an awesome choice!  The Lobster Pot does not take reservations and is open for lunch and dinner starting at 11:30 am!  4. Ciro and Sal’s   Address : 4 Kiley Ct, Provincetown, MA 02657 Ciro and Sal’s is another Provincetown institution that has been serving Italian cuisine since 1954. The restaurant has been owned by the same family for generations and is known for its authentic and cozy ambiance. The place serves dinner nightly and offers seating in its intimate brick wine cellar area filled with candlelit tables, as well as in its hidden gem of a bar that is extremely romantic with strong Italian vibes. Additionally, Ciro and Sal’s has a beautiful garden gazebo twirled with vines and giving off amazing views.  Ciro and Sal’s offers nightly and weekly specials and the menu promotes the use of local ingredients: seafood, pasta, chicken, veal, and tons of house-crafted sauces. For appetizers, the bruschetta with homemade pesto bread and the gnocchi caprese are both fresh and packed with flavor. If you decide to order pasta for an entree, the lasagna is rich and amazing, as is the carbonara. Pasta dishes can also be substituted with gluten-free pasta. For veggies, I urge you to go with the sauteed spinach and roasted walnuts, or the chef’s nightly choice of sauteed seasonal vegetables.  If you plan to try a seafood item, the Pesce al limone, Native Fish with lemon caper white wine sauce is absolutely mouthwatering. Chicken or veal can be prepared in a variety of ways, including marsala, Milanese, and parmesan. And, if you still have room for dessert, the menu has a huge specialty coffee list and yummy choices like tiramisu and a beautiful, light lemon cake with powdered sugar and lemon cream.  Reservations at Ciro and Sal’s are required for dining, so book ahead of time! Lastly, while kids are certainly welcome, I find the vibe of the restaurant to be much more attuned to groups of adults or those out for a romantic date night!  5. The Canteen Address : 225 Commercial St, Provincetown, MA 02657 The Canteen is a classic seafood shack with a modern, elevated vibe that is casual and welcoming. The restaurant is open for lunch and dinner as well as brunch on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. The style of the spot is quirky and eclectic and sits inside a 200-year-old building. The dining style is described as “communal” and features indoor seating, tent seating, and beach seating–all with gorgeous views. If you’re like me and love the feel of warm sand between your toes, try to get a spot on the beach! There is even a full beach bar and dogs are encouraged to join their family for outside dining.  The Canteen is counter-serve and seat-yourself, making it a fun spot for shoppers or beachgoers to stop for a meal. The menu has unconventional yet delicious choices, like the Bahn min Dog or Taco dog–taking the regular hot dog to a very elevated level. Personally, I recommend trying the crab rangoon grilled cheese sandwich, the idea is so creative and the taste is perfect. The French fries are another hit and are made from scratch right on-site!  However, there are also traditional choices like hot and cold lobster rolls, fried lobster tail, and a beautiful summer wedge salad. If you’re looking for vegan alternatives, there is a cauliflower sandwich and vegan grilled cheese. There are also plenty of gluten-free choices throughout the menu and options for kids!  Moreover, if you try the Canteen for brunch, make sure to indulge in the croissant lobster roll or vegan egg panini. You can also put an egg atop any regular menu item! Brunch is even accompanied by a free coffee with sandwich orders between 10 a.m. and 12 p.m. If you want a more refreshing morning beverage, try the homemade lemonade or iced tea–or make it an Arnold Palmer!  The Canteen does not take reservations but be sure to stop by for an incredibly enjoyable and memorable meal!  6. The Red Inn Address : 15 Commercial St, Provincetown, MA 02657 The Red Inn is a beautiful harbor-adjacent spot offering a fine-dining, romantic experience. The restaurant has a gorgeous and elegant dining room inside, as well as a beautiful bar and fireplace. There is also an oceanfront deck that opens at 2 p.m. daily. The deck serves cocktails and is lined with Adirondack chairs, making it a great place to relax and enjoy the view.  The Red Inn is open daily for happy hour, and dinner, and also serves brunch every Sunday from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. If you go to the restaurant for brunch, raw bar items and appetizers are available. They also have classics like steak and eggs, chicken N biscuits, and cinnamon French toast.  Happy Hour begins at 2 p.m. and goes until 4:30, serving an abundance of raw bar items, specialty cocktails, and other upscale “bar snacks,” like lobster or Kobe beef sliders, creole pate, and spicy corn chowder. For specialty cocktails, I suggest the spicy margarita!  If you go to the Red Inn for a full dinner, I urge you to start your meal with lobster and artichoke fondue or bacon-wrapped oysters accompanied with a zesty remoulade sauce. For entrees, the pepper-crusted filet mignon with truffle mashed potatoes is absolutely luxurious. They also do a delightful smoked long island duck and a local scallop dish. If you want a vegetarian alternative, the savory vegetable bread pudding is enticing and creative. For dessert, I personally suggest the classic pecan pie–it speaks for itself!   The Red Inn Restaurant definitely boasts more of a sophisticated, adult vibe ideal for a date night. Sometimes there are even local musicians performing, adding to the romantic feel. The restaurant does accept reservations, which are recommended.  7. Mistralino Ristorante Address : 133 Bradford St, Provincetown, MA 02657 Mistralino Ristorante is an authentic Italian spot located right near Town Hall inside of a historic Provincetown home. The quaint and cozy restaurant features beautiful brick fireplaces, wooden beams, and very unique decor, as the walls are lined with different plates, which may sound odd but is actually quite beautiful. The outdoor seating along the garden terrace with string lights and a gorgeous fountain also adds to the romantic and intimate environment–as does the level of sophistication and attentiveness of the service.  Open for dinner, Mistralino’s offers new specials nightly along with early bird specials. However, the regular menu also has tons of delicious choices, all of which come with generous portion sizes. For appetizers, I encourage you to try the truffle arancini or escargot. The antipasto salad is also amazing. For entrees, the linguine and clams with your choice of red or white sauce are super tasty. The parmigiana can be served with eggplant, veal, or chicken. Additionally, if you crave meat, the filet mignon and pork osso buco are both rich in flavor. For dessert, try the homemade cannoli or bread pudding!  Definitely make a reservation if you plan to enjoy a meal at Mistralino Ristorante. Also, don’t forget to check out the “M” bar on the upper level of the restaurant, which is a great place to stop for a pre or post-dinner cocktail!  8. The Pointe Restaurant Addresss : 82 Bradford St, Provincetown, MA 02657 The Pointe Restaurant is an upscale, farm-to-table spot featuring coastal cuisine in a modern, beautiful dining room within the Crowne Pointe Historic Inn & Spa. Serving dinner Thursday through Sunday from 5:30 to 9 p.m., The Pointe promotes a romantic and intimate atmosphere for anyone looking to enjoy a quiet and elegant meal. Whether you decide to eat in the dining room or the gorgeous lounge area and wine bar, you are sure to have an amazing experience. However, if you do choose to dine in the lounge area, make sure to revel in the glassed-in wine cellar and tables with comfy chairs. Also, try a signature cocktail like the ginger martini or negroni!  The menu at The Pointe Restaurant features a lot of locally caught seafood and organic produce. For appetizers, I recommend the escargot or chopped salad. They also have an amazingly creamy clam chowder with thyme-smoked bacon. For entrees, the butter-poached lobster with pappardelle is luscious and rich. The Pan-seared halibut is another great seafood dish. For those not craving seafood, the roasted chicken is hearty and tender, and the filet mignon is cooked to perfection. They also offer an Impossible Burger, which is a great vegetarian alternative.  The Pointe even does specialty Thanksgiving and New Year’s Eve menus! Make sure to make a reservation! 9. Front Street Restaurant Address : 230 Commercial St, Provincetown, MA 02657 Front Street Restaurant is another intimate Italian spot serving a more contemporary style of cuisine. Located within a gorgeous Victorian-style home, Front Street is chef-owned and operated and has a cozy Old Cape Cod feel that is accentuated by the brick throughout the dining room and the romantic, dim lighting.  Front Street has an amazing wine list and also offers nightly specials in addition to its regular menu. For appetizers, their traditional Caesar salad is crisp and delicious, and the French onion soup is hearty with flavor and gooey cheese. I also suggest the shrimp and grits or mussels bianco!  If you decide to go with pasta for your entree, the wild boar ragu and potato gnocchi with white truffle cream are both rich and fulfilling dishes. For seafood, you can choose between various shrimp preparations, from tetrazzini, scampi, saltimbocca, and francese. They also serve a delicious plate of linguine and clams. If you want chicken or veal, the chicken cacciatore is a tasty dish, as well as the veal parmigiana. Lastly, for dessert, the vanilla bean panna cotta is super creamy and delicate.  This spot definitely considers itself to be family-friendly, but personally, I would describe it as more of a romantic, date-night location. Reservations at The Front Street Restaurant are very much recommended!  10. Strangers & Saints Address : 404 Commercial St, Provincetown, MA 02657 Strangers and Saints is a charming Mediterranean-style tavern and gastropub serving a wide variety of shareable plates for dinner. Located in a former sea captain’s home, this restaurant is filled with beautiful decor, like ships, gold-accented tables, and nautical, ocean scenes painted along the walls. The place consists of a gorgeous wooden bar that is only accentuated by the wooden beams along the ceiling. The dining room is slightly formal but equally relaxing, and it truly feels as though you are on a ship. Whether you sit at the bar, at a table, or enjoy the cozy leather chairs near the fireplace, you are bound to have a one-of-a-kind meal. There is also seasonal dining on the patio, which is great for people-watching and lovely sea views!   If you start your meal with a cocktail, I suggest the Barrel-aged Manhattan or Vintage Cosmopolitan–you can truly tell the level of ingredients used by how smooth and refreshing these drinks are!  As mentioned, Stranger’s and Saints focuses on shareable plates that aim to create an intimate and participatory dining experience. For seafood plates, I recommend the grilled Spanish octopus with fresh herbs or the pan-seared cod cheeks with chorizo, which are so, so good. For meat-based dishes, the pork belly Chicharron with spicy popcorn and queso fundido is unique and perfectly savory. Looking at vegetarian choices? The poached ricotta dumplings and charred shishito peppers are super tasty. The homemade hummus with bread is also a yummy dish to share among your table. For dessert, try “Mom’s Ricotta Cheesecake” which is infused with fresh berries!  Due to the sophisticated level of cuisine and lively environment, I consider Stranger’s and Saints to be more of an adult-style place probably not suited for young kids. However, the staff and service are so wonderful and attentive, so I’m sure kids would be welcome! Finally, the restaurant does accept reservations!  11. Jimmy’s HideAway Another spot located along Commercial Street, Jimmy’s HideAway is a hidden gem serving up American cuisine with European flare. The romantic ambiance in the restaurant’s dining room is immediately apparent, with the dim lighting, beautiful dark-wood bar, and a fun combination of high tops and regular tables. However, the delightful atmosphere is equally present along the outdoor patio, which is right along the water and features umbrella-clad tables perfect for appreciating ocean views and having a drink, like their spicy Paloma or a local draft beer.  For appetizers, the braised-short rib sliders are comforting and tender and the grilled Wellfleet oysters with warm jalapeno lemon butter have the perfect combination of acidity and richness. For a vegetarian alternative, the tofu wings are also super great and flavorful. For an entree, try the Provincetown Fisherman’s Stew–seriously, it is ridiculously good, with indulgent broth and loaded with fresh seafood, chorizo, and topped with crostinis. The menu also has a “comfort” section, with choices like fish and chips, Southern fried chicken, and fried shrimp.  For dessert, the key lime pie is extremely bright and tangy, and the bread pudding is warm and makes for a delicious end to your meal.  You can also find Jimmy’s nightly specials listed online!  I do consider the restaurant to be a spot more appropriate to enjoy without the kids, however, the staff at Jimmy’s HideAway is incredibly friendly and warm to all of its diners. Jimmy’s is open for dinner every night except for Wednesday and the restaurant does recommend making a reservation!  12. The Mews Restaurant & Cafe Address : 429 Commercial St, Provincetown, MA 02657 The Mews Restaurant & Cafe is a waterfront spot serving American cuisine with a seafood twist. The restaurant is divided into two levels: the bistro level and the beach level. The bistro, or upstairs dining room, consists of a neon-lit bar, high-top and regular tables, and beautiful bay views. The bistro level is definitely a bit more lively than downstairs, and is a great area to sit with friends! The beach level downstairs is a more quiet and intimate area ideal for a romantic date night. The floor features French doors and floor-to-ceiling windows that provide gorgeous views of the ocean and one of Provincetown’s lighthouses.  Mews has a fantastic raw bar and does offer nightly specials. For appetizers, I recommend fried cod fritters or lobster dumplings. If you want a salad, however, the arugula salad is very fresh and bright. For entrees, the duck leg confit is tender yet crispy and come with rich foie gras mashed potatoes. I also suggest the pan-seared scallops, which are perfectly cooked and come with a fried potato nest–both fun to eat and very tasty. For a classic dinner, try one of the steak or chicken dishes. If you’re looking for a vegan alternative, the menu offers a great vegan lemon pesto pasta with toasted pine nuts! For dessert, the mocha panna cotta with mascarpone whipped cream is luscious and creamy.  The restaurant does not have a kid’s menu, but with choices like cheeseburgers and chicken sandwiches, there are certainly some options for children!  The Mews Restaurant is open for dinner Tuesday through Saturday and does accept reservations.  13. The Squealing Pig Provincetown Address : 335 Commercial St, Provincetown, MA 02657 The Squealing Pig Provincetown is a pub-style establishment well-known for its lively environment and an amazing selection of tasty food and drinks. The restaurant has both indoor and outdoor dining, as well as a very cool bar with chalkboard listings and a large TV. The Squealing Pig has a lengthy beer selection, with tons of choices on draft, many local beers, and a wide array of hard ciders. There are also plenty of signature cocktails, like the “Pig Punch” and Cape Cod Mule. Additionally, there is nonalcoholic beer and seltzer available.  The raw bar at the Squealing Pig has tons of fresh seafood, including platters, shrimp cocktail, and daily ceviche specials. If you’re feeling especially adventurous, try the oyster shooter!  Furthermore, the raw bar offers a Happy Hour with deals on oysters.  For appetizers, the chicken wings and smoky seafood chowder are both delicious. I also urge you to try the amazing hand-cut and twice-fried French fries, which can be prepared in multiple ways–parmesan truffle, Tuscan, or Nepali curry. If you want something a bit lighter to start your meal, the house salad is very fresh and tasty.  For entrees, there is an abundance of options, from sandwiches to fried plates to homestyle classics, like shepherd’s pie and fried chicken. For seafood, I recommend the fish and chips or salmon burger. And, for a sandwich, the Cubano Toastie is loaded with slow-roasted pork and an amazing jalapeno mustard relish that packs a bright and tangy kick.  The Squealing Pig even has live music sometimes and while the regular restaurant hours are from 11 a.m. to 10 p.m., the bar stays open late!  14. Napi’s Restaurant Address : 7 Freeman St, Provincetown, MA 02657 Napi’s Restaurant coins itself an “unusual joint” and serves seafood and international cuisine. The restaurant is filled with unique decor and a copious amount of art. Offering dinner nightly, Napi’s has been open for 49 years and maintains its “old school” vibe while still exhibiting an eclectic environment filled with stained glass, lots of brick, and very cool light fixtures. There is also a beautiful fireplace, which is lovely if you enjoy a meal at Napi’s during the winter!  The menu at Napi’s Restaurant is known for being quite creative and inventive, and it lives up to expectations. For appetizers, I recommend the Portuguese kale soup, classic Caesar salad, or crispy fried calamari. Looking at entrees, the Mediterranean roasted vegetable ravioli is extremely vibrant and tasty. The roasted duck with orange sauce is also delicious and very generous with its portion. I also urge you to try one of the classics, like chicken alfredo or parmesan!  If you want a warm, inviting dinner that will leave you smiling, definitely check out Napi’s!  You can call to make a reservation!  15. Nor’ East Beer Garden Address : 206 Commercial St, Provincetown, MA 02657 Nor’ East Beer Garden is a wonderful brother and sister-owned restaurant offering great food and great beer in a beautiful outdoor setting. The restaurant has a rustic feel, filled with lots of wood, and a stunning bar. The tables are surrounded by greenery, flowers, trellises, and lots of vines. Even more, the staff is wonderfully welcoming and helpful to newcomers when it comes to both beer and food selections. Everything at Nor’ East is homemade, from the syrups used in drinks to the tortillas used in some dishes. If you do plan to try a beer, the specialty list is impressively large, with tons on draft, many local beers, and beers from all across the world. Also, make sure to ask about whichever limited-edition beer is available at the time! However, if you’d rather have a cocktail, the arugula mojito and lavender sidecar are creative and balanced.  The small plates menu at Nor’ East Beer Garden is separated into cold and hot dishes. For cold plates, I recommend the whipped ricotta on sourdough toast or the steamed and chilled mussels. For hot plates, the arancini and chicken parm are both comforting and packed with flavor. If you decide to order a main dish, the ribeye steak with chimichurri sauce is amazing and the roasted bluefish, one of my favorites, is super yummy.  The Nor’ East Beer Garden does not accept reservations but you can join the waitlist at the front of the garden and enjoy a beer while you await your table!  The post 15 Best Restaurants In Provincetown Massachusetts appeared first on Cape Cod Today .

title: 15 Best Restaurants in Harwich Massachusetts
author: Nicole Schneeberger
content: Looking for a place to eat in Harwich? Are you vacationing here? Or maybe you just moved to the Cape after  buying a home in Harwich ? Either way, I’m here to be your guide! Harwich Massachusetts is another picturesque Cape Cod town filled with boutique shops, gorgeous beaches, and amazing cuisine. As a kid, visiting Main Street in Harwich was one of my favorite things to do in the Summer. Admittedly, this was mostly because I really liked going to Dr. Gravity’s Kite Shop as a child, but also because of the food. As an adult, this is even more true. Harwich’s cuisine has only grown since I was younger, and while some classic gems still thrive and amaze me, there are tons of new restaurants that are worth checking out as well!  If you’re hungry and in the Harwich area, check out these restaurants below!  1. Cape Sea Grille Cape Sea Grille is an upscale Harwich Port spot serving new American cuisine and local seafood inside a 19th-century sea captain’s home. The restaurant has a refined, elegant atmosphere while still being warm and cheery, and the quaint style of the house it resides in adds to that warm “Cape” feeling. The dining room tables feature white linens and are candle lit. There is also seating at the bar and in the indoor porch area, which has large windows that give diners views of the street.  If you plan to start your meal with an adult beverage, the kiwi Aperol spritz is tasty and unique. There is also a specialty mocktail option if you don’t want to indulge!  The menu at Cape Sea Grille is often changing with what’s fresh and in season and it’s clear from the beautiful flair and presentation of the plating just how much care is put into each dish. For appetizers, the crispy duck confit is absolutely delectable, tender, and savory. The housemade pork pate is a hearty flavorful choice. The chilled summer gazpacho is another great option that is bright and refreshing on a hot day.  For entrees, the seared sea scallops are velvety and cooked to perfection. The flat iron steak is a great choice for anyone craving red meat–and it comes with a potato cake that is amazing. For vegetarians and vegans, the summer vegetable stew is loaded with fresh veggies and a delicate garlic broth. The menu also has many shareable sides, like the creamed spinach and mac and cheese.  If you still have room for dessert, try the unbeatable flourless chocolate cake or warm pecan tart!  The restaurant serves dinner Wednesday through Sunday from 5 pm to 9 pm and reservations are highly recommended. Also–when you make a reservation, make sure to specify if you want to sit inside the dining room or on the porch! Lastly, I would personally consider Cape Sea Grille to be a spot better enjoyed without the kids, as there is no kid’s menu and the food options are quite sophisticated!  2. Buca’s Tuscan Roadhouse Buca’s Tuscan Roadhouse is a very special experience that makes diners feel transported to Italy as soon as they walk inside. The Tuscan-themed spot serves high-end Italian cuisine in a cozy, intimate environment furnished with gorgeous wine-barrel decor and red-checkered table clothes along with low lighting. These intentional choices made by Buca’s owners enhance the romantic ambiance for customers.  Buca’s has seating inside their dining room, as well as some outdoor seating. There are also spots at their bar, which has a TV showing scenic clips of the Amalfi Coast. The food and beverage menus are both extensive, and the waitstaff is incredibly knowledgeable and great for giving recommendations, especially with the wine list!  When it comes to the food itself at Buca, there is a lot to discuss. Your meal will start with delicious homemade bread that is very much worth indulging in. For an appetizer, I urge you to try the Carciofi Ripieni, which are prosciutto-wrapped, grilled artichoke hearts with gorgonzola, mascarpone, and balsamic. These are absolutely amazing, and I say this as someone who is not exactly in love with artichokes. The grilled romaine salad is another starter that lives up to expectations.  For entrees, the veal scallopini is crisp, and flavorful, and can be ordered with a red wine or white wine sauce. If you want seafood, the pan-fried sole is melt-in-your-mouth and comes with fresh pappardelle pasta. Furthermore, Buca serves Italian classics like chicken or eggplant parmesan. There are also nightly specials and there are plenty of menu options for kids if you want to bring the whole family! For dessert, the Profiteroles–cream puffs with chocolate sauce are light and so, so yummy. The tiramisu and luxurious chocolate Italian wedding cake are other sweet choices.  Buca’s Tuscan Roadhouse serves dinner seven days a week from 4:30 pm to 9:30 pm. The restaurant is quite busy, so reservations are recommended. These can be made online or over the phone. You can also order takeout online, but I highly suggest eating in the restaurant if you want the full experience!  3. George’s Pizza House George’s Pizza House is my number one, absolute favorite pizza spot on the Cape. The restaurant has been owned and operated by the same family for 52 years. It also sits along Main Street in Harwich Port, making it the perfect spot to grab a slice in between perusing the local stores. George’s is a very casual, counter-order spot that is perfect for families. I have many fond memories of going to George’s as a young kid, drinking grape soda with my brother (back when I liked grape soda), and awaiting my pizza!  Speaking of pizza, lets talk about George’s. The crust is slightly thicker and the pies themselves are always hot, fresh, and crispy. There are specialty pizzas like the Mediterranean or the Kimopita pizza, which is topped with homemade meat sauce and cheese. If you don’t want a specialty pizza, there are plenty of toppings to build your own pizza–my go-to at George’s is usually sausage, onion, and green pepper! Additionally, during lunchtime, cheese and pepperoni slices are available.  If you aren’t craving pizza, the restaurant offers pasta, grinders, salads, calzones, and sides like cheesy garlic bread and onion rings. The steak bomb and meatball subs are both extremely flavorful and delicious. The Greek salad at George’s is also one of my favorites.  George’s is usually pretty busy, but the staff is always hard at work and the wait never feels too long. The restaurant does offer delivery if you live in the Harwich area, as well as take-out for everyone. There are also seat-yourself tables inside as well as a few benches out front if you want to eat while enjoying the charming hustle and bustle of Main Street.   If you want to try, what I consider, a Cape Cod institution, make sure to add George’s Pizza House to your restaurant list!  4. Twenty-eight Atlantic   Twenty-eight Atlantic is a high-end restaurant located within Wequassett Resort & Golf Club. The place has floor-to-ceiling windows that give jaw-dropping views of the sunset over Pleasant Bay. Offering both breakfast and dinner daily, twenty-eight Atlantic is ideal for a fun romantic date night when you feel excited about dressing up! The dining experience at twenty-eight Atlantic is quite formal, allowing patrons to choose between a three-course pre-fixe menu or a seven-course tasting menu (pricy, but worth it). You can also choose to add a fixed wine pairing with the seven-course meal. Some standouts within the menu include the rich and delectable lobster carbonara, the black cod (my favorite), and the foie gras trifle. For dessert, the coconut panna cotta is creamy and even comes with a refreshing pina colada sorbet.  Reservations are highly suggested at twenty-eight Atlantic as it’s a very popular spot for diners seeking a formal meal. If you end up having to wait, there are fire pits with comfy chairs outside, overlooking the tranquil water views!  If you have plans to treat yourself to a gorgeous, upscale meal, definitely consider twenty-eight Atlantic a strong contender!  5. Mooncusser’s Tavern Inn & Restaurant Mooncusser’s Tavern Inn & Restaurant serves up plenty of cocktails, tapas, and entrees in a lively yet relaxing atmosphere. The lighting is romantic and the decor is elegant but casual. The ambiance at Mooncusser is incredibly warm, inviting, and down to earth. There is seating in the dining room, or in the adjacent  ‘tavern’ area near the bar where some high-top tables are located as well. Even more, there is seating outside on their patio!  The drinks at Mooncusser’s Tavern are certainly a standout. There is a vast martini menu with choices like a spicy dirty martini and a pear martini. The wine list is also extensive and there are many local beers on tap.  If you plan to split some tapas between your table, I insist you try the gambas al ajillo (garlic shrimp), which are tangy and filled with flavor. The elote and local lobster dip is another dish that is fun to share!  For entrees, I suggest the Limoncello lobster pasta, which is rich and full of flavor. If you’re wanting a burger, Mooncusser’s is the place to fulfill that craving, as they arguably have one of the best burgers on the Cape. Their Original Mooncusser’s Burger is topped with a fried duck egg, bacon jam, and Havarti–and it’s ridiculously delicious. There is also the Flower Power burger, which uses Beyond Meat, providing a plant-based alternative. Mooncusser even has a featured nightly burger special in addition to their regular specials, so make sure to ask your server!  If you still have room for dessert, definitely warm molten chocolate cake, which is honestly heavenly and luscious.  While Mooncusser can accommodate kids, they do not have a children’s menu. And, given the vibe of the place, I would consider it more of an ‘adult’s night out’ type of spot.  The restaurant is open Wednesday through Sunday from 5 to 9 pm and does accept reservations!  6. Mad Minnow Bar & Kitchen Mad Minnow Bar & Kitchen is a casual, modern, and cheerful spot offering craft beers, cocktails, and local favorites with a twist. The restaurant itself is warm and has tables inside as well as seating at the bar. Although, I think the true essence of Mad Minnow is expressed when you walk outside and see the outdoor dining area. A large white tent with string lights is set up over picnic tables, along with cornhole, fire pits, and outdoor couches. There is even an outdoor beer garden with selections on tap and wines available. If you’re craving a refreshing cocktail, try the dark and stormy, which is topped with a housemade popsicle.  For an appetizer, I suggest trying the tuna cannoli, which is filled with fresh poke-style tuna, citrus, and sriracha aioli. The clam chowder is also a good starter if you want something a bit more filling.  Looking at entrees, there are many options for every type of craving. From rigatoni bolognese to lobster rolls to the shrimp and crab cake po boy–everyone will have their needs met. I recommend trying Mad Minnow’s take on a ‘Filet-O-Fish’ which comes with cornflake-crusted cod and housemade tartar sauce on a brioche bun. Furthermore, a gluten-free menu is available.  The restaurant does not accept reservations, so it’s first come first serve at Mad Minnow, but it’s worth the wait! Mad Minnow Bar & Kitchen does have a kid’s menu and with all of the activities in their outdoor area, it surely is a great spot to bring the family!  7. Villa Roma Villa Roma is a Cape Cod staple for anyone craving classic Italian food in a fine-dining setting. The restaurant has been open for over twenty years and has a very “North End Boston” vibe that is cozy and dimly lit. The tables are a bit close together, but that only adds to the authentic, intimate vibe–and it never feels overly crowded. Additionally, there is outdoor seating in the patio area as well as seats at the fully-stocked bar. The service at Villa Roma is exceptional, with attentive and helpful waitstaff.  Your meal will begin with a yummy serving of fresh bread and butter. If you plan to have an appetizer, the Italian Wedding Soup is absolutely amazing. I also recommend the chicken marsala or alfredo for an entree, both of which have greatly generous portions. However. Villa Roma is also known for its homemade lasagna. Additionally, the restaurant has nightly specials, which can be found on the front page of its website . For dessert, the housemade tiramisu is incredible, rich, and melts in your mouth.  I would definitely make reservations if you plan to dine here, and while the place does technically welcome children, there is no kids menu and it is much more suited for a romantic evening or a kid-free, adult-only evening. Overall, Villa Roma is a gem that should be known to all on the Cape looking for a relaxing Italian meal!  8. Outer Bar + Grille Outer Bar + Grille is another lovely spot located within the Wequassett Resort & Golf Club. The restaurant overlooks Pleasant Bay and promotes an open-air atmosphere, as displayed by its large outdoor deck. The indoor decor is chic, modern, and beachy, with additional views of the pool below. The deck also has canopies to shade outdoor seating while still allowing you to enjoy the wonderful ocean breeze.  The staff at Outer Bar and Grille is especially personable and knowledgeable of the wine list and able to make suggestions for what specialty cocktail to try (I’d go for the toasted coconut margarita, but that’s just me!). There are also mocktails and non-alcoholic beers available.  The food at Outer Bar + Grille promotes local seafood cuisine with creative twists. For starters, the raw bar offers fresh choices like shrimp, oysters, and their luxurious caviar flight. If you want something vibrant and bright, the menu has a variety of poke bowls and salads to choose from. For more traditional fare, try the lobster roll or one of their pizzas–they even have a pizza topped with shaved potato and caramelized onion! If you want to indulge a little extra, try the beach dog–topped with mac and cheese and bacon. And for dessert, don’t miss out on the brownie sundae or NY-style cheesecake.  For vegetarians, there is a tofu poke bowl as well as a chickpea shawarma dish and a cauliflower steak alternative!  The restaurant does accept reservations, which are recommended. However, if you do end up having to wait for a table, take a stroll to the beach or the docks! The Grille serves lunch from 11:30 to 3 pm and dinner until 10 pm daily! Moreover, there is a kid’s menu with plenty of choices. Finally, don’t be deterred that Outer Bar + Grille is located within a resort and golf club–it’s welcome to everyone, not just those staying at the Inn or golfing! While the restaurant is a bit pricy, it’s totally worth it to treat yourself to a meal here!  Lastly, check their social media to see if they have live entertainment going on before you visit!  9. Red River BBQ Good BBQ is a cuisine difficult to find among Cape Cod’s well-known seafood fare, but Red River BBQ has proven to be the spot for real, authentic BBQ cuisine. Serving lunch and dinner from 11:30 am to 8 pm, the restaurant sports a cozy ambiance with cowboy-ish decor and a casual vibe. Red River has seating in the dining room and at their gorgeous wooden bar.  The staff at Red River is clearly experienced and very hardworking, and the chef works closely with local farmers to source fresh ingredients, which is proven through the quality of the food. The menu has a wide array of small plates, large plates, sides, and a changing nightly selection of desserts. For small plates, the hush puppies and fried green tomatoes are both amazing. If you want a lighter appetizer, the watermelon and cojita cheese salad is vibrant and yummy. For large plates, the brisket is tender and smoky and the rack of ribs falls off the bone. Each large plate also comes with a generous portion and includes cornbread, coleslaw, and your choice of side, whether that’s cheddar mac and cheese or cowboy beans!  If you aren’t craving one of their larger plates, the restaurant also offers items like juicy smash burgers, crispy chicken sandwiches, and pulled pork shoulder sandwiches. Red River even has menu offerings like fish and chips and their crispy shrimp basket if you do want seafood! Red River BBQ is also a great place to dine if you’re looking for some entertainment! There is live music Tuesdays and Fridays as well as events every so often like Trivia Night. Additionally, Thursday night is smoked prime rib night, so make sure to arrive early while the meat lasts, because trust me–it actually melts in your mouth.  BBQ is one of my favorite cuisines and Red River does not disappoint! Certainly, check this place out if you need a seafood break or have a BBQ craving!  10. The Lanyard Bar & Grill The Lanyard Bar & Grill is a spot I have frequented many times over the years. The restaurant has lunch and dinner, serving classic American food along with seafood fare and an amazing selection of craft beers. The Lanyard vibes are casual and pub-esque, with classic decor and walls adorned with various signs and memorabilia. While there is plenty of seating inside, there is also ample space at the bars in and outdoors, as well as tables on the patio. If you’re looking to catch a game, try snagging a seat at the bar! The food at the Lanyard is tavern styled while still including quintessential seafood classics. I usually start with the loaded nachos or smoked chicken wings, along with one of their delicious cocktails. The Cape Cod Reuben is a tasty lunch choice, featuring crispy cod instead of the usual corn beef. Lanyard also has great burgers and a veggie burger alternative. If you want a traditional seafood dish, the stuffed quahogs and fish and chips are amazing if available. The Lanyard has nightly specials, which are usually posted on their Facebook page if you wish to check them out prior to your visit. They also have a kid’s menu and are very family-friendly! There is even outdoor live music some nights.  Check out The Lanyard Bar & Grill if you want to enjoy a casual, fun meal in a relaxing and welcoming environment!  11. Hot Stove Saloon Hot Stove Saloon is an exciting, lively spot located in Harwich Port Village. The restaurant is a sports-pub-styled place adorned with vintage baseball decor and thirteen flat-screen TVs, providing assurance that you won’t miss your team playing. Hot Stove Saloon is a cozy spot perfect for a fun night out or lunch and dinner with the family. The friendly staff even offers a complimentary handful of baseball cards to kids as they look over the children’s menu!  There are two bars within the saloon, as well as a dining room area. The bars are fully stocked with beers on tap and a lengthy wine list. The food at Hot Stove Saloon can be described as elevated ball-park food with Cape Cod flare. For starters, the homemade potato chips are crisp and salty and the chili is packed with flavor. You can also get an order of their delicious chicken wings, which have unique sauce choices, like pesto parmesan and teriyaki.  If you want pizza, the Saloon’s thin-crust style pies are crisp and topped with their housemade tomato sauce. You can also substitute gluten-free crust upon request!  For entrees, look out for the daily specials! Additionally, looking at the regular menu, the steak tip dinner is flavor-filled and the baked cod with Ritz cracker crust is delectable. My go-to is the cod tacos, for something refreshing and light!  If you want dessert, snag a rootbeer float and soak in the nostalgia! Hot Stove Saloon does not take reservations but they do have a happy hour! They are also open from 11:30 am to 1 am!  12. Brax Landing Brax Landing is a spot well-known to most who’ve spent any time in Harwich. The restaurant is located on Saquatucket Harbor, giving patrons a lovely water view. The large outdoor deck has plenty of tables for anyone wanting to enjoy the scenery (try to get a seat outside if you’re eating during the sunset–it’s gorgeous!). There is also ample seating at the bar and tables indoors, surrounded by the rustic, nostalgic decor that lines Brax Landing’s walls.  Brax has a large selection of craft beers on tap and a huge cocktail menu with many frozen drinks, like the Brax Pina Colada, which I highly recommend!  When it comes to food, there are daily specials offered and a good kid’s menu for the young ones. The regular menu itself is quite substantial. Really, anything you would hope to be good at a casual Cape Cod spot is good at Brax. From the lobster rolls to the burgers to the oysters, all of the food is fresh and delicious. Whether you want a whole steamed lobster with melted butter or a full rack of baby-back ribs, Brax Landing has you covered! Personally, I recommended trying their fish and chips or crab cake sandwich if you have a seafood craving!  Brax Landing is open seven days a week from 11:30 am to 1 am, making it a great spot for lunch, dinner, or some late-night fun! They also offer brunch on Sundays and sometimes have deals where burgers and appetizers are half-priced! The restaurant does not accept reservations, and there can sometimes be a wait for dinner, but in my experience, the staff is pretty efficient at moving the wait along. But if you do have to wait, there is a beautiful fire pit with chairs right over the harbor, perfect for sitting and sipping on a pre-dinner cocktail.  Head to Brax Landing if you want a casual, fun, family-friendly experience filled with good food and yummy drinks!  13. 400 East 400 East is another clean, casual spot with a tavern vibe that is perfect for a family lunch or dinner. The restaurant serves lunch and dinner daily, offering American comfort food and local seafood cuisine. There is ample seating within the restaurant’s dining room as well as at their full-service TV-filled bar. 400 East is very family-friendly and accommodating to larger parties of diners. The staff is also very friendly and kind! 400 East has fresh ground burgers with fun options like the Tennessee BBQ burger or the cheesy patty melt. Additionally, the menu has salads, sandwiches, seafood, and grilled thin-crust pizza, which can be made with a cauliflower crust! If you want an appetizer, the buffalo wings are spicy and well-cooked. Personally, I have enjoyed the Cobb salad as well as the salmon burger. And, if it’s not too hot of a day, the French onion soup is one of the best I’ve ever had. The restaurant is also known for its perfectly crisp french fries, which I can attest, are delicious.  Furthermore, 400 East has a great kid’s menu and daily specials, which can be found posted on the restaurant’s website!  While 400 East does not accept reservations, they do have call-ahead seating!  14. 3 Monkeys Street Bar + Kitchen 3 Monkeys Street Bar + Kitchen is a unique, modern spot serving a combo of East Asian, Japanese, and American-styled cuisine right on Main Street in Harwich Port. The restaurant promotes an “open air” concept along with quirky decor, and brightly painted, fun, graffiti-esque walls that add to the dining experience. There is outdoor seating on the patio, tables inside, and two bars! The drinks are tiki-inspired and umbrella-clad, contributing to the overall vibe of the place. The beverage menu has an extensive Japanese whiskey list, as well as many frozen classics, draft beers, and sake. I personally would go for the Monkey Mai Thai or Ninja Punch! Looking at 3 Monkey’s food offerings, the menu has a wide variety of choices. From ramen to bao buns, to pad thai, to sushi, there are options for every craving. For starters, I suggest the popcorn shrimp or edamame. For your main meal, I recommend the salmon poke bowl or spicy tuna cucumber roll. Their California Roll also features real blue crab (not imitation!). All of the fish is incredibly fresh and flavorful. If you’re looking for a vegan or vegetarian alternative, the Tofu Tots and Veg Head Rolls are both delicious.  If you’re craving Asian Fusion in a casual, exciting environment, 3 Monkeys Street Bar + Kitchen is the place to go! The restaurant does not accept reservations, so make sure to plan accordingly, or try and snag some seats at the gorgeous bar!  15. The Port Restaurant + Bar The Port is a well-known, lively spot along Main Street in Harwich Port. Serving dinner seven days a week and lunch on Saturday and Sunday, The Port maintains an elegant, upscale vibe with plenty of seating. Inside, you’ll find a modern, almost Boston-esque atmosphere with black leather booths and a gorgeous bar. In contrast, outside you’ll experience a much more casual, relaxing environment, filled with corn hole, ring toss, and an outdoor bar sporting nautical, beachy decor.  For food, start with the raw bar! The Port has one-dollar fresh and chilled oysters from 3 to 5 pm. I also recommend the Caesar salad as an appetizer–this place has one of the best Caesar’s I’ve had in a long time. For dinner, the Portuguese stew is loaded with seafood and linguica sausage. The roasted chicken is a hearty, tasty option if you want something a little more basic for your meal. I also urge you to try the lobster rasta pasta filled with butter-poached lobster and a parmesan cream sauce over penne pasta. If you have room for dessert, try the bananas fosters for two!  The Port Restaurant + Bar does accept reservations, which I would be sure to make, especially on the weekends in the Summer season. While the restaurant can accommodate children, I find the atmosphere to be much more suited to adults of all ages. And…. for young adults, or anyone wanting to stay up late, The Port doesn’t close until 1 am, making it a place perfect to relax, play some games, and have some fun! Score!
