title: 21 Best Things To Do In Provincetown Right Now (Local Secrets Revealed)
author: Kathy Jameson
content: As one of the most LGBTQ-friendliest town in the United States, Provincetown is an exciting town that’s filled with lots of fun things to do. It attracts members of the LGBTQ community, traveling from different parts of the country (and even world) to everything this lovely town has to offer.  During different seasons of the year, the town hosts annual LGBTQ events and invites everyone to participate in such events. It’s also worthwhile to note that many businesses cater to and are owned by LGBTQ-friendly folk. Apart from that, P-town also gives you insight into the United States history, from the time the pilgrims landed on Cape Cod to the progressive LGBTQ movement.  If you are visiting the town or perhaps recently purchased a home for sale in Provincetown , try out some of the things listed below: 1. Watch whales swimming in the ocean  Don’t miss the chance to see whales in real-life! Well, different types of whales are always spotted swimming close to Cape Cod. As a result, Provincetown is packed with lots of tour companies specializing in whale-watching expeditions. One of the most popular tour expedition companies is the Dolphin Fleet Whale Watch .  It takes you on a tour that lasts for about three to four hours, so you might come across five to six whales. During this guided tour, you might see fin whales or humpback whales as they are feeding or diving.      On top of that, the crew gives you more insight into marine life by explaining the behavior of whales and what they love. And once you come across a certain whale, the tour guide will tell you which type of whale it is.   2. Shop at Commercial Street The commercial street stretches for about 3 miles, and it’s packed with various shops and galleries that are quite intriguing. If you take a walk along this street, there are high chances that you might find something that captures your attention.  Examples of such things include paintings, jewelry, and beautiful cutlery. The surrounding buildings are beautiful, with breathtaking architectural designs. 3. Embark on a sailing expedition  If you want to explore the Atlantic Ocean and visit places with breathtaking views, you should embark on a sailing expedition. Well, the ocean can be quite calming and relaxing.  Just imagine this for a moment: waves splashing into the ocean, the sound of winds blowing past your body, and clear blue skies. Well, this is an experience that can make you forget all your troubles. Luckily, sailing charters have different vessels, so you’ll get the chance to choose the vessel that you want to sail in.  For example, Moment Sailing Adventures takes you on a sailing expedition, using a vintage yacht. Besides that, the sailing charter offers a wide variety of sailing packages. Sails are categorized into different groups, depending on the time duration of the expedition.  Alternatively, you can sail in a schooner if that is your most preferred sailing vessel. The Schooner Bay Lady II is an example of an agency that takes you on a sailing expedition, using a schooner. 4. Go fishing  With a large coastline that stretches past multiple bays and harbors, Provincetown is quite popular for its fishing activities.  Examples of areas with tons of fish include Long Point, Race Point, and Wood End.   However, each area has different fish species, with the most common being tunas, pollocks, and bluefish. It’s also quite normal to come across a large tuna or bass that’s 40 pounds or 50 pounds.  From deep sea fishing to shore fishing, Provincetown is the perfect destination for various fishing activities. For starters, fishing on the shoreline may be challenging, especially if you are not used to it. But, you can still have a lot of fun by trying out new techniques such as surfcasting.  Moreover, this town is packed with multiple fishing charters that’ll guide you as you are fishing in the nearby waters. The Beth Ann Fishing Charters is a good example of a business that focuses on fishing and related activities. It offers various fishing packages, giving you a wide variety of fishing options. You can opt for bluefish fishing, tuna fishing, or blue-fin tuna fishing, based on your preference.  Besides that, you’ll also choose the boat that you want to ride on.  5. Spend the day at Herring Cove Beach Popular due to its clear waters, Herring Cove Beach is one of the most aesthetic beaches in Provincetown.  Once you get to the beach, you’ll be mesmerized by the beauty of lagoons and sand dunes. Such features always attract wildlife to the beach, bringing you closer to nature while you are having fun at the beach. And as you swim in the Atlantic Ocean, you’ll spot different birds diving into the ocean.  Unlike other beaches in the area, Herring Cove Beach is quite large, with enough space for setting up beach umbrellas. So if you want to enjoy beautiful views while sunbathing, add Herring Cove Beach to your list.  During the Summer season, the management invites musicians and local bands to the beach, giving them a chance to showcase their skills. Most bands usually perform on Wednesdays, from 6 pm to 7 pm, to keep you entertained on the beach. And since the place is packed with different eateries, you can easily grab a snack before live performances.       Besides that, this beach has a clothing-optional area, which is subdivided into different sections to accommodate everyone. While the area might not be officially recognized by the management, everyone on the beach treats it as an officially-recognized zone.  6. Dining at the local restaurants Provincetown is a foodie paradise! The local cuisine is quite fascinating as it focuses on seafood. Nevertheless, the town has various restaurants that specialize in different cuisines, offering you a wide variety of options to choose from. Visit the Lobster Pot to try out local seafood that’s prepared in a French manner. The menu features Portuguese fish, Sea Scallop Crudo, Lobster Avocado cocktail, and other delicacies.  Italian dishes, on the other hand, are offered by restaurants such as the Front Street Restaurant , Sal’s Place , and Mistralino Ristorante all of these fantastic restaurants made our Best Restaurants In Provincetown list ! 7. Visit the Provincetown Art Association and Museum Dating back to 1914, the Provincetown Art Association and Museum has a wide variety of art pieces and artifacts that were passed down from local artists.  By visiting this museum and art gallery, you’ll get a chance to view art collections that illustrate how beautiful Cape Cod is. It also becomes easier to understand the meaning behind different artwork pieces. Some art pieces have a deep sense of history, giving you an insight into historical events that took place in Cape Cod.  The Arrival 1620 is an example of an artwork that has a deep sense of history. It takes you back to the 17th century, when pilgrims arrived at Cape Cod’s Coast, painting a clear picture of historical events.  And as an age-inclusive artwork museum, the Provincetown Art Association and Museum hosts events, which are suitable for kids and adults.  For instance, the Little Artists Summer Program is a workshop program for teaching kids how to come up with artistic ideas. Adult workshops, on the other hand, will cover everything from portrait drawing to sculpting. 8. Riding a bike on Cape Cod Province Lands Bike Trail Designed to cut through hilly places, the Province Lands Bike Trail is one of the most physically challenging trails in Provincetown. It passes through Herring Cove Beach, Beech Forest, and Race Point Beach. It’s also surrounded by an environment that’s rich in nature, bringing you closer to mother nature during your trip. You’ll also find unique things on each stretch.  For instance, as you are cycling from Province Lands Visitor Center towards Race Point Beach, you’ll see some sand dunes, just a few miles from Race Point Beach. And while this stretch has some breathtaking scenes, it is quite steep.  Nevertheless, the terrain gets better when you pass Race Point Beach. After that, your next stop will be Herring Cove Beach. But, before you get to Herring Cove Beach, you have to cycle through a certain loop that is surrounded by woodlands and sand dunes. Also, don’t be surprised when a deer, coyote, or fox jumps on the trail.                      Since the Province Lands Bike Trail is paved with asphalt, you’ll have a smooth ride while you are cycling from one point to the next. 9. Visit the Shark Center As the name hints, this conservation protects sharks and conducts a lot of scientific research. Since it’s open to the public, you can visit the conservation center if you want to learn more about sharks.   The staff gives you insight into the most popular shark species in Cape Cod — the Great white shark. It’s worthwhile to note that the conservative center organizes exhibitions, from Monday to Friday. Videos are always used to complement other sources of information. And if you want to have a memorable experience, don’t forget to visit the VR room. This is where the magic happens. Once you wear a VR headset, your attention will be captured by a virtual world that’s quite similar to ours. And after a few seconds, the VR recreates how the Bahamas looks like.  You’ll feel as if you are swimming next to Hammerhead sharks. The VR headsets are programmed to show you how different shark species behave in their natural habitats. This shark center also has a special room that’s designed for kids. 10. Birdwatching at Beech Forest Grab your binoculars, camera, and hiking boots, and go on a birdwatching trip.  For starters, the Beech Forest has a lot of trails that are suitable for hiking and birdwatching.  During fall and spring, birds always flock to the Beech forest. Due to seasonal changes, they always migrate from multiple regions — the Mexican Gulf and South America — while searching for better climatic conditions.  For example, in the first few months of spring, birds might migrate, but at a slower rate as compared to the following months.  Between the months of April and May, you might get lucky and spot wood warblers. It’s one of the most beautiful birds due to its contrasting body colors. While the yellow and orange hues complement each other, the blue color forms a deep contrast. Examples of other bird species that you’ll spot include tufted titmouse, hairy woodpecker, gray catbird, and cedar waxwing.  11. Go to the Provincetown Public Library While this library gives you access to books and educational media, it’s also a historical momentum that goes way back to the 19th century.   It was designed to incorporate Cape Cod’s way of life. For example, an old vintage ship was rebuilt inside the library, just to give you a glimpse into the old way of life. On top of that, the old vintage ship complements the interior design and makes the place look more appealing.  Besides that, the Provincetown Public Library preserves other art collections and artifacts. By visiting the library, you’ll get a chance to view some of the items that are featured in the 40,000-piece art collection. From time to time, the library organizes book-themed events, with different programs, to keep you entertained during your visit. And one of the most popular themed events is inspired by Moby-Dick. During this event, multiple readers usually meet up to discuss the book in detail.  The main building has a section, where young kids can have some fun. The kid’s section is located next to the old vintage ship.  12. Watch a live performance at Provincetown Theatre Whether you are planning to visit Provincetown during Spring, Winter, or Summer, you’ll always find an interesting play in the local theater. Featuring multiple types of theatrical productions, the Provincetown Theater is suitable for anyone who loves classical and modern theater.  It is packed with artists and performers who use their talent to convey deep messages through dramatization.  And as you are watching theatrical performances, you’ll be full of emotions. Some performances will make you laugh while other acts will make you cry.  For example, Terrence McNally’s Love Play evokes a wide range of strong emotions, from compassion to sadness. Carry some paper towels just in case.   And if you love humorous performances, watch something like the Thoroughly Modern Millie play. Thanks to the compact design of the theater, you can easily watch performances from different seats. Also, the lighting and sound system is amazing. 13. Enjoy the nightlife   The nightlife in Provincetown is out of this world!  Since Provincetown is an LGBTQ-friendly town, it has interesting gay bars and clubs, which are welcoming to everyone who wants to have fun.    When it comes to partying, you have two options — you can either take it easy or get wild! Whichever the case, Provincetown has suitable spots for every kind of activity, wild or not. Nightlife starts at around 6.30 pm and extends to midnight and the early morning hours. During this time frame, the town is always filled with lots of fun activities and events.   For instance, if you want to have a chilled and relaxed night, visit the Provincetown Brewing Co. and try the local beers. The place has a laid-back and funky vibe.  For those who love dancing, the Crown & Anchor will be the perfect spot for blowing off steam with fancy dance moves.  And even if you have two left feet, you can learn a thing or two while dancing. The Crown & Anchor features multiple restaurants, bars, and nightclubs. Think of it as a one-stop shop for entertainment-related activities.  Finally, you can take the party to the ocean by visiting the Aqua Bar. It sits on the edge of the Atlantic Ocean, giving you an amazing experience while you are partying. 14. Take a hike on the Dune Shacks Trail The Dune Shacks Trail is found in one of the most aesthetically-pleasing geographical zones. Just as the name hints, the trail has breathtaking views of big sand dunes, since it cuts through different landscapes. Such sightings are always complemented by views of the blue Ocean and clear skies. And thanks to these beautiful sightings, hiking on this trail can be quite calming, relaxing, and rejuvenating.  As it turns out, a long stretch of the Dune Shacks Trail is covered with fine sand, so you can take off your shoes and walk barefoot on the white sand. Apparently, nothing comes close to this therapeutic feeling.     Don’t forget to take a few pictures of the landscape and the surrounding scenery. 15. Try out kayaking and paddle boarding Apart from the Atlantic Ocean, Provincetown is also in close proximity to other water bodies and waterways, which are suitable for watersports. So, kayaking and paddle boarding are the most popular water sports in Provincetown. Moreover, there are multiple watersports companies that specialize in rentals, kayaking lessons, and paddle boarding lessons such as Coyote Kayaks . For those who love kayaking and paddle boarding, the might be an ideal choice for you, especially if you are planning to rent a kayak or paddle board. It is a one-stop shop for everything that’s related to paddle boarding and kayaking.   Once you rent a kayak or a paddleboard, a tour guide will show you the route you’ll follow during your expedition. In most scenarios, the guide takes you on a tour through the Herring Cove Tidal Lake. After covering a certain distance in the Herring Cove tidal lake, various landmarks will become more visible. You’ll paddle past huge sand dunes and aesthetic landscapes. This expedition gets better as you go farther.  If you are keen enough, you’ll notice some of the mud caves that are located close to other features. The main highlight of the expedition is the Wood Island Lighthouse.  16. Watch the ocean from the Pilgrim Monument & Provincetown Museum The pilgrim monument is about 253 feet tall — it overlooks the ocean and gives you a superb view of harbors, bays, and the horizon. However, you have to get to the highest floor for a clear view.   The Provincetown Museum preserves information and data that goes way back to the 17th century, when pilgrims settled in the town. Various historical artifacts are exhibited in the museum to help you comprehend Cape Cod’s history. Such exhibitions will take you through different time periods, from the time the monument was built to the most recent developments. Speaking of which, the museum also features multiple exhibitions that can give you more insight into the history of the LGBTQ community. These historical exhibitions explain how the LGBTQ community grew in Provincetown and the significance of the community in the town.  17. Jet skiing in the ocean  Challenge your friends or family members to race you to a predetermined point! This watersport is all about speed and thrill.  Still, jet skiing can be treated as an ocean exploration expedition. And as the adrenaline is pumping through your veins, you’ll feel psyched up to visit different parts of the Atlantic Ocean. The sun will also be shining on your face whilst the ocean breeze blows past you.  Apart from that, Provincetown has different jet ski rentals that’ll offer you what you need for your expedition.  You should check out Ptown Watersport if you want to get an adrenaline kick while riding a jet ski.   18. Go for an evening stroll at the Macmillan Pier Stretching a few miles into the ocean, the Macmillan Pier is a perfect spot for evening strolls. It’s a center point for different activities. For starters, multiple boats, yachts, and ferries are always docked quite close to the Macmillan Pier. So don’t be surprised when you see different types of boats and ferries.  That’s not all, the Macmillan Pier also preserves the country’s history by sheltering artifacts and vessels that were used in previous centuries. A great example of a sea vessel that’s found along the Macmillan Pier is the Santa Maria . As one of the few ships that was used by Christopher Colombus, the Santa Maria goes way back to the 15th century. To preserve the history of the country, the town reconstructed the ancient ship and placed it along the Macmillan Pier. As a result, Santa Maria complements the scenery, making it look more attractive.  Besides that, you’ll also find a few benches, which face the Atlantic Ocean. And if you want to enjoy the views, just sit on a bench and relax.  Speaking of spectacular views, there are high chances that you might catch a glance of whales diving into the ocean, once you take a seat and become observant enough.  Since the pier is surrounded by beautiful scenery, multiple artists usually set up painting stations along the pier to capture the breathtaking views. Anyone who’d love to paint the horizon will be offered a few painting lessons by some of the artists. After that, you’ll have the freedom to paint whatever you want on a blank canvas.  19. Watch sunsets and seals sunbathing at Race Point Beach  Seals love sunbathing during the afternoon hours when the sun is not too hot. It’s also worthwhile to note that seals like playing with one another while they are in the water. And as they are sunbathing and playing, you’ll see them moving around on the beach.    The depth of the ocean is about 150 ft — this depth is optimum for the survival of different fish species. Seals always visit such spots so they can feed.  Featuring a coastline that stretches for miles, Race Point Beach has the most spectacular and amazing sunset views. However, sunsets may look different, depending on where you are viewing them from. If you are planning to catch sunsets from the south, you’ll see reddish rays with hints of orange hues.    20. Check out the place where the pilgrims touched down  While Provincetown has multiple museums, it is also the home of various historical sites. Found along the Provincetown Harbor, the ‘First Landing Park’ is the first place where the pilgrims visited after their arrival.     From the sound of it, you can easily tell that it’s a simple historical park that’s designed to give you more insight into the pilgrim journey. 21. Attend The Family Week Event If you want to have fun and meet like-minded individuals, you should attend the Family Week event . Considered to be the biggest LGBTQ event, the Family Week event hosts visitors from multiple parts of the country and the world.  Every single day is packed with different fun activities to keep you entertained during your stay in Provincetown. And the good thing is that every activity has an age limit. Some activities are suitable for kids, while other activities are ideal for adults. Featuring a wide variety of activities such as Yoga sessions, art shows, and organized sports, you can easily find the right activity to participate in.   Organizers always publish a list of upcoming events, making it easier for you to plan for an upcoming event.   What will you do here? With so many interesting spots, Provincetown is one of the most exciting towns in Cape Cod. If you visit the town, please attend some of the annual events that are hosted in different spots. The nightlife is out of this world and you’ll have a great time in some of the nightclubs. Take some time, review this list and discover everything that Provincetown Massachusetts has to offer those of you visiting or even living here! The post 21 Best Things To Do In Provincetown Right Now (Local Secrets Revealed) appeared first on Cape Cod Today .

title: 21 Best Things To Do In Falmouth Right Now (Local Secrets Revealed)
author: Kathy Jameson
content: Looking for an adventure to take on while visiting Falmouth Massachusetts? Whether you are planning to try out the local food or participate in water sports, you’ll find the perfect options in Falmouth for trying out new things.  While you might be charged a fee to access some of our recommendations don’t fret, some places don’t have admission fees and are 100% free for you to enjoy. For instance, if you go on a hiking trip on the Quissett Harbor trails, you won’t be charged any admission fees because it’s always open to the public. Here are the best things to do while on the Cape in Falmouth Massachusetts. We know you will enjoy them as much as we do! 1. Try out different wines at Cape Cod Winery  Without a doubt, Cape Cod Winery is one of the most ideal spots for wine tasting. For starters, this winery offers you more than ten different wines, making it possible for you to taste a wide variety of wines.  On top of that, everything is set out in an open outdoor space. As a result, you’ll get a chance to try out multiple wines from a beautiful outdoor garden.  Thanks to the beautiful scenery, this wine-tasting expedition can also be treated as a nature retreat. Once the wine is served, swirl it gently, take a whiff, and taste it as you enjoy the breathtaking views. And if you are lucky enough, the weather conditions might favor you with amazing sunsets.  To keep you entertained while you are drinking wine, the management team invites artists and bands to play live music. On top of that, this place also offers you different types of board games to keep you occupied while you are sipping wine.  2. Fish in the nearby waters  Fishing makes it easier for you to explore different water bodies in Falmouth. You’ll also come across new fish species when you try out new places. Examples of some of the fish you’ll come across include chain pickerel and striped bass. Many fishing charters will take you to the right fishing spots for an amazing experience. For instance, if you go on a fishing trip in June, you’ll be taken to the water close to Robinsons Hole, Woods Hole, and Quicks Hole. From August to September, fishing charters will take you to other fishing areas, surrounding the Buzzards Bay.   As the sun sets over the horizon, you’ll see a beautiful orangish reflection on the water, which can be quite breathtaking. Check out Jakamo Fishing Charters and get a reservation before it’s too late! 3. Go on a cycling trip on the Shining Sea Bikeway For those who love physical activities, cycling on the Shining Sea Bikeway could be a suitable activity for calming your mind. A large section of the Shining Sea Bikeway neighbors the coast, giving you amazing views of the ocean while you are cycling. Apart from that, other sections of this trail are close to harbors, so don’t be surprised when you see some water vessels docking.      Make some stops and take a moment to enjoy the ocean views as the breeze blows against your skin.  While a long stretch of this trail is constructed next to the coastline, you’ll spot some woodlands as you move farther from Falmouth.    There are a lot of scenic places, which are located along the bike trail, so you’ll get a glimpse of amazing landmarks such as the Nobska Lighthouse.   4. Go for a swim at the Old Silver Beach  If you love swimming in the ocean, add Old Silver Beach to your list. It has beautiful sand and spectacular views of the ocean. Since the beach is quite clean, you can go for a swim, and then relax on the beach.  Speaking of which, the beach has shallow waters, which are ideal for kids. And if you bring your kids along, you can easily watch them while you are relaxing at the beach. The place is not crowded. It’s also worthwhile to note that the beach is packed with different food stands, where you can grab a quick snack.   5. Visit The O’Malley-Keyes Fine Arts Packed with countless oil paintings, the O’Malley-Keyes Fine Arts Gallery is one of the most popular galleries in Falmouth. Paintings that are exhibited in the gallery are the life’s work of a local artist, named Julia O’Malley.  As an artist who grew up in Cape Cod, Julia O’Malley uses her talent to depict how beautiful Cape Cod is. She has painted the most beautiful landmarks on Cape Cod, such as the Quissett Harbor and the Nobska Lighthouse.  Her paintings always capture the beauty of landscapes, beaches, and waterbodies in Cape Cod, bringing them to life. By visiting the gallery, you’ll get a chance to view Cape Cod from an artist’s perspective. Not to mention, most paintings are well-detailed to give you a glimpse of picturesque landscapes and landmarks, indulging you in an amazing experience. Since such paintings can evoke powerful emotions, you’ll feel as if you’ve ever visited the landmarks that are captured by the paintings.  And if you love decorating your home with paintings, you can buy paintings from this gallery to remind you of beautiful places in Cape Code.  6. Take a nature walk in Spohr Gardens There’s nothing more satisfying than taking a nature walk in a garden with a scenic environment.  Spread out on a 6-acre piece of land, Spohr Garden has a beautiful environment, which is covered with lots of vegetation, flowers, and waterbodies.  Once you get into the garden, you’ll come across multiple trails that cut through different sections of the garden, with different views.  Your attention will also be captured by flowers, growing on the edges of the trails. Examples of such flowers include daylilies, spring bulbs, and azaleas. Without a doubt, such scenic views will help you relax, improving your overall mood. The air is always filled with therapeutic sounds of birds chirping and frogs croaking. And if you get tired along the way, you can rest on a bench as you listen to the sounds of nature.    7. Collect books at The Falmouth Public Library Designed to accommodate visitors of different ages, the Falmouth Public Library gives you access to a wide variety of books, audiobooks, and DVDs. It is also worthwhile to note that the main library building is partitioned into multiple rooms to separate visitors of different age groups. Due to this, you’ll have an easy time while looking for books. Besides that, the Falmouth Public Library hosts big book sale events in July. So, if you want to add more books to your home library, attend a book sale event and take a look at the books that are exhibited there. You might find an interesting book. Not to mention, the prices might be lower due to discounts.  8. Try out local cuisines Since Falmouth is located right next to the ocean, it has a lot of restaurants that serve seafood and other cuisines. Once you visit these restaurants, you’ll get a taste of delicious food.  And if you like places with breathtaking views, you’ll love the Flying Bridge Restaurant . It sits on the edge of the coastline, giving you amazing views of the ocean.  For those who love foreign cuisines, the Osteria La Civetta may be a suitable restaurant for you. It serves Italian cuisine, making it easier for you to sample three different Italian dishes at the same spot. Visit the Water Street Kitchen if you want to try out the local cuisine. To get a sample of everything that’s featured on the menu, order the seafood platter. It comes with perfectly-seasoned mussels, oysters, and crabs. 9. Watch a live theater performance at the College Light Opera Company As the name hints, the College Light Opera Company focuses on arts, music, film, and theater. During the summer season, this theater company hosts talented musicians, artists, and actors from all over the country. It educates talented artists and gives them a chance to showcase their skills in theater performances. Performers usually organize different kinds of shows, musical plays, and drama acts; from the likes of Gilbert and Sullivan’s HMS Pinafore to the likes of Thoroughly Modern Millel.  For those who love theaters and operas, this is everything you could ever dream of! You’ll be indulged in an amazing theatrical experience with beautifully orchestrated drama acts and songs.  The main theater is designed to give you a clear view of the main stage. On top of that, seats are positioned in sections with a clear field of view. So, whether you are planning to get front-row tickets or third-row tickets, you can comfortably watch live performances from any seat. Speaking of which, the College Light Opera Company has an outdoor seating area, which is located next to small shops — you can relax here while taking your food, snack, or beer.  Visit the official website and check the theater’s schedule. This makes it easier for you to know when a show starts. Tickets are also purchased via the official website.    10. Take a trip to the Nobska Lighthouse and enjoy the views   A trip to Nobska Lighthouse can be quite rejuvenating! Surrounded by a beautiful landscape, the Nobska Lighthouse is one of the  most lovely spots in Falmouth. The road that leads to the lighthouse is a stone’s throw from the ocean. As you are headed towards the lighthouse, you’ll get a good glimpse of the ocean.  The lighthouse sits on an elevated promontory. And from an elevated point of view, it becomes much easier to view different regions at once. Examples of such regions include Elizabeth Islands, Martha’s Vineyards, Woods Hole Passage, and Vineyard Sound.  Martha’s Vineyard is one of few islands, which is close to Falmouth town. Elizabeth Island, on the other hand, is an archipelago that’s located a few miles from Falmouth’s coastline. The Vineyard Sound lies in between Martha’s Vineyard and Elizabeth Islands, separating the two sets of lands.   11. Attend cultural exhibitions at Highfield Hall & Gardens Highfield Hall is a diversified cultural center that sits on a 400-acre parcel of land. The encircling conservative area features well-trimmed gardens, hiking trails, woodlands, and beautiful vegetation. In short, Highfield Hall & Gardens has the perfect environment for outdoor exhibitions. The Passing Fancy is an example of a piece of art that’s exhibited in Highfield Hall’s conservative land. It’s a huge stickwork monument, built to convey various artistic concepts. While children love playing around with the Passing Fancy, it might fascinate you, especially if you see it in real life.  Clearly, this cultural center deals with culinary art, contemporary art, garden-related programs, and musical performances. By taking a trip to the cultural center, you’ll view different art exhibitions such as paintings and artistic musical instruments.  And if something sparks your interest, don’t hesitate to sign up for the available classes to learn more about the subject.  Dating back to the 19th century, the Highfield Hall mansion is also an old vintage house, which can give you insight into historical events.  12. Pet a fish at the Woods Hole Science Aquarium  Featuring multiple types of aquariums, the Woods Hole Science Aquarium is the home of different types of fish and marine life. And since the government runs this institution, it doesn’t charge you any access fees. You need to get close enough to an aquarium to get a clear view. The staff gives you insight into different types of marine life and helps you understand how ocean conditions affect marine life.  Visiting the research section can be quite thrilling. The research section has open aquariums, making it easier for you to pet a fish. You’ll also learn more about the types of marine food that fish consume.  13. Visit the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution If you’re always amazed by deep-sea mysteries and marine life, the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution will be the perfect place to look for answers.  To give you more insight into marine-related research, the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution will offer you a guided tour that takes you through different research labs and centers. The Ocean Science Discovery Centre & Store will be your first stop on this tour. Once you get into the research center, you’ll be taken through the types of sea vessels that are often used in ocean exploration.  And since this institution investigates ocean mysteries, it also gives you a tour of successful discoveries and solved mysteries. One of the biggest mysteries that was solved by this institution is related to the Titanic. So, everything about The Titanic ship is clearly explained and illustrated in the research center — from the moment it set sail to the moment it sank into the ocean. A lot of pictures are also exhibited in the research center to show you the damage The Titanic took after sinking. If guided tours don’t have satisfactory answers, you can get more insight by picking the brains of oceanographic scientists. The institution allocates time for one-on-one interactions with scientists. 14. Go on a historical expedition in the Museums On The Green  The Museums on The Green is made up of multiple vintage houses, monuments, and historical sites. Think of it as a collection of various museums, which are located in a neighborhood, extending over a 2-acre parcel of land.  As the name hints, the parcel of land is surrounded by a lot of greenery and vegetation, drawing you closer to nature during your historical expedition. Plus, it has multiple nature trails, making it easier for you to walk from one house to the next.   The Conant house is an example of a vintage house that’s located inside the historically-preserved zone. Dating back to the 1700s, the Conant house preserves artifacts, which depicts Falmouth’s old ways of life. For instance, it has a cannonball that goes way back to the 1800s and a jukebox that dates back to the 1930s.   The Falmouth Historical Society converted the house into a small exhibition center, extending its functionalities. From time to time, the society offers some exhibition shows, painting a clear picture of past events.  You might get lucky enough to watch a historical film titled “ A Day in the Life: Falmouth in the Forties” . It was recorded in the early ‘40s and captured Falmouth’s way of life in the early ‘40s. The Hallett Barn is another example of an old structure that preserves Falmouth’s history. Just like the Conant House, the Falmouth Historical Society uses the Hallett Barn to exhibit artifacts that streamlined economic trade. Examples of such artifacts include business receipts from the 1800s, local bank notes, business permits, old wallets, and trading tools.     15. Play golf at the Cape Cod Country Club The Cape Cod Country Club is one of the most suitable spots for playing golf. It features an 18-course golf course, which can be quite thrilling and challenging at the same time. Stretched out on a sloped terrain, the golf course has fascinating greens and fairways. Besides that, the place is surrounded by a beautiful environment, made up of woodlands, ponds, and lots of greenery. It also neighbors the Coonamessett Pond, which happens to be one of the largest kettle ponds in the town.  Playing golf in such an environment can be quite rejuvenating. When you swing your golf club, you’ll spot a few birds flying to the kettle pond. Not to mention, the sounds of nature will also calm your nerves while you are playing golf. 16. Catch the Sunset at Chapoquoit Beach Even if you’ve seen a thousand sunsets in your lifetime, you’ll never get tired of catching beautiful sunsets from new spots. Every landscape offers you a unique experience. Chapoquoit Beach is very popular for its breathtaking sunset views. And the good thing about this beach is that it is very calm and peaceful. So, it is also a perfect spot for an evening beach walk. The sand is clean, making it easier for you to walk barefoot on the sandy beach.  While you are walking on the beach, sand particles will rub through your toes and feet, just to be washed away by low tides a few seconds later. The feeling can be therapeutic and relaxing, especially if it’s complemented by a light ocean breeze and the calming sounds of ocean tides.  17. Participate in paddle boarding sports  Loosen up and challenge yourself by participating in paddleboarding sports.  Falmouth is packed with water sports companies that rent out paddle boards at an affordable price. It’s also worthwhile to note that these water sports companies can also offer you paddleboarding lessons if you are not so familiar with the activity. Thanks to the surrounding water bodies, Falmouth has a lot of suitable spots for paddleboarding. For example, the Waquoit Bay is a great starting point for a paddleboarding expedition. It’s in close proximity to interesting places. If you are experienced in paddleboarding, you can easily get to Washburn Island.        Apart from that, the stretch of water and land, extending from Falmouth to Washburn Island, is surrounded by beautiful scenery.  Falmouth also has inland water bodies, such as the Great Pond, that are ideal for paddle boarding.    Be sure to check out Peace Love SUP for a perfect paddle boarding tour/lession excursion adventure. 18. Explore the vastness of The Atlantic Ocean in a sailing expedition Exploring the Atlantic Ocean can be quite thrilling, especially if you are sailing in an open vessel. A Schooner can be the perfect vessel for a sailing expedition tour. Fortunately enough, you can book a trip on one of the most popular Schooners in Falmouth — the Liberte.  The Liberte is managed by an enthusiastic team that offers you drinks, food, and light entertainment while you are exploring the Atlantic Ocean. Since the sailing team is familiar with Cape Cod, it steers the schooner towards the most beautiful spots in Cape Cod.  Depending on the speed of the winds, the schooner might be steered towards the Woods Hole region. From that position, it becomes much easier to get a clear view of the Nobska Lighthouse and the neighboring homes.     Besides that, the schooner may also get farther into the ocean, offering you clear views of the Elizabeth Islands.   As the schooner sails toward the South, you’ll get closer to Martha’s Vineyard. The first few things you’ll notice as you are approaching Martha’s Vineyard are the vintage cottages.  19. Hike in a trail with amazing ocean views and sounds such as The Knob Found along the Quissett Harbor Trail, the Knob overlooks the ocean and has amazing views of the bay.  The Quissett Harbor Trail stretches all the way from Falmouth and is surrounded by marshes, thick vegetation, and woodlands. However, you’ll notice a slight change in the environment once you get closer to the coastline. For starters, the hiking trail may get more sandy as you are headed toward the coastline. Not to mention, different bird species always fly close to the conservative land, neighboring the Quisett hiking trail. And if you are lucky, you’ll see a few birds flying above you. This is an example of a natural experience that makes your trip more exciting.  Once you get to the Knob, your attention will be captured by the beautiful shores, which are completely covered with boulders. Sunset views from the bay are quite breathtaking.   20. Experience the thrill of windsurfing  Falmouth has the perfect spots for winding surfing activities. For instance, if you are a novice, you can practice your skills in some of the tidal ponds that are close to the ocean. Experienced surfers will also find suitable places for showing off their skills. A lot of beaches have offshore winds, which are fast enough to indulge you in an amazing surfing experience. The Old Silver Beach is an example of a destination with good offshore winds. Besides that, the place is packed with companies, specializing in water sports activities. Whether you are looking for surfing lessons or rental offers, check out Cape Cod Windsurfing & Paddle Board a water sports vender that’ll offer you amazing services. 21. Stop counting calories and go get some ice cream at Smitty’s  Have you been eating good and looking good too? Time to let loose and go to a good ice cream place. Smitty’s is a homemade ice cream place and hangout with open grass, tables & outdoor lights for relaxing a summer treat. Located on the main highway in Falmouth, not downtown but a quick drive nearby. Smitty’s has a very large variety of flavors, toppings and sundae creations. You just might fall in love with the mint chip ice cream, and the hot fudge is not to be left off any sundae! What will you choose? The harbors, the conservative areas, the hiking trails, and the marine research centers deserve a visit.  All those spots will give you an amazing experience. Don’t forget to visit beautiful beaches such as Old Silver Beach and Falmouth Heights Beach. You’ll have fun as you swim in the ocean. Not to mention, Falmouth beaches have various water sport activities. And if you love exploring the vastness of the ocean, go on a sailing expedition and learn about marine life.   Lastly, did we miss anything? Have a recommendation of your own? title: Going Places: Grassroots, Volunteerism Builds the Great American Rail-Trail
author: Karen Rubin
content: By Karen Rubin, Travel Features Syndicate, goingplacesfarandnear.com Within this one mile that cuts through Ohio forest, there are stories: reclusive Hellbender salamanders that grow to 28 inches long; a bridge where Abraham Lincoln nearly lost his life on the way to his inauguration; a rail tunnel, slightly askew, built by warring groups of Irish immigrants; a Ghost Wall, where they carved their initials that today appear, disappear and new initials reveal themselves. It’s only a mile long now slicing through Hellbender Preserve, but it is the first new mile of multi-use trail in Jefferson County; four more miles will soon be added. Ultimately, it will be part of a 15-mile connector along the Great American Rail-Trail, a 3,700-mile network of biking/walking trails across America, from Washington DC to Washington State. Even the story about how the Hellbender trail was re-discovered is worthy of a novel. This was the Old Panhandler Rail Line, but after they built a new route and bypassed this one, the 273 acre-property was abandoned in 1949 and taken over by forest. Hellbender Preserve is only one year old – it opened on National Trails Day 2025 – and within the first six months after opening, 30,000 visited. The “Ghost Wall” in Hellbender Preserve, where the first new mile of multi-use trail in Ohio’s Jefferson County has just opened and eventually will connect to the Great American Rail-Trail, 3,700-miles across the USA from Washington DC to Washington State © Karen Rubin/goingplacesfarnandnear.com “The trail builds community, provides an opportunity to meet, get out. We’re in the Rust Belt where healthcare isn’t a priority. This is passive way to get out, get fit,” Aaron Dodds, program manager for Jefferson Soil Water Conservation District, tells us as we walk through. “It’s great for conservation and railroad history.” “The railroad hired Irish workers to build it because they were cheap and expendable. They came for the American Dream and carved their names and initials in the rock walls.” When they expanded the railroad from single to double track, they brought freed slaves who also carved their names. Depending on the light, you can see the names, which later disappear and other names emerge. The names come and go. They have identified 80 different names so far. That’s why they call it the Ghost Wall. Initials in the “Ghost Wall” in Hellbender Preserve, where the first new mile of multi-use trail in Ohio’s Jefferson County has just opened and eventually will connect to the Great American Rail-Trail © Karen Rubin/goingplacesfarnandnear.com “The Irish were cheap, expendable. They first used old canal diggers from County Cork (Corkonians) and then Far Downers (from farther down Ireland). They hated each other.” They lived in separate camps and worked different sides of the tunnel. But when they came together, they found they were four feet off. “A war broke out. They went at each other with pick axes. The Corkonians raided Far Downers, chased them to the hillsides, then throw them off.” The tunnel which triggered a war between factions of Irish railroad workers is now part of the trail through Hellbender Preserve © Karen Rubin/goingplacesfarnandnear.com Far Downers broke into the Steubenville Armory and rolled out a cannon to Market Street, and fired on the Corkonians. The governor called in the state militia – it took four days to quell the violence. In the end, they figured out how to link up the tunnel (it is only slightly askew today). “It wasn’t worth a war.” Dodds wears a t-shirt with the newspaper clipping printed on the back, We come to the Lincoln Bridge and Dodds tells of a critical historical event that was almost lost to history – how Abraham Lincoln, traveling by rail to his inauguration, got stuck in a severe rainstorm that damaged this bridge and the passengers were told to walk over in case the train would have caused it to collapse; he nearly lost his life as he walked, holding his sons’ hands when he fell and was nearly swept into the water. “Lincoln Bridge,” on the former railroad line, where the president-elect nearly lost his life and rebuilt to serve Union troops during the Civil War © Karen Rubin/goingplacesfarnandnear.com Lincoln made it to Fort Steuben in Steubenville where he gave a speech on the train platform – the first time against a backdrop of seven states succeeding from the union in reaction to his election. “Now Steubenville didn’t love Lincoln,” Dodds related. “He was described as ugly and an awful speaker (with a high-pitched voice). That is what was reported when in fact, he was ‘workshopping’ his inaugural address,” considered one of his most important, in which he set the Constitutional and moral framework for keeping the Union together. Remarkably, Lincoln’s speech was forgotten until they began searching for the provenance of the land to acquire the preserve. “This event was lost to history, but a railroad vice president had collected newspaper clippings” which reported the event “and a railroad engineer atlas verified it.” The Steubenville Herald reported on the four-day riot by Irish tunnel workers, now part of the trail through Hellbender Preserve © Karen Rubin/goingplacesfarnandnear.com After the Battle of Fort Sumter in April 1861, Lincoln remembered the bridge. The Battle of Bull Run was looming. Lincoln knew he needed to get Union troops to the east, so he directed that the bridge where he almost lost his life be rebuilt. It took just eight months with a massive workforce and now named for him. The bridge is just before we enter the 970-foot long, double track tunnel. Just feet beyond the tunnel is where the trail ends for now. This one-mile is in the middle of what will be a 15-mile-long trail; so far, they have three miles and are working to open five more. The State of Ohio owned the land – acquired from ConRail – but was inaccessible to the public for all this time. The state didn’t even realize it owned it until 2015 when the commission did a title search in order to acquire it (and uncovered the Lincoln story). The state willingly donated the land to the commission for a multi-use trail, but it still took five more years. Good neighbor Mike Ruthen sets out bikes for visitors to Hellbender Preserve to use and is one of the volunteers who help maintain the rail-trail which will ultimately connect to the Great American Rail-Trail © Karen Rubin/goingplacesfarandnear.com Mike Ruthen, whose gorgeous property along the creek is immediately adjacent to the property, puts bikes out for visitors to use and volunteers to help maintain the trail. “He saw the joy on people’s faces when they come,” Dodds said. “One mile at a time. The trail builds community,” he said. Hellbender Trail, https://www.traillink.com/trail/hellbender-preserve-trail/ Ribbon Cutting in Orrville As we drive into Orrville, Ohio, we see Amish driving horse-drawn carriages, pass a Lehman’s store (everything you ever needed to buy is at Lehman’s), and the headquarters for The J.M. Smucker Company (Smucker’s!), where you see railroad tracks that come right up to the entrance. We have come to Orrville to celebrate with Rails to Trails of Wayne County the ribbon cutting for 2.7 new miles of the Heartland Trail, a connector to the Great American Rail-Trail. Don Noble of Rails to Trails Allegheny, with state and local leaders and Brandi Horton, Rails to Trails Conservancy’s Vice President, Communications, cut the ribbon celebrating the opening of 2.7 new miles of Ohio’s Heartland Trail which will ultimately connect to the Great American Rail-Trail © Karen Rubin/goingplacesfarandnear.com The new section begins at the downtown trailhead, just 3 blocks from the Orrville Historical Museum and Orville Railroad Heritage Society on Depot Street. The trail then threads northward through the downtown business district and Orrville Dog Park before connecting to the former Cleveland, Akron, and Columbus (CA&C) rail corridor near Little Chippewa Creek, then continues along the former railbed to Marshallville, terminating at Coal Bank Road. Don Noble, Board President Rails to Trails of Wayne County, noted that along the trail in Marshallville, there is an unusual “geologic unconformity” dating from the Carboniferous Period (360–299 million years ago) when erosion removed older (Mississippian) rocks before younger (Pennsylvanian) rocks were deposited. The rare geologic feature was revealed during the construction of the railroad. Victor Schantz of Orrville, takes a ride on the new section of Ohio’s Heartland Trail, one of more than 150 trails that will connect 3,700 miles of the Great American Rail-Trail, from Washington DC to Washington state © Karen Rubin/goingplacesfarandnear.com Rails to Trails of Wayne County put in an application to Ohio Department of Transportation in 2020 and received $1.33 million – 58% of the total cost – but the city and donors had to come up with the rest – Ohio Clean put up $200,000; the City of Orrville, $238,000, and a foundation gave $535,000, The group has managed to complete two sections in one year (1.7 and 1.1 miles each), from downtown Orrville north of Marshallville – a total of 7 miles in order to eventually connect to the Great American Rail-Trail. Rails to Trails of Wayne County hopes to complete another extension of the trail that will connect it to Clinton where it will connect to the Ohio & Erie Towpath Trail , which spans 80 miles from Cleveland to Bolivar. “This is a great day for Orrville,” Mayor Matt Plybon said. “Years ago, people saw the old railroad bed and saw what could become. This moves Orrville closer to becoming true trail town, neighbors and beyond…We welcome people who come- shop, eat, experience community, meet people. Trails may connect place but their best value is when they connect people.” Don Noble of Rails to Trails Allegheny and Kevin Belle, Rails to Trails Conservancy’s Project Director, celebrate the opening of 2.7 new miles of the Heartland Trail, a connector to the Great American Rail-Trail © Karen Rubin/goingplacesfarandnear.com As we sit together for lunch with many of the Rails to Trails of Wayne County volunteers and officials it becomes clear: It may take years before all 3,700 miles of the Great American Rail-Trail across America are connected, but every foot and every mile of trail impacts people today in tangible ways – those who live in community and those who come to visit – economically, health and wellness, building community and social connections, and pride. Leaving Orrville, Kevin Belle, who has spent 10 years as Rails to Trails Conservancy’s Project Director for the Great American Rail-Trail, reflected that they have successfully closed 10 gaps in less than 10 years. “They are coming more frequently now,” he said, with the pride of a new father or more accurately, a midwife who has helped in the birth of a baby. “Close the gap. Open the trail.” The Great American Rail-Trail will extend 3,700 miles across the USA, enabling biking, walking, hiking from Washington DC to Washington State. “This is the most ambitious public lands project in generations, but unlike other projects, this is the result of the determination of regular people, groups, private donations, working in conjunction with local, state and federal government, reflected Brandi Horton, Rails to Trails Conservancy’s Vice President, Communications. title: New Wantagh childcare center keeps needs of local community in mind
author: Vivian Rose
content: Nearly 17.5% of workers living in Wantagh work from home, while more than 64% work outside of the home, according to aggregated data . To help meet the needs of working parents, a new childcare center has opened at 3309 Merrick Rd., co-founder Melissa Borger said. The center officially opened in September and began accepting students ranging from infants to five-year-olds. The center, known as Creative Play Childcare Center, was co-founded by Borger and her business partner, Dhanaive Nunez. The center is open five days a week, from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. and offers extended hours for parents traveling from work. Borger, who has lived in the area for about 25 years, said the duo opened the center with Wantagh working families in mind and engaged with the community before opening. [caption id="attachment_377764" align="alignnone" width="469"] Creative Play Childcare Center in Wantagh offers care for students between six weeks to 5 years old. ( Provided by Melissa Borger) [/caption] She said families expressed interest in a smaller, more individualized care center and that the location can accommodate no more than 38 students: eight in the infant room, 12 in the toddler room, and 18 in the prekindergarten classroom. Borger said the infant room is led by a teacher, an assistant teacher and a floater, and that students can range from 6 weeks to 18 months old. She said that once students age out of the infant room, they can move to the toddler room, which serves students ages 18 months to 3 years old. She said the room is led by a certified teacher, an assistant and another floater. Once students are 3 years old, they transition to the prekindergarten room, which is for students between 3 and 5 years old, who are instructed by a lead and assistant teacher. “I've watched it change over the years,” Borger said. “We know that Wantagh is a family-based community, with a lot of young families, a lot of two-family working homes, so we wanted to provide for that. And I think also in this neighborhood, what it was lacking was that more individualized approach that meets the need.” The center is Montessori-inspired, which encourages students to learn through play, Nunez said. [caption id="attachment_377765" align="alignnone" width="700"] Classes are Montessori-inspired, which encourages a play-based curriculum. ( Provided by Melissa Borger) [/caption] She said she was interested in making the curriculum play-based after observing that her grandson, who is on the spectrum, did not show progression in his socialization skills while at a traditional childcare center. “After a whole year of preparation and going through the process with the town of Hempstead, with [the Office of Children and Family Services], we're so happy to open our first center to be able to offer this same great quality care with amazing qualified certified teachers for the Wantagh location,” Nunez said. Nunez said she went to art school prior to entering the medical industry and later pivoted into childcare. In 2023, she opened her first group family daycare in Elmont and a second location in Valley Stream before teaming up with Borger, who has nearly 35 years of experience in healthcare and business operations. “This idea of partnering with Danny was something that just felt right,” Borger said. “Being able to build something in this community that wasn't just another daycare, but the kind of childcare center that I wish I would have had when my kids were young enough to attend. So I know what a blessing it is for the community here.”

title: Port Washington Water Pollution Control District proposes 12% budget hike, remains under tax cap
author: Larissa Fuentes
content: A 12% spending increase in the Port Washington Water Pollution Control District’s overall proposed 2027 budget is being driven by infrastructure needs, rising operating costs and preparations for costly sewer emergencies — but district officials say the tax levy would increase by just 1%. The Port Washington Water Pollution Control District is proposing a $12.3 million budget for 2027, an increase of about 12.4% from the current year, with district officials attributing the spending plan to infrastructure needs, rising operating costs and preparations for unexpected sewer system emergencies. Commissioner Melanie Cassens and Business Manager Giovanna DiFiore said in an interview that the proposed budget totals $12,292,781, compared with $10,937,814 in 2026. They emphasized that the overall budget increase does not translate into an equivalent increase in the amount collected from taxpayers. The proposed tax levy is $8,632,621, up from $8,549,830 this year, an increase of about 1%, according to DiFiore. The district is approximately 1.6% below its state-mandated tax cap, Cassens said. “The 12% increase overall is not a 12% — it doesn't affect our taxpayers 12%,” Cassens said. “What would be concerning to the public would be if we were to pierce the tax cap.” The tentative budget outlines expenses for sewer administration, sanitary sewer operations, sewage treatment and disposal, employee benefits and debt service. Among the increases are costs for professional services, equipment, sewage and sludge disposal, and a contingency fund intended to cover unexpected repairs. DiFiore said the district is budgeting $1.1 million for sewage and sludge treatment and disposal, an increase of $100,000 from the previous year. The expense covers the hauling of solid and liquid waste, including the possibility that liquid waste may need to be removed if the treatment plant experiences operational problems. The district also is increasing its contingency allocation to prepare for emergency repairs. Officials said the district began setting aside contingency funds last year, initially budgeting $50,000, but that amount would not be sufficient to cover a major sewer line break. Cassens cited a significant break on Beacon Hill Road in 2025 that required repairs approximately 20 feet underground and cost about $300,000. “We don't have that budget,” Cassens said of the potential cost of a major break, explaining that a larger contingency fund would give the district more flexibility to respond to unforeseen problems. Other proposed spending increases include a full actuarial valuation, grant-writing assistance, media transcription services, additional website maintenance and security, and a new district newsletter. Cassens said the newsletter is intended to improve communication with residents, supplementing the district's website and recently established Facebook page. The newsletter will provide information about the district's operations, infrastructure improvements, grant funding and sewer system issues that residents may not otherwise know about, she said. Cassens cited saltwater intrusion into sewer pipes as one example of an issue the district hopes to explain to the public. Saltwater entering the system can place additional strain on operations and interfere with the district's ability to properly treat wastewater before it is discharged into the bay. Infrastructure rehabilitation is another major financial consideration. Cassens said the district must continue investing in its sewer collection system and treatment plant because the facilities operate around the clock throughout the year. The proposed budget includes $1,562,497 in benefits and debt service, compared with $1,704,255 in the adopted 2026 budget. District officials said borrowing remains part of their long-term strategy for financing improvements to the collection system and treatment plant. Cassens also addressed concerns about the district's ownership and upkeep of Sunset Park, saying the park was not responsible for the overall budget increase. The district has historically paid for landscaping, garbage removal and snow removal at the property. Additional expenses arose when the district worked to bring the park's clubhouse up to safety standards, she said. [caption id="attachment_377766" align="alignnone" width="584"] The Port Washington Water Pollution Control District has made changed to the clubhouse at Sunset Park after regaining control over it. [/caption] Cassens said those additional costs have been covered with non-tax revenue, including fees from permitting the athletic fields for sports and payments for advertising signs on the field's fencing. The district also received a donation from the Dejana Foundation through the Friends of Sunset Park, a nonprofit organization established in 2020. The district is working on a license agreement with the nonprofit to formalize its arrangement, Cassens said.

title: New Hyde Park Halloween festival returns Oct. 31 with pie-eating contests, pumpkin decorating and more
author: Miao Li
content: Families looking for a festive way to celebrate Halloween will have plenty of activities to choose from when the Village of New Hyde Park hosts its annual Halloween Fall Festival on Oct. 31. The event will begin at noon at Memorial Park and will mark the sixth year of the village’s Halloween celebration. The afternoon will feature costume contests for different age groups, with gift sets planned for first-, second- and third-place winners. Children will also be able to participate in games and win prizes, as well as decorate small pumpkins donated by Milena Garden Center. title: Long Island freight trains get cleaner with $10.9 million investment
author: Miao Li
content: For many Long Islanders, freight trains are easy to miss. Operating largely during midday and late-night hours on the same tracks used by the Long Island Rail Road, they quietly haul heavy loads that help keep stores, businesses and supply chains moving. That largely unseen network is about to get cleaner. New York & Atlantic Railway has secured a $10.9 million public-private investment to upgrade four locomotives with Tier 4 emissions technology, the strictest U.S. Environmental Protection Agency standard for diesel locomotives. The investment includes a $6.5 million federal Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements grant, $2 million from New York state and $2.4 million from NYA. The project is part of the railway’s goal of having a Tier 4-compliant fleet by 2030. The upgrades will replace engines and engine components and add new emissions technology, said NYA President Marlon Taylor. The four locomotives operate throughout NYA’s territory, including Brooklyn, Queens and Long Island, so the benefits will extend along the system. “Everybody will see a benefit,” Taylor said. The grant process and related paperwork are expected to be completed by the end of the first quarter of 2027, with rebuilding potentially beginning later that year. Each locomotive is expected to take about nine months to rebuild, with the four potentially completed by 2029. Read More: Mineola awards $11M grant for lead water line replacements For residents living near the rail lines, the upgrades are expected to reduce nitrogen oxide and particulate matter emissions. The locomotives will undergo testing after rebuilding to measure performance, Taylor said. The project also highlights the less-visible role freight rail plays in Long Island’s economy. NYA moves more than 30,000 rail cars annually. Each can carry roughly the weight of four loaded trucks, representing more than 120,000 truckloads. The freight includes lumber for Home Depot’s 22 Long Island stores, recyclable metals from Gershow Recycling in Medford that are shipped to markets outside the Northeast, and food products delivered to DiCarlo Food in Holtsville. In Queens, NYA also transports imported beer, including Modelo and Corona from Mexico. Freight rail becomes particularly useful when goods must travel long distances, Taylor said. “If you want to get your goods across the U.S., that’s where railroads show up,” he said, particularly for “heavy, bulky material.” NYA currently has three Tier 4 locomotives. The four upgrades would bring that number to seven, while the LIRR is working on funding for eight additional locomotives, Taylor said. The upgrades are expected to bring NYA closer to its 2030 goal while making the freight trains traveling on Long Island’s familiar LIRR rails cleaner and more efficient.

title: U.S. News ranks Nassau County’s best elementary and middle schools for 2027
author: Miao Li
content: Two Nassau County schools earned top placements in New York state in the 2027 Best Elementary and Middle Schools rankings released by U.S. News & World Report. Lakeville Elementary School in Great Neck ranked No. 35 statewide among elementary schools, while Manhasset Middle School ranked No. 39 among middle schools, according to the rankings. The annual report, released Oct. 20, evaluates public elementary and middle schools nationwide. It covers about 46,000 elementary schools and more than 24,000 middle schools, with rankings at the state and district levels. Other Nassau County elementary schools also placed among New York’s top 100. Willits Elementary School in Syosset ranked No. 40, followed by George A. Jackson School in Jericho at No. 58 and South Grove Elementary School in Syosset at No. 61. Shelter Rock Elementary School in Manhasset ranked No. 66, McVey Elementary School in East Meadow ranked No. 68, and Jeffrey Ratner-Robert Seaman Elementary School in Jericho ranked No. 71. Glenwood Landing Elementary School in the North Shore School District ranked No. 72, Village Elementary School in Syosset ranked No. 78, and Munsey Park Elementary School in Manhasset ranked No. 82. Read More: Syosset tops Niche’s Nassau County high school rankings Among middle schools, Great Neck South Middle School ranked No. 49 statewide. Syosset’s H.B. Thompson Middle School and South Woods Middle School ranked No. 52 and No. 54, respectively. Jericho Middle School ranked No. 61, Herricks Middle School ranked No. 67, and North Shore Middle School ranked No. 72. Willets Road School in the East Williston School District ranked No. 74, Academy Charter School in Hempstead ranked No. 88, and Roslyn Middle School ranked No. 95. Manhasset UFSD Interim Superintendent Christopher Pellettieri said the ranking reflects the dedication of school staff, family support and the strength of the school community. “We are very proud to see Manhasset Middle School recognized as the highest-ranked public middle school in Nassau County,” Pellettieri said. “Ultimately, this honor reflects the collective efforts of everyone who works together on behalf of every child, every day to ensure our students have the opportunity to learn, grow, and succeed.” Great Neck Public Schools Superintendent Kenneth Bossert also welcomed the recognition of Lakeville Elementary School, which ranked No. 35 in New York state. “We’re proud that our schools continue to be recognized for academic excellence, which reflects the work of all our students and educators, and the support of our parents, residents and Board of Education,” Bossert said. The 2027 rankings use data collected directly from state education agencies by RTI International, along with data from the U.S. Department of Education. The updated approach assesses student performance in reading and mathematics across proficiency levels while accounting for student backgrounds and absolute performance on state assessments. U.S. News evaluates math and reading/language arts performance alongside student demographics to measure overall achievement and school effectiveness. Student-teacher ratios are used to break ties in overall scores. The rankings are intended to help families and educators assess school performance, though they represent one measure of a school’s academic outcomes.

title: West Hempstead synagogue arson case results in hate crime charges
author: Timothy Bolger
content: A Lakeview man who was arrested for allegedly vandalizing a West Hempstead synagogue is facing upgraded hate crimes charges, Nassau County authorities said. Azzm Khan pleaded not guilty on Oct. 22 at Nassau County court to charges of arson as a hate crime, criminal mischief as a hate crime, and related counts. Nassau police said the 29-year-old suspect lit a lawn sign on fire and tried to stuff it under the door of Young Israel of West Hempstead on Hempstead Avenue at 11:30 p.m. Oct. 21. Khan then put the sign in a bush, which caught fire, repeatedly kicked the back door of the synagogue, and broke the sideview mirror of a Nassau police auxiliary vehicle, authorities added. Fifth Squad detectives took the suspect into custody without incident, say there are no known threats to the community, and are continuing the investigation. Bail for Kahn was set at $50,000 cash, $125,000 bond or $250,000 partially secured bond. He is due back in court on Nov. 4. His attorney did not respond to a request for comment. title: Hicksville school board optimistic about scholarship program offering benefits for students, tax breaks for donors
author: Nicholas Gordon
content: Members of the Hicksville Board of Education expressed optimism about a forthcoming Scholarship Granting Organization (SGO) program at the board’s meeting on Wednesday Oct. 21. Under the federal program, which Gov. Kathy Hochul recently announced the state intends to join starting Jan. 1, 2027, residents can donate money to approved scholarship organizations and receive federal tax credits. Board members also discussed efforts to gain greater oversight of district funding for local charter schools. Under the program, SGOs can collect charitable contributions from individuals or corporations and use the funds for K–12 scholarships or educational expenses. Individual donors can receive a federal tax credit of up to $1,700 per year for qualifying contributions, and married couples filing jointly can claim up to $3,400. “It’s a benefit for our taxpayers for a tax break while giving back to the school district, and also for our staff members to be able to give back to the students they serve,” Superintendent for Hicksville Public Schools Theodore Fulton said. The program will allow qualifying 501(c)(3) tax-exempt nonprofit SGOs to receive financial contributions from community members. Fulton said the board would share SGO regulations and timelines with the community when they become available. In the meantime, the board is researching the program and communicating with other districts, he added. Fulton cited examples of eligible uses for donations, including tuition and mandatory fees, tutoring and academic instruction, special education services, after-school programs, books, and school supplies, academic equipment, student transportation, and educational technology. “We can’t be the full drivers of the creation of the SGOs so we’ll need community partners to work with us,” Fulton said, noting that there has been talk of a potential Nassau County SGO in which multiple districts could collaborate. Pivoting to the school budget, Fulton discussed the board’s efforts to gain oversight of funding for local charter schools. The district is currently required to fund two charter schools for a total of $975,000 to cover enrollments for 34 students, he said. “The issue is right now we don’t have a say in whether or not a charter school expands or recruits students,” Fulton said. “We don’t have a say in how our tax revenue is being spent or where it’s being sent in that regard. It’s a significant portion of our budget that we have no say on, which is contradictory to the governance we have over our fiscal tax dollars.” Fulton said the district, along with several other school districts he’s been communicating with, is urging elected officials to create legislation giving local communities a voice in charter school expansion within their districts, as well as greater fiscal oversight on how their tax dollars are spent. “We’re asking for a voice at the table with regards to charter schools,” Fulton said, adding that the effort will require community support through measures such as a letter-writing campaign or social media push. “It’ll be old-fashioned, grassroots, boots-on-the-ground advocacy and lobbying for local control of charter schools, so that when we meet with our elected officials we can show that we have the support,” Fulton said. “Our taxpayers should have a voice in how we spend our tax dollars.”

title: Manhasset parents raise student safety concerns at school board meeting
author: Nicholas Gordon
content: The public comment section of a school board meeting typically comes at the end of the session, after numerous agenda items and committee presentations. But at the Manhasset Board of Education’s meeting on Thursday, Oct. 22, the board made an exception to accommodate the large number of parents who showed up in the small conference room, holding public comment at the outset. Half a dozen parents stepped up to voice grave concerns about student safety. While the parents did not cite specific incidents of violence, they expressed deep concern over the district’s handling of recently reported incidents, urging the board to act with greater transparency and accountability in responding to students’ reports. Some called for a reassessment of the district’s safety protocols. “We can’t normalize violence in our schools,” one parent said. “We must show our students that when they report an incidence of violence, immediate action will be taken.” Another resident, who identified as “a parent of two children in the district,” said, “After a recent safety failure, the school reassured me that the school will put more safeguards in place. Yet this month, October, more children were harmed, and the parents of these children are here today, asking why are safety failures ongoing?” The resident said the district’s current safety review process fails to connect related incidents and identify recurring patterns of violence, allowing problems to persist. One resident pleaded with the board in a trembling voice to “please support honest students and properly address their reports of incidents of violence.” Another resident who identified as “a proud parent and grateful member of the community of Manhasset” said, “Historically a feeling of safety was a baseline expectation. However, with the repetitive incidents happening in our community, teachers can’t work properly and students can’t learn safely. We must ensure safety so our children can excel. We want to know what concrete steps the school is willing to take on this issue.” “It’s painful to lose trust in the very institution responsible for protecting our children,” the resident added. “We’re not asking for anything extraordinary, but basic safety.” The final resident who spoke on the issue said families were struggling to obtain accurate information about why their children had been injured and were being denied access to video footage. The resident asked the board to investigate whether the district’s procedures align with SHERPA (Systematic Human Error Reduction and Prediction Approach), a framework used by administrators to mitigate potential safety issues. “At what point does repeated aggression prompt reassessment of the safety protocols?” the resident asked. The district’s interim superintendent of schools, Christopher Pellettieri, who has held the role since August 2025, thanked the parents for sharing their concerns and vowed to investigate the matter and share his findings. The meeting then shifted to academic achievement, with several instructors presenting data on students’ performance on Regents Exams across English Language Arts, math, science, and social studies. Presenters also highlighted that 98% of the district’s graduating seniors are college-bound and that the number of students taking Advanced Placement exams has increased by 45% since 2022. Assistant superintendent of curriculum and instruction Rebecca Chowske reviewed updates regarding New York Inspires, an initiative introduced by the New York State Education Department and the Board of Regents to modernize high school graduation requirements and redefine the merits of a diploma. In the 2026-2027 school year, the district will begin implementing the initiative’s Portrait of a Graduate framework, which outlines the skills and personal qualities students are expected to develop by graduation. Starting in the 2027–2028 school year, the district will transition to a unified diploma, phasing out Regents Exams as a mandatory graduation requirement under the initiative. Chowske presented a points system showing how the Regents Exams will continue to be used under a “do no harm” approach in that scores can improve a student’s final grade but cannot lower it. “We can use this in between time as a creative learning space,” Chowske said, acknowledging the uncertainty as the new initiative continues to roll out. At the meeting’s close, Pellettieri returned to the parent’s concerns on student safety. “We heard some really important things from the community tonight,” Pellettieri said, reiterating that student safety is a priority. “I will take on looking into these concerns. We will commit ourselves to winning back the trust with our community.”
